A five-year-old boy is helping his grandmother cook by cutting out biscuits from the dough she's made, and he's doing it rather badly. He instructs the family robot to take over and, even though the robot's never done this before, it quickly learns what to do, and cuts out the biscuits perfectly. The grandmother is rather disappointed, remembering fondly the lopsided biscuits, complete with grubby fingerprints, that her son had charmingly baked for her at that age. Her grandson continues to use the robot for such tasks, and will grow up with pretty poor manual dexterity.

When the boy's parents come home, he says: 'Look, I've made these biscuits for you.' One parent says: 'Oh how lovely, may I have one?' The other thinks silently: 'No you didn't make these yourself, you little cheat.'

Artificial intelligence (AI) might have the potential to change how we approach tasks, and what we value. If we are using AI to do our thinking for us, employing AI might atrophy our thinking skills.

The AI we have at the moment is narrow AI – it can perform only selected, specific tasks. And even when an AI can perform as well as, or better than, humans at certain tasks, it does not necessarily achieve these results in the same way that humans do. One thing that AI is very good at is sifting through masses of data at great speed. Using machine learning, an AI that's been trained with thousands of images can develop the capacity to recognise a photograph of a cat (an important achievement, given the predominance of pictures of cats on the internet). But humans do this very differently. A small child can often recognise a cat after just one example.

Because AI might 'think' differently to how humans think, and because of the general tendency to get swept up in its allure, its use could well change how we approach tasks and make decisions. The seductive allure that tends to surround AI in fact represents one of its dangers. Those working in the field despair that almost every article about AI hypes its powers, and even those about banal uses of AI are illustrated with killer robots.

The impact of technology on shaping our values is well-established. At a recent roundtable discussion on the ethics of AI, the group I was in spent most of our time discussing the well-known example of the washing machine, which did not simply 'take over' the laundry, but which has had a major impact on attitudes to cleanliness and housework, and on the manufacture of clothing. Because AI is designed to contribute not merely to the laundry, but to how we think and make decisions over an indeterminate number of tasks, we need to consider seriously how it might change our own thought and behaviour.

It's important to remember that AI can take many forms, and be applied in many different ways, so none of this is to argue that using AI will be 'good' or 'bad'. In some cases, AI might nudge us to improve our approach. But in others, it could reduce or atrophy our approach to important issues. It might even skew how we think about values.

We can get used to technology very swiftly. Change-blindness and fast adaptation to technology can mean we're not fully aware of such cultural and value shifts. For example, attitudes to privacy have changed considerably along with the vast technological shifts in how we communicate and how data is shared and processed. One of the very things driving progress in AI is indeed the vast amounts of data now available, much of it about us, collected as we go about our daily lives. Many people are extremely wary of the organisations that have control of our data, while nonetheless continuing to post large amounts of very personal information that even a few years ago would have been considered private. Research shows that people's concerns about data privacy are inconsistent from one situation to the next. This is not to say that technology 'alone' has done this, since there are always other social changes operating at the same time.

And perhaps we are especially blind to the effects of some technology because it does so much to shape how we see the world. The challenge of AI is that it might operate in ways we aren't fully aware of. It helps to mould how we communicate with each other, how we think, how we find the world. This is not completely new: writing technology, the printing press and the telephone have already altered how we perceive and interact with our world, and even changed our brains. But AI might be even more powerful. Algorithms embedded into the technology through which we access so much information could be shaping what information we receive, how we receive it, even how we react to it. And AI might be shaping our behaviour, not as an unintended consequence of its use, but by design. Technology, often aided by AI, is exploiting human psychology to shape how we behave. Phones and social media platforms are designed by drawing upon psychological research about how to produce addictive responses to their use.

So let's explore a few examples of the use or potential use of AI, focusing on how machines and humans use and analyse data.

First, let's be clear that there can be great advantages in using AI over human decision making. The fast sharing and robust data-analysis that AI performs can be extremely advantageous. For example, the information engineer Paul Newman of the Oxford Mobile Robotics Group points out that learning from accidents in vehicles driven by humans is a slow and complex process. Other humans can't learn directly from each individual case, and even the human involved might learn little or nothing. But whenever an autonomous car has an accident, all the data can immediately be shared among all other autonomous vehicles, and used to reduce the chances of a future accident.

This aspect of AI – the ability to share information like a hive mind and to analyse data rapidly and rigorously – might then constitute a real improvement in how we solve problems. Sharing pooled data is something AI is extremely good at. Analysing data quickly is another. That's how training AI on thousands of pictures of cats works. In fact, it's access to vast pools of data, together with the ability to analyse this data at speed, that's helping to drive the current boom in AI.

Although autonomous vehicles can also make errors, this example demonstrates the human faults that AI can overcome. There are all sorts of ways in which humans fail to take in or analyse the data needed to make good decisions and to act on them. An autonomous vehicle will never be ashamed to admit fault, never be too vain to wear driving glasses, never insist on driving when tired, never refuse to go on an advanced driver course. Overcoming bias, partiality and irrationality is one way of improving human decision making – especially where issues of value are concerned. Some of these biases and irrationalities involve the rejection of, or failure to process, relevant information. So this model of using AI to pool data seems to be an advantage we can apply to decision making.

But such a conclusion might be hasty. Not all our problems can be solved by a purely data-led approach. It is pretty clear that avoiding car accidents is good. It's a safety issue where what we're doing is mostly applying technological fixes, and it's pretty easy to measure success. The vehicle either crashes or it doesn't, and deaths and injuries can be determined. It's also pretty easy to measure near-misses. But for problems that are less purely technical, it's not so clear that a data-driven, 'hive mind' approach is always good.

Take medicine, for example, one of the most promising areas of AI. Medicine is both a science, and an art: it combines science and technology with the pursuit of values: the value of health, the value of good patient relations, the value of person-centred care, the value of patient autonomy, and others. In medicine, we are not just looking for a technological fix.

The use of AI in diagnosis is very promising, for example, in assisting with the interpretation of medical images by trawling through vast amounts of data. The evidence seems to be that AI can detect minute differences between images that the human eye doesn't notice. But it can also make blatant errors that a human would never make. So, currently, combining AI with human skills seems the best option for improving diagnosis. So far, this is excellent news.

But a piece in The New England Journal of Medicine in 2018 by Danton Char, Nigam Shah and David Magnus of the Stanford University School of Medicine in California raises serious questions about using AI in diagnosis and treatment decisions. Think about medicine as a science. If AI forms the 'repository for the collective medical mind', we'd have to be extremely careful before using it in a way that moves towards uniformity of professional thinking, which might foreclose independent thought and individual clinical experience. At the moment, it's recognised that there might be different bodies of medical opinion about diagnosis and treatment. If we could be utterly confident that AI was only improving accuracy, then greater uniformity of medical thinking would be good. But there's a danger that AI might prematurely shut off options or lead us down particular treatment routes. Moreover, the authors warn that such machine learning might even be used to nudge treatment towards hitting targets or achieving profits for vested interests, rather than what's best for patients. The data might drive the medicine, rather than the other way around.

Think about medicine as an art. It involves relating to patients as real individuals living their own lives. Although AI might help us better achieve the goal of health, treatments with a lower chance of success might be the better option for some patients, all things considered. A data-driven approach alone cannot tell us this. And we need to be cautious we're not carried away by the power of technology. For we already know that free and informed consent is extremely hard to achieve in practice, and that the medical establishment influences patients' consent. But with the added gravitas of technology, and of blanket professional agreement, the danger is that wedding the existing power of the medical profession to the added power of AI, 'Computer says take the drugs' might become a reality.

The relationship between physician and patient is at the heart of medicine, and of our understanding of medical ethics. But the use of AI could subtly, even radically, alter this. Precisely how we implement the morally laudable aim of using AI to improve patient care needs careful consideration.

AI's ability to manipulate and process vast amounts of data might push us into giving undue or sole prominence to data-driven approaches to identifying and solving problems. This might lead to uniformity of thinking, even in cases where there are reasons to aspire to variety of thought and approach. It might also eclipse other factors and, in doing so, distort not just our thinking, but our values.

How a decision is made, and by whom; how an action is performed, and by whom – these are critical issues in many circumstances. It's especially the case where values are concerned. The parent who was skeptical that the boy had really made the cookies himself has a point. Perhaps if he'd first designed and built the robot, his claim would have had more validity. The significance of these factors will vary from case to case, as will the potential significance of replacing or supplementing human intelligence with machine intelligence.

Take the use of juries. We all know that juries are flawed: they sometimes get the wrong answer. Algorithms are already helping US courts come to some decisions regarding sentencing and parole, drawing on data such as information about recidivism rates, to considerable controversy. There are fears that this can help entrench existing biases against certain groups. But imagine that we have reached the point at which feeding all the available evidence into a computer has led to more accurate verdicts than those reached by juries. In such a case, the computer would be able to pool and analyse all data with speed and (in this imagined example) accuracy and efficiency. Compare how actual juries work, where individuals might have made differing notes about the case, recall different things and, even after hours of deliberations, still have different views of the evidence. The power of AI to gather and analyse data might go a long way to address these shortcomings.

But this example readily demonstrates that we care about more than simply getting things right. Even if, by using a machine, we get a more accurate answer, there can still be some reason to value the distinctive contribution of having humans serving on juries. Consider the history of how legal reforms and individual rights have been fought for, and the value of the common person that's enshrined in the notion of being tried by 'a jury of one's peers'. Perhaps we want to hand that over to an AI – but perhaps not.

The bias that humans can display, the tendency to be swayed by emotion, is of course a potential weakness in reaching a verdict. But it has also been the impetus for changes in the law. There are instances of 'jury nullification' where, swayed by those pesky human feelings of injustice, juries have simply failed to convict, even though the defendant is clearly guilty in terms of a strict application of the law. No matter how good at assessing evidence a machine might be, we're a long way off developing machines with a finely tuned sense of justice, an eye for the underdog, and the moral backbone to defy the apparatus of the legal system.

But the more general idea remains that juries perform the role of an independent source of judgment as a counter to the vested interests of the most powerful. As Lord Devlin said in the House of Lords in 2004: '[T]rial by jury is more than an instrument of justice and more than one wheel of the constitution: it is the lamp that shows that freedom lives.' And note this: the very feature of AI that is a strength in avoiding accidents for autonomous vehicles – the pooling of information, the melding of insights – in the context of the law directly undermines the basic moral principle of independence of juries. This independence is a counter to the ever-present possibility of powerful vested interests and gives a reason to keep trial by jury while being concerned with more than the mere processing of information presented in court.

A critic might say that we need this independence only because humans are so unreliable: the legal profession alone can't be left in charge of justice, but an accurate AI would solve the problem and maybe, with the passage of time, we'd get used to the idea, and hand over our justice system to the machines.

But it's utterly utopian to think that we'll ever escape the power imbalances and vested interests that are the reason for having juries. There are alternatives to the miscarriage of justice problem than handing over justice to the machines, such as a fast, accessible appeals system. Perhaps, in the future, AI might assist judges and juries to come to decisions – but this is rather different to envisaging that AI might replace humans in legal decision making. Even here, we'd need to think carefully about the impact of AI, and whether it was nudging us towards a more technocratic approach. The law developed as a human political and social system through much struggle. But the use of AI within the law could, over time, help to change this. We need to consider this carefully, in full awareness of the many implications for justice and democracy.

One great attraction of using AI is simply the sheer speed at which it can analyse data. Efficiency is a virtue, but this virtue depends upon the ends to which it is being used. It's also by no means the only virtue. If a machine can accomplish something quickly and efficiently, we might be more tempted to use it than is really merited. And the speed with which it accomplishes tasks might make us overlook problems in how it achieves its ends. We might then end up placing too great a value on such efficiently generated results.

The Anti-Defamation League (ADL) in conjunction with D-Lab at the University of California, Berkeley, is developing an Online Hate Index (OHI) using machine learning in an attempt to detect hate speech online. This is an interesting example: it's a 'tech on tech' solution – the alleged proliferation of 'hate speech' online is (seemingly) a product of computerised technology. Yet hurling abuse at opponents is hardly new. Long before the World Wide Web was even a twinkle in the eye of Tim Berners-Lee, the 17th-century French philosopher René Descartes described the work of rival mathematician Pierre de Fermat as 'shit'. The long pedigree of insults is worth noting, given the way that hype around AI encourages us to think of issues as new, or uniquely dangerous. One way in which we can be steered in the direction of over-reliance on the narrow range of capacities that AI has is precisely by the combined assumptions that 'tech cause = tech solution', together with the idea that today's tech is especially full of novel moral perils.

The concept of 'hate speech' is itself controversial. Some consider that attempting to eliminate certain uses of language, whether by law or by those managing online platforms, is necessary to achieve goals such as the elimination of discrimination. Others worry that this is a danger to free speech, and represents a form of censorship. There are concerns that what counts as hate speech to one person is merely banter to another, and that it's extremely hard to classify something as 'hate speech' out of context. Additionally, there are concerns that, with the vast amount of material posted online, any policing of 'hate speech' will be patchy, and there are fears that some groups or individuals might be disproportionately targeted.

If we could automate the detection of hate speech online, it might help with classification and consistency. The OHI could address these issues by processing data faster than a human, and applying the policy correctly, without bias. (Of course, this depends on how it's programmed. If it's programmed to be biased, it will be biased with great efficiency.)

So here is the problem. Enthused with the idea that an AI can detect, categorise and eliminate 'hate speech' with a speed and consistency that leaves humans standing, coupled with fears that the online world is turning so many of us into irresponsible hate-filled trolls, we could use this technology with such alacrity that the other problems of hate speech get somewhat overlooked. This then could help to drive the debate that could be roughly summarised as 'hate speech versus free speech' in one particular direction. In other words, it might help to mould our values. It might easily help to change the ways in which people communicate online, for fear that the hate-speech bot might oust them from the platform in question. Some aspects of this might be good, some not so good.

The virtues of AI include its particular ability to share data to reach a universal view of things; its capacity to help exclude human bias; the speed and efficiency with which it operates. It can transcend human capacity in all these things. But these virtues must all be measured up against our other values. Without doing so, we might be entranced by the power of AI into allowing it to take the lead in determining how we think about some of our most important values and activities.

Using machine learning, an AI that's been trained with thousands of images can develop the capacity to recognise a photograph of a cat (an important achievement, given the predominance of pictures of cats on the internet). But humans do this very differently. A small child can often recognise a cat after just one example.

paragraphs.cn: 由于 AI 的「思维」方式可能与人类不同，再加上人们普遍容易被其魅力所裹挟，它的使用很可能会改变我们处理任务和做出决策的方式。围绕 AI 的那种诱人光环，实际上正是它的危险之一。业内人士几乎对每一篇关于 AI 的报道都在夸大其能力感到绝望，即使是那些关于 AI 平淡用途的文章，配图也是杀人机器人。
paragraphs.en: Because AI might 'think' differently to how humans think, and because of the general tendency to get swept up in its allure, its use could well change how we approach tasks and make decisions. The seductive allure that tends to surround AI in fact represents one of its dangers. Those working in the field despair that almost every article about AI hypes its powers, and even those about banal uses of AI are illustrated with killer robots.

paragraphs.cn: 技术对价值观的塑造影响是公认的。在最近一次关于 AI 伦理的圆桌讨论中，我所在的小组把大部分时间花在讨论洗衣机这个经典案例上——洗衣机并不仅仅是「接管」了洗衣工作，它对人们关于清洁和家务的态度，以及服装制造业，都产生了深远的影响。由于 AI 被设计出来的目的不仅仅是处理洗衣这样的具体事务，还要参与我们在无数不确定任务中的思考和决策过程，我们需要认真考虑它可能如何改变我们自身的思想和行为。
paragraphs.en: The impact of technology on shaping our values is well-established. At a recent roundtable discussion on the ethics of AI, the group I was in spent most of our time discussing the well-known example of the washing machine, which did not simply 'take over' the laundry, but which has had a major impact on attitudes to cleanliness and housework, and on the manufacture of clothing. Because AI is designed to contribute not merely to the laundry, but to how we think and make decisions over an indeterminate number of tasks, we need to consider seriously how it might change our own thought and behaviour.

paragraphs.cn: 需要记住的是，AI 可以采取多种形式，并以多种不同方式应用，因此上述一切并不是要论证使用 AI 是「好」还是「坏」。在某些情况下，AI 可能会促使我们改进方法。但在其他情况下，它可能会削弱或退化我们处理重要问题的方式。它甚至可能扭曲我们对价值观的思考。
paragraphs.en: It's important to remember that AI can take many forms, and be applied in many different ways, so none of this is to argue that using AI will be 'good' or 'bad'. In some cases, AI might nudge us to improve our approach. But in others, it could reduce or atrophy our approach to important issues. It might even skew how we think about values.

paragraphs.cn: 我们可以非常迅速地习惯技术。变化盲视和对技术的快速适应意味着我们可能并不完全意识到这种文化和价值观的转变。例如，随着通信方式以及数据共享和处理方式的巨大技术变革，人们对隐私的态度发生了显著变化。推动 AI 进步的因素之一恰恰是如今可获取的海量数据，其中很大一部分是关于我们的——在我们的日常生活中被收集。许多人对控制我们数据的组织极其警惕，但同时又继续发布大量非常私人的信息，而这些信息在几年前还会被视为私密。研究表明，人们对数据隐私的关注在不同情境之间并不一致。这并不是说技术「单独」造成了这一切，因为总有其他社会变化在同时起作用。
paragraphs.en: We can get used to technology very swiftly. Change-blindness and fast adaptation to technology can mean we're not fully aware of such cultural and value shifts. For example, attitudes to privacy have changed considerably along with the vast technological shifts in how we communicate and how data is shared and processed. One of the very things driving progress in AI is indeed the vast amounts of data now available, much of it about us, collected as we go about our daily lives. Many people are extremely wary of the organisations that have control of our data, while nonetheless continuing to post large amounts of very personal information that even a few years ago would have been considered private. Research shows that people's concerns about data privacy are inconsistent from one situation to the next. This is not to say that technology 'alone' has done this, since there are always other social changes operating at the same time.

paragraphs.cn: 也许我们对某些技术的影响特别盲目，因为它在很大程度上塑造了我们看待世界的方式。AI 的挑战在于它可能以我们并不完全意识到的方式运作。它帮助塑造了我们彼此交流的方式、我们思考的方式、我们发现世界的方式。这并非全新现象：书写技术、印刷术和电话已经改变了我们感知世界和与世界互动的方式，甚至改变了我们的大脑。但 AI 可能更加强大。嵌入在我们获取大量信息的技术中的算法，可能正在塑造我们接收什么信息、如何接收信息，甚至如何对其做出反应。而 AI 可能在塑造我们的行为——这并非其使用的意外后果，而是有意为之。技术——往往在 AI 的辅助下——正在利用人类心理学来塑造我们的行为。手机和社交媒体平台的设计借鉴了心理学研究——关于如何让用户对其使用产生成瘾性反应的研究。
paragraphs.en: And perhaps we are especially blind to the effects of some technology because it does so much to shape how we see the world. The challenge of AI is that it might operate in ways we aren't fully aware of. It helps to mould how we communicate with each other, how we think, how we find the world. This is not completely new: writing technology, the printing press and the telephone have already altered how we perceive and interact with our world, and even changed our brains. But AI might be even more powerful. Algorithms embedded into the technology through which we access so much information could be shaping what information we receive, how we receive it, even how we react to it. And AI might be shaping our behaviour, not as an unintended consequence of its use, but by design. Technology, often aided by AI, is exploiting human psychology to shape how we behave. Phones and social media platforms are designed by drawing upon psychological research about how to produce addictive responses to their use.

paragraphs.cn: 那么，让我们探讨几个使用或可能使用 AI 的例子，重点关注机器和人类如何使用和分析数据。
paragraphs.en: So let's explore a few examples of the use or potential use of AI, focusing on how machines and humans use and analyse data.

paragraphs.cn: 首先，我们要明确，使用 AI 代替人类做决策可能有很大的优势。AI 执行的快速信息共享和稳健的数据分析是非常有益的。例如，牛津移动机器人组的信息工程师保罗·纽曼（Paul Newman）指出，从人类驾驶的车辆事故中学习是一个缓慢而复杂的过程。其他人类无法从每一个具体案例中直接学习，即使是当事人本身也可能学到的很少甚至什么也没学到。但是，每当一辆自动驾驶汽车发生事故时，所有数据都可以立即在所有其他自动驾驶车辆之间共享，用于降低未来事故发生的概率。
paragraphs.en: First, let's be clear that there can be great advantages in using AI over human decision making. The fast sharing and robust data-analysis that AI performs can be extremely advantageous. For example, the information engineer Paul Newman of the Oxford Mobile Robotics Group points out that learning from accidents in vehicles driven by humans is a slow and complex process. Other humans can't learn directly from each individual case, and even the human involved might learn little or nothing. But whenever an autonomous car has an accident, all the data can immediately be shared among all other autonomous vehicles, and used to reduce the chances of a future accident.

paragraphs.cn: AI 的这一特性——像蜂群思维一样共享信息，以及快速、严格地分析数据的能力——可能构成我们解决问题方式的真正改进。汇聚数据共享是 AI 极其擅长的事情。快速分析数据是另一个强项。这就是用数千张猫的图片训练 AI 的原理。事实上，正是对海量数据池的获取能力，加上以极快速度分析这些数据的能力，正在推动当前 AI 的蓬勃发展。
paragraphs.en: This aspect of AI – the ability to share information like a hive mind and to analyse data rapidly and rigorously – might then constitute a real improvement in how we solve problems. Sharing pooled data is something AI is extremely good at. Analysing data quickly is another. That's how training AI on thousands of pictures of cats works. In fact, it's access to vast pools of data, together with the ability to analyse this data at speed, that's helping to drive the current boom in AI.

paragraphs.cn: 虽然自动驾驶车辆也会犯错，但这个例子展示了 AI 能够克服的人类缺陷。人类在获取和分析做出良好决策并据此行动所需的数据方面，存在各种各样的失败方式。一辆自动驾驶车辆永远不会因为羞耻而不愿承认错误，永远不会因为虚荣而拒绝佩戴驾驶眼镜，永远不会在疲劳时坚持驾驶，永远不会拒绝参加高级驾驶课程。克服偏见、偏颇和非理性是改善人类决策的一种方式——尤其是在涉及价值观的问题上。其中一些偏见和非理性涉及对相关信息的拒绝或未能处理。因此，这种利用 AI 来汇聚数据的模型，似乎是我们应用于决策的一种优势。
paragraphs.en: Although autonomous vehicles can also make errors, this example demonstrates the human faults that AI can overcome. There are all sorts of ways in which humans fail to take in or analyse the data needed to make good decisions and to act on them. An autonomous vehicle will never be ashamed to admit fault, never be too vain to wear driving glasses, never insist on driving when tired, never refuse to go on an advanced driver course. Overcoming bias, partiality and irrationality is one way of improving human decision making – especially where issues of value are concerned. Some of these biases and irrationalities involve the rejection of, or failure to process, relevant information. So this model of using AI to pool data seems to be an advantage we can apply to decision making.

paragraphs.cn: 但这样的结论可能过于草率。并非我们所有的问题都能通过纯粹的数据驱动方法来解决。避免汽车事故是好事，这一点相当清楚。这是一个安全问题，我们主要是在应用技术修复方案，而且成功与否很容易衡量。车辆要么撞了要么没撞，死亡和受伤人数可以确定。未遂事故也不难统计。但对于不那么纯粹技术性的问题，数据驱动的「蜂群思维」方法是否总是好的，就不那么清楚了。
paragraphs.en: But such a conclusion might be hasty. Not all our problems can be solved by a purely data-led approach. It is pretty clear that avoiding car accidents is good. It's a safety issue where what we're doing is mostly applying technological fixes, and it's pretty easy to measure success. The vehicle either crashes or it doesn't, and deaths and injuries can be determined. It's also pretty easy to measure near-misses. But for problems that are less purely technical, it's not so clear that a data-driven, 'hive mind' approach is always good.

paragraphs.cn: 以医学为例——这是 AI 最有前景的应用领域之一。医学既是一门科学，也是一门艺术：它将科学和技术与价值观的追求结合在一起——健康的价值、良好医患关系的价值、以患者为中心的护理的价值、患者自主权的价值，等等。在医学中，我们不仅仅是在寻找一个技术修复方案。
paragraphs.en: Take medicine, for example, one of the most promising areas of AI. Medicine is both a science, and an art: it combines science and technology with the pursuit of values: the value of health, the value of good patient relations, the value of person-centred care, the value of patient autonomy, and others. In medicine, we are not just looking for a technological fix.

paragraphs.cn: AI 在诊断中的应用前景非常广阔，例如在辅助解读医学图像方面，通过筛选海量数据来实现。证据表明，AI 能够检测到人眼注意不到的图像间的细微差异。但它也可能犯人类绝不会犯的低级错误。因此，目前将 AI 与人类技能结合似乎是改善诊断的最佳选择。到目前为止，这是非常好的消息。
paragraphs.en: The use of AI in diagnosis is very promising, for example, in assisting with the interpretation of medical images by trawling through vast amounts of data. The evidence seems to be that AI can detect minute differences between images that the human eye doesn't notice. But it can also make blatant errors that a human would never make. So, currently, combining AI with human skills seems the best option for improving diagnosis. So far, this is excellent news.

paragraphs.cn: 但是，2018 年《新英格兰医学杂志》上由加州斯坦福大学医学院的丹顿·夏尔（Danton Char）、尼甘·沙阿（Nigam Shah）和大卫·马格努斯（David Magnus）发表的一篇文章，对使用 AI 进行诊断和治疗决策提出了严肃的质疑。从医学作为一门科学的角度来想。如果 AI 成为「集体医学思维的存储库」，我们在以某种方式使用它之前就必须极其谨慎，因为那种方式可能会导致专业思维的趋同，从而可能排除独立思考和个人的临床经验。目前，人们承认在诊断和治疗方面可能存在不同的医学观点。如果我们能完全确信 AI 只是在提高准确性，那么医学思维更大的趋同性就是好事。但存在一种危险，即 AI 可能过早地切断某些选择，或将我们引向特定的治疗路径。此外，作者警告说，这种机器学习甚至可能被用来将治疗推向达成指标或为既得利益者创造利润，而非为患者提供最佳方案。数据可能主导医学，而非反过来。
paragraphs.en: But a piece in The New England Journal of Medicine in 2018 by Danton Char, Nigam Shah and David Magnus of the Stanford University School of Medicine in California raises serious questions about using AI in diagnosis and treatment decisions. Think about medicine as a science. If AI forms the 'repository for the collective medical mind', we'd have to be extremely careful before using it in a way that moves towards uniformity of professional thinking, which might foreclose independent thought and individual clinical experience. At the moment, it's recognised that there might be different bodies of medical opinion about diagnosis and treatment. If we could be utterly confident that AI was only improving accuracy, then greater uniformity of medical thinking would be good. But there's a danger that AI might prematurely shut off options or lead us down particular treatment routes. Moreover, the authors warn that such machine learning might even be used to nudge treatment towards hitting targets or achieving profits for vested interests, rather than what's best for patients. The data might drive the medicine, rather than the other way around.

paragraphs.cn: 从医学作为一门艺术的角度来想。它涉及将患者视为过着各自生活的真实个体。虽然 AI 可能帮助我们更好地实现健康目标，但综合考虑所有因素，成功率较低的治疗方案对某些患者可能是更好的选择。纯粹数据驱动的方法无法告诉我们这一点。而且我们需要警惕不被技术的力量冲昏头脑。因为我们已经知道，自由和知情同意在实践中极难实现，而医疗体制会影响患者的同意。但在技术的额外权威和全面的专业共识的加持下，将医疗行业现有的权力与 AI 的附加权力结合起来的危险在于——「电脑说该吃药」可能会成为现实。
paragraphs.en: Think about medicine as an art. It involves relating to patients as real individuals living their own lives. Although AI might help us better achieve the goal of health, treatments with a lower chance of success might be the better option for some patients, all things considered. A data-driven approach alone cannot tell us this. And we need to be cautious we're not carried away by the power of technology. For we already know that free and informed consent is extremely hard to achieve in practice, and that the medical establishment influences patients' consent. But with the added gravitas of technology, and of blanket professional agreement, the danger is that wedding the existing power of the medical profession to the added power of AI, 'Computer says take the drugs' might become a reality.

paragraphs.cn: 医患关系是医学的核心，也是我们理解医学伦理的核心。但 AI 的使用可能微妙地，甚至从根本上改变这一点。究竟如何实现使用 AI 改善患者护理这一道德上值得称赞的目标，需要仔细考量。
paragraphs.en: The relationship between physician and patient is at the heart of medicine, and of our understanding of medical ethics. But the use of AI could subtly, even radically, alter this. Precisely how we implement the morally laudable aim of using AI to improve patient care needs careful consideration.

paragraphs.cn: AI 操纵和处理海量数据的能力可能会推动我们过度重视或唯一重视数据驱动的方法来识别和解决问题。这可能导致思维的趋同，即使在有理由追求思想和方法多样性的情况下也是如此。它还可能使其他因素黯然失色，并在此过程中不仅扭曲我们的思维，还扭曲我们的价值观。
paragraphs.en: AI's ability to manipulate and process vast amounts of data might push us into giving undue or sole prominence to data-driven approaches to identifying and solving problems. This might lead to uniformity of thinking, even in cases where there are reasons to aspire to variety of thought and approach. It might also eclipse other factors and, in doing so, distort not just our thinking, but our values.

paragraphs.cn: 一个决策是如何做出的，由谁做出的；一个行动是如何执行的，由谁执行的——在许多情况下这些都是关键问题。在涉及价值观的问题上尤其如此。那位怀疑男孩是否真的自己做饼干的家长是有道理的。也许如果他先设计并制造了那个机器人，他的说法会更有说服力。这些因素的重要性因具体情况而异，用机器智能替代或补充人类智能的潜在意义也是如此。
paragraphs.en: How a decision is made, and by whom; how an action is performed, and by whom – these are critical issues in many circumstances. It's especially the case where values are concerned. The parent who was skeptical that the boy had really made the cookies himself has a point. Perhaps if he'd first designed and built the robot, his claim would have had more validity. The significance of these factors will vary from case to case, as will the potential significance of replacing or supplementing human intelligence with machine intelligence.

paragraphs.cn: 以陪审团制度为例。我们都知道陪审团有缺陷：他们有时会得出错误的结论。算法已经在帮助美国法院就量刑和假释做出某些决定，利用再犯率等数据，这引发了相当大的争议。人们担心这可能有助于固化对某些群体的既有偏见。但想象一下，我们已经达到了这样的阶段：将所有可用证据输入计算机后得出的裁决比陪审团达成的更准确。在这种情况下，计算机能够以极快的速度汇聚和分析所有数据，并且（在这个假想的例子中）准确高效。对比一下现实中陪审团的运作方式——不同的人可能对案件做了不同的笔记，回忆起不同的内容，即使经过数小时的审议，仍然对证据持有不同看法。AI 收集和分析数据的能力可能大大弥补这些不足。
paragraphs.en: Take the use of juries. We all know that juries are flawed: they sometimes get the wrong answer. Algorithms are already helping US courts come to some decisions regarding sentencing and parole, drawing on data such as information about recidivism rates, to considerable controversy. There are fears that this can help entrench existing biases against certain groups. But imagine that we have reached the point at which feeding all the available evidence into a computer has led to more accurate verdicts than those reached by juries. In such a case, the computer would be able to pool and analyse all data with speed and (in this imagined example) accuracy and efficiency. Compare how actual juries work, where individuals might have made differing notes about the case, recall different things and, even after hours of deliberations, still have different views of the evidence. The power of AI to gather and analyse data might go a long way to address these shortcomings.

paragraphs.cn: 但这个例子清楚地表明，我们关心的不仅仅是把事情做对。即使使用机器能得到更准确的答案，我们仍然可能有理由重视人类担任陪审团所带来的独特贡献。想一想法律改革和个人权利是如何经过斗争争取而来的，以及「由同等地位的同类人组成的陪审团」这一概念中所体现的普通人的价值。也许我们想把这一切交给 AI——但也许不想。
paragraphs.en: But this example readily demonstrates that we care about more than simply getting things right. Even if, by using a machine, we get a more accurate answer, there can still be some reason to value the distinctive contribution of having humans serving on juries. Consider the history of how legal reforms and individual rights have been fought for, and the value of the common person that's enshrined in the notion of being tried by 'a jury of one's peers'. Perhaps we want to hand that over to an AI – but perhaps not.

paragraphs.cn: 人类可能表现出的偏见、容易被情绪左右的倾向，当然是在做出裁决时的潜在弱点。但它也是法律变革的推动力。存在「陪审团否决」的案例——在那些令人头疼的、关于不公正的人类情感的驱使下，陪审团拒绝定罪，即使被告在法律条文上明显有罪。无论一台机器在评估证据方面多么出色，我们距离开发出具有敏锐正义感、关注弱者、并且有道德勇气反抗法律体系机器的机器还差得远。
paragraphs.en: The bias that humans can display, the tendency to be swayed by emotion, is of course a potential weakness in reaching a verdict. But it has also been the impetus for changes in the law. There are instances of 'jury nullification' where, swayed by those pesky human feelings of injustice, juries have simply failed to convict, even though the defendant is clearly guilty in terms of a strict application of the law. No matter how good at assessing evidence a machine might be, we're a long way off developing machines with a finely tuned sense of justice, an eye for the underdog, and the moral backbone to defy the apparatus of the legal system.

paragraphs.cn: 但更广泛的观点仍然是：陪审团作为独立判断来源的角色，是对抗最有权势者的既得利益的制衡。正如德夫林勋爵（Lord Devlin）2004 年在上议院所说：「陪审团审判不仅是正义的工具，也不仅是宪法的一个齿轮：它是显示自由尚存的明灯。」还需要注意的是：AI 在自动驾驶车辆避免事故方面的优势——汇聚信息、融合洞察——在法律的语境下恰恰破坏了陪审团独立性的基本道德原则。这种独立性是对抗始终存在的强大既得利益集团可能性的制衡，也为我们提供了一个理由来保留陪审团审判制度，同时关注的不仅仅是法庭上呈现的信息的处理。
paragraphs.en: But the more general idea remains that juries perform the role of an independent source of judgment as a counter to the vested interests of the most powerful. As Lord Devlin said in the House of Lords in 2004: '[T]rial by jury is more than an instrument of justice and more than one wheel of the constitution: it is the lamp that shows that freedom lives.' And note this: the very feature of AI that is a strength in avoiding accidents for autonomous vehicles – the pooling of information, the melding of insights – in the context of the law directly undermines the basic moral principle of independence of juries. This independence is a counter to the ever-present possibility of powerful vested interests and gives a reason to keep trial by jury while being concerned with more than the mere processing of information presented in court.

paragraphs.cn: 批评者可能会说，我们需要这种独立性仅仅是因为人类如此不可靠：不能仅仅把司法交给法律行业，但一个准确的 AI 就能解决这个问题，而且也许随着时间的推移，我们会习惯这个想法，把我们的司法系统交给机器。
paragraphs.en: A critic might say that we need this independence only because humans are so unreliable: the legal profession alone can't be left in charge of justice, but an accurate AI would solve the problem and maybe, with the passage of time, we'd get used to the idea, and hand over our justice system to the machines.

paragraphs.cn: 但认为我们能够永远逃脱权力失衡和既得利益——这正是拥有陪审团制度的原因——的想法完全是乌托邦式的幻想。解决司法误判问题有其他替代方案，而不是把司法交给机器，比如一个快速、便捷的申诉系统。也许在未来，AI 可以辅助法官和陪审团做出决定——但这与设想 AI 可能取代人类进行法律决策完全不同。即便如此，我们也需要仔细考虑 AI 的影响，以及它是否正在推动我们走向一种更加技术官僚化的方式。法律作为一个人类政治和社会系统，是经过许多斗争才发展起来的。但在法律中使用 AI 可能会随着时间推移帮助改变这一点。我们需要在充分意识到对正义和民主诸多影响的情况下仔细考虑这个问题。
paragraphs.en: But it's utterly utopian to think that we'll ever escape the power imbalances and vested interests that are the reason for having juries. There are alternatives to the miscarriage of justice problem than handing over justice to the machines, such as a fast, accessible appeals system. Perhaps, in the future, AI might assist judges and juries to come to decisions – but this is rather different to envisaging that AI might replace humans in legal decision making. Even here, we'd need to think carefully about the impact of AI, and whether it was nudging us towards a more technocratic approach. The law developed as a human political and social system through much struggle. But the use of AI within the law could, over time, help to change this. We need to consider this carefully, in full awareness of the many implications for justice and democracy.

paragraphs.cn: 使用 AI 的一个巨大吸引力仅仅在于它分析数据的惊人速度。效率是一种美德，但这种美德取决于它被用于什么目的。它也绝不是唯一的美德。如果一台机器能快速高效地完成某件事，我们可能受到的诱惑超出了实际合理的程度。而且它完成任务的速度可能会让我们忽视它在达成目的过程中存在的问题。我们最终可能对这种高效生成的结果赋予过高的价值。
paragraphs.en: One great attraction of using AI is simply the sheer speed at which it can analyse data. Efficiency is a virtue, but this virtue depends upon the ends to which it is being used. It's also by no means the only virtue. If a machine can accomplish something quickly and efficiently, we might be more tempted to use it than is really merited. And the speed with which it accomplishes tasks might make us overlook problems in how it achieves its ends. We might then end up placing too great a value on such efficiently generated results.

paragraphs.cn: 反诽谤联盟（Anti-Defamation League，简称 ADL）与加州大学伯克利分校的 D-Lab 合作，正在开发一种使用机器学习的在线仇恨指数（Online Hate Index，简称 OHI），试图检测网上的仇恨言论。这是一个有趣的例子：它是一种「以技术对付技术」的方案——网上所谓「仇恨言论」的泛滥（表面上看）是计算机技术的产物。然而，向对手恶言相向绝非新鲜事。远在万维网在蒂姆·伯纳斯-李（Tim Berners-Lee）眼中还只是一丝微光之前，17 世纪的法国哲学家笛卡尔（René Descartes）就将竞争对手数学家费马（Pierre de Fermat）的作品称为「狗屎」。侮辱的悠久血统值得注意，因为围绕 AI 的炒作往往鼓励我们将问题视为全新的，或认为其具有独特的危险性。我们可能被引向过度依赖 AI 所拥有的那类狭窄能力范围的一种方式，恰恰是以下两个假设的结合：「技术原因 = 技术解决方案」，以及当今技术尤其充满了新颖的道德危险这一观念。
paragraphs.en: The Anti-Defamation League (ADL) in conjunction with D-Lab at the University of California, Berkeley, is developing an Online Hate Index (OHI) using machine learning in an attempt to detect hate speech online. This is an interesting example: it's a 'tech on tech' solution – the alleged proliferation of 'hate speech' online is (seemingly) a product of computerised technology. Yet hurling abuse at opponents is hardly new. Long before the World Wide Web was even a twinkle in the eye of Tim Berners-Lee, the 17th-century French philosopher René Descartes described the work of rival mathematician Pierre de Fermat as 'shit'. The long pedigree of insults is worth noting, given the way that hype around AI encourages us to think of issues as new, or uniquely dangerous. One way in which we can be steered in the direction of over-reliance on the narrow range of capacities that AI has is precisely by the combined assumptions that 'tech cause = tech solution', together with the idea that today's tech is especially full of novel moral perils.

paragraphs.cn: 「仇恨言论」这一概念本身就有争议。一些人认为，试图消除语言的某些用法——无论是通过法律还是通过管理在线平台的机构——对于实现消除歧视等目标是必要的。另一些人则担心这对言论自由构成威胁，代表了一种审查形式。人们担忧的是，对一个人来说是仇恨言论的内容，对另一个人来说可能只是玩笑，而且在脱离语境的情况下极难将某事物归类为「仇恨言论」。此外，鉴于网上发布的海量内容，任何对「仇恨言论」的监管都将是零散的，而且人们担心某些群体或个人可能被不成比例地针对。
paragraphs.en: The concept of 'hate speech' is itself controversial. Some consider that attempting to eliminate certain uses of language, whether by law or by those managing online platforms, is necessary to achieve goals such as the elimination of discrimination. Others worry that this is a danger to free speech, and represents a form of censorship. There are concerns that what counts as hate speech to one person is merely banter to another, and that it's extremely hard to classify something as 'hate speech' out of context. Additionally, there are concerns that, with the vast amount of material posted online, any policing of 'hate speech' will be patchy, and there are fears that some groups or individuals might be disproportionately targeted.

paragraphs.cn: 如果我们能自动化检测网上的仇恨言论，可能有助于分类和提高一致性。OHI 可以通过比人类更快地处理数据、正确执行政策且不带偏见来解决这些问题。（当然，这取决于它是如何被编程的。如果它被编程为有偏见的，那它将以极高的效率持有偏见。）
paragraphs.en: If we could automate the detection of hate speech online, it might help with classification and consistency. The OHI could address these issues by processing data faster than a human, and applying the policy correctly, without bias. (Of course, this depends on how it's programmed. If it's programmed to be biased, it will be biased with great efficiency.)

paragraphs.cn: 所以问题就在这里。在为 AI 能够以令人类望尘莫及的速度和一致性检测、分类和消除「仇恨言论」的想法所鼓舞，加上担心网络世界正在把我们中太多人变成不负责任的、充满仇恨的网络喷子的情况下，我们可能会迫不及待地使用这项技术，以至于仇恨言论的其他问题在某种程度上被忽视了。这可能有助于推动一场大致可以概括为「仇恨言论对抗言论自由」的辩论朝某一特定方向发展。换言之，它可能有助于塑造我们的价值观。它可能轻易地改变人们在网上交流的方式——因为害怕仇恨言论机器人会将其从相关平台上驱逐。其中某些方面可能是好的，某些则不那么好。
paragraphs.en: So here is the problem. Enthused with the idea that an AI can detect, categorise and eliminate 'hate speech' with a speed and consistency that leaves humans standing, coupled with fears that the online world is turning so many of us into irresponsible hate-filled trolls, we could use this technology with such alacrity that the other problems of hate speech get somewhat overlooked. This then could help to drive the debate that could be roughly summarised as 'hate speech versus free speech' in one particular direction. In other words, it might help to mould our values. It might easily help to change the ways in which people communicate online, for fear that the hate-speech bot might oust them from the platform in question. Some aspects of this might be good, some not so good.

paragraphs.cn: AI 的优点包括其分享数据以达成普遍看法的独特能力；它帮助排除人类偏见的能力；以及它运作的速度和效率。在所有这些方面，它都能超越人类的能力。但这些优点都必须与我们的其他价值观加以衡量。如果不这样做，我们可能会被 AI 的力量所迷惑，任由它在决定我们如何看待一些最重要的价值观和活动方面占据主导地位。
paragraphs.en: The virtues of AI include its particular ability to share data to reach a universal view of things; its capacity to help exclude human bias; the speed and efficiency with which it operates. It can transcend human capacity in all these things. But these virtues must all be measured up against our other values. Without doing so, we might be entranced by the power of AI into allowing it to take the lead in determining how we think about some of our most important values and activities.

articles.title: 我们应该干预进化吗？「编辑」自然的伦理问题
articles.author: Aeon
articles.summary: 1939 年 8 月底，德国考古学家奥托·弗尔青（Otto Völzing）在德国南部一个洞穴的深处发现了大约 200 块雕刻过的猛犸象牙碎片。距离战争爆发仅剩一周，弗尔青的发现被匆忙收入一个箱子，在博物馆档案室里静静躺了几十年无人问津。直到 20 世纪 60 年代这些碎片被编目时，这堆破碎的残片中
articles.content_cn:
1939 年 8 月底，德国考古学家奥托·弗尔青（Otto Völzing）在德国南部一个洞穴的深处发现了大约 200 块雕刻过的猛犸象牙碎片。距离战争爆发仅剩一周，弗尔青的发现被匆忙收入一个箱子，在博物馆档案室里静静躺了几十年无人问津。直到 20 世纪 60 年代这些碎片被编目时，这堆破碎的残片中才浮现出一件令人惊叹的物品。它们组成了一尊不完整的雕像，具有一种混合特征：人的身体，洞穴狮的头和前臂。20 世纪 70 年代的后续发掘又找到了更多碎片——这就是后来被称为霍伦施泰因-施塔德的狮人（Lion-Man of Hohlenstein-Stadel）的文物。它约在 40,000 年前用一根猛犸象牙雕刻而成，是人类想象自然界不存在之物的能力的最早例证之一。

自狮人以来的每一个人类历史时代，都试图超越自然去思考。在约公元前 700 年赫西俄德（Hesiod）所作的《神谱》中，喀迈拉是一种复合生物，拥有狮子的头、龙的身体和蛇头形状的尾巴（为了更加完整，背上还多出一个山羊头）。在 W·B·叶芝（W B Yeats）1920 年的诗作《第二次降临》中，一头类似的「猛兽」是毁灭的先兆。

在我们自己的时代，混合体变成了另一种样子。生物圈各个角落的生物都因气候变化、污染和非本地物种的扩散而被迫改造身体和行为，以适应一个被人类塑造的星球。它们可能没有像狮人那样可见的融合形态，但它们确实带有另一个物种的印记：我们。

人类成为地球上最强大的进化力量并非我们的初衷；然而，我们确实是这一事实迫使我们面对一个紧迫而艰难的问题。一些动物、植物和昆虫能够适应，但对许多物种来说，变化的速度太快了。我们是否应该通过刻意干预它们的进化来试图拯救它们？

像 CRISPR-Cas9 这样的精准基因编辑技术的出现，使一个混合物种的世界成为可能——这种技术如同一把精细到可以替换 DNA 中单个字母的分子手术刀。对一些人来说，将已灭绝的巨兽如恐狼和猛犸象的 DNA 拼接到灰狼或亚洲象体内，是复活一个久远失落世界的机会。但借助合成生物学，我们有可能拯救当下的世界——干预脆弱物种的进化，使它们能够在不断变化的气候和崩溃的生态系统中存活下来。植物可以被编辑以应对干旱，或改善农作物的光合作用。微生物可以被编程来感知污染并消耗毒素，甚至是那些塞满海鸟消化道的海洋塑料。通过辅助进化，我们或许能使珊瑚礁系统免于崩溃。

转基因救援的技术挑战是艰巨的。每一种生物的特征都是其基因和环境的组合。但我们很难精确知道哪种基因组合产生了特定的特征组合；仅仅编辑基因组也不能改变这样一个事实——那些对塑造它们至关重要的复杂生态关系可能也在不断变化之中。伦理问题或许更加巨大。主导其他物种的进化看起来很像是在扮演上帝。在一个跨国公司比生物系统拥有更强法律人格权利的时代，在肉鸡等商品化物种的基因组已被申请专利的时代，谁来决定改变哪些动物以及如何改变的问题不容忽视。对一些人来说，我们能为自然做的最好的事情就是不去干预它。

但以为此时此刻我们这个物种还能简单地抽身而退，不过是一种错觉。「自然」以一种纯粹状态存在的观念本身就值得怀疑，而即便曾经如此，那个时代也早已远去。「我们」存在于每一分子人为添加到大气或海洋中的碳中——即使我们立即停止燃烧化石燃料，这些碳仍将继续塑造生物圈。据世界自然保护联盟（IUCN）红色名录统计，近 50,000 个物种面临灭绝风险。不干预可能意味着接受一种坦率地说令人无法容忍的规模的损失。

四十亿年的进化证明，转化是自然的天赋。但人类影响的规模和速度表明，即使是天赋也可能需要一些帮助。如果是这样，我们不应仅仅将其视为技术的变革，而应将其视为一次心态转变的契机。数千年来，我们将大部分进化发展委托给了我们的文化和技术，作为次级遗传系统——通过社会学习以及我们的基因，在时间中传递信息和技能。每一件新工具，从石刀到互联网，都改变了握持它的那只手。那么问题是，如果我们必须编辑其他物种，我们能以合乎伦理和智慧的方式来做到吗？而这又应如何改变我们自己？

珊瑚也许是自然混合体的最佳范例。从外表看，它们似乎横跨了植物与矿物的边界；从生物学上看，它们是动物与微生物之间古老的联盟。珊瑚虫——一种微小的软体生物，其碳酸钙分泌物建造了广大的礁石都市——依赖微小的虫黄藻提供养分和能量，以及那些将珊瑚礁染成迷幻色彩的光合色素。

珊瑚表明，一种动物不仅仅是它的 DNA；任何生物都是与其他物种的联系矩阵（去灭绝的批评者经常指出这一点：如果脱离了支撑它的生命关系网络，一头复活的猛犸象真的还是猛犸象吗？）。如果生态学教会了我们什么，那就是：存在即协作。但关系可能是脆弱的。珊瑚的联盟容易受到温度变化的影响，随着我们破碎的气候将热量倾入海洋，这种联盟正在被稳步地拆解。被热应激困扰的珊瑚虫吐出它们的虫黄藻后将白化并饥饿。连续的热浪已使热带珊瑚礁承受了不堪忍受的压力。始于 2023 年 1 月的当前全球白化事件，已使世界上超过 80% 的珊瑚礁暴露在致命温度之下。而珊瑚也是一个密集居住环境的基础——超过 4,000 种鱼类以及无数无脊椎动物、鲨鱼，甚至座头鲸，都在热带礁石上生活或觅食。如果我们拯救了珊瑚，我们也将拯救一个支撑着海洋中约四分之一生命的生态系统；但过去五年中大堡礁已经经历了三次大规模白化事件，时间可能所剩无几。

2015 年，生态遗传学家玛德琳·范奥彭（Madeleine van Oppen）、海洋生物学家露丝·盖茨（Ruth Gates）及其同事设计了一套帮助珊瑚跟上升温步伐的技术。他们称之为「辅助进化」的方法包括「硬化」（将耐热性状选择性培育到珊瑚中）、辅助基因流动（将耐热珊瑚移植到挣扎中的珊瑚礁）以及基因编辑。他们的想法是介入珊瑚虫与虫黄藻之间的裂缝，维持它们的联盟，直到我们能够降低排放、为海洋降温。

范奥彭务实而直率。在我为撰写《自然的天赋》（Nature's Genius, 2025）一书而进行研究和写作时，她向我解释了她的动机。「我不想控制自然，」她说，她的荷兰口音几乎未因多年在澳大利亚的生活和工作而有所改变。「我只是想帮它跨过那道坎。」

即使我们希望，完全的控制也可能无法实现。辅助珊瑚进化尚不是一门精确的科学。耐热性的精确基因图谱尚未绘制完成，我们不知道哪些编辑可能带来不愉快的权衡（例如，耐热珊瑚可能处理养分的能力较弱）。意外后果的风险应当成为谨慎行事的理由。话虽如此，目前大多数辅助进化的努力看起来很像一种更古老、更保守的辅助进化形式：驯化。正如早期农民通过选择具有最理想特征的个体来繁殖以培育作物和牲畜一样，大多数辅助进化涉及为珊瑚自身创造条件，使其分享可能帮助珊瑚礁存活的基因资源。

一些最有前景的项目涉及与在这些生态系统旁生活了数千年的人们的合作。伊尔甘吉人已在道乌鲁（Dawul Wuru）——昆士兰北部约 500 平方公里的海岸线——居住了数千年。库尔-布尔（Kul-Bul），即「海洋之国」，从海岸线向海延伸数十公里，包括一些受热害最严重的珊瑚礁。2022 年，伊尔甘吉土地与海洋护林员管理了从邻近的贡甘吉海域将耐热珊瑚幼虫转移到道乌鲁的工作，将海洋资源利用的传统理解与范奥彭的辅助进化原理相结合。他们是众多与传统所有者群体合作的案例之一——西方科学与传统生态知识的联盟，共同帮助脆弱的珊瑚跨越温度升高的障碍。

「国」是伊尔甘吉文化的根基。它是「梦幻」的源泉——那是一种滋养澳大利亚原住民文化的故事与景观的活态宝库：就像喂养珊瑚虫的珊瑚甲藻一样，「梦幻」滋养着联系。对于伊尔甘吉土地与海洋护林员来说，干预进化意味着作为其他物种的伙伴而行动。辅助进化，归根结底，是关于结成联盟——与其他物种的联盟，以及与认识生物世界的不同方式的联盟。

辅助进化依赖于珊瑚礁科学家和传统所有者之间的合作。但如果有一种真正超凡的技术——一种实质上可以一挥手就重塑整个生态系统的技术呢？

凯文·埃斯维尔特（Kevin Esvelt）是一位生物学家，他已经证明这是可能的——如果我们选择这样做的话。2013 年的某一天，埃斯维尔特意识到他可以通过创建能从一代传递到下一代的 CRISPR 编辑来解决地方性的生态问题。基因驱动是基因组中其遗传潜力被增强的元素。通过利用系统中的这种偏向，埃斯维尔特意识到他可以构建一种合成基因驱动：一种 DNA 编辑机器，一旦加入基因组，就会在每一个后续世代中重复出现。

合成基因驱动的力量怎么高估都不过分。用于善途，它可以在珊瑚种群中传播耐热性，或对人为疾病的免疫力，或根除外来掠食者；用于恶途，它可以成为一种可怕的生物武器。基因驱动可以成为灭绝引擎，赋予操控者对整个物种的生杀大权。

埃斯维尔特无法忽视基因驱动的潜力，但同样无法忽视其风险。「第二天，我在冷汗中醒来，」他告诉我。他设计了一系列安全措施，通过将基因驱动的架构部分分散到基因组各处来限制其扩散，降低每一代中出现功能完整基因驱动的可能性。但仅靠技术修复并不能确保这种令人敬畏的技术被负责任地使用。

2014 年，埃斯维尔特合著了一篇论文，建议基因驱动可以控制奥特亚罗瓦/新西兰的入侵物种。8,500 万年来，那里的青蛙、蝙蝠、鸟类和蜥蜴在生物学隔离中生活。欧洲殖民者粗暴地终结了这一切——先是老鼠，然后是鼬鼠和白鼬，大肆吞噬毫无防御能力的当地动物。该国现在拥有地球上最糟糕的灭绝记录之一，其中很大程度上归因于外来物种的影响。一种名为「最后一窝」的定向基因驱动——编辑雄性使其无法产生可育雌性后代——可以在几代之内抑制鼬科动物的种群数量。

然而，正如他后来在 MIT 媒体实验室网站上的一篇帖子中承认的那样，埃斯维尔特在提出这个建议之前并未咨询毛利人。毛利保育主义者梅兰妮·马克-沙德博尔特（Melanie Mark-Shadbolt）指出，他在基因驱动问题上对毛利人共同治理的需要表现得「天真」，埃斯维尔特承认这「一针见血」。「我对当地生态系统的了解和对当地政治的了解一样少，」他说。「我无法评估可能的后果。」他总结道，是否使用基因驱动的决定应该包括将最受其影响的社区，并以指导他们与土地世代关系的原则为依据。埃斯维尔特从错误中吸取了教训，投入时间与不同的伊维（iwi，即部落）进行协商，听取他们对基因驱动的看法。在与毛利保育主义者交流之后，我更清楚地理解了为什么这件事如此重要——以及世界其他地方在权衡对自然的干预时可以从中学习什么。

毛利人的世界观建立在「毛陶兰加」（mātauranga）之上——一个与奥特亚罗瓦/新西兰生态系统相适配的精妙知识和价值体系。毛利保育主义者塔姆·马尔科姆（Tame Malcolm）带着温暖的微笑和热情的举止向我解释了毛陶兰加如何产生两个原则，它们是毛利式保育方法的基石。第一个，他说，是「瓦卡瓦纳翁加坦加」（whakawhanaungatanga）。与许多毛利概念一样，它没有直接对应的英语翻译，但马尔科姆的定义简单得令人释然：「万物皆有亲缘。」瓦卡瓦纳翁加坦加是一种根深蒂固的建立关系的过程——在人与人、物种与景观之间。

第二个概念是「瓦卡帕帕」（whakapapa）。同样，英语中缺乏对应的概念。对马尔科姆来说，它意味着谱系。瓦卡帕帕描述了一条家族血脉，延伸回创世之初，但同时也包括个体所生活的河流和山脉。但另一位毛利保育主义者马库斯-隆戈维提奥·沙德博尔特（Marcus-Rongowhitiao Shadbolt）向我提出了另一种翻译。与其说是谱系，沙德博尔特认为瓦卡帕帕更像是一种分类学。「它是一种整理自然世界的方式，」他说。但不同于西方动植物学所依据的林奈分类法的生理共性，瓦卡帕帕根据关系来归类生物。

「与其因为两种鸟在基因上密切相关而把它们放在一起，在瓦卡帕帕中，你会因为它们的生态位重叠而把它们放在一起，」他解释道。或者你可能把两种在西方科学看来似乎不可调和地截然不同的生物放在一起。

曾经，贝壳杉——一种针叶树——和托霍拉——南露脊鲸——是陆地上的兄弟姐妹。但贝壳杉热爱土壤和天空，而托霍拉渴望海洋。在托霍拉离去之前，它们交换了礼物：托霍拉用他的鳞片皮肤为贝壳杉穿上，成为了粗糙的树皮，而他自己则变得光滑如许，能在浪间滑行。贝壳杉给了托霍拉油脂以保暖并保护他免受盐分侵蚀，还教会了鲸鱼歌唱。

「贝壳杉说：『我留在这里照看这个地方；你去探索，然后回来告诉我你发现了什么。』」沙德博尔特解释道。「我们的故事告诉我们，贝壳杉和鲸鱼彼此之间有着最亲密的关系。」

值得注意的是，这不仅仅是一个故事。20 世纪 70 年代，贝壳杉树开始遭受一种侵袭其根系的真菌感染。感染在 2000 年代初蔓延，现在每年杀死大量树木。「毛利人的第一反应是去看鲸鱼在做什么，」沙德博尔特说。有人说鲸鱼搁浅是因为它们被吸引来帮助受困的兄弟。随后毛利治疗师（即托杭加，tohunga）发现，用搁浅鲸鱼的骨头制成的药膏可以治愈感染的贝壳杉树。

沙德博尔特说，这似乎是治疗贝壳杉枯萎病的成功方案。「所以，如果你告诉某人你可以用贝壳杉树的基因来拯救鲸鱼，毛利人不会反对，因为在他们看来，你只是回溯了一代人的关系。」如果得到科学研究的证实，这不会是毛利知识首次启发治疗方案。借助毛利人对当地植物生态的经验，研究人员在 2019 年证明，昆麻植物的提取物可以抑制困扰贝壳杉的类真菌生物的生长。

沙德博尔特和马尔科姆还帮助我认识到，我们对其他物种进化所做的任何干预，都必须建立在一种深刻而持久的关系感之上。毛利人关于基因编辑所问的问题围绕着它是否会增强或削弱诸如瓦卡帕帕这样的核心价值。马尔科姆说，毛利人并没有统一的基因编辑观点。每个伊维可能以不同方式看待这些问题。用合成生物学来增强一个物种或一个生态系统的韧性可以提升「凯蒂亚基坦加」（kaitiakitanga）——这一守护原则使毛利人对生物世界的其余部分负有责任；但基因驱动可能失控的可能性——尽管埃斯维尔特在系统中精心设计了制动机制——却冒着削弱凯蒂亚基坦加的风险，使毛利人成为不负责任的管理者。一些毛利人可能对基因编辑持怀疑态度，因为向一个物种引入外来基因可能会削弱其瓦卡帕帕（马尔科姆解释说，即使是老鼠和负鼠等非本地物种也拥有瓦卡帕帕）；但如果它有助于一个物种的长期福祉或一个生态系统的功能，它也可能增强瓦卡帕帕。

埃斯维尔特与毛利人就合成基因驱动进行了长时间的对话，至少目前还没有就是否它们代表了解决奥特亚罗瓦/新西兰困境缠身的生态系统的方案达成共识。政府正在谨慎行事，技术受到严格监管。但对基因驱动的兴趣依然浓厚；如果它们有朝一日被使用，那么瓦卡帕帕——以生态关系的纽带取代物种边界——告诉我们一些至关重要的信息，关于我们应如何对待合成生物学。

所有生物都有瓦卡帕帕；就其他动物而言，它是身体、行为和栖息地之间进化出来的关系，使动物适应其环境和与之共存或依赖的其他生物。不幸的是，没有任何动物能够对编辑其基因组给予许可；不存在一个物种议会来提供授权。但我们可以，打个比方说，探询它的瓦卡帕帕——那些将它与更大的生命网络联系起来的继承和关系的脉络。这并不是说其他文化应当挪用毛利人的信仰，而是说同样的问题——这会增强还是削弱物种之间的联系？——应该普遍适用。

编辑牛使其耐热可能无法通过这个测试——如果我们的动机只是继续吃牛肉的话。这无疑会在更广泛的意义上削弱我们的关系，延续一种深刻的生态失衡局面——牲畜占哺乳动物生物量的三分之二，并导致森林生态系统被进一步破坏以腾出牧场。但有些变化培育了关系：用源自小麦的基因编辑美国板栗树，使其能够与一种几乎消灭了整个板栗种群的真菌病原体共存。（尽管转基因板栗在野外表现不佳——小麦基因产生一种抑制真菌的酶，但也降低了树木耐旱的能力——这说明了成功编辑一个物种基因组的深刻困难。）使用基因编辑帮助热带珊瑚抵御白化也将维系数以千计与珊瑚礁共存的物种。即使这需要使用来自完全不同物种的遗传物质，对珊瑚基因组的干预也将被无数其他物种感受到——作为一种延续，一种对生命的推进。

确立一种动物的瓦卡帕帕涉及追溯它的关系回到阿图阿（Atua）——掌管其栖息地的神灵。毛利式的方法并非将人类置于神的位置，而是邀请我们认识到，我们与所有生物一样，继承了神圣的一缕。这是基因驱动以及基因编辑技术整体上提出的根本问题：拥有如此巨大的力量，做一个人意味着什么？

1968 年，作家斯图尔特·布兰德（Stewart Brand）——他后来成为去灭绝遗传技术的支持者——宣告：「我们如同神明，不妨练好这个角色。」但是，「练好」扮演上帝意味着什么？我们将自己视为超然物种的意识——以技术力量为镀金——正是生物多样性遭到大量破坏的种子。相反，我们可以再次看看狮人——在它的形态中，人与动物无缝融合为一体。我们的祖先知道，重新想象其他存在就是重新想象我们自己。如果我们必须干预其他物种的进化，我们应该怀着对贯穿万物的神圣生命之丝的敬意来做，并问自己一个简单的问题：这会拉紧还是松开那些将我们编织进生物世界之网中的丝线？
