articles.title: 我们的科技霸主正在规划让有意识的AI征服宇宙。会出什么问题？
articles.author: Eduardo Porter
articles.summary: 最近，世界首富埃隆·马斯克（Elon Musk）——去年曾一度获得重构美国联邦政府的权力——在其社交媒体平台X上宣称，「越来越明显，人类只是数字超级智能的生物引导程序」——我们在宇宙历史中的角色被降格为那种低级代码，即在你运行复杂程序之前启动计算机的引导代码。
articles.content_cn:
最近，世界首富埃隆·马斯克（Elon Musk）——去年曾一度获得重构美国联邦政府的权力——在其社交媒体平台X上宣称，「越来越明显，人类只是数字超级智能的生物引导程序」——我们在宇宙历史中的角色被降格为那种低级代码，即在你运行复杂程序之前启动计算机的引导代码。

而在进化论主张方面，马斯克还算温和的一端。据硅谷传闻，他曾反驳谷歌联合创始人拉里·佩奇（Larry Page）的论断——佩奇认为，继今天你看到的血肉之躯的人类之后，我们的下一形态必然是数字形式，以便在银河系中传播。（事实上，他最近在法庭上作证称，正是这些忧虑促使他与奥特曼（Altman）共同创办了OpenAI。）血肉之躯并不能成为高效的星际旅行者。

谁在乎人工智能是否会消灭平凡的人类劳动，当它为我们提供了超越肉身、征服银河系的机会？把这些怪异的世界观理解为最终无害的科技人观点——他们从小吃着反乌托邦科幻小说长大——将是一个错误。我们正在接近智人（homo sapiens）的终结这一观念——正如自达尔文（Darwin）时代以来所定义的那样——正在掌舵我们技术未来的精英中凝聚成一个持久的信仰体系。

他们的梦想并非完全一致。但就像围绕更成熟的宗教传统一直旋转的民间故事和迷信一样，硅谷寡头们正在写入我们未来的一系列离奇场景，展现出一种正在形成的宗教的特征——一套信仰体系，旨在为他们的高科技项目赋予宇宙超越感和必然性。

阅读更多在他们心中，他们正在构建人类的下一个阶段，一个「超人类」（transhuman）的未来。在这个未来中，他们可以满足对永生的渴望，并在超人类繁衍扩张至银河系的过程中实现对宇宙的权力掌控。他们的终极目标：执行一个技术神秘主义的梦想，将人之为人的一切本质——包括意识——提炼为信息比特，以二进制代码下载到某种非生物基底（如硅芯片）上，或以电磁波的形式穿越太空传播。

在旧金山及其周边构建的神话基础设施，对我们所知的 humanity 构成了风险。它为沿着一条路径引导技术提供了正当性——这条路径最好也不过是对日常人类的需求、希望和抱负漠不关心，旨在交付一个只有对这些宇宙主宰者才看起来像乌托邦的未来。

谁在乎人工智能是否会消灭平凡的人类劳动，当它为我们提供了超越肉身、征服银河系的机会？这种幻想指引着技术方向：AI的霸主们不是在建造能帮助人类拓展能力的经济实用工具，而是在投入巨资追逐建造超人类的梦想。

这些信念在过去四分之一世纪中浮上台面，伴随着信息技术的发展——这些技术为新兴的IT精英带来了巨额财富和权力——这个精英群体致力于基于科学的进步，渴望超越性的意义，但对有组织宗教的主张和道德约束漠不关心甚至敌视。

「硅谷一直是一个激进世俗的空间，」一位因雇主不愿让其公开表态而拒绝具名的知名科技思想家告诉我。「它制造了一个上帝形状的空洞，然后用自己的形象填补了它。」拒绝了标准宗教的意义来源后，他们通过科幻超人类梦想找到了一条替代路径，为自己的生活赋予意义。或者正如马斯克在X上一条吟诵般的帖子中所说：「 atheism 留下了一个空洞。世俗宗教占据了它的位置。」

虽然这种新创的宇宙创世论至少从互联网早期就开始拼凑，但它在人工智能的肩膀上达到了令人叹为观止的新视野——人工智能为超人类梦想开辟了广阔的新可能性。技术寡头及其野心的批评者道格拉斯·拉什科夫（Douglas Rushkoff）这样表述，他引用了1980年代的讽刺作品——其中 featured 有史上第一个「计算机生成」的电视主持人。「我想AI让拥有马克斯·黑德room（Max Headroom）式存在的概念变得可信了。」

尽管硅谷提出的乌托邦看似怪异，但它符合一个更长的传统——拥有巨额不受约束财富的商业巨头寻求为其事业赋予超越性价值。正如历史学家卡蒂·柯茨（Kati Curts）所写，亨利·福特（Henry Ford）也相信他的使命不仅仅是改造制造业来生产汽车；他相信他肩负着重新工程设计世界以改善社会的使命。

福特建造了福特兰迪亚（Fordlândia）——一项在巴西雨林中试图创建由工业规模橡胶种植园支撑的和谐社会秩序的尝试。奥特曼、马斯克和硅谷团伙想要将意识与AI融合并征服宇宙。这些愿景之间的差距主要与他们时代的技术可能性有关。他们声称正在工程实现某种人类应当感恩的乌托邦愿景——这一主张并不那么不同。

对于我们其余人来说，危险在于技术寡头的野心将如何重塑我们当下的经济和社会——当他们重新配置资源——资本、能源、矿产、水——来加速AI的发展，以当下时代的医疗、教育或减贫为代价来推进超人类梦想。

虽然美国人开始显示出对这些AI巨头不受约束的胃口感到不安的迹象，但特朗普（Trump）政府迄今为止几乎没有表现出想要设置监管护栏或以任何方式约束他们努力的迹象。

硅谷对于未来人类应该是什么样子存在多种观点。

奥特曼和佩奇或许是最致力于将人类与超级智能技术融合并抛弃血肉之躯的人。奥特曼早期就订阅了Nectome——一家硅谷初创公司，该公司提出从大脑的解剖结构和分子细节中提取信息，以便在未来复制意识。「我假设我的大脑将被上传到云端，」奥特曼告诉《MIT技术评论》（MIT Technology Review）。

马斯克想要的略有不同——同样是太空方向的，但坚持保留血肉之躯，通过类似他自己的大脑-计算机接口公司Neuralink的方式用计算机增强。PayPal和Palantir的著名人物彼得·蒂尔（Peter Thiel）对「只是一个模拟我的计算机程序」嗤之以鼻，但被「你的人类自然身体转化为不朽身体」这种技术理想所吸引。

然而，这些愿景趋于一致。例如，佩奇曾建议，与其把钱捐给慈善机构，他可能直接把钱给马斯克。正如他曾对查理·罗斯（Charlie Rose）所说，马斯克想去火星为人类扩张提供一个备份星球，这是一个值得贡献的崇高目标。

有一些共同的来源为各种科幻野心提供了某种道德目的感。一个核心出发点相当接地气：有效利他主义（Effective Altruism，EA）运动——它以毫不退缩的理性主义吸引了技术精英。EA论者认为，慈善事业在很大程度上被浪费了，比如资助当地图书馆。捐赠者必须有目的性，仔细将资金导向能为最多人做最多好事的地方。

这并非不合理的命题。它鼓励了值得赞扬的努力，比如在非洲根除疟疾——理由是你可以用少量美元挽救一个完整的人的生命。但它最终偏离了当下地球人的需求。

很容易迷失在信念和抱负的纠缠之中——这些信念由威廉·麦卡斯kill（William MacAskill）和尼克·博斯特罗姆（Nick Bostrom）等学者阐述和精炼，在由技术寡头膨胀的财富资助的大学部门或智库中。它们取材于非正统伦理学和物理学定律的独特解读。目标：论证将人类（或至少其最特权的那部分）带到前所未有的地方的 imperative。

这个群体的一个目标是沿卡尔达舍夫等级（Kardashev scale）攀升——这是一种衡量文明消耗能量多少的标尺——以获取超越我们生物局限所需的能量和技术能力。当今人类处于阶梯的底部，甚至没有消耗地球的全部能量。按照这种思路，先进文明预计至少要消耗其恒星的所有能量，如果不是银河系的所有能量的话。

在1990年代推动超人类未来的较早群体之一是超自由主义的extropians，其中包括杰出知识分子如埃利泽·尤德科夫斯基（Eliezer Yudkowsky）、博斯特罗姆和经济学家罗宾·汉森（Robin Hanson）。在其核心原则中，他们提出「无界扩张：追求更多的智慧、智慧和效力，无限寿命，以及消除政治、文化、生物和心理上对自我实现和自我实现的限制。永远克服对我们进步和可能性的约束。向宇宙扩张，无止境地前进。」

另一个更近的分支是有效加速主义者。他们试图将物理学征召到他们的事业中，有争议地论证最大化智能生命是一种 imperative，因为生命擅长从环境中提取可用能量并将其耗散——增加物理学中所称的「熵」（entropy）。

正如贝夫·耶佐斯（Beff Jezos）——即纪尧姆·韦尔东（Guillaume Verdon），该运动的领军人物之一的在线身份——所说：「有效加速主义旨在遵循『宇宙的意志』：顺应热力学对更庞大、更聪慧的文明未来的偏好——这些文明更有效地从宇宙中寻找/提取自由能量，并以越来越宏大的规模将其转化为效用。」

阅读更多在一个肯定令硅谷亿万富翁们愉悦的哲学转折中，有效加速主义者主张不受监管、政府和其他麻烦阻碍的猖獗技术资本主义——因为这将最大化宇宙资源的消耗，「捕获文明效用」，并将残余耗散到无序的虚空中。

梦想的细节实际上并不太重要。因为它们都把我们带到大致相同的地方。现在重要的是，这些宇宙主宰者——投资于 harnessing 恒星能量、被一种道德计算所诱惑——该计算将当下人民的福祉置于价值低于未来数量远为庞大的人形生物的位置——是否有耐心关怀我们其余人。

迹象并不乐观。例如，硅谷风险投资家马克·安德烈森（Marc Andreessen）想要「确保技术资本上升螺旋永远持续」。他的敌人名单几乎囊括了任何可能反对技术事业的人或理念。其中包括「可持续性」、「社会责任」和「技术伦理」。

如果你创造了上帝但你拥有上帝你就成了独裁者贾伦·拉尼尔（Jaron Lanier）蒂尔在这群人中不同寻常——他坚定地致力于一种独特的基督教变体，其中任何阻碍技术的人，或试图向他征税的政府，都表现为反基督。虽然他声称与安德烈森几乎没有亲和力，但他似乎有相似的口味。作为一个死硬的自由主义者，他对政府再分配嗤之以鼻。他的慈善事业是对推进技术进步项目的营利性投资。慈善，正如通常理解的那样，等于浪费技术人员超越我们当下所需的资源。马斯克曾称 empathy 是「西方文明的基本弱点」。

不管他们超人类梦想的具体特征如何，硅谷亿万富翁编织的叙事为他们的巨大权力积累提供了正当性。正如计算机科学先驱和技术远见者贾伦·拉尼尔告诉我的：「如果你创造了上帝但你拥有上帝你就成了独裁者。」而这些独裁者似乎不认为地球上的人类——至少我们中的大多数——特别有价值。二月份被问及AI消耗的大量能源时，奥特曼略带轻蔑地指出，「训练一个人类也需要大量能量。」

然而他们承认不知道自己在做什么。「领域外的人常常惊讶和不安地得知，我们不理解自己的AI创造物是如何运作的，」Anthropic联合创始人达里奥·阿莫代伊（Dario Amodei）去年写道。「他们的担忧是对的：这种理解缺失在技术史上基本上是前所未有的。」阿莫代伊与有效利他主义有深厚联系；他的姐妹丹妮拉·阿莫代伊（Daniela Amodei），Anthropic的总裁，嫁给了该运动的一位创始人。不过最近，两人都已与该运动拉开了距离。

尤其令人忧虑的是，这些巨头在追逐他们计划用机器建造的未来乌托邦时是多么不受约束。科技亿万富翁正在向政治竞选投入数亿美元，以抵御监管尝试、逃避问责以防他们的事业出错。他们要确保在他们重塑社会的工作中没有人插手。而他们在很大程度上正在成功——目前为止，没有任何有能力阻止他们的人正在插手。

社会应该如何干预？我们的政治体系是否提供了帮助将过程引导至亲社会方向的工具？超越技术对我们未来经济和社会格局的不确定影响，我们应该如何应对将这些建造拥有硅脑的超人类赛博格的努力的成果过度集中于少数人手中的问题？

特朗普政府迄今为止几乎没有表现出抵制技术寡头幻想的兴趣。但这不一定意味着硅谷寡头的技术统治项目是不可避免的。疑虑正在Maga基础中出现：弗吉尼亚乡村地区那些抵制数据中心吞噬电力和水供应的人们，警惕于声称诉诸技术色彩更高权威的世界主义精英的福音派基督徒。

AI项目的其他麻烦迹象正在酝酿——从大学毕业生向鼓吹AI的毕业典礼演讲者喝倒彩，到特朗普短暂关注Anthropic新模型Mythos的潜在犯罪能力，然后最终决定不监管这个东西。在5月初最新的Times-Siena民调中，认为AI主要是坏事的登记选民数量是认为它主要是好事的人的两倍多。

或许最有力的人本立场来自圣父本人。周一，教皇利奥（Pope Leo）发布了教皇通谕《Magnifica Humanitas》，反击以牺牲就业和社会公平为代价不受约束地发展AI。「这创造了一种物质进步与人类学退行的悖论，动摇了公正稳定的社会和平的基础，」他补充道。

那里有育儿室的废墟——正如费德里科·古兹曼·鲁比奥（Federico Guzmán Rubio）在其著作《有这样的地方》（There is Such a Place）中所写，福特对牛的厌恶意味着工人的孩子被引入从远处运来的豆奶。那里有学校的废墟，孩子们在那里被教导关于亨利·沃兹沃思·朗费罗（Henry Wadsworth Longfellow）。留下的遗迹证明了一个寡头团体不协调的梦想——它高估了自己的权力，将自己的胃口与更大利益混淆。

阅读更多AI驱动的宇宙幻想同样疯狂。暂且不论将人类意识以数字形式呈现、与AI融合并穿越银河系传输的部分。那个表面上更接地气的主张——有意识的AI不仅可能而且即将到来——与我们自己对意识是什么的脆弱理解存在根本矛盾。甚至更平凡的目标，比如让人工智能自我训练，也在不断被推入事件视界。

也许这一次，这些离奇的声称也将消退为无关紧要；《星际迷航》（Star Trek）中人被非物质化并在银河系上下传输的愿景将衰变为一堆锈迹斑斑的废墟。也许超人类项目会让位于一个多少可以辨认的人类未来——附带一些酷炫的新AI插件。也许它甚至能以一种服务于我们久被遗忘的公平繁荣梦想的方式实现。

不过到目前为止，我们的技术远见者正在推动别的东西——一个以巨额财富和权力集中为标志的未来，对芸芸众生的平凡抱负漠不关心。万一它成功将佩奇、马斯克及其同类的基本本质装载到硅躯体中前往「无人曾至之处」，我们只能希望他们在这一过程中不要摧毁我们所知的世界。

More recently, Elon Musk, the world’s richest man, who at one point last year was granted the power to reconfigure the US federal government, argued on his social media platform, X, that “it increasingly appears that humanity is a biological bootloader for digital superintelligence” – our role in the history of the cosmos reduced to that of the low level code that boots up a computer before you can run sophisticated programs on it.

And Musk is on the tame side of the evolutionary proposition. According to Silicon Valley lore, he once pushed back against Google co-founder Larry Page’s claim that our next manifestation, to follow in the steps of the meat-and-bone humans you see walking about today, would necessarily have digital form in order to spread throughout the galaxy. (In fact, he recently testified in court that it was those concerns that prompted him to found OpenAI with Altman.) Meat and bones do not make for efficient interstellar travelers.

Who cares if artificial intelligence obliterates humdrum human labor when it offers us the opportunity to transcend our body and conquer the galaxy?It would be a mistake to understand these weird worldviews as an ultimately harmless take by techies who grew up on a diet of dystopian science fiction. The notion that we are approaching the end of the homo sapiens, as defined since Darwin’s day, is coalescing into a durable body of belief among the elites at the helm of our technological future.

Their dreams are not all perfectly aligned. But like the folk stories and superstitions that have for ever revolved around more established religious traditions, the collection of far-fetched scenarios valley oligarchs are writing into our future exhibits the hallmarks of a religion in the making, a body of belief to confer a sense of cosmic transcendence and inevitability to their hi-tech project.

Read moreIn their minds, they are on their way to build the next phase of humanity, a “transhuman” future. In this future, they can satisfy their desire for immortality and assert power over the cosmos as transhumans multiply and expand across the galaxy. Their ultimate goal: to execute on a techno-mystical dream to distill the essence of what it is to be human, consciousness and all, into bits of information to be downloaded as binary code on to some non-biological substrate such as a silicon chip, or beamed through space as electromagnetic waves.

The mythopoeic infrastructure assembled in and around San Francisco carries risk for humanity as we know it. It justifies steering technology along a path that is, at best, indifferent to the needs, hopes and aspirations of everyday humans in a quest to deliver a future that only looks like utopia to these masters of the universe.

Who cares if artificial intelligence obliterates humdrum human labor when it offers us the opportunity to transcend our body and conquer the galaxy? The fantasy directs the technology: rather than building economically useful tools that can help humans expand their capabilities, the overlords of AI are sinking vast resources into a dream of building superhumans.

These beliefs have pushed to the fore over the last quarter century, accompanying the advance of information technologies that have delivered enormous wealth and power to a new IT elite, one committed to science-based progress and hungry for transcendent meaning, but indifferent or even hostile to the propositions and moral constraints of organized religion.

“Silicon Valley has been a militantly secular space,” a prominent thinker about technology whose employer would be unhappy if he went on record told me. “It created a God-shaped hole, which it filled in its image.” Having rejected standard religious sources of purpose, they found an alternative path to provide their lives with significance via sci-fi transhuman dreams. Or as Musk observed in a singsong post on X: “Atheism left an empty space. Secular religion took its place.”

While this newfangled cosmogony has been cobbled together at least since the early days of the Internet, it reached toward breathtaking new horizons on the shoulders of artificial intelligence, which opened up vast new possibilities for the transhuman dream. Douglas Rushkoff, a critic of the technological oligarchy and its ambitions, put it thus, referencing the 1980s-era satire featuring the first ever “computer-generated” TV host. “I guess AI makes the notion of having a Max Headroom existence plausible.”

Weird though the valley’s proposed utopia may appear, it fits a longer tradition of business titans with vast unrestrained wealth seeking to endow their endeavors with transcendent value. Henry Ford, as historian Kati Curts has written, also believed his calling was about more than transforming manufacturing to make cars; he believed he was on a mission to re-engineer the world to improve society.

Ford built Fordlândia, an attempt to create a harmonic social order supported by an industrial-scale rubber plantation in the Brazilian rainforest. Altman, Musk and the valley gang want to merge consciousness with AI and conquer the cosmos. The distance between these visions has mostly to do with the technological possibilities of their time. The proposition that they are engineering some utopian vision that humanity should be grateful for is not that dissimilar.

The danger, for the rest of us, is how the technological oligarchy’s aspirations will reshape the economies and societies of our present, as they redirect resources – capital, energy, minerals, water – to turbocharge AI and bring about the transhuman dream at the expense of healthcare, education or poverty reduction in the here and now.

While Americans are starting to show some signs of discomfort over the unrestrained appetites of this crop of AI moguls, the Trump administration has shown few signs so far of wanting to put in place regulatory guardrails and constrain their efforts in any way.

There are a variety of views in the valley about what a future humanity should look like.

Altman and Page are perhaps the most committed to the goal of merging humans with superintelligent technology and abandoning the flesh. Altman was an early subscriber to Nectome, a valley startup that proposes to retrieve information present in the brain’s anatomical layout and molecular details in order to replicate consciousness in the future. “I assume my brain will be uploaded to the cloud,” Altman told the MIT Technology Review.

Musk wants something a bit different, also spacebound but committed to flesh, enhanced by computers via something like his own brain-to-computer interface company Neuralink. Peter Thiel, of PayPal and Palantir fame, frowns on “just a computer program that simulates me”, but is drawn to the techno-ideal of “this radical transformation where your human, natural body gets transformed into an immortal body”.

And yet, the visions converge. Page, for instance, has suggested that rather than giving money to charity he might just give it to Musk. As he once told Charlie Rose, Musk wants to go to Mars to provide a backup planet for humanity to expand and that is a worthy goal to contribute to.

There are shared sources that provide some sense of moral purpose to the various flavors of sci-fi ambition. One of the core starting points is rather earthbound: the movement for effective altruism (EA), which seduced the technological elite with its appeal to unflinching rationality. Philanthropy, the EAs argued, was largely wasted by funding, say, the local library. Donors had to be purposeful, carefully directing their money to where it would do the most good for the most people.

That is not an unreasonable proposition. It encouraged laudable efforts to, say, eradicate malaria in Africa, on the grounds that one could save a whole human life for a small fistfull of dollars. But it eventually departed from the needs of present earthlings.

It’s easy to get lost in the tangle of beliefs and aspirations – articulated and refined by academics like William MacAskill and Nick Bostrom, at university departments or thinktanks funded by the techno-oligarch’s mushrooming wealth. They draw from unorthodox ethics, and from idiosyncratic readings of the laws of physics. The goal: to justify the imperative to take humanity (or at least the most privileged part of it) where it has never gone before.

One of this crew’s goals is to advance up the Kardashev scale – a measure of the amount of energy a civilization consumes – to harness the energy and acquire the technological capabilities needed to transcend our biological confines. Present day humanity, at the bottom of the ladder, doesn’t even consume all of the energy of the Earth. Advanced civilizations, the thinking goes, are expected to consume all the energy of their star, at least, if not all that of the galaxy.

One of the earlier groups pushing for a transhuman future in the 1990s were the ultra-libertarian Extropians, which included leading intellectuals such as Eliezer Yudkowsky, Bostrom and economist Robin Hanson. Outlined in their core principles, they proposed “Boundless Expansion: Seeking more intelligence, wisdom, and effectiveness, an unlimited lifespan, and the removal of political, cultural, biological, and psychological limits to self-actualization and self-realization. Perpetually overcoming constraints on our progress and possibilities. Expanding into the universe and advancing without end.”

Another, more recent branch, are the effective accelerationists. They have tried to conscript physics to their cause, arguing – controversially – that maximizing intelligent life is an imperative, because life is good at extracting available energy from the environment and dissipating it – increasing what is known in physics as “entropy”.

As Beff Jezos – the online identity of Guillaume Verdon, one of the leading lights of the movement – puts it: “Effective accelerationism aims to follow the ‘will of the universe’: leaning into the thermodynamic bias towards futures with greater and smarter civilizations that are more effective at finding/extracting free energy from the universe and converting it to utility at grander and grander scales.”

Read moreIn a philosophical twist that surely pleases Silicon Valley’s billionaires, effective accelerationists argue for rampant techno-capitalism, unhindered by regulation, government and other nuisances, because this would maximize the consumption of the universe’s resources, “capture civilizational utility”, and dissipate the residue into the disorganized void.

The details of the dream don’t actually make much of a difference. Because they all take us roughly to the same place. What matters now is whether the masters of the universe – invested in harnessing the energy of the stars, tempted by a moral calculus that posits that the wellbeing of the people of the present is of inferior value to the vastly more numerous humanoids of the future – will have the patience to care for the rest of us.

The signs are not great. Silicon Valley venture capitalist Marc Andreessen, for instance, wants to “ensure the techno-capital upward spiral continues forever”. His list of enemies encompasses pretty much any person or idea that might stand against technological endeavor. That includes “sustainability”, “social responsibility” and “tech ethics”.

If you create God but you own God you become the dictatorJaron LanierThiel is unusual in this crowd in that he is fiercely committed to an idiosyncratic variant of Christianity in which anybody standing in the way of technology, or governments that try to tax him, show up as the antichrist. But though he claims little affinity with Andreesen, he seems to have similar tastes. A diehard libertarian, he is contemptuous of government redistribution. His philanthropy is about for-profit investments in projects to further technological progress. Charity, as commonly understood, amounts to wasting resources that technologists will need to transcend our present. Musk has called empathy “the fundamental weakness of western civilization”.

Regardless of the specific features of their transhuman dreams, the narrative crafted by Silicon Valley billionaires justifies their vast accumulation of power. As computer science pioneer and tech visionary Jaron Lanier told me: “If you create God but you own God you become the dictator.” And these dictators don’t seem to believe earthbound humans – most of us, at least – are particularly valuable. Questioned in February about the vast amounts of energy sucked up by AI, Altman noted, somewhat disparagingly, that “it also takes a lot of energy to train a human.”

Yet they admittedly have no idea what they are doing. “People outside the field are often surprised and alarmed to learn that we do not understand how our own AI creations work,” Anthropic co-founder Dario Amodei wrote last year. “They are right to be concerned: this lack of understanding is essentially unprecedented in the history of technology.” Amodei has deep ties to effective altruism; his sister Daniela, Anthropic’s president, is married to a founder of the movement. Recently, though, they’ve both distanced themselves from it.

What’s particularly distressing is how unconstrained these moguls are, as they pursue the futuristic utopia they plan to build with their machines. Tech billionaires are plowing hundreds of millions into political campaigns, to fend off attempts at regulation and evade accountability lest their endeavors go awry. They want to make sure nobody butts in as they work to reshape society. And they are largely succeeding – for now, no one with the power to stop them is butting in.

How should society intervene? Does our political system provide the tools to help steer the process in a pro-social direction? Beyond the uncertain impact of technology on our future economic and social landscape, how should we address the narrow concentration of the fruits of these endeavors to build transhuman cyborgs with silicon brains?

The Trump administration has shown little interest so far in resisting the tech oligarch’s fantasy. But that doesn’t necessarily mean that the valley oligarchs’ project of techno-domination is inevitable. Misgivings are emerging among the Maga base: The folks in rural Virginia who push back against datacenters hogging power and water supplies, evangelicals wary of a cosmopolitan elite claiming recourse to a tech-inflected higher authority.

Other signs of trouble are brewing for the AI project – from college graduates booing commencement speakers who extol AI, to Trump’s brief moment of concern over the potential criminal capabilities of Anthropic’s new Mythos model before deciding not to regulate the thing after all. In the latest Times-Siena poll from earlier in May, more than twice as many registered voters said AI is mostly bad, compared with those saying it was mostly good.

Perhaps the most forceful, pro-human position has come from the Holy Father himself. On Monday, Pope Leo published the encyclical Magnifica Humanitas, pushing back against the unfettered development of AI at the expense of jobs and social equity. “This creates a paradox of material progress and anthropological regression that undermines the foundations of a just and stable social peace,” he added.

There are the ruins of nurseries, where as Federico Guzmán Rubio writes in his book There is Such a Place, Ford’s aversion to cows meant the children of workers were introduced to soy milk, shipped in from miles away. There are the ruins of schools where kids were taught about Henry Wadsworth Longfellow. What’s left is testament to the incongruous dreams of an oligarchy that overvalued its power and confused its appetites with the greater good.

Read moreThe AI-fueled cosmic fantasy is no less nuts. Forget the part where human consciousness is rendered in digital form, merged with AI and beamed across the galaxy. The ostensibly more down-to-earth proposition that conscious AI is not just possible but around the corner is in fundamental tension with our tenuous grasp of what consciousness is. Even more mundane objectives, such as getting artificial intelligence to train itself, keep getting pushed forward into the event horizon.

Perhaps this time too the outlandish claims will fade into irrelevance; the Star-Trek vision of people being dematerialized and beamed up and down around the galaxy will decay into some rustbound heap. Maybe the transhuman project will give way to a more or less recognizably human future with some cool new AI plugins. Maybe it can even be achieved in a way that serves our long-forgotten dream of equitable prosperity.

So far, though, our technological visionaries are pushing for something else, a future marked by vast concentrations of wealth and power, indifferent to the humdrum aspirations of the unwashed many. In the unlikely event that it succeeds in taking the essence of Page, Musk and their ilk aboard a silicon body to “where no man has gone before”, here’s hoping that they don’t destroy the world we know in the process.

paragraphs.cn: 最近，世界首富埃隆·马斯克（Elon Musk）——去年曾一度获得重构美国联邦政府的权力——在其社交媒体平台X上宣称，「越来越明显，人类只是数字超级智能的生物引导程序」——我们在宇宙历史中的角色被降格为那种低级代码，即在你运行复杂程序之前启动计算机的引导代码。
paragraphs.en: More recently, Elon Musk, the world’s richest man, who at one point last year was granted the power to reconfigure the US federal government, argued on his social media platform, X, that “it increasingly appears that humanity is a biological bootloader for digital superintelligence” – our role in the history of the cosmos reduced to that of the low level code that boots up a computer before you can run sophisticated programs on it.

paragraphs.cn: 而在进化论主张方面，马斯克还算温和的一端。据硅谷传闻，他曾反驳谷歌联合创始人拉里·佩奇（Larry Page）的论断——佩奇认为，继今天你看到的血肉之躯的人类之后，我们的下一形态必然是数字形式，以便在银河系中传播。（事实上，他最近在法庭上作证称，正是这些忧虑促使他与奥特曼（Altman）共同创办了OpenAI。）血肉之躯并不能成为高效的星际旅行者。
paragraphs.en: And Musk is on the tame side of the evolutionary proposition. According to Silicon Valley lore, he once pushed back against Google co-founder Larry Page’s claim that our next manifestation, to follow in the steps of the meat-and-bone humans you see walking about today, would necessarily have digital form in order to spread throughout the galaxy. (In fact, he recently testified in court that it was those concerns that prompted him to found OpenAI with Altman.) Meat and bones do not make for efficient interstellar travelers.

paragraphs.cn: 谁在乎人工智能是否会消灭平凡的人类劳动，当它为我们提供了超越肉身、征服银河系的机会？把这些怪异的世界观理解为最终无害的科技人观点——他们从小吃着反乌托邦科幻小说长大——将是一个错误。我们正在接近智人（homo sapiens）的终结这一观念——正如自达尔文（Darwin）时代以来所定义的那样——正在掌舵我们技术未来的精英中凝聚成一个持久的信仰体系。
paragraphs.en: Who cares if artificial intelligence obliterates humdrum human labor when it offers us the opportunity to transcend our body and conquer the galaxy?It would be a mistake to understand these weird worldviews as an ultimately harmless take by techies who grew up on a diet of dystopian science fiction. The notion that we are approaching the end of the homo sapiens, as defined since Darwin’s day, is coalescing into a durable body of belief among the elites at the helm of our technological future.

paragraphs.cn: 他们的梦想并非完全一致。但就像围绕更成熟的宗教传统一直旋转的民间故事和迷信一样，硅谷寡头们正在写入我们未来的一系列离奇场景，展现出一种正在形成的宗教的特征——一套信仰体系，旨在为他们的高科技项目赋予宇宙超越感和必然性。
paragraphs.en: Their dreams are not all perfectly aligned. But like the folk stories and superstitions that have for ever revolved around more established religious traditions, the collection of far-fetched scenarios valley oligarchs are writing into our future exhibits the hallmarks of a religion in the making, a body of belief to confer a sense of cosmic transcendence and inevitability to their hi-tech project.

paragraphs.cn: 阅读更多在他们心中，他们正在构建人类的下一个阶段，一个「超人类」（transhuman）的未来。在这个未来中，他们可以满足对永生的渴望，并在超人类繁衍扩张至银河系的过程中实现对宇宙的权力掌控。他们的终极目标：执行一个技术神秘主义的梦想，将人之为人的一切本质——包括意识——提炼为信息比特，以二进制代码下载到某种非生物基底（如硅芯片）上，或以电磁波的形式穿越太空传播。
paragraphs.en: Read moreIn their minds, they are on their way to build the next phase of humanity, a “transhuman” future. In this future, they can satisfy their desire for immortality and assert power over the cosmos as transhumans multiply and expand across the galaxy. Their ultimate goal: to execute on a techno-mystical dream to distill the essence of what it is to be human, consciousness and all, into bits of information to be downloaded as binary code on to some non-biological substrate such as a silicon chip, or beamed through space as electromagnetic waves.

paragraphs.cn: 在旧金山及其周边构建的神话基础设施，对我们所知的 humanity 构成了风险。它为沿着一条路径引导技术提供了正当性——这条路径最好也不过是对日常人类的需求、希望和抱负漠不关心，旨在交付一个只有对这些宇宙主宰者才看起来像乌托邦的未来。
paragraphs.en: The mythopoeic infrastructure assembled in and around San Francisco carries risk for humanity as we know it. It justifies steering technology along a path that is, at best, indifferent to the needs, hopes and aspirations of everyday humans in a quest to deliver a future that only looks like utopia to these masters of the universe.

paragraphs.cn: 谁在乎人工智能是否会消灭平凡的人类劳动，当它为我们提供了超越肉身、征服银河系的机会？这种幻想指引着技术方向：AI的霸主们不是在建造能帮助人类拓展能力的经济实用工具，而是在投入巨资追逐建造超人类的梦想。
paragraphs.en: Who cares if artificial intelligence obliterates humdrum human labor when it offers us the opportunity to transcend our body and conquer the galaxy? The fantasy directs the technology: rather than building economically useful tools that can help humans expand their capabilities, the overlords of AI are sinking vast resources into a dream of building superhumans.

paragraphs.cn: 这些信念在过去四分之一世纪中浮上台面，伴随着信息技术的发展——这些技术为新兴的IT精英带来了巨额财富和权力——这个精英群体致力于基于科学的进步，渴望超越性的意义，但对有组织宗教的主张和道德约束漠不关心甚至敌视。
paragraphs.en: These beliefs have pushed to the fore over the last quarter century, accompanying the advance of information technologies that have delivered enormous wealth and power to a new IT elite, one committed to science-based progress and hungry for transcendent meaning, but indifferent or even hostile to the propositions and moral constraints of organized religion.

paragraphs.cn: 「硅谷一直是一个激进世俗的空间，」一位因雇主不愿让其公开表态而拒绝具名的知名科技思想家告诉我。「它制造了一个上帝形状的空洞，然后用自己的形象填补了它。」拒绝了标准宗教的意义来源后，他们通过科幻超人类梦想找到了一条替代路径，为自己的生活赋予意义。或者正如马斯克在X上一条吟诵般的帖子中所说：「 atheism 留下了一个空洞。世俗宗教占据了它的位置。」
paragraphs.en: “Silicon Valley has been a militantly secular space,” a prominent thinker about technology whose employer would be unhappy if he went on record told me. “It created a God-shaped hole, which it filled in its image.” Having rejected standard religious sources of purpose, they found an alternative path to provide their lives with significance via sci-fi transhuman dreams. Or as Musk observed in a singsong post on X: “Atheism left an empty space. Secular religion took its place.”

paragraphs.cn: 虽然这种新创的宇宙创世论至少从互联网早期就开始拼凑，但它在人工智能的肩膀上达到了令人叹为观止的新视野——人工智能为超人类梦想开辟了广阔的新可能性。技术寡头及其野心的批评者道格拉斯·拉什科夫（Douglas Rushkoff）这样表述，他引用了1980年代的讽刺作品——其中 featured 有史上第一个「计算机生成」的电视主持人。「我想AI让拥有马克斯·黑德room（Max Headroom）式存在的概念变得可信了。」
paragraphs.en: While this newfangled cosmogony has been cobbled together at least since the early days of the Internet, it reached toward breathtaking new horizons on the shoulders of artificial intelligence, which opened up vast new possibilities for the transhuman dream. Douglas Rushkoff, a critic of the technological oligarchy and its ambitions, put it thus, referencing the 1980s-era satire featuring the first ever “computer-generated” TV host. “I guess AI makes the notion of having a Max Headroom existence plausible.”

paragraphs.cn: 尽管硅谷提出的乌托邦看似怪异，但它符合一个更长的传统——拥有巨额不受约束财富的商业巨头寻求为其事业赋予超越性价值。正如历史学家卡蒂·柯茨（Kati Curts）所写，亨利·福特（Henry Ford）也相信他的使命不仅仅是改造制造业来生产汽车；他相信他肩负着重新工程设计世界以改善社会的使命。
paragraphs.en: Weird though the valley’s proposed utopia may appear, it fits a longer tradition of business titans with vast unrestrained wealth seeking to endow their endeavors with transcendent value. Henry Ford, as historian Kati Curts has written, also believed his calling was about more than transforming manufacturing to make cars; he believed he was on a mission to re-engineer the world to improve society.

paragraphs.cn: 福特建造了福特兰迪亚（Fordlândia）——一项在巴西雨林中试图创建由工业规模橡胶种植园支撑的和谐社会秩序的尝试。奥特曼、马斯克和硅谷团伙想要将意识与AI融合并征服宇宙。这些愿景之间的差距主要与他们时代的技术可能性有关。他们声称正在工程实现某种人类应当感恩的乌托邦愿景——这一主张并不那么不同。
paragraphs.en: Ford built Fordlândia, an attempt to create a harmonic social order supported by an industrial-scale rubber plantation in the Brazilian rainforest. Altman, Musk and the valley gang want to merge consciousness with AI and conquer the cosmos. The distance between these visions has mostly to do with the technological possibilities of their time. The proposition that they are engineering some utopian vision that humanity should be grateful for is not that dissimilar.

paragraphs.cn: 对于我们其余人来说，危险在于技术寡头的野心将如何重塑我们当下的经济和社会——当他们重新配置资源——资本、能源、矿产、水——来加速AI的发展，以当下时代的医疗、教育或减贫为代价来推进超人类梦想。
paragraphs.en: The danger, for the rest of us, is how the technological oligarchy’s aspirations will reshape the economies and societies of our present, as they redirect resources – capital, energy, minerals, water – to turbocharge AI and bring about the transhuman dream at the expense of healthcare, education or poverty reduction in the here and now.

paragraphs.cn: 虽然美国人开始显示出对这些AI巨头不受约束的胃口感到不安的迹象，但特朗普（Trump）政府迄今为止几乎没有表现出想要设置监管护栏或以任何方式约束他们努力的迹象。
paragraphs.en: While Americans are starting to show some signs of discomfort over the unrestrained appetites of this crop of AI moguls, the Trump administration has shown few signs so far of wanting to put in place regulatory guardrails and constrain their efforts in any way.

paragraphs.cn: 硅谷对于未来人类应该是什么样子存在多种观点。
paragraphs.en: There are a variety of views in the valley about what a future humanity should look like.

paragraphs.cn: 奥特曼和佩奇或许是最致力于将人类与超级智能技术融合并抛弃血肉之躯的人。奥特曼早期就订阅了Nectome——一家硅谷初创公司，该公司提出从大脑的解剖结构和分子细节中提取信息，以便在未来复制意识。「我假设我的大脑将被上传到云端，」奥特曼告诉《MIT技术评论》（MIT Technology Review）。
paragraphs.en: Altman and Page are perhaps the most committed to the goal of merging humans with superintelligent technology and abandoning the flesh. Altman was an early subscriber to Nectome, a valley startup that proposes to retrieve information present in the brain’s anatomical layout and molecular details in order to replicate consciousness in the future. “I assume my brain will be uploaded to the cloud,” Altman told the MIT Technology Review.

paragraphs.cn: 马斯克想要的略有不同——同样是太空方向的，但坚持保留血肉之躯，通过类似他自己的大脑-计算机接口公司Neuralink的方式用计算机增强。PayPal和Palantir的著名人物彼得·蒂尔（Peter Thiel）对「只是一个模拟我的计算机程序」嗤之以鼻，但被「你的人类自然身体转化为不朽身体」这种技术理想所吸引。
paragraphs.en: Musk wants something a bit different, also spacebound but committed to flesh, enhanced by computers via something like his own brain-to-computer interface company Neuralink. Peter Thiel, of PayPal and Palantir fame, frowns on “just a computer program that simulates me”, but is drawn to the techno-ideal of “this radical transformation where your human, natural body gets transformed into an immortal body”.

paragraphs.cn: 然而，这些愿景趋于一致。例如，佩奇曾建议，与其把钱捐给慈善机构，他可能直接把钱给马斯克。正如他曾对查理·罗斯（Charlie Rose）所说，马斯克想去火星为人类扩张提供一个备份星球，这是一个值得贡献的崇高目标。
paragraphs.en: And yet, the visions converge. Page, for instance, has suggested that rather than giving money to charity he might just give it to Musk. As he once told Charlie Rose, Musk wants to go to Mars to provide a backup planet for humanity to expand and that is a worthy goal to contribute to.

paragraphs.cn: 有一些共同的来源为各种科幻野心提供了某种道德目的感。一个核心出发点相当接地气：有效利他主义（Effective Altruism，EA）运动——它以毫不退缩的理性主义吸引了技术精英。EA论者认为，慈善事业在很大程度上被浪费了，比如资助当地图书馆。捐赠者必须有目的性，仔细将资金导向能为最多人做最多好事的地方。
paragraphs.en: There are shared sources that provide some sense of moral purpose to the various flavors of sci-fi ambition. One of the core starting points is rather earthbound: the movement for effective altruism (EA), which seduced the technological elite with its appeal to unflinching rationality. Philanthropy, the EAs argued, was largely wasted by funding, say, the local library. Donors had to be purposeful, carefully directing their money to where it would do the most good for the most people.

paragraphs.cn: 这并非不合理的命题。它鼓励了值得赞扬的努力，比如在非洲根除疟疾——理由是你可以用少量美元挽救一个完整的人的生命。但它最终偏离了当下地球人的需求。
paragraphs.en: That is not an unreasonable proposition. It encouraged laudable efforts to, say, eradicate malaria in Africa, on the grounds that one could save a whole human life for a small fistfull of dollars. But it eventually departed from the needs of present earthlings.

paragraphs.cn: 很容易迷失在信念和抱负的纠缠之中——这些信念由威廉·麦卡斯kill（William MacAskill）和尼克·博斯特罗姆（Nick Bostrom）等学者阐述和精炼，在由技术寡头膨胀的财富资助的大学部门或智库中。它们取材于非正统伦理学和物理学定律的独特解读。目标：论证将人类（或至少其最特权的那部分）带到前所未有的地方的 imperative。
paragraphs.en: It’s easy to get lost in the tangle of beliefs and aspirations – articulated and refined by academics like William MacAskill and Nick Bostrom, at university departments or thinktanks funded by the techno-oligarch’s mushrooming wealth. They draw from unorthodox ethics, and from idiosyncratic readings of the laws of physics. The goal: to justify the imperative to take humanity (or at least the most privileged part of it) where it has never gone before.

paragraphs.cn: 这个群体的一个目标是沿卡尔达舍夫等级（Kardashev scale）攀升——这是一种衡量文明消耗能量多少的标尺——以获取超越我们生物局限所需的能量和技术能力。当今人类处于阶梯的底部，甚至没有消耗地球的全部能量。按照这种思路，先进文明预计至少要消耗其恒星的所有能量，如果不是银河系的所有能量的话。
paragraphs.en: One of this crew’s goals is to advance up the Kardashev scale – a measure of the amount of energy a civilization consumes – to harness the energy and acquire the technological capabilities needed to transcend our biological confines. Present day humanity, at the bottom of the ladder, doesn’t even consume all of the energy of the Earth. Advanced civilizations, the thinking goes, are expected to consume all the energy of their star, at least, if not all that of the galaxy.

paragraphs.cn: 在1990年代推动超人类未来的较早群体之一是超自由主义的extropians，其中包括杰出知识分子如埃利泽·尤德科夫斯基（Eliezer Yudkowsky）、博斯特罗姆和经济学家罗宾·汉森（Robin Hanson）。在其核心原则中，他们提出「无界扩张：追求更多的智慧、智慧和效力，无限寿命，以及消除政治、文化、生物和心理上对自我实现和自我实现的限制。永远克服对我们进步和可能性的约束。向宇宙扩张，无止境地前进。」
paragraphs.en: One of the earlier groups pushing for a transhuman future in the 1990s were the ultra-libertarian Extropians, which included leading intellectuals such as Eliezer Yudkowsky, Bostrom and economist Robin Hanson. Outlined in their core principles, they proposed “Boundless Expansion: Seeking more intelligence, wisdom, and effectiveness, an unlimited lifespan, and the removal of political, cultural, biological, and psychological limits to self-actualization and self-realization. Perpetually overcoming constraints on our progress and possibilities. Expanding into the universe and advancing without end.”

paragraphs.cn: 另一个更近的分支是有效加速主义者。他们试图将物理学征召到他们的事业中，有争议地论证最大化智能生命是一种 imperative，因为生命擅长从环境中提取可用能量并将其耗散——增加物理学中所称的「熵」（entropy）。
paragraphs.en: Another, more recent branch, are the effective accelerationists. They have tried to conscript physics to their cause, arguing – controversially – that maximizing intelligent life is an imperative, because life is good at extracting available energy from the environment and dissipating it – increasing what is known in physics as “entropy”.

paragraphs.cn: 正如贝夫·耶佐斯（Beff Jezos）——即纪尧姆·韦尔东（Guillaume Verdon），该运动的领军人物之一的在线身份——所说：「有效加速主义旨在遵循『宇宙的意志』：顺应热力学对更庞大、更聪慧的文明未来的偏好——这些文明更有效地从宇宙中寻找/提取自由能量，并以越来越宏大的规模将其转化为效用。」
paragraphs.en: As Beff Jezos – the online identity of Guillaume Verdon, one of the leading lights of the movement – puts it: “Effective accelerationism aims to follow the ‘will of the universe’: leaning into the thermodynamic bias towards futures with greater and smarter civilizations that are more effective at finding/extracting free energy from the universe and converting it to utility at grander and grander scales.”

paragraphs.cn: 阅读更多在一个肯定令硅谷亿万富翁们愉悦的哲学转折中，有效加速主义者主张不受监管、政府和其他麻烦阻碍的猖獗技术资本主义——因为这将最大化宇宙资源的消耗，「捕获文明效用」，并将残余耗散到无序的虚空中。
paragraphs.en: Read moreIn a philosophical twist that surely pleases Silicon Valley’s billionaires, effective accelerationists argue for rampant techno-capitalism, unhindered by regulation, government and other nuisances, because this would maximize the consumption of the universe’s resources, “capture civilizational utility”, and dissipate the residue into the disorganized void.

paragraphs.cn: 梦想的细节实际上并不太重要。因为它们都把我们带到大致相同的地方。现在重要的是，这些宇宙主宰者——投资于 harnessing 恒星能量、被一种道德计算所诱惑——该计算将当下人民的福祉置于价值低于未来数量远为庞大的人形生物的位置——是否有耐心关怀我们其余人。
paragraphs.en: The details of the dream don’t actually make much of a difference. Because they all take us roughly to the same place. What matters now is whether the masters of the universe – invested in harnessing the energy of the stars, tempted by a moral calculus that posits that the wellbeing of the people of the present is of inferior value to the vastly more numerous humanoids of the future – will have the patience to care for the rest of us.

paragraphs.cn: 迹象并不乐观。例如，硅谷风险投资家马克·安德烈森（Marc Andreessen）想要「确保技术资本上升螺旋永远持续」。他的敌人名单几乎囊括了任何可能反对技术事业的人或理念。其中包括「可持续性」、「社会责任」和「技术伦理」。
paragraphs.en: The signs are not great. Silicon Valley venture capitalist Marc Andreessen, for instance, wants to “ensure the techno-capital upward spiral continues forever”. His list of enemies encompasses pretty much any person or idea that might stand against technological endeavor. That includes “sustainability”, “social responsibility” and “tech ethics”.

paragraphs.cn: 如果你创造了上帝但你拥有上帝你就成了独裁者贾伦·拉尼尔（Jaron Lanier）蒂尔在这群人中不同寻常——他坚定地致力于一种独特的基督教变体，其中任何阻碍技术的人，或试图向他征税的政府，都表现为反基督。虽然他声称与安德烈森几乎没有亲和力，但他似乎有相似的口味。作为一个死硬的自由主义者，他对政府再分配嗤之以鼻。他的慈善事业是对推进技术进步项目的营利性投资。慈善，正如通常理解的那样，等于浪费技术人员超越我们当下所需的资源。马斯克曾称 empathy 是「西方文明的基本弱点」。
paragraphs.en: If you create God but you own God you become the dictatorJaron LanierThiel is unusual in this crowd in that he is fiercely committed to an idiosyncratic variant of Christianity in which anybody standing in the way of technology, or governments that try to tax him, show up as the antichrist. But though he claims little affinity with Andreesen, he seems to have similar tastes. A diehard libertarian, he is contemptuous of government redistribution. His philanthropy is about for-profit investments in projects to further technological progress. Charity, as commonly understood, amounts to wasting resources that technologists will need to transcend our present. Musk has called empathy “the fundamental weakness of western civilization”.

paragraphs.cn: 不管他们超人类梦想的具体特征如何，硅谷亿万富翁编织的叙事为他们的巨大权力积累提供了正当性。正如计算机科学先驱和技术远见者贾伦·拉尼尔告诉我的：「如果你创造了上帝但你拥有上帝你就成了独裁者。」而这些独裁者似乎不认为地球上的人类——至少我们中的大多数——特别有价值。二月份被问及AI消耗的大量能源时，奥特曼略带轻蔑地指出，「训练一个人类也需要大量能量。」
paragraphs.en: Regardless of the specific features of their transhuman dreams, the narrative crafted by Silicon Valley billionaires justifies their vast accumulation of power. As computer science pioneer and tech visionary Jaron Lanier told me: “If you create God but you own God you become the dictator.” And these dictators don’t seem to believe earthbound humans – most of us, at least – are particularly valuable. Questioned in February about the vast amounts of energy sucked up by AI, Altman noted, somewhat disparagingly, that “it also takes a lot of energy to train a human.”

paragraphs.cn: 然而他们承认不知道自己在做什么。「领域外的人常常惊讶和不安地得知，我们不理解自己的AI创造物是如何运作的，」Anthropic联合创始人达里奥·阿莫代伊（Dario Amodei）去年写道。「他们的担忧是对的：这种理解缺失在技术史上基本上是前所未有的。」阿莫代伊与有效利他主义有深厚联系；他的姐妹丹妮拉·阿莫代伊（Daniela Amodei），Anthropic的总裁，嫁给了该运动的一位创始人。不过最近，两人都已与该运动拉开了距离。
paragraphs.en: Yet they admittedly have no idea what they are doing. “People outside the field are often surprised and alarmed to learn that we do not understand how our own AI creations work,” Anthropic co-founder Dario Amodei wrote last year. “They are right to be concerned: this lack of understanding is essentially unprecedented in the history of technology.” Amodei has deep ties to effective altruism; his sister Daniela, Anthropic’s president, is married to a founder of the movement. Recently, though, they’ve both distanced themselves from it.

paragraphs.cn: 尤其令人忧虑的是，这些巨头在追逐他们计划用机器建造的未来乌托邦时是多么不受约束。科技亿万富翁正在向政治竞选投入数亿美元，以抵御监管尝试、逃避问责以防他们的事业出错。他们要确保在他们重塑社会的工作中没有人插手。而他们在很大程度上正在成功——目前为止，没有任何有能力阻止他们的人正在插手。
paragraphs.en: What’s particularly distressing is how unconstrained these moguls are, as they pursue the futuristic utopia they plan to build with their machines. Tech billionaires are plowing hundreds of millions into political campaigns, to fend off attempts at regulation and evade accountability lest their endeavors go awry. They want to make sure nobody butts in as they work to reshape society. And they are largely succeeding – for now, no one with the power to stop them is butting in.

paragraphs.cn: 社会应该如何干预？我们的政治体系是否提供了帮助将过程引导至亲社会方向的工具？超越技术对我们未来经济和社会格局的不确定影响，我们应该如何应对将这些建造拥有硅脑的超人类赛博格的努力的成果过度集中于少数人手中的问题？
paragraphs.en: How should society intervene? Does our political system provide the tools to help steer the process in a pro-social direction? Beyond the uncertain impact of technology on our future economic and social landscape, how should we address the narrow concentration of the fruits of these endeavors to build transhuman cyborgs with silicon brains?

paragraphs.cn: 特朗普政府迄今为止几乎没有表现出抵制技术寡头幻想的兴趣。但这不一定意味着硅谷寡头的技术统治项目是不可避免的。疑虑正在Maga基础中出现：弗吉尼亚乡村地区那些抵制数据中心吞噬电力和水供应的人们，警惕于声称诉诸技术色彩更高权威的世界主义精英的福音派基督徒。
paragraphs.en: The Trump administration has shown little interest so far in resisting the tech oligarch’s fantasy. But that doesn’t necessarily mean that the valley oligarchs’ project of techno-domination is inevitable. Misgivings are emerging among the Maga base: The folks in rural Virginia who push back against datacenters hogging power and water supplies, evangelicals wary of a cosmopolitan elite claiming recourse to a tech-inflected higher authority.

paragraphs.cn: AI项目的其他麻烦迹象正在酝酿——从大学毕业生向鼓吹AI的毕业典礼演讲者喝倒彩，到特朗普短暂关注Anthropic新模型Mythos的潜在犯罪能力，然后最终决定不监管这个东西。在5月初最新的Times-Siena民调中，认为AI主要是坏事的登记选民数量是认为它主要是好事的人的两倍多。
paragraphs.en: Other signs of trouble are brewing for the AI project – from college graduates booing commencement speakers who extol AI, to Trump’s brief moment of concern over the potential criminal capabilities of Anthropic’s new Mythos model before deciding not to regulate the thing after all. In the latest Times-Siena poll from earlier in May, more than twice as many registered voters said AI is mostly bad, compared with those saying it was mostly good.

paragraphs.cn: 或许最有力的人本立场来自圣父本人。周一，教皇利奥（Pope Leo）发布了教皇通谕《Magnifica Humanitas》，反击以牺牲就业和社会公平为代价不受约束地发展AI。「这创造了一种物质进步与人类学退行的悖论，动摇了公正稳定的社会和平的基础，」他补充道。
paragraphs.en: Perhaps the most forceful, pro-human position has come from the Holy Father himself. On Monday, Pope Leo published the encyclical Magnifica Humanitas, pushing back against the unfettered development of AI at the expense of jobs and social equity. “This creates a paradox of material progress and anthropological regression that undermines the foundations of a just and stable social peace,” he added.

paragraphs.cn: 那里有育儿室的废墟——正如费德里科·古兹曼·鲁比奥（Federico Guzmán Rubio）在其著作《有这样的地方》（There is Such a Place）中所写，福特对牛的厌恶意味着工人的孩子被引入从远处运来的豆奶。那里有学校的废墟，孩子们在那里被教导关于亨利·沃兹沃思·朗费罗（Henry Wadsworth Longfellow）。留下的遗迹证明了一个寡头团体不协调的梦想——它高估了自己的权力，将自己的胃口与更大利益混淆。
paragraphs.en: There are the ruins of nurseries, where as Federico Guzmán Rubio writes in his book There is Such a Place, Ford’s aversion to cows meant the children of workers were introduced to soy milk, shipped in from miles away. There are the ruins of schools where kids were taught about Henry Wadsworth Longfellow. What’s left is testament to the incongruous dreams of an oligarchy that overvalued its power and confused its appetites with the greater good.

paragraphs.cn: 阅读更多AI驱动的宇宙幻想同样疯狂。暂且不论将人类意识以数字形式呈现、与AI融合并穿越银河系传输的部分。那个表面上更接地气的主张——有意识的AI不仅可能而且即将到来——与我们自己对意识是什么的脆弱理解存在根本矛盾。甚至更平凡的目标，比如让人工智能自我训练，也在不断被推入事件视界。
paragraphs.en: Read moreThe AI-fueled cosmic fantasy is no less nuts. Forget the part where human consciousness is rendered in digital form, merged with AI and beamed across the galaxy. The ostensibly more down-to-earth proposition that conscious AI is not just possible but around the corner is in fundamental tension with our tenuous grasp of what consciousness is. Even more mundane objectives, such as getting artificial intelligence to train itself, keep getting pushed forward into the event horizon.

paragraphs.cn: 也许这一次，这些离奇的声称也将消退为无关紧要；《星际迷航》（Star Trek）中人被非物质化并在银河系上下传输的愿景将衰变为一堆锈迹斑斑的废墟。也许超人类项目会让位于一个多少可以辨认的人类未来——附带一些酷炫的新AI插件。也许它甚至能以一种服务于我们久被遗忘的公平繁荣梦想的方式实现。
paragraphs.en: Perhaps this time too the outlandish claims will fade into irrelevance; the Star-Trek vision of people being dematerialized and beamed up and down around the galaxy will decay into some rustbound heap. Maybe the transhuman project will give way to a more or less recognizably human future with some cool new AI plugins. Maybe it can even be achieved in a way that serves our long-forgotten dream of equitable prosperity.

paragraphs.cn: 不过到目前为止，我们的技术远见者正在推动别的东西——一个以巨额财富和权力集中为标志的未来，对芸芸众生的平凡抱负漠不关心。万一它成功将佩奇、马斯克及其同类的基本本质装载到硅躯体中前往「无人曾至之处」，我们只能希望他们在这一过程中不要摧毁我们所知的世界。
paragraphs.en: So far, though, our technological visionaries are pushing for something else, a future marked by vast concentrations of wealth and power, indifferent to the humdrum aspirations of the unwashed many. In the unlikely event that it succeeds in taking the essence of Page, Musk and their ilk aboard a silicon body to “where no man has gone before”, here’s hoping that they don’t destroy the world we know in the process.

articles.title: 阿兹特克人可以教给我们的十课
articles.author: Sebastian Purcell
articles.summary: 你不需要在整顿生活之前先解决灵魂的问题。事实上，外在的道路或许正是通往内心平静的途径。
articles.content_cn:
你不需要在整顿生活之前先解决灵魂的问题。事实上，外在的道路或许正是通往内心平静的途径。

古代阿兹特克人（Aztecs）通常不被归入当今自助导师的行列。但他们的哲学——保存在早期后征服时代的记录中——为现代生活提供了出奇敏锐的工具。与斯多葛主义（stoicism）或佛教不同，后者强调内在反思是通向更好生活的路径，阿兹特克人认为你应该从你的周遭环境、人际关系、身体和言辞开始。在他们看来，智慧始于外部。以下是来自他们「外在道路」的10课，从那些澄清人生目标的开始。

对幸福的追求被写入美国《独立宣言》（Declaration of Independence）。亚里士多德（Aristotle）在两千多年前就撰写了大量关于幸福作为我们生命首要目标的论述。虽然这是我们文化中的常见概念，阿兹特克人采取了更现实的立场。「幸福」——当它不是什么偏离了我们寻常含义的复杂概念时——是转瞬即逝的，往往紧随其后的是其对立面：痛苦或至少是疲惫。

这意味着「幸福」不是人生的合适目标，尽管它乍看之下似乎合理。你真正想要的是更丰富的东西，他们将之比拟为扎根感：在身体、心智、社会和自然中稳稳扎根。我们毕竟会为朋友和孩子做出牺牲，并认为我们的生活因此而更好。这正是阿兹特克人的观点。

第二个想法——在斯多葛主义和佛教中有所体现——是你追求的是一种不可摧毁的生活。这种观念认为，如果你是一个好人，你生活中重要的一切都不会受生活不可预测事件的影响，甚至不受悲剧影响。

阿兹特克人不会同意。生命中最好的东西——如爱、正直和正义——也让你暴露在痛苦之下。埃米利亚诺·萨帕塔（Emiliano Zapata），墨西哥的人民革命家，精通纳瓦特尔语（Nahuatl）并忠诚于他的人民，因为拒绝背叛自己的价值观而英年早逝。阿兹特克伦理拥抱这种张力：意义源于涉及风险的选择。一个扎根深厚的生活接受心碎作为意义代价的一部分。

人们很容易认为，只要足够聪明，你就会拥有所有答案。我们倾向于尊崇那种比众人更懂的「独狼」式个体。但对阿兹特克人来说，如果你生活在一个由朋友和家人组成的健康社群中，你不应该需要「独自行动」。理想情况下，好的思考是在好的群体中完成的。

阿兹特克人举行有结构的群体审议，即使年轻人也有发言权，尽管经验具有分量。他们会建议你建立自己的「决策圈」，与那些既能挑战你又能支持你的人一起审视你的目标。如果你在独自思考，你很可能没有在最佳状态下思考。

殖民时期阿兹特克英雄主义的故事不胜枚举。例如，事实证明科尔特斯（Cortés）与一位原住民女性生了一个儿子，名叫马丁（Martín）。尽管马丁理应受到善待，在他那位（臭名昭著的）父亲去世一段时间后，他失去了政治庇护。当地当局抓获了他，强迫他忍受酷刑以逼迫虚假供认。马丁从未屈服。

虽然这种忍耐的壮举部分源于一个人的先天性格，马丁很可能学到了一些阿兹特克人通过反复的小磨练来灌输勇气的方式。他们不以安逸为优化目标。他们教孩子黎明前扫地，搬运沉重的木头，熬夜。但在这些许多小壮举中，他们也教他们如何在工作时唱歌，如何管理自己的心态。勇气从小处开始，逐渐壮大。

我们生活在一个处于他人持续注视下的世界。然而，如果你想活出自己的人生，而不是「他们」告诉你应该过的生活，你将必须学会忽略「他们」。同样，如果你想活得很好，保全自己自我价值的价值，那你需要学会什么才是真正有价值的。有一位父亲被记录下来——他自豪地讲述自己从事卑微艰辛的劳动来养育儿子，从未偷取哪怕一粒粮食。

你可以通过策略性的脆弱来培养这项技能。尝试做一些稍微令人尴尬的事。在尴尬时说出真相。让你的社交面具滑落。这就是你可以尝试与「他们」的目光拉开距离的方式。

我在研究生院注意到一个悖论：我可以毫无问题地投入数小时枯燥的学习，但如果有人在我面前放一块饼干，我就会在节食目标上崩溃。阿兹特克人采取了一种解决这个悖论的方法。意志力有三种形式：

不同的挑战需要不同的工具。冲进被水淹没的地下室与抵制深夜蛋糕不同。你需要训练这三种。

持续的行动催生更多持续的行动。阿兹特克学生每天日出前扫地并保持房间整洁。今天，这可能意味着每天花15分钟学习一门外语或整理床铺。无论是什么，将你的新努力挂钩到现有习惯上，以建立更多持续的行动。

阿兹特克人斋戒不是为了羞辱身体，而是为了训练它。斋戒与盛宴相伴，用于练习纪律——那种对抗诱惑的意志力。目标是更高层次地觉察自己的反应。例如，你可能会注意到饥饿是波浪式的，而非无限递增。渴望，如同情绪一样，如果你知道预期什么以及为何忍耐，就可以被撑过去。

阿兹特克人强调「正言」（right speech）作为将外在习惯与内在价值对齐的方式。话语一旦说出，就会将你的心智推入特定的思维框架。因此他们训练孩子审慎、真实、谦逊地说话，避免八卦。现代心理学家如罗伯特·西奥迪尼（Robert Cialdini）也得出类似结论。你说出口的话微妙地重塑你的思维方式。所以要小心：你的话语传达思想，也校准你的期望。

阿兹特克人相信智慧不是始于内省，而是始于习惯、仪式和环境。清理你的空间。谨慎言说。有意识地进食。建立训练你的身体并调谐你的心智的习惯。当你这样做时，你的内在世界就会趋于对齐。

你不需要在整顿生活之前先解决灵魂的问题。事实上，外在的道路或许正是通往内心平静的途径。
articles.content_en:
You don’t need to solve your soul before setting your house in order. In fact, the outer path might just be the way to reach your inner peace

The ancient Aztecs aren’t usually grouped with today’s self-help gurus. But their philosophy, preserved in early post-conquest records, offers surprisingly sharp tools for modern life. Unlike stoicism or Buddhism, which emphasize internal reflection as the path to a better life, the Aztecs believed that you should start with your surroundings, your relationships, your body and speech. In their view, wisdom begins outside. Here are 10 lessons from their “outward path”, starting with those that clarify life goals.

The pursuit of happiness is written into the US Declaration of Independence. Aristotle wrote volumes about its role as the chief aim of our life more than 2,000 years before that. While it’s a staple notion in our culture, the Aztecs took a more realistic approach. “Happiness”, when it’s not some complicated idea that’s drifted from our ordinary meaning, is fleeting and tends to be followed by its opposite: pain or at least fatigue.

That means “happiness” isn’t a suitable goal in life, though it at first looks plausible. What you truly want is something richer, and they likened it to rootedness: being firmly grounded in your body, mind, society and nature. We make sacrifices for our friends and our children, after all, and we think our lives are better for it. That’s exactly the Aztec point.

A second idea, which finds some expression in stoicism and Buddhism, is that you’re after a life that is invulnerable. It’s the notion that if you’re a good person, none of the things that matter in your life can be affected by life’s unpredictable events, even by tragedies.

The Aztecs wouldn’t agree. The best things in life, such as love, integrity and justice, also expose you to pain. Emiliano Zapata, the people’s revolutionary in Mexico who was fluent in Nahuatl and loyal to his people, died young because he refused to betray his values. Aztec ethics embrace this tension: that meaning arises from choices that involve risk. A well-rooted life accepts heartbreak as part of the price of significance.

It’s tempting to think that if you were just smart enough, you’d have all the answers. We tend to valorize the “lone wolf” individual who knows better than the crowd. But for the Aztecs, you shouldn’t need to “go it alone” if you live in a healthy community of friends and family. Ideally, good thinking is done in good groups.

The Aztecs held structured group deliberations, where even the young had a voice, though experience carried weight. They would advise that you could build your own “decision circle” and vet your goals with people who challenge and support you. If you’re thinking alone, you’re probably not thinking at your best.

The stories of Aztec heroism during the colonial period are legion. For example, it turns out that Cortés had a son, named Martín, with a Native woman. And though Martín should have been treated well, he was left bereft of political protection some time after his (in)famous father died. Local authorities captured him and forced him to endure brutal torture in an attempt to provoke a false confession. Martín never gave in.

While such feats of endurance are partly grounded in a person’s innate personality, Martín may well have learned some of the ways the Aztecs instilled courage through repeated small hardships. They didn’t optimize for ease. They taught their children to sweep before dawn, to carry heavy logs, and to stay up late. But in these many small feats, they also taught them how to sing while they worked and to manage their outlook. Courage starts small and grows strong.

We live in a world under the constant gaze of others. Yet, if you want to live your life, and not the life “they” tell you to lead, you will have to learn to ignore “them”. Similarly, if you want to live well, to preserve the value of your own self-worth, then you need to learn what is of real value. One father is documented as he proudly recounts doing humble, hard work to raise his son, never stealing even a grain.

You can build this skill through strategic vulnerability. Try doing something mildly embarrassing. Speak the truth when it’s awkward. Let your social mask slip. That’s how you can try to gain some distance from “their” gaze.

A paradox I noticed in graduate school was that I had no problem putting in hours of tedious study, but I would cave on my dieting goals if someone put a cookie in front of me. The Aztecs took an approach that solves this paradox. Willpower comes in three forms:

You need different tools for different challenges. Running into a flooded basement is not the same as resisting late-night cake. You need to train all three.

Consistent action begets more consistent action. Aztec students swept daily before sunrise and kept their rooms clean. Today, it might be spending 15 minutes each day on a foreign language or making your bed. Whatever it is, hook your new effort to an existing habit to build yet more consistent actions.

The Aztecs fasted not to shame their bodies but to train them. Fasting was paired with feasting and used to practice discipline, the kind of willpower that opposes temptation. The goal was a higher-level awareness of your reactions. For example, you might notice that hunger comes in waves, rather than building infinitely. Craving, like emotion, can be ridden out if you know what to expect and why you endure.

The Aztecs emphasized “right speech” as a way of aligning outer habits with inner values. Words, once spoken, nudge your mind into specific frames of thought. So they trained children to speak deliberately, truthfully, humbly, and to avoid gossip. Modern psychologists like Robert Cialdini have come to similar conclusions. What you say out loud subtly rewires how you think. So be careful: your words communicate thoughts and calibrate your expectations.

The Aztecs believed wisdom starts not with introspection but with habit, ritual and environment. Clean your space. Speak with care. Eat with intention. Build habits that train your body and attune your mind. As you do, your inner world comes into alignment.

You don’t need to solve your soul before setting your house in order. In fact, the outer path might just be the way to reach your inner peace.

paragraphs.cn: 你不需要在整顿生活之前先解决灵魂的问题。事实上，外在的道路或许正是通往内心平静的途径。
paragraphs.en: You don’t need to solve your soul before setting your house in order. In fact, the outer path might just be the way to reach your inner peace

paragraphs.cn: 古代阿兹特克人（Aztecs）通常不被归入当今自助导师的行列。但他们的哲学——保存在早期后征服时代的记录中——为现代生活提供了出奇敏锐的工具。与斯多葛主义（stoicism）或佛教不同，后者强调内在反思是通向更好生活的路径，阿兹特克人认为你应该从你的周遭环境、人际关系、身体和言辞开始。在他们看来，智慧始于外部。以下是来自他们「外在道路」的10课，从那些澄清人生目标的开始。
paragraphs.en: The ancient Aztecs aren’t usually grouped with today’s self-help gurus. But their philosophy, preserved in early post-conquest records, offers surprisingly sharp tools for modern life. Unlike stoicism or Buddhism, which emphasize internal reflection as the path to a better life, the Aztecs believed that you should start with your surroundings, your relationships, your body and speech. In their view, wisdom begins outside. Here are 10 lessons from their “outward path”, starting with those that clarify life goals.

paragraphs.cn: 对幸福的追求被写入美国《独立宣言》（Declaration of Independence）。亚里士多德（Aristotle）在两千多年前就撰写了大量关于幸福作为我们生命首要目标的论述。虽然这是我们文化中的常见概念，阿兹特克人采取了更现实的立场。「幸福」——当它不是什么偏离了我们寻常含义的复杂概念时——是转瞬即逝的，往往紧随其后的是其对立面：痛苦或至少是疲惫。
paragraphs.en: The pursuit of happiness is written into the US Declaration of Independence. Aristotle wrote volumes about its role as the chief aim of our life more than 2,000 years before that. While it’s a staple notion in our culture, the Aztecs took a more realistic approach. “Happiness”, when it’s not some complicated idea that’s drifted from our ordinary meaning, is fleeting and tends to be followed by its opposite: pain or at least fatigue.

paragraphs.cn: 这意味着「幸福」不是人生的合适目标，尽管它乍看之下似乎合理。你真正想要的是更丰富的东西，他们将之比拟为扎根感：在身体、心智、社会和自然中稳稳扎根。我们毕竟会为朋友和孩子做出牺牲，并认为我们的生活因此而更好。这正是阿兹特克人的观点。
paragraphs.en: That means “happiness” isn’t a suitable goal in life, though it at first looks plausible. What you truly want is something richer, and they likened it to rootedness: being firmly grounded in your body, mind, society and nature. We make sacrifices for our friends and our children, after all, and we think our lives are better for it. That’s exactly the Aztec point.

paragraphs.cn: 第二个想法——在斯多葛主义和佛教中有所体现——是你追求的是一种不可摧毁的生活。这种观念认为，如果你是一个好人，你生活中重要的一切都不会受生活不可预测事件的影响，甚至不受悲剧影响。
paragraphs.en: A second idea, which finds some expression in stoicism and Buddhism, is that you’re after a life that is invulnerable. It’s the notion that if you’re a good person, none of the things that matter in your life can be affected by life’s unpredictable events, even by tragedies.

paragraphs.cn: 阿兹特克人不会同意。生命中最好的东西——如爱、正直和正义——也让你暴露在痛苦之下。埃米利亚诺·萨帕塔（Emiliano Zapata），墨西哥的人民革命家，精通纳瓦特尔语（Nahuatl）并忠诚于他的人民，因为拒绝背叛自己的价值观而英年早逝。阿兹特克伦理拥抱这种张力：意义源于涉及风险的选择。一个扎根深厚的生活接受心碎作为意义代价的一部分。
paragraphs.en: The Aztecs wouldn’t agree. The best things in life, such as love, integrity and justice, also expose you to pain. Emiliano Zapata, the people’s revolutionary in Mexico who was fluent in Nahuatl and loyal to his people, died young because he refused to betray his values. Aztec ethics embrace this tension: that meaning arises from choices that involve risk. A well-rooted life accepts heartbreak as part of the price of significance.

paragraphs.cn: 人们很容易认为，只要足够聪明，你就会拥有所有答案。我们倾向于尊崇那种比众人更懂的「独狼」式个体。但对阿兹特克人来说，如果你生活在一个由朋友和家人组成的健康社群中，你不应该需要「独自行动」。理想情况下，好的思考是在好的群体中完成的。
paragraphs.en: It’s tempting to think that if you were just smart enough, you’d have all the answers. We tend to valorize the “lone wolf” individual who knows better than the crowd. But for the Aztecs, you shouldn’t need to “go it alone” if you live in a healthy community of friends and family. Ideally, good thinking is done in good groups.

paragraphs.cn: 阿兹特克人举行有结构的群体审议，即使年轻人也有发言权，尽管经验具有分量。他们会建议你建立自己的「决策圈」，与那些既能挑战你又能支持你的人一起审视你的目标。如果你在独自思考，你很可能没有在最佳状态下思考。
paragraphs.en: The Aztecs held structured group deliberations, where even the young had a voice, though experience carried weight. They would advise that you could build your own “decision circle” and vet your goals with people who challenge and support you. If you’re thinking alone, you’re probably not thinking at your best.

paragraphs.cn: 殖民时期阿兹特克英雄主义的故事不胜枚举。例如，事实证明科尔特斯（Cortés）与一位原住民女性生了一个儿子，名叫马丁（Martín）。尽管马丁理应受到善待，在他那位（臭名昭著的）父亲去世一段时间后，他失去了政治庇护。当地当局抓获了他，强迫他忍受酷刑以逼迫虚假供认。马丁从未屈服。
paragraphs.en: The stories of Aztec heroism during the colonial period are legion. For example, it turns out that Cortés had a son, named Martín, with a Native woman. And though Martín should have been treated well, he was left bereft of political protection some time after his (in)famous father died. Local authorities captured him and forced him to endure brutal torture in an attempt to provoke a false confession. Martín never gave in.

paragraphs.cn: 虽然这种忍耐的壮举部分源于一个人的先天性格，马丁很可能学到了一些阿兹特克人通过反复的小磨练来灌输勇气的方式。他们不以安逸为优化目标。他们教孩子黎明前扫地，搬运沉重的木头，熬夜。但在这些许多小壮举中，他们也教他们如何在工作时唱歌，如何管理自己的心态。勇气从小处开始，逐渐壮大。
paragraphs.en: While such feats of endurance are partly grounded in a person’s innate personality, Martín may well have learned some of the ways the Aztecs instilled courage through repeated small hardships. They didn’t optimize for ease. They taught their children to sweep before dawn, to carry heavy logs, and to stay up late. But in these many small feats, they also taught them how to sing while they worked and to manage their outlook. Courage starts small and grows strong.

paragraphs.cn: 我们生活在一个处于他人持续注视下的世界。然而，如果你想活出自己的人生，而不是「他们」告诉你应该过的生活，你将必须学会忽略「他们」。同样，如果你想活得很好，保全自己自我价值的价值，那你需要学会什么才是真正有价值的。有一位父亲被记录下来——他自豪地讲述自己从事卑微艰辛的劳动来养育儿子，从未偷取哪怕一粒粮食。
paragraphs.en: We live in a world under the constant gaze of others. Yet, if you want to live your life, and not the life “they” tell you to lead, you will have to learn to ignore “them”. Similarly, if you want to live well, to preserve the value of your own self-worth, then you need to learn what is of real value. One father is documented as he proudly recounts doing humble, hard work to raise his son, never stealing even a grain.

paragraphs.cn: 你可以通过策略性的脆弱来培养这项技能。尝试做一些稍微令人尴尬的事。在尴尬时说出真相。让你的社交面具滑落。这就是你可以尝试与「他们」的目光拉开距离的方式。
paragraphs.en: You can build this skill through strategic vulnerability. Try doing something mildly embarrassing. Speak the truth when it’s awkward. Let your social mask slip. That’s how you can try to gain some distance from “their” gaze.

paragraphs.cn: 我在研究生院注意到一个悖论：我可以毫无问题地投入数小时枯燥的学习，但如果有人在我面前放一块饼干，我就会在节食目标上崩溃。阿兹特克人采取了一种解决这个悖论的方法。意志力有三种形式：
paragraphs.en: A paradox I noticed in graduate school was that I had no problem putting in hours of tedious study, but I would cave on my dieting goals if someone put a cookie in front of me. The Aztecs took an approach that solves this paradox. Willpower comes in three forms:

paragraphs.cn: 不同的挑战需要不同的工具。冲进被水淹没的地下室与抵制深夜蛋糕不同。你需要训练这三种。
paragraphs.en: You need different tools for different challenges. Running into a flooded basement is not the same as resisting late-night cake. You need to train all three.

paragraphs.cn: 持续的行动催生更多持续的行动。阿兹特克学生每天日出前扫地并保持房间整洁。今天，这可能意味着每天花15分钟学习一门外语或整理床铺。无论是什么，将你的新努力挂钩到现有习惯上，以建立更多持续的行动。
paragraphs.en: Consistent action begets more consistent action. Aztec students swept daily before sunrise and kept their rooms clean. Today, it might be spending 15 minutes each day on a foreign language or making your bed. Whatever it is, hook your new effort to an existing habit to build yet more consistent actions.

paragraphs.cn: 阿兹特克人斋戒不是为了羞辱身体，而是为了训练它。斋戒与盛宴相伴，用于练习纪律——那种对抗诱惑的意志力。目标是更高层次地觉察自己的反应。例如，你可能会注意到饥饿是波浪式的，而非无限递增。渴望，如同情绪一样，如果你知道预期什么以及为何忍耐，就可以被撑过去。
paragraphs.en: The Aztecs fasted not to shame their bodies but to train them. Fasting was paired with feasting and used to practice discipline, the kind of willpower that opposes temptation. The goal was a higher-level awareness of your reactions. For example, you might notice that hunger comes in waves, rather than building infinitely. Craving, like emotion, can be ridden out if you know what to expect and why you endure.

paragraphs.cn: 阿兹特克人强调「正言」（right speech）作为将外在习惯与内在价值对齐的方式。话语一旦说出，就会将你的心智推入特定的思维框架。因此他们训练孩子审慎、真实、谦逊地说话，避免八卦。现代心理学家如罗伯特·西奥迪尼（Robert Cialdini）也得出类似结论。你说出口的话微妙地重塑你的思维方式。所以要小心：你的话语传达思想，也校准你的期望。
paragraphs.en: The Aztecs emphasized “right speech” as a way of aligning outer habits with inner values. Words, once spoken, nudge your mind into specific frames of thought. So they trained children to speak deliberately, truthfully, humbly, and to avoid gossip. Modern psychologists like Robert Cialdini have come to similar conclusions. What you say out loud subtly rewires how you think. So be careful: your words communicate thoughts and calibrate your expectations.

paragraphs.cn: 阿兹特克人相信智慧不是始于内省，而是始于习惯、仪式和环境。清理你的空间。谨慎言说。有意识地进食。建立训练你的身体并调谐你的心智的习惯。当你这样做时，你的内在世界就会趋于对齐。
paragraphs.en: The Aztecs believed wisdom starts not with introspection but with habit, ritual and environment. Clean your space. Speak with care. Eat with intention. Build habits that train your body and attune your mind. As you do, your inner world comes into alignment.
