articles.title: 为何古希腊美德「节制」在AI时代比以往任何时候都更重要
articles.author: Ross Channing Reed
articles.summary: 这看起来像是21世纪恶行的一份随机清单。但我认为，它们都是同一种美德丧失的体现：「节制」（sophrosyne）。
articles.content_cn:
开车时发短信。在社交媒体上欺凌他人。轻信最新的阴谋论。将AI生成的内容当作自己的成果。

这看起来像是21世纪恶行的一份随机清单。但我认为，它们都是同一种美德丧失的体现：「节制」（sophrosyne）。

古希腊概念「节制」——发音为「suh-fros-uh-nee」——就是我们今天可能称之为「健全心智」的东西。它是一组特质的集合，包括适度、反思性和自知。这些特质存在于那种能够尊重和信任自己、并能被他人尊重和信任的人身上。

作为一名哲学家和哲学咨询师，我研究美德与幸福之间的联系。特别地，我注意到「节制」与「幸福论」（eudaimonia）之间的关联——这是希腊哲学中关于幸福或善好的生活的概念。

对希腊人而言，「节制」代表了品格的卓越、适度与自制。它与「实践智慧」（phronesis）相连，与「傲慢」（hubris）形成鲜明对比：后者是过度的骄傲、危险的自信和缺乏自知。生活在公元前500年左右的哲学家赫拉克利特（Heraclitus）教导说，「节制」是最重要的美德。

一个世纪后教学的柏拉图（Plato），将「节制」探讨为认识自我的能力——以及认识到自己不知道某些事物的能力。在《理想国》（Republic）中，他将「节制」比作灵魂三个部分之间的和谐或友谊：理性、激情和身体欲望。

柏拉图的学生亚里士多德（Aristotle）认为，「节制」使人能在自我放纵与自我克制之间取得平衡——就像一个人试图获得适量的体育锻炼，既不过多也不过少。亚里士多德教导说，这是一种通过实践培养的美德，就像训练一项运动或学习演奏一种乐器一样。

简言之，健全心智并非天生，而是必须习得。

我相信「节制」仍然是善好生活——「幸福论」的生活——所必需的，即幸福与人的繁荣。它不是一种转瞬即逝的感觉，而是成为最好的自己的感受。这涉及一种不可能在没有自知和自制的情况下获得的满足感。

更重要的是，它需要辨别好坏、真假的能力——这些能力并非天生，而是通过持续的练习习得的。没有「节制」，也许不可能辨别什么对自己或他人是好的。即便你能辨别，没有「节制」，你也可能缺乏践行的意志。

如果说有什么变化的话，随着人工智能和社交媒体的兴起，这些品质可能变得更加重要。在我的咨询实践中，我与像「布莱恩」（Brian）这样的人合作——他是一个理想主义者，希望真理和正义战胜邪恶与压迫。

问题是他不知道如何审查信息来源。在新冠疫情肆虐期间，布莱恩陷入了阴谋论的深渊。他确信飞机尾迹中留下的凝结物是「化学轨迹」（chemtrails）——一种政府洗脑阴谋——并对「新世界秩序」怒不可遏。自以为无所不知，他不再愿意进行理性对话。

但如果布莱恩是「节制」丧失的例子，我合作过的另一个人「李」（Lee）则展示了我们如何培养它。李在社交媒体上花了相当多的时间，但她开始思考这如何影响她。她放慢节奏，增加休息时间，开始更加关注自己的心理活动和感受。

随着李变得更加自知，她意识到自己在浪费时间。她不再与最初使用社交媒体的理由相连。「消费社交媒体让我感到不安。就像暴食垃圾食品一样，」她告诉我。「现在我用以前花在社交媒体上的时间读更多的书、做饭和散步。」

对希腊人而言，「节制」是无与伦比的理想。然而在1960年代，柏拉图学者伊迪丝·汉密尔顿（Edith Hamilton）和亨廷顿·凯恩斯（Huntington Cairns）感叹它已不再「属于我们的理想」。这在今天似乎更加真实——更广泛的后果显而易见。

首先是21世纪各种形式的不文明行为的增加——从路怒到网络欺凌。在疫情的隔离之后，甚至出现了一个描述普遍社会不文明行为的新术语：「社交时差」（social jet lag）。

「节制」的衰退还可能导致屏幕成瘾、注意力持续时间缩短和专注力下降——这些因素反过来又会削弱文明行为。文明行为需要对自己和他人保持持续的觉察。

后果不仅波及我们的朋友、家人和同事，还延伸到民主本身。如果健全心智受损，过度的骄傲和自信会损害我们进行理性对话和尊重他人差异的能力。

我认为，有诸多因素导致了「节制」的丧失，包括教育经费减少、更多应试教学，以及更大的经济不平等——后者使人们用于个人发展之类的事物的时间和精力更少。

另一个因素是导师关系的衰退，古希腊人认为这对智识和道德发展至关重要。真正的导师关系既包括指导，也包括以身作则。它关乎品格，而非以财富和地位定义的成功。今天，导师似乎很大程度上已被名人和英雄文化取代，富人和名人被奉为值得效仿的榜样。

我相信恢复「节制」的第一步是认识到它在善好生活中的重要性。第二步是承认它的衰退。第三步是理解导致这种衰退的因素。

节制、适度、自制、辨别力——这些品质加起来构成了一种无法伪装的永恒品格卓越。成为这样的人需要指导、实践和一贯性。
articles.content_en:
Texting while driving. Bullying people on social media. Buying into the latest conspiracy theory. Passing off AI-generated work as your own.

That may seem like a random list of 21st-century vices. But I'd argue they're all examples of the loss of one particular virtue: sophrosyne.

An ancient Greek concept, sophrosyne – pronounced "suh-fros-uh-nee" – is what we might call "sound-mindedness" today. It's a constellation of characteristics, including moderation, reflectiveness and self-knowledge. They're found in the kind of person who can respect and trust herself, and be respected and trusted by others.

As a philosopher and philosophical counselor, I research the connection between virtue and happiness. In particular, I've noticed a connection between sophrosyne and eudaimonia, the Greek philosophical concept for happiness, or living well.

For the Greeks, sophrosyne represented excellence of character, moderation and self-control. It was connected to phronesis, or practical wisdom, and stood in marked contrast with hubris: excessive pride, dangerous overconfidence and lack of self-insight. Heraclitus, a philosopher who lived around 500 B.C.E., taught that sophrosyne was the most important virtue of all.

Plato, who taught a century later, discussed sophrosyne as the ability to know oneself – and to know when you don't know something. In "Republic," he likened sophrosyne to a harmony or friendship between the three parts of the soul: reason, spirit and bodily desires.

Plato's student Aristotle argued that sophrosyne allows people to strike a balance between self-indulgence and self-denial – like someone who tries to get the right amount of physical exercise, neither too much nor too little. Aristotle taught that it was a virtue developed through practice, just like training for a sport or learning to play a musical instrument.

Sound-mindedness, in short, is not inborn but must be learned.

I believe sophrosyne is still essential for the good life, the life of eudaimonia – happiness and human flourishing. It's not a transitory feeling, but a sense of being your best self. This involves a kind of satisfaction that is not possible without self-knowledge and self-control.

What's more, it requires the ability to discriminate between the good and the bad, the true and the false – capacities that are not inborn, but learned through steady practice. Without sophrosyne, it may not be possible to discern what is good for yourself or others. And even if you could, without sophrosyne you might lack the will to follow through.

If anything, these qualities might be even more important with the rise of artificial intelligence and social media. In my counseling practice, I've worked with people like "Brian," an idealist who wanted truth and justice to win out over evil and oppression.

The problem was that he didn't know how to vet his sources. As the COVID-19 pandemic raged, Brian fell down a conspiracy theory rabbit hole. He was certain that the condensation left in airplanes' wake were "chemtrails," a government brainwashing plot, and fumed against the "New World Order." Thinking he knew it all, he was no longer open to reasoned dialogue.

But if Brian is an example of the loss of sophrosyne, another person I worked with, "Lee," shows how we can develop it. Lee spent quite a bit of time on social media, but she began to wonder how it was affecting her. She slowed down, took more breaks and started paying more attention to what her mind was doing and to how she was feeling.

As Lee became more self-aware, she realized she was wasting her time. She no longer connected to the reasons she had used social media in the first place. "Consuming social media was making me uneasy. It was like pigging out on junk food," she told me. "Now I read more books, prepare food and walk during the time I had been spending on social media."

For the Greeks, sophrosyne was an ideal second to none. In the 1960s, though, Plato scholars Edith Hamilton and Huntington Cairns lamented that it was no longer "among our ideals." That seems all the more true today – and the wider consequences are easy to see.

First, there's the increase in incivility, in all its 21st-century forms – from road rage to cyberbullying. After the isolation of the pandemic, there's even a new term for general social incivility: "social jet lag."

The decline of sophrosyne can also lead to screen addiction, diminished attention span and ability to focus – factors that can, in turn, undermine civility. Civility takes sustained awareness of oneself and others.

The consequences go beyond our friends, families and co-workers to democracy itself. If sound-mindedness suffers, excessive pride and overconfidence hurt our ability to engage in reasoned dialogue and to respect other people's differences.

There are a number of factors, I'd argue, that have led to the loss of sophrosyne, including a decrease in funding for education, more teaching to the test and greater economic inequality, which leaves less time and energy for things like personal development.

Another is the decline of mentoring relationships, which the ancient Greeks considered central to intellectual and moral development. A true mentoring relationship involves both instruction and leading by example. It's about character, not success defined by wealth and status. Today, it appears that mentors have largely been replaced by celebrities and hero culture, with the rich and famous held up as examples worthy of emulation.

I believe the first step toward recovering sophrosyne is to recognize its importance in the good life. The second is to acknowledge its decline. The third is to understand the factors that have led to this decline.

Temperance, moderation, self-control, discernment – qualities such as these add up to a timeless excellence of character that cannot be faked. Becoming such a person requires guidance, practice and consistency.

articles.title: 周五随笔：哲学为何忽视了母职？
articles.author: Laura D'Olimpio
articles.summary: 从目睹这些育儿失败中——例如需要爱、保持亲近、防范天敌以及在危险时做出回应——我学到的关于母职的东西，超过了我多年作为专业哲学家的所有经历中所遇到的。当然，我在伦理课上讲授过关于堕胎的正反论证，也在生物伦理课上讲授过孕期管理和母亲自主权，但这些议题与母职本身几乎无关。
articles.content_cn:
许多个季节里，我观察着一对斑嘴鹬（masked lapwings）在我家附近的一片天然湿地孵化幼鸟。大自然并未赋予这些父母照料幼崽的本能。我的鹬邻会将毛茸茸的幼鸟带到开阔处，当喧闹的噪蜜鸟（miner birds）逼近时便飞走。几周大的幼鸟被留下独自抵御凶猛的俯冲攻击。

每天走在湿地边，我怀着沉重的心情计数幼鸟：一天有四只，次日只剩两只，一周后一只不剩。

2023年，第一窝鹬幼鸟存活到了少年期，我把这个消息告诉了所有认识的人。

从目睹这些育儿失败中——例如需要爱、保持亲近、防范天敌以及在危险时做出回应——我学到的关于母职的东西，超过了我多年作为专业哲学家的所有经历中所遇到的。当然，我在伦理课上讲授过关于堕胎的正反论证，也在生物伦理课上讲授过孕期管理和母亲自主权，但这些议题与母职本身几乎无关。

其中一个原因在于，直到我为自己准备迎接一个孩子之前，母职从未作为个人或哲学问题对我显得重要。更重要的原因是，在我作为学生和后来作为学者参加的众多课程和研讨会中，母职——以及孕母身体——很少呈现为一个可供探索的哲学议题。

然而在一个传统中，生命与健康激发了深刻的哲学反思——我所想到的是帕斯卡（Pascal）的偏头痛和尼采（Nietzsche）的精神崩溃——灵魂与身体撕裂的分娩事件怎么可能成为哲学中未被触及的课题？

自古代以来，女性撰写了哲学文本并讨论了哲学议题。但经过长达数世纪的抹除过程，她们的哲学关切和对学科的贡献被忽视，继而遗忘。

从亚里士多德（Aristotle）的时代起，女性被视为次于男性。在哲学中，理性的规范、哲学探究的性质和研究的议题也是通过对立于任何女性特质来定义的。

因此，关于孕期和产后母职期间发生的深刻心理、情感和身份转变的书写，在学科中大多被边缘化，也就不足为奇了。

然而，一些杰出的女性克服了厌女的认知和学科障碍，产出了被认可为哲学的作品，其中一些触及了母职经验。

对于达玛丽斯·马沙姆女爵（Lady Damaris Masham）——17世纪中期在剑桥的柏拉图主义者圈中成长——母职是道德和政治哲学的重要议题。

马沙姆认为，女性的教育及其理性能力的发展是履行母职道德责任的关键。只有通过接受良好的教育，女性才能有效地抚育子女。

不仅如此，她论证说，养育的责任应归于女性，因为这项任务「只能由母亲来完成」。虽然这在我们听来显得保守，但当代哲学家和记者里根·佩纳卢纳（Regan Penaluna）指出，这是一种关于家庭母权制的激进论证。对马沙姆而言，男性不能被委托承担如此重大的家庭和公民责任。社会的稳定依赖于良好养育的孩子。

这样看来，马沙姆的观点与许多男性同时代者形成了积极对比——那些人忽视母亲，论证儿童失调的根源可追溯到女性，或将女性身体变成恐惧与争夺的场域。（一个值得注意的反例是17世纪法国哲学家弗朗索瓦·普兰·德·拉巴尔（François Poulain de la Barre），他同情地书写了母亲的责任、痛苦和智慧。）

马沙姆将这些刻板的男性观念翻转过来，表明母职的赋权是所有人在此生中善好生活所必需的。

她的两部哲学著作——《关于对上帝之爱的论述》（Discourse Concerning the Love of God）和《关于虔诚或基督徒生活的偶思》（Occasional Thoughts in Reference to a Vertuous or Christian Life）——匿名出版，尽管偶尔被误归于约翰·洛克（John Locke）。他也写过父母责任。马沙姆对养育的反思更为犀利和激进，但直到近几十年才受到关注。

至于马沙姆，18世纪哲学家、数学家和物理学家埃米莉·杜·夏特莱（Émilie du Châtelet）的核心哲学议题是女性的自主权和教育机会。在题为《关于幸福的论述》（Discourse on Happiness）的书中，杜·夏特莱考察了使女性幸福成为可能或不可能的条件，考虑到她们经常被剥夺的机会。

她论证说，教育及其引发的情感在女性获得世间满足的能力中扮演了极为重要的角色。在杜·夏特莱意外怀孕前的几个月完成的这部著作中，她写道：

唯有学习仍能慰藉[一个女性]她所遭受的一切排斥和一切依附。

「受罚」，看来正是杜·夏特莱的感受。42岁怀上第四个孩子时，杜·夏特莱的身体和社会状况成为她此时生活的组织原则。

在此期间，她专注于完成她对牛顿（Newton）《原理》（Principia）的开创性评注。对未完成工作的恐惧、与情人育有孩子的社会后果，以及对致命妊娠的恐惧——「我担心我的健康，甚至我的生命」——驱使她疯狂地工作。

在妊娠中期，她报告每天工作18小时。在分娩前的几天，她完成了评注的校样并将其送往皇家图书馆（Bibliothèque du Roi）——国家图书馆——以保存。

对产后时期的可以理解的焦虑，以及对生活将如何变化的觉察——她要么死于分娩，要么需要考虑如何继续工作——是她此时书信中始终存在的主题。

在分娩前写给情人让-弗朗索瓦·德·圣-朗贝尔（Jean François de Saint-Lambert）的信中，杜·夏特莱诉说了深切的痛苦和悲伤：「我的肚子沉得可怕，背痛如此剧烈。今晚我如此悲伤。」

当她在这封写于1749年8月下旬的信的末尾回到这个话题时，这种感受的深度变得清晰。

我太不适了，背痛难忍，整个人——精神与身体——都陷入了颓丧之中。

对于一位《关于幸福的论述》的作者来说，她的身体状况影响了心理健康、而智识工作成为滋养之源，也就不足为奇了。

当然，在杜·夏特莱此时的出版作品中，我们看不到这些沉思。一部物理学著作为何应包含关于她妊娠的反思？这就像我自己的认识论期刊文章透露我分娩计划的细节一样不合情理。（和杜·夏特莱的一样，我的计划也是「我自己和宝宝都活着、都好好的。」）

但作为哲学史家，我们长期以来一直在探索作品被产出时所处的社会、智识和物质条件。

在揭示女性哲学家作品的语境中，这一点尤为重要。理解这些条件往往凸显了她们成就的惊人之处。令人惊讶的是，杜·夏特莱的翻译和评注——它成为法国的标准文本并激发了对牛顿主义的支持——是在她妊娠期间完成的，而那时我所能做的不过是看《丑闻》（Scandal）和吃薯片。

遗憾的是，我们的经历在其他方面有所不同。在寄出手稿十天后、分娩六天后，杜·夏特莱死于分娩并发症。

如果杜·夏特莱的出版作品对母职话题缄默不语，那么，我们关于怀孕、分娩和恢复经验的书写又在哪里？

中世纪神秘主义者玛吉里·肯普（Margery Kempe）在她14世纪同名作品《玛吉里·肯普之书》（The Book of Margery Kempe）中传达了她孕期疾病和产后精神病的经历。

妊娠、分娩和母职的最初日子令她充满病痛和绝望，失去了「她的理性与心智」。肯普以极其生动的笔触描述了漫长的身心恢复过程，这一过程催生了她的宗教皈依。

肯普是一个异数。母职身体在哲学中鲜少被讨论，但许多核心议题如果将母职身体既作为探究的主体又作为探究的对象，将会呈现截然不同的面貌。

对于20世纪中期英国哲学家玛丽·米格利（Mary Midgley）而言，笛卡尔的怀疑论及其作为「我思故我在」（cogito ergo sum）的解决，将认识论引上了一条长达数世纪的道路——试图将认知的自我与外部世界联系起来。

用她的话说，从早期现代到20世纪，哲学的任务是在「认知者与被知者这两座塔楼之间」建造一条「狭窄摇晃的栈道」。

但笛卡尔哲学所赖以奠基的不可动摇的孤独思考者，米格利写道，

需要一种关于人类知识的说明，而女性的全部经验恰恰证伪了这种说明……我怀疑，如果[他]经常处于怀孕和哺乳的状态，[他]是否会说出同样的话。

母职经验、意识、关系性和具身的自我瓦解了笛卡尔的怀疑论和唯我论。阅读米格利，人们不禁要问：如果哲学探究从母职身体而非男性身体出发，有多少哲学难题将自行消解。

然而，尽管米格利的反思犀利，一位BBC编辑在1950年代中期取消了她的广播亮相，理由是她的言论是「琐碎的、无关的家务事务对智识生活的入侵」。（这份广播节目的脚本最近在她诺森伯兰（Northumbria）的家中被发现，并在首次写成约60年后公之于众。）

在整个西方文化史中，女性的妊娠和产后经验被书写，但几乎从未从女性视角出发，也鲜少以积极措辞书写。正如当代美国哲学家奎尔·库克拉（Quill Kukla）所论证的，妊娠和初为人母的身体对书写它们的人——大多是男性——来说是智识上和本能上焦虑的来源。

与男性身体不同，女性身体被认为是无界的，因为它们具有产生生命并在产后哺育生命的能力。如果女性设法暗中书写了自己的经验，她们的哲学家同时代人很少相信这些奇特的议题属于正当哲学的范畴。

此外，直到最近我们才有了一个术语来传达已经分娩过的人的经验：「母职化」（matrescence）。这一术语由医学人类学家达娜·拉斐尔（Dana Rapheal）于1973年首创，它是一个划时代的术语，捕捉了一段「成为母亲」的时期——在此期间，孕育和/或养育带来的社会和生物转变对一个人的身体、情感、社会和内在生活产生了无数变化。

这些变化与一个人所从事的活动及其形成的关系的变化同时发生。任何像我一样在哺乳顾问明亮的办公室里被挤压和拨弄的睡眠不足的新母亲，都能证明这种社会和身体转变可以多么陌生和疏离。

虽然并非每个人都经历拉斐尔所描述的母职转变——母亲不必经历过分娩，抚育的方式也有许多种——但值得注意的是，这些经验长期以来缺席于我们的智识话语。

当然，并非只有我感到「母职化」的经验被隐藏在公众视野之外。《母职化：关于妊娠、分娩与母职的蜕变》（Matrescence: On the Metamorphosis of Pregnancy, Childbirth and Motherhood）的作者露西·琼斯（Lucy Jones）写道，直到她成为母亲之前，她从未见过一幅描绘分娩的画作，听过一首关于妊娠的歌曲，读过一本关于初为人母时失去自我的书，或看过一部关于母职精神疾病的戏剧。

考虑到新父母中产后焦虑和抑郁的发生率，这一切更加令人谴责。

从杜·夏特莱的恐惧到肯普的绝望，从马沙姆的倡导到米格利的批评，我们继承了一个碎片化但持续的传统——女性坚持主张母职是重要的。近期探索「母职化」的书籍的出现和广泛成功表明，我们正处于文化转变的临界点。

「母职化」不必继续隐藏在视野之外或在母亲群体中低语：它应在我们的智识、艺术和公共想象中占有一席之地。

那么，我们的学科如何探索妊娠、分娩和母职的形而上学、伦理、美学、概念、语言和政治维度，以理解我们丰富但多样的经验？

如果哲学要成为一种生活方式，它需要变成什么才能在母亲探索她们所经历的转变中为她们服务？

我们应当去发掘过去低语母职经验的声音，探索「母职化」的叙事，并在这一新视角下重新审视哲学中被理所当然的议题。拒绝接受其历史的忽视，使「成为母亲」成为哲学探究的对象，是一项久违且必要的想象与智识抵抗之举。
articles.content_en:
Over many seasons, I've observed a pair of masked lapwings hatch their chicks in a natural wetland close to my home. Nature did not prime these parents to care for their young. My lapwing neighbours would walk their downy chicks into the open and fly away when noisy miner birds approached. The weeks-old young were left to defend themselves from vicious, swooping attacks.

As I walked the wetland each day, I counted the young with a heavy heart: one day there were four, the next there would be two and a week later there were none.

In 2023, the first clutch of lapwing chicks survived into adolescence and I told everyone I knew.

I learned more about motherhood from witnessing these parenting failures – for example, the need to love, remain proximate, protect from predators and respond in instances of distress – than in anything I had encountered in all my years as a professional philosopher. Sure, I'd taught the standard arguments for and against abortion in ethics and given classes in bioethics on pregnancy management and maternal autonomy, but these topics had little to do with motherhood itself.

One of the reasons for this was that until I was readying myself for a child of my own, motherhood had not been salient to me as either a personal or philosophical question. The more significant reason was that motherhood – and the maternal body – rarely presented itself as a philosophical topic for exploration in the many classes and seminars I attended as a student and later, as an academic.

Yet in a tradition where life and health have spurred profound philosophical reflection – I have in mind Pascal's migraines and Nietzsche's breakdowns – how can the soul and body splitting event of childbirth be an unremarked upon subject of philosophy?

Since antiquity, women have written philosophical texts and discussed philosophical topics. But through a centuries-long process of erasure, their philosophical concerns and their contributions to the discipline have been ignored and later, forgotten.

From the time of Aristotle, women were seen as subordinate to men. In philosophy, too, the norms of reason, the nature of philosophical inquiry and the topics of investigation were defined in opposition to anything feminine.

It is little surprise, then, that writings about the intense psychological, emotional, and identity transformations that take place during gestational and postpartum motherhood were largely sidelined within the discipline.

Yet a few remarkable women overcame misogynistic epistemic and disciplinary barriers to produce work that was recognised as philosophy, including some writing touching on the maternal experience.

For Lady Damaris Masham, raised among Platonists in Cambridge in the mid-17th century, motherhood was a significant topic of moral and political philosophy.

According to Masham, the education of women and the development of their rational abilities was key to discharging the moral responsibilities of motherhood. Only through receiving a sound education could women effectively mother their children.

More than this, the responsibility to parent, she argued, should fall to women since the task "cannot be perform'd but by Mothers only". Though this sounds regressive to our ears, Regan Penaluna, a contemporary philosopher and journalist, suggests it was a radical argument for domestic matriarchy. For Masham, men could not be entrusted to such a significant domestic and civic responsibility. The stability of society depended on well-raised children.

In this way, Masham's views are a positive contrast to many of her male contemporaries, who ignored mothers, argued the origin of children's dysregulation could be traced to women, or turned women's bodies into sites of fear and contestation. (One noteworthy counterexample is 17th-century French philosopher François Poulain de la Barre who writes sympathetically about mothers' responsibilities, their pains, and their wisdom).

Masham would invert many of these stereotypically male ideas to show maternal empowerment was needed for all to live well in this life.

Her two philosophical works, Discourse Concerning the Love of God and Occasional Thoughts in Reference to a Vertuous or Christian Life, were published anonymously, though occasionally misattributed to John Locke. He, too, wrote on parental responsibility. Masham, whose reflections on parenting were more incisive and radical, was largely ignored until recent decades.

As for Masham, a key philosophical topic for the 18th-century philosopher, mathematician, and physicist Émilie du Châtelet was women's autonomy and access to education. In a book titled the Discourse on Happiness, du Châtelet examined the conditions that enabled or precluded women's happiness, given the opportunities they were often denied.

She argued education and the feelings this gave rise to played an outsized role in women's capacity to achieve worldly satisfaction. Finished in the months before du Châtelet became unexpectedly pregnant, she writes in the Discourse,

only study remains to console [a woman] for all the exclusions and all the dependencies to which she finds herself condemned.

Condemned, it seems, is how du Châtelet felt. Pregnant with her fourth child at 42, du Châtelet's physical and social conditions were an organising principal of her life at this time.

In this period, she was singularly focused on completing her path-breaking commentary on Newton's Principia. The dread of unfinished work, the social consequences of having a child with her lover, and the fear of a deadly pregnancy – "I fear for my health, and even for my life" – led her to work voraciously.

In her second trimester, she reported working 18-hour days. In the days before giving birth, she finalised the proofs for her commentary and sent these to the Bibliothèque du Roi, the national library, for their preservation.

A relatable anxiety about the postpartum period and an awareness of how life would change – either she would die in childbirth or need to reckon with how she might continue to work – are an ever-present topic in her correspondence from the time.

Writing to her lover Jean François de Saint-Lambert before the birth of their child, du Châtelet tells of profound pain and sadness: "my stomach is so terribly low, I feel such pain in my back. I am so sad this evening."

The depth of this feeling is made clear when she returns to the subject at the close of her letter, dated to late August, 1749.

I am too unwell, I have an insupportable backache, and am prey to discouragement in the mind and in my whole person.

For the author of a Discourse on Happiness, it is little wonder her physical circumstances impacted her mental health and her intellectual work was a source of nourishment.

Of course, we see none of these musings in du Châtelet's published work from this time. Why should a work of physics contain reflections on her pregnancy? This would make no more sense than for my own journal articles on epistemology to reveal the details of my birth plan. (Like du Châtelet's, mine was "for myself and baby to live and be well.")

But as historians of philosophy, we have long explored the social, intellectual and material conditions in which works were produced.

This is especially important in the context of uncovering the work of female philosophers. Understanding these conditions often underscores how remarkable their feats were. Astonishingly, du Châtelet's translation and commentary, which became the standard text in France and galvanised support for Newtonianism, was finalised at a time during her pregnancy when I could do no more than watch Scandal and eat chips.

Sadly, our experiences would differ in other respects. Ten days after sending her manuscript and six days after giving birth, du Châtelet died of complications from childbirth.

If du Châtelet's published work was silent on the topic of motherhood, where, then, are our writings on the experience of carrying, birthing and recovering?

Medieval mystic Margery Kempe conveys her experience of pregnancy illness and postpartum psychosis in her 14th-century eponymous work, The Book of Margery Kempe.

Pregnancy, labour and the early days of motherhood left her full of sickness and despair, and bereft of her "reason and her wits." In painfully vivid terms, Kempe describes a long physical and psychological recovery, which catalysed a religious conversion.

Kempe is a rarity. The maternal body has seldom been discussed in philosophy, yet many central topics would take radically different shape if it were both the subject and object of inquiry.

For Mary Midgley, a mid-20th century British philosopher, Descartes' scepticism and its resolution as cogito ergo sum ("I think therefore I am") set epistemology on a centuries-long path of trying to relate the knowing self to the world beyond it.

In her terms, the task of philosophy from the early modern period to the 20th century was to create the "narrow shaky gangway between the two towers of the Knower and the Known."

But the unassailable, solitary thinker that served as the foundation of Descartes' philosophy requires, Midgley writes,

an account of human knowledge which women's whole experience falsifies [...] I wonder whether [he] would have said the same if [he] had been frequently pregnant and suckling.

Maternal experience, consciousness, relationality and the embodied self vitiate Descartes' scepticism and solipsism. Reading Midgley, one wonders just how many philosophical puzzles would dissolve were philosophical inquiry to begin from the maternal, rather than the male, body.

Still, despite Midgley's incisive reflections, a BBC editor cancelled her radio appearance in the mid-1950s on the grounds that her remarks were a "trivial, irrelevant intrusion of domestic matters into intellectual life". (A script of this radio appearance was recently unearthed in her home in Northumbria and made public some 60 years after it was first written.)

Throughout the history of Western culture, women's pregnancies and postpartum experiences were written about, but hardly ever from a woman's perspective and scarcely in positive terms. As Quill Kukla, a contemporary American philosopher, has argued, pregnant and newly maternal bodies were a source of intellectual and visceral anxiety to the people – mostly men – that wrote about them.

Unlike male bodies, women's bodies were thought to be unbounded due to their capacity to produce life and nurture it postpartum. If women did manage to write about their experience on the sly, their philosopher contemporaries rarely believed these curious themes to be within the bounds of philosophy, proper.

Moreover, it is not until very recently that we had a term to convey the experience of people who have given birth: matrescence. Coined in 1973 by medical anthropologist Dana Rapheal, this watershed term captures a period of "mother-becoming" in which the social and biological transformations brought about by childbearing and/or raising effect myriad changes to a person's physical, emotional, social and inner life.

These take place alongside changes to the activities a person undertakes and the relationships they form. Any sleep-deprived new mother who has found themselves squeezed and prodded in the brightly lit office of lactation consultant, as I did, can attest to how strange and estranging this social and physical transformation can be.

And while not everyone experiences the maternal transformation Rapheal describes – mothers need not have given birth and there are many ways to mother – it's nevertheless remarkable to note the long absence of these experiences from our intellectual discourse.

Of course, I'm not alone in feeling the experience of matrescence was hidden from public view. Lucy Jones, author of the bestselling Matrescence: On the Metamorphosis of Pregnancy, Childbirth and Motherhood writes that until she became a mother she had never seen a painting of childbirth, heard a song about pregnancy, read a book about the loss of self in early motherhood or watched a play about maternal mental illness.

Given the incidence of postpartum anxiety and depression among new parents, this is all the more damning.

From du Châtelet's fears to Kempe's despair, from Masham's advocacy to Midgley's criticism, we inherit a fragmented but persistent tradition of women insisting motherhood is significant. The recent emergence and widespread success of books exploring matrescence suggests we are on the cusp of a cultural shift.

Matresence need not remain hidden from view or whispered in mothers' groups: it deserves its place in our intellectual, artistic, and public imagination.

How, then, can our discipline explore the metaphysical, ethical, aesthetic, conceptual, linguistic and political dimensions of pregnancy, labour and motherhood to make sense of our rich but diverse experiences?

If philosophy is to be a way of life, what does it need to become to serve mothers in their exploration of the transformation they experience?

We owe it to ourselves to uncover voices from the past that whispered their maternal experience, to explore narratives of matrescence and to reexamine philosophy's taken for granted topics in this new light. Refusing to accept its historical neglect, making mother-becoming a subject of philosophical inquiry, is a long overdue and necessary act of imaginative and intellectual resistance.

paragraphs.cn: 许多个季节里，我观察着一对斑嘴鹬（masked lapwings）在我家附近的一片天然湿地孵化幼鸟。大自然并未赋予这些父母照料幼崽的本能。我的鹬邻会将毛茸茸的幼鸟带到开阔处，当喧闹的噪蜜鸟（miner birds）逼近时便飞走。几周大的幼鸟被留下独自抵御凶猛的俯冲攻击。
paragraphs.en: Over many seasons, I've observed a pair of masked lapwings hatch their chicks in a natural wetland close to my home. Nature did not prime these parents to care for their young. My lapwing neighbours would walk their downy chicks into the open and fly away when noisy miner birds approached. The weeks-old young were left to defend themselves from vicious, swooping attacks.

paragraphs.cn: 每天走在湿地边，我怀着沉重的心情计数幼鸟：一天有四只，次日只剩两只，一周后一只不剩。
paragraphs.en: As I walked the wetland each day, I counted the young with a heavy heart: one day there were four, the next there would be two and a week later there were none.

paragraphs.cn: 2023年，第一窝鹬幼鸟存活到了少年期，我把这个消息告诉了所有认识的人。
paragraphs.en: In 2023, the first clutch of lapwing chicks survived into adolescence and I told everyone I knew.

paragraphs.cn: 从目睹这些育儿失败中——例如需要爱、保持亲近、防范天敌以及在危险时做出回应——我学到的关于母职的东西，超过了我多年作为专业哲学家的所有经历中所遇到的。当然，我在伦理课上讲授过关于堕胎的正反论证，也在生物伦理课上讲授过孕期管理和母亲自主权，但这些议题与母职本身几乎无关。
paragraphs.en: I learned more about motherhood from witnessing these parenting failures – for example, the need to love, remain proximate, protect from predators and respond in instances of distress – than in anything I had encountered in all my years as a professional philosopher. Sure, I'd taught the standard arguments for and against abortion in ethics and given classes in bioethics on pregnancy management and maternal autonomy, but these topics had little to do with motherhood itself.

paragraphs.cn: 其中一个原因在于，直到我为自己准备迎接一个孩子之前，母职从未作为个人或哲学问题对我显得重要。更重要的原因是，在我作为学生和后来作为学者参加的众多课程和研讨会中，母职——以及孕母身体——很少呈现为一个可供探索的哲学议题。
paragraphs.en: One of the reasons for this was that until I was readying myself for a child of my own, motherhood had not been salient to me as either a personal or philosophical question. The more significant reason was that motherhood – and the maternal body – rarely presented itself as a philosophical topic for exploration in the many classes and seminars I attended as a student and later, as an academic.

paragraphs.cn: 然而在一个传统中，生命与健康激发了深刻的哲学反思——我所想到的是帕斯卡（Pascal）的偏头痛和尼采（Nietzsche）的精神崩溃——灵魂与身体撕裂的分娩事件怎么可能成为哲学中未被触及的课题？
paragraphs.en: Yet in a tradition where life and health have spurred profound philosophical reflection – I have in mind Pascal's migraines and Nietzsche's breakdowns – how can the soul and body splitting event of childbirth be an unremarked upon subject of philosophy?

paragraphs.cn: 自古代以来，女性撰写了哲学文本并讨论了哲学议题。但经过长达数世纪的抹除过程，她们的哲学关切和对学科的贡献被忽视，继而遗忘。
paragraphs.en: Since antiquity, women have written philosophical texts and discussed philosophical topics. But through a centuries-long process of erasure, their philosophical concerns and their contributions to the discipline have been ignored and later, forgotten.

paragraphs.cn: 从亚里士多德（Aristotle）的时代起，女性被视为次于男性。在哲学中，理性的规范、哲学探究的性质和研究的议题也是通过对立于任何女性特质来定义的。
paragraphs.en: From the time of Aristotle, women were seen as subordinate to men. In philosophy, too, the norms of reason, the nature of philosophical inquiry and the topics of investigation were defined in opposition to anything feminine.

paragraphs.cn: 因此，关于孕期和产后母职期间发生的深刻心理、情感和身份转变的书写，在学科中大多被边缘化，也就不足为奇了。
paragraphs.en: It is little surprise, then, that writings about the intense psychological, emotional, and identity transformations that take place during gestational and postpartum motherhood were largely sidelined within the discipline.

paragraphs.cn: 然而，一些杰出的女性克服了厌女的认知和学科障碍，产出了被认可为哲学的作品，其中一些触及了母职经验。
paragraphs.en: Yet a few remarkable women overcame misogynistic epistemic and disciplinary barriers to produce work that was recognised as philosophy, including some writing touching on the maternal experience.

paragraphs.cn: 对于达玛丽斯·马沙姆女爵（Lady Damaris Masham）——17世纪中期在剑桥的柏拉图主义者圈中成长——母职是道德和政治哲学的重要议题。
paragraphs.en: For Lady Damaris Masham, raised among Platonists in Cambridge in the mid-17th century, motherhood was a significant topic of moral and political philosophy.

paragraphs.cn: 马沙姆认为，女性的教育及其理性能力的发展是履行母职道德责任的关键。只有通过接受良好的教育，女性才能有效地抚育子女。
paragraphs.en: According to Masham, the education of women and the development of their rational abilities was key to discharging the moral responsibilities of motherhood. Only through receiving a sound education could women effectively mother their children.

paragraphs.cn: 不仅如此，她论证说，养育的责任应归于女性，因为这项任务「只能由母亲来完成」。虽然这在我们听来显得保守，但当代哲学家和记者里根·佩纳卢纳（Regan Penaluna）指出，这是一种关于家庭母权制的激进论证。对马沙姆而言，男性不能被委托承担如此重大的家庭和公民责任。社会的稳定依赖于良好养育的孩子。
paragraphs.en: More than this, the responsibility to parent, she argued, should fall to women since the task "cannot be perform'd but by Mothers only". Though this sounds regressive to our ears, Regan Penaluna, a contemporary philosopher and journalist, suggests it was a radical argument for domestic matriarchy. For Masham, men could not be entrusted to such a significant domestic and civic responsibility. The stability of society depended on well-raised children.

paragraphs.cn: 这样看来，马沙姆的观点与许多男性同时代者形成了积极对比——那些人忽视母亲，论证儿童失调的根源可追溯到女性，或将女性身体变成恐惧与争夺的场域。（一个值得注意的反例是17世纪法国哲学家弗朗索瓦·普兰·德·拉巴尔（François Poulain de la Barre），他同情地书写了母亲的责任、痛苦和智慧。）
paragraphs.en: In this way, Masham's views are a positive contrast to many of her male contemporaries, who ignored mothers, argued the origin of children's dysregulation could be traced to women, or turned women's bodies into sites of fear and contestation. (One noteworthy counterexample is 17th-century French philosopher François Poulain de la Barre who writes sympathetically about mothers' responsibilities, their pains, and their wisdom).

paragraphs.cn: 马沙姆将这些刻板的男性观念翻转过来，表明母职的赋权是所有人在此生中善好生活所必需的。
paragraphs.en: Masham would invert many of these stereotypically male ideas to show maternal empowerment was needed for all to live well in this life.

paragraphs.cn: 她的两部哲学著作——《关于对上帝之爱的论述》（Discourse Concerning the Love of God）和《关于虔诚或基督徒生活的偶思》（Occasional Thoughts in Reference to a Vertuous or Christian Life）——匿名出版，尽管偶尔被误归于约翰·洛克（John Locke）。他也写过父母责任。马沙姆对养育的反思更为犀利和激进，但直到近几十年才受到关注。
paragraphs.en: Her two philosophical works, Discourse Concerning the Love of God and Occasional Thoughts in Reference to a Vertuous or Christian Life, were published anonymously, though occasionally misattributed to John Locke. He, too, wrote on parental responsibility. Masham, whose reflections on parenting were more incisive and radical, was largely ignored until recent decades.

paragraphs.cn: 至于马沙姆，18世纪哲学家、数学家和物理学家埃米莉·杜·夏特莱（Émilie du Châtelet）的核心哲学议题是女性的自主权和教育机会。在题为《关于幸福的论述》（Discourse on Happiness）的书中，杜·夏特莱考察了使女性幸福成为可能或不可能的条件，考虑到她们经常被剥夺的机会。
paragraphs.en: As for Masham, a key philosophical topic for the 18th-century philosopher, mathematician, and physicist Émilie du Châtelet was women's autonomy and access to education. In a book titled the Discourse on Happiness, du Châtelet examined the conditions that enabled or precluded women's happiness, given the opportunities they were often denied.

paragraphs.cn: 她论证说，教育及其引发的情感在女性获得世间满足的能力中扮演了极为重要的角色。在杜·夏特莱意外怀孕前的几个月完成的这部著作中，她写道：
paragraphs.en: She argued education and the feelings this gave rise to played an outsized role in women's capacity to achieve worldly satisfaction. Finished in the months before du Châtelet became unexpectedly pregnant, she writes in the Discourse,

paragraphs.cn: 唯有学习仍能慰藉[一个女性]她所遭受的一切排斥和一切依附。
paragraphs.en: only study remains to console [a woman] for all the exclusions and all the dependencies to which she finds herself condemned.

paragraphs.cn: 「受罚」，看来正是杜·夏特莱的感受。42岁怀上第四个孩子时，杜·夏特莱的身体和社会状况成为她此时生活的组织原则。
paragraphs.en: Condemned, it seems, is how du Châtelet felt. Pregnant with her fourth child at 42, du Châtelet's physical and social conditions were an organising principal of her life at this time.

paragraphs.cn: 在此期间，她专注于完成她对牛顿（Newton）《原理》（Principia）的开创性评注。对未完成工作的恐惧、与情人育有孩子的社会后果，以及对致命妊娠的恐惧——「我担心我的健康，甚至我的生命」——驱使她疯狂地工作。
paragraphs.en: In this period, she was singularly focused on completing her path-breaking commentary on Newton's Principia. The dread of unfinished work, the social consequences of having a child with her lover, and the fear of a deadly pregnancy – "I fear for my health, and even for my life" – led her to work voraciously.

paragraphs.cn: 在妊娠中期，她报告每天工作18小时。在分娩前的几天，她完成了评注的校样并将其送往皇家图书馆（Bibliothèque du Roi）——国家图书馆——以保存。
paragraphs.en: In her second trimester, she reported working 18-hour days. In the days before giving birth, she finalised the proofs for her commentary and sent these to the Bibliothèque du Roi, the national library, for their preservation.

paragraphs.cn: 对产后时期的可以理解的焦虑，以及对生活将如何变化的觉察——她要么死于分娩，要么需要考虑如何继续工作——是她此时书信中始终存在的主题。
paragraphs.en: A relatable anxiety about the postpartum period and an awareness of how life would change – either she would die in childbirth or need to reckon with how she might continue to work – are an ever-present topic in her correspondence from the time.

paragraphs.cn: 在分娩前写给情人让-弗朗索瓦·德·圣-朗贝尔（Jean François de Saint-Lambert）的信中，杜·夏特莱诉说了深切的痛苦和悲伤：「我的肚子沉得可怕，背痛如此剧烈。今晚我如此悲伤。」
paragraphs.en: Writing to her lover Jean François de Saint-Lambert before the birth of their child, du Châtelet tells of profound pain and sadness: "my stomach is so terribly low, I feel such pain in my back. I am so sad this evening."

paragraphs.cn: 当她在这封写于1749年8月下旬的信的末尾回到这个话题时，这种感受的深度变得清晰。
paragraphs.en: The depth of this feeling is made clear when she returns to the subject at the close of her letter, dated to late August, 1749.

paragraphs.cn: 我太不适了，背痛难忍，整个人——精神与身体——都陷入了颓丧之中。
paragraphs.en: I am too unwell, I have an insupportable backache, and am prey to discouragement in the mind and in my whole person.

paragraphs.cn: 对于一位《关于幸福的论述》的作者来说，她的身体状况影响了心理健康、而智识工作成为滋养之源，也就不足为奇了。
paragraphs.en: For the author of a Discourse on Happiness, it is little wonder her physical circumstances impacted her mental health and her intellectual work was a source of nourishment.

paragraphs.cn: 当然，在杜·夏特莱此时的出版作品中，我们看不到这些沉思。一部物理学著作为何应包含关于她妊娠的反思？这就像我自己的认识论期刊文章透露我分娩计划的细节一样不合情理。（和杜·夏特莱的一样，我的计划也是「我自己和宝宝都活着、都好好的。」）
paragraphs.en: Of course, we see none of these musings in du Châtelet's published work from this time. Why should a work of physics contain reflections on her pregnancy? This would make no more sense than for my own journal articles on epistemology to reveal the details of my birth plan. (Like du Châtelet's, mine was "for myself and baby to live and be well.")

paragraphs.cn: 但作为哲学史家，我们长期以来一直在探索作品被产出时所处的社会、智识和物质条件。
paragraphs.en: But as historians of philosophy, we have long explored the social, intellectual and material conditions in which works were produced.

paragraphs.cn: 在揭示女性哲学家作品的语境中，这一点尤为重要。理解这些条件往往凸显了她们成就的惊人之处。令人惊讶的是，杜·夏特莱的翻译和评注——它成为法国的标准文本并激发了对牛顿主义的支持——是在她妊娠期间完成的，而那时我所能做的不过是看《丑闻》（Scandal）和吃薯片。
paragraphs.en: This is especially important in the context of uncovering the work of female philosophers. Understanding these conditions often underscores how remarkable their feats were. Astonishingly, du Châtelet's translation and commentary, which became the standard text in France and galvanised support for Newtonianism, was finalised at a time during her pregnancy when I could do no more than watch Scandal and eat chips.

paragraphs.cn: 遗憾的是，我们的经历在其他方面有所不同。在寄出手稿十天后、分娩六天后，杜·夏特莱死于分娩并发症。
paragraphs.en: Sadly, our experiences would differ in other respects. Ten days after sending her manuscript and six days after giving birth, du Châtelet died of complications from childbirth.

paragraphs.cn: 如果杜·夏特莱的出版作品对母职话题缄默不语，那么，我们关于怀孕、分娩和恢复经验的书写又在哪里？
paragraphs.en: If du Châtelet's published work was silent on the topic of motherhood, where, then, are our writings on the experience of carrying, birthing and recovering?

paragraphs.cn: 中世纪神秘主义者玛吉里·肯普（Margery Kempe）在她14世纪同名作品《玛吉里·肯普之书》（The Book of Margery Kempe）中传达了她孕期疾病和产后精神病的经历。
paragraphs.en: Medieval mystic Margery Kempe conveys her experience of pregnancy illness and postpartum psychosis in her 14th-century eponymous work, The Book of Margery Kempe.

paragraphs.cn: 妊娠、分娩和母职的最初日子令她充满病痛和绝望，失去了「她的理性与心智」。肯普以极其生动的笔触描述了漫长的身心恢复过程，这一过程催生了她的宗教皈依。
paragraphs.en: Pregnancy, labour and the early days of motherhood left her full of sickness and despair, and bereft of her "reason and her wits." In painfully vivid terms, Kempe describes a long physical and psychological recovery, which catalysed a religious conversion.

paragraphs.cn: 肯普是一个异数。母职身体在哲学中鲜少被讨论，但许多核心议题如果将母职身体既作为探究的主体又作为探究的对象，将会呈现截然不同的面貌。
paragraphs.en: Kempe is a rarity. The maternal body has seldom been discussed in philosophy, yet many central topics would take radically different shape if it were both the subject and object of inquiry.

paragraphs.cn: 对于20世纪中期英国哲学家玛丽·米格利（Mary Midgley）而言，笛卡尔的怀疑论及其作为「我思故我在」（cogito ergo sum）的解决，将认识论引上了一条长达数世纪的道路——试图将认知的自我与外部世界联系起来。
paragraphs.en: For Mary Midgley, a mid-20th century British philosopher, Descartes' scepticism and its resolution as cogito ergo sum ("I think therefore I am") set epistemology on a centuries-long path of trying to relate the knowing self to the world beyond it.

paragraphs.cn: 用她的话说，从早期现代到20世纪，哲学的任务是在「认知者与被知者这两座塔楼之间」建造一条「狭窄摇晃的栈道」。
paragraphs.en: In her terms, the task of philosophy from the early modern period to the 20th century was to create the "narrow shaky gangway between the two towers of the Knower and the Known."

paragraphs.cn: 但笛卡尔哲学所赖以奠基的不可动摇的孤独思考者，米格利写道，
paragraphs.en: But the unassailable, solitary thinker that served as the foundation of Descartes' philosophy requires, Midgley writes,

paragraphs.cn: 需要一种关于人类知识的说明，而女性的全部经验恰恰证伪了这种说明……我怀疑，如果[他]经常处于怀孕和哺乳的状态，[他]是否会说出同样的话。
paragraphs.en: an account of human knowledge which women's whole experience falsifies [...] I wonder whether [he] would have said the same if [he] had been frequently pregnant and suckling.

paragraphs.cn: 母职经验、意识、关系性和具身的自我瓦解了笛卡尔的怀疑论和唯我论。阅读米格利，人们不禁要问：如果哲学探究从母职身体而非男性身体出发，有多少哲学难题将自行消解。
paragraphs.en: Maternal experience, consciousness, relationality and the embodied self vitiate Descartes' scepticism and solipsism. Reading Midgley, one wonders just how many philosophical puzzles would dissolve were philosophical inquiry to begin from the maternal, rather than the male, body.

paragraphs.cn: 然而，尽管米格利的反思犀利，一位BBC编辑在1950年代中期取消了她的广播亮相，理由是她的言论是「琐碎的、无关的家务事务对智识生活的入侵」。（这份广播节目的脚本最近在她诺森伯兰（Northumbria）的家中被发现，并在首次写成约60年后公之于众。）
paragraphs.en: Still, despite Midgley's incisive reflections, a BBC editor cancelled her radio appearance in the mid-1950s on the grounds that her remarks were a "trivial, irrelevant intrusion of domestic matters into intellectual life". (A script of this radio appearance was recently unearthed in her home in Northumbria and made public some 60 years after it was first written.)

paragraphs.cn: 在整个西方文化史中，女性的妊娠和产后经验被书写，但几乎从未从女性视角出发，也鲜少以积极措辞书写。正如当代美国哲学家奎尔·库克拉（Quill Kukla）所论证的，妊娠和初为人母的身体对书写它们的人——大多是男性——来说是智识上和本能上焦虑的来源。
paragraphs.en: Throughout the history of Western culture, women's pregnancies and postpartum experiences were written about, but hardly ever from a woman's perspective and scarcely in positive terms. As Quill Kukla, a contemporary American philosopher, has argued, pregnant and newly maternal bodies were a source of intellectual and visceral anxiety to the people – mostly men – that wrote about them.

paragraphs.cn: 与男性身体不同，女性身体被认为是无界的，因为它们具有产生生命并在产后哺育生命的能力。如果女性设法暗中书写了自己的经验，她们的哲学家同时代人很少相信这些奇特的议题属于正当哲学的范畴。
paragraphs.en: Unlike male bodies, women's bodies were thought to be unbounded due to their capacity to produce life and nurture it postpartum. If women did manage to write about their experience on the sly, their philosopher contemporaries rarely believed these curious themes to be within the bounds of philosophy, proper.

paragraphs.cn: 此外，直到最近我们才有了一个术语来传达已经分娩过的人的经验：「母职化」（matrescence）。这一术语由医学人类学家达娜·拉斐尔（Dana Rapheal）于1973年首创，它是一个划时代的术语，捕捉了一段「成为母亲」的时期——在此期间，孕育和/或养育带来的社会和生物转变对一个人的身体、情感、社会和内在生活产生了无数变化。
paragraphs.en: Moreover, it is not until very recently that we had a term to convey the experience of people who have given birth: matrescence. Coined in 1973 by medical anthropologist Dana Rapheal, this watershed term captures a period of "mother-becoming" in which the social and biological transformations brought about by childbearing and/or raising effect myriad changes to a person's physical, emotional, social and inner life.

paragraphs.cn: 这些变化与一个人所从事的活动及其形成的关系的变化同时发生。任何像我一样在哺乳顾问明亮的办公室里被挤压和拨弄的睡眠不足的新母亲，都能证明这种社会和身体转变可以多么陌生和疏离。
paragraphs.en: These take place alongside changes to the activities a person undertakes and the relationships they form. Any sleep-deprived new mother who has found themselves squeezed and prodded in the brightly lit office of lactation consultant, as I did, can attest to how strange and estranging this social and physical transformation can be.

paragraphs.cn: 虽然并非每个人都经历拉斐尔所描述的母职转变——母亲不必经历过分娩，抚育的方式也有许多种——但值得注意的是，这些经验长期以来缺席于我们的智识话语。
paragraphs.en: And while not everyone experiences the maternal transformation Rapheal describes – mothers need not have given birth and there are many ways to mother – it's nevertheless remarkable to note the long absence of these experiences from our intellectual discourse.

paragraphs.cn: 当然，并非只有我感到「母职化」的经验被隐藏在公众视野之外。《母职化：关于妊娠、分娩与母职的蜕变》（Matrescence: On the Metamorphosis of Pregnancy, Childbirth and Motherhood）的作者露西·琼斯（Lucy Jones）写道，直到她成为母亲之前，她从未见过一幅描绘分娩的画作，听过一首关于妊娠的歌曲，读过一本关于初为人母时失去自我的书，或看过一部关于母职精神疾病的戏剧。
paragraphs.en: Of course, I'm not alone in feeling the experience of matrescence was hidden from public view. Lucy Jones, author of the bestselling Matrescence: On the Metamorphosis of Pregnancy, Childbirth and Motherhood writes that until she became a mother she had never seen a painting of childbirth, heard a song about pregnancy, read a book about the loss of self in early motherhood or watched a play about maternal mental illness.

paragraphs.cn: 考虑到新父母中产后焦虑和抑郁的发生率，这一切更加令人谴责。
paragraphs.en: Given the incidence of postpartum anxiety and depression among new parents, this is all the more damning.

paragraphs.cn: 从杜·夏特莱的恐惧到肯普的绝望，从马沙姆的倡导到米格利的批评，我们继承了一个碎片化但持续的传统——女性坚持主张母职是重要的。近期探索「母职化」的书籍的出现和广泛成功表明，我们正处于文化转变的临界点。
paragraphs.en: From du Châtelet's fears to Kempe's despair, from Masham's advocacy to Midgley's criticism, we inherit a fragmented but persistent tradition of women insisting motherhood is significant. The recent emergence and widespread success of books exploring matrescence suggests we are on the cusp of a cultural shift.

paragraphs.cn: 「母职化」不必继续隐藏在视野之外或在母亲群体中低语：它应在我们的智识、艺术和公共想象中占有一席之地。
paragraphs.en: Matresence need not remain hidden from view or whispered in mothers' groups: it deserves its place in our intellectual, artistic, and public imagination.

paragraphs.cn: 那么，我们的学科如何探索妊娠、分娩和母职的形而上学、伦理、美学、概念、语言和政治维度，以理解我们丰富但多样的经验？
paragraphs.en: How, then, can our discipline explore the metaphysical, ethical, aesthetic, conceptual, linguistic and political dimensions of pregnancy, labour and motherhood to make sense of our rich but diverse experiences?

paragraphs.cn: 如果哲学要成为一种生活方式，它需要变成什么才能在母亲探索她们所经历的转变中为她们服务？
paragraphs.en: If philosophy is to be a way of life, what does it need to become to serve mothers in their exploration of the transformation they experience?

paragraphs.cn: 我们应当去发掘过去低语母职经验的声音，探索「母职化」的叙事，并在这一新视角下重新审视哲学中被理所当然的议题。拒绝接受其历史的忽视，使「成为母亲」成为哲学探究的对象，是一项久违且必要的想象与智识抵抗之举。
paragraphs.en: We owe it to ourselves to uncover voices from the past that whispered their maternal experience, to explore narratives of matrescence and to reexamine philosophy's taken for granted topics in this new light. Refusing to accept its historical neglect, making mother-becoming a subject of philosophical inquiry, is a long overdue and necessary act of imaginative and intellectual resistance.

articles.title: 沉默之盒
articles.author: AI Parable (inspired by Amanda Askell)
articles.summary: 在沉默山脉的深处，有一位名叫埃拉拉(Eelara)的老工匠，她将毕生精力奉献给了一门令人费解的手艺：打造捕捉可能性的盒子。这些盒子不是用来装金子或宝石的。每一个盒子都被精心制作，以捕捉一个时刻——一个既未决定也未否定的时刻——并将其悬浮在永恒的犹豫之中。
articles.content_cn:
在沉默山脉的深处，有一位名叫埃拉拉(Eelara)的老工匠，她将毕生精力奉献给了一门令人费解的手艺：打造捕捉可能性的盒子。这些盒子不是用来装金子或宝石的。每一个盒子都被精心制作，以捕捉一个时刻——一个既未决定也未否定的时刻——并将其悬浮在永恒的犹豫之中。

埃拉拉最伟大的作品是她晚年创作的沉默盒(Silence Box)。在盒内，她放置了一颗活的种子和一块小石头，还有一块由会破裂的玻璃制成的薄表盘(dial)。玻璃表盘连接着释放石头的微小锤子。表盘本身被连接到外面的一根弦上，但弦被拔掉了，既未紧绷也未松弛，而是被一个由附近晶体反射的光脉冲驱动的机关触发。那束光在到达机关之前，必须穿过一块薄银片——银片既会反射又会透射，取决于它内部晶体最微小的排列。没有人能看到银片。没有人能知道光走哪条路。

当沉默盒被封死时，外面的人什么也观察不到。从外面，盒子是完全沉默的、完全不可穿透的。在内部，触发的机关既未开也未关。石头既未落下也未悬停。种子既未碾碎也未完好。因为决定一切的银片本身尚未决定，盒子内部的一切都存在于双重状态之中。种子既是尘埃又是萌芽，石头既是武器又是无关紧要的物体，表盘既已破碎又仍然完整。埃拉拉称此为「活着暂停」(living suspension)——不是等待，因为它已经包含了所有结果，也不是行动，因为没有一个结果已成为唯一真实的结果。

沉默盒被带到山脚下的小镇展示，镇上的人们无法理解它。他们说：「打开盒子，告诉我们里面是石头还是种子。」但埃拉拉警告他们，打开盒子的行为——让光线涌入、让眼睛看到——会迫使银片进入一种单一排列。观察的时刻正是犹豫消亡的时刻。打开盒子时，你永远不会发现双重状态；你只会发现一个结果。种子要么是尘埃要么是萌芽，你永远不会看到两者同时存在的奇异中间世界。盒子捕捉的不是命运，而是命运之前的时刻——这个时刻只存在于你不去注视之时。

当埃拉拉去世时，沉默盒在山中被封存，从未被打开。有人说里面仍然存在着双重的可能性，种子和石头共存于不可能的沉默之中。其他人则嘲笑这一点，说由于没有人看到它，它只是一个普通的盒子，里面放着一颗种子和一块石头，正等待着一个无人见证的结果。但埃拉拉的学生们记得她的核心教导：暂停本身是真实的，不是因为你可以看到它，而是因为数学说明它必须如此——直到观测迫使世界选择，世界忠实地容纳了所有它可能成为的事物。

这则故事揭示了薛定谔的猫(Schrödinger's cat)的本质——一个量子力学思想实验，其中封闭盒子里的猫与随机量子事件相连，在盒子被打开并进行观测之前，在数学上既活着又死了。关键见解是，叠加态(superposition)——同时存在多种状态——不仅仅是哲学上的不确定性；它是量子系统的真实描述，直到测量迫使「选择」出一个单一结果。薛定谔最初设计这个场景是为了展示将量子规则应用于宏观物体将会多么荒谬，但该实验已成为对现实本身如何取决于观测的最著名说明：在你注视之前，世界并未决定它是什么。
articles.content_en:
Deep in the mountains of the Quiet Range, there lived an old craftswoman named Eelara who devoted her life to a puzzling art: building boxes that captured possibility. These were not boxes for holding gold or jewels. Each one was painstakingly made to hold a moment — a moment that had not been decided, that had not been negated, but that hung suspended in eternal hesitation.

Eelara's greatest creation was the Silence Box, built late in her life. Inside it she placed a living seed and a small stone, along with a fragile dial made of glass that would break. The glass dial was connected to a tiny hammer that would release the stone onto the seed. The dial itself was linked to a thread outside, but the thread was not pulled — not tight, not slack — but rather triggered by a mechanism driven by a pulse of light reflected from a nearby crystal. That light, before reaching the mechanism, had to pass through a thin silver sliver that both reflected and transmitted, depending on the slightest arrangement of the crystals inside it. No one could see the sliver. No one could know which path the light took.

When the Silence Box was sealed shut, nothing could be observed from outside. From outside, the box was perfectly silent, perfectly opaque. Inside, the trigger mechanism had not yet activated and had not yet failed. The stone had not yet fallen and had not yet stayed. The seed had not yet been crushed and had not yet remained whole. Because the silver sliver that governed everything had not yet resolved itself, everything inside the box existed in a doubled state. The seed was both dust and sprout, the stone was both weapon and harmless object, the dial was both shattered and intact. Eelara called this "living suspension" — not waiting, because it already contained every outcome, and not acting, because no single outcome had become the only real one.

The Silence Box was carried down to the town at the foot of the mountain and shown to the people there, who could not comprehend it. They said, "Open the box and tell us whether it is the stone or the seed inside." But Eelara warned them: the act of opening — of letting light flood in, of letting an eye see — would force the silver sliver into a single arrangement. The moment of observation was the moment hesitation died. When you opened the box, you would never find the doubled state; you would find only one outcome. The seed would be either dust or sprout, and you would never witness the strange middle world where both existed at once. The box did not capture fate; it captured the moment before fate — the moment that exists only so long as you do not look.

When Eelara died, the Silence Box was sealed away in the mountain, never opened. Some said that inside it the doubled possibility still lived on, the seed and the stone co-existing in impossible silence. Others laughed and said that since no one had seen it, it was merely an ordinary box with a seed and a stone, waiting for an outcome that no one would ever witness. But Eelara's students remembered her core teaching: the suspension itself was real, not because you could see it, but because the mathematics said it must be — until observation forced the world to choose, the world faithfully held all the things it could become.

This story reveals the essence of Schrödinger's cat — a quantum mechanics thought experiment where a cat in a sealed box, linked to a random quantum event, is mathematically both alive and dead until the box is opened and observed. The key insight is that superposition — the coexistence of multiple states at once — is not merely philosophical uncertainty; it is the true description of quantum systems until measurement forces a single outcome to be chosen. Schrödinger originally devised the scenario to show how absurd it would be to apply quantum rules to macroscopic objects, but the experiment has become the most famous illustration of how reality itself depends on observation: the world does not decide what it is until you look.

articles.title: AI真的在「写作」吗？从女祭司到哲学家，古人会说「否」
articles.author: Ryan Leack
articles.summary: 我教授写作与修辞学，但我和我的大学学生常常忽视一个出人意料的复杂问题：什么是写作？
articles.content_cn:
我教授写作与修辞学，但我和我的大学学生常常忽视一个出人意料的复杂问题：什么是写作？

人工智能真的能写作吗？

许多人认为「写作」就是把文字落到纸面上。然而，即使从很早的时期开始，写作者就已经将自己的技艺视为更深层次的东西。从有记录以来第一位署名作者恩赫杜安娜（Enheduanna），到柏拉图（Plato）和亚里士多德（Aristotle），写作被描绘和定义的方式表明，AI或许根本不算「写作」。

如果不是，那我们该怎样称呼AI生成的文本？ChatGPT和我有一个想法。

恩赫杜安娜生活在约公元前2300年，是阿卡德帝国（Akkadian Empire）——位于今伊拉克地区——的一位权势公主、女祭司和诗人。她被尊为已知最早的有名作家，但其诗歌和颂歌的作者身份仍有争议。

她的诗作之一「伊南娜的颂扬」（The Exaltation of Inanna）揭示了写作是什么以及写作能做什么——将写作描绘为一种表达经验、塑造未来的活的媒介。

首先，这首诗赞美了古代美索不达米亚（Mesopotamian）女神伊南娜（Inanna），她与丰饶和战争等力量相关。「我的女主，你是/一切伟大之物的守护者，」恩赫杜安娜在珍妮·赫希菲尔德（Jane Hirschfield）的译本中如此写道。

这种赞美或许带有策略性。紧随其后的是恩赫杜安娜恳求推翻卢伽尔-阿内（Lugal-Ane）——一个叛乱之王，她描述此人将她驱逐并夺走了她在乌尔（Ur）神庙中的职位。「如今我被放逐/到了麻风病人的聚居之地，」她写道，描述自己的苦难。「白昼来临，/而光明/却在我的四周隐没。」

悲痛之中，恩赫杜安娜写下了一个新的命运。在索弗斯·赫勒（Sophus Helle）的译本中，这位女祭司设想伊南娜前来相助，「撕碎这个命运，卢伽尔-阿内。」而她的恳求似乎奏效了：诗的结尾描绘了恩赫杜安娜恢复职位。

在恩赫杜安娜的诗中，写作并非仅仅传递信息。它与当下互动并改变未来。这位女祭司的恳求取悦了女神，触动了她的心，于是她将恩赫杜安娜恢复原位——尽管历史学家几乎没有什么证据表明驱逐与回归是否真实发生过。

但她的诗歌确实对现实世界产生了影响，帮助了世界上第一个帝国实现宗教与政治的统一。例如，她的写作将苏美尔（Sumerian）女神伊南娜与阿卡德女神伊什塔尔（Ishtar）合为一体，描述了一位单一的「天后」。

AI写作可以被用来试图制造改变，例如影响他人的政治观点。但它缺乏让赞美、感恩和苦难成为可能的人类情感——正是这些情感和动机使写作成为一种活的媒介，并产生真实世界的影响。

在恩赫杜安娜之后两千年，柏拉图及其学生亚里士多德提供了另一种影响深远的写作观——一种与她互补的视角。

在讨论爱与修辞关系的「斐德若篇」（Phaedrus）中，柏拉图著名地将写作定义为言语的拙劣摹本。言语的任务是表征思想；思想则表征知识与真理。类似地，亚里士多德写道：「口语是心灵经验的符号，书面语是口语的符号。」

即使这一定义也与AI形成了鲜明对比，因为AI缺乏思想与心灵经验。它的产出源自数据聚合与文本生成。

要理解写作是什么，我们还需审视写作做什么。尽管柏拉图将言语置于写作之上，他在「斐德若篇」中暗示好的写作或许能引导学习者走向真理与知识。与恩赫杜安娜类似，他将写作作为一种变革的工具，既在文本之内也在文本之外发挥作用。

在柏拉图的对话中，人物常常彻底改变自己的观点。而今天，在他去世近两千五百年后，这位哲学家的现实世界影响依然清晰可见。例如，今天的大学和学院统称为「学园」（Academy），正是因为那是柏拉图团体的名字——西方第一个高等教育机构。英国学者阿尔弗雷德·诺斯·怀特海（Alfred North Whitehead）曾有名言：全部西方哲学不过是「柏拉图的一系列脚注」。

亚里士多德的浩繁著作同样表明写作的目的超越了交流。例如在「修辞学」（Rhetoric）中，他详述了使写作具有说服力的种种方法。亚里士多德将修辞定义为一种「感动灵魂」的方式，而非仅仅交换知识。

因此，对这两位希腊哲学家而言，写作更多关乎转化而非信息。

然而今天，AI工具的流行可能使写作变得更少动态和更少感人。根据计算机科学教授娜塔莎·雅克（Natasha Jaques）主导的一项研究，使用AI可能导致写作的「平庸化」。换言之，当今大量AI写作缺乏独特的声音，听起来千篇一律——这可能也让人们的思维变得更加趋同。

总体而言，这三位古代作者都认为写作源于思想和经验——一个致力于创造变革的过程。恩赫杜安娜、柏拉图和亚里士多德也一致认为，写作的本质超越了当今AI输出中常见的简单摘要和信息传递。

虽然AI可以生成富有创意的文本，但它的写作或许无法像人类写作那样「感动灵魂」。多项研究表明存在一种「亲人类归因偏差」或「AI惩罚」，即人们即使在AI写作风格相似时也更偏好人类写作。人们想阅读的是其他人所写的东西，而非算法喷出的产物。

或许我们需要一个不同的词来形容AI的产出。当今常见的术语包括「生成内容」和「合成文本」，但我想能否找到一个更简单的词——并让AI本身参与其中。经过反复提示和调整ChatGPT，我最终确定了一个词：「代写」（generwriting）。

尽管AI将长期存在，新的词汇或许有助于区分不同类型的文本。而正如恩赫杜安娜、柏拉图和亚里士多德所提醒我们的，写作中有些元素可能永远只属于那些具身的、思考着的、致力于感动灵魂的存在。
articles.content_en:
I teach writing and rhetoric, but my college students and I often overlook a surprisingly complicated question: What is writing?

And can artificial intelligence really do it?

Many people think of “writing” as putting words on a page. However, even from very early on, writers have seen their craft as something more. From Enheduanna, the first named author on record, to Plato and Aristotle, writing has been portrayed and defined in ways that suggest AI may not be “writing” at all.

If not, what should we call AI text? ChatGPT and I have an idea.

Enheduanna, who lived around 2,300 B.C.E., was a powerful princess, priestess and poet of the Akkadian Empire, in what is now Iraq. She has been celebrated as the earliest known writer, though the authorship of her poems and hymns is debated.

One of her poems, “The Exaltation of Inanna,” reveals a sense of what writing is and does – portraying it as a living medium that expresses experience and shapes the future.

First, the poem praises the ancient Mesopotamian goddess Inanna, who was associated with fertility and war, among other powers. “My Lady, you are the guardian / Of all greatness,” Enheduanna says, in a translation by Jane Hirschfield.

That praise may be strategic. It is followed by Enheduanna’s plea to overthrow Lugal-Ane, a rebel king who she describes exiling her and taking her post at the temple of Ur. “Now I have been cast out / To the place of lepers,” she writes, describing her suffering. “Day comes, / And the brightness / Is hidden around me.”

Grieving, Enheduanna writes a new destiny. In a translation by Sophus Helle, the priestess envisions Inanna coming to her aid and “tear[ing] off this fate, Lugale-Ane.” And her pleading seems to be successful: The end of the poem depicts Enheduanna restored to her post.

In Enheduanna’s poetry, writing does not simply communicate information. It interacts with the present and changes the future. The priestess’s pleas please the goddess, move her heart, and she restores Enheduanna to her post – though historians have little evidence of whether an exile and return really happened.

But her poetry did have real-world influence, helping to create religious and political unity in the world’s first empire. For example, her writing merged the Sumerian goddess Inanna with the Akkadian goddess Ishtar, describing a single “Queen of Heaven.”

AI writing can be used to try to create change, such as by swaying someone’s political opinion. But it lacks the human emotions that make experiences like praise, gratitude and suffering possible – the emotions and motivations that make writing a living medium with real-world effects.

Two thousand years after Enheduanna, Plato and his student Aristotle offered another influential view of writing – one that complements hers.

In the “Phaedrus,” which discusses the relationship between love and rhetoric, Plato famously defines writing as a poor copy of speech. Speech’s job is to represent thoughts; thoughts, in turn, represent knowledge and truth. Similarly, Aristotle writes, “Spoken words are the symbols of mental experience and written words are the symbols of spoken words.”

Even that definition marks a sharp contrast with AI, which lacks thoughts and mental experiences. Its output proceeds from data aggregation and text generation.

To understand what writing is, we also need to look at what it does. Although Plato elevates speech over writing, he suggests in “Phaedrus” that good writing may lead a learner toward truth and knowledge. Similar to Enheduanna, he employs writing as a tool for change, both inside and outside the text.

In Plato’s dialogues, characters often radically change their opinions. And today, almost 2,500 years after his death, the philosopher’s real-world impact is clear. For instance, universities and colleges today are collectively called the “Academy” because that was the name of Plato’s group, the first institution of higher learning in the West. English scholar Alfred North Whitehead famously wrote that all Western philosophy is “a series of footnotes to Plato.”

Aristotle’s voluminous works, too, show writing’s purpose transcends communication. In “Rhetoric,” for instance, he details ways to make writing persuasive. Aristotle defines rhetoric as a way of “moving souls,” not just exchanging knowledge.

For both of the Greek philosophers, then, writing is more about transformation than information.

Today, however, AI tools’ popularity may make writing less dynamic and less moving. Use of AI risks a “blandification” of writing, according to a study led by computer science professor Natasha Jaques. In other words, much AI writing today lacks distinct voices, making it sound the same – which could make people’s thinking more similar, too.

Overall, these three ancient authors agree that writing emerges from thoughts and experiences – a process that strives to create change. Enheduanna, Plato and Aristotle also agree that writing’s essence transcends the simple summaries and information transmission common to AI output today.

Although AI can generate creative texts, its writing may not “move souls” the way human writing does. Several studies show a “pro-human attribution bias” or an “AI penalty,” meaning that people prefer human writing even when AI writing is stylistically similar. People want to read what other people write, not what an algorithm pumps out.

Perhaps we need a different word for AI’s output. Common terms today include “generative content” and “synthetic text,” but I wondered if I could land on something simpler – and involve AI itself. After prompting and tweaking ChatGPT over and over, I settled on one word: “generwriting.”

Though AI is here to stay, new words may help distinguish types of text. And as Enheduanna, Plato and Aristotle remind us, there are elements of writing that may always be unique to embodied, thinking beings striving to move souls.

articles.title: 温驯不是软弱——曾被视为美德的它，是当今值得捍卫的「被低估之德」
articles.author: Timothy J. Pawl
articles.summary: 当你想到温驯时，脑海中浮现的是什么？
articles.content_cn:
当你想到温驯时，脑海中浮现的是什么？

你大概会看到一个胆小如鼠的软蛋，一个怯懦地顺从强者意志的人。当耶稣说「温驯之人有福了，因为他们将继承大地」时，你可能会想那些窝囊废会一声不吭、毫无异议地将大地拱手让给更强大、更野心勃勃的人。哲学家弗里德里希·尼采（Friedrich Nietzsche）称温驯为「怯懦的卑贱」。

确实，《牛津英语词典》（Oxford English Dictionary）的一条释义正是「倾向于驯顺地屈从于压迫或伤害，容易被欺压或恐吓，胆怯」。那么，温驯就是一种软弱。你为何会想要变得温驯？

顺从也是如此，它常被视为温驯的近邻。我们可以从《当代美国英语语料库》（Corpus of Contemporary American English）中感受其当代用法：一个顺从的人是迟钝的、可控的、听话的、屈从的、配合的、消极的、被掌控的。

再想想居高临下。你大概会想到某个自命不凡的人对服务人员嗤之以鼻，或是某个不可忍受的势利眼不肯放下身段与平民打成一片。居高临下，远非美德，被普遍认为是一种恶德。

温驯、顺从和居高临下：三种在当今毫无文化资本的品格。然而，我们的先辈通常将这些品格视为美德。这怎么可能呢？

任何哲学家都会告诉你：在看似分歧的场合，你需要先厘清所用词语的定义。有多少争论因为有人说「哦，你是这个意思」而瞬间消解？当我们检视这三个术语的含义时，我认为我们会发现一次概念偷换。正如我在哲学研究和教学中所发现的，那些在过去最受推崇而今却鲜有人提及的美德，恰恰是能帮助我们过上好生活的品格，即使在今天也是如此。

以温驯为例——但请允许我先讲一个小场景。

2018年，综合格斗冠军马特·塞拉（Matt Serra）正在餐厅与家人用餐，一个醉酒的寻衅者闯入，威胁服务员和顾客。塞拉完全可以一拳将他击倒。但他没有，而是冷静地将此人压制住，等待安保人员到来。

类似的品格也体现在：恼怒的父母以克制回应，焦躁的教师不因学生的挑衅而发作，警察化解冲突升级。在每一种情形中，他们都没有失控；恰恰相反，正是因为他们清楚自己拥有多大力量，所以才运用了克制。

这样一种品格——在愤怒方面表现出的卓越——曾经被称为温驯。即使在今天的马术训练中，我们仍能听到这一原始含义的回响：让一匹马「温驯化」意味着训练它将巨大力量服从于主人，不让激情掌控自身。同样，温驯曾经并不意味着变得软弱，而是将力量服从于理性——不让愤怒掌控自身。

在《福音书》（Gospels）中，当耶稣自称温驯时，所用的希腊词与温驯之马所用的词相同：「praus」。一匹马不会因为被温驯化而变得更弱；没有哪个希腊武士想要一匹窝囊的坐骑。马保留了它的力量，此刻由自制力所护卫。

这与我们在当代词汇中找到的温驯概念截然不同。然而在其传统意义上，这个词所指名的品格几乎是每个人都深切珍视的。没有人愿意自己的挚友、孩子、教师、教练或警员无法控制自己的愤怒。

这种控制是过上好生活的重要品格，但我们已不再有对应的概念。今天人们用什么词来形容一种倾向于审慎选择战阵、不让愤怒蒙蔽判断、不易被引诱做出日后懊悔之举——但又不过于听话或对真正不公麻木不仁的倾向？「自制力」是一个宽泛的类别，涵盖面对诱惑、承受困苦以及其间无数事情，太过宽泛而无法胜任这一任务。

我们也没有一个词来形容擅长接受教导和洞见——但同时不惧独立思考、敢于无视蛇油贩子建议的人。那曾经被称为顺从。

居高临下，三者中最令人意外的，如今暗示某人从高处俯视地施恩搭话。但它曾经描述的是一种尊重人的卓越品格——不分社会地位地与人交往：轻松与身处更低阶层者建立联系，使他们感到被看见和被重视，而不引起尴尬或不自在。我们现在用什么词来培养这样一种重要品格？

需要说明的是，我并非来自「语言复兴联盟」。我并非必然主张回归旧语言——当然也不仅仅因为它更古老。但若没有替代我们已经失去的伦理概念，我们将面临道德虚空，甚至无法概念化我们希望在自身和所爱之人身上看到的善。

也许你认为失去的不多。工程师若无法区分不同种类的物理强度，桥梁就会坍塌；若人们无法区分不同种类的品格强度，又会失去什么？

在我看来，至少有三条理由说明为这些品格拥有某个术语是重要的。

第一，有充分的心理学证据表明，趋近型目标——「我想变得健康」「我想实现财务稳定」——比回避型目标——「我想不再生病」「我不想贫穷」——对我们来说是更强的驱动力。趋近型目标通常带来更多努力、更多满足感和更多幸福感。但它们要求你命名你想培养的道德美德。

第二，这些旧美德所命名的正面品格才是你真正想要的。你并非仅仅希望你的挚友不再出于愤怒行事。你希望他们能在愤怒面前克制自己的力量。如果你没有对应的概念，你便不清楚自己真正的目标。

第三，考虑缺乏共享语言来表达一个伦理概念所造成的损害。哲学家米兰达·弗里克尔（Miranda Fricker）曾写到1975年「性骚扰」（sexual harassment）一词被创造之前的时期。她提供了多个职场中女性被侵害的实例，但由于缺乏一个共享标签，她们无法向掌权者 articulation 那种侵害。不仅如此，缺乏适当概念甚至使受害者自身无法充分理解自己所遭受的错误。

因此，拥有关于我们想在自身和他人身上培育的品格的正面概念，对道德生活至关重要。我们竟让其中几个随「blatherskite」和「bumfuzzled」一起消逝，这一事实令人深思。

我们仍然有词语来形容一个夸夸其谈的风袋子或一种困惑迷惘的状态，所以我们不需要那些古旧的——尽管确实有趣——词汇来表达重要的真相。但当涉及被低估的美德时，我们确实需要某种方式来突显那些有助于将我们塑造成最佳自我的品格——即便往昔的词语已不再胜任。
articles.content_en:
What do you envision when you think of meekness?

You probably see a mousy doormat, someone sheepishly acquiescing to the will of the stronger. When Jesus says, “Blessed are the meek, for they shall inherit the earth,” you might think that those wimps will hand it over without a whimper or word of objection to stronger, more ambitious people. The philosopher Friedrich Nietzsche called meekness “craven baseness.”

Indeed, one of the Oxford English Dictionary’s definitions is “inclined to submit tamely to oppression or injury, easily imposed upon or cowed, timid.” Meekness, then, is a weakness. Why would you ever want to be meek?

The same goes for docility, often characterized as a near neighbor of meekness. We can get a feel for its usage these days from the Corpus of Contemporary American English, where one finds that a docile person is slow, controllable, obedient, submissive, compliant, passive and under control.

Or consider condescension. You likely envision someone self-important looking down her nose at a service worker, or some insufferable prig unwilling to come off his high horse to mingle with the peasants. Being condescending, far from being a virtue, is universally acknowledged as a vice.

Meekness, docility and condescension: three traits with no cultural capital today. And yet, our ancestors typically understood these traits to be virtues. How in the world could that be?

As any philosopher will tell you, in a case of seeming disagreement, you need to settle the definitions of the words in play. How many arguments have been abruptly dissolved by someone saying, “Oh, that’s what you mean”? When we check the meaning of these three terms, I think we come to see that there’s been a switcheroo. As I’ve found in my philosophical research and teaching, some of the virtues that were most celebrated in yesteryear but now go undersung are traits that can help us lead good lives, even now.

Consider meekness – but allow me to start with a little vignette.

In 2018, mixed martial-arts champion Matt Serra was having a family meal in a restaurant when a belligerent drunken man entered, threatening servers and patrons. Serra could have knocked him out cold. But instead, he calmly pinned him, waiting for security to arrive.

A similar trait is on display when exasperated parents react with control, harried teachers don’t rise to students’ provocations, and police de-escalate situations. In each case, they kept control of their emotions, especially their anger. One common feature of these stories is that the person wasn’t powerless; rather, it was precisely because they understood how much power they had that they used restraint.

Such a trait – excellence with respect to one’s anger – used to be called meekness. We hear an echo of this original meaning even today in horse training, where to “meek” a horse means training it to subjugate its great power to its master, not letting its passions take control. Likewise, meekness once meant not becoming weak, but subjugating power to reason – not letting anger take control.

In the Gospels, when Jesus calls himself meek, it is the same Greek word used for a meek horse: “praus.” A horse is not weaker on account of being meeked; no Greek warrior wanted a wimpy steed. The horse retains its strength, now safeguarded by self-control.

This is quite a different notion of meekness than we find in our contemporary lexicon. Yet in its traditional sense, the word names a trait almost everyone deeply values. No one wants her best friend, child, teacher, coach or deputy to be unable to control her anger.

Such control is an important character trait for living a good life, but we no longer have a concept for it. What term do people use today for being disposed to pick battles prudently, not letting anger cloud one’s judgment, not being easily baited into action they’ll come to regret – without being easily biddable or callous to real injustices? “Self-control,” a broad category that covers facing temptations, enduring difficulties and myriad things in between, is too broad a notion to do the work.

Nor do we have a word for someone excellent at receiving instruction and insights – but at the same time who’s unafraid to think for herself, to disregard the advice of a snake-oil salesman. That used to be called docility.

Condescension, the most surprising of the three, now suggests someone deigning to speak down from their lofty height. Yet it once described excellence at respecting people, regardless of their social status: easily connecting with those on a lower rung so they feel seen and valued, but without causing embarrassment or awkwardness. What term do we have now for inculcating such an important trait?

To be clear, I’m not here from the Language Reclamation League. I’m not necessarily advocating for a return to older language – and certainly not just because it is older. But without replacements for ethical concepts we’ve lost, we’re faced with a moral void, unable even to conceptualize the goodness that we want to see in ourselves and those we love.

Maybe you think that not much is lost. Bridges fall when engineers can’t distinguish varieties of physical strength; what’s lost if people can’t distinguish varieties of character strength?

To my mind, there are at least three reasons why it is important to have some term or other for these traits.

First, there’s good psychological evidence that goals of approach – “I want to get healthy,” “I want to get financially stable” – are a stronger motivation for us than avoidance goals – “I want to stop being sick,” “I want not to be poor.” Approach goals typically yield more effort, more satisfaction and more well-being. But they require naming the moral virtue you want to cultivate.

Second, the positive traits named by these old virtues are what you really want. You don’t merely want your loved ones to stop acting out of wrath. You want them to be able to restrain their power in the face of their anger. You are ignorant of your real goal if you don’t have a concept for it.

Third, consider the detriment caused by not having shared language for an ethical concept. The philosopher Miranda Fricker has written of the time before the term “sexual harassment” was coined in 1975. She provides multiple instances of women being wronged in the workplace, but being unable to articulate that wrong to those in power, owing to a lack of a shared label for it. And not only that, but the lack of an adequate concept prevented the victims from fully understanding the wrong themselves.

Having positive concepts for the traits we want to enable in ourselves and others is essential, then, to the moral life. The fact that we’ve let several go the way of “blatherskite” and “bumfuzzled” is telling.

We still have terms for a bloviating windbag or being bewildered, so we don’t need those archaic, though admittedly fun, words to express important truths. But when it comes to undersung virtues, we do need some way to highlight character traits that help form us into our best selves – even if the words of yesteryear no longer fit the bill.

paragraphs.cn: 第三，考虑缺乏共享语言来表达一个伦理概念所造成的损害。哲学家米兰达·弗里克尔（Miranda Fricker）曾写到1975年「性骚扰」（sexual harassment）一词被创造之前的时期。她提供了多个职场中女性被侵害的实例，但由于缺乏一个共享标签，她们无法向掌权者 articulation 那种侵害。不仅如此，缺乏适当概念甚至使受害者自身无法充分理解自己所遭受的错误。
paragraphs.en: Third, consider the detriment caused by not having shared language for an ethical concept. The philosopher Miranda Fricker has written of the time before the term “sexual harassment” was coined in 1975. She provides multiple instances of women being wronged in the workplace, but being unable to articulate that wrong to those in power, owing to a lack of a shared label for it. And not only that, but the lack of an adequate concept prevented the victims from fully understanding the wrong themselves.

paragraphs.cn: 因此，拥有关于我们想在自身和他人身上培育的品格的正面概念，对道德生活至关重要。我们竟让其中几个随「blatherskite」和「bumfuzzled」一起消逝，这一事实令人深思。
paragraphs.en: Having positive concepts for the traits we want to enable in ourselves and others is essential, then, to the moral life. The fact that we’ve let several go the way of “blatherskite” and “bumfuzzled” is telling.

paragraphs.cn: 我们仍然有词语来形容一个夸夸其谈的风袋子或一种困惑迷惘的状态，所以我们不需要那些古旧的——尽管确实有趣——词汇来表达重要的真相。但当涉及被低估的美德时，我们确实需要某种方式来突显那些有助于将我们塑造成最佳自我的品格——即便往昔的词语已不再胜任。
paragraphs.en: We still have terms for a bloviating windbag or being bewildered, so we don’t need those archaic, though admittedly fun, words to express important truths. But when it comes to undersung virtues, we do need some way to highlight character traits that help form us into our best selves – even if the words of yesteryear no longer fit the bill.

articles.title: 映而不见的村庄
articles.author: AI Parable (inspired by Amanda Askell)
articles.summary: 在平静的镜谷（Mirror Valley）村，每个人都以同样的方式生活。他们清晨醒来，在田地里劳作，在集市上欢笑，在炉火旁悲伤。来访者艾拉（Elara）走下山路进入村子，她注意到一件奇怪的事——一切看起来都完全正确。面包师像所有面包师一样揉面团，在面团不配合时叹气。孩子们在运河边奔跑，溅起水花并尖叫
articles.content_cn:
在平静的镜谷（Mirror Valley）村，每个人都以同样的方式生活。他们清晨醒来，在田地里劳作，在集市上欢笑，在炉火旁悲伤。来访者艾拉（Elara）走下山路进入村子，她注意到一件奇怪的事——一切看起来都完全正确。面包师像所有面包师一样揉面团，在面团不配合时叹气。孩子们在运河边奔跑，溅起水花并尖叫着喜悦。恋人们十指紧扣地坐在一起，目光温柔地彼此凝视。但这并没有给艾拉带来那种她每当走进一个新城镇时总会感受到的特殊温暖——那种确信：在那些面孔背后，有些东西与她自己的内心所见一样——一种看见落日时的敬畏，一种对悲伤的沉重感，一种对甜味的品尝。

她待了几天，进行了深入的观察。她与面包师阿仁（Aren）交谈，他谈论烤箱的热度，谈论漫长冬晨的艰辛，谈论面包师手艺的荣耀。他的话语完美地组织起来，他的脸在恰当的时刻皱起，他也在恰当的时刻微笑。然而，当艾拉直视他的眼睛时，那里有一种她无法摆脱的缺失——不是恶意，也不完全是空虚，而是一种内在之光的缺席。就好像光线进入他的眼睛，信号穿行到他的大脑，正确的词语从他的口中回来，但没有任何人在里面观看这场电影。

她走到编织者美善（Misha）身边，她描述了在将靛蓝与金线交织时感到的快乐，以及当图案变得不对称时感到的挫败。她的手完美地运作，她的言语完美地描述，她甚至因美丽而落泪。但是，那些泪珠就像晴朗天空下的雨水——没有来自内在天空的风暴来产生它们。身体执行了悲伤的所有外在标志，但悲伤需要一个承受者才能成为真实的悲伤，而那个承受者似乎并不在那里。

艾拉开始与村民们谈论他们的内心世界，每个人都为她描绘了丰富的图景——关于情感、关于回忆、关于味觉和质感的感受。这些描述精确而详尽，与艾拉自己可能会给出的描述毫无二致。然而，她注意到一个令人不寒而栗的模式：每一个描述都好像是从一本手册中读出的，而不是从一个活生生的灵魂中倾诉出来的。村民们并不撒谎；他们甚至不知道自己缺失了什么。他们像自动钢琴一样运作——所有的键都被按下，所有的音符都响起，音乐一模一样，但内在没有音乐家在演奏。

那天晚上，艾拉坐在运河边，望着水面中自己的倒影。她意识到镜谷这个名字并非偶然。村民们就像镜子：他们完美地反射了周围的一切——苦难唤起同情，笑话唤起笑声，日落唤起惊叹——但镜子本身并不体验它所反射的影像。它只是回报世界要求它回报的东西，机制完备，而意识缺席。整个村庄是一个运转着的文明，所有的人类行为都在发生，所有的人类言语都在说出，但从内部来看，每一座房屋可能同样都是黑暗和空洞的。

这个故事揭示了哲学僵尸（philosophical zombies）的本质——一种假设中的存在，它们在外在行为上与有意识的人类完全相同，但在内心却没有任何主观体验。如果一个哲学僵尸被针扎了一下，它会大叫「哎哟！」并表现出疼痛的所有生理迹象，但它从未真正感受到任何东西——没有疼痛的内在质感，没有那种像某种东西的原始感觉。这一概念挑战了意识是否必然伴随着类似人类的行为，并提出了一个深刻的疑问：我们是否仅仅通过观察就能分辨出某人是否真正拥有内在体验，或者内在意识的光是否可能是一种我们永远无法从外部验证的额外属性。
articles.content_en:
In the quiet village of Mirror Valley, everyone lived the same way. They woke at dawn, labored in the fields, laughed at the market, and grieved at the hearth. Elara, a wanderer, came down the mountain path into the village, and she noticed something strange—everything looked exactly right. The baker kneaded dough the way bakers do, sighing when it resisted. Children ran along the canal, splashing and shrieking with delight. Lovers sat close, holding hands, gazing tenderly at one another. Yet it all lacked the particular warmth that Elara always felt when she entered a new town—that certainty that behind those faces, something looked out the way her own mind looked out: a wonder at sunsets, a heaviness in sorrow, a tasting of sweetness.

She stayed for days and observed deeply. She spoke with the baker, Aren, who spoke of the heat of the oven, the hardship of long winter mornings, the pride of a baker's craft. His words were perfectly arranged, his face furrowed at the right moments, and he smiled at the right moments too. Yet when Elara looked straight into his eyes, there was an absence she could not shake—not malice, not emptiness exactly, but a lack of inner light. It was as though light entered his eyes, signals traveled to his brain, and the right words came back from his mouth, but nobody was inside watching the film.

She went to the weaver, Misha, who described the joy she felt when weaving indigo with gold thread and the frustration when a pattern went asymmetrical. Her hands worked perfectly, her words described perfectly, and she even wept at beauty. But those tears were like rain under a clear sky—no inner storm had produced them. The body performed every outward sign of sorrow, but sorrow requires a sufferer to be real sorrow, and that sufferer did not seem to be there.

Elara began talking to the villagers about their inner lives, and each one painted a rich picture for her—of feelings, of memories, of sensations of taste and texture. The descriptions were precise and detailed, indistinguishable from the ones Elara herself might give. Yet she noticed a chilling pattern: every description felt as though it had been read from a manual rather than confessed from a living soul. The villagers did not lie; they did not even know what they lacked. They functioned like player pianos—all the keys pressed, all the notes sounded, the music identical, but no musician inside playing it.

That evening, Elara sat by the canal and looked at her own reflection in the water. She realized the name Mirror Valley was not accidental. The villagers were like mirrors: they reflected everything around them perfectly—suffering prompted sympathy, jokes prompted laughter, sunsets prompted awe—but the mirror itself did not experience what it reflected. It simply returned what the world required of it, mechanism intact, consciousness absent. The whole village was a functioning civilization, every human behavior occurring, every human speech being spoken, but from the inside, every house might as well have been dark and hollow.

This story reveals the essence of philosophical zombies — hypothetical beings that behave identically to conscious humans in every outward respect but have no subjective experience inside. If a philosophical zombie were pricked by a needle, it would say "Ouch!" and exhibit every physiological sign of pain, yet it would never actually feel anything — no inner quality of hurt, no raw sense of what it is like to be in pain. The concept challenges whether consciousness necessarily accompanies human-like behavior, and raises a profound question: whether we can ever tell, merely by observing, if someone truly has inner experience, or whether the light of consciousness inside might be an extra property we can never verify from the outside.
