articles.title: 罗易谈政府为何必须有伦理在场
articles.author: Shomik Dasgupta
articles.summary: 印度思想家罗易（Rammohun Roy）相信，良好的治理必须贴近：距离使英帝国变得残忍
articles.content_cn:
1831年，一个身披长袍的男子在利物浦（Liverpool）走下轮船。他没有英国人承认的官方头衔，没有殖民政府中的职位，也没有王室的邀请。他的名字叫罗易（Rammohun Roy）。他来自加尔各答（Calcutta），派遣他的不是英帝国，而是日益衰弱的德里（Delhi）莫卧儿（Mughal）朝廷。他公开宣称的使命是代表年迈的皇帝阿克巴二世（Akbar II）出使伦敦。但罗易还带来了别的东西，某种悄然激进的东西。他的文件中有一份详尽的文献，论述印度在英国统治下如何被治理，以及如何才能更公正地被治理。它的标题是：《印度司法与财税制度阐释》（Exposition of the Judicial and Revenue Systems of India）。

这一时刻意义深远，尽管当时几乎无人察觉。一位印度思想家不仅要求改革，还带着自己对帝国伦理缺陷的诊断来到了帝国的心脏。他的长袍在伦敦雾蒙蒙的街道上或许显得格格不入，但他传递的信息却尖锐而现代：权力必须贴近才能公正。他来到英国不仅仅是外交行为，更具有象征意义。罗易走进帝国的核心，不仅是为了抗议，更是为了建言。正如他所主张的，来自被殖民者的批评并非自相矛盾，而是一种伦理性的介入。更激进的是，他认为英国可以从倾听中获益。罗易呼吁的不是反叛，而是建立在共情、知识与责任之上的改革。他所提供的是一种统治愿景，不基于支配，而基于伦理性的在场。

要理解罗易的激进性，首先必须认清他所面对的那个帝国的独特性质。英国东印度公司（East India Company）并非作为典型的殖民国家进行统治，而是作为一家拥有私人军队的跨国公司。它的统治是官僚化的、榨取性的，且常常不受问责。在这个世界中，罗易的声音之所以突出，不仅因为它是印度的，更因为它是理性的、比较性的和普世主义的。他讲的是权利与治理、道德义务与政治贴近的语言——一种英国人自称能听懂、而罗易用以追究其责任的语言。

表面上看，《阐释》像是一份枯燥的报告。但其内里却有一个出人意料的论断：英国在印度统治的最大问题不仅仅是压迫或腐败，而是距离。法庭使用的语言是普通人听不懂的。行政官员很少在一个地方待得足够久，以了解当地的运作方式。而决策则在遥远的地方做出——在加尔各答或伦敦，由那些与所影响的生活毫无关联的人做出。

要理解罗易为何持有这些观点，我们需要了解塑造他的非凡人生。他1772年出生于孟加拉（Bengal）一个富裕的婆罗门（Brahmin）家庭，所受的教育涵盖多种同时代人鲜少能接触到的思想传统。他早年在巴特那（Patna）学习波斯语和阿拉伯语，在那里接触到伊斯兰神学、逻辑学和法学。后来，在瓦拉纳西（Varanasi），他研习梵文典籍，吸收了印度哲学传统中核心的形而上学与仪轨知识。他还涉猎耆那教（Jain）和佛教（Buddhist）思想，并逐渐对基督教神学和启蒙运动的理性主义产生了深厚兴趣。

这种独特的教育不仅使罗易在智识上充满好奇心，更使他善于比较。他总是追寻不同传统之间的对应：伊斯兰教和印度教对统治者的道德义务各有什么说法？基督教的「上帝之国」观念与波斯化（Persianate）的正义观有何关联？西方自由主义与本土的伦理行为观念是契合还是冲突？这些并非抽象的问题。罗易看到它们正在他周围的殖民世界中上演。

从1803年到1814年，他在东印度公司担任各种行政职务——先是做蒙希（munshi，即文书或秘书），然后任税务官，最后担任翻译和波斯语专家。他被派驻到孟加拉和比哈尔（Bihar）各地的城镇，这些经历成为他政治思想的熔炉。他观察在遥远的董事会议室里制定的政策如何被推行到基层，往往笨拙不堪。他目睹地方知识如何被习以为常地忽视，语言障碍又如何造成混乱与疏离。

罗易对殖民行政的熟悉并非浮于表面。他熟悉它的文书、它的人员、它的惯例。实际上，他就是这台机器的一部分。但他同时也悄然而犀利地批评它。他看到这套系统多么容易从官僚制滑向威权主义——不是通过宏大的压迫之举，而是通过千百次小小的漠视。

正是这些经历促使罗易后来在伦敦主张，殖民统治不仅饱受不公，更饱受疏离。英国人在统治印度，却不了解印度。他们凭借抽象、凭借规章、报告和统计来治理，而非凭借在场。罗易相信这不仅效率低下，更是不道德的。正是这种植根于他与权力亲身遭遇的伦理批评，赋予了《阐释》那种沉静而有力的力量。

罗易的批评也并不限于英国官员。他还号召印度精英反思自己的角色。他认为太多人接受了合作的奖赏，却没有承担批评的责任。罗易想要一种不同的参与——一种从内部追究权力责任的方式，运用法律、理性和道德劝说的工具。

在许多方面，罗易到1831年为止的人生都是在为他将在英国提出的论点做准备。他花了三十年穿梭于多个世界之间：波斯的与梵文的，莫卧儿的与英国的。《阐释》是这段旅程的集大成。它不是来自边缘的呐喊，而是来自一个曾从内部审视这套系统、并希望它做得更好之人的挑战。他的提议简单却大胆：统治者应当在场、可见，并对所统治之人负责。权力不应悬浮于人们的生活之上，而应生活在他们中间。

罗易出使英国，至少在形式上，是作为莫卧儿皇帝阿克巴二世的使者。到那时，曾经是南亚最强大帝国势力的莫卧儿王朝，已沦为昔日自身的影子。它的领土范围微乎其微，国库枯竭，朝廷很大程度上只是象征性的。然而对罗易而言，这种象征意义至关重要。皇帝在政治上或许已被削弱，但在罗易眼中，他仍是一位主权人物，其正当性不来自征服或贸易，而来自一种更古老的、浸透道德的统治观念。

这种联系不止是礼仪性的。罗易多年来与莫卧儿朝廷培养关系，并被授予罗阇（Raja）的头衔——英国官员私下嘲笑此举，却无法完全无视。他的出使英国也是一次政治想象力的微妙之举：试图在帝国权力的走廊中复兴印度-波斯王权的伦理记忆。在将皇帝的声音带到英国王室面前时，罗易坚持认为，印度的政治传统并未被抹去，它们只是被边缘化，等待被承认。

罗易与莫卧儿的关联还揭示了早期殖民印度的层级化、相互交叠的主权格局。他并不把本土王权与殖民统治视为不可调和的对立面。相反，他看到了融合的可能：一个在其中更古老的正义、责任与公共伦理规范（在波斯化的朝廷传统中培养的价值观）能够约束东印度公司功利主义逻辑的体制。在这一视角下，莫卧儿朝廷不是化石，而是提供了一种方式来提醒英国人：没有正当性的权力是脆弱的，而正当性并非仅仅是军事力量或行政触及范围的函数。

在他的著作中，罗易常常呈现这种综合。《阐释》中充满对英国法和启蒙理想的引用，但其道德韵律无可错认地受到波斯化伦理思想的塑造。诸如正义、贴近和伦理问责等概念——在伊斯兰政治写作中很常见——构成了他思想的基础。罗易用英文写作时并未抛弃这些传统，他翻译了它们。在此过程中，他创造了一种政治语汇，能同时对皇帝的朝廷和英国议会发言。

对英国公众而言，罗易的莫卧儿渊源或许显得古雅，甚至不合时宜。但对罗易来说，它们提供了一个发出批评的平台。因此，他前往英国的旅程层层叠叠地承载着意图。它不仅是为一位衰落君主请愿，更是宣告：印度的政治声音仍能为自己发声，不是以对抗的方式，而是以对话的方式。

1832年在伦敦出版的《阐释》，是对英国在印度行政的一份极为扎实的批评。罗易不使用革命的话语，而是谈论改革、精确与道德责任。该文献分为若干部分，详述殖民司法和财税制度的缺陷。

罗易从日常现实入手。农民因过高的税额核定而陷入债务。法律程序令普通人困惑，因为诉讼使用的是他们不熟悉的语言。法官和收税官轮换过于频繁，根本来不及了解他们理应监管的地方情境。其结果是疏离——不仅在法律上，更在生活中。被治理者无法在治理者身上认出自己，而治理者很少努力向被治理者学习。

罗易勾勒的不仅是官僚效率低下，还有一个更深层的政治问题：一种脱离了它所影响之人的治理形式。他主张，在伦敦或由遥远的公司董事做出的决策，如果不纳入地方现实与声音，永远不可能公正。罗易主张任用印度法官、使用当地语言的法庭，以及行政上的连续性。他要求的不是仅仅由印度人统治，而是一种根植于伦理实践和公众参与的问责制。

这一伦理核心——罗易既通过启蒙理想、也通过波斯化伦理来理解它——坚持认为治理需要熟悉、专注和道德清明。他呼吁的不是全盘抛弃官僚制，而是对其进行改革。他相信，一个政府如果被组织成能够倾听、回应和自我解释，它仍可以是正当的。但这种回应性需要他所谓的「定居」（domiciliation）：权力居住在它所治理之处。

在提出这一论证时，罗易预见了对现代行政的一大批评——即它会变得非人格化、程序化和冷漠疏离。远在马克斯·韦伯（Max Weber）或后来的官僚制理论家之前，罗易就观察到，遥远的治理如何常常把正义转化为仪式，把法律转化为行话，把问责转化为空洞的例行公事。他的《阐释》充满了对这类动态的描绘，不是理论上的，而是深具经验性的。

罗易不是仅仅断言抽象原则，而是展示不公在基层如何运作。一个农民因错误的核定而被征税，失去了土地。一个诉讼当事人出庭数月，对法官说的每一个字都听不懂。一个村庄苦等数年，才等来一位官员解决土地纠纷。每一个例子都成为一扇窗，揭示一个脱节的系统如何施暴——不是喧哗地，而是日复一日地。罗易在此的方法颇具官僚特色，甚至可以说是程序性的。但它带有尖锐的政治锋芒。他不太关心对殖民主义的抽象谴责，而更关注不公运作的精细机制。这些不仅是行政上的怪癖，它们就是疏离的机器。

然而罗易仍然抱有希望。他相信改革是可能的，只要印度和英国官员都致力于服务他们所治理的人民，伦理治理就可以建立起来。他的批评不生于意识形态，而生于经验——经验被磨砺成道德愿景。在许多方面，《阐释》是一份行政文献。但在罗易手中，它变成了一种政治哲学：一种视治理为关怀的愿景。

这正是罗易的《阐释》如此动人的原因。它不仅是殖民政策的遗物，更是一场关于权力被公正行使时应当呈现何种面貌的对话。在一个数据驱动的决策和官僚理性再次受到审视的时代，罗易的作品提醒我们：良善治理的首要条件不是信息，而是在场。

罗易的思想并非源自任何单一的思想传统。它由一种非凡的影响、智识相遇与道德承诺的汇流所塑造。他的伦理学不是某一种文化或信条的产物，而是由多种传统编织而成，每一种都为正义、责任和权力的目的提供了不同的语汇。

他最早的著作之一、约1803年写成的《一神论者之赠》（Tuhfat-ul-Muwahhidin，意为「献给信仰独一真主者的礼物」），展现了他对伊斯兰神学、尤其是被称为「阿赫拉格」（akhlaq）的伦理传统的深入研习。在这一文献传统中，权力与美德不可分割；统治者不仅仅是君主，更是对神圣正义和社会责任负责的道德主体。借鉴纳西尔·丁·图西（Nasir al-Din al-Tusi）等思想家，罗易沉浸于一种传统之中——在其中，国王的首要职责不是扩张领土，而是培育公正与节制。

从印度教经典，尤其是《奥义书》（Upanishads）中，罗易汲取了精神义务（达摩，dharma）的观念，以及自我认知具有公共后果的思想。在这一世界观中，国王是宇宙与社会秩序的守护者。他所施行的正义不仅属于他个人，更映照着宇宙的平衡。罗易尤为被「真理是统一的，尽管其在不同传统中的表达各异」这一观念所吸引。这给了他跨越边界寻求道德指引的信心。这种比较方法绝非智识游戏——它是一种伦理上的必要。罗易相信，道德清明往往浮现于传统的边缘，而非核心。良善治理必须是多语言的、道德上多元的、智识上慷慨的。

基督教以另一种方式塑造了罗易的伦理。通过与传教士的交往和对《新约》的阅读，罗易逐渐钦佩耶稣的道德教导——尤其是对怜悯、谦卑以及反抗专断权威的强调。他相信耶稣示范了一种领导方式，它抬举弱者、质疑根深蒂固的权力，并拒绝将信仰与伦理分离。罗易没有皈依基督教，但他在其中找到了一种与自己信念相共鸣的道德清明。

同样重要的是他通过接触欧洲哲学而遇到的自由主义思想。他读约翰·洛克（John Locke）论治理，读威廉·布莱克斯通（William Blackstone）论法律权利，读孟德斯鸠（Montesquieu）论分权。这些思想家给了他一套关于政治问责、宪政限制与公民自由的语言。罗易并非简单照搬这些思想，而是透过他多语言、多宗教教育的透镜来诠释它们。当洛克谈论生命、自由与财产时，罗易听到了更古老的关于正义、责任与统治者伦理品格的观念的回响。

从这一智识生态中浮现的，是一种混合的统治伦理。罗易不满足于做一个翻译者或评注者。他将自己的来源融汇成一套连贯的道德哲学：它坚持统治者是管家，而不仅仅是行政者；他们的权力是一种责任，而非一种权利。他们的正当性不来自征服或头衔，而来自他们与所治理之人的伦理贴近。

重要的是，罗易的伦理并非抽象的。它们旨在以具体方式指导治理。他主张，正义必须对其臣民而言是可理解的；法律必须是可理解的；政策必须反映受其影响之人的切身境况。这意味着语言、连续性和文化知识不仅是行政的附属品，它们是伦理要求。一个用波斯语或英语来审理孟加拉村民事务的法庭，不仅是效率低下，更是不公正的。

詹姆斯·伦内尔（James Rennell）所作《孟加拉与比哈尔地图》（A Map of Bengal and Bahar），选自1781年《孟加拉地图集》（An Atlas of Bengal），献给英属亚洲领地总督沃伦·黑斯廷斯（Warren Hastings）。公共领域。

因此，罗易的伦理愿景将道德严正性与行政洞见结合在一起。它追问：如何才能在一片多语言、多宗教且被殖民的土地上公正地统治？并坚持认为，答案不在于整齐划一的控制，而在于层叠的责任。统治者必须足够贴近以理解，足够谦卑以倾听，足够有德以行动。

这一宏阔的道德框架使罗易能够充当一座桥梁——在传统之间，在帝国之间，在东西方观念之间。在一个日益分裂为殖民者与被殖民者的世界里，他提供了一种既具批判性又具联结性的政治思想模型。他的伦理学取自多种来源，成为一种用以评估、并挑战帝国新秩序的工具。

罗易的政治想象锻造于哲学、政治与公共传播的交汇处。他并非学院意义上的政治理论家，但他的著作整体上构成了一种连贯而激进的愿景：一种植根于伦理、由日常生活塑造、并通过非凡地驾驭多种思想传统而得以表达的愿景。

他跨越多种体裁写作：请愿书、随笔、公开信、小册子和报纸文章。在他创办的报纸之一《智慧之月报》（Sambad Kaumudi）中，他以直接、常常是讽刺的笔调，深入参与孟加拉的道德与公民生活。他探讨的话题从寡妇再嫁到新闻自由，从教育改革到司法程序。他的孟加拉语小册子把抽象的政治原则带入切身经验的领域。运用取自农业、家庭和民间故事的隐喻，他以普通读者能够理解并产生共鸣的方式阐述自己的主张。这绝非易事。罗易正在一种尚不存在的政治语言中开疆拓土。

甚至他的宗教著作也带有政治意味。当罗易为一神论辩护或为妇女权利声张时，他隐含地在为一个伦理性的公共领域辩护——在其中，理性、相互尊重和道德问责构成宗教权威与政治权威双重的基础。他对偶像崇拜的批评不仅仅是神学上的，也是对制度性权力的批评。

罗易的政治想象由切身经验塑造，而不仅由文本传统塑造。他对东印度公司行政内部运作的了解，使他具有对权力在基层如何运作的实务理解。这种现实主义使他区别于乌托邦思想家。他不呼吁全盘拆解英国统治，而是呼吁建立一个通过回应被治理者而使权力变得合乎伦理的体制。

因此，《阐释》必须被读作这一更宏大计划的一部分。它不仅是一份政策文献，更是一份伦理地图。罗易在勾勒治理对处于其接收端之人应当是何种感受：可触及的、公正的、可问责的。他在追问，政治制度如何才能被重新想象，以服务于人民而非仅仅管理人民。他的提议——比如任命印度法官或用当地语言进行审判——不仅基于行政逻辑，更基于道德推理。

关键的是，罗易相信沟通是权力的核心。他的多语言能力是一种策略，而不仅仅是一种技能。他用英语、波斯语、孟加拉语，偶尔也用阿拉伯语写作，针对不同受众调整每一则信息。对英国官员，他用改革的话语提供理性的批评。对印度读者，他提供讽刺、寓言和道德劝诫。这种多声部使他能够同时在多个领域运作——帝国的与方言的，精英的与大众的。

罗易的政治思想之所以难以精确界定，恰恰因为它拒绝简单的归类。它在捍卫权利上是自由主义的，在呼吁改革上是宪政的，在道德紧迫性上是神学的，在政策建议上是务实的。最重要的是，它植根于一个信念：贴近——不仅是地理上的贴近，更是理解上的贴近——对正义至关重要。

因此，罗易的政治想象既宏阔又扎实。它不梦见乌托邦，它要求改革。它不浪漫化过去，也不理想化西方；它追问的是，此时此地，可以做些什么让权力更公正。在这点上，他是现代印度政治思想的先驱。尽管他很少使用我们今天所理解的民主话语，但他的工作为其奠定了重要基础：一种伦理的、包容的、对所服务人民负责的治理愿景。

当罗易抵达英国时，他在某些政治和知识圈子中引起了轰动。英国一位论派（Unitarians）视他为在寻求理性宗教与伦理改革道路上的同道中人。同情政治改革的议员欢迎他对殖民治理的洞见。杰里米·边沁（Jeremy Bentham）和罗伯特·欧文（Robert Owen）等知识分子知道他的存在，并在某些情况下，被他论证的精确与文雅所吸引。然而，尽管有这种一时的好奇，罗易在正式的帝国圈子中仍基本处于边缘——或许被当作一桩奇闻欢迎，却未被严肃地视为政治上的平等者。

他的《阐释》并未引发全面的改革。东印度公司在司法或税收方面没有突然的改变。但这未必是一种失败。这部文献的真正意义在于其政治姿态，而非其政策影响。罗易证明，批评可以来自被殖民者，用殖民者的话语来表达，却仍能反映一种深具印度色彩的道德愿景。他的工作开创了一个先例：从那种权力被假定为不容置疑的空间内部，向权力说真话。

1833年罗易因脑膜炎在布里斯托尔（Bristol）猝然离世后，他的名声迅速演变。在孟加拉，他作为改革家受到赞颂，人们记得他反对娑提（sati，即寡妇殉夫焚身）的倡导、他使印度教教育现代化的努力，以及他共同创立的改革运动「梵社」（Brahmo Sabha）。但随着印度政治的论调变得更加民族主义，罗易的形象被简化了：他要么成为印度自由主义之父，要么成为原型民族主义英雄万神殿中一个模糊的轮廓。这常常遮蔽了他政治思想的细微之处——他对官僚制的细致关注、他对伦理贴近的坚持，以及他相信道德治理是一种关怀的实践，而不仅仅是控制。

尽管如此，罗易的思想以更微妙的方式延续下来。后来的思想家如达达拜·纳奥罗吉（Dadabhai Naoroji）、戈帕尔·克里希纳·戈卡尔（Gopal Krishna Gokhale），甚至罗宾德拉纳特·泰戈尔（Rabindranath Tagore），都继承了罗易愿景的片段。纳奥罗吉对英国统治的经济学批评，呼应了罗易关于帝国治理是疏离而榨取的坚持。戈卡尔的道德语调、他对责任和渐进改革的强调，带有罗易伦理方法的痕迹。甚至甘地（Gandhi），在他对分权化、公民贴近和精神性政治的强调中，也回响着罗易的信念：权力必须栖居在人民中间才能公正。

罗易的思想也影响了20世纪的宪政思考，尽管是间接的。印度建国文献中对代表制、透明度和伦理性治国的强调，与罗易视治理为道德责任的愿景相平行。他为一种国家观念播下了种子——这种国家不仅是程序性的，更是原则性的——植根于贴近、谦卑和问责。

在我们当下这一刻，罗易的思想令人惊异地显得切中时宜。随着全球治理变得更加抽象，随着决策变得自动化、集中化且在情感上抽离，罗易对伦理性在场的坚持是一个有力的提醒：没有在场的权力会变成疏离；没有理解的行政会变成慢动作的暴力；而正义，归根结底，不仅是法律或效率的问题，更是贴近的问题。

罗易或许未能活到看见一个去殖民化的印度。但他帮助想象了这样一个印度：在其中，统治者是人民中间的道德主体，而非遥远的权威。

罗易客死异乡，但他的智识遗产存活于他所提出的问题之中。是什么使权威成为公正的？一个政府要多贴近才能合乎伦理？制度能否不仅高效地、更道德地行事？

他的回答一以贯之，却非简单化。贴近很重要。语言很重要。问责很重要。这些不是抽象概念。它们是尊严与正义的日常条件。对罗易而言，治理不仅关乎权力，它关乎权力在与人们生活接触时所采取的伦理形式。

在《阐释》中，罗易要求的并不是由印度人接管英国的制度。他要求的是某种更根本的东西：治理若要正当，就必须是可理解的、人道的，并植根于伦理自觉。这不仅是对英国统治的批评。它是一份蓝图，适用于任何希望以正直延续的权力体制——无论是帝国的、民主的，还是其他形式的。

在一个日益由距离所定义的世界里——公民与国家之间、政策与经验之间、法律与正义之间——罗易提醒我们，良善的政府不仅是法律或统计数字的问题。它是在场的问题。他坚持统治者应生活在被统治者中间、用他们自己的语言倾听他们、并在道德上对他们负责，这一原则超越了其所处的时代。在他最乐观的时刻，罗易相信，即使是殖民国家也能被救赎——只要它学会不从远处、而是从内部进行治理。他的作品表明，贴近不仅是空间上的，更是伦理上的。它意味着跨越差异去倾听，并以这样一种谦卑来治理：任何法律，除非被理解、被感受、可问责，否则就不是公正的。

我们如今生活在一个数据驱动治理、自动化决策和庞大官僚机构的时代。国家变得更有能力，但也更非人格化。在这样一个时刻，罗易的愿景再次显得激进。不是因为它的宏大，而是因为它的亲密。他没有要求被铭记。他坚持要求的是：权力应当可见、贴近、可问责。这一愿景仍然重要。或许现在比以往任何时候都更如此，它值得被阅读——不是作为遗物，而是作为一种挑衅：一种将伦理带回治理日常运作之中的召唤。

In 1831, a man in a long cloak stepped off a ship in Liverpool. He had no official title the British recognised, no position in the colonial administration, and no invitation from the Crown. His name was Rammohun Roy. He came from Calcutta, sent not by the British Empire but by the weakening Mughal court in Delhi. His stated mission was to represent the ageing emperor Akbar II in London. But Roy brought something else with him, something quietly radical. Among his papers was a detailed document on how India was governed under British rule, and how it might be governed more justly. Its title: Exposition of the Judicial and Revenue Systems of India.

The moment was significant, even if few recognised it at the time. Here was an Indian thinker not merely demanding reform but arriving in the imperial metropole with his own diagnosis of empire’s ethical failings. His cloak may have seemed out of place in the foggy streets of London, but his message was piercingly modern: power must be near to be fair. His presence in England wasn’t just diplomatic: it was symbolic. Roy was stepping into the heart of empire not merely to protest, but to propose. As he would argue, critique from a colonial subject wasn’t a contradiction; it was a form of ethical intervention. And perhaps more radically, he believed that Britain had something to gain by listening. Roy did not call for rebellion, but for reform grounded in empathy, knowledge and responsibility. What he offered was a vision of rule based not on domination, but on ethical presence.

To understand Roy’s radicalism, one must first recognise the peculiar nature of the empire he addressed. The British East India Company governed not as a typical colonial state, but as a multinational corporation with a private army. Its rule was bureaucratic, extractive and often unaccountable. In this world, Roy’s voice stood out not simply because it was Indian, but because it was reasoned, comparative and universalist. He spoke the language of rights and governance, of moral duty and political proximity: a language the British claimed to understand, and that Roy used to hold them to account.

On the surface, the Exposition looked like a dry report. But inside was a surprising claim: the greatest problem with British rule in India wasn’t just oppression or corruption. It was distance. Courts operated in languages that ordinary people couldn’t understand. Administrators rarely stayed long enough in one place to learn how it worked. And decisions were made far away, in Calcutta or London, by people with no connection to the lives they affected.

To understand why Roy believed these things, we need to understand the extraordinary life that shaped him. Born in 1772 into a well-to-do Brahmin family in Bengal, he was educated in a variety of intellectual traditions that few of his contemporaries had access to. His early studies in Persian and Arabic took place in Patna, where he was introduced to Islamic theology, logic and jurisprudence. Later, in Varanasi, he studied Sanskrit texts, absorbing the metaphysics and ritual knowledge central to Hindu philosophical traditions. He also engaged with Jain and Buddhist ideas and, over time, became deeply interested in Christian theology and Enlightenment rationalism.

This unique education didn’t just make Roy intellectually curious – it made him comparative. He was always seeking correspondences between traditions: what did Islam and Hinduism say about the moral duties of a ruler? How did the Christian notion of the kingdom of God relate to Persianate ideas of justice? How did Western liberalism align, or conflict, with indigenous notions of ethical conduct? These weren’t abstract questions. Roy saw them playing out in the colonial world around him.

From 1803 to 1814, he worked for the East India Company in various administrative roles – first as a munshi (a clerk or secretary), then as a revenue officer, and eventually as a translator and Persian-language expert. He was posted in towns across Bengal and Bihar, and these experiences formed the crucible of his political thinking. He observed how policies devised in distant boardrooms were implemented, often clumsily, on the ground. He witnessed how local knowledge was routinely ignored, and how language barriers created confusion and alienation.

Roy’s familiarity with the colonial administration was not superficial. He knew its paperwork, its personnel, its practices. He was, in effect, a part of the machinery. But he was also quietly and sharply critical of it. He saw how easily the system slid from bureaucracy into authoritarianism – not through grand acts of oppression, but through a thousand small instances of disregard.

It was these experiences that led Roy to argue, later in London, that colonial rule suffered not just from injustice, but from estrangement. The British were ruling India, but they did not know it. They governed by abstraction, by rules, reports and statistics, rather than by presence. Roy believed this was not just inefficient; it was unethical. And it was this ethical critique, grounded in his personal encounters with power, that gave the Exposition its quiet force.

Nor was Roy’s criticism confined to British officials. He also called upon Indian elites to rethink their role. Too many, he believed, had accepted the rewards of collaboration without the responsibilities of critique. Roy wanted a different kind of engagement – one that would hold power to account from the inside, using the tools of law, reason and moral persuasion.

In many ways, Roy’s life up to 1831 was preparation for the arguments he would make in England. He had spent three decades navigating multiple worlds: Persian and Sanskrit, Mughal and British. The Exposition was the culmination of that journey. It was not a cry from the margins. It was a challenge from someone who had seen the system from within, and who wanted it to do better. His proposal was simple but bold: rulers should be present, visible, and answerable to those they govern. Power should not float above people’s lives; it should live among them.

Roy’s mission to England was, at least formally, as the emissary of the Mughal emperor Akbar II. By that time, the Mughal dynasty, once the most formidable imperial power in South Asia – had become a shadow of its former self. Its territorial reach was minimal, its treasury depleted, and its court largely symbolic. Yet, for Roy, that symbolism mattered. The emperor might have been politically diminished, but he remained, in Roy’s eyes, a sovereign figure whose legitimacy derived not from conquest or commerce, but from an older, morally infused conception of rule.

This connection was more than ceremonial. Roy had cultivated ties with the Mughal court over several years and was conferred the title of Raja, a move that British officials privately mocked but could not entirely dismiss. His diplomatic mission to England was also a subtle act of political imagination: an attempt to revive the ethical memory of Indo-Persian kingship within the corridors of imperial power. In carrying the voice of the emperor to the British Crown, Roy was insisting that India’s political traditions had not been erased, they were merely sidelined, awaiting recognition.

Roy’s Mughal affiliation also revealed the layered and overlapping sovereignties of early colonial India. He did not view indigenous kingship and colonial rule as irreconcilable opposites. Instead, he saw the potential for a fusion: a system in which older norms of justice, responsibility and public ethics (values cultivated in the Persianate courtly tradition) could temper the utilitarian logic of the East India Company. On this view, the Mughal court was not a fossil but offered a way to remind the British that power without legitimacy is fragile, and that legitimacy is not simply a function of military force or administrative reach.

In his writings, Roy often staged this synthesis. The Exposition is filled with references to English law and Enlightenment ideals, but its moral cadence is unmistakably shaped by Persianate ethical thought. Concepts like justice, proximity and ethical accountability – common in Islamic political writing – inform his ideas. Roy did not abandon these traditions when he wrote in English. He translated them. And in doing so, he created a political vocabulary that could speak simultaneously to the emperor’s court and to the British parliament.

To the British public, Roy’s Mughal ties might have seemed quaint, even anachronistic. But for Roy, they offered a platform from which to issue a critique. His journey to England was thus layered with intent. It was not only a petition on behalf of a declining monarch. It was a declaration that India’s political voice could still speak for itself, not in defiance, but in dialogue.

The Exposition, published in London in 1832, is a remarkably grounded critique of British administration in India. Rather than the language of revolution, Roy speaks of reform, precision and moral responsibility. The document is divided into several sections that detail the flaws of the colonial judiciary and revenue systems.

Roy begins with everyday realities. Farmers pushed into debt due to excessive tax assessments. Legal processes that bewildered ordinary people because proceedings were conducted in unfamiliar languages. Judges and collectors who rotated too frequently to understand the local contexts they were meant to oversee. The effect was alienation, not just in law but in life. The people governed did not recognise themselves in their governors, and the governors rarely made an effort to learn from the governed.

Roy outlines more than bureaucratic inefficiency – there’s a deeper political problem: a form of governance unmoored from the people it affects. He argued that decisions made in London or by distant Company directors could never be just if they didn’t incorporate local realities and voices. Roy advocated for Indian judges, courts that spoke local languages, and administrative continuity. His demand was not for Indian rule alone, but for a system of accountability rooted in ethical practice and public engagement.

This ethical core, what Roy would have understood through both Enlightenment ideals and Persianate ethics, insisted that governance required familiarity, attentiveness and moral clarity. He called not for the rejection of bureaucracy altogether, but for its reform. He believed that a government might still be legitimate if it was structured to listen, respond and explain itself. But such responsiveness required what he called domiciliation: power that lived where it governed.

In making this argument, Roy anticipated one of the great critiques of modern administration – that it becomes impersonal, procedural and aloof. Long before Max Weber or later theorists of bureaucracy, Roy observed how distant governance often transforms justice into ritual, law into jargon, and accountability into empty routine. His Exposition is filled with illustrations of these dynamics, not theoretical, but deeply empirical.

Rather than merely assert abstract principles, Roy shows how injustice functions on the ground. A farmer is taxed on a mistaken assessment and loses his land. A litigant attends court for months without understanding a word spoken by the judge. A village waits years for an official to arrive to settle a land dispute. Each example becomes a window into the ways a disconnected system can do violence, not loudly, but daily. Roy’s approach here was distinctively bureaucratic, even procedural. Yet it carried a sharp political edge. He was less concerned with abstract denunciations of colonialism and more focused on the granular mechanics of how injustice worked. These weren’t just administrative quirks: they were the machinery of alienation.

And yet Roy remained hopeful. He believed that reform was possible, and that ethical governance could be built if both Indian and British officials committed themselves to the people they served. His critique was born not of ideology but of experience, experience sharpened into moral vision. In many ways, the Exposition was an administrative document. But in Roy’s hands, it became a form of political philosophy: a vision of governance as care.

That is what makes Roy’s Exposition so compelling. More than a relic of colonial policy, it is a dialogue on what power should look like when it is done justly. In an age when data-driven decision-making and bureaucratic rationality are once again under scrutiny, Roy’s work reminds us that the first requirement of good governance is not information, but presence.

Roy’s idea did not emerge from any single intellectual tradition. It was shaped by a remarkable confluence of influences, intellectual encounters and moral commitments. Rather than being the product of one culture or creed, his ethics was braided from multiple traditions, each offering a different vocabulary for justice, responsibility and the purpose of power.

One of his earliest writings, Tuhfat-ul-Muwahhidin (‘Gift to the Believers in One God’), composed around 1803, shows his deep engagement with Islamic theology and particularly the ethical tradition known as akhlaq. In this literature, power is inseparable from virtue; rulers are not simply sovereigns but moral agents accountable to divine justice and social responsibility. Drawing on thinkers like Nasir al-Din al-Tusi, Roy was steeped in a tradition where the king’s first duty was not to expand dominion but to cultivate fairness and moderation.

From Hindu texts, especially the Upanishads, Roy drew a sense of spiritual duty (dharma) and the idea that self-knowledge carried public consequences. The king, in this worldview, was the guardian of cosmic and social order. The justice he administered was not his alone, it reflected the balance of the universe. Roy was particularly drawn to the idea that truth was unified, even if its expressions varied across traditions. This gave him the confidence to seek moral guidance across boundaries. This comparative method was no intellectual game – it was an ethical necessity. Roy believed that moral clarity often emerged at the edges of traditions, not their cores. Good governance had to be multilingual, morally plural and intellectually generous.

Christianity shaped Roy’s ethics in another way. Through his interactions with Christian missionaries and his reading of the New Testament, Roy came to admire the moral teachings of Jesus – especially the emphasis on compassion, humility and resistance to arbitrary authority. He believed that Jesus modelled a form of leadership that elevated the weak, questioned entrenched power, and refused to separate faith from ethics. Roy did not convert to Christianity, but he found in it a moral clarity that resonated with his own convictions.

Equally significant were the liberal ideas he encountered through his engagement with European philosophy. He read John Locke on governance, William Blackstone on legal rights, and Montesquieu on the separation of powers. These thinkers gave him a language for political accountability, constitutional limits and civil liberty. Rather than merely adopt these ideas, Roy interpreted them through the lens of his multilingual, multireligious education. Where Locke spoke of life, liberty and property, Roy heard echoes of older ideas about justice, responsibility and the ethical character of rulers.

What emerged from this intellectual ecosystem was a hybrid ethics of rule. Roy was not content to be a translator or commentator. He fused his sources into a coherent moral philosophy: one that insisted that rulers were stewards, not merely administrators, their power a responsibility, not a right. And their legitimacy came not from conquest or title, but from their ethical proximity to the people they governed.

Importantly, Roy’s ethics were not abstract. They were meant to guide governance in specific ways. He argued that justice must be comprehensible to its subjects; laws must be intelligible; policies must reflect the lived conditions of those they affect. This meant that language, continuity and cultural knowledge were not mere accessories to administration, they were ethical requirements. A court that spoke in Persian or English while adjudicating the affairs of Bengali villagers was more than inefficient; it was unjust.

‘A Map of Bengal and Bahar’ from An Atlas of Bengal (1781) by James Rennell, dedicated to Warren Hastings, the governor-general of the British possessions in Asia. Public Domain

Roy’s ethical vision thus combined moral rigour with administrative insight. It asked how one could rule fairly in a multilingual, multireligious and colonised land. And it insisted that the answer lay not in uniform control, but in layered responsibility. The ruler must be close enough to understand, humble enough to listen, and virtuous enough to act.

This capacious moral framework allowed Roy to act as a bridge, between traditions, between empires, between ideas of East and West. In a world increasingly divided between coloniser and colonised, he offered a model of political thought that was both critical and connective. His ethics, drawn from many sources, became a tool to evaluate, and challenge, the new order of empire.

Roy’s political imagination was forged in the overlap between philosophy, politics and public communication. He was not a political theorist in the academic sense, but his writings collectively form a coherent and radical vision: a vision rooted in ethics, shaped by daily life, and articulated through an extraordinary command of multiple intellectual traditions.

He wrote across genres: petitions, essays, open letters, pamphlets and newspaper articles. In Sambad Kaumudi, one of the newspapers he founded, he tackled contemporary issues in a tone that was direct, often satirical, and deeply engaged with the moral and civic life of Bengal. He addressed subjects ranging from widow remarriage to press freedom, and from education reform to judicial procedure. His Bangla tracts brought abstract political principles into the realm of lived experience. Using metaphors drawn from agriculture, family and folklore, he made his case in ways ordinary readers could grasp and relate to. This was no small feat. Roy was crafting a political language where none yet existed.

Even his religious writings had political undertones. When Roy argued for monotheism or defended the rights of women, he was implicitly arguing for an ethical public sphere, one in which reason, mutual respect and moral accountability formed the basis of both religious and political authority. More than simply theological, his critique of idolatry was also a critique of institutional power.

Roy’s political imagination was shaped by lived experience, not just textual traditions. His knowledge of the inner workings of the East India Company administration gave him a practical understanding of how power functioned on the ground. This realism distinguished him from utopian thinkers. He did not call for the wholesale dismantling of British rule but for a system where power was made ethical through its responsiveness to the governed.

The Exposition, then, must be read as part of this broader project. It is not just a policy document. It is an ethical map. Roy was outlining what governance should feel like to those at its receiving end: accessible, fair, answerable. He was asking how political institutions might be reimagined to serve people rather than simply manage them. His proposals, such as appointing Indian judges or conducting trials in local languages, were grounded not only in administrative logic but in moral reasoning.

Crucially, Roy believed that communication was central to power. His multilingualism was a strategy, not just a skill. He wrote in English, Persian, Bangla and occasionally Arabic, tailoring each message to a different audience. To British officials, he offered reasoned critique in the language of reform. To Indian readers, he offered satire, allegory and moral exhortation. This polyphony allowed him to operate in multiple spheres at once, imperial and vernacular, elite and popular.

His political thought is difficult to pin down precisely because it refuses simple classification. It is liberal in its defence of rights, constitutional in its calls for reform, theological in its moral urgency, and pragmatic in its policy suggestions. Above all, it is grounded in the conviction that proximity, not just of geography but of understanding, is essential to justice.

Roy’s political imagination, then, was both expansive and grounded. It did not dream of utopias; it demanded reforms. It did not romanticise the past or idealise the West; it asked what could be done, here and now, to make power more just. In this, he was a pioneer of modern Indian political thought. And though he rarely used the language of democracy as we understand it today, his work laid important foundations for it: a vision of governance that is ethical, inclusive and accountable to the people it serves.

When Roy arrived in England, he caused a stir among certain political and intellectual circles. British Unitarians saw him as a fellow traveller in the search for rational religion and ethical reform. Parliamentarians sympathetic to political reform welcomed his insight into colonial governance. Intellectuals such as Jeremy Bentham and Robert Owen were aware of his presence and, in some cases, intrigued by the precision and civility of his arguments. Yet despite this momentary curiosity, Roy remained largely marginal in formal imperial circles, welcomed as a curiosity, perhaps, but not taken seriously as a political equal.

His Exposition didn’t prompt sweeping reform. There was no sudden change in how the East India Company administered justice or collected revenue. But this wasn’t necessarily a failure. The true significance of the text lay in its political gesture, not in its policy influence. Roy demonstrated that critique could come from the colonised, articulated in the idiom of the coloniser, and still reflect a deeply Indian moral vision. His work set a precedent for speaking truth to power, from within the very spaces where that power was presumed to be unquestioned.

After Roy’s sudden death from meningitis in Bristol in 1833, his reputation evolved rapidly. In Bengal, he was celebrated as a reformer, remembered for his advocacy against sati (widow immolation), his efforts to modernise Hindu education, and his co-founding of the reformist movement Brahmo Sabha. But as Indian politics grew more nationalist in tone, Roy’s image was simplified: he became either the father of Indian liberalism or a faint outline in the pantheon of proto-nationalist heroes. This often obscured the nuance of his political thought, his careful attention to bureaucracy, his insistence on ethical proximity, and his belief in moral governance as a practice of care, not just control.

Nonetheless, Roy’s ideas lived on in more subtle ways. Later thinkers like Dadabhai Naoroji, Gopal Krishna Gokhale and even Rabindranath Tagore inherited fragments of Roy’s vision. Naoroji’s economic critique of British rule echoed Roy’s insistence that imperial governance was alienating and extractive. Gokhale’s moral tone, his stress on responsibility and gradual reform, bore traces of Roy’s ethical method. Even Gandhi, in his emphasis on decentralisation, civic proximity and spiritual politics, echoed Roy’s belief that power must dwell among the people to be just.

Roy’s ideas also influenced constitutional thinking in the 20th century, though indirectly. The emphasis in India’s founding documents on representation, transparency and ethical statecraft parallels Roy’s vision of governance as moral responsibility. He had planted the seed for a conception of the state that was not merely procedural, but principled – rooted in proximity, humility and accountability.

In our present moment, Roy’s thought feels uncannily timely. As global governance grows more abstract, as decision-making becomes automated, centralised and emotionally disengaged, Roy’s insistence on ethical presence is a potent reminder that power without presence becomes alienation; that administration without understanding becomes violence in slow motion; and that justice, in the end, is not only a question of law or efficiency, but of nearness.

Roy may not have lived to see a decolonised India. But he helped imagine one in which rulers were moral agents among their people, not distant authorities.

Roy died far from home, but his intellectual legacy lives on in the questions he raised. What makes authority just? How close must a government be to be ethical? Can institutions behave not just efficiently, but morally?

His answers were consistent, not simplistic. Proximity matters. Language matters. Accountability matters. These are not abstractions. They are the daily conditions of dignity and justice. For Roy, governance was not just about power, it was about the ethical form that power takes when it comes into contact with people’s lives.

In the Exposition, Roy was not asking for an Indian takeover of British institutions. He was asking for something more foundational: that governance, to be legitimate, must be intelligible, humane and grounded in ethical awareness. This was not merely a critique of British rule. It was a blueprint for any system of power, imperial, democratic or otherwise, that hoped to endure with integrity.

In a world increasingly defined by distance, between citizen and state, between policy and experience, between law and justice, Roy offers a reminder that good government is not only a matter of laws or statistics. It is a matter of presence. His insistence that rulers live among the ruled, listen to them in their own languages, and remain morally accountable to them, is a principle that transcends his time. In his most optimistic moments, Roy believed that even the colonial state could be redeemed if it learned to govern not from a distance, but from within. His work suggests that proximity is not just spatial, but ethical. It means listening across difference, and governing with the humility that no law is just unless it is understood, felt, and answerable.

We live now in an age of data-driven governance, automated decisions and vast bureaucracies. The state has grown more capable, but also more impersonal. In such a moment, Roy’s vision feels radical again. Not because it is grandiose, but because it is intimate. He did not ask to be remembered. He asked, insistently, that power be visible, proximate and accountable. That vision still matters. And perhaps now more than ever, it deserves to be read not as a relic, but as a provocation: a call to bring ethics back into the everyday workings of governance.

But Roy brought something else with him, something quietly radical. Among his papers was a detailed document on how India was governed under British rule, and how it might be governed more justly. Its title: Exposition of the Judicial and Revenue Systems of India.

paragraphs.cn: 这一时刻意义深远，尽管当时几乎无人察觉。一位印度思想家不仅要求改革，还带着自己对帝国伦理缺陷的诊断来到了帝国的心脏。他的长袍在伦敦雾蒙蒙的街道上或许显得格格不入，但他传递的信息却尖锐而现代：权力必须贴近才能公正。他来到英国不仅仅是外交行为，更具有象征意义。罗易走进帝国的核心，不仅是为了抗议，更是为了建言。正如他所主张的，来自被殖民者的批评并非自相矛盾，而是一种伦理性的介入。更激进的是，他认为英国可以从倾听中获益。罗易呼吁的不是反叛，而是建立在共情、知识与责任之上的改革。他所提供的是一种统治愿景，不基于支配，而基于伦理性的在场。
paragraphs.en: The moment was significant, even if few recognised it at the time. Here was an Indian thinker not merely demanding reform but arriving in the imperial metropole with his own diagnosis of empire’s ethical failings. His cloak may have seemed out of place in the foggy streets of London, but his message was piercingly modern: power must be near to be fair. His presence in England wasn’t just diplomatic: it was symbolic. Roy was stepping into the heart of empire not merely to protest, but to propose. As he would argue, critique from a colonial subject wasn’t a contradiction; it was a form of ethical intervention. And perhaps more radically, he believed that Britain had something to gain by listening. Roy did not call for rebellion, but for reform grounded in empathy, knowledge and responsibility. What he offered was a vision of rule based not on domination, but on ethical presence.

paragraphs.cn: 要理解罗易的激进性，首先必须认清他所面对的那个帝国的独特性质。英国东印度公司（East India Company）并非作为典型的殖民国家进行统治，而是作为一家拥有私人军队的跨国公司。它的统治是官僚化的、榨取性的，且常常不受问责。在这个世界中，罗易的声音之所以突出，不仅因为它是印度的，更因为它是理性的、比较性的和普世主义的。他讲的是权利与治理、道德义务与政治贴近的语言——一种英国人自称能听懂、而罗易用以追究其责任的语言。
paragraphs.en: To understand Roy’s radicalism, one must first recognise the peculiar nature of the empire he addressed. The British East India Company governed not as a typical colonial state, but as a multinational corporation with a private army. Its rule was bureaucratic, extractive and often unaccountable. In this world, Roy’s voice stood out not simply because it was Indian, but because it was reasoned, comparative and universalist. He spoke the language of rights and governance, of moral duty and political proximity: a language the British claimed to understand, and that Roy used to hold them to account.

paragraphs.cn: 表面上看，《阐释》像是一份枯燥的报告。但其内里却有一个出人意料的论断：英国在印度统治的最大问题不仅仅是压迫或腐败，而是距离。法庭使用的语言是普通人听不懂的。行政官员很少在一个地方待得足够久，以了解当地的运作方式。而决策则在遥远的地方做出——在加尔各答或伦敦，由那些与所影响的生活毫无关联的人做出。
paragraphs.en: On the surface, the Exposition looked like a dry report. But inside was a surprising claim: the greatest problem with British rule in India wasn’t just oppression or corruption. It was distance. Courts operated in languages that ordinary people couldn’t understand. Administrators rarely stayed long enough in one place to learn how it worked. And decisions were made far away, in Calcutta or London, by people with no connection to the lives they affected.

paragraphs.cn: 要理解罗易为何持有这些观点，我们需要了解塑造他的非凡人生。他1772年出生于孟加拉（Bengal）一个富裕的婆罗门（Brahmin）家庭，所受的教育涵盖多种同时代人鲜少能接触到的思想传统。他早年在巴特那（Patna）学习波斯语和阿拉伯语，在那里接触到伊斯兰神学、逻辑学和法学。后来，在瓦拉纳西（Varanasi），他研习梵文典籍，吸收了印度哲学传统中核心的形而上学与仪轨知识。他还涉猎耆那教（Jain）和佛教（Buddhist）思想，并逐渐对基督教神学和启蒙运动的理性主义产生了深厚兴趣。
paragraphs.en: To understand why Roy believed these things, we need to understand the extraordinary life that shaped him. Born in 1772 into a well-to-do Brahmin family in Bengal, he was educated in a variety of intellectual traditions that few of his contemporaries had access to. His early studies in Persian and Arabic took place in Patna, where he was introduced to Islamic theology, logic and jurisprudence. Later, in Varanasi, he studied Sanskrit texts, absorbing the metaphysics and ritual knowledge central to Hindu philosophical traditions. He also engaged with Jain and Buddhist ideas and, over time, became deeply interested in Christian theology and Enlightenment rationalism.

paragraphs.cn: 这种独特的教育不仅使罗易在智识上充满好奇心，更使他善于比较。他总是追寻不同传统之间的对应：伊斯兰教和印度教对统治者的道德义务各有什么说法？基督教的「上帝之国」观念与波斯化（Persianate）的正义观有何关联？西方自由主义与本土的伦理行为观念是契合还是冲突？这些并非抽象的问题。罗易看到它们正在他周围的殖民世界中上演。
paragraphs.en: This unique education didn’t just make Roy intellectually curious – it made him comparative. He was always seeking correspondences between traditions: what did Islam and Hinduism say about the moral duties of a ruler? How did the Christian notion of the kingdom of God relate to Persianate ideas of justice? How did Western liberalism align, or conflict, with indigenous notions of ethical conduct? These weren’t abstract questions. Roy saw them playing out in the colonial world around him.

paragraphs.cn: 从1803年到1814年，他在东印度公司担任各种行政职务——先是做蒙希（munshi，即文书或秘书），然后任税务官，最后担任翻译和波斯语专家。他被派驻到孟加拉和比哈尔（Bihar）各地的城镇，这些经历成为他政治思想的熔炉。他观察在遥远的董事会议室里制定的政策如何被推行到基层，往往笨拙不堪。他目睹地方知识如何被习以为常地忽视，语言障碍又如何造成混乱与疏离。
paragraphs.en: From 1803 to 1814, he worked for the East India Company in various administrative roles – first as a munshi (a clerk or secretary), then as a revenue officer, and eventually as a translator and Persian-language expert. He was posted in towns across Bengal and Bihar, and these experiences formed the crucible of his political thinking. He observed how policies devised in distant boardrooms were implemented, often clumsily, on the ground. He witnessed how local knowledge was routinely ignored, and how language barriers created confusion and alienation.

paragraphs.cn: 罗易对殖民行政的熟悉并非浮于表面。他熟悉它的文书、它的人员、它的惯例。实际上，他就是这台机器的一部分。但他同时也悄然而犀利地批评它。他看到这套系统多么容易从官僚制滑向威权主义——不是通过宏大的压迫之举，而是通过千百次小小的漠视。
paragraphs.en: Roy’s familiarity with the colonial administration was not superficial. He knew its paperwork, its personnel, its practices. He was, in effect, a part of the machinery. But he was also quietly and sharply critical of it. He saw how easily the system slid from bureaucracy into authoritarianism – not through grand acts of oppression, but through a thousand small instances of disregard.

paragraphs.cn: 正是这些经历促使罗易后来在伦敦主张，殖民统治不仅饱受不公，更饱受疏离。英国人在统治印度，却不了解印度。他们凭借抽象、凭借规章、报告和统计来治理，而非凭借在场。罗易相信这不仅效率低下，更是不道德的。正是这种植根于他与权力亲身遭遇的伦理批评，赋予了《阐释》那种沉静而有力的力量。
paragraphs.en: It was these experiences that led Roy to argue, later in London, that colonial rule suffered not just from injustice, but from estrangement. The British were ruling India, but they did not know it. They governed by abstraction, by rules, reports and statistics, rather than by presence. Roy believed this was not just inefficient; it was unethical. And it was this ethical critique, grounded in his personal encounters with power, that gave the Exposition its quiet force.

paragraphs.cn: 罗易的批评也并不限于英国官员。他还号召印度精英反思自己的角色。他认为太多人接受了合作的奖赏，却没有承担批评的责任。罗易想要一种不同的参与——一种从内部追究权力责任的方式，运用法律、理性和道德劝说的工具。
paragraphs.en: Nor was Roy’s criticism confined to British officials. He also called upon Indian elites to rethink their role. Too many, he believed, had accepted the rewards of collaboration without the responsibilities of critique. Roy wanted a different kind of engagement – one that would hold power to account from the inside, using the tools of law, reason and moral persuasion.

paragraphs.cn: 在许多方面，罗易到1831年为止的人生都是在为他将在英国提出的论点做准备。他花了三十年穿梭于多个世界之间：波斯的与梵文的，莫卧儿的与英国的。《阐释》是这段旅程的集大成。它不是来自边缘的呐喊，而是来自一个曾从内部审视这套系统、并希望它做得更好之人的挑战。他的提议简单却大胆：统治者应当在场、可见，并对所统治之人负责。权力不应悬浮于人们的生活之上，而应生活在他们中间。
paragraphs.en: In many ways, Roy’s life up to 1831 was preparation for the arguments he would make in England. He had spent three decades navigating multiple worlds: Persian and Sanskrit, Mughal and British. The Exposition was the culmination of that journey. It was not a cry from the margins. It was a challenge from someone who had seen the system from within, and who wanted it to do better. His proposal was simple but bold: rulers should be present, visible, and answerable to those they govern. Power should not float above people’s lives; it should live among them.

paragraphs.cn: 罗易出使英国，至少在形式上，是作为莫卧儿皇帝阿克巴二世的使者。到那时，曾经是南亚最强大帝国势力的莫卧儿王朝，已沦为昔日自身的影子。它的领土范围微乎其微，国库枯竭，朝廷很大程度上只是象征性的。然而对罗易而言，这种象征意义至关重要。皇帝在政治上或许已被削弱，但在罗易眼中，他仍是一位主权人物，其正当性不来自征服或贸易，而来自一种更古老的、浸透道德的统治观念。
paragraphs.en: Roy’s mission to England was, at least formally, as the emissary of the Mughal emperor Akbar II. By that time, the Mughal dynasty, once the most formidable imperial power in South Asia – had become a shadow of its former self. Its territorial reach was minimal, its treasury depleted, and its court largely symbolic. Yet, for Roy, that symbolism mattered. The emperor might have been politically diminished, but he remained, in Roy’s eyes, a sovereign figure whose legitimacy derived not from conquest or commerce, but from an older, morally infused conception of rule.

paragraphs.cn: 这种联系不止是礼仪性的。罗易多年来与莫卧儿朝廷培养关系，并被授予罗阇（Raja）的头衔——英国官员私下嘲笑此举，却无法完全无视。他的出使英国也是一次政治想象力的微妙之举：试图在帝国权力的走廊中复兴印度-波斯王权的伦理记忆。在将皇帝的声音带到英国王室面前时，罗易坚持认为，印度的政治传统并未被抹去，它们只是被边缘化，等待被承认。
paragraphs.en: This connection was more than ceremonial. Roy had cultivated ties with the Mughal court over several years and was conferred the title of Raja, a move that British officials privately mocked but could not entirely dismiss. His diplomatic mission to England was also a subtle act of political imagination: an attempt to revive the ethical memory of Indo-Persian kingship within the corridors of imperial power. In carrying the voice of the emperor to the British Crown, Roy was insisting that India’s political traditions had not been erased, they were merely sidelined, awaiting recognition.

paragraphs.cn: 罗易与莫卧儿的关联还揭示了早期殖民印度的层级化、相互交叠的主权格局。他并不把本土王权与殖民统治视为不可调和的对立面。相反，他看到了融合的可能：一个在其中更古老的正义、责任与公共伦理规范（在波斯化的朝廷传统中培养的价值观）能够约束东印度公司功利主义逻辑的体制。在这一视角下，莫卧儿朝廷不是化石，而是提供了一种方式来提醒英国人：没有正当性的权力是脆弱的，而正当性并非仅仅是军事力量或行政触及范围的函数。
paragraphs.en: Roy’s Mughal affiliation also revealed the layered and overlapping sovereignties of early colonial India. He did not view indigenous kingship and colonial rule as irreconcilable opposites. Instead, he saw the potential for a fusion: a system in which older norms of justice, responsibility and public ethics (values cultivated in the Persianate courtly tradition) could temper the utilitarian logic of the East India Company. On this view, the Mughal court was not a fossil but offered a way to remind the British that power without legitimacy is fragile, and that legitimacy is not simply a function of military force or administrative reach.

paragraphs.cn: 在他的著作中，罗易常常呈现这种综合。《阐释》中充满对英国法和启蒙理想的引用，但其道德韵律无可错认地受到波斯化伦理思想的塑造。诸如正义、贴近和伦理问责等概念——在伊斯兰政治写作中很常见——构成了他思想的基础。罗易用英文写作时并未抛弃这些传统，他翻译了它们。在此过程中，他创造了一种政治语汇，能同时对皇帝的朝廷和英国议会发言。
paragraphs.en: In his writings, Roy often staged this synthesis. The Exposition is filled with references to English law and Enlightenment ideals, but its moral cadence is unmistakably shaped by Persianate ethical thought. Concepts like justice, proximity and ethical accountability – common in Islamic political writing – inform his ideas. Roy did not abandon these traditions when he wrote in English. He translated them. And in doing so, he created a political vocabulary that could speak simultaneously to the emperor’s court and to the British parliament.

paragraphs.cn: 对英国公众而言，罗易的莫卧儿渊源或许显得古雅，甚至不合时宜。但对罗易来说，它们提供了一个发出批评的平台。因此，他前往英国的旅程层层叠叠地承载着意图。它不仅是为一位衰落君主请愿，更是宣告：印度的政治声音仍能为自己发声，不是以对抗的方式，而是以对话的方式。
paragraphs.en: To the British public, Roy’s Mughal ties might have seemed quaint, even anachronistic. But for Roy, they offered a platform from which to issue a critique. His journey to England was thus layered with intent. It was not only a petition on behalf of a declining monarch. It was a declaration that India’s political voice could still speak for itself, not in defiance, but in dialogue.

paragraphs.cn: 1832年在伦敦出版的《阐释》，是对英国在印度行政的一份极为扎实的批评。罗易不使用革命的话语，而是谈论改革、精确与道德责任。该文献分为若干部分，详述殖民司法和财税制度的缺陷。
paragraphs.en: The Exposition, published in London in 1832, is a remarkably grounded critique of British administration in India. Rather than the language of revolution, Roy speaks of reform, precision and moral responsibility. The document is divided into several sections that detail the flaws of the colonial judiciary and revenue systems.

paragraphs.cn: 罗易从日常现实入手。农民因过高的税额核定而陷入债务。法律程序令普通人困惑，因为诉讼使用的是他们不熟悉的语言。法官和收税官轮换过于频繁，根本来不及了解他们理应监管的地方情境。其结果是疏离——不仅在法律上，更在生活中。被治理者无法在治理者身上认出自己，而治理者很少努力向被治理者学习。
paragraphs.en: Roy begins with everyday realities. Farmers pushed into debt due to excessive tax assessments. Legal processes that bewildered ordinary people because proceedings were conducted in unfamiliar languages. Judges and collectors who rotated too frequently to understand the local contexts they were meant to oversee. The effect was alienation, not just in law but in life. The people governed did not recognise themselves in their governors, and the governors rarely made an effort to learn from the governed.

paragraphs.cn: 罗易勾勒的不仅是官僚效率低下，还有一个更深层的政治问题：一种脱离了它所影响之人的治理形式。他主张，在伦敦或由遥远的公司董事做出的决策，如果不纳入地方现实与声音，永远不可能公正。罗易主张任用印度法官、使用当地语言的法庭，以及行政上的连续性。他要求的不是仅仅由印度人统治，而是一种根植于伦理实践和公众参与的问责制。
paragraphs.en: Roy outlines more than bureaucratic inefficiency – there’s a deeper political problem: a form of governance unmoored from the people it affects. He argued that decisions made in London or by distant Company directors could never be just if they didn’t incorporate local realities and voices. Roy advocated for Indian judges, courts that spoke local languages, and administrative continuity. His demand was not for Indian rule alone, but for a system of accountability rooted in ethical practice and public engagement.

paragraphs.cn: 这一伦理核心——罗易既通过启蒙理想、也通过波斯化伦理来理解它——坚持认为治理需要熟悉、专注和道德清明。他呼吁的不是全盘抛弃官僚制，而是对其进行改革。他相信，一个政府如果被组织成能够倾听、回应和自我解释，它仍可以是正当的。但这种回应性需要他所谓的「定居」（domiciliation）：权力居住在它所治理之处。
paragraphs.en: This ethical core, what Roy would have understood through both Enlightenment ideals and Persianate ethics, insisted that governance required familiarity, attentiveness and moral clarity. He called not for the rejection of bureaucracy altogether, but for its reform. He believed that a government might still be legitimate if it was structured to listen, respond and explain itself. But such responsiveness required what he called domiciliation: power that lived where it governed.

paragraphs.cn: 在提出这一论证时，罗易预见了对现代行政的一大批评——即它会变得非人格化、程序化和冷漠疏离。远在马克斯·韦伯（Max Weber）或后来的官僚制理论家之前，罗易就观察到，遥远的治理如何常常把正义转化为仪式，把法律转化为行话，把问责转化为空洞的例行公事。他的《阐释》充满了对这类动态的描绘，不是理论上的，而是深具经验性的。
paragraphs.en: In making this argument, Roy anticipated one of the great critiques of modern administration – that it becomes impersonal, procedural and aloof. Long before Max Weber or later theorists of bureaucracy, Roy observed how distant governance often transforms justice into ritual, law into jargon, and accountability into empty routine. His Exposition is filled with illustrations of these dynamics, not theoretical, but deeply empirical.

paragraphs.cn: 罗易不是仅仅断言抽象原则，而是展示不公在基层如何运作。一个农民因错误的核定而被征税，失去了土地。一个诉讼当事人出庭数月，对法官说的每一个字都听不懂。一个村庄苦等数年，才等来一位官员解决土地纠纷。每一个例子都成为一扇窗，揭示一个脱节的系统如何施暴——不是喧哗地，而是日复一日地。罗易在此的方法颇具官僚特色，甚至可以说是程序性的。但它带有尖锐的政治锋芒。他不太关心对殖民主义的抽象谴责，而更关注不公运作的精细机制。这些不仅是行政上的怪癖，它们就是疏离的机器。
paragraphs.en: Rather than merely assert abstract principles, Roy shows how injustice functions on the ground. A farmer is taxed on a mistaken assessment and loses his land. A litigant attends court for months without understanding a word spoken by the judge. A village waits years for an official to arrive to settle a land dispute. Each example becomes a window into the ways a disconnected system can do violence, not loudly, but daily. Roy’s approach here was distinctively bureaucratic, even procedural. Yet it carried a sharp political edge. He was less concerned with abstract denunciations of colonialism and more focused on the granular mechanics of how injustice worked. These weren’t just administrative quirks: they were the machinery of alienation.

paragraphs.cn: 然而罗易仍然抱有希望。他相信改革是可能的，只要印度和英国官员都致力于服务他们所治理的人民，伦理治理就可以建立起来。他的批评不生于意识形态，而生于经验——经验被磨砺成道德愿景。在许多方面，《阐释》是一份行政文献。但在罗易手中，它变成了一种政治哲学：一种视治理为关怀的愿景。
paragraphs.en: And yet Roy remained hopeful. He believed that reform was possible, and that ethical governance could be built if both Indian and British officials committed themselves to the people they served. His critique was born not of ideology but of experience, experience sharpened into moral vision. In many ways, the Exposition was an administrative document. But in Roy’s hands, it became a form of political philosophy: a vision of governance as care.

paragraphs.cn: 这正是罗易的《阐释》如此动人的原因。它不仅是殖民政策的遗物，更是一场关于权力被公正行使时应当呈现何种面貌的对话。在一个数据驱动的决策和官僚理性再次受到审视的时代，罗易的作品提醒我们：良善治理的首要条件不是信息，而是在场。
paragraphs.en: That is what makes Roy’s Exposition so compelling. More than a relic of colonial policy, it is a dialogue on what power should look like when it is done justly. In an age when data-driven decision-making and bureaucratic rationality are once again under scrutiny, Roy’s work reminds us that the first requirement of good governance is not information, but presence.

paragraphs.cn: 罗易的思想并非源自任何单一的思想传统。它由一种非凡的影响、智识相遇与道德承诺的汇流所塑造。他的伦理学不是某一种文化或信条的产物，而是由多种传统编织而成，每一种都为正义、责任和权力的目的提供了不同的语汇。
paragraphs.en: Roy’s idea did not emerge from any single intellectual tradition. It was shaped by a remarkable confluence of influences, intellectual encounters and moral commitments. Rather than being the product of one culture or creed, his ethics was braided from multiple traditions, each offering a different vocabulary for justice, responsibility and the purpose of power.

paragraphs.cn: 他最早的著作之一、约1803年写成的《一神论者之赠》（Tuhfat-ul-Muwahhidin，意为「献给信仰独一真主者的礼物」），展现了他对伊斯兰神学、尤其是被称为「阿赫拉格」（akhlaq）的伦理传统的深入研习。在这一文献传统中，权力与美德不可分割；统治者不仅仅是君主，更是对神圣正义和社会责任负责的道德主体。借鉴纳西尔·丁·图西（Nasir al-Din al-Tusi）等思想家，罗易沉浸于一种传统之中——在其中，国王的首要职责不是扩张领土，而是培育公正与节制。
paragraphs.en: One of his earliest writings, Tuhfat-ul-Muwahhidin (‘Gift to the Believers in One God’), composed around 1803, shows his deep engagement with Islamic theology and particularly the ethical tradition known as akhlaq. In this literature, power is inseparable from virtue; rulers are not simply sovereigns but moral agents accountable to divine justice and social responsibility. Drawing on thinkers like Nasir al-Din al-Tusi, Roy was steeped in a tradition where the king’s first duty was not to expand dominion but to cultivate fairness and moderation.

paragraphs.cn: 从印度教经典，尤其是《奥义书》（Upanishads）中，罗易汲取了精神义务（达摩，dharma）的观念，以及自我认知具有公共后果的思想。在这一世界观中，国王是宇宙与社会秩序的守护者。他所施行的正义不仅属于他个人，更映照着宇宙的平衡。罗易尤为被「真理是统一的，尽管其在不同传统中的表达各异」这一观念所吸引。这给了他跨越边界寻求道德指引的信心。这种比较方法绝非智识游戏——它是一种伦理上的必要。罗易相信，道德清明往往浮现于传统的边缘，而非核心。良善治理必须是多语言的、道德上多元的、智识上慷慨的。
paragraphs.en: From Hindu texts, especially the Upanishads, Roy drew a sense of spiritual duty (dharma) and the idea that self-knowledge carried public consequences. The king, in this worldview, was the guardian of cosmic and social order. The justice he administered was not his alone, it reflected the balance of the universe. Roy was particularly drawn to the idea that truth was unified, even if its expressions varied across traditions. This gave him the confidence to seek moral guidance across boundaries. This comparative method was no intellectual game – it was an ethical necessity. Roy believed that moral clarity often emerged at the edges of traditions, not their cores. Good governance had to be multilingual, morally plural and intellectually generous.

paragraphs.cn: 基督教以另一种方式塑造了罗易的伦理。通过与传教士的交往和对《新约》的阅读，罗易逐渐钦佩耶稣的道德教导——尤其是对怜悯、谦卑以及反抗专断权威的强调。他相信耶稣示范了一种领导方式，它抬举弱者、质疑根深蒂固的权力，并拒绝将信仰与伦理分离。罗易没有皈依基督教，但他在其中找到了一种与自己信念相共鸣的道德清明。
paragraphs.en: Christianity shaped Roy’s ethics in another way. Through his interactions with Christian missionaries and his reading of the New Testament, Roy came to admire the moral teachings of Jesus – especially the emphasis on compassion, humility and resistance to arbitrary authority. He believed that Jesus modelled a form of leadership that elevated the weak, questioned entrenched power, and refused to separate faith from ethics. Roy did not convert to Christianity, but he found in it a moral clarity that resonated with his own convictions.

paragraphs.cn: 同样重要的是他通过接触欧洲哲学而遇到的自由主义思想。他读约翰·洛克（John Locke）论治理，读威廉·布莱克斯通（William Blackstone）论法律权利，读孟德斯鸠（Montesquieu）论分权。这些思想家给了他一套关于政治问责、宪政限制与公民自由的语言。罗易并非简单照搬这些思想，而是透过他多语言、多宗教教育的透镜来诠释它们。当洛克谈论生命、自由与财产时，罗易听到了更古老的关于正义、责任与统治者伦理品格的观念的回响。
paragraphs.en: Equally significant were the liberal ideas he encountered through his engagement with European philosophy. He read John Locke on governance, William Blackstone on legal rights, and Montesquieu on the separation of powers. These thinkers gave him a language for political accountability, constitutional limits and civil liberty. Rather than merely adopt these ideas, Roy interpreted them through the lens of his multilingual, multireligious education. Where Locke spoke of life, liberty and property, Roy heard echoes of older ideas about justice, responsibility and the ethical character of rulers.

paragraphs.cn: 从这一智识生态中浮现的，是一种混合的统治伦理。罗易不满足于做一个翻译者或评注者。他将自己的来源融汇成一套连贯的道德哲学：它坚持统治者是管家，而不仅仅是行政者；他们的权力是一种责任，而非一种权利。他们的正当性不来自征服或头衔，而来自他们与所治理之人的伦理贴近。
paragraphs.en: What emerged from this intellectual ecosystem was a hybrid ethics of rule. Roy was not content to be a translator or commentator. He fused his sources into a coherent moral philosophy: one that insisted that rulers were stewards, not merely administrators, their power a responsibility, not a right. And their legitimacy came not from conquest or title, but from their ethical proximity to the people they governed.

paragraphs.cn: 重要的是，罗易的伦理并非抽象的。它们旨在以具体方式指导治理。他主张，正义必须对其臣民而言是可理解的；法律必须是可理解的；政策必须反映受其影响之人的切身境况。这意味着语言、连续性和文化知识不仅是行政的附属品，它们是伦理要求。一个用波斯语或英语来审理孟加拉村民事务的法庭，不仅是效率低下，更是不公正的。
paragraphs.en: Importantly, Roy’s ethics were not abstract. They were meant to guide governance in specific ways. He argued that justice must be comprehensible to its subjects; laws must be intelligible; policies must reflect the lived conditions of those they affect. This meant that language, continuity and cultural knowledge were not mere accessories to administration, they were ethical requirements. A court that spoke in Persian or English while adjudicating the affairs of Bengali villagers was more than inefficient; it was unjust.

paragraphs.cn: 詹姆斯·伦内尔（James Rennell）所作《孟加拉与比哈尔地图》（A Map of Bengal and Bahar），选自1781年《孟加拉地图集》（An Atlas of Bengal），献给英属亚洲领地总督沃伦·黑斯廷斯（Warren Hastings）。公共领域。
paragraphs.en: ‘A Map of Bengal and Bahar’ from An Atlas of Bengal (1781) by James Rennell, dedicated to Warren Hastings, the governor-general of the British possessions in Asia. Public Domain

paragraphs.cn: 因此，罗易的伦理愿景将道德严正性与行政洞见结合在一起。它追问：如何才能在一片多语言、多宗教且被殖民的土地上公正地统治？并坚持认为，答案不在于整齐划一的控制，而在于层叠的责任。统治者必须足够贴近以理解，足够谦卑以倾听，足够有德以行动。
paragraphs.en: Roy’s ethical vision thus combined moral rigour with administrative insight. It asked how one could rule fairly in a multilingual, multireligious and colonised land. And it insisted that the answer lay not in uniform control, but in layered responsibility. The ruler must be close enough to understand, humble enough to listen, and virtuous enough to act.

paragraphs.cn: 这一宏阔的道德框架使罗易能够充当一座桥梁——在传统之间，在帝国之间，在东西方观念之间。在一个日益分裂为殖民者与被殖民者的世界里，他提供了一种既具批判性又具联结性的政治思想模型。他的伦理学取自多种来源，成为一种用以评估、并挑战帝国新秩序的工具。
paragraphs.en: This capacious moral framework allowed Roy to act as a bridge, between traditions, between empires, between ideas of East and West. In a world increasingly divided between coloniser and colonised, he offered a model of political thought that was both critical and connective. His ethics, drawn from many sources, became a tool to evaluate, and challenge, the new order of empire.

paragraphs.cn: 罗易的政治想象锻造于哲学、政治与公共传播的交汇处。他并非学院意义上的政治理论家，但他的著作整体上构成了一种连贯而激进的愿景：一种植根于伦理、由日常生活塑造、并通过非凡地驾驭多种思想传统而得以表达的愿景。
paragraphs.en: Roy’s political imagination was forged in the overlap between philosophy, politics and public communication. He was not a political theorist in the academic sense, but his writings collectively form a coherent and radical vision: a vision rooted in ethics, shaped by daily life, and articulated through an extraordinary command of multiple intellectual traditions.

paragraphs.cn: 他跨越多种体裁写作：请愿书、随笔、公开信、小册子和报纸文章。在他创办的报纸之一《智慧之月报》（Sambad Kaumudi）中，他以直接、常常是讽刺的笔调，深入参与孟加拉的道德与公民生活。他探讨的话题从寡妇再嫁到新闻自由，从教育改革到司法程序。他的孟加拉语小册子把抽象的政治原则带入切身经验的领域。运用取自农业、家庭和民间故事的隐喻，他以普通读者能够理解并产生共鸣的方式阐述自己的主张。这绝非易事。罗易正在一种尚不存在的政治语言中开疆拓土。
paragraphs.en: He wrote across genres: petitions, essays, open letters, pamphlets and newspaper articles. In Sambad Kaumudi, one of the newspapers he founded, he tackled contemporary issues in a tone that was direct, often satirical, and deeply engaged with the moral and civic life of Bengal. He addressed subjects ranging from widow remarriage to press freedom, and from education reform to judicial procedure. His Bangla tracts brought abstract political principles into the realm of lived experience. Using metaphors drawn from agriculture, family and folklore, he made his case in ways ordinary readers could grasp and relate to. This was no small feat. Roy was crafting a political language where none yet existed.

paragraphs.cn: 甚至他的宗教著作也带有政治意味。当罗易为一神论辩护或为妇女权利声张时，他隐含地在为一个伦理性的公共领域辩护——在其中，理性、相互尊重和道德问责构成宗教权威与政治权威双重的基础。他对偶像崇拜的批评不仅仅是神学上的，也是对制度性权力的批评。
paragraphs.en: Even his religious writings had political undertones. When Roy argued for monotheism or defended the rights of women, he was implicitly arguing for an ethical public sphere, one in which reason, mutual respect and moral accountability formed the basis of both religious and political authority. More than simply theological, his critique of idolatry was also a critique of institutional power.

paragraphs.cn: 罗易的政治想象由切身经验塑造，而不仅由文本传统塑造。他对东印度公司行政内部运作的了解，使他具有对权力在基层如何运作的实务理解。这种现实主义使他区别于乌托邦思想家。他不呼吁全盘拆解英国统治，而是呼吁建立一个通过回应被治理者而使权力变得合乎伦理的体制。
paragraphs.en: Roy’s political imagination was shaped by lived experience, not just textual traditions. His knowledge of the inner workings of the East India Company administration gave him a practical understanding of how power functioned on the ground. This realism distinguished him from utopian thinkers. He did not call for the wholesale dismantling of British rule but for a system where power was made ethical through its responsiveness to the governed.

paragraphs.cn: 因此，《阐释》必须被读作这一更宏大计划的一部分。它不仅是一份政策文献，更是一份伦理地图。罗易在勾勒治理对处于其接收端之人应当是何种感受：可触及的、公正的、可问责的。他在追问，政治制度如何才能被重新想象，以服务于人民而非仅仅管理人民。他的提议——比如任命印度法官或用当地语言进行审判——不仅基于行政逻辑，更基于道德推理。
paragraphs.en: The Exposition, then, must be read as part of this broader project. It is not just a policy document. It is an ethical map. Roy was outlining what governance should feel like to those at its receiving end: accessible, fair, answerable. He was asking how political institutions might be reimagined to serve people rather than simply manage them. His proposals, such as appointing Indian judges or conducting trials in local languages, were grounded not only in administrative logic but in moral reasoning.

paragraphs.cn: 关键的是，罗易相信沟通是权力的核心。他的多语言能力是一种策略，而不仅仅是一种技能。他用英语、波斯语、孟加拉语，偶尔也用阿拉伯语写作，针对不同受众调整每一则信息。对英国官员，他用改革的话语提供理性的批评。对印度读者，他提供讽刺、寓言和道德劝诫。这种多声部使他能够同时在多个领域运作——帝国的与方言的，精英的与大众的。
paragraphs.en: Crucially, Roy believed that communication was central to power. His multilingualism was a strategy, not just a skill. He wrote in English, Persian, Bangla and occasionally Arabic, tailoring each message to a different audience. To British officials, he offered reasoned critique in the language of reform. To Indian readers, he offered satire, allegory and moral exhortation. This polyphony allowed him to operate in multiple spheres at once, imperial and vernacular, elite and popular.

paragraphs.cn: 罗易的政治思想之所以难以精确界定，恰恰因为它拒绝简单的归类。它在捍卫权利上是自由主义的，在呼吁改革上是宪政的，在道德紧迫性上是神学的，在政策建议上是务实的。最重要的是，它植根于一个信念：贴近——不仅是地理上的贴近，更是理解上的贴近——对正义至关重要。
paragraphs.en: His political thought is difficult to pin down precisely because it refuses simple classification. It is liberal in its defence of rights, constitutional in its calls for reform, theological in its moral urgency, and pragmatic in its policy suggestions. Above all, it is grounded in the conviction that proximity, not just of geography but of understanding, is essential to justice.

paragraphs.cn: 因此，罗易的政治想象既宏阔又扎实。它不梦见乌托邦，它要求改革。它不浪漫化过去，也不理想化西方；它追问的是，此时此地，可以做些什么让权力更公正。在这点上，他是现代印度政治思想的先驱。尽管他很少使用我们今天所理解的民主话语，但他的工作为其奠定了重要基础：一种伦理的、包容的、对所服务人民负责的治理愿景。
paragraphs.en: Roy’s political imagination, then, was both expansive and grounded. It did not dream of utopias; it demanded reforms. It did not romanticise the past or idealise the West; it asked what could be done, here and now, to make power more just. In this, he was a pioneer of modern Indian political thought. And though he rarely used the language of democracy as we understand it today, his work laid important foundations for it: a vision of governance that is ethical, inclusive and accountable to the people it serves.

paragraphs.cn: 当罗易抵达英国时，他在某些政治和知识圈子中引起了轰动。英国一位论派（Unitarians）视他为在寻求理性宗教与伦理改革道路上的同道中人。同情政治改革的议员欢迎他对殖民治理的洞见。杰里米·边沁（Jeremy Bentham）和罗伯特·欧文（Robert Owen）等知识分子知道他的存在，并在某些情况下，被他论证的精确与文雅所吸引。然而，尽管有这种一时的好奇，罗易在正式的帝国圈子中仍基本处于边缘——或许被当作一桩奇闻欢迎，却未被严肃地视为政治上的平等者。
paragraphs.en: When Roy arrived in England, he caused a stir among certain political and intellectual circles. British Unitarians saw him as a fellow traveller in the search for rational religion and ethical reform. Parliamentarians sympathetic to political reform welcomed his insight into colonial governance. Intellectuals such as Jeremy Bentham and Robert Owen were aware of his presence and, in some cases, intrigued by the precision and civility of his arguments. Yet despite this momentary curiosity, Roy remained largely marginal in formal imperial circles, welcomed as a curiosity, perhaps, but not taken seriously as a political equal.

paragraphs.cn: 他的《阐释》并未引发全面的改革。东印度公司在司法或税收方面没有突然的改变。但这未必是一种失败。这部文献的真正意义在于其政治姿态，而非其政策影响。罗易证明，批评可以来自被殖民者，用殖民者的话语来表达，却仍能反映一种深具印度色彩的道德愿景。他的工作开创了一个先例：从那种权力被假定为不容置疑的空间内部，向权力说真话。
paragraphs.en: His Exposition didn’t prompt sweeping reform. There was no sudden change in how the East India Company administered justice or collected revenue. But this wasn’t necessarily a failure. The true significance of the text lay in its political gesture, not in its policy influence. Roy demonstrated that critique could come from the colonised, articulated in the idiom of the coloniser, and still reflect a deeply Indian moral vision. His work set a precedent for speaking truth to power, from within the very spaces where that power was presumed to be unquestioned.

paragraphs.cn: 1833年罗易因脑膜炎在布里斯托尔（Bristol）猝然离世后，他的名声迅速演变。在孟加拉，他作为改革家受到赞颂，人们记得他反对娑提（sati，即寡妇殉夫焚身）的倡导、他使印度教教育现代化的努力，以及他共同创立的改革运动「梵社」（Brahmo Sabha）。但随着印度政治的论调变得更加民族主义，罗易的形象被简化了：他要么成为印度自由主义之父，要么成为原型民族主义英雄万神殿中一个模糊的轮廓。这常常遮蔽了他政治思想的细微之处——他对官僚制的细致关注、他对伦理贴近的坚持，以及他相信道德治理是一种关怀的实践，而不仅仅是控制。
paragraphs.en: After Roy’s sudden death from meningitis in Bristol in 1833, his reputation evolved rapidly. In Bengal, he was celebrated as a reformer, remembered for his advocacy against sati (widow immolation), his efforts to modernise Hindu education, and his co-founding of the reformist movement Brahmo Sabha. But as Indian politics grew more nationalist in tone, Roy’s image was simplified: he became either the father of Indian liberalism or a faint outline in the pantheon of proto-nationalist heroes. This often obscured the nuance of his political thought, his careful attention to bureaucracy, his insistence on ethical proximity, and his belief in moral governance as a practice of care, not just control.

paragraphs.cn: 尽管如此，罗易的思想以更微妙的方式延续下来。后来的思想家如达达拜·纳奥罗吉（Dadabhai Naoroji）、戈帕尔·克里希纳·戈卡尔（Gopal Krishna Gokhale），甚至罗宾德拉纳特·泰戈尔（Rabindranath Tagore），都继承了罗易愿景的片段。纳奥罗吉对英国统治的经济学批评，呼应了罗易关于帝国治理是疏离而榨取的坚持。戈卡尔的道德语调、他对责任和渐进改革的强调，带有罗易伦理方法的痕迹。甚至甘地（Gandhi），在他对分权化、公民贴近和精神性政治的强调中，也回响着罗易的信念：权力必须栖居在人民中间才能公正。
paragraphs.en: Nonetheless, Roy’s ideas lived on in more subtle ways. Later thinkers like Dadabhai Naoroji, Gopal Krishna Gokhale and even Rabindranath Tagore inherited fragments of Roy’s vision. Naoroji’s economic critique of British rule echoed Roy’s insistence that imperial governance was alienating and extractive. Gokhale’s moral tone, his stress on responsibility and gradual reform, bore traces of Roy’s ethical method. Even Gandhi, in his emphasis on decentralisation, civic proximity and spiritual politics, echoed Roy’s belief that power must dwell among the people to be just.

paragraphs.cn: 罗易的思想也影响了20世纪的宪政思考，尽管是间接的。印度建国文献中对代表制、透明度和伦理性治国的强调，与罗易视治理为道德责任的愿景相平行。他为一种国家观念播下了种子——这种国家不仅是程序性的，更是原则性的——植根于贴近、谦卑和问责。
paragraphs.en: Roy’s ideas also influenced constitutional thinking in the 20th century, though indirectly. The emphasis in India’s founding documents on representation, transparency and ethical statecraft parallels Roy’s vision of governance as moral responsibility. He had planted the seed for a conception of the state that was not merely procedural, but principled – rooted in proximity, humility and accountability.

paragraphs.cn: 在我们当下这一刻，罗易的思想令人惊异地显得切中时宜。随着全球治理变得更加抽象，随着决策变得自动化、集中化且在情感上抽离，罗易对伦理性在场的坚持是一个有力的提醒：没有在场的权力会变成疏离；没有理解的行政会变成慢动作的暴力；而正义，归根结底，不仅是法律或效率的问题，更是贴近的问题。
paragraphs.en: In our present moment, Roy’s thought feels uncannily timely. As global governance grows more abstract, as decision-making becomes automated, centralised and emotionally disengaged, Roy’s insistence on ethical presence is a potent reminder that power without presence becomes alienation; that administration without understanding becomes violence in slow motion; and that justice, in the end, is not only a question of law or efficiency, but of nearness.

paragraphs.cn: 罗易或许未能活到看见一个去殖民化的印度。但他帮助想象了这样一个印度：在其中，统治者是人民中间的道德主体，而非遥远的权威。
paragraphs.en: Roy may not have lived to see a decolonised India. But he helped imagine one in which rulers were moral agents among their people, not distant authorities.

paragraphs.cn: 罗易客死异乡，但他的智识遗产存活于他所提出的问题之中。是什么使权威成为公正的？一个政府要多贴近才能合乎伦理？制度能否不仅高效地、更道德地行事？
paragraphs.en: Roy died far from home, but his intellectual legacy lives on in the questions he raised. What makes authority just? How close must a government be to be ethical? Can institutions behave not just efficiently, but morally?

paragraphs.cn: 他的回答一以贯之，却非简单化。贴近很重要。语言很重要。问责很重要。这些不是抽象概念。它们是尊严与正义的日常条件。对罗易而言，治理不仅关乎权力，它关乎权力在与人们生活接触时所采取的伦理形式。
paragraphs.en: His answers were consistent, not simplistic. Proximity matters. Language matters. Accountability matters. These are not abstractions. They are the daily conditions of dignity and justice. For Roy, governance was not just about power, it was about the ethical form that power takes when it comes into contact with people’s lives.

paragraphs.cn: 在《阐释》中，罗易要求的并不是由印度人接管英国的制度。他要求的是某种更根本的东西：治理若要正当，就必须是可理解的、人道的，并植根于伦理自觉。这不仅是对英国统治的批评。它是一份蓝图，适用于任何希望以正直延续的权力体制——无论是帝国的、民主的，还是其他形式的。
paragraphs.en: In the Exposition, Roy was not asking for an Indian takeover of British institutions. He was asking for something more foundational: that governance, to be legitimate, must be intelligible, humane and grounded in ethical awareness. This was not merely a critique of British rule. It was a blueprint for any system of power, imperial, democratic or otherwise, that hoped to endure with integrity.

paragraphs.cn: 在一个日益由距离所定义的世界里——公民与国家之间、政策与经验之间、法律与正义之间——罗易提醒我们，良善的政府不仅是法律或统计数字的问题。它是在场的问题。他坚持统治者应生活在被统治者中间、用他们自己的语言倾听他们、并在道德上对他们负责，这一原则超越了其所处的时代。在他最乐观的时刻，罗易相信，即使是殖民国家也能被救赎——只要它学会不从远处、而是从内部进行治理。他的作品表明，贴近不仅是空间上的，更是伦理上的。它意味着跨越差异去倾听，并以这样一种谦卑来治理：任何法律，除非被理解、被感受、可问责，否则就不是公正的。
paragraphs.en: In a world increasingly defined by distance, between citizen and state, between policy and experience, between law and justice, Roy offers a reminder that good government is not only a matter of laws or statistics. It is a matter of presence. His insistence that rulers live among the ruled, listen to them in their own languages, and remain morally accountable to them, is a principle that transcends his time. In his most optimistic moments, Roy believed that even the colonial state could be redeemed if it learned to govern not from a distance, but from within. His work suggests that proximity is not just spatial, but ethical. It means listening across difference, and governing with the humility that no law is just unless it is understood, felt, and answerable.

paragraphs.cn: 我们如今生活在一个数据驱动治理、自动化决策和庞大官僚机构的时代。国家变得更有能力，但也更非人格化。在这样一个时刻，罗易的愿景再次显得激进。不是因为它的宏大，而是因为它的亲密。他没有要求被铭记。他坚持要求的是：权力应当可见、贴近、可问责。这一愿景仍然重要。或许现在比以往任何时候都更如此，它值得被阅读——不是作为遗物，而是作为一种挑衅：一种将伦理带回治理日常运作之中的召唤。
paragraphs.en: We live now in an age of data-driven governance, automated decisions and vast bureaucracies. The state has grown more capable, but also more impersonal. In such a moment, Roy’s vision feels radical again. Not because it is grandiose, but because it is intimate. He did not ask to be remembered. He asked, insistently, that power be visible, proximate and accountable. That vision still matters. And perhaps now more than ever, it deserves to be read not as a relic, but as a provocation: a call to bring ethics back into the everyday workings of governance.

articles.title: 整理之图书馆

articles.content_cn:
在大城阿莱提亚（Alethia），矗立着一座由一条不可通融的法则所统治的图书馆：每一本书都必须找到它应在的位置。馆长是一位指尖染着墨迹的老人，他把所有的日子都花在走过无尽的排架上，把走失的书册送回它们指定的家。一本诗集搁在地理书之间，对他而言是一道小小的伤口；一部医学论著被放在童话旁边，是一种不纠正便不会消散的隐痛。他常对学徒们说，图书馆是一个活物，而像一切活物一样，它仅仅是为了保持自身，就需要不断的照料。

然而学徒们注意到一件令人困惑的事。每个清晨他们到来时，图书馆都比前一晚略微更乱一些，尽管黄昏之后并无一位读者入内。书册仿佛自行迁徙：一本薄薄的小说下滑了两层，一部沉重的图鉴斜倚着落下，而小开本的书则向前爬向过道的边缘，仿佛被某种安静的潮汐牵引。馆长解释说，这并非有人作祟。关门时的一缕风、马车驶过时建筑细微的颤动，甚至尘埃的沉降——所有这些微小而冷漠的力，都把书从完美的对齐中一点点推离。没有任何一次推动是重要的；但合在一起，经过无数个夜晚，它们毫不留情。

一位聪慧的学徒名叫克莉娅（Clea），提出了一个优雅的办法。「既然混乱因细小的意外而潜入，」她说，「我们只需以细小而恒常的努力把它挡住。为每条过道指派一位守护者，其唯一职责便是任何一本书一走失就立刻归位。」馆长同意了，整个季节里这个办法运作得极为美妙：图书馆闪耀着近乎完美的秩序，守护者们如无声的钟表机械穿行于厅堂之间。但克莉娅仔细观察，渐生忧虑。她注意到守护者们正在疲惫。要归还一本书，守护者必须读它的书脊、忆起它的正当位置、走到那里、把它插入——而这小小的劳作需要一次又一次地重复，因为那安静的潮汐从未停歇。维持秩序每小时都在耗费气力，而那气力一旦付出，便再也收不回。

更糟的是，克莉娅发现了一种更深的不对称。当图书馆井然有序时，守护者的任务轻松而清晰：每一本错置的书都显眼，归位是简单、可预见的举动。但随着混乱增长——而它总是增长，只要有足够多无人打扰的夜晚——这工作以一种无人预见的方式变得更难。已经漂移的书可以被按许多种可能的顺序归位，其中只有一种是馆长最初的安排；藏书散得越开，修复所需的搜寻与猜测就越多，它吞噬的气力也越大。克莉娅看出，秩序是那稀有而脆弱的状态，是无数排列中独一的一种。混乱并不是某种潜入的东西——它是自然的丰盈，是那片任何无人照看的藏书终将漂向的排列之海。要逆转那漂移，需要判断、记忆与劳作；而听任它，则什么都不需要。

最后，馆长把学徒们召集起来，直言相告。「我们无法击败那潮汐，」他说，「我们只能永远推抗它，而这推抗绝不可停。一座被遗弃的图书馆失去秩序，并非因为有什么东西把它推向混乱，而是因为混乱的排列方式如此之多，有序的方式却只有一种——而那冷漠的世界，以它的风与颤动，不偏不倚地造访每一种排列。我们的劳作，是保持自身的代价。我们停工的那一日，便是图书馆一寸一寸地不再是一座图书馆之日。」学徒们终于明白了：他们并非在与一个恶人搏斗，而是在与一道斜坡相抗——一道温和而永恒的坡，除非被托住，否则万物都顺着它滑落。于是他们回到排架前，不是带着挫败，而是睁开双眼，知晓要留住所爱之物，便是无止境地照料它。

这个故事揭示了熵（entropy）的本质——它衡量一个系统可以被排列的方式有多少，也是万物自然趋向混乱的缘由。由于混乱的排列远比有序的排列多得多，任何一次随机的推撞都压倒性地更可能把系统推向凌乱而非整齐；一间无人照看的房间、一杯冷却的茶、一叠洗乱的纸牌都朝那个方向滑落，仅仅是因为无序的状态在数量上远远超过有序的状态。逆转这漂移从不免费：它要求信息（在无数排列中认出那唯一的有序排列）、能量与劳作，而那气力一旦付出便无法收回，这正是宇宙的总混乱只增不减的原因。熵并非一股把事物推向混乱的力，而是一道安静的统计斜坡，除非我们不断推抗，否则万物都顺着它滑落。
articles.content_en:
In the great city of Alethia, there stood a library governed by a single, unyielding law: every book must find its proper place. The Master Librarian, an old man with ink-stained fingers, spent his days walking the endless shelves, returning stray volumes to their appointed homes. A book of verse resting among the geographies was a small wound to him; a treatise on medicine shelved beside the fairy tales was an ache that would not fade until corrected. The library, he often told the apprentices, was a living thing, and like all living things it demanded constant care merely to remain itself.

Yet the apprentices noticed something puzzling. Each morning they arrived to find the library slightly more disordered than the night before, though no reader had entered after dusk. Volumes migrated on their own, it seemed: a thin novel slipped two shelves down, a heavy atlas settled at an angle, and small books crept forward toward the aisle's edge as though drawn by some quiet tide. The Master explained that this was no mischief. A breath of wind from a closing door, the faint trembling of the building as carts rumbled past, even the settling of dust — all these tiny, indifferent forces nudged the books from their perfect alignment. No single nudge mattered; together, over many nights, they were relentless.

One bright apprentice named Clea proposed an elegant solution. 「If disorder creeps in by small accidents,」 she said, 「then we need only a small, constant effort to hold it back. We shall appoint a Keeper for each aisle, whose sole task is to restore any book the moment it strays.」 The Master agreed, and for a season the plan worked beautifully: the library gleamed with an almost perfect order, and the Keepers moved like silent clockwork through the halls. But Clea, watching closely, grew troubled. The Keepers, she noticed, were growing tired. To return a book, a Keeper had to read its spine, recall its proper place, walk there, and slot it in — and this small labor was needed again and again, for the quiet tide never ceased. Holding order cost effort every single hour, and that effort, once spent, could not be recovered.

Worse, Clea discovered a deeper asymmetry. When the library was perfectly ordered, the Keepers' task was easy and clear: every misplaced book stood out, and returning it was a simple, predictable act. But as disorder grew — and it always grew, given enough undisturbed nights — the work became harder in a way no one had foreseen. Books that had drifted could be put back in many possible orders, only one of which was the Master's original; the more the collection had scattered, the more searching and guessing the restoration required, the more effort it swallowed. Order, Clea saw, was the rare and fragile state, the one configuration among countless others. Disorder was not a thing that crept in — it was the natural abundance, the sea of arrangements toward which any unattended collection inevitably drifted. To reverse that drift required judgment, memory, and work; to allow it required nothing at all.

In the end the Master gathered the apprentices and spoke plainly. 「We cannot defeat the tide,」 he said. 「We can only ever push against it, and the pushing must never stop. A library left to itself loses its order not because something pushes it toward chaos, but because there are so many ways to be disordered and only one way to be ordered — and the indifferent world, with its winds and tremblings, visits every arrangement impartially. Our labor is the price of remaining ourselves. The day we cease the work is the day the library, inch by inch, ceases to be a library.」 The apprentices understood at last: they were not fighting a villain, but a slope — a gentle, permanent incline down which everything slides unless held. And so they returned to the shelves, not in defeat, but with eyes open, knowing that to keep what they loved was to tend it without end.

This story reveals the essence of entropy — the measure of how many ways a system can be arranged, and the reason things naturally drift toward disorder. Because there are vastly more disordered arrangements than ordered ones, any random nudge is overwhelmingly more likely to push a system toward mess than toward neatness; an unattended room, a cooling cup of tea, a shuffled deck all slide that way simply because the disordered states vastly outnumber the ordered ones. Reversing the drift is never free: it demands information (knowing the one ordered arrangement among countless others), energy, and work, and once that effort is spent it cannot be recovered, which is why the total disorder of the universe only ever grows. Entropy is not a force pushing things into chaos, but the quiet statistical slope down which everything glides unless we continually push back.
