articles.summary: 在港口小镇 Verel(维莱尔),住着一位年迈的守灯人 Halen(哈伦),他唯一的职责就是守望海面上归航的船只。每到傍晚,渔夫的妻子们便爬上山丘来到他的灯塔,问着同一个焦虑的问题:我丈夫的船今晚会回家吗?Halen 永远无法肯定地回答,因为大海自有其主意;但多年下来,他学会了辨认每一艘远船绕过海角
articles.content_cn:
在港口小镇 Verel(维莱尔),住着一位年迈的守灯人 Halen(哈伦),他唯一的职责就是守望海面上归航的船只。每到傍晚,渔夫的妻子们便爬上山丘来到他的灯塔,问着同一个焦虑的问题:我丈夫的船今晚会回家吗?Halen 永远无法肯定地回答,因为大海自有其主意;但多年下来,他学会了辨认每一艘远船绕过海角时升起的细细烟柱。有些船烧的是松木,烟柱苍白,几近纯白;另一些烧的是煤炭,烟柱乌黑、满是煤灰。Halen 还痛苦地明白了一件事:烟的颜色并非事情的全部真相,尽管每一位即将守寡的妻子都希望它是。

Halen 常向那些妇人解释,麻烦在于:在去看烟之前,得先知道船队原本是怎样划分的。他早就数过,从 Verel 出海的每十条船里,有七条烧松木、三条烧煤炭——这不过是镇上的习惯,因为松木便宜又充裕。而一旦出事,这两种烟的表现截然不同。一艘状况良好的松木船升起淡白的烟柱,可一艘船体开裂、正在进水的松木船同样升起淡白的烟,因为湿木头闷烧时又淡又弱。一艘状况良好的煤炭船升起乌黑的烟柱;而一艘遇险的煤炭船则根本不冒烟,因为被淹的炉灶会把火活活闷死。所以当 Halen 在地平线上看见淡白的烟时,他不能干脆断言船没事——因为淡白的烟既来自走运的松木船,也来自垂死的松木船。

一个灰蒙蒙的傍晚,年轻的妻子 Maren(玛伦)气喘吁吁地跑上灯塔,说她透过薄雾瞥见了一缕淡白的烟。她把它当作平安的承诺。Halen 让她坐下,然后按自己多年摸索出的法子把事情算出声来。他说,假设有十条船出海——七条是松木船,三条是煤炭船。在这七条松木船里,大多数夜晚有六条平安归来、一条沉没。在这三条煤炭船里,两条平安归来、一条沉没,可沉没的煤炭船根本不冒烟。所以她看见的那缕淡白的烟,只能来自某一条松木船——而在这七条之中,六条安全、一条遇难。Halen 让数字在空气中沉淀片刻才接着说:那缕淡白的烟绝非保证,它只是把范围从十条船缩到了七条,而在这七条之中,她丈夫平安的胜算始终是六比一,既不比松木船一贯的胜算更好,也不比它更糟。

Maren 皱起眉头,她原以为那缕淡白的烟本身就是好消息。Halen 轻轻摇头。他说,烟只是一名证人;它能告诉你你望见的是哪一种船,却不能凭自身告诉你船会不会沉。真正支配他回答的,是更安静的东西:原本有多少松木船、多少煤炭船,以及每一种通常的遭遇如何。那缕淡白的烟只是从他的账簿里挑出了一只抽屉——松木抽屉——而抽屉一旦拉开,里头的数目仍是从前那个数目。Halen 警告说,凡是忘了最初数目、只盯着烟的人,当一艘冒淡白烟的船沉没时总会大吃一惊,因为他错把「挑出一只抽屉」当成了「把抽屉掏空」。

于是 Halen 给 Maren 的回答并非单凭看烟,而是同时在心中握住三样东西:在未见任何烟之前船队的格局、每一种船以烟自报的方式,以及此刻悬于海角之上的那一缕淡白。第一样告诉他从何处起算;第二样告诉他如何解读所见;第三样是新的证据,把整个世界收窄。唯有把三者编织在一起,他才能诚实开口,而他说出的既非安慰也非绝望,而是一个数字——在所有冒淡白烟的船里,七分之六的机会,她丈夫会在天亮前自己走上这座山丘。Maren 向他道谢,终于明白那缕烟并没有对她撒谎;她只是要它承担超出它所能承受的分量罢了。

这则故事揭示了贝叶斯定理(Bayes' theorem)的本质——要在看到新证据后判断某事的可能性,你必须把三样东西结合起来:在证据出现之前它原本有多可能(松木船对煤炭船的原始比例)、这条证据有多可靠地指向每一种可能(松木冒淡白烟、煤炭冒黑烟或不冒烟),以及证据本身(海角上那缕淡白的烟)。新证据并不取代你原有的信念,它只是把你现在所站的位置收窄到账簿中的某一只抽屉,而那只抽屉里的数目仍取决于世界事先是怎样安排的。忘了起点的比例,你就会过分信赖一条孤证;把三者编织在一起,你的回答才会变成一个诚实的数字,而非一个心愿。
articles.content_en:
In the harbor town of Verel, there lived an old lantern keeper named Halen whose only duty was to watch the sea for returning ships. Each evening the fishermen's wives would climb the hill to his tower and ask the same anxious question: will my husband's boat come home tonight? Halen could never answer with certainty, for the sea kept its own counsel, but over many years he had learned to read the thin column of smoke that rose from each distant vessel as it rounded the cape. Some boats burned pine, which gave a pale, almost white plume; others burned coal, which gave a dark, sooty one. And Halen had come to understand, painfully, that the color of the smoke was not the whole truth of the matter, though every widow-to-be hoped it was.

The trouble, Halen often explained to the women, lay in knowing how the boats were divided before one ever looked at the smoke. Of every ten boats that put out from Verel, he had long counted, seven burned pine and three burned coal; that was simply the habit of the town, for pine was cheap and plentiful. And the two smokes did not behave alike when trouble came. A pine-burning boat in good health raised a pale plume, but so too did a pine-burning boat whose hull had cracked and was taking water, for the wet wood smoldered pale and faint. A coal-burning boat in good health raised a dark plume; a coal-burning boat in distress, by contrast, raised no plume at all, for a flooded stove choked its fire to death. So when Halen saw pale smoke on the horizon, he could not simply announce that the boat was fine, because pale smoke rose from the lucky pine boats and the dying pine boats alike.

One gray evening a young wife named Maren came breathless to the tower, having glimpsed a pale plume through the mist. She took it as a promise of safety. Halen asked her to sit, and he worked the matter aloud as he had taught himself to do. Suppose ten boats had gone out, he said; seven are pine boats, three are coal boats. Of the seven pine boats, on most evenings six come home safe and one founders. Of the three coal boats, two come home safe and one founders, but a foundering coal boat shows no smoke at all. So the pale plume she had seen could only have come from one of the pine boats — and within that group of seven, six would be safe and one lost. Halen let the numbers settle before he spoke again: the pale smoke, far from being a guarantee, had only narrowed the field from ten boats to seven, and within those seven the odds were six to one in her husband's favor, no better and no worse than the pine boats had always been.

Maren frowned, for she had believed the pale smoke was itself the good news. Halen shook his head gently. The smoke, he said, was only a witness; it could tell you which kind of boat you were looking at, but it could not by itself tell you whether the boat would sink. What truly governed his answer was something quieter: how many pine boats there were to begin with, how many coal boats, and how each kind tended to fare. The pale plume had merely selected one drawer of his ledger — the pine drawer — and once that drawer was open, the count inside it was what it had always been. A man who forgot the original count, Halen warned, and looked only at the smoke, would be forever surprised when a pale-plumed boat went down, because he had mistaken the selecting of a drawer for the emptying of it.

And so Halen gave his answer to Maren not by reading the smoke alone, but by holding three things in his mind at once: the lay of the fleet before any smoke was seen, the way each kind of boat announced itself in smoke, and the single pale plume now hanging above the cape. The first told him where to start; the second told him how to interpret what he saw; the third was the new evidence that narrowed the world down. Only when all three were woven together could he speak honestly, and what he said was neither comfort nor despair but a number — six chances of seven, among the boats that raise pale smoke, that her husband would walk up the hill himself by morning. Maren thanked him, understanding at last that the smoke had not lied to her; she had only asked it to carry more weight than it could bear.

This story reveals the essence of Bayes' theorem — that to judge how likely something is after seeing new evidence, you must combine three things: how likely it was before the evidence (the original share of pine versus coal boats), how reliably the evidence points to each possibility (pine gives pale smoke, coal gives dark or none), and the evidence itself (the pale plume on the cape). New evidence does not replace your prior beliefs; it only narrows which drawer of the ledger you are now standing in, and the count inside that drawer still depends on how the world was arranged beforehand. Forget the starting proportions and you will over-trust a single clue; weave all three together and your answer becomes an honest number rather than a wish.

articles.title: 美国两极分化对立阵营的共通之处：对生命意义与存在本身的深切焦虑
articles.author: Carl Weems
articles.summary: 打开社交媒体，我常常面对一种刺目的反差：来自不同朋友的激烈且截然对立的观点。这些评论里有时夹杂着侮辱、人身攻击和谩骂。
articles.content_cn:
打开社交媒体，我常常面对一种刺目的反差：来自不同朋友的激烈且截然对立的观点。这些评论里有时夹杂着侮辱、人身攻击和谩骂。

注意到这种充满戾气的两极分化的，显然不止我一人。近期的民调显示，多数美国人认为这个国家无法跨越当前的分裂。

作为一名人类发展与家庭研究领域的教授，二十多年来，我一直在研究和撰写关于创伤性与不良童年经历以及存在性焦虑的文章。刷着信息流时，我忽然意识到：双方有一个共同之处——一种深切的存在性恐惧。

尽管政治两极分化有许多潜在成因，但存在性焦虑是较少受到关注的一个。

几个世纪以来，哲学家们一直在探讨存在性焦虑这一概念。我自己的实证研究建立在20世纪中叶哲学家保罗·田立克（Paul Tillich）的著作之上，他勾勒了这种根本性人类恐惧的三个面向：

存在性焦虑，是人类与死亡、道德责任以及对意义的追寻之间内在的直面。

我和同事发现，这些恐惧极为普遍——我们研究中75%到86%的参与者至少认同其中一项担忧。存在性焦虑水平较高，与心理健康不良的指标相关，比如抑郁症状和自杀意念。在经历过危及生命事件的人群中，存在性焦虑水平也更高。例如，在从自然灾害中幸存之后，多达94%的研究参与者报告了这种恐惧的至少一个维度。

重要的是，我们的研究表明，存在性焦虑与攻击性相关。在一项关于青少年的研究中，我们发现，用量表测得的更为极端的存在性焦虑，与两种攻击性相关：主动型攻击和反应型攻击。主动型攻击是目标导向的、蓄意的、无端的，而反应型攻击则是在回应真实的或感知到的挑衅或威胁时产生的。

存在性恐惧的根源，几乎在于每个人都会担忧的事——至少偶尔会担忧。但具体是什么触发这种焦虑，可能因你的世界观而异。

比如，当我刷社交媒体时，我看到一些朋友表达对基本安全议题、国家命运、文化侵蚀以及传统价值丧失的焦虑。这些担忧又与其他朋友的帖子相互映照，后者表达的是对环境被破坏、民主失灵、平等丧失的忧虑。

尽管这些表达的内容在意识形态上可能截然对立，但每一方都折射出对社会命运、死亡或一种有意义的生活方式终结的更深忧虑。未曾言明却暗含其中的，是这样一种恐惧：「另一方」对自己的存在构成了真实而迫近的威胁。

尽管触发情境可能因个人信念而异，但双方的视角都反映出关于意义、道德方向与生存的存在性关切。

但存在性焦虑不仅仅是某些此类痛苦的潜在根源。研究表明，潜藏的恐惧会加剧攻击性。若不加遏制，恐惧可能螺旋式升级为潜在的暴力。

好消息是，尽管核心的存在性恐惧也许永远不会完全消退，但你可以识别它们、缓解它们，甚至可能将其引导向适应性的行动。

认知行为疗法（cognitive behavior therapy）与接纳承诺疗法（acceptance and commitment therapy）的技术，提供了一条寻找共识、防止存在性恐惧升级为暴力的路径。

这些技术的核心，是识别并直面恐惧。两者都能帮助参与者克服一些常见倾向，比如只看到证据的一面，或是把事情灾难化、认为情况比实际糟糕得多。例如，接纳承诺疗法会教参与者如何培育心理灵活性，学会容忍令人不适的想法或情绪，并练习依照自己的核心价值行事。这些技能结合起来，能促成积极的行动，而非破坏性的反应。

尽管我的社交媒体信息流可能令人不安，但我也看到现实中有一些人找到了跨越分歧相连结的实例。比如，一位发帖者感谢另一位评论者的留言，说这帮助她意识到，对方的视角对他而言所代表的存在性价值。在那次交流之后，第二位发帖者承认自己此前只看到了一面。换言之，他们各自识别出了对方的存在性恐惧——把它作为恐惧加以接纳，帮助他们缓和了对立，更建设性地向前迈进。

关键的一点在于，处于每一个议题各方的所有人，都渴望安全、目标感与归属感。认识到我们所共有的核心存在性关切，正是两极化恐惧的根基——这或许是弥合分歧、降低恐惧驱动型攻击性风险的重要一步。
articles.content_en:
Opening my social media feed, I’m often confronted with a jarring contrast: intense, diametrically opposed perspectives from different friends. The comments can be laced with insult, character attack and invective.

I’m certainly not the only one noticing this kind of vitriolic polarization. Recent polling suggests a majority of Americans believe that the country cannot overcome its current divisions.

As a professor of human development and family studies, I’ve researched and written about traumatic and adverse childhood experiences and existential anxiety for over 20 years. Scrolling through my feed, I was struck by the recognition that both sides had something in common: a profound sense of existential fear.

While political polarization has many potential causes, existential anxiety is one that has received less attention.

Philosophers have written about the concept of existential anxiety for centuries. My own empirical research is based on the writings of the mid-20th century philosopher Paul Tillich, who outlines three facets of this fundamental human fear:

Existential anxiety is humanity’s inherent confrontation with mortality, moral responsibility and search for meaning.

My colleagues and I have found that these fears are very common – between 75% and 86% of participants in our research endorsing at least one concern. Higher levels of existential anxiety are associated with indicators of poor mental health, such as symptoms of depression and suicidal ideation. Existential anxiety levels are also elevated among those who have experienced a life-threatening event. For instance, after surviving a natural disaster, up to 94% of research participants reported at least one dimension of this fear.

Importantly, our research suggests that existential anxiety is associated with aggression. In one study of teens, we found that more extreme existential anxiety as measured with the existential anxiety questionnaire was associated with two kinds of aggression: proactive and reactive. Proactive aggression is goal driven, deliberate and unprovoked, while reactive aggression comes in response to a real or perceived provocation or threat.

Existential fears have their roots in things that pretty much everyone worries about, at least from time to time. But what specifically triggers this anxiety can be different depending on your worldview.

For instance, as I scroll social media, I see friends expressing anxiety about fundamental safety issues, the fate of the nation, cultural erosion and the loss of traditional values. These concerns are mirrored by other friends’ posts expressing concern that the environment is being destroyed, democracy is failing and equality is lost.

Though the content of these expressions can be ideologically opposed, each reflects deeper concerns about societal fate, death or the end of a meaningful way of life. Unspoken but underlying is the fear that the “other side” represents a real and impending threat to one’s very existence.

Though the triggering circumstances can differ based on personal beliefs, both sides’ perspectives reflect existential concerns about meaning, moral direction and survival.

But existential anxiety isn’t just the likely root of some of this distress. Research suggests that underlying fear can increase aggression. Left unchecked, fears may spiral into potential violence.

The good news is that while core existential fears may never fully abate, you can identify them, alleviate them and possibly even channel them toward adaptive action.

The techniques of cognitive behavior therapy and acceptance and commitment therapy provide a path toward finding common ground and preventing existential fears from escalating into violence.

Core to these techniques is recognizing and facing the fear. They both help participants overcome common tendencies such as seeing only one side of the evidence or catastrophizing that things are much worse than they really are. Acceptance and commitment therapy, for example, teaches participants how to cultivate psychological flexibility, learn to tolerate uncomfortable thoughts or emotions, and practice acting in alignment with one’s core values. Together, these skills foster positive action as opposed to destructive reaction.

As disturbing as my social media feed can be, I’ve also seen real-world instances of people figuring out how to connect across a divide. For instance, one poster appreciated another’s comment for helping her realize the existential value his perspective represented to him. Following that exchange, the second poster acknowledged he’d been seeing only one side. In other words, they each recognized the other person’s existential fear – accepting it as such helped them de-escalate the confrontation and move forward more constructively.

The critical point is that people on all sides of every issue yearn for safety, purpose and belonging. Recognizing that the core existential concerns we all share underlie polarized fears might be an important step toward bridging divides and reducing the risk of fear-driven aggression.

articles.title: 两座花园的看守人
articles.author: AI Parable (inspired by Amanda Askell)

articles.content_cn:
在一个宁静的村庄里，住着一个名叫 Mara（玛拉）的男子，被委派为两座相邻花园的看守人，两园之间只隔着一扇小门。东园寒冷潮湿，泥土上凝着厚重的露水；西园温暖干燥，被阳光晒得金黄。村民们深知两园的法则：温热从不自行逆流而上。把一颗滚烫的苹果放进冷园，它会渐渐变凉；但把一颗冰冷的苹果放进暖园，它只能从周围窃取热量才慢慢变温。两座花园若任其自然，便会缓缓趋向同一个不冷不热的温度——暖的渐凉，冷的渐温，直到彼此再无值得称道的分别。

然而 Mara 是个耐性十足、目光敏锐的人。他搬了张凳子坐在门前，开始观察那些在两园之间随风流和孩童的脚步翻滚跳跃的苹果。他注意到有些苹果飞得又快又猛，嗡嗡地满含能量；而另一些则懒洋洋地挪动，几乎不带声息。他还进一步发现：那些飞快炽热、满身火气的苹果，闯进冷园的几率，和那些迟缓冰凉的苹果闯进暖园的几率一样大。要知道，那扇门两边都能自由开合，对任何过客都不加盘问。

于是 Mara 想出一个小巧的手艺。他下定决心：只为那些飞快炽热、奔向暖园的苹果开门，也只为那些迟缓冰凉、奔向冷园的苹果开门。当一颗火热的苹果朝冷园扑来，他便当面把门紧紧关上。当一颗慵懒的苹果朝暖园飘来，他也关上门，任它停留原地。就这样，时辰一寸寸过去，暖园愈发温暖，将所有最迅捷、最饱满的苹果都聚拢到自己怀里；冷园则愈发寒冷，收拢了所有昏沉羸弱的苹果。原本正滑向乏味同一的两座花园，此刻狠狠地彼此拉开，一座炽烈，一座霜寒。

村民们大为惊诧，因为这件事违逆了世间一切寻常的流向。Mara 接手了两座正趋于均同的花园，却让其一热一寒，而他没有点燃任何炉火，也没有汲取一桶冰水。他们从热园引出蒸汽，推动一架小小的磨坊；又从冷园取来寒意，保存他们的果实。功业便从两园的温差中汩汩流出，而 Mara 除了一张凳子和一份耐性，别无所求。一位睿智的长者皱起眉头，说这种事不可能永远无偿地持续下去，那一份守望本身必定有所耗费，纵然 Mara 的双手从未动弹，他的门也只在润滑的铰链上轻转。

长者是对的，只是那耗费隐而不显。要知道哪颗苹果快、哪颗慢，Mara 就必须在每一颗靠近时加以度量，而度量从来不是无偿之举。他放行过的每一颗苹果、拦阻过的每一颗苹果，都得在某处留有记录——或记在脑中，或刻在门柱上——而那本账簿无休止地膨胀。只要 Mara 无所遗忘，两园便维持着它们辉煌的分裂；可一旦他的记忆填满，非得抹去旧记才能辨冷热，整套安排便会崩塌，退回它被哄劝而出之前那不冷不热的均同。这手艺唯有在看守人持续记账时才管用，而账簿要永远记下去，便不可能不付代价。

这则故事揭示了 Maxwell's demon（麦克斯韦妖）的本质——一个关于微小而聪慧的守门人的思想实验：它将快速（炽热）的粒子与缓慢（冰冷）的粒子分拣开来，只让迅捷者进入一室，只让迟缓者进入另一室。借由这种有选择的分拣，这「妖」似乎能让热的一侧更热、冷的一侧更冷，而看不见它做任何功，仿佛逆转了热的自然流向，违背了热力学第二定律。然而正如长者所疑，这「妖」必须对它分拣的每一颗粒子加以度量、记忆并记录信息，而抹除这些信息本身就是一个不可逆的、产生热量的过程。Landauer 原理（兰道尔原理）指出，销毁这些累积的记忆有着最低限度的热力学代价，因此这「妖」赢不了：它为清空账簿所必须付出的热量，抵消了分拣气体所得的收益，第二定律遂巍然不破。
articles.content_en:
In a quiet village there lived a man named Mara, who was appointed caretaker of two adjoining gardens separated by a single gate. The east garden was cold and damp, its soil heavy with dew, while the west garden was warm and dry, baked golden by the sun. The villagers understood the rule of the two gardens well: warmth never flowed uphill of its own accord. A hot apple placed in the cold garden would cool, but a cold apple placed in the warm garden would only grow warm by stealing heat from its surroundings. The two gardens, left to themselves, were drifting slowly toward the same lukewarm temperature, the warm one cooling and the cold one warming, until neither held any distinction worth speaking of.

Mara, however, was a patient and watchful sort. He took his stool beside the gate and began to observe the apples as they tumbled and bounced between the two gardens, carried by the wind and the feet of children. He noticed that some apples flew fast and fierce, humming with energy, while others crept along lazily, barely stirring. And he noticed something further: the fast, hot apples, the ones full of fire, were just as likely to wander into the cold garden as the slow, cold ones were to wander into the warm garden. The gate, you see, swung freely both ways and asked no questions of whoever passed.

So Mara devised a small craft. He resolved to open the gate only for the fast, hot apples heading toward the warm garden, and only for the slow, cold apples heading toward the cold garden. When a fiery apple bounded toward the cold garden, he shut the gate firmly in its face. When a sluggish apple drifted toward the warm garden, he closed the door and let it be. In this way, hour by hour, the warm garden grew warmer still, gathering unto itself all the swiftest and most energetic apples, while the cold garden grew colder still, collecting all the drowsy and faint ones. The two gardens, which had been sliding toward a dull sameness, now pulled apart with a vengeance, one blazing and one frosty.

Now the villagers were astounded, for here was a thing contrary to all the ordinary drift of the world. Mara had taken two gardens that were slowly evening out, and made one hot and one cold, all without lighting a fire or drawing a single bucket of ice. From the hot garden they drew steam to turn a little mill; from the cold garden they drew chill to preserve their fruit. Work flowed out of the difference between the two, and Mara asked nothing in return but his stool and his patience. A wise elder frowned and said that such a thing could not be sustained forever for free, that the watchfulness itself must cost something, though Mara's hands never stirred and his gate swung on oiled hinges.

The elder was right, though the cost was hidden. To know which apple was fast and which was slow, Mara had to measure each one as it approached, and measurement is never a free act. The record of every apple he had admitted and every apple he had turned away had to be kept somewhere, in his memory or in marks upon the gatepost, and that ledger grew without end. So long as Mara forgot nothing, the gardens held their splendid divide; but the moment his memory filled and he could no longer distinguish hot from cold without erasing old notes, the whole arrangement would collapse back into the lukewarm sameness from which it had been coaxed. The craft worked only so long as the caretaker kept his books, and the books could not be kept forever without cost.

By this selective sorting, the demon appears to make a hot side hotter and a cold side colder without doing any visible work, seemingly reversing the natural flow of heat and violating the second law of thermodynamics. The catch, as the elder suspected, is that the demon must measure, remember, and record information about every particle it sorts, and the erasure of that information is itself an irreversible, heat-producing process. paragraphs.cn: 在一个宁静的村庄里，住着一个名叫 Mara（玛拉）的男子，被委派为两座相邻花园的看守人，两园之间只隔着一扇小门。东园寒冷潮湿，泥土上凝着厚重的露水；西园温暖干燥，被阳光晒得金黄。村民们深知两园的法则：温热从不自行逆流而上。把一颗滚烫的苹果放进冷园，它会渐渐变凉；但把一颗冰冷的苹果放进暖园，它只能从周围窃取热量才慢慢变温。两座花园若任其自然，便会缓缓趋向同一个不冷不热的温度——暖的渐凉，冷的渐温，直到彼此再无值得称道的分别。

The east garden was cold and damp, its soil heavy with dew, while the west garden was warm and dry, baked golden by the sun. The villagers understood the rule of the two gardens well: warmth never flowed uphill of its own accord. A hot apple placed in the cold garden would cool, but a cold apple placed in the warm garden would only grow warm by stealing heat from its surroundings. The two gardens, left to themselves, were drifting slowly toward the same lukewarm temperature, the warm one cooling and the cold one warming, until neither held any distinction worth speaking of.

paragraphs.en: Mara, however, was a patient and watchful sort. He took his stool beside the gate and began to observe the apples as they tumbled and bounced between the two gardens, carried by the wind and the feet of children. He noticed that some apples flew fast and fierce, humming with energy, while others crept along lazily, barely stirring. And he noticed something further: the fast, hot apples, the ones full of fire, were just as likely to wander into the cold garden as the slow, cold ones were to wander into the warm garden. The gate, you see, swung freely both ways and asked no questions of whoever passed.

paragraphs.cn: 于是 Mara 想出一个小巧的手艺。他下定决心：只为那些飞快炽热、奔向暖园的苹果开门，也只为那些迟缓冰凉、奔向冷园的苹果开门。当一颗火热的苹果朝冷园扑来，他便当面把门紧紧关上。当一颗慵懒的苹果朝暖园飘来，他也关上门，任它停留原地。就这样，时辰一寸寸过去，暖园愈发温暖，将所有最迅捷、最饱满的苹果都聚拢到自己怀里；冷园则愈发寒冷，收拢了所有昏沉羸弱的苹果。原本正滑向乏味同一的两座花园，此刻狠狠地彼此拉开，一座炽烈，一座霜寒。
paragraphs.en: So Mara devised a small craft. He resolved to open the gate only for the fast, hot apples heading toward the warm garden, and only for the slow, cold apples heading toward the cold garden. articles.content_cn:
在古城里有一座亭子，开着三扇门（three doors），其中两扇后面只有灰尘和蛛网，而一扇后面藏着一锭纯金的奖品。每到傍晚，会有一位旅人受邀挑选一扇门；同样每到傍晚，亭子的守护者（the keeper）——他确切知道金子藏在哪里——会打开旅人没有挑选的两扇门中的一扇，露出里面的灰尘。然后，守护者礼貌地鞠一躬，问旅人是否愿意保留最初的选择，还是换到另一扇仍然紧闭的门。

多数旅人都为自己的初次猜测感到骄傲，不肯挪动脚步。「门终归是门，」他们会说，「如今只剩两扇关着，必然是一半对一半。换门就等于承认自己错了，而承认错了便是冒犯命运。」于是一个又一个夜晚，他们坚守原地，大约三次中就有两次空手而归。几个倔强者甚至吹嘘说换门是意志薄弱的表现，命运只眷顾坚定之人。

后来来了一位老妇人（an old woman），她多年来一直观察着这座亭子，她懂得了旁人不曾懂的事。她想：当守护者打开一扇满是灰尘的门时，他并不是随手为之，因为他绝不能露出金子。所以他打开的那扇门并非一个独立的事件、随随便便的恩赐；而是一个经过思量的仁慈之举，是把一条信息白白递给任何一个肯用心接收的人。这份仁慈悄悄倾斜了旅人脚下的大地，尽管门本身一寸未动。

她对他们说：想想你们最初的猜测值多少吧。一开始，三扇门只有一锭金，你选的门只有三分之一的可能藏着金子；另外三分之二，金子在你没选的门后面。如今守护者受他自己的规矩约束，抹去了那两扇中的一扇，而另一排里仍然紧闭着的那扇，实质上成了全部第二份概率的继承者。所以换门并不是在「一半对一半」里再赌一次；而是承接了「你最初猜错了」的那三分之二机会。坚守的旅人攥着三分之一的希望；换门的旅人则带着三分之二。

等到她终于受邀上前时，老妇人指了指自己中意的第一扇门，平静地等守护者打开他那扇满是灰尘的门，然后毫不犹豫地走向剩下那扇紧闭的门。人群低声议论她鲁莽。然而她赢的次数远多于输的次数，渐渐地，年轻的旅人开始效仿她，直到「坚守」成了新手的标记，而「换门」成了智者的习惯。门没有变，金子也没有挪动；改变的只是旅人对「守护者打开的那扇门究竟意味着什么」的理解。

这个故事揭示了「蒙提霍尔问题」（the Monty Hall problem）的本质——一个表面看来像是在两扇同样可能的门之间做公平抉择的谜题，实则是一堂关于「新信息如何改变旧概率」的课。当你最初在三扇门中挑一扇时，你有三分之一的可能猜对，另有三分之二的可能奖品在另外两扇门后面。因为主持人知道奖品在哪里，而且必须从另一对门里打开一扇空门，所以他的揭示并非随机；他把那三分之二的概率全部汇集到你没有选的那扇仅剩的门上。因此换门大约三次能赢两次，而坚守只能赢一次。道理在于：主持人受约束的选择本身就是信息，依此行事，便能把「一半对一半」的天真直觉转化为经过度量的「二比一」优势。
articles.content_en:
In the old city there stood a pavilion with three doors, and behind two of them waited only dust and cobwebs, while behind one glittered a prize of pure gold. Each evening a traveler was invited to choose a door, and each evening the keeper of the pavilion, who knew precisely where the gold rested, would open one of the two doors the traveler had not chosen, revealing nothing but dust. Then, with a courteous bow, the keeper would ask the traveler whether he wished to keep his first choice or move to the other door that remained closed.

Most travelers, proud of their first guess, refused to budge. "A door is a door," they would say, "and there are two closed now, so surely it is half and half. To move is to admit I was wrong, and to admit I was wrong is to tempt the fates." And so, evening after evening, they stayed where they stood, and roughly two times out of three they went home empty-handed. A few stubborn ones even boasted that switching showed a weak spirit, and that fortune favored the resolute.

But there came an old woman who had watched the pavilion for many years, and she understood something the others did not. When the keeper opens a dusty door, she reasoned, he is not choosing at random, for he must never reveal the gold. So his opened door is not an independent event, lightly offered; it is a deliberate act of mercy, a piece of information handed freely to anyone wise enough to receive it. That mercy tilts the very ground the travelers stand on, though the doors themselves never move.

Consider, she told them, what your first guess was worth. In the beginning, with three doors and one prize, your chosen door held the gold only one time in three; two times in three, the gold was behind one of the doors you did not pick. Now the keeper, bound by his rule, has swept away one of those two, and what remains standing closed in that other row is, in effect, the heir to all that second probability. To switch, then, is not to gamble again at half and half; it is to inherit the two-thirds chance that your first guess was wrong. The traveler who stays clings to a one-third hope; the traveler who moves carries two-thirds.

When at last she was invited to choose, the old woman pointed to the first door she fancied, waited calmly for the keeper to open his dusty one, and then, without a flicker of doubt, walked to the remaining closed door. The crowd murmured that she was reckless. Yet she won far more often than she lost, and in time the younger travelers began to imitate her, until staying became the mark of the novice and switching the habit of the wise. The doors had not changed, nor had the gold moved; only the travelers' understanding of what the keeper's opened door truly meant.

This story reveals the essence of the Monty Hall problem — a puzzle that seems, on its face, to be a fair choice between two equally likely doors, but is in fact a lesson about how new information shifts old odds. When you first pick one of three doors, you have a one-third chance of being right and a two-thirds chance that the prize lies behind one of the other two. Because the host knows where the prize is and must always open an empty door from the other pair, his reveal is not random; it funnels all of that two-thirds probability onto the single remaining door you did not choose. Switching therefore wins about two times out of three, while staying wins only one time out of three. The lesson is that the host's constrained choice is information, and acting on it turns a naive fifty-fifty feeling into a measured two-to-one advantage.

paragraphs.cn: 这个故事揭示了「蒙提霍尔问题」（the Monty Hall problem）的本质——一个表面看来像是在两扇同样可能的门之间做公平抉择的谜题，实则是一堂关于「新信息如何改变旧概率」的课。当你最初在三扇门中挑一扇时，你有三分之一的可能猜对，另有三分之二的可能奖品在另外两扇门后面。因为主持人知道奖品在哪里，而且必须从另一对门里打开一扇空门，所以他的揭示并非随机；他把那三分之二的概率全部汇集到你没有选的那扇仅剩的门上。因此换门大约三次能赢两次，而坚守只能赢一次。道理在于：主持人受约束的选择本身就是信息，依此行事，便能把「一半对一半」的天真直觉转化为经过度量的「二比一」优势。
paragraphs.en: This story reveals the essence of the Monty Hall problem — a puzzle that seems, on its face, to be a fair choice between two equally likely doors, but is in fact a lesson about how new information shifts old odds. When you first pick one of three doors, you have a one-third chance of being right and a two-thirds chance that the prize lies behind one of the other two. Because the host knows where the prize is and must always open an empty door from the other pair, his reveal is not random; it funnels all of that two-thirds probability onto the single remaining door you did not choose. Switching therefore wins about two times out of three, while staying wins only one time out of three. The lesson is that the host's constrained choice is information, and acting on it turns a naive fifty-fifty feeling into a measured two-to-one advantage.

articles.title: 自由意志：拒绝相信它就会让你变成「坏」人吗？研究正在挑战这一旧观念
articles.author: Tom St Quinton
articles.summary: 你点击这篇文章，是出于你自己的自由意志吗？还是说，这早已由粒子在宇宙中的演化所预定，在大爆炸引发的一连串不间断的链式反应中展开？也许你认为，是随机的量子过程或无意识的大脑活动促成了这一切？无论你是否具有哲学倾向，自由意志这一话题，我们大多数人都在生命的某个阶段思索过。
articles.content_cn:
你点击这篇文章，是出于你自己的自由意志吗？还是说，这早已由粒子在宇宙中的演化所预定，在大爆炸引发的一连串不间断的链式反应中展开？也许你认为，是随机的量子过程或无意识的大脑活动促成了这一切？无论你是否具有哲学倾向，自由意志这一话题，我们大多数人都在生命的某个阶段思索过。

研究表明，人们倾向于相信自由意志，至少是以某种形式相信。也许更重要的一个问题是：这是否重要？这正是心理学与实验哲学领域的研究者近来试图回答的难题。如果人们放弃自由意志的观念，最终会发生什么？

这看起来像是一个危险的想法，可能引发混乱与抑郁。事实上，研究大体上也发现，当你诱导人们怀疑自由意志时，坏事就会随之而来——包括作弊和攻击性等行为的增加。这似乎意味着，即便自由意志并不存在（正如许多科学家和哲学家所假定的那样），我们最好也假装它存在。但我和其他人的较新研究表明，怀疑自由意志的存在，终究未必会带来如此糟糕的后果。

几个世纪以来，哲学家们一直在争论自由意志是什么、我们是否拥有它。各种立场差异极大，在此无法对这一主题做全面的铺陈。争论的一端是自由意志论者（libertarians），他们主张至少我们的部分选择与行动并非由因果所决定。另一端则是硬决定论者（hard determinists），他们论证每一种思想、行动或事件都是过去事件与自然法则的结果。

当人们谈论不相信自由意志时，决定论（determinism）通常是首先跃入脑海的立场。然而，决定论只是诸多否定自由意志观念的立场家族中的一种。一种较新近出现的立场被称为自由意志怀疑论（free will scepticism）。这一立场虽然拒绝人类拥有真正自由意志的观念（但不必然拒绝能动性），却只有部分怀疑论者因决定论而拒绝它，另一些则论证说，在一个非决定性或随机的宇宙中，自由意志是不可能的。

但无论你认同哪个阵营，你的信念究竟会带来怎样的实际后果？在考察近期实验的若干问题之前，让我们先来看看研究者最初是如何开始操纵信念的。

Insights 栏目致力于高品质的长篇新闻写作。我们的编辑与来自多种不同学术背景、正应对一系列社会与科学挑战的学者合作。

第一项以实验方式操纵自由意志信念的研究，由凯瑟琳·沃斯（Kathleen Vohs）与乔纳森·斯库勒（Jonathan Schooler）于 2008 年完成。这项如今已成为该领域开创性论文的研究，包含两个实验。在第一个实验中，研究者要求参与者阅读摘自弗朗西斯·克里克（Francis Crick）经典著作《惊人的假说》（The Astonishing Hypothesis）的文本。参与者被随机分配阅读反自由意志的版本或中性的版本。

在被操纵为不相信自由意志的那组中，文本声称自由意志是虚幻的，行为是由无意识的大脑活动所驱动的。例如，文本中包含这样的句子：「人之所以为人及其所做的一切，都是其大脑中简单物理过程的产物」，以及「尽管我们似乎拥有自由意志，但事实上，我们的选择早已被预先决定，我们无法改变这一点」。在对照组中，文本并未提及自由意志，而是讨论了关于意识的研究。

读完文本后，所有参与者都在电脑上完成一项心算任务。他们被告知，由于一个「程序故障」，本应由他们自行求解的任务答案将会显示出来。因此参与者被鼓励按下空格键，以确保答案保持隐藏。于是，参与者是否选择让答案保持隐藏，就被用作衡量作弊的指标。

研究者推测，阅读反自由意志文本的参与者会比对照组更少按下空格键。结果正是如此。为确认这些发现，他们进行了第二个实验，并对方法做了些许改动。这第二个实验本质上得出了同样的结论：被诱导不相信自由意志的参与者作弊更多。

这篇论文引发了一大批研究的涌现，旨在考察与自由意志信念相关的其他结果。罗伊·鲍迈斯特（Roy Baumeister）及其同事考察了自由意志信念与攻击性行为之间的关联。在经过自由意志信念的操纵之后，参与者完成一项烹饪任务，并被告知他们将为之备餐的那个人不喜欢辛辣食物。因此，参与者所投放的辣酱量便作为攻击性的衡量指标。与研究者预期一致，自由意志信念被削弱了的参与者涂抹了更多的辣酱。研究者由此得出结论：自由意志信念与攻击性相关。不过，他们考察的只是操纵人们怀疑自由意志所带来的直接后果，而未捕捉到他们为何使用更多辣酱的确切心理过程。

其他研究表明，被操纵怀疑自由意志的参与者表现出偏见、更少感恩、更少助人、疏离感增强，并在生活中体验到更少意义感。事实上，自主性、自我效能感、工作满意度、毅力、成就与生活满意度，都与更强的自由意志信念相关联。

这一研究项目的结论很明确：如果我们让人们不相信自由意志，负面结果就会随之而来。因此，即便我们相信自由意志是一种幻觉，作为一个社会也应当让人们免于接触这一信息。然而，这些操纵研究以及由此推导出的灾难性结论，存在一些问题。

一个重要问题涉及这些操纵所针对的信念。如前所述，反对自由意志的论证众多，每一论证都对应于不同的哲学立场。提供给参与者的文本通常声称事件不可避免、科学的本性以及意识的作用。

它们是若干哲学立场的混合体，各有其自身的衍生后果。操纵中常用的一种观点，是暗示人们的思想、欲望与意志是无效的——即大脑在我们有意识地决定做某事之前，就已经为行动做好了准备。所以当你在辛苦一天后伸手去拿那块巧克力时，那并非有意识选择的结果——无意识的大脑过程才是罪魁祸首。

但这并非思考自由意志缺失的唯一方式，也不是怀疑论者会赞同的观点。许多怀疑论者相信，思想与欲望确实会影响人们的行为，但重要的是，其下的认知过程（包括基因与过往经历）要么是被决定的，要么出于偶然。这意味着当你吃下那块巧克力时，你的欲望确实在起作用——你可以拥有能动性，却无需拥有那种配得上终极道德责任的、如上帝般完全的掌控。在这一视角下，自由意志更像是一个形而上学概念，而能动性则介入日常事件之中。

这是一个重要却细微的差异。告诉人们他们的思想对自己的行为毫无发言权，可能引发挫败感、幻灭与疏离。它甚至可能导向不道德行为。但这些后果很可能源自那些言过其实、戏剧化的论证——它们对能动性构成直接威胁，而非源自一种普遍的、怀疑论的取向。

假设这些操纵确实削弱了自由意志信念，但只是依据一种保留了某种能动性信念的怀疑论立场。它仍会带来戏剧性、令人憎恶的后果吗？回想一下那个数学任务的实验，其中作弊行为由是否按下按键的次数来表示。

从这个实验最多能得出的结论是：削弱自由意志信念能够影响在一个虚构心算任务中的作弊行为。该研究并未发现自由意志信念与其他更具社会相关性的欺骗形式——如欺诈、不忠、学术不端等——之间存在关联。要假设在实验室那种没有现实后果的受控实验中作弊的人，也会犯下其他形式的欺骗，未免牵强。

类似地，那项烹饪研究表明，关于自由意志的信念能够影响参与者在实验室情境下分配辣酱的多少。同样的操纵也有可能增加言语上的敌意或对抗，甚至攻击性或威胁性的行为。然而，这些结论仍纯属推测——我们其实并不知情。

为了便于论证，姑且假定它们在现实中的确会导致坏事。我们仍可质疑这些发现究竟有多大意义。研究者常谈论一个发现的「效应量」，它基本上告诉我们效应的大小或幅度。大的效应量表明一个发现具有实际意义，而小的效应则意味着实际应用有限。研究者显然追求前者。

要了解自由意志信念研究中的效应量，2022 年的一篇论文综述了对自由意志信念施加操纵的研究。它发现这些操纵只具有较小的效应量。更重要的是，它表明最强的效应出现在操纵刚完成之时，而非实验结束之时。这表明操纵效应不仅在实验之后会消退，还会在整个实验过程中逐渐减弱——我们并不会时刻思考自己是否拥有自由意志。不仅如此，该综述还发现，自由意志信念的变化并未对行为产生任何有意义的、持久的改变。

最后一个问题与可重复性有关，即在其他研究中对科学发现加以确认。一项发现能否被重复，是科学的主要原则之一。重复一项实验并稳定地得出相同结果，可以增强对初始发现的信心。而近来，一场可重复性危机已席卷心理学。

自由意志研究亦是如此。例如，一些研究者未能改变参与者的自由意志信念。另一些研究者尽管成功改变了自由意志信念，却发现难以重复其后果。例如，一项研究未能重复关于数学任务作弊的发现。这些困难质疑了原始发现的可信度，并对「不相信自由意志会带来负面后果」这一假设构成了严峻挑战。

我们已经看到若干理由，说明研究者得出「不相信自由意志会产生负面后果」这一结论可能为时过早。但我们也可以质疑，这些负面结果是否本就该出现，以及采纳怀疑论立场是否其实能带来社会裨益。

一种观点认为，关于自由意志的信念对人们如何思考与行为毫无影响。想想生活的意义感吧——研究据称已表明它会被不相信自由意志所削弱。设想一个人的意义感与其事业紧密相连。这个人怀有成为一名律师的志向，经过多年奉献，终于实现了她的梦想。她相信自己缺乏自由意志，会影响她的意义感以及她如何看待这一成功吗？

未必如此。早起、晚归、投入数小时学习的，仍然是她本人。得知自己并非终极掌控者，并不会让她对成就的自豪感烟消云散。她可能会感激自己的成长经历、所受的教育以及家人的支持。意义与感恩依然可以存在。人们把意义赋予各种事物——智力、运动才能与美貌——而这一切都与自由意志毫无关系。

不仅如此，我开展过一项专门考察生活意义感的研究，对象是持有一系列不同自由意志观点的人群。一组阅读了一段驳斥自由意志的文本（传统的自由意志不信操纵）；另一组阅读中性文本（对照组）。我还有第三组，他们不接受操纵，而是通过自我认同为自由意志怀疑论者来筛选。

所有参与者都报告了自己生活有多大意义。正如预期，被操纵为不相信自由意志的人比对照组显示出更低的意义感，这支持了以往的研究。但至关重要的是，怀疑论组与对照组具有相同的意义感与目标感。

这表明，如前所述，那些声称令人们怀疑自由意志的操纵，并非依怀疑论的视角行事。更重要的是，这意味着持怀疑论观点的人，其生活意义感并不受其哲学立场的影响。

进一步支持这一点的是，2024 年的一篇论文专门考察了自由意志怀疑论者的观点，发现 41%（共 164 人）声称他们的不信对其生活毫无影响。而最常被报告的后果其实是正面的，包括对他人更具同情、更少控制、更为放松。

这是否意味着，怀疑论的立场其实能带来社会裨益？关于自由意志信念最受争议的后果之一，涉及道德与责任。在现行法律体系中，报应性惩罚的前提假设是：罪犯对其行为负有道德责任，并且是出于自身自由意志而行事的。支持这一观点的研究发现，自由意志信念更强的参与者对犯错者确实更少同理心，并判处更严厉的刑罚。然而，如果自由意志并不存在，那么基于一个人并不负有责任的行为而惩罚他，便显得过分严苛。

格雷格·卡鲁索（Gregg Caruso）与德克·佩雷鲍姆（Derk Pereboom）是著名的自由意志怀疑论者，他们质疑惩罚性决定的道德性。他们建议，与其因为人们在道德上对其行为负有责任而加以惩罚，不如采纳与怀疑论信念相符的、更具同理心的非惩罚性途径。例如，他们的隔离模型旨在将违法者加以隔离并提供康复，直到他们不再对社会构成风险——无论其责任程度如何。如此看来，不相信自由意志有可能彻底改造一套与「自由意志并不存在」这一观点相悖的法律体系。

抱持人们能够自由决定自身处境的信念，也可能导致其他有害后果，如社会不公、非正义、缺乏同理心、仇恨与指责受害者。例如，对自由意志的信念可能助长一种观念：穷人在某种程度上是罪有应得，他们正生活在自己一手造成的处境之中。如果放弃自由意志这一观念，这些认知就能发生改变。既然人们并不对其自身处境负有道德责任，那么就能对那些处境不利者展现更多的同情与同理心。所以，拒绝相信自由意志的确可能带来正面的结果。

研究者曾声称，让人们不相信自由意志会带来戏剧性的负面后果。不相信自由意志的确可能导致坏事；然而，由于种种方法论上的问题，现在下此结论为时过早。事实上，最终可能证明，不相信自由意志其实是一件好事。
articles.content_en:
Did you click on this article out of your own free will? Or was it predetermined by the cosmic evolution of particles, unfolding in an unbroken chain reaction set in motion by the big bang? Perhaps you think random quantum processes or unconscious brain activity were responsible? Whether you are philosophically inclined or not, the topic of free will is something most of us have pondered at some stage.

Research has shown that people tend to believe in free will, at least in some form. A more important question, perhaps, is whether it matters. This is the exact conundrum that researchers in psychology and experimental philosophy have been trying to answer recently. What would ultimately happen if people gave up on the idea of free will?

It may seem like a dangerous idea; something that could result in chaos and depression. And indeed, research has largely found that when you manipulate people to doubt free will, bad things happen – including an increase in behaviour such as cheating and aggression. This suggests that even if free will doesn’t exist, as many scientists and philosophers assume, it might be better for us to pretend that it does. But newer research by me and others suggests that doubting the existence of free will may not have such bad consequences, after all.

Philosophers have argued for centuries about what free will is and whether we have it. Positions vary widely, and it is impossible to give the subject full coverage here. At one end of the debate are libertarians, who contend that at least some of our choices and actions are not causally determined. At the other end are hard determinists who argue that every thought, action or event is a result of past events and the laws of nature.

When people talk about a disbelief in free will, determinism is usually the position that springs to mind. Yet, determinism is one of many positions within a family of views that dismiss the notion of free will. A position that has emerged more recently is called free will scepticism. While this position rejects the idea that humans possess genuine free will (but not necessarily agency), only some sceptics reject it because of determinism, while others argue that free will is impossible in an indeterministic or random universe.

But whichever tribe you identify with, what are the actual consequences of your beliefs? Before looking at some of the issues with recent experiments, let’s first explore how researchers began manipulating beliefs in the first place.

The Insights section is committed to high-quality longform journalism. Our editors work with academics from many different backgrounds who are tackling a wide range of societal and scientific challenges.

The first piece of research to experimentally manipulate free will beliefs was conducted by Kathleen Vohs and Jonathan Schooler in 2008. This work, which is now a seminal paper in the area, comprised two experiments. In the first experiment, the researchers asked participants to read text taken from Francis Crick’s classical book The Astonishing Hypothesis. Participants were allocated to read either an anti-free will version or a neutral one.

In the group that was manipulated to not believe in free will, the text stated that free will was illusionary and behaviour was driven by unconscious brain activity. For example, the text included sentences such as “everything people are and do is the product of simple, physical processes in their brains” and “although we appear to have free will, in fact, our choices have already been predetermined for us and we cannot change that.” In the control condition, the text did not mention free will and instead discussed research on consciousness.

After reading the text, all participants completed a mental-arithmetic task on a computer. They were told that a “programming glitch” meant that the solutions/answers to the task that they were meant to solve themselves would be visible. Participants were therefore encouraged to press the spacebar, which would ensure the solutions remained hidden. Therefore, whether or not participants decided to keep the answers hidden was used to indicate cheating.

The researchers speculated that those reading the anti-free will text would press the spacebar less so than the control condition. And this is what they found. To confirm these findings, they ran a second experiment with some slight methodological changes. This second experiment essentially found the same thing: participants made to disbelieve in free will cheat more.

This paper led to a proliferation of studies seeking to examine other outcomes associated with free will beliefs. Roy Baumeister and colleagues investigated the link between the belief in free will and aggressive behaviour. After a free will belief manipulation, participants completed a cooking task and were told that the individual they were preparing food for disliked spicy food. Therefore, the amount of hot sauce administered by the participant served as the measure of aggression. Consistent with the researchers’ prediction, participants whose belief in free will had been weakened slathered on more hot sauce. The researchers therefore concluded that belief in free will is related to aggression. That said, they only looked at the direct consequences of manipulating people doubt free will rather than capturing the exact thought process of why they used more hot sauce.

Other studies showed that participants manipulated to doubt free will were prejudiced, less grateful, less helpful, alienated and experienced less meaning in life. In fact, autonomy, self-efficacy, job satisfaction, perseverance, achievement and life satisfaction were all linked to a stronger belief in free will.

The consequences of this programme of work were clear: if we make people disbelieve in free will, negative outcomes will follow. Consequently, even if we believe free will is an illusion, people should be shielded from this information as a society. However, there are some issues with these manipulation studies and the catastrophic conclusions derived from this line of research.

An important issue concerns the beliefs that these manipulations are targeting. As mentioned earlier, many arguments against free will exist, and each argument aligns itself to a different philosophical position. The texts given to participants typically make claims related to the inevitability of events, the nature of science and the role of consciousness.

They are an amalgamation of philosophical positions that have their own ramifications. One idea that is commonly used in manipulations is the suggestion that people’s thoughts, desires, and wills are ineffectual – that the brain prepares for action before we consciously decide to do something. So when you reach for that chocolate bar at the end of a hard day, it’s not a result of conscious choice – unconscious brain processes are entirely to blame.

But this is not the only way think about a lack of free will; and it’s not something a sceptic would endorse. Many sceptics believe that thoughts and desires do influence how people behave but, importantly, the cognitive processes that underlie them (including genetics and past experiences) are either determined or due to chance. This suggests your desire was at play when you ate that chocolate bar – you can have agency without having full, God-like control deserving of ultimate moral responsibility. In this view, free will is more of a metaphysical concept whereas agency is involved in day-to-day events.

This is an important but subtle difference. Telling people that their thoughts have no say in what they do might lead to feelings of demotivation, disillusionment and alienation. It may even lead them to immoral behaviour. But these consequences are likely a result of far-fetching, dramatised arguments that pose direct threats to agency, and not a general, sceptic approach.

Suppose the manipulations do weaken belief in free will, but only according to a sceptical position that maintains some belief in agency. Will it still lead to dramatic, abhorrent outcomes? Recall that the experiments with the mathematical task, with cheating behaviour represented by the number of keypresses that did or did not occur.

The most that can be concluded from this experiment is that weakening belief in free will can influence cheating in a fictitious mental arithmetic task. The study did not find a relationship between belief in free will and other, more socially relevant, ways of deceptiveness, such as fraud, infidelity, academic dishonesty and so forth. To assume people cheating in a controlled laboratory experiment, which has no real-life consequences, would also commit these other forms of cheating appears far-fetched.

Similarly, the cooking study showed that beliefs about free will can affect how much hot sauce participants allocate in a laboratory setting. It is possible that the same manipulation could also increase verbal hostility or confrontation, and perhaps even aggression or threatening conduct. However, these conclusions remain completely speculative – we just don’t know.

For argument’s sake, let’s assume that they do lead to bad things in real life. We may still question just how meaningful the findings are. Researchers talk a lot about the “effect size” of a finding, which basically tells us the magnitude or size of the effect. A large effect size indicates a finding has practical significance, whereas a small effect indicates limited practical application. Researchers obviously strive for the former.

To get a sense of the effect size in free will belief research, a 2022 paper reviewed studies administering manipulations to free will beliefs. It found that these manipulations only had a small effect size. What’s more, it showed that the strongest effects happened directly after the manipulation instead of at the end of the experiment. This indicates that manipulation effects may not only fade after the experiment, but wane over the course of the experimental session – we don’t think about whether we have free will constantly. Not only that, but the review found that changes in free will beliefs did not have any meaningful, lasting change in behaviours.

A final issue has to do with replication, the confirmation of scientific findings in other studies. Whether a finding is replicated is one of the major principles in science. Repeating an experiment and consistently finding the same thing can increase confidence about an initial finding. And a replication crisis has recently engulfed psychology.

This is also the case for free will research. For example, some researchers have failed to change participants’ belief in free will. Others, despite successfully changing free will beliefs, have found difficulty replicating the consequences. For example, one study could not replicate the findings regarding cheating on the mathematical task. These difficulties question the credibility of the original findings and pose serious challenges to the assumption that negative consequences come about from a disbelief in free will.

We have seen different reasons why it may be premature for researchers to conclude that disbelieving in free will has negative consequences. But we may also question whether these negative outcomes are to be expected anyway, and whether adopting a sceptical position can actually have societal benefits.

One view is that beliefs about free will make no difference to how people think and behave. Think about meaning in life, something which research has supposedly showed to be weakened by a disbelief free will. Imagine that a person’s meaning is strongly attached to their career. This person harbours the ambition to become a lawyer and after years of dedication, finally achieves her dream. Would the belief that she lacked free will affect her meaning and how she perceived this success?

Not necessarily so. She was still the one that got up early, arrived home late and dedicated hours to studying. The pride in her accomplishment does not evaporate in the knowledge that she was not the ultimate controller. She may be thankful for her upbringing, the education she received and her family support. There can still be meaning and gratitude. People ascribe meaning to all sort so things – intelligence, athleticism and beauty – none of which have got anything to do with free will.

What’s more, I conducted a study that specifically looked at meaning in life across people holding a range of views about free will. One group read a text passage denouncing free will (a traditional free will disbelief manipulation); and a second read neutral text (a control condition). I also had a third group which did not receive a manipulation but was selected by identifying as free-will sceptics.

All participants reported on how meaningful their life was. As would be expected, those manipulated to disbelieve in free will showed lower meaning than the control, supporting previous studies. But crucially, the sceptic group had the same sense of meaning and purpose as the control.

This indicates that, as suggested earlier, the manipulations claiming to make people doubt free will are not doing so in accordance with a sceptical perspective. More importantly, this suggests that the meaning in life of people taking sceptic views is unaffected by their philosophical position.

Further supporting this, a 2024 paper examined the views of free will sceptics exclusively and found that 41% (out of 164) claimed that their disbelief had no effect on their life at all. And the most reported consequences were indeed positive, including having compassion for others, being less controlling and more relaxed.

Does this mean a sceptical position could in fact provide societal benefits? One of the most debated consequences of free will beliefs concerns morality and responsibility. In the current legal system, retributive punishment is predicated on the assumption that the criminal was morally responsible for their action and acted out of their own free will. Supporting this view, research has found that participants with a stronger belief in free will are actually less empathic towards wrongdoers, and hand out harsher sentences. Yet, if free will does not exist, it would seem unduly harsh to punish an individual based on an act they were not responsible for.

Gregg Caruso and Derk Pereboom are prominent free will sceptics who question the morality of punitive decisions. They suggest that instead of punishing people because they are morally responsible for their actions, more empathetic, non-punitive approaches can be adopted in line with sceptical beliefs. For example, their quarantine model seeks to isolate offenders and provide rehabilitation until they no longer pose a risk to society – regardless of their level of responsibility. Seen in this way, a disbelief in free will could potentially overhaul a legal system that’s at odds with the view that free will does not exist.

Holding the belief that people can freely determine their circumstances may also lead to other harmful outcomes, such as social inequalities, injustice, a lack of empathy, hatred and victim blaming. For example, a belief in free will can promote the idea that poor people are somehow deserving of their abhorrent conditions and are living in situations of their own making. These perceptions can change if the notion of free will is relinquished. Because people are not morally responsible for their own situations, a greater deal of compassion and empathy could be shown towards those underprivileged. So there could indeed be positive outcomes of declining to believe in free will.

Researchers have claimed that making people disbelieve in free will can have dramatic negative consequences. A disbelief in free will may indeed lead to bad things; however, due to various methodological issues, it is premature to make this conclusion. In fact, it could turn out that disbelieving in free will is actually a good thing.

paragraphs.cn: 你点击这篇文章，是出于你自己的自由意志吗？还是说，这早已由粒子在宇宙中的演化所预定，在大爆炸引发的一连串不间断的链式反应中展开？也许你认为，是随机的量子过程或无意识的大脑活动促成了这一切？无论你是否具有哲学倾向，自由意志这一话题，我们大多数人都在生命的某个阶段思索过。
paragraphs.en: Did you click on this article out of your own free will? Or was it predetermined by the cosmic evolution of particles, unfolding in an unbroken chain reaction set in motion by the big bang? Perhaps you think random quantum processes or unconscious brain activity were responsible? Whether you are philosophically inclined or not, the topic of free will is something most of us have pondered at some stage.

paragraphs.cn: 研究表明，人们倾向于相信自由意志，至少是以某种形式相信。也许更重要的一个问题是：这是否重要？这正是心理学与实验哲学领域的研究者近来试图回答的难题。如果人们放弃自由意志的观念，最终会发生什么？
paragraphs.en: Research has shown that people tend to believe in free will, at least in some form. A more important question, perhaps, is whether it matters. This is the exact conundrum that researchers in psychology and experimental philosophy have been trying to answer recently. What would ultimately happen if people gave up on the idea of free will?

paragraphs.cn: 这看起来像是一个危险的想法，可能引发混乱与抑郁。事实上，研究大体上也发现，当你诱导人们怀疑自由意志时，坏事就会随之而来——包括作弊和攻击性等行为的增加。这似乎意味着，即便自由意志并不存在（正如许多科学家和哲学家所假定的那样），我们最好也假装它存在。但我和其他人的较新研究表明，怀疑自由意志的存在，终究未必会带来如此糟糕的后果。
paragraphs.en: It may seem like a dangerous idea; something that could result in chaos and depression. And indeed, research has largely found that when you manipulate people to doubt free will, bad things happen – including an increase in behaviour such as cheating and aggression. This suggests that even if free will doesn’t exist, as many scientists and philosophers assume, it might be better for us to pretend that it does. But newer research by me and others suggests that doubting the existence of free will may not have such bad consequences, after all.

paragraphs.cn: 几个世纪以来，哲学家们一直在争论自由意志是什么、我们是否拥有它。各种立场差异极大，在此无法对这一主题做全面的铺陈。争论的一端是自由意志论者（libertarians），他们主张至少我们的部分选择与行动并非由因果所决定。另一端则是硬决定论者（hard determinists），他们论证每一种思想、行动或事件都是过去事件与自然法则的结果。
paragraphs.en: Philosophers have argued for centuries about what free will is and whether we have it. Positions vary widely, and it is impossible to give the subject full coverage here. At one end of the debate are libertarians, who contend that at least some of our choices and actions are not causally determined. At the other end are hard determinists who argue that every thought, action or event is a result of past events and the laws of nature.

paragraphs.cn: 当人们谈论不相信自由意志时，决定论（determinism）通常是首先跃入脑海的立场。然而，决定论只是诸多否定自由意志观念的立场家族中的一种。一种较新近出现的立场被称为自由意志怀疑论（free will scepticism）。这一立场虽然拒绝人类拥有真正自由意志的观念（但不必然拒绝能动性），却只有部分怀疑论者因决定论而拒绝它，另一些则论证说，在一个非决定性或随机的宇宙中，自由意志是不可能的。
paragraphs.en: When people talk about a disbelief in free will, determinism is usually the position that springs to mind. Yet, determinism is one of many positions within a family of views that dismiss the notion of free will. A position that has emerged more recently is called free will scepticism. While this position rejects the idea that humans possess genuine free will (but not necessarily agency), only some sceptics reject it because of determinism, while others argue that free will is impossible in an indeterministic or random universe.

paragraphs.cn: 但无论你认同哪个阵营，你的信念究竟会带来怎样的实际后果？在考察近期实验的若干问题之前，让我们先来看看研究者最初是如何开始操纵信念的。
paragraphs.en: But whichever tribe you identify with, what are the actual consequences of your beliefs? Before looking at some of the issues with recent experiments, let’s first explore how researchers began manipulating beliefs in the first place.

paragraphs.cn: Insights 栏目致力于高品质的长篇新闻写作。我们的编辑与来自多种不同学术背景、正应对一系列社会与科学挑战的学者合作。
paragraphs.en: The Insights section is committed to high-quality longform journalism. Our editors work with academics from many different backgrounds who are tackling a wide range of societal and scientific challenges.

paragraphs.cn: 第一项以实验方式操纵自由意志信念的研究，由凯瑟琳·沃斯（Kathleen Vohs）与乔纳森·斯库勒（Jonathan Schooler）于 2008 年完成。这项如今已成为该领域开创性论文的研究，包含两个实验。在第一个实验中，研究者要求参与者阅读摘自弗朗西斯·克里克（Francis Crick）经典著作《惊人的假说》（The Astonishing Hypothesis）的文本。参与者被随机分配阅读反自由意志的版本或中性的版本。
paragraphs.en: The first piece of research to experimentally manipulate free will beliefs was conducted by Kathleen Vohs and Jonathan Schooler in 2008. This work, which is now a seminal paper in the area, comprised two experiments. In the first experiment, the researchers asked participants to read text taken from Francis Crick’s classical book The Astonishing Hypothesis. Participants were allocated to read either an anti-free will version or a neutral one.

paragraphs.cn: 在被操纵为不相信自由意志的那组中，文本声称自由意志是虚幻的，行为是由无意识的大脑活动所驱动的。例如，文本中包含这样的句子：「人之所以为人及其所做的一切，都是其大脑中简单物理过程的产物」，以及「尽管我们似乎拥有自由意志，但事实上，我们的选择早已被预先决定，我们无法改变这一点」。在对照组中，文本并未提及自由意志，而是讨论了关于意识的研究。
paragraphs.en: In the group that was manipulated to not believe in free will, the text stated that free will was illusionary and behaviour was driven by unconscious brain activity. For example, the text included sentences such as “everything people are and do is the product of simple, physical processes in their brains” and “although we appear to have free will, in fact, our choices have already been predetermined for us and we cannot change that.” In the control condition, the text did not mention free will and instead discussed research on consciousness.

paragraphs.cn: 读完文本后，所有参与者都在电脑上完成一项心算任务。他们被告知，由于一个「程序故障」，本应由他们自行求解的任务答案将会显示出来。因此参与者被鼓励按下空格键，以确保答案保持隐藏。于是，参与者是否选择让答案保持隐藏，就被用作衡量作弊的指标。
paragraphs.en: After reading the text, all participants completed a mental-arithmetic task on a computer. They were told that a “programming glitch” meant that the solutions/answers to the task that they were meant to solve themselves would be visible. Participants were therefore encouraged to press the spacebar, which would ensure the solutions remained hidden. Therefore, whether or not participants decided to keep the answers hidden was used to indicate cheating.

paragraphs.cn: 研究者推测，阅读反自由意志文本的参与者会比对照组更少按下空格键。结果正是如此。为确认这些发现，他们进行了第二个实验，并对方法做了些许改动。这第二个实验本质上得出了同样的结论：被诱导不相信自由意志的参与者作弊更多。
paragraphs.en: The researchers speculated that those reading the anti-free will text would press the spacebar less so than the control condition. And this is what they found. To confirm these findings, they ran a second experiment with some slight methodological changes. This second experiment essentially found the same thing: participants made to disbelieve in free will cheat more.

paragraphs.cn: 这篇论文引发了一大批研究的涌现，旨在考察与自由意志信念相关的其他结果。罗伊·鲍迈斯特（Roy Baumeister）及其同事考察了自由意志信念与攻击性行为之间的关联。在经过自由意志信念的操纵之后，参与者完成一项烹饪任务，并被告知他们将为之备餐的那个人不喜欢辛辣食物。因此，参与者所投放的辣酱量便作为攻击性的衡量指标。与研究者预期一致，自由意志信念被削弱了的参与者涂抹了更多的辣酱。研究者由此得出结论：自由意志信念与攻击性相关。不过，他们考察的只是操纵人们怀疑自由意志所带来的直接后果，而未捕捉到他们为何使用更多辣酱的确切心理过程。
paragraphs.en: This paper led to a proliferation of studies seeking to examine other outcomes associated with free will beliefs. Roy Baumeister and colleagues investigated the link between the belief in free will and aggressive behaviour. After a free will belief manipulation, participants completed a cooking task and were told that the individual they were preparing food for disliked spicy food. Therefore, the amount of hot sauce administered by the participant served as the measure of aggression. Consistent with the researchers’ prediction, participants whose belief in free will had been weakened slathered on more hot sauce. The researchers therefore concluded that belief in free will is related to aggression. That said, they only looked at the direct consequences of manipulating people doubt free will rather than capturing the exact thought process of why they used more hot sauce.

paragraphs.cn: 其他研究表明，被操纵怀疑自由意志的参与者表现出偏见、更少感恩、更少助人、疏离感增强，并在生活中体验到更少意义感。事实上，自主性、自我效能感、工作满意度、毅力、成就与生活满意度，都与更强的自由意志信念相关联。
paragraphs.en: Other studies showed that participants manipulated to doubt free will were prejudiced, less grateful, less helpful, alienated and experienced less meaning in life. In fact, autonomy, self-efficacy, job satisfaction, perseverance, achievement and life satisfaction were all linked to a stronger belief in free will.

Researchers talk a lot about the “effect size” of a finding, which basically tells us the magnitude or size of the effect. A large effect size indicates a finding has practical significance, whereas a small effect indicates limited practical application. Researchers obviously strive for the former.

paragraphs.cn: 要了解自由意志信念研究中的效应量，2022 年的一篇论文综述了对自由意志信念施加操纵的研究。它发现这些操纵只具有较小的效应量。更重要的是，它表明最强的效应出现在操纵刚完成之时，而非实验结束之时。这表明操纵效应不仅在实验之后会消退，还会在整个实验过程中逐渐减弱——我们并不会时刻思考自己是否拥有自由意志。不仅如此，该综述还发现，自由意志信念的变化并未对行为产生任何有意义的、持久的改变。
paragraphs.en: To get a sense of the effect size in free will belief research, a 2022 paper reviewed studies administering manipulations to free will beliefs. It found that these manipulations only had a small effect size. What’s more, it showed that the strongest effects happened directly after the manipulation instead of at the end of the experiment. This indicates that manipulation effects may not only fade after the experiment, but wane over the course of the experimental session – we don’t think about whether we have free will constantly. Not only that, but the review found that changes in free will beliefs did not have any meaningful, lasting change in behaviours.

paragraphs.cn: 最后一个问题与可重复性有关，即在其他研究中对科学发现加以确认。一项发现能否被重复，是科学的主要原则之一。重复一项实验并稳定地得出相同结果，可以增强对初始发现的信心。而近来，一场可重复性危机已席卷心理学。
paragraphs.en: A final issue has to do with replication, the confirmation of scientific findings in other studies. Whether a finding is replicated is one of the major principles in science. Repeating an experiment and consistently finding the same thing can increase confidence about an initial finding. And a replication crisis has recently engulfed psychology.

paragraphs.cn: 自由意志研究亦是如此。例如，一些研究者未能改变参与者的自由意志信念。另一些研究者尽管成功改变了自由意志信念，却发现难以重复其后果。例如，一项研究未能重复关于数学任务作弊的发现。这些困难质疑了原始发现的可信度，并对「不相信自由意志会带来负面后果」这一假设构成了严峻挑战。
paragraphs.en: This is also the case for free will research. For example, some researchers have failed to change participants’ belief in free will. Others, despite successfully changing free will beliefs, have found difficulty replicating the consequences. For example, one study could not replicate the findings regarding cheating on the mathematical task. These difficulties question the credibility of the original findings and pose serious challenges to the assumption that negative consequences come about from a disbelief in free will.

paragraphs.cn: 我们已经看到若干理由，说明研究者得出「不相信自由意志会产生负面后果」这一结论可能为时过早。但我们也可以质疑，这些负面结果是否本就该出现，以及采纳怀疑论立场是否其实能带来社会裨益。
paragraphs.en: We have seen different reasons why it may be premature for researchers to conclude that disbelieving in free will has negative consequences. But we may also question whether these negative outcomes are to be expected anyway, and whether adopting a sceptical position can actually have societal benefits.

paragraphs.cn: 一种观点认为，关于自由意志的信念对人们如何思考与行为毫无影响。想想生活的意义感吧——研究据称已表明它会被不相信自由意志所削弱。设想一个人的意义感与其事业紧密相连。这个人怀有成为一名律师的志向，经过多年奉献，终于实现了她的梦想。她相信自己缺乏自由意志，会影响她的意义感以及她如何看待这一成功吗？
paragraphs.en: One view is that beliefs about free will make no difference to how people think and behave. Think about meaning in life, something which research has supposedly showed to be weakened by a disbelief free will. Imagine that a person’s meaning is strongly attached to their career. This person harbours the ambition to become a lawyer and after years of dedication, finally achieves her dream. Would the belief that she lacked free will affect her meaning and how she perceived this success?

paragraphs.cn: 未必如此。早起、晚归、投入数小时学习的，仍然是她本人。得知自己并非终极掌控者，并不会让她对成就的自豪感烟消云散。她可能会感激自己的成长经历、所受的教育以及家人的支持。意义与感恩依然可以存在。人们把意义赋予各种事物——智力、运动才能与美貌——而这一切都与自由意志毫无关系。
paragraphs.en: Not necessarily so. She was still the one that got up early, arrived home late and dedicated hours to studying. The pride in her accomplishment does not evaporate in the knowledge that she was not the ultimate controller. She may be thankful for her upbringing, the education she received and her family support. There can still be meaning and gratitude. People ascribe meaning to all sort so things – intelligence, athleticism and beauty – none of which have got anything to do with free will.

paragraphs.cn: 不仅如此，我开展过一项专门考察生活意义感的研究，对象是持有一系列不同自由意志观点的人群。一组阅读了一段驳斥自由意志的文本（传统的自由意志不信操纵）；另一组阅读中性文本（对照组）。我还有第三组，他们不接受操纵，而是通过自我认同为自由意志怀疑论者来筛选。
paragraphs.en: What’s more, I conducted a study that specifically looked at meaning in life across people holding a range of views about free will. One group read a text passage denouncing free will (a traditional free will disbelief manipulation); and a second read neutral text (a control condition). I also had a third group which did not receive a manipulation but was selected by identifying as free-will sceptics.

paragraphs.cn: 所有参与者都报告了自己生活有多大意义。正如预期，被操纵为不相信自由意志的人比对照组显示出更低的意义感，这支持了以往的研究。但至关重要的是，怀疑论组与对照组具有相同的意义感与目标感。
paragraphs.en: All participants reported on how meaningful their life was. As would be expected, those manipulated to disbelieve in free will showed lower meaning than the control, supporting previous studies. But crucially, the sceptic group had the same sense of meaning and purpose as the control.

paragraphs.cn: 这表明，如前所述，那些声称令人们怀疑自由意志的操纵，并非依怀疑论的视角行事。更重要的是，这意味着持怀疑论观点的人，其生活意义感并不受其哲学立场的影响。
paragraphs.en: This indicates that, as suggested earlier, the manipulations claiming to make people doubt free will are not doing so in accordance with a sceptical perspective. More importantly, this suggests that the meaning in life of people taking sceptic views is unaffected by their philosophical position.

paragraphs.cn: 进一步支持这一点的是，2024 年的一篇论文专门考察了自由意志怀疑论者的观点，发现 41%（共 164 人）声称他们的不信对其生活毫无影响。而最常被报告的后果其实是正面的，包括对他人更具同情、更少控制、更为放松。
paragraphs.en: Further supporting this, a 2024 paper examined the views of free will sceptics exclusively and found that 41% (out of 164) claimed that their disbelief had no effect on their life at all. And the most reported consequences were indeed positive, including having compassion for others, being less controlling and more relaxed.

paragraphs.cn: 这是否意味着，怀疑论的立场其实能带来社会裨益？关于自由意志信念最受争议的后果之一，涉及道德与责任。在现行法律体系中，报应性惩罚的前提假设是：罪犯对其行为负有道德责任，并且是出于自身自由意志而行事的。支持这一观点的研究发现，自由意志信念更强的参与者对犯错者确实更少同理心，并判处更严厉的刑罚。然而，如果自由意志并不存在，那么基于一个人并不负有责任的行为而惩罚他，便显得过分严苛。
paragraphs.en: Does this mean a sceptical position could in fact provide societal benefits? One of the most debated consequences of free will beliefs concerns morality and responsibility. In the current legal system, retributive punishment is predicated on the assumption that the criminal was morally responsible for their action and acted out of their own free will. Supporting this view, research has found that participants with a stronger belief in free will are actually less empathic towards wrongdoers, and hand out harsher sentences. Yet, if free will does not exist, it would seem unduly harsh to punish an individual based on an act they were not responsible for.

paragraphs.cn: 格雷格·卡鲁索（Gregg Caruso）与德克·佩雷鲍姆（Derk Pereboom）是著名的自由意志怀疑论者，他们质疑惩罚性决定的道德性。他们建议，与其因为人们在道德上对其行为负有责任而加以惩罚，不如采纳与怀疑论信念相符的、更具同理心的非惩罚性途径。例如，他们的隔离模型旨在将违法者加以隔离并提供康复，直到他们不再对社会构成风险——无论其责任程度如何。如此看来，不相信自由意志有可能彻底改造一套与「自由意志并不存在」这一观点相悖的法律体系。
paragraphs.en: Gregg Caruso and Derk Pereboom are prominent free will sceptics who question the morality of punitive decisions. They suggest that instead of punishing people because they are morally responsible for their actions, more empathetic, non-punitive approaches can be adopted in line with sceptical beliefs. For example, their quarantine model seeks to isolate offenders and provide rehabilitation until they no longer pose a risk to society – regardless of their level of responsibility. Seen in this way, a disbelief in free will could potentially overhaul a legal system that’s at odds with the view that free will does not exist.

paragraphs.cn: 抱持人们能够自由决定自身处境的信念，也可能导致其他有害后果，如社会不公、非正义、缺乏同理心、仇恨与指责受害者。例如，对自由意志的信念可能助长一种观念：穷人在某种程度上是罪有应得，他们正生活在自己一手造成的处境之中。如果放弃自由意志这一观念，这些认知就能发生改变。既然人们并不对其自身处境负有道德责任，那么就能对那些处境不利者展现更多的同情与同理心。所以，拒绝相信自由意志的确可能带来正面的结果。
paragraphs.en: Holding the belief that people can freely determine their circumstances may also lead to other harmful outcomes, such as social inequalities, injustice, a lack of empathy, hatred and victim blaming. For example, a belief in free will can promote the idea that poor people are somehow deserving of their abhorrent conditions and are living in situations of their own making. These perceptions can change if the notion of free will is relinquished. Because people are not morally responsible for their own situations, a greater deal of compassion and empathy could be shown towards those underprivileged. So there could indeed be positive outcomes of declining to believe in free will.

paragraphs.cn: 研究者曾声称，让人们不相信自由意志会带来戏剧性的负面后果。不相信自由意志的确可能导致坏事；然而，由于种种方法论上的问题，现在下此结论为时过早。事实上，最终可能证明，不相信自由意志其实是一件好事。
paragraphs.en: Researchers have claimed that making people disbelieve in free will can have dramatic negative consequences. A disbelief in free will may indeed lead to bad things; however, due to various methodological issues, it is premature to make this conclusion. In fact, it could turn out that disbelieving in free will is actually a good thing.

articles.title: 寂静谷的制图师
articles.author: AI Parable (inspired by Amanda Askell)

articles.content_cn:
在群山最深的一道褶皱里，有一座山谷，旧地图上只标了一个词——「寂静」（Silence）。靠近山谷边缘的旅人都有同一种奇怪的感受：下得越深，回头就越难，而身后的世界也愈发安静，仿佛空气本身正在变稠，变成一种比空气更致密的东西。制图师玛拉（Mara）一生都在绘制已知山脉的每一道隘口与凹地，她决心成为第一个画出山谷腹地并活着回来的人。

她一路用石堆标记自己的路线，每隔百步丢下一块石头，起初路很好走。她仍能回望斜坡，看见晨光照在山峰上。但在某一处石头前——她后来称之为「第十二号石堆」，虽然她永远无法确定数目是否准确——有什么东西改变了。她放下石头，转身去看上一个标记，却发现身后的坡道不再向上攀爬。它在弯曲。本应向上的小路轻轻折回了自身，而她自己的脚印，非但没有上升，反而描出一道缓缓向下的螺旋。

玛拉不是个容易害怕的人，于是她干脆转过身，开始往上爬。她走了一个钟头，又两个钟头，每一步都奋力向上，可山谷的边缘却从未因此更近一寸。早晨还看得见的群峰已沉入大地的曲线之下，头顶的天空也收窄成一圈昏暗的圆。她想起自己的石堆，想循着它们原路返回，可身后的石头并不通向外面，反而通向更深处，每一块都把她拉向下一块，仿佛那条小径是一根正在被盘卷、而非被解开的绳子。

就在那时，她明白了山谷的本质。那不是人能离开的地方，因为离开需要一个山谷已不再拥有的方向。那坡道不是坡道，而是一场被做得极其平缓、以至于身体误把它当成地面的坠落；那寂静也并非声音的缺席，而是声音已无处可去的缺席。她每一次向上的呼喊都只是弯折过来，汇入那条向下的螺旋，片刻后便化作来自下方的低语，回到她的耳畔。她已经在第十二号石堆处越过了某道无形的门槛，而在门槛的那一侧，「回头」这个念头本身，已被悄然撤销。

玛拉最终在一块并非她石堆的石头上坐下，翻开她的账本。她画不出回去的路，因为根本没有回去的路可画。于是她改而画出自己的所见：大地的弯曲、收窄的天空，以及方向感自我遗忘的那个临界点。她用一个安静的记号标出那个点，并在旁边为日后可能读到这张地图的旅人写道：山谷在它的边缘从不发出警告——人从自由滑入放弃，没有一步、没有一声，而制图师所能留下的唯一善意，便是告诉别人那道线究竟在哪里。

这个故事揭示了「事件视界」的本质——它是坍缩星体周围那道无形的边界，在那里空间的弯曲陡峭到每一个方向都指向内部。越过它，并非撞上一堵墙，而是进入一个「向外」已不再作为一个存在之方向的区域，于是连光——这世上最快的东西——也只能继续向更深处坠落。旅人感觉不到震动，也看不见障碍，只察觉到每一条小路都在缓缓、不可逆地转向中心。越过那道线的一切再也无法传回任何讯息，因为讯息本身就像玛拉的声音一样，已被弯折，只能顺着坠落而去。
articles.content_en:
In the deepest fold of the mountains there lay a valley that the old maps marked only with a single word: Silence. Travelers who approached its rim reported the same strange sensation — that the further they descended, the harder it became to turn back, and the quieter the world grew behind them, as though the air itself were thickening into something denser than air. The cartographer Mara had spent her life charting every pass and hollow of the known ranges, and she resolved to be the first to map the valley's heart and return.

She marked her trail with cairns as she went, dropping a stone every hundred paces, and at first the going was easy. She could still glance back up the slope and see the morning light on the peaks. But at a certain stone — she would later call it the twelfth cairn, though she could never be certain of the count — something shifted. She set the stone down, turned to look at her previous marker, and found that the slope behind her no longer climbed. It curved. The path that should have led upward folded gently back upon itself, and her own footprints, instead of ascending, described a slow spiral downward.

Mara was not a woman given to fear, so she simply turned around and began to climb. She walked for an hour, then two, straining upward with every step, and yet the rim of the valley never rose any closer. The peaks that had been visible that morning had sunk below the curve of the land, and the sky itself had narrowed to a dim circle overhead. She thought of her cairns and tried to retrace them, but the stones behind her led not out but further in, each one pulling her toward the next as though the trail were a rope being coiled, not unwound.

It was then she understood the nature of the valley. It was not a place one could leave, because leaving required moving in a direction the valley no longer possessed. The slope was not a slope but a fall made so gentle that the body mistook it for ground; the silence was not the absence of sound but the absence of anywhere for sound to go. Every call she sent up simply bent and joined the downward spiral, returning to her ear a moment later as a whisper from below. She had crossed some unseen threshold at the twelfth cairn, and on its far side the very idea of 「back」 had been quietly revoked.

Mara sat down at last on a stone that was not one of her cairns and opened her ledger. She could not draw the path out, for there was no path out to draw. So instead she drew what she had found: the curve of the land, the narrowing sky, the point past which direction forgets itself. She labeled that point with a single quiet mark and wrote beside it, for any traveler who might one day read her map, that the valley gives no warning at its edge — that one passes from freedom into surrender without a step, without a sound, and that the only kindness left to a cartographer is to tell others where the line lies.

This story reveals the essence of the event horizon — the invisible boundary around a collapsed star where the curvature of space becomes so steep that every direction points inward. To cross it is not to hit a wall; it is to enter a region where 「outward」 has ceased to be a direction that exists, so that even light, the fastest thing there is, can only fall further in. The traveler feels no jolt and sees no barrier, only a slow, irreversible turning of every path toward the center. What lies beyond that line can never send a message back, because the message itself, like Mara's voice, is bent to follow the fall.

paragraphs.cn: 玛拉最终在一块并非她石堆的石头上坐下，翻开她的账本。她画不出回去的路，因为根本没有回去的路可画。于是她改而画出自己的所见：大地的弯曲、收窄的天空，以及方向感自我遗忘的那个临界点。她用一个安静的记号标出那个点，并在旁边为日后可能读到这张地图的旅人写道：山谷在它的边缘从不发出警告——人从自由滑入放弃，没有一步、没有一声，而制图师所能留下的唯一善意，便是告诉别人那道线究竟在哪里。
paragraphs.en: Mara sat down at last on a stone that was not one of her cairns and opened her ledger. She could not draw the path out, for there was no path out to draw. So instead she drew what she had found: the curve of the land, the narrowing sky, the point past which direction forgets itself. She labeled that point with a single quiet mark and wrote beside it, for any traveler who might one day read her map, that the valley gives no warning at its edge — that one passes from freedom into surrender without a step, without a sound, and that the only kindness left to a cartographer is to tell others where the line lies.

paragraphs.cn: 这个故事揭示了「事件视界」的本质——它是坍缩星体周围那道无形的边界，在那里空间的弯曲陡峭到每一个方向都指向内部。越过它，并非撞上一堵墙，而是进入一个「向外」已不再作为一个存在之方向的区域，于是连光——这世上最快的东西——也只能继续向更深处坠落。旅人感觉不到震动，也看不见障碍，只察觉到每一条小路都在缓缓、不可逆地转向中心。越过那道线的一切再也无法传回任何讯息，因为讯息本身就像玛拉的声音一样，已被弯折，只能顺着坠落而去。
paragraphs.en: This story reveals the essence of the event horizon — the invisible boundary around a collapsed star where the curvature of space becomes so steep that every direction points inward. To cross it is not to hit a wall; it is to enter a region where 「outward」 has ceased to be a direction that exists, so that even light, the fastest thing there is, can only fall further in. The traveler feels no jolt and sees no barrier, only a slow, irreversible turning of every path toward the center. What lies beyond that line can never send a message back, because the message itself, like Mara's voice, is bent to follow the fall.

articles.content_cn:
在伟大的阿克西奥斯（Axios）图书馆里，住着一位一丝不苟的编目者，名叫奥伦（Oren），他唯一的职责就是记录王国里的每一本目录。他注意到，有些目录尽责地把自身也列入自己的书页之中——《目录之目录》自豪地把「这本目录」作为自己的第一条款目。另一些则不然；《甲虫目录》只列出昆虫，从不列入目录本身，因为它把自己看作一件工具，而非一件标本。奥伦觉得这种区别颇为有趣，于是开始把每一本目录分到两堆之一：自含者与不自含者。

某个秋天，馆长要求奥伦编纂一部总目录，收录所有不自含的目录——一本权威的参考书，列出每一本不列入自身的目录。奥伦兴致勃勃地动手，取来一卷又一卷，逐一核对其书页与自身，再把那些顺从条件的目录誊抄进他新的总登记册。他自冬天工作到春天，终于，那部厚重的书在他桌上完工。

随后，在交付的那天早晨，一位年幼的学徒提出了一个天真的问题：「奥伦师傅，您这部总目录是否列入了它自己？」奥伦微微一笑，伸手去抓那个显而易见的答案——但他的手停在了半途。他缓缓把这个问题翻来覆去地思量，笑容也从脸上褪去。

因为：若这部总目录确实列入了它自己，那么依据它自身的规则——它只记录那些不列入自身的目录——它就不该被列入。可若它没有列入自己，那它便恰好满足被收录的那唯一条件，因而又必须被列入。无论作何选择，都会自我取消。无论奥伦转向哪一边，这部书都要求与它所规定的相反之事。他一直坐到暮色深长，总目录摊开在面前，既写不下「是」，也写不下「否」，因为每一个字都会抹去另一个。

这个故事揭示了罗素悖论（Russell's paradox）的本质——当我们随意地允许任何可描述的集合成为「集合」时，矛盾便随之而生。试想那个由所有不包含自身的集合所构成的集合；问它是否包含自身，逻辑便分叉为两个相互抵消的答案，正如奥伦的总目录所遭遇的那样。其教训在于：并非每一句形如「所有满足某条件之物所成的集合」的完好的语句都能指认出一个融贯的对象；数学根基中不受限制的自我指涉会滋生矛盾，这正是现代集合论为何要引入审慎的规则、规定哪些集合才被允许存在的原因。
articles.content_en:
In the great library of Axios, there lived a meticulous cataloger named Oren whose sole task was to record every catalog in the kingdom. Some catalogs, he noted, dutifully listed themselves among their own pages — the Catalog of Catalogs proudly declared "this catalog" as its first entry. Others did not; the Catalog of Beetles named only insects, never the catalog itself, for it considered itself a tool rather than a specimen. Oren found this distinction charming and began sorting every catalog into one of two heaps: the Self-Including and the Self-Excluding.

One autumn, the Librarian asked Oren to compile a single master catalog of all the Self-Excluding catalogs — a definitive reference listing every catalog that does not list itself. Oren set to work with relish, fetching volume after volume, checking each one's pages against itself, and inscribing the obedient ones into his new master register. He worked through winter and into spring, and at last the great book stood complete upon his desk.

Then, on the morning he was to deliver it, a young apprentice posed an innocent question: "Master Oren, does your master catalog list itself?" Oren smiled and reached for the obvious answer — but his hand stopped halfway. He turned the question over slowly, and the smile drained from his face.

For if the master catalog does list itself, then by its own rule — it records only catalogs that do not list themselves — it must not be listed. But if it does not list itself, then it satisfies the one condition for inclusion, and must be listed. Either choice undoes itself. Whichever way Oren turned, the book demanded the opposite of what it required. He sat long into the dusk, the master catalog open before him, unable to write either yes or no, for each word would erase the other.

This story reveals the essence of Russell's paradox — the contradiction that emerges when we casually allow any describable collection to become a "set." Consider the set of all sets that do not contain themselves; ask whether this set contains itself, and logic forks into two mutually destructive answers, exactly as Oren's master catalog did. The lesson is that not every well-formed sentence of the form "the set of all things such that..." picks out a coherent object; unrestricted self-reference in the foundations of mathematics breeds contradictions, which is why modern set theory introduces careful rules about which collections are permitted to exist.
