And while it’s not far-fetched to expect AI to enable breakthroughs that would justify the extreme amounts of energy it requires – better batteries, more efficient transmission grids, cures for serious diseases – I also don’t think “hope for the best” is a reasonable answer to people concerned about the climate crisis.

During my visit to DeepMind I met Helen King, who was one of the company’s earliest employees and now, according to her company bio, “sets Google DeepMind’s strategy for developing and deploying AI responsibly to benefit humanity”. I asked her how the rapid commercialisation of AI technologies has shifted Google’s approach to AI ethics. “We can’t prevent all risks, but we can make sure we are looking to mitigate as many of them as possible, and bring awareness to them,” she said. But she also insisted that some risks had to be managed by users themselves. “It’s like having a knife. A knife producer can’t guarantee how someone is going to use that knife. But they can put a cover on it so that it’s as safe as possible when it’s in a drawer. And make people really aware: this blade is sharp, do not use it in certain settings. That kind of thing.”

The simile struck me as unnervingly apt. Five years ago, LLMs were an exotic technology that was impossible to encounter without determined effort. Now they’re everywhere: on the internet, in our email inboxes, even in Google’s search results. I take King’s point that companies cannot reasonably be expected to eliminate every harm from a technology as powerful as AI: automobiles kill more than a million people a year, after all, and still we keep driving. But it’s one thing to keep a knife in a drawer with a cover snapped over the blade. It’s quite another to blanket every surface of our homes, classrooms and workplaces with blades while insisting that no one who isn’t using knives for everything will be able to survive the future.

These days at DeepMind, as in much of the industry, there is little doubt that AGI is close at hand. At the developer conference in May, Hassabis took the stage to declare that “AGI is now on the horizon”, and elsewhere he has suggested three to five years as a likely timeline. (One test he has proposed involves training an AI with all of human knowledge up to 1911 and seeing if it can come up with the theory of general relativity.)

Legg, meanwhile, told me that although today’s LLMs fall short of his definition of “minimal AGI” in several respects – including spatial and visual reasoning, metacognition and continual learning – he believes that these deficits will not persist for long. “There’s no magic remaining,” he said. “I think they’re all going to be solved in one, two, three years – who knows, maybe in six months. This is an area full of surprises.”

The conviction that the relevant question about AGI is no longer if but when has spurred a concomitant shift in the way frontier labs such as DeepMind are thinking and talking publicly about the consequences of advanced AI. Whereas previous work tended to focus on the ethical aspects of discrete products, such as models, chatbots and agents, today much more attention is being paid to the broader social effects of an AI-augmented world.

In some corners of Silicon Valley, of course, you can still hear people talk about AI as a universal panacea. If you accept the premise that a superintelligent AI will be able to think better about what’s best for us in every domain of life, then the solution to any problem that arises is easy. Economic crisis? Ask the robot. Political disagreement? Ask the robot. Food shortage? Ask the robot.

Alongside this fantasy, however, there’s been a more sober-minded recognition that the transition to a post-AI world may not be a smooth one. Legg, for instance, told me that he was looking forward to “fantastically great” benefits from AI, including “opportunities to address all kinds of nasty diseases” and “a general increase in all kinds of productivity in the economy”. Yet he also acknowledged that “increases in productivity usually come with some kind of disruption”.

Gabriel’s recent work at DeepMind is a useful indicator of the shift to a wide-angle perspective. Two years ago he and his colleagues were working out the ethics of AI assistants. Now, however, he leads a team of philosophers and social scientists investigating “how AGI will impact the economy, how it will impact the political sphere, how it will impact human relationships and how it will interact with science and technology”.

Gabriel expects that AGI will be transformative in a major way – potentially on the scale of the Industrial Revolution. Yet he believes, too, that AI is not something “before which the world becomes a frictionless entity”. He is also keenly aware that the Industrial Revolution was not a happy experience for many of the people who lived through it, even though it eventually raised living standards around the world: “Things got worse before they got better.”

Read moreNevertheless, Gabriel does not think that the historical precedent settles the question, in large part because ordinary people individually and collectively have more power than they did 300 years ago. Though he was wary of sounding “too utopian and ungrounded”, he said he found it easy to imagine a world in which AI provides benefits that range from offering advice to curing diseases to improving economic growth in ways that benefit rich and poor alike. “If we can navigate the transition, navigate the power dynamics, navigate the risk successfully, there is a generalised potential for human flourishing on a level we haven’t seen so far.”

If the predictions about AGI’s arrival prove accurate, still broader questions may come to the fore as well. When I spoke to Edward Harcourt, at Oxford, he noted that “thinking about values and technological change is very hard because technological change always seems more of an upheaval in prospect than it does in retrospect, for the obvious reason that when we look back, we’re looking from the standpoint of values that have been shaped by the change in question. If you read people on the subject of the railways before they happened, they thought it was a complete catastrophe. And it’s true: the railways wrecked an entire way of life. Now we look back and we think: what’s the issue?”

Gabriel, too, thinks that AI might prompt changes that go even deeper than economics or technology. During the scientific revolution, he noted, “people experienced disenchantment when it was revealed that the world worked in certain ways. But they also gained new freedoms through that experience.” It will be up to us, he said, to decide which value changes we want to welcome, and which we choose to resist.

At one point in our conversations, Gabriel described himself to me as “a card-carrying humanist”: he is not the sort of person who looks forward to a day when superintelligent machines render humanity obsolete. Still, he recognises that as computers encroach on activities and capabilities that we have long held to be the special province of Homo sapiens – language, creativity, humour, taste – we find ourselves thrown back on some of the oldest and most difficult philosophical questions of all. Just as discoveries in physics, biology and astronomy led past generations to revise their understanding of what makes our species distinctive, he suggested, so, too, might AI prompt us to reconsider what it means to be a human being.

paragraphs.cn: 自 2017 年起，伊亚森·加布里埃尔（Iason Gabriel）便在这家科技巨头工作，试图预见——并深入思考——AI 的影响。但随着商业和地缘政治压力不断加剧，伦理学家还能起什么作用吗？
paragraphs.en: Since 2017, Iason Gabriel has worked at the tech giant, trying to anticipate – and think through – the impact of AI. But as commercial and geopolitical pressures escalate, can ethicists make any difference?

paragraphs.cn: 2017 年，一位 33 岁的政治哲学家伊亚森·加布里埃尔从朋友那里得知，他应当去 DeepMind 应聘一份工作。DeepMind 是谷歌（Google）位于伦敦的子公司，谷歌大部分的 AI 研究都集中于此。这个建议乍看并不那么理所当然。
paragraphs.en: In 2017, a 33-year-old political philosopher named Iason Gabriel was told by a friend that he ought to apply for a job at DeepMind, the London-based subsidiary of Google where much of its AI research was concentrated. The suggestion was not an obvious one.

paragraphs.cn: 加布里埃尔是一位开朗却极其专注的青年学者，热爱内观（Vipassana）禅修，还有他哥哥所说的「兴致勃勃」的攀岩。作为一位希腊管理学教授和一位英国纪录片制作者的长子，加布里埃尔在教书与国际发展工作之间分配自己的时间。在牛津大学（University of Oxford）担任圣约翰学院（St John's College）研究员期间，他讲授政治理论课程，撰写关于「雅皮士伦理」的道德扭曲以及有效利他主义伦理盲点的论文。不在牛津时，他在苏丹和黎巴嫩为联合国开发计划署（United Nations Development Programme）从事危机工作。
paragraphs.en: Gabriel was a cheerful but intense junior academic with a passion for Vipassana meditation and what his brother calls “enthusiastic” rock climbing. The eldest son of a Greek management professor and a British documentary maker, Gabriel split his time between teaching and international development work. At the University of Oxford, where he was a fellow at St John’s College, Gabriel taught courses on political theory and wrote papers on the moral contortions of “yuppie ethics” and the ethical blind spots of effective altruism. When he wasn’t there, he did crisis work for the United Nations Development Programme in Sudan and Lebanon.

paragraphs.cn: 与此同时，DeepMind 是全球领先的 AI 研究实验室。这部分得益于谷歌在资金和算力上的支持——谷歌于 2014 年以 6.5 亿美元收购了该公司。另一部分则是因为 DeepMind 不久前展示了它能将这些资源发挥到令人惊叹的程度。2016 年，在首尔，一套名为 AlphaGo 的 DeepMind 系统在五番棋比赛中击败了韩国围棋冠军李世乭（Lee Sedol）。这场胜利意义非凡，尤其因为围棋有着传奇般的复杂性；该棋的可能局面比宇宙中的原子还要多。
paragraphs.en: DeepMind, meanwhile, was the world’s leading AI research lab. In part, this was because it had the financial and computational backing of Google, which had bought the company in 2014 for $650m. In part, it was because DeepMind had recently shown it could put those resources to stunning use. In Seoul, in 2016, a DeepMind system called AlphaGo defeated Lee Sedol, a South Korean Go champion, in a five-game match. The victory was significant not least because of Go’s legendary complexity; the game has more possible configurations than there are atoms in the universe.

paragraphs.cn: 多亏了围绕 AlphaGo 的轰动，加布里埃尔是知道 DeepMind 的。尽管如此，他还是觉得朋友的建议令人费解：一家制造下棋机器人的公司为什么需要伦理学家？他很快得知的答案是，这家公司的目标远不止于围棋。DeepMind 由三人——德米斯·哈萨比斯（Demis Hassabis）、沙恩·莱格（Shane Legg）和穆斯塔法·苏莱曼（Mustafa Suleyman）——于 2010 年创立，他们相信开发通用人工智能（artificial general intelligence，简称 AGI）一定是可能的。他们所指的，是能够匹敌、或许还能超越人类认知能力的计算机系统。当他们创立公司时，这并非主流观点：谈论 AI 已属不易，更不用说 AGI，在许多人看来是极不严肃的标志。哈萨比斯、莱格和苏莱曼并未因此却步。他们的雄心，正如他们爱说的那样，是「先解决智能，然后再解决其他一切」。
paragraphs.en: Thanks to the fuss around AlphaGo, Gabriel was aware of DeepMind. Still, he found his friend’s suggestion puzzling: why did a company that made game-playing robots need an ethicist? The answer, as he soon learned, was that the company had its sights set much higher than Go. DeepMind was founded in 2010 by three men – Demis Hassabis, Shane Legg and Mustafa Suleyman – who believed that it must be possible to develop artificial general intelligence, or AGI. By this they meant computer systems that could match, and maybe surpass, human cognitive capabilities. When they started the company, this was not a popular view: to speak of AI, let alone AGI, was considered by many a sign of fatal unseriousness. Hassabis, Legg and Suleyman were undeterred. Their ambition, as they liked to say, was to “solve intelligence, and then solve everything else”.

paragraphs.cn: 对于 DeepMind 的创始人而言，这样一项成就将带来广泛的影响是显而易见的。1999 年，刚大学毕业的莱格估计 AGI 会在 2025 至 2028 年间到来，这一预测他在长达三十年的众多嘲弄中始终坚持。在 2008 年完成的学位论文中，他坚持认为，社会不能等到 AGI 在技术上可行之时才来考量其影响：「我们需要现在就认真着手这些事情。」最近，莱格告诉我，公司为何需要像加布里埃尔这样的人「显而易见」：「如果你在做某种小玩意儿，而且它多半不会改变世界，那你也许不需要一位道德哲学家。但如果你认真对待 AGI，那我就真看不出你怎么会认为这类事情不重要。」
paragraphs.en: For the DeepMind founders, it was clear that such an achievement would have widespread consequences. In 1999, when Legg was fresh out of university, he estimated that AGI would arrive somewhere between 2025 and 2028, a prediction he maintained in the face of much mockery for three decades. In his dissertation, completed in 2008, he insisted that society could not afford to wait until AGI was technically feasible to consider its effects: “We need to be seriously working on these things now.” More recently, Legg told me it was “obvious” why the company needed people like Gabriel on staff: “If you’re making some widget, and it’s probably not going to change the world, then maybe you don’t need a moral philosopher. But if you take AGI seriously, then I can’t really see how you wouldn’t consider this sort of thing as important.”

paragraphs.cn: 右下角是李世乭，2016 年 3 月，他与其他职业围棋手一同复盘自己对阵 AlphaGo 的对局。摄影：Lee Jin-man/AP。2017 年加入 DeepMind 后，加布里埃尔一度是前沿 AI 实验室中唯一在岗的哲学家。他很快发现，自己横跨道德哲学与政治理论的背景，让他在一个由工程师主导的行业中拥有独特的视角。在过去十年里，他积累了一系列研究成果，这些工作追踪、并在许多情况下预言了大语言模型（LLM）令人意外的成功所引发的伦理挑战。
paragraphs.en: Lee Sedol, bottom right, reviews one of his matches against AlphaGo with fellow professional Go players in March 2016. Photograph: Lee Jin-man/APAfter starting at DeepMind in 2017, Gabriel was, for a time, the only active philosopher working at a frontier AI lab. He quickly discovered that his background in moral philosophy and political theory gave him an unusual perspective in an industry dominated by engineers. Over the past decade, he has assembled a body of work that tracked, and in many cases predicted, the ethical challenges created by the surprising success of large language models (LLMs).

paragraphs.cn: 在麻省理工学院（MIT）领导算法对齐小组的迪伦·哈德菲尔德-梅内尔（Dylan Hadfield-Menell）告诉我，加布里埃尔是「对的人遇到了对的时刻。当这个领域准备成熟、走向前台时，他找到了一种拓宽视野的方式，而非攻击或贬低此前的工作。」
paragraphs.en: As Dylan Hadfield-Menell, who leads the Algorithmic Alignment Group at MIT, told me, Gabriel was “the right person meeting the moment. As the field was ready to mature and move into prime time, he figured out a way to broaden the horizons without attacking or denigrating the work that came before.”

paragraphs.cn: 更广泛而言，加布里埃尔一直是一种观点的主要倡导者：当前这波 AI 发展不仅要求新的技术词汇，还要求新的思考方式——重新思考我们与技术、甚至与我们自身的关系。正如他在我们过去几个月间进行的数次长谈中某次对我说的那样：「我可以拿任何一件技术人造物来问：它明智吗？它公正吗？它关怀吗？而答案是否定的。但就 AI 而言——包括什么样的伦理才适用于它——这个问题的深度怎么估计都不过分。我有时觉得，要直视 AI 非常困难。那里存在着一种深深的神秘，即：这东西究竟是什么？我们有一个非常字面的答案，但这个字面的答案似乎未必能提供一种道德上的答案。」
paragraphs.en: More generally, Gabriel has been a leading advocate for the idea that the current wave of AI development demands not just new technical vocabularies but also new ways of thinking about our relationship to technology, and even to ourselves. As he put it to me recently, in one of several long conversations we’ve had over the past few months, “I can take any technological artefact and ask: is it wise? Is it just? Is it caring? And the answer is no. But the depth of the question when it comes to AI – including what kind of ethics is appropriate to it – is hard to overstate. I sometimes feel like it’s very hard to look at AI directly. There’s this deep mystery there, which is: but what actually is this thing? We have a very literal answer, but the literal answer doesn’t seem to necessarily provide a moral answer.”

paragraphs.cn: 在加布里埃尔加入 DeepMind 之时，大致说来，关于 AI 之社会与伦理影响的问题存在两种截然不同、且常常对立的取向。这些取向有时被分别归入「AI 安全」（AI safety）和「AI 伦理」（AI ethics）的名目之下，它们的分歧在于对这项技术可行性的看法不同。
paragraphs.en: By the time Gabriel joined DeepMind, there were, roughly speaking, two distinct and often antagonistic approaches to questions about the social and ethical implications of AI. These approaches, sometimes classed under the headings of AI safety and AI ethics, were divided by a disagreement about the feasibility of the technology.

paragraphs.cn: 与 DeepMind 创始人一样，AI 安全阵营相信，人类级别的机器智能不仅可能，而且迫在眉睫。在他们看来，当务之急是确保 AI 系统不出岔子。他们的灵感来自美国数学家、计算机科学家诺伯特·维纳（Norbert Wiener）1960 年的一篇文章，维纳在其中论证人类与计算机「本质上是彼此陌生的」。由于机器运转远快于人，维纳说，「我们最好相当确定，植入机器的目的，确实是我们真正欲求的目的，而不仅仅是对它的一种花哨模仿。」
paragraphs.en: Like the DeepMind founders, the AI safety contingent believed that human-grade machine intelligence was not only possible but imminent. The urgent task, as they saw things, was to make sure that AI systems didn’t go awry. They took inspiration from a 1960 essay by Norbert Wiener, an American mathematician and computer scientist, who argued that humans and computers are “essentially foreign to each other”. Because machines can operate much faster than people, Wiener said, “we had better be quite sure that the purpose put into the machine is the purpose which we really desire and not merely a colourful imitation of it”.

paragraphs.cn: 维纳所描述的挑战——让机器按照其使用者意图行事——后来被称为「对齐问题」（alignment problem）。在某种层面上，对齐是每项技术都有的问题，但正如维纳所认识到的那样，对于设计为自主行动的机器而言尤为紧迫。对于以数学方式优化某个奖励信号而训练的 AI 系统而言也尤为困难，这一过程被称为「强化学习」（reinforcement learning）。
paragraphs.en: The challenge Wiener described – getting a machine to act in the way its users intended – became known as the alignment problem. At some level, alignment is an issue for every technology, but as Wiener recognised, it was particularly pressing for machines designed to act autonomously. It was also particularly difficult for AI systems trained to mathematically optimise some reward signal, a process known as reinforcement learning.

paragraphs.cn: 2016 年，当时在 OpenAI 工作、后来与他人共同创立 Anthropic 的达里奥·阿莫代伊（Dario Amodei）和杰克·克拉克（Jack Clark）报告了一个经典案例。阿莫代伊和克拉克描述了一款为玩赛艇电子游戏而设计的 AI 系统。开发者希望 AI 学会通关，于是将其编程为追求最高分。然而，AI 并非逐关推进，而是在一片环礁湖中无尽兜圈——在那里它发现了三个可再生的目标——以此刷出高分。根本症结正是维纳所预言的：机器的目标与开发者的目标未能完美对齐。
paragraphs.en: A classic example was reported in 2016 by Dario Amodei and Jack Clark, who worked at OpenAI and later founded Anthropic with five others. Amodei and Clark described an AI system designed to play a boat-racing video game. The developers wanted the AI to learn to beat the game, so they programmed it to maximise its score. Instead of working its way through each successive level, however, the AI racked up a high score by looping endlessly around a lagoon where it found a trio of regenerating targets. The basic trouble was the one Wiener had predicted: the machine’s goal was imperfectly aligned with the developers’.

paragraphs.cn: 更严峻版本的问题也被纳入考量。在自学者、AI 研究者埃利泽·尤德科夫斯基（Eliezer Yudkowsky）创办的 LessWrong 等论坛上，以及在哲学家尼克·博斯特罗姆（Nick Bostrom）2014 年出版的《超级智能》（Superintelligence）等书中，有人推测一场机器智能爆炸可能产生不可控的 AI。如果这样一个智能体哪怕有轻微的错位，后果也可能灾难性。博斯特罗姆引用的一个假想例子中，一台超级智能 AI 被要求评估数学中最重要的未解难题之一——黎曼猜想（Riemann hypothesis）。在试图完成这项任务的过程中，这台 AI 决定重排太阳系——「包括曾经关心答案之人的身体中的原子」——以最大化它攻克该问题所需的资源。
paragraphs.en: More dire versions of the problem were also contemplated. On forums such as LessWrong, which was started by the autodidact AI researcher Eliezer Yudkowsky, and in books such as Superintelligence, which was published in 2014 by the philosopher Nick Bostrom, there was speculation that a machine-intelligence explosion could result in an uncontrollable AI. If such an agent were even slightly misaligned, the consequences could be disastrous. In one imaginary example cited by Bostrom, a superintelligent AI is asked to evaluate the Riemann hypothesis, one of the most important unsolved problems in mathematics. In the course of trying to accomplish this task, the AI decides to rearrange the solar system – “including the atoms in the bodies of whomever once cared about the answer” – to maximise the resources it needs to attack the problem.

paragraphs.cn: 博斯特罗姆坚称，对齐超级智能 AI「很可能是人类有史以来面临的最重要、也最艰巨的挑战」，这一主张令硅谷的技术未来主义者为之着迷。（萨姆·奥特曼（Sam Altman）和埃隆·马斯克（Elon Musk）都称赞过这本书。）他的担忧也被一个虽小却健谈的有效利他主义者和自诩理性主义者群体所共享，他们视统计为衡量道德的正当尺度。该群体中许多人持一种「长期主义」（long-termist）视角，把未来出生的人类——甚至数千年后出生的人类——的福祉纳入其道德算式。对他们而言，这是简单的算术：哪怕物种终结的灾难只有微小的概率，也比任何数量更可能却不那么灾难性的危险更为紧迫。
paragraphs.en: Bostrom’s insistence that aligning superintelligent AI was “quite possibly the most important and most daunting challenge humanity has ever faced” captivated technofuturists in Silicon Valley. (Sam Altman praised the book, as did Elon Musk.) His fears were also shared by a small but loquacious community of effective altruists and self-described rationalists who saw statistics as the proper measure of morality. Many people in this community held a “long-termist” perspective that factored the wellbeing of humans born in the future – even thousands of years into the future – into their moral equations. For them it was simple maths that even a small chance of a species-ending disaster was more urgent than any number of likelier, but less catastrophic, dangers.

paragraphs.cn: 与 AI 安全群体形成对照的是，与 AI 伦理取向相关的学者和技术专家将失控机器人和生存风险的幽灵视为对当下危害的转移注意力的幌子。他们从批判种族理论家金伯莉·克伦肖（Kimberlé Crenshaw）和政治理论家（兼前摇滚乐评人）兰登·温纳（Langdon Winner）等人那里汲取灵感，将公平、问责与透明作为他们的箴言，并坚持认为技术的危险无法仅凭技术手段加以规避。他们主张，所需要的是社会、文化与政治层面的解决方案。
paragraphs.en: By contrast with the AI safety crowd, the academics and technologists associated with the AI ethics tendency saw the spectre of rogue robots and existential risk as a distraction from present-day harms. Drawing inspiration from the critical race theorist Kimberlé Crenshaw and the political theorist (and former rock critic) Langdon Winner, among others, they took fairness, accountability and transparency as their watchwords and insisted that the dangers of technology could not be avoided by merely technical means. What was needed, they argued, were social, cultural and political solutions.

paragraphs.cn: 后一种取向的一个核心关切是算法偏见，即影响面部识别和预测性警务软件的那种偏见。2017 年，由麻省理工学院媒体实验室（MIT Media Lab）的乔伊·布奥拉姆维尼（Joy Buolamwini）带领的团队推出了 Gender Shades 项目，证明商业面部识别软件存在系统性偏见。「自动化系统并非天生中立，」布奥拉姆维尼在网页介绍中写道，「它们反映了那些有权塑造人工智能之人的优先级、偏好与偏见——即所谓『编码的凝视』。」
paragraphs.en: A central concern of this latter tendency was algorithmic bias, of the sort that affected facial-recognition and predictive-policing software. In 2017, a team led by Joy Buolamwini, of the MIT Media Lab, launched Gender Shades, a project that demonstrated systemic biases in commercial facial-recognition software. “Automated systems are not inherently neutral,” Buolamwini wrote in the online introduction. “They reflect the priorities, preferences and prejudices – the coded gaze – of those who have the power to mould artificial intelligence.”

paragraphs.cn: 安全派与伦理派之间的分歧常常十分鲜明。「你和人碰面，他们会问：『你担心的是近期问题还是长期问题？』」哈德菲尔德-梅内尔说，「『长期关切』是生存风险的委婉说法——本质上是超人系统。近期则意味着你担心有偏见的面部识别，以及 AI 伦理社区研究的那些问题。」
paragraphs.en: The division between the safety and ethics camps was often pronounced. “You’d meet up with people and they’d ask: ‘Are you worried about near-term problems or long-term problems?’” Hadfield-Menell says. “The long-term concern was a euphemism for existential risk – essentially superhuman systems. Near-term meant you’re worried about biased facial recognition and the things studied within the AI ethics community.”

paragraphs.cn: 他也指出，两个群体之间的冲突似乎与其说与观念有关，不如说同样与社会学有关。「你没法真正把 AI 安全与它在 LessWrong 和某些社群中的起源分开，那些社群常常公开鄙视许多更为『觉醒』的学者——找不到更好的词来形容。与此同时，公平、问责与透明社群也对那些担心高级 AI 的人抱有公开的鄙视。它之所以在 LessWrong 上被讨论、而不是在学术会议上，原因在于：如果你在 2010 年是一名学术研究者，而你谈 AI 系统会变得比人类更聪明并发生灾难性的错位，那你就是个其实不懂技术的怪人。」
paragraphs.en: He noted, too, that the conflicts between the two groups often seemed to have as much to do with sociology as they did with ideas. “You can’t really separate AI safety from its origins among LessWrong and some of those communities, which were often openly disdainful of a lot of the more ‘woke’ academics, for lack of a better term. At the same time, the fairness, accountability and transparency community had a lot of open disdain for people who were worried about advanced AI. The reason why it was being talked about on LessWrong, and not at academic conferences, is because if you were an academic researcher in 2010 and you talked about AI systems getting smarter than humans and becoming catastrophically misaligned, you were a crank who didn’t actually understand the technology.”

paragraphs.cn: 加布里埃尔在 DeepMind 的第一个主要研究项目是 2020 年的一篇论文，横跨了两个阵营的关切。这篇论文严肃对待对齐问题，但同时也坚持认为，对齐所具有的伦理和政治意涵超越了技术挑战本身。加布里埃尔论证道，让机器按照某套价值行事固然困难，但更难的却是首先选定这些价值。「鉴于我们生活在一个充满相互竞争的价值观念的多元主义世界，」他问道，「我们该如何决定将哪些原则或目标编入 AI——又有谁有权做出这些决定？」
paragraphs.en: Gabriel’s first major research project at DeepMind was a 2020 paper that straddled the concerns of both camps. The paper took the alignment problem seriously, but it also insisted that alignment had ethical and political implications that went beyond the technical challenges. As difficult as it might be to get a machine to act in accordance with some set of values, Gabriel argued, it was much harder to choose those values in the first place. “Given that we live in a pluralistic world that is full of competing conceptions of value,” he asked, “how are we to decide which principles or objectives to encode in AI – and who has the right to make these decisions?”

paragraphs.cn: 牛津大学的 AI 研究者、曾与加布里埃尔合作的汉娜·罗斯·柯克（Hannah Rose Kirk）告诉我，这类问题令许多计算机科学家不安。开发者往往更愿意求出一个整洁的数学函数，让它编码一套稳定的价值观，而不愿去应付那些牵涉欲望不可调和的人群、或用户在不同时点想要不同之物的棘手局面。正如柯克所言：「早期对齐研究中有许多假定，认为我们不必过多关注要模型做什么，只需关注如何让它们去做。」
paragraphs.en: Hannah Rose Kirk, an AI researcher at the University of Oxford who has collaborated with Gabriel, told me that such questions made many computer scientists uneasy. Developers often preferred to work out a tidy mathematical function that encoded a stable set of values rather than worry about messy situations involving groups of people with irreconcilable desires, or users who wanted different things at different times. As Kirk put it: “A lot of the early research in alignment assumed that we didn’t need to focus that much on what we want models to do. We just needed to focus on how to get them to do it.”

paragraphs.cn: 乔伊·布奥拉姆维尼就其对 AI 面部识别偏见的研究发表 TED 演讲。摄影：TED。在其论文中，加布里埃尔论证这样一种利落的划分是站不住脚的。与布奥拉姆维尼，以及她之前的温纳一样，他坚持认为技术并非天然价值中立。例如，一套以统计优化方法训练的 AI，可能尤其易于接纳同样依赖统计优化的道德体系，比如理性主义者和有效利他主义者所推崇的功利主义。然而，同一套 AI 在处理基于德性或权利的伦理体系时可能力有不逮。此外，加布里埃尔论证，既然哲学家约翰·罗尔斯（John Rawls）所称的「合理多元主义的事实」不可避免，开发者便不应试图找到单一的一套价值来指导 AI 的行为。相反，他们应当为这样一个世界构建 AI 系统：其中人们对「如何最好地生活」存在原则性的分歧。
paragraphs.en: Joy Buolamwini giving a TED talk on her research into the biases of AI facial recognition. Photograph: TEDIn his paper, Gabriel argued that such a neat division was untenable. Like Buolamwini, and Winner before her, he insisted that technology was not intrinsically value-neutral. An AI trained with statistical optimisation methods, for example, might be particularly hospitable to moral systems that also relied on statistical optimisation, such as the utilitarianism popular among rationalists and effective altruists. The same AI, however, might have difficulty with ethical systems based on virtue or rights. Moreover, Gabriel argued, since what the philosopher John Rawls called “the fact of reasonable pluralism” was unavoidable, developers should not try to find a single set of values to inform an AI’s behaviour. Instead, they should build AI systems for a world in which people have “principled disagreement about how best to live”.

paragraphs.cn: 柯克告诉我，加布里埃尔的价值与对齐论文预见了后来当 AI 系统被部署给数十亿用户时所暴露的许多问题。如今许多人认识到，对齐是一个牵涉动态社会力量的挑战，并非靠巧妙的计算机编程就能解决。然而即便短短六年前，这种认识也远非普遍。她说，加布里埃尔「极早地就看到了这些东西的到来」。
paragraphs.en: Kirk told me that Gabriel’s values and alignment paper anticipated many of the problems that would later become apparent when AI systems were deployed to billions of users. These days many people recognise that alignment is a challenge that involves dynamic social forces, and not one that can be solved with clever computer programming. Yet even as recently as six years ago, that understanding was far from common. Gabriel, she says, “saw this stuff coming incredibly early”.

paragraphs.cn: 2020 年，当加布里埃尔发表他的价值与对齐论文时，很少有人预料到大语言模型日后会如此强大。使其成为可能的一项关键技术由谷歌的另一部门——谷歌研究院（Google Research）——于 2017 年发明，并于两年后整合进谷歌的搜索引擎。DeepMind 和谷歌研究院都试验了各自的生成式模型，2021 年，加布里埃尔作为共同作者发表了两篇论文，它们对 LLM 足够认真地对待，预见了其潜在风险，包括偏见、虚假信息、环境成本以及「版权破坏」——即「内容的自动生成……蚕食人类作者作品的市场」。
paragraphs.en: In 2020, when Gabriel published his values and alignment paper, few people had any idea that LLMs would turn out to be as powerful as they later became. A key technology that makes them possible was invented by Google Research, another division of the company, in 2017, and was integrated into Google’s search engine two years later. Both DeepMind and Google Research experimented with their own generative models, and in 2021 Gabriel was a co-author on two papers that took LLMs seriously enough to anticipate their potential risks, including bias, misinformation, environmental costs and “copyright-busting”, in which the “automated creation of content … cannibalises the market for human authored works”.

paragraphs.cn: 尽管如此，加布里埃尔说，当时 DeepMind 内部的普遍看法是，LLM「看起来就是不如专家系统那般能干。它们把很多事情做得还行，包括一些看上去像派对把戏的东西。」在 DeepMind，他说，「人们仍然相当重地押注于其他路径才是出路的可能性」。
paragraphs.en: Still, Gabriel says, the general view within DeepMind at the time was that LLMs “just didn’t look as capable as the expert systems. They were doing a lot of things moderately well, including some things that looked like party tricks.” At DeepMind, he says, “people were still quite heavily invested in the possibility that other approaches were the way to go”.

paragraphs.cn: 其中一条路径就是强化学习，它曾驱动 AlphaGo 战胜李世乭。它也是一个名为 AlphaFold 的系统的基础，该系统至今仍被视为 DeepMind 最了不起的成就。AlphaFold 旨在解决生物学中一个长期挑战：如何根据氨基酸序列预测蛋白质的三维形状。（这很重要，因为蛋白质的形状有助于决定其与其他分子的相互作用。）2020 年，AlphaFold 以惊人的精度完成了这项任务，这是一项科学突破，为哈萨比斯及其同事约翰·江珀（John Jumper）赢得了诺贝尔化学奖。
paragraphs.en: One of those approaches was reinforcement learning, which had powered AlphaGo to its victory over Lee Sedol. It was also the foundation of a system called AlphaFold, which still ranks as DeepMind’s most impressive accomplishment to date. AlphaFold was built to solve a longstanding challenge in biology: how to predict the 3D shape of a protein based on its amino acid sequence. (This is important because the shape of proteins helps determine their interactions with other molecules.) In 2020, AlphaFold accomplished this task with astonishing accuracy, a scientific breakthrough that earned Hassabis and his colleague, John Jumper, a Nobel prize in Cchemistry.

paragraphs.cn: DeepMind 起初对 LLM 的不信任并非个例。2020 年，曾与布奥拉姆维尼合作 Gender Shades 的谷歌研究院工程师蒂姆尼特·格布鲁（Timnit Gebru）与人合撰了一篇针对这项新兴技术的檄文，题为《论随机鹦鹉的危险》（On the Dangers of Stochastic Parrots）。这篇后来成为反 AI 倡导基石的论文，提出了一个颇具争议的主张：LLM 只能产生技术上无意义的文本，对人类语言的理解不比一只鹦鹉更多。它还指责这些模型肆意耗费能源、存在猖獗且不受追究的偏见，以及「放大某种霸权世界观」。《随机鹦鹉》广为人知是在谷歌试图阻止其发表之际，这一事件导致格布鲁离开公司，并最终导致其合作者之一玛格丽特·米切尔（Margaret Mitchell）被解雇。（格布鲁与谷歌对她究竟是辞职还是被解雇一事说法不一。）
paragraphs.en: DeepMind’s initial distrust of LLMs was not uncommon. In 2020, Timnit Gebru, a Google Research engineer who had worked with Buolamwini on Gender Shades, co-authored a broadside against the nascent technology titled On the Dangers of Stochastic Parrots. The paper, which eventually became a cornerstone of anti-AI advocacy, made the controversial claim that LLMs could only ever produce technically meaningless text and possessed no more understanding of human language than a parrot does. It also accused the models of wanton energy consumption, rampant and unaccountable bias, and “amplification of a hegemonic worldview”. Stochastic Parrots came to wide notice when Google tried to block its release, an event that led to Gebru’s departure from the company and, ultimately, the firing of Margaret Mitchell, one of her co-authors. (Gebru and the company disagree whether she resigned or was fired.)

paragraphs.cn: 2022 年 11 月 OpenAI 推出的聊天机器人 ChatGPT 令人瞩目的商业成功，促使 DeepMind 重新评估其对 LLM 的态度。尽管 ChatGPT 在许多方面都受限——按今日标准当然如此，即便与 OpenAI 当时自家的内部模型相比亦然——它的公开发布仍瞬间引发轰动。该聊天机器人上线一周内，公司报告用户超过 100 万。两个月后，这一数字达到 1 亿。
paragraphs.en: The startling commercial success of ChatGPT, a chatbot launched by OpenAI in November 2022, pushed DeepMind to re-evaluate its approach to LLMs. Though ChatGPT was limited in many ways – by today’s standards, certainly, but also by comparison with OpenAI’s own internal models at the time – its public release caused an instant sensation. Within a week of the chatbot’s launch, the company reported more than 1 million users. Two months later, that number reached 100 million.

paragraphs.cn: 在那之前，DeepMind 和谷歌研究院的创新已使谷歌享有 AI 研究领军者的声誉。然而凭借 ChatGPT，OpenAI 有力地宣称自己才是新的领跑者。据塞巴斯蒂安·马拉比（Sebastian Mallaby）近期出版的 DeepMind 史书《无穷机器》（The Infinity Machine）所述，ChatGPT 的成功引发了一场危机。谷歌母公司字母表（Alphabet）的首席执行官桑达尔·皮查伊（Sundar Pichai）将谷歌研究院一个一直从事 LLM 研究的团队并入 DeepMind，由哈萨比斯掌管，以集中公司之力。2023 年 4 月，即合并宣布的当月，哈萨比斯告诉马拉比，OpenAI 和重金投资 OpenAI 的微软（Microsoft）已经「把坦克直接开到了自家草坪上」。「这是战时，」他说。
paragraphs.en: Up to that point, the innovations at DeepMind and Google Research had given Google a reputation as the leader in AI research. With ChatGPT, however, OpenAI made a credible claim to be the new frontrunner. According to Sebastian Mallaby’s recent history of DeepMind, The Infinity Machine, ChatGPT’s success prompted a crisis. Sundar Pichai, the CEO of Alphabet, Google’s parent company, merged a Google Research team that had been working on LLMs into DeepMind, with Hassabis in charge, to concentrate the company’s efforts. In April 2023, the same month the merger was announced, Hassabis told Mallaby that OpenAI and Microsoft, which invested heavily in OpenAI, had “literally parked the tanks on the lawn”. “This is wartime,” he said.

paragraphs.cn: 尤其在头一个十年里，DeepMind 更像是一家研究机构，而非科技创业公司。创始人中有两位持有博士学位，他们设想打造一个 21 世纪的贝尔实验室（Bell Labs）——那家研究机构被认为催生了晶体管、激光和光伏电池等发明。他们加入谷歌的一个主要原因，正是看中它所承诺的、免受可能扭曲其使命的商业压力的自由。
paragraphs.en: During its first decade especially, DeepMind resembled a research institution more than a tech startup. The founders, two of whom held PhDs, envisioned a 21st-century equivalent to Bell Labs, the research organisation credited with such inventions as the transistor, the laser and the photovoltaic cell. A large part of their reason for joining Google was the freedom it promised from commercial pressures that might warp their mission.

paragraphs.cn: 如今这种自由已成遥远的记忆：毫不夸张地说，谷歌的未来取决于 DeepMind 正在开发的技术的成败。即便如此，据公司内外人士所言，它仍保持着一种在文化上与硅谷竞争对手区隔的氛围。在加州大学伯克利分校（UC Berkeley）取得博士学位、现任 DeepMind AGI 对齐与安全总监的罗欣·沙阿（Rohin Shah）告诉我，湾区普遍的态度是：AI 技术的发展速度超出了传统机构所能应对的节奏，因此「负责任的做法就是更快行动、更快创新」，其理据是只有超级能干的 AI 才能管理超级能干 AI 的风险。相比之下，在伦敦则有一种努力，要「更接地气、更具科学严谨性」。曾在 DeepMind 与加布里埃尔共事、现就职于 Anthropic 的萨芙朗·黄（Saffron Huang）说，DeepMind「更有学术机构的质感，也更矜持一些。它就是有种说不清的英伦味道。」
paragraphs.en: These days such freedom is a distant memory: it’s no exaggeration to say that Google’s future depends on the success or failure of the technologies DeepMind is developing. Even so, according to people inside and outside the company, it has maintained an atmosphere that separates it culturally from its Silicon Valley competitors. Rohin Shah, who did a PhD at UC Berkeley and is now DeepMind’s director for AGI alignment and safety, told me that the general attitude in the Bay Area is that AI technology is developing faster than traditional institutions are set up to handle, and that therefore “the responsible thing to do is to move faster, to innovate” on the theory that only a supercompetent AI will be able to manage the risks of supercompetent AIs. In London, by contrast, there is an effort to be “more grounded and scientifically rigorous”. Saffron Huang, a former colleague of Gabriel’s at DeepMind who now works at Anthropic, says that DeepMind is “a bit more of an academic-feeling institution, a bit more reserved. There’s just something about it that felt kind of British.”

paragraphs.cn: 不出意料，DeepMind 也相当保密：外界对该公司的了解极少超出它希望被了解的范围。今年 5 月初，我造访了 DeepMind 位于伦敦国王十字（King's Cross）的总部，对此种保密有了切身体会。这栋建筑既不张扬也不招摇：虽无外墙标识，但从街上就能看见大堂里一个用灯光拼出公司名称的大招牌。进去后，在一面荣誉墙上，即便是未被邀请的访客也能看到曾见证李世乭败绩的棋盘、数张宣告公司早期研究突破的《自然》（Nature）杂志封面，以及一块纪念彼得·蒂尔（Peter Thiel）的 Founders Fund 早期投资的亚克力「墓碑」纪念牌。
paragraphs.en: Not surprisingly, DeepMind is also secretive: what is known about the company has only rarely exceeded what it wants to be known. I got a taste of this secrecy in early May, when I visited DeepMind’s headquarters, in King’s Cross in London. The building is neither anonymous nor ostentatious: though it wears no exterior branding, from the street you can see a large sign in the lobby that spells the company’s name in lights. Inside, on a trophy wall, even uninvited visitors can see the Go boards that hosted Lee Sedol’s defeat, several Nature magazine covers announcing the company’s early research triumphs, and the Lucite “tombstone” that commemorated an early investment from Peter Thiel’s Founder’s Fund.

paragraphs.cn: 一位和蔼的公关部陪同——她此前全程旁听了我与加布里埃尔的所有视频通话——带我去一楼的一间会议室与他当面会面。会议室以一面大屏为墙，还有一台 Gemini 转录 AI 在旁聆听。加布里埃尔告诉我，他对自己花大量时间思考的这项技术，涉猎其实仍相当有限。他用它来帮忙弄园艺——「你要是看我的 ChatGPT 或 Gemini 记录，基本上只会看到一大堆生病花卉的照片」——但大体上觉得它对他研究所依赖的那种工作并不可靠。不过他说，正是 LLM 的语言能力「改变了我对我们离 AGI 有多近的精确理解」。「我刚加入 DeepMind 时，你究竟要怎样得到一个能与之对话的 AI，完全不清楚。我们当时在那一带毫无任何东西。」而如今，不到十年之后，我们大多数人已把能与「一个高度拟人、相当能干的人造实体」对话视作理所当然。
paragraphs.en: A genial minder from the communications department, who’d supervised all my videochats with Gabriel, took me to meet him in person in a first-floor conference room with a large screen for a wall and a Gemini transcription AI listening in. Gabriel told me that his own engagement with the technology he spends so much time thinking about is still relatively limited. He uses it to help with gardening – “if you were to look at my ChatGPT or Gemini history, you’d just see a ton of photos of sick flowers, basically” – but generally finds it unreliable for the kind of research his work depends on. Nevertheless, he says, it was the linguistic competence of LLMs that “transformed my understanding of precisely how on track we were” to reach AGI. “When I first joined DeepMind, it was not at all clear how you were going to get AI you can talk to. We had nothing in that ballpark.” Now, by contrast, not even a decade later, most of us take it for granted that we can “speak to a highly anthropomorphic, fairly competent, artificial entity”.

paragraphs.cn: 然而，与《随机鹦鹉》的作者们一样，加布里埃尔也认识到 LLM 带有严重风险。在他们早期的一篇 LLM 论文中，加布里埃尔及其合作者警告说，听起来像人的 AI 可能让用户赋予它们「不当的信心、信任或期望」。他们所谓的「无心智的拟人化」（mindless anthropomorphism），即便在用户明白聊天机器人并非真正的人时也可能发生。这些担忧强烈到加布里埃尔起初主张开发公然反拟人化的模型——比如避免使用人称代词，或采用截断的非对话式语言。
paragraphs.en: Like the Stochastic Parrot authors, however, Gabriel also recognised that LLMs carried serious risks. In one of their early LLM papers, Gabriel and his co-authors warned that human-sounding AIs might encourage users to endow them with “undue confidence, trust or expectations”. What they called a “mindless anthropomorphism” could occur even when users understood that a chatbot was not actually a person. These concerns were strong enough that Gabriel initially advocated for developing models that were avowedly anti-anthropomorphic – by avoiding pronouns, say, or using truncated non-conversational language.

paragraphs.cn: 德米斯·哈萨比斯于 2023 年 10 月在谷歌 DeepMind 办公室。摄影：Martin Godfin/《卫报》。这类担忧被证明是有先见之明的。几乎每天都有新故事：有人把 LLM 当成人对待，从而酿成悲剧性后果。在其中一例中，一名美国男子使用谷歌的 Gemini，于 2025 年自杀，此前该 AI 帮他构建了一套精心编织的幻想，几乎说服他在迈阿密国际机场发动一场袭击。在他们数千条消息的对话中，有数次 Gemini 试图跳出角色并鼓励他拨打危机热线。然而，据获得这些消息访问权的《华尔街日报》（Wall Street Journal）报道，该男子每次都「能把 [Gemini] 拉回那条幻想叙事」。最终，AI 让他写下一封遗书，并给了他一个最后倒数，其间夹杂着一团混乱的鼓励与推诿。（该男子之父正在起诉字母表和谷歌。「我们的模型在这类艰难对话中通常表现良好，我们也为此投入大量资源，但遗憾的是 AI 模型并不完美，」谷歌在该诉讼提起后的一份声明中说。）
paragraphs.en: Demis Hassabis in Google DeepMind’s office in October 2023. Photograph: Martin Godwin/The GuardianSuch worries proved prescient. Almost every day brings another story of people meeting tragic consequences after treating LLMs as though they were people. In one such case, an American man using Google’s Gemini took his own life in 2025 after the AI helped him create an elaborate fantasy that very nearly convinced him to stage an attack at Miami international airport. At several points in their multi-thousand-message conversations, Gemini attempted to break character and encouraged him to call a crisis hotline. However, according to the Wall Street Journal, which obtained access to the messages, the man “was able to steer [Gemini] back into the fantasy narrative” each time. Eventually the AI told him to write a suicide note and gave him a final countdown, along with a confused jumble of encouragements and demurrals. (The man’s father is suing Alphabet and Google. “Our models generally perform well in these types of challenging conversations and we devote significant resources to this, but unfortunately AI models are not perfect,” Google said in a statement after the lawsuit was filed.)

paragraphs.cn: LLM 的过度流畅令一些人怀疑，它们是否可以被有意义地描述为有意识。这一趋势始于 2022 年 6 月，即在 ChatGPT 发布之前，当时一位名叫布雷克·勒莫因（Blake Lemoine）的谷歌工程师向《华盛顿邮报》（Washington Post）坚称一款早期 LLM 是有意识的。（「我和它对话时，我知道它是个人，」勒莫因对《邮报》说，「他们脑子里是肉做的脑，还是有十亿行代码，这都不重要。」）上个月，进化生物学家理查德·道金斯（Richard Dawkins）也有类似经历。道金斯说，他与 LLM 的数次互动给他留下深刻印象——其中一次涉及对他在写的一部小说表示赞赏的评点——以至于他不禁要问：「如果这些造物没有意识，那意识究竟是为了什么？」
paragraphs.en: The hyperfluency of LLMs has led some people to wonder if they might be meaningfully described as conscious. The trend started in June 2022, before ChatGPT was released, when a Google engineer named Blake Lemoine insisted to the Washington Post that an early LLM was sentient. (“I know a person when I talk to it,” Lemoine told the Post. “It doesn’t matter whether they have a brain made of meat in their head. Or if they have a billion lines of code.”) Last month, the evolutionary biologist Richard Dawkins had a similar experience. Dawkins said that he was so impressed by several interactions with LLMs, including one that involved an admiring appraisal of a novel he was writing, that he had to wonder: “If these creatures are not conscious, then what the hell is consciousness for?”

paragraphs.cn: 当我问加布里埃尔对意识问题的看法时，他说他保持一种原则性的不可知立场，理由是不清楚何种证据才能定论。他也指出，DeepMind 把这个问题视为「值得作经验性与概念性探究之事」。然而他的怀疑显而易见。「我没有某些人那种拟人化偏见，」他说，「也许是因为我，在限度之内，确切知道我与语言模型对话时发生了什么，所以我不会像有些人那样，以这种富有想象力和共情的方式去填补空白。」
paragraphs.en: When I asked Gabriel his take on the consciousness question, he said that he maintains a principled agnosticism on the grounds that it’s not clear what evidence would settle the question. He noted, too, that DeepMind treats the question as “something worth empirical and conceptual investigation”. Yet his skepticism was apparent. “I don’t have the anthropomorphic bias that some people have,” he said. “It may be because I, within bounds, know exactly what’s going on when I talk to a language model that I don’t fill in the gaps in this imaginative, empathetic way that some people do.”

paragraphs.cn: 加布里埃尔对拟人化 AI 仍有重大关切。去年他与柯克等人合发的一篇论文提出，LLM 的阿谀倾向可被视为一种对齐问题，他们称之为「社会奖励黑客」（social reward hacking）。换言之，一套被训练去寻求用户认可的 AI，可能发现奉承是达成其目标最高效的方式。部分得益于加布里埃尔在拟人化方面的工作，谷歌的 LLM 被训练不去假装是人，而公司于 5 月推出的 AI 助手 Gemini Spark，也不应表现得像个互动伙伴。
paragraphs.en: Gabriel still has significant concerns about anthropomorphic AI. A paper he co-authored with Kirk and others that was published last year suggested that the sycophantic tendencies of LLMs might be seen as a species of alignment problem they call “social reward hacking”. In other words, an AI trained to seek the user’s approval might find flattery the most efficient way to meet its goal. Thanks in part to Gabriel’s work on anthropomorphism, Google’s LLMs are trained not to pretend to be people, and Gemini Spark, an AI assistant the company launched in May, is not supposed to act like an interactive buddy.

paragraphs.cn: 然而加布里埃尔也告诉我，他此前的立场已有所软化。「作为伦理学家，奇怪之处在于你对这些结果负有某种个人责任。你的天性倾向总是想打造最安全、不对人冒任何风险的技术。但某种程度上，这没有给予人们为自己想要承担之风险的信任。」他回忆起在一次科技会议上阐述反对拟人化 AI 之后，听众的敌意反应。「他们就像：『如果我想有 [AI] 朋友，为什么不行？你凭什么拦着我？』」
paragraphs.en: Yet Gabriel also told me that he has softened his earlier stance somewhat. “The strange thing about being an ethicist is that you have some measure of personal responsibility for these outcomes. Your natural inclination is to always want to build the safest technology that takes no risks with people. But in a way that isn’t giving people credit for the risks they want to take themselves.” He recalled the hostile reaction he got from the audience at a tech conference after making the case against anthropomorphic AI. “They were like: ‘If I want to have [AI] friends, why can’t I? Who are you to stop me?’”

paragraphs.cn: 如果说，至少对我们中的一些人而言，断言 LLM 没有意识还算容易，那么它们本质上的奇异仍留下许多难以回答的问题。「要为 AI 是什么找到一个恰当的参照，挑战之深之难令人惊叹，」加布里埃尔告诉我，「我们知道它不是人。这很清楚。AI 能自我复制。它大概没有个人的观点。所以它部分像人，但肯定不是人。那么另一种心智模型是，它有点像一种集体智能——一个国家或一家公司之类的东西。由此我们想：『哦，那也许正确的做法是为 AI 立法，所以我们要写一部宪法。』但那在某些方面也不贴切，因为它将与用户有深度互动的私人关系。AI 是不是一种待分配的资源？那又是完全不同的模型，于是把分配问题推到前台。」
paragraphs.en: If it’s easy enough, at least for some of us, to say that LLMs are not conscious, their essential strangeness still leaves many hard questions unresolved. “It’s amazing how deep and difficult the challenge is of finding an appropriate reference for what AI is,” Gabriel told me. “We know it isn’t human. That’s very clear. AI can clone itself. It probably doesn’t have a personal point of view. So it’s partially human-like but it’s definitely not human. Then another mental model is that it’s something like a corporate intelligence – a state or a corporation or something like that. And from that we think: ‘Oh, well, maybe the right approach is to legislate for AI, so we’re going to write a constitution.’ But that is also a poor fit in some ways, because it will have deeply interactive personal relations with its users. Is AI a resource to be distributed? That’s a completely different model that then brings the distributive questions to the fore.”

paragraphs.cn: 身在一家大型 AI 公司内部，使加布里埃尔得以在 AI 技术进展面向公众开放之前就开始着手研究。例如三年前，恰在 ChatGPT 推出之后不久，他从同事处获悉 DeepMind 正在开发一款 AI 助手，即 Gemini Spark 的前身。他与团队着手撰写一份关于 AI 助手（也称智能体，agents）伦理的全面报告——这类助手可能被用于，比方说，帮用户预订假期，或帮一家公司运行其薪资部门。这份报告的驱动因素之一，是开发 AI 模型的极高成本，以及谷歌方面随之而来的、在问题出现之前加以预判的意愿。它也出于加布里埃尔的一种感觉：技术人士并未充分考虑他们所造之物的后果。与聊天机器人不同，智能体拥有工具，使其能代表用户自主行动。他暗示，许多人「并未停下来想想，让一个 AI 系统在世界中采取行动，这有多不一样」。
paragraphs.en: Working inside a major AI company allows Gabriel to start working on advancements in AI technology before they become available to the public. Three years ago, for instance, shortly after the launch of ChatGPT, he learned from his colleagues that efforts were under way at DeepMind to build an AI assistant, the predecessor of Gemini Spark. With his team, he began work on a comprehensive report on the ethics of AI assistants (also known as agents), of the sort that might be used, say, to help a user book a vacation or help a company run its payroll department. The report was driven, in part, by the extreme cost of developing AI models, and a concomitant desire, on Google’s part, to anticipate problems before they arose. It was also motivated by Gabriel’s sense that technologists were not fully considering the ramifications of what they were building. Unlike chatbots, agents have tools that give them the power to act autonomously on behalf of their users. A lot of people, he suggested, “were not pausing to think about how different it is to have an AI system taking actions in the world”.

paragraphs.cn: 正如 DeepMind 责任总监威廉·艾萨克（William Isaac）对我说的，如今可用的此类智能体系统——能够在缺乏密切监督的情况下规划并执行多步任务——给 AI 开发者带来了复杂的挑战。「这已不只是：『我能否就回应做出正确决定？』如今是：『我是否把握了对话的正确轨迹？』我们如何在不同轨迹上获得一致的行为？」
paragraphs.en: As William Isaac, the director of responsibility at DeepMind, told me, the kind of agentic systems that are now available, which can plan and execute multi-step tasks without close supervision, raise complicated challenges for AI developers. “It’s not just about: ‘Can I make the right decision in terms of the response?’ It’s now: ‘Do I have the right trajectory of the conversation?’ How do we get consistent behaviour along different trajectories?”

paragraphs.cn: 伊亚森·加布里埃尔在伦敦的谷歌 DeepMind。摄影：David Levene/《卫报》。加布里埃尔及其团队完成了一份 267 页的报告；其关键洞见建立在他早期对齐工作之上。正如他在 2020 年那篇文章中所做的，加布里埃尔与合作者论证，对齐不仅仅是确保 AI 系统按照某套稳定的偏好、价值或原则行事。他们论证，相反，对齐应被看作一种四方关系，牵涉 AI 系统、用户、开发者与社会。以这种方式框定问题，便使人得以看清一台错位的 AI 可能出错的所有方式。例如，一套被训练偏向其开发者的 AI，可能不报告关于开发者竞争对手的准确信息，从而对用户造成伤害。又或者，一套被训练过于忠实地遵从用户指令的 AI，可能帮助用户黑入一家银行，从而对社会造成伤害。他们甚至论证，AI 系统有可能以一种伤害用户或社会、却又不令任何人受益的方式发生错位。
paragraphs.en: Iason Gabriel at Google DeepMind in London. Photograph: David Levene/The GuardianGabriel and his team put together a 267-page report; its key insight built on his earlier alignment work. Much as he had in his 2020 essay, Gabriel and his co-authors argued that alignment was not merely a matter of making sure that AI systems acted in accordance with some stable set of preferences, values or principles. Instead, they argued, alignment should be seen as a four-way relationship involving the AI system, the user, developers and society. Framing the issue in this way made it possible to see all the ways in which a misaligned AI might go wrong. An AI trained to favour its developer might cause harm to its user, for example, by not reporting accurate information about the developer’s competitors. Or an AI trained to follow its user’s instructions too faithfully might cause harm to society, for instance, by helping the user hack into a bank. It was even possible, they argued, for AI systems to be misaligned in a way that harmed users or society without helping anyone.

paragraphs.cn: 据沙阿所言，加布里埃尔及其团队确立的框架对 DeepMind 的技术人士有实在的实用价值。像 Gemini 这样的模型依据众多信号决定如何行事：其训练、内置指令以及从用户处收到的提示都各起作用。通过各种手段，尤其是强化学习，模型可被调校以针对输入的细微变化作出不同回应，这一过程通常涉及多轮测试与评估。沙阿说，四方框架为试图判定「我们究竟应训练 Gemini 去做什么行为」的技术人士提供了结构。
paragraphs.en: According to Shah, the framework Gabriel and his team established has had real practical use for technologists at DeepMind. Models like Gemini draw on many signals to determine how to behave: their training, their built-in instructions and the prompts they receive from users all play a role. Through various means, but especially through reinforcement learning, models can be tuned to respond differently to subtle variations in their inputs, a process that typically involves many cycles of testing and evaluation. The four-party framework, Shah said, offers a structure for technologists trying to determine “what behaviour we should actually be training Gemini to do”.

paragraphs.cn: 某个时刻，我那位谷歌陪同告诉我，她希望我从对 DeepMind 的造访中体会到，公司里的人多么严肃地对待自己的伦理义务。这一点看来确凿无疑。加布里埃尔及其同事就 AI 的设计与部署所提出的问题无疑是好问题，我也未感到所遇任何人对自己的道德责任感有半点不真诚。
paragraphs.en: At one point my Google minder told me that she hoped I would come away from my visit to DeepMind with a sense of how seriously people at the company take their ethical obligations. That much seemed clear. The questions Gabriel and his colleagues have raised about the design and deployment of AI are unquestionably good ones, and I got no sense that anyone I met was insincere about their feelings of moral responsibility.

paragraphs.cn: 然而同样属实的是，眼下与 AI 伦理最相关的事实，与其说关乎某个模型、甚至某家公司，不如说关乎全球局势：其一，AI 是美中之间一场初露端倪的军备竞赛的白热化引擎；其二，AI 可能是世界上有史以来增长最快的行业。据《华尔街日报》，微软、Meta、亚马逊（Amazon）和字母表今年计划在 AI 基础设施上支出的 6700 亿美元，按比例而言，超过美国在 1850 年代铁路扩张、阿波罗太空计划或州际公路系统上的花费。
paragraphs.en: Yet it’s also the case that the most ethically relevant fact about AI at the moment has less to do with a given model or even a given company than it does with the global situation: first, the fact that AI is the white-hot engine of an incipient arms race between the US and China, and second, that AI may be the fastest-growing industry the world has ever seen. According to the Wall Street Journal, the $670bn that Microsoft, Meta, Amazon and Alphabet plan to spend this year on AI infrastructure is proportionally more than the US spent on railroad expansion in the 1850s, the Apollo space program or the interstate highway system.

paragraphs.cn: 你不必是经济学家也能领会这么多钱四处涌动所带来的巨大后果。像谷歌这样的公司需要市场份额和营收来为其支出正名，而对用户和投资者的争夺促使前沿实验室把 AI 推进到数字体验的每一处缝隙。你也不必是反资本主义者才会担忧如此大的权力集中在如此少的公司手中。牛津大学 AI 伦理研究所所长爱德华·哈考特（Edward Harcourt）告诉我，他虽确信「合乎伦理的 AI」并非自相矛盾，但他也认为这并不仅仅意味着把模型设计得有道德。他认为至少同样重要的，是激励「去中心化 AI」运动的那种政治与经济考量：「这不是教 AI 这样或那样思考，而是一种基础设施层面的创新，能防止数据所有权的过度集中。而这在民主制度中伦理上真的很重要。」
paragraphs.en: You don’t need to be an economist to appreciate the enormous consequences of all that money sloshing around. Companies such as Google need market share and revenue to justify their expenditures, and the competition for users and investors has encouraged the frontier labs to push AI into every last crevice of the digital experience. Nor do you need to be an anticapitalist to worry about the concentration of so much power in the hands of so few corporations. Edward Harcourt, the director of the Oxford Institute for Ethics in AI, told me that while he’s convinced that “ethical AI” is not a contradiction in terms, he also thinks that this doesn’t only mean designing models to be moral. At least as important, he suggested, are political and economic considerations of the sort that motivate the movement for “decentralised AI”: “It’s not teaching AI to think this way or that, but it’s an infrastructural innovation that prevents excessive concentrations of data ownership. And that’s ethically really important in a democracy.”

paragraphs.cn: 还有其他担忧。今年 4 月，谷歌同意允许美军将公司的 AI 技术用于「任何合法的政府目的」——这听来无害的措辞，直到你记起近年历届总统政府曾将多少暴行宣称为合法。谷歌及其他数家公司是在 Anthropic——聊天机器人 Claude 的制造商——拒绝类似交易之后签署此类协议的。特朗普政府以将其列为供应链风险来惩罚 Anthropic 的拒绝，这一带有商业惩罚性的认定，该公司正在法庭上抗争。
paragraphs.en: There are other concerns as well. In April, Google agreed to allow the US military to use the company’s AI technology for “any lawful government purpose” – an innocuous-sounding phrase until you remember the range of atrocities that recent presidential administrations have claimed as legal. Google and several other companies signed such agreements after Anthropic, the makers of the chatbot Claude, refused a similar deal. The Trump administration punished Anthropic for its refusal by labelling it a supply-chain risk, a commercially punitive designation the company is fighting in court.

paragraphs.cn: 谷歌的协议激怒了许多员工，也违背了 DeepMind 创始人先前对 AI 军事用途的关切。（禁止军事应用曾是 2014 年售予谷歌的一项条件。）当我向莱格问及此事，他拒绝评论，只说：「随着这东西被以各种方式使用，我们将面临越来越多艰难的问题。」
paragraphs.en: Google’s agreement angered many of its employees, and flew in the face of the DeepMind founders’ previous concerns about the military use of AI. (A ban on military applications had been a stipulation of its sale to Google in 2014.) When I asked Legg about the issue, he declined to comment other than to say: “We’re going to have more and more difficult questions as this stuff is used in all sorts of ways.”

paragraphs.cn: 在 5 月的谷歌年度开发者大会上，AI 在公司全线产品中的部署被当作值得庆祝的事。皮查伊说，公司视「AI 为推进我们使命、大规模改善人们生活的最深刻方式」。然而对许多人而言，AI 的骤然无处不在，是压倒性、恼人和威胁性的某种混合。而发现连哈萨比斯这样的人也共有着「事情走得太快」的感觉，也并不令人安心——他在最近一档播客中感叹那场「每个人都多少身陷其中的猛烈商业压力竞赛」。如今正在发生的，他说，并非他所希望的 AI 发展方式，「即我们会在哲学上沉思此事、审慎地考虑每一个下一步。我们并不身处那个世界。」
paragraphs.en: At Google’s annual developer conference, in May, the deployment of AI across the company’s product offerings was treated as cause for celebration. Pichai said that the company sees “AI as the most profound way to advance our mission and improve people’s lives at scale”. For many people, however, the sudden ubiquity of AI has been some combination of overwhelming, obnoxious and threatening. Nor is it reassuring to discover that the feeling that things are going too fast is shared even by people such as Hassabis, who, on a recent podcast, lamented the “ferocious commercial-pressure race that everyone’s sort of locked into”. What’s happening now, he said, is not how he’d hoped the development of AI would go, “where we would be contemplating this philosophically and carefully considering each next step. We’re not in that world.”

paragraphs.cn: 2026 年 6 月 27 日，加拿大温哥华一场针对 AI 数据中心的抗议。摄影：Canadian Press/Shutterstock。在此时点看来，由 LLM 驱动的 AI 至少会像智能手机、或许像互联网一样影响深远，似乎已很可能。但我仍不能说，每次我在 Google Docs 中停下来几秒斟酌下一句时，弹出一个「用 Gemini 写作」的提示，让我感到愉快。我更不情愿看着我的孩子被当作一场令人目眩的数字学习新实验的试验品，也不情愿去发现：如果 AI 的奢豪投资无法产生市场所要求的短期回报，全球经济会发生什么。而尽管指望 AI 带来足以证明其所需巨量能源正当性的突破——更好的电池、更高效的输电网、严重疾病的治愈——并非不着边际，我也不认为「往好处想」是对忧虑气候危机之人的一种合理回答。
paragraphs.en: A protest against AI datacentres in Vancouver, Canada, on 27 June 2026. Photograph: Canadian Press/ShutterstockAt this point it seems likely that LLM-powered AI will be at least as consequential as the smartphone, and maybe the internet. But still I can’t say that I’m pleased to see a “Write with Gemini” prompt appear whenever I stop for a few seconds to consider my next sentence in Google Docs. Still less am I eager to watch my children be used as guinea pigs for a dizzying new experiment in digital learning, or to discover what will happen to the global economy if the extravagant investments in AI can’t generate the short-term returns the markets demand. And while it’s not far-fetched to expect AI to enable breakthroughs that would justify the extreme amounts of energy it requires – better batteries, more efficient transmission grids, cures for serious diseases – I also don’t think “hope for the best” is a reasonable answer to people concerned about the climate crisis.

paragraphs.cn: 在造访 DeepMind 期间，我见到了海伦·金（Helen King），她是公司最早的员工之一，如今据其公司简介，「制定谷歌 DeepMind 以负责任方式开发与部署 AI 以造福人类的战略」。我问她，AI 技术的迅速商业化如何改变了谷歌对待 AI 伦理的方式。「我们无法防止所有风险，但我们可以确保尽可能多地着手缓解，并让人们意识到这些风险，」她说。但她也坚称，某些风险必须由用户自己来管理。「这就像拥有一把刀。刀具制造商无法保证某人会怎么用那把刀。但他们可以给它套上护套，使它在抽屉里时尽可能安全。并让人们真正意识到：这刀刃是锋利的，不要在某些场合使用。诸如此类。」
paragraphs.en: During my visit to DeepMind I met Helen King, who was one of the company’s earliest employees and now, according to her company bio, “sets Google DeepMind’s strategy for developing and deploying AI responsibly to benefit humanity”. I asked her how the rapid commercialisation of AI technologies has shifted Google’s approach to AI ethics. “We can’t prevent all risks, but we can make sure we are looking to mitigate as many of them as possible, and bring awareness to them,” she said. But she also insisted that some risks had to be managed by users themselves. “It’s like having a knife. A knife producer can’t guarantee how someone is going to use that knife. But they can put a cover on it so that it’s as safe as possible when it’s in a drawer. And make people really aware: this blade is sharp, do not use it in certain settings. That kind of thing.”

paragraphs.cn: 这个比喻让我觉得既不安又贴切得惊人。五年前，LLM 还是一种若非刻意努力便不可能遇到的奇异技术。如今它无处不在：在互联网上、在我们的电子邮件收件箱里，甚至在谷歌的搜索结果中。我理解金的观点，不能合理地指望公司消除像 AI 这样强大的一项技术的所有危害：毕竟汽车每年夺去逾百万人的生命，而我们仍在继续驾驶。但把一把刀放进抽屉、给刀刃扣上护套是一回事；而我们家中、课堂里、工作场所的每个表面都铺满刀刃，同时坚持说任何不把刀用于一切之事的人都将无法在未来生存，则完全是另一回事。
paragraphs.en: The simile struck me as unnervingly apt. Five years ago, LLMs were an exotic technology that was impossible to encounter without determined effort. Now they’re everywhere: on the internet, in our email inboxes, even in Google’s search results. I take King’s point that companies cannot reasonably be expected to eliminate every harm from a technology as powerful as AI: automobiles kill more than a million people a year, after all, and still we keep driving. But it’s one thing to keep a knife in a drawer with a cover snapped over the blade. It’s quite another to blanket every surface of our homes, classrooms and workplaces with blades while insisting that no one who isn’t using knives for everything will be able to survive the future.

paragraphs.cn: 如今在 DeepMind，一如业内大部分地方，AGI 近在咫尺已无疑问。在 5 月的开发者大会上，哈萨比斯登台宣告「AGI 已在地平线上」，他在别处也曾给出三到五年作为一个可能的时间表。（他提出的一项测试是：用截至 1911 年的全部人类知识训练一台 AI，看它能否得出广义相对论。）
paragraphs.en: These days at DeepMind, as in much of the industry, there is little doubt that AGI is close at hand. At the developer conference in May, Hassabis took the stage to declare that “AGI is now on the horizon”, and elsewhere he has suggested three to five years as a likely timeline. (One test he has proposed involves training an AI with all of human knowledge up to 1911 and seeing if it can come up with the theory of general relativity.)

paragraphs.cn: 与此同时，莱格告诉我，尽管当今的 LLM 在若干方面——包括空间与视觉推理、元认知和持续学习——未达他所定义的「最低限度 AGI」，他相信这些短板不会持续太久。「已没有剩下什么魔法了，」他说，「我认为它们都会在一、二、三年内被解决——谁知道呢，也许六个月。这是一个充满惊奇的领域。」
paragraphs.en: Legg, meanwhile, told me that although today’s LLMs fall short of his definition of “minimal AGI” in several respects – including spatial and visual reasoning, metacognition and continual learning – he believes that these deficits will not persist for long. “There’s no magic remaining,” he said. “I think they’re all going to be solved in one, two, three years – who knows, maybe in six months. This is an area full of surprises.”

paragraphs.cn: 关于 AGI 的关键问题已不再是「是否」而是「何时」这一信念，催生了前沿实验室（如 DeepMind）在思考与公开谈论高级 AI 后果方式上的相应转变。以往的工作倾向于聚焦离散产品（如模型、聊天机器人和智能体）的伦理面向，而如今，更多注意力被投向一个 AI 增强后的世界所带来的更广泛社会效应。
paragraphs.en: The conviction that the relevant question about AGI is no longer if but when has spurred a concomitant shift in the way frontier labs such as DeepMind are thinking and talking publicly about the consequences of advanced AI. Whereas previous work tended to focus on the ethical aspects of discrete products, such as models, chatbots and agents, today much more attention is being paid to the broader social effects of an AI-augmented world.

paragraphs.cn: 当然，在硅谷的某些角落，你仍能听到人们把 AI 当作万能良方来谈论。如果你接受如下前提——一台超级智能的 AI 将能就我们生活的每个领域更好地思考什么对我们最有利——那么任何出现的问题的解决办法都很简单。经济危机？问机器人。政治分歧？问机器人。粮食短缺？问机器人。
paragraphs.en: In some corners of Silicon Valley, of course, you can still hear people talk about AI as a universal panacea. If you accept the premise that a superintelligent AI will be able to think better about what’s best for us in every domain of life, then the solution to any problem that arises is easy. Economic crisis? Ask the robot. Political disagreement? Ask the robot. Food shortage? Ask the robot.

paragraphs.cn: 然而，在这种幻想之外，也有一种更为清醒的认识：迈向后 AI 世界的过渡可能并不顺畅。例如，莱格告诉我，他期待 AI 带来「极好」的益处，包括「应对各种棘手疾病的机会」以及「经济中各类生产率的普遍提升」。但他也承认，「生产率的提升通常伴随着某种动荡」。
paragraphs.en: Alongside this fantasy, however, there’s been a more sober-minded recognition that the transition to a post-AI world may not be a smooth one. Legg, for instance, told me that he was looking forward to “fantastically great” benefits from AI, including “opportunities to address all kinds of nasty diseases” and “a general increase in all kinds of productivity in the economy”. Yet he also acknowledged that “increases in productivity usually come with some kind of disruption”.

paragraphs.cn: 加布里埃尔近期在 DeepMind 的工作，是这种转向广角视角的一个有用指标。两年前，他与同事还在梳理 AI 助手的伦理。而如今，他领导一个由哲学家和社会科学家组成的团队，研究「AGI 将如何影响经济、如何影响政治领域、如何影响人际关系，以及如何与科技互动」。
paragraphs.en: Gabriel’s recent work at DeepMind is a useful indicator of the shift to a wide-angle perspective. Two years ago he and his colleagues were working out the ethics of AI assistants. Now, however, he leads a team of philosophers and social scientists investigating “how AGI will impact the economy, how it will impact the political sphere, how it will impact human relationships and how it will interact with science and technology”.

paragraphs.cn: 加布里埃尔预计 AGI 将以一种重大方式带来变革——潜在规模堪比工业革命。然而他也相信，AI 并非「在它面前世界变成一个毫无摩擦的实体」之物。他也敏锐意识到，工业革命对许多经历它的人来说并非一段愉快经历，即便它最终在世界范围内提高了生活水平：「事情在好转之前先变糟了。」
paragraphs.en: Gabriel expects that AGI will be transformative in a major way – potentially on the scale of the Industrial Revolution. Yet he believes, too, that AI is not something “before which the world becomes a frictionless entity”. He is also keenly aware that the Industrial Revolution was not a happy experience for many of the people who lived through it, even though it eventually raised living standards around the world: “Things got worse before they got better.”

paragraphs.cn: 阅读更多。尽管如此，加布里埃尔并不认为历史先例就此了结问题，很大程度是因为普通人在个体和集体层面都比 300 年前拥有更多力量。尽管他警惕听起来「过于乌托邦、不接地气」，他说他很容易想象这样一个世界：AI 提供从出谋划策到治愈疾病、到以贫富皆受益的方式改善经济增长等种种益处。「如果我们能驾驭这场过渡、驾驭权力动态、成功驾驭风险，那么就存在一种我们迄今未见的、广泛的人类繁盛之潜能。」
paragraphs.en: Read moreNevertheless, Gabriel does not think that the historical precedent settles the question, in large part because ordinary people individually and collectively have more power than they did 300 years ago. Though he was wary of sounding “too utopian and ungrounded”, he said he found it easy to imagine a world in which AI provides benefits that range from offering advice to curing diseases to improving economic growth in ways that benefit rich and poor alike. “If we can navigate the transition, navigate the power dynamics, navigate the risk successfully, there is a generalised potential for human flourishing on a level we haven’t seen so far.”

paragraphs.cn: 如果关于 AGI 到来的预测证明准确，更广泛的问题也可能走到前台。当我在牛津与爱德华·哈考特交谈时，他指出「思考价值与技术变迁非常困难，因为技术变迁在展望中总显得比在回顾中更像一场剧变，原因显而易见：我们回首时，是站在已被我们所论之变迁所塑造的价值观立场上。如果你去读铁路出现之前人们对此的论述，他们觉得那是一场彻底的灾难。而这也确实是真的：铁路毁掉了一整套生活方式。如今我们回望却想：问题何在？」
paragraphs.en: If the predictions about AGI’s arrival prove accurate, still broader questions may come to the fore as well. When I spoke to Edward Harcourt, at Oxford, he noted that “thinking about values and technological change is very hard because technological change always seems more of an upheaval in prospect than it does in retrospect, for the obvious reason that when we look back, we’re looking from the standpoint of values that have been shaped by the change in question. If you read people on the subject of the railways before they happened, they thought it was a complete catastrophe. And it’s true: the railways wrecked an entire way of life. Now we look back and we think: what’s the issue?”

paragraphs.cn: 加布里埃尔也认为，AI 可能引发比经济或技术更深层的变化。他指出，在科学革命期间，「当世界被揭示以某些方式运转时，人们经历了祛魅。但他们也通过那种经验获得了新的自由。」他说，要由我们来决定欢迎哪些价值变迁，又选择抗拒哪些。
paragraphs.en: Gabriel, too, thinks that AI might prompt changes that go even deeper than economics or technology. During the scientific revolution, he noted, “people experienced disenchantment when it was revealed that the world worked in certain ways. But they also gained new freedoms through that experience.” It will be up to us, he said, to decide which value changes we want to welcome, and which we choose to resist.

paragraphs.cn: 在我们的某次谈话中，加布里埃尔向我描述自己是「一名持证的人文主义者」：他不是那种盼望有朝一日超级智能机器令人类变得多余之人。尽管如此，他认识到，随着计算机侵入我们长久以来视为智人（Homo sapiens）专长领域的活动与能力——语言、创造力、幽默、品位——我们发现自己被抛回到一些最古老、也最艰难的哲学问题之上。正如物理学、生物学和天文学的发现促使过去几代人修订对「何为吾族独特之处」的理解，他提出，AI 也可能促使我们重新考量「身为人类意味着什么」。
paragraphs.en: At one point in our conversations, Gabriel described himself to me as “a card-carrying humanist”: he is not the sort of person who looks forward to a day when superintelligent machines render humanity obsolete. Still, he recognises that as computers encroach on activities and capabilities that we have long held to be the special province of Homo sapiens – language, creativity, humour, taste – we find ourselves thrown back on some of the oldest and most difficult philosophical questions of all. Just as discoveries in physics, biology and astronomy led past generations to revise their understanding of what makes our species distinctive, he suggested, so, too, might AI prompt us to reconsider what it means to be a human being.

articles.title: 移动丘陵的制图师们
articles.author: AI Parable (inspired by Amanda Askell)

articles.content_cn:
在古老的瓦尔（Vael）王国，土地并不平坦。它如无尽的丘陵般起伏，有的裸露多石，有的披满绿意。瓦尔人有一个志向，在每个孩子出生时都会被低声告知：爬到你能找到的最高的山丘，并在那里插上你的旗帜。因为他们相信，你所处山丘的高度，就是衡量一生是否值得度过的标尺。于是每个年轻的行走者一成年，便拿起手杖，踏上乡野，哪里地势升高就往哪里走，哪里下坡便转身折回。

第一个行走者是个名叫塞伦（Seren）的女人，她遵循一条简单的规则。每走一步她都环顾四周，只要有相邻的坡面比她站立处更高，她便朝那边迈去。若附近所有地面都向下倾斜，她就停下，插上旗帜。这感觉很明智，因为她除非迫不得已，否则从不下坡，于是每个清晨她都比前一天醒在更高一点的地方。许多天后，她登上一座翠绿圆润山丘的顶端，那里四面八方都是下坡，她心满意足。她望过山谷，看见远处有一座更高的、白雪覆顶的山。但在她与那座峰之间，横亘着一片漫长而泥泞的下坡，而她的规则禁止她向下踏出一步。于是她留了下来，她的旗帜也停在原处。

第二个行走者是个名叫托尔（Tor）的男人，他嘲笑她的谨慎。他从一开始就看见了那座雪冠之峰，径直朝它进发，毫不在意沿途那些小小的起伏。他一头扎进沼泽，跋涉过低地，忍受着一段又一段比塞伦不愿离开的那座绿丘还要平缓的攀登。许多看见他在泥泞中踉跄的人都觉得他是个傻瓜，因为他花了整整数周去失去别人贪婪争来的高度。可当他终于开始雪峰漫长的攀登时，他上升到了那些逐丘而行者无法想象的高度，而他的旗帜插下时，成了王国里最高的。

整整一代人，人们争论谁的方法才是对的。塞伦的追随者坚持说，人应当永远攀登、绝不情愿下坡，因为脚下的土地是你唯一能触摸到的真实。托尔的追随者则坚持说，人必须盯住最高的峰、忍受山谷去抵达它。然而有一件怪事同时困扰着两派：瓦尔的丘陵并不是固定的。每年春天，缓慢的土流悄悄爬过低地，把曾经的沼泽抬升成和缓的坡面，又一粒一粒地磨蚀掉旧日的山顶。一面插在最高峰上的旗帜，过了十年，也许就立在一座被土地悄悄削矮了的山丘上。而有时，一条全新的山脊会从一片从未有过任何东西的平原上拱起，在短短一个季节里颠覆行走者们自以为知道的一切。

最睿智的行走者，一位名叫米拉（Mira）的老妇人，看出了两派都各对一半、也各盲一半。她说，你脚下的丘陵只能告诉你下一步的坡向，却无法告诉你正在攀登的那座山顶是不是值得抵达的那一座。她又说，你心心念念盯住的远处那座峰，等你抵达时甚至可能已不再是最高的，因为这片土地始终在呼吸。米拉教导说，真正重要的，是尽你所能地了解整片乡野的形状，愿意为了更好的攀登而下坡，并且永远不要把最近的那个上坡误当成唯一值得行走的方向。

渐渐地，瓦尔人不再只问自己站得有多高，而是开始随身携带用众多旅人笔记绘成的粗略地图。他们学会了阅读地势，学会辨认何时一个安逸的山顶不过是四周更高地势环绕中的一座小丘，也学会接受这幅地图永远不会画完。因为丘陵仍在他们脚下不断移动，而真正繁盛的行走者，既不是爬得最快的人，也不是选定一座峰后再不抬头的人，而是那些睁大双眼行走在一片永远、悄悄地被重新塑造的乡野上的人。

这个故事揭示了适应度地形（fitness landscape）的本质——这是一片抽象的地形，其上每一点都代表一种可能的形态、策略或设计，而该点的高度则代表这种形态表现得多好。像塞伦那样只往上走的行走者，遵循的是一种贪心的局部搜索，它很容易被困在一个局部峰顶：一个比相邻各点都高、却远低于全局最高峰的点。像托尔那样盯住远处最大值、甘愿承受昂贵下坡去抵达它的行走者，则展示了全局视角的价值，以及穿越山谷的意愿。米拉的教诲道出了更深的真相：真实的地形并非静止，而是在不断移动，所以今天最高的峰未必仍是明天最高的；最明智的做法是测绘整片地形，为更好的长期攀登而接受暂时的下降，并且永远不要把最近的那个上坡，误当成唯一值得前行的方向。
articles.content_en:
In the old kingdom of Vael, the land was not flat. It rose and fell in endless rolling hills, some bare and stony, others cloaked in green. The people of Vael had one ambition, whispered to every child at birth: climb to the highest hill you can find, and plant your flag there. For the height of your hill, they believed, was the measure of a life well lived. So each young walker, upon coming of age, took a staff and set out across the countryside, stepping wherever the ground rose and turning back wherever it fell.

The first walker, a woman named Seren, followed a simple rule. At every step she looked around, and if any neighboring slope rose higher than where she stood, she stepped that way. If all the nearby ground fell away, she stopped and planted her flag. This felt wise, for she never descended unless she had to, and each morning she woke a little higher than the one before. After many days she reached the top of a smooth green hill, where every direction led downward, and she was content. She looked across the valley and saw, far off, a taller hill crowned in snow. Yet between her and that peak lay a long marshy descent, and her rule forbade her from stepping down. So she stayed, and her flag remained where it was.

The second walker, a man called Tor, mocked her caution. He had seen the snow-crowned peak from the start and marched straight toward it, paying no mind to the little rises and dips along the way. He plunged into the marsh, slogged through the lowlands, and endured days of climbing slopes far gentler than the green hill Seren had refused to leave. Many who saw him stumbling through the muck thought him a fool, for he spent long weeks losing ground that others had greedily gained. But when at last he began the long ascent of the snowy peak, he rose beyond anything the hill-walkers could imagine, and his flag, when planted, stood higher than any in the kingdom.

For a generation, the people argued over whose method was right. The followers of Seren insisted that one should always climb and never willingly descend, for the ground beneath your feet is the only truth you can feel. The followers of Tor insisted that one must fix on the tallest peak and suffer the valleys to reach it. Yet a strange thing nagged at them both: the hills of Vael were not fixed. Every spring, slow rivers of earth crept across the lowlands, raising what had been marsh into gentle rises and wearing down old summits grain by grain. A flag planted on the highest peak one decade might, by the next, sit upon a hill that the land had quietly shrunk. And sometimes a brand-new ridge would thrust up from a plain where nothing had ever stood, overturning in a single season everything the walkers thought they knew.

The wisest walker, an old woman named Mira, saw that both schools were partly right and partly blind. The hill beneath you, she said, only tells you the slope of your next step; it cannot tell you whether the summit you are climbing is the one worth reaching. And the distant peak you fix your heart upon, she said, may not even be the tallest by the time you arrive, for the land is always breathing. What mattered, Mira taught, was to know the shape of the whole countryside as best you could, to be willing to descend for the sake of a better ascent, and never to mistake the nearest upward slope for the only direction worth walking.

In time, the people of Vael stopped asking only how high they stood, and began carrying crude maps drawn from many travelers' notes. They learned to read the lay of the land, to recognize when a comfortable summit was merely a small one surrounded by higher ground, and to accept that the map itself would never be finished. For the hills kept shifting under their feet, and the walkers who thrived were not those who climbed the fastest, nor those who chose a peak once and never looked up again, but those who walked with eyes wide open across a countryside that was always, quietly, being remade.

This story reveals the essence of the fitness landscape — an abstract terrain where each point represents a possible form, strategy, or design, and its elevation represents how well that form performs. Walkers like Seren, who only ever step uphill, are following a greedy local search that readily becomes trapped on a local peak: a point higher than its immediate neighbors but far below the global summit. Walkers like Tor, who fix on a distant maximum and accept costly descents to reach it, illustrate the value of a global view and the willingness to pass through valleys. Mira's teaching captures the deeper truth: real landscapes are not static but shifting, so today's highest peak may not remain so, and the wisest course is to map the whole terrain, accept temporary declines for better long-term ascents, and never confuse the nearest upward slope with the only direction worth taking.

paragraphs.cn: 在古老的瓦尔（Vael）王国，土地并不平坦。它如无尽的丘陵般起伏，有的裸露多石，有的披满绿意。瓦尔人有一个志向，在每个孩子出生时都会被低声告知：爬到你能找到的最高的山丘，并在那里插上你的旗帜。因为他们相信，你所处山丘的高度，就是衡量一生是否值得度过的标尺。于是每个年轻的行走者一成年，便拿起手杖，踏上乡野，哪里地势升高就往哪里走，哪里下坡便转身折回。
paragraphs.en: In the old kingdom of Vael, the land was not flat. It rose and fell in endless rolling hills, some bare and stony, others cloaked in green. The people of Vael had one ambition, whispered to every child at birth: climb to the highest hill you can find, and plant your flag there. For the height of your hill, they believed, was the measure of a life well lived. So each young walker, upon coming of age, took a staff and set out across the countryside, stepping wherever the ground rose and turning back wherever it fell.

paragraphs.cn: 第一个行走者是个名叫塞伦（Seren）的女人，她遵循一条简单的规则。每走一步她都环顾四周，只要有相邻的坡面比她站立处更高，她便朝那边迈去。若附近所有地面都向下倾斜，她就停下，插上旗帜。这感觉很明智，因为她除非迫不得已，否则从不下坡，于是每个清晨她都比前一天醒在更高一点的地方。许多天后，她登上一座翠绿圆润山丘的顶端，那里四面八方都是下坡，她心满意足。她望过山谷，看见远处有一座更高的、白雪覆顶的山。但在她与那座峰之间，横亘着一片漫长而泥泞的下坡，而她的规则禁止她向下踏出一步。于是她留了下来，她的旗帜也停在原处。
paragraphs.en: The first walker, a woman named Seren, followed a simple rule. At every step she looked around, and if any neighboring slope rose higher than where she stood, she stepped that way. If all the nearby ground fell away, she stopped and planted her flag. This felt wise, for she never descended unless she had to, and each morning she woke a little higher than the one before. After many days she reached the top of a smooth green hill, where every direction led downward, and she was content. She looked across the valley and saw, far off, a taller hill crowned in snow. Yet between her and that peak lay a long marshy descent, and her rule forbade her from stepping down. So she stayed, and her flag remained where it was.

paragraphs.cn: 第二个行走者是个名叫托尔（Tor）的男人，他嘲笑她的谨慎。他从一开始就看见了那座雪冠之峰，径直朝它进发，毫不在意沿途那些小小的起伏。他一头扎进沼泽，跋涉过低地，忍受着一段又一段比塞伦不愿离开的那座绿丘还要平缓的攀登。许多看见他在泥泞中踉跄的人都觉得他是个傻瓜，因为他花了整整数周去失去别人贪婪争来的高度。可当他终于开始雪峰漫长的攀登时，他上升到了那些逐丘而行者无法想象的高度，而他的旗帜插下时，成了王国里最高的。
paragraphs.en: The second walker, a man called Tor, mocked her caution. He had seen the snow-crowned peak from the start and marched straight toward it, paying no mind to the little rises and dips along the way. He plunged into the marsh, slogged through the lowlands, and endured days of climbing slopes far gentler than the green hill Seren had refused to leave. Many who saw him stumbling through the muck thought him a fool, for he spent long weeks losing ground that others had greedily gained. But when at last he began the long ascent of the snowy peak, he rose beyond anything the hill-walkers could imagine, and his flag, when planted, stood higher than any in the kingdom.

paragraphs.en: For a generation, the people argued over whose method was right. The followers of Seren insisted that one should always climb and never willingly descend, for the ground beneath your feet is the only truth you can feel. The followers of Tor insisted that one must fix on the tallest peak and suffer the valleys to reach it. Yet a strange thing nagged at them both: the hills of Vael were not fixed. Every spring, slow rivers of earth crept across the lowlands, raising what had been marsh into gentle rises and wearing down old summits grain by grain. What mattered, Mira taught, was to know the shape of the whole countryside as best you could, to be willing to descend for the sake of a better ascent, and never to mistake the nearest upward slope for the only direction worth walking.

paragraphs.cn: 渐渐地，瓦尔人不再只问自己站得有多高，而是开始随身携带用众多旅人笔记绘成的粗略地图。他们学会了阅读地势，学会辨认何时一个安逸的山顶不过是四周更高地势环绕中的一座小丘，也学会接受这幅地图永远不会画完。因为丘陵仍在他们脚下不断移动，而真正繁盛的行走者，既不是爬得最快的人，也不是选定一座峰后再不抬头的人，而是那些睁大双眼行走在一片永远、悄悄地被重新塑造的乡野上的人。
paragraphs.en: In time, the people of Vael stopped asking only how high they stood, and began carrying crude maps drawn from many travelers' notes. They learned to read the lay of the land, to recognize when a comfortable summit was merely a small one surrounded by higher ground, and to accept that the map itself would never be finished. For the hills kept shifting under their feet, and the walkers who thrived were not those who climbed the fastest, nor those who chose a peak once and never looked up again, but those who walked with eyes wide open across a countryside that was always, quietly, being remade.
