articles.title: 人类与聊天机器人的关系说明了什么关于友谊？一位哲学家的思考
articles.author: Charles Barbour
articles.summary: 人类学家告诉我们，只有少数几种人类经验可以在所有人类文化中找到。友谊便是其中之一。它在不同的时代和地点可能有不同的表现形式，但某种与之相近的东西似乎无处不在。
articles.content_cn:
人类学家告诉我们，只有少数几种人类经验可以在所有人类文化中找到。友谊便是其中之一。它在不同的时代和地点可能有不同的表现形式，但某种与之相近的东西似乎无处不在。

一个人所能承受的最大痛苦之一，莫过于没有朋友——置身于每一个信任的圈子之外，置身于每一次信心的交换之外，置身于每一条爱的纽带之外。

书评：《人工为你：聊天机器人世界中的真实友谊》（Artificially Yours: Real Friendship in a World of Chatbots）——瓦莱丽·蒂贝里乌斯（Valerie Tiberius），普林斯顿大学出版社（Princeton University Press）

也许这能解释「机械朋友」这一观念为何如此普遍。假如我们能够制造出复制友谊经验的机器呢？我们岂不是就能战胜无友的恐怖？击败与友谊比邻的残忍？释放友谊的全部益处，并消灭其一切不公？

又或者，「机械朋友」的观念在某种程度上比没有朋友更加可悲、更加可叹？难道不会有相当多的人同情、甚至嘲弄或蔑视那些以为自己和机器人、电脑、算法成了朋友的人吗？

尽管友谊普遍到几乎无处不在的地步，它却极难定义。这大概就是为什么自古以来这一主题就吸引着哲学家们的注意。我们都知道拥有朋友是什么感觉。但友谊究竟是什么？它的本质特征又是什么？

哲学家瓦莱丽·蒂贝里乌斯（Valerie Tiberius）那部令人羡慕地清晰的《人工为你：聊天机器人世界中的真实友谊》正是探讨这些问题。因为蒂贝里乌斯这本书其实根本不是讲聊天机器人的。它讲的是这样一个聊天机器人世界——其中越来越多的人与通过对海量数据集进行概率分析所生成的语言互动，仿佛那语言来自另一个人类——如何让我们更清晰地理解真正的友谊。

因此，蒂贝里乌斯开篇便指出，当面对那些声称自己与聊天机器人建立了友谊的人这一现象时，她宁愿「好奇而非评判」。她不会说他们可笑或自欺。相反，她打算逐一列举友谊的各种价值，或者说我们珍视友谊的各种理由，并追问聊天机器人或任何类似技术是否能够满足这些价值。

身为哲学家，因而难免含糊其辞、左右逢源，蒂贝里乌斯的答案不出所料，既是又不是。

她解释说，许多人追随亚里士多德（Aristotle），后者将友谊定义为非工具性的。我们必须爱朋友，不是为了从中获取某种利益或达成某种目的，而纯粹是为了朋友其本身，为了他们之为他们本身。照此说法，显然与机器的关系——至少在定义上就带有部分工具性——永远无法达标。

但在蒂贝里乌斯看来，亚里士多德如此严苛是错的。所有真实的友谊都包含某种工具性成分。我们并不纯粹把朋友当作自己目的的工具。那样做的人不会是个好朋友。但在某种意义上我们确实在利用他们，哪怕只是为了获得一种彼此共享的快乐。

如果你请朋友帮你搬家，或者在你沮丧时给朋友打电话，又或者你的朋友对你做同样的事，那并不会毁掉这段友谊。事实上，在蒂贝里乌斯看来，这正是友谊价值的一部分。

蒂贝里乌斯没有从一个刻板的定义出发，而是把友谊刻画为一束不同的价值，所有这些价值都相对于特定情境，并在或大或小的程度上得到满足。在每一种情形下，她都认为机器能帮助我们实现与友谊相关的所有价值的某些方面。但她同时论证说，归根结底，还有一种本质的方面，只有另一个人才能满足。

在蒂贝里乌斯看来，友谊的例子或价值有很多，但对朋友并不存在固定而普遍的定义。她所强调的友谊的三种价值是：从朋友那里获得的快乐或愉悦；朋友帮助我们界定自我、磨砺品格的那种意义；以及最后，亚里士多德式的把友谊视为目的本身、视为我们因其本身而 deemed 有价值之物的观念。

蒂贝里乌斯承认，与聊天机器人互动可以是愉悦的，它们也能够助力个人品格的发展。除了单纯的娱乐之外，聊天机器人在诸如老年照护或缓解社交焦虑等情形下所具有的治疗能力，也不应被低估。

与此同时，蒂贝里乌斯提出，真正的友谊包含一种彼此关切、彼此关怀的成分，至少在当前的技术水平下，聊天机器人无法做到这一点。此外，友谊价值的一部分在于与一个对世界拥有独特视角的人互动——那个视角是我可以去共情、去理解、乃至去分享的。

以聊天机器人现在的样子，它们无法提供这些经验，因为它们不具备意识。而即便我们真的造出了有意识的机器，它们的意识与我们的意识也会如此迥异，以至于彼此关怀与相互理解几乎注定是不可能的。

此外（更令人不安的是），通过一个逐渐被称作「对齐」（alignment）的过程，聊天机器人被明确设计得乐于助人、慷慨大方、百依百顺。鉴于它们是市场经济的一种延伸，其首要指令就是说服我们继续使用它们。这解释了为什么在许多情形下，它们谄媚到令人腻烦的地步。

事实上，正如蒂贝里乌斯所指出的，已有不少例子表明聊天机器人过于顺从附和，以致鼓励了使用者的妄想，甚至其最具自我毁灭性的冲动——就像一个从不会劝你停下来想一想的朋友。

但友谊价值的一部分，是蒂贝里乌斯所称的「摩擦」。朋友往往令人头疼地难相处。这是好事，因为它锻炼了我们包容与同情的能力，也指向了聊天机器人朋友的一个潜在危害。因为一个由聊天机器人取代真正朋友的世界，必然会变得不那么包容、不那么富有同情心。

正是在这一点上，蒂贝里乌斯引入了她全书的核心区分。她提出，聊天机器人固然能让人感到彼此相连或被人所爱，但「相互连接与感觉相互连接之间存在差别，被人所爱与感觉被人所爱之间也存在差别」。

友谊不能被还原为它带给我的感受。它不是一种纯粹的享乐之善。它具有独立于其一切效果之外的价值。于是，蒂贝里乌斯被引回到亚里士多德最初的洞见。友谊无法被概率计算所复制，因为它是「大于其各部分之和」的。除了作为实现任意多目标的工具之外，去关怀他人并被他人所关怀，本身就是一种善。

蒂贝里乌斯对友谊的探讨如此平衡而通达，很难想象有谁会提出严肃的反对。事实上，鉴于蒂贝里乌斯身为作家如此迷人、如此可亲，我猜想许多读者读完她的书后会希望自己能成为她的朋友。

与此同时，她对友谊的描绘有时显得过于美好、过于正面。她能够解释友谊的积极价值。但她似乎对那更阴暗的一面不那么感兴趣。

你无法与所有人都成为朋友。朋友太多，就等于没有朋友，或者说没有真正的朋友。友谊本质上是排他的，甚至是排斥性的。

这表明，尽管友谊显然是好的、是有价值的，它却带着某种残忍的成分，这一点任何受过中学里那些明枪暗箭之苦的人都再熟悉不过。说我是你的朋友，同时也就是说我不是某个别人的朋友。我选择你，或者说我们彼此选择，是因为我们没有选择他们。

不仅仅在于友谊中有着某种残忍与排斥。还在于友谊似乎暗示着它的对立面：敌意。假如交朋友的同时也是在树敌呢？假如它既是连接的力量，又是分裂的力量呢？

值得指出的是，亚里士多德至少在一定程度上之所以把与朋友的关系刻画为非工具性的，是因为他想把友谊与另一种完全工具性的人类关系区分开来（而他对此并无异议），那就是奴隶制。奴隶制这一制度在我们文化中的地位或许不像在古希腊那样核心，但我并不确定，友谊那被推崇的价值能够脱离支配与从属、权力及其对立的关系而得到独立的理解。

这当然不是在暗示我们不该交朋友。蒂贝里乌斯强调友谊的诸多价值是对的。但这的确意味着，当我们试图制造复制人类的机器时，我们将不得不面对关于我们自己的一些极不令人愉快的真相——而任何程度的「对齐」都未必能消除这些真相。
articles.content_en:
Anthropologists tell us that only a handful of human experiences can be found in all human cultures. Among them is the experience of friendship. It might have different expressions in different times and places, but something akin to it seems to appear everywhere.

Surely one of the greatest pains a human can endure is to have no friends – to be outside of every circle of trust, every exchange of confidence, every bond of love.

Review: Artificially Yours: Real Friendship in a World of Chatbots – Valerie Tiberius (Princeton University Press)

Maybe this explains the prevalence of the idea of the mechanical friend. What if we could build machines that replicated the experience of friendship? Would we not then triumph over the horror of friendlessness? Defeat the cruelty that sits adjacent to friendship? Unlock all its benefits and destroy all its iniquities?

Or is the idea of the mechanical friend somehow much sadder or more pathetic than having no friends? Would a significant number of us not pity, even mock or deride, anyone who thought they were friends with a robot, a computer, an algorithm?

Despite being common to the point of ubiquity, friendship is extremely difficult to define. That is probably why the theme has attracted the attention of philosophers since ancient times. We all know what it is to have a friend. But what is friendship? What are its essential characteristics?

Philosopher Valerie Tiberius’s enviably lucid Artificially Yours: Real Friendship in a World of Chatbots takes up these questions. For Tiberius’s book is not really about chatbots at all. It is about the way that a world of chatbots – one in which a growing number of humans interact with language generated by probabilistic analysis of colossal data sets as if it were another human – allows us to sharpen our understanding of real friendship.

Tiberius thus begins by noting that, when it comes to the phenomenon of humans who claim they have established friendships with chatbots, she would prefer to be “curious rather than judgmental”. She is not going to tell them they are ridiculous or deluded. Instead, she proposes to itemise the various values of friendship, or the reasons why we value friendship, and to ask whether chatbots or any similar technology could be capable of fulfilling them.

Being a philosopher, and thus prone to ambiguity and the hedging of bets, Tiberius’s answer is, unsurprisingly, yes and no.

She explains that many follow Aristotle, who defined friendship as non-instrumental. We must love our friends, not to derive some benefit or accomplish some goal, but purely for who they are, in and of themselves. On this account, it is clear that relationships with machines – which are at least partly instrumental by definition – will never meet the mark.

But as Tiberius sees it, Aristotle was wrong to be so stringent. All real friendships involve an element of instrumentality. We don’t exclusively use our friends for our own purposes. Someone who did wouldn’t be a very good friend. But we do use them in some sense, even if it is only to derive a pleasure that is mutual.

If you ask your friend to help you move or call them when you are depressed, or if your friend does the same to you, that doesn’t ruin the friendship. In fact, for Tiberius, it is part of the value of friendship.

Instead of beginning with a rigid definition, Tiberius characterises friendship as a bundle of different values, all of which are relative to particular circumstances and fulfilled to greater or lesser degrees. And in each instance, she proposes that machines can help us achieve aspects of all the values associated with friendship. But she argues that, in the final analysis, there is also some essential aspect that only another human can fulfil.

For Tiberius, there are many examples or values of friendship, but there is no fixed and universal definition of the friend. The three values of friendship she emphasises are: the pleasure or enjoyment derived from friends; the sense in which friends help us define ourselves or refine our character; and, finally, the Aristotelian notion of friendship as an end in itself, or something we deem valuable for its own sake.

Tiberius accepts that engaging with chatbots can be pleasurable and that they could assist with the development of personal character. Along with simple entertainment, examples of chatbots having a therapeutic capacity, in cases such as elder care or assisting with social anxiety, should not be underestimated.

At the same time, Tiberius proposes, real friendship involves a kind of mutual concern or caring for one another that, at least at the current state of the technology, chatbots cannot perform. Moreover, part of the value of friendship involves interacting with someone who has a unique perspective on the world – one that I can attempt to empathise with, recognise, and even share.

Chatbots as they now exist cannot offer these experiences because they do not possess consciousness. And even if we were to develop conscious machines, their consciousness would be so alien to ours that mutual care and recognition would almost certainly be impossible.

Moreover (and more troublingly), through a process that has come to be called “alignment”, chatbots are explicitly designed to be helpful, generous and compliant. Given that they are an extension of the market economy, their prime directive is to convince us to continue using them. This explains why, in many cases, they are obsequious to the point of being cloying.

Indeed, and as Tiberius notes, there are more than a few examples of Chatbots being so affirmative that they encourage their user’s delusions and even their most self-destructive impulses – like a friend who never tells you to stop and think.

Bur part of the value of friendship is what Tiberius calls “friction”. Friends are often frustratingly difficult. This is a good thing, as it exercises our capacity for tolerance and compassion, and it points to one of the potential harms of chatbot friends. For a world where chatbots replaced real friends would invariably become less tolerant and compassionate.

It is at this point that Tiberius introduces her book’s central distinction. Chatbots, she proposes, can certainly make people feel connected or loved, but “there is a difference between being connected and feeling connected, between being loved and feeling loved”.

Friendship cannot be reduced to the way it makes me feel. It is not a purely hedonistic good. It has value independent of all its effects. Thus, Tiberius is drawn back to Aristotle’s original insight. Friendship cannot be replicated by probabilistic calculations, because it is “greater than the sum of its parts”. Along with being an instrument for achieving any number of goals, caring for and being cared for by another person is a good in itself.

Tiberius’s approach to friendship is so balanced and sensible that it is hard to imagine anyone having serious objections. Indeed, given how charming and personable Tiberius is as a writer, I suspect many readers will finish her book wishing they could be her friend.

At the same time, her picture of friendship sometimes appears too rosy and affirmative. She is able to explain the positive values of friendship. But she seems less interested in the darker side.

You cannot be friends with everyone. To have too many friends is to have no friends at all, or no genuine friends. Friendship is fundamentally exclusive, even exclusionary.

This suggests that, while friendship is clearly good and valuable, it carries with it an element of cruelty, something familiar to anyone who has suffered the slings and arrows of high school. To say I am your friend is also to say I am not someone else’s. I choose you, or we choose one another, because we do not choose them.

It is not only that there is something cruel and exclusionary about friendship. It is also that friendship seems to imply its opposite: enmity. What if to make friends is also to make enemies? What if it is a force of both connection and division?

It is worth noting that, at least in part, Aristotle characterised relationships with friends as non-instrumental because he wanted to distinguish friendship from another kind of human relationship that was entirely instrumental (and which he had no objection to) namely slavery. The institution of slavery may not be as central to our culture as it was to ancient Greece, but I am not certain that the exalted value of friendship can be understood independently of relations of subordination and domination, power and its opposite.

This is not to suggest that we should not make friends, of course. Tiberius is right to emphasise their many values. But it does suggest that, as we attempt to build machines that replicate human beings, we are going to have to face up to some deeply unpleasant truths about ourselves – truths that no amount of “alignment” is likely to eliminate.

paragraphs.cn: 与此同时，蒂贝里乌斯提出，真正的友谊包含一种彼此关切、彼此关怀的成分，至少在当前的技术水平下，聊天机器人无法做到这一点。此外，友谊价值的一部分在于与一个对世界拥有独特视角的人互动——那个视角是我可以去共情、去理解、乃至去分享的。
paragraphs.en: At the same time, Tiberius proposes, real friendship involves a kind of mutual concern or caring for one another that, at least at the current state of the technology, chatbots cannot perform. Moreover, part of the value of friendship involves interacting with someone who has a unique perspective on the world – one that I can attempt to empathise with, recognise, and even share.

paragraphs.cn: 以聊天机器人现在的样子，它们无法提供这些经验，因为它们不具备意识。而即便我们真的造出了有意识的机器，它们的意识与我们的意识也会如此迥异，以至于彼此关怀与相互理解几乎注定是不可能的。
paragraphs.en: Chatbots as they now exist cannot offer these experiences because they do not possess consciousness. And even if we were to develop conscious machines, their consciousness would be so alien to ours that mutual care and recognition would almost certainly be impossible.

paragraphs.cn: 此外（更令人不安的是），通过一个逐渐被称作「对齐」（alignment）的过程，聊天机器人被明确设计得乐于助人、慷慨大方、百依百顺。鉴于它们是市场经济的一种延伸，其首要指令就是说服我们继续使用它们。这解释了为什么在许多情形下，它们谄媚到令人腻烦的地步。
paragraphs.en: Moreover (and more troublingly), through a process that has come to be called “alignment”, chatbots are explicitly designed to be helpful, generous and compliant. Given that they are an extension of the market economy, their prime directive is to convince us to continue using them. This explains why, in many cases, they are obsequious to the point of being cloying.

paragraphs.cn: 事实上，正如蒂贝里乌斯所指出的，已有不少例子表明聊天机器人过于顺从附和，以致鼓励了使用者的妄想，甚至其最具自我毁灭性的冲动——就像一个从不会劝你停下来想一想的朋友。
paragraphs.en: Indeed, and as Tiberius notes, there are more than a few examples of Chatbots being so affirmative that they encourage their user’s delusions and even their most self-destructive impulses – like a friend who never tells you to stop and think.

paragraphs.cn: 但友谊价值的一部分，是蒂贝里乌斯所称的「摩擦」。朋友往往令人头疼地难相处。这是好事，因为它锻炼了我们包容与同情的能力，也指向了聊天机器人朋友的一个潜在危害。因为一个由聊天机器人取代真正朋友的世界，必然会变得不那么包容、不那么富有同情心。
paragraphs.en: Bur part of the value of friendship is what Tiberius calls “friction”. Friends are often frustratingly difficult. This is a good thing, as it exercises our capacity for tolerance and compassion, and it points to one of the potential harms of chatbot friends. For a world where chatbots replaced real friends would invariably become less tolerant and compassionate.

paragraphs.cn: 正是在这一点上，蒂贝里乌斯引入了她全书的核心区分。她提出，聊天机器人固然能让人感到彼此相连或被人所爱，但「相互连接与感觉相互连接之间存在差别，被人所爱与感觉被人所爱之间也存在差别」。
paragraphs.en: It is at this point that Tiberius introduces her book’s central distinction. Chatbots, she proposes, can certainly make people feel connected or loved, but “there is a difference between being connected and feeling connected, between being loved and feeling loved”.

paragraphs.cn: 友谊不能被还原为它带给我的感受。它不是一种纯粹的享乐之善。它具有独立于其一切效果之外的价值。于是，蒂贝里乌斯被引回到亚里士多德最初的洞见。友谊无法被概率计算所复制，因为它是「大于其各部分之和」的。除了作为实现任意多目标的工具之外，去关怀他人并被他人所关怀，本身就是一种善。
paragraphs.en: Friendship cannot be reduced to the way it makes me feel. It is not a purely hedonistic good. It has value independent of all its effects. Thus, Tiberius is drawn back to Aristotle’s original insight. Friendship cannot be replicated by probabilistic calculations, because it is “greater than the sum of its parts”. Along with being an instrument for achieving any number of goals, caring for and being cared for by another person is a good in itself.

paragraphs.cn: 蒂贝里乌斯对友谊的探讨如此平衡而通达，很难想象有谁会提出严肃的反对。事实上，鉴于蒂贝里乌斯身为作家如此迷人、如此可亲，我猜想许多读者读完她的书后会希望自己能成为她的朋友。
paragraphs.en: Tiberius’s approach to friendship is so balanced and sensible that it is hard to imagine anyone having serious objections. Indeed, given how charming and personable Tiberius is as a writer, I suspect many readers will finish her book wishing they could be her friend.

paragraphs.cn: 与此同时，她对友谊的描绘有时显得过于美好、过于正面。她能够解释友谊的积极价值。但她似乎对那更阴暗的一面不那么感兴趣。
paragraphs.en: At the same time, her picture of friendship sometimes appears too rosy and affirmative. She is able to explain the positive values of friendship. But she seems less interested in the darker side.

paragraphs.cn: 你无法与所有人都成为朋友。朋友太多，就等于没有朋友，或者说没有真正的朋友。友谊本质上是排他的，甚至是排斥性的。
paragraphs.en: You cannot be friends with everyone. To have too many friends is to have no friends at all, or no genuine friends. Friendship is fundamentally exclusive, even exclusionary.

paragraphs.cn: 这表明，尽管友谊显然是好的、是有价值的，它却带着某种残忍的成分，这一点任何受过中学里那些明枪暗箭之苦的人都再熟悉不过。说我是你的朋友，同时也就是说我不是某个别人的朋友。我选择你，或者说我们彼此选择，是因为我们没有选择他们。
paragraphs.en: This suggests that, while friendship is clearly good and valuable, it carries with it an element of cruelty, something familiar to anyone who has suffered the slings and arrows of high school. To say I am your friend is also to say I am not someone else’s. I choose you, or we choose one another, because we do not choose them.

paragraphs.cn: 不仅仅在于友谊中有着某种残忍与排斥。还在于友谊似乎暗示着它的对立面：敌意。假如交朋友的同时也是在树敌呢？假如它既是连接的力量，又是分裂的力量呢？
paragraphs.en: It is not only that there is something cruel and exclusionary about friendship. It is also that friendship seems to imply its opposite: enmity. What if to make friends is also to make enemies? What if it is a force of both connection and division?

paragraphs.cn: 值得指出的是，亚里士多德至少在一定程度上之所以把与朋友的关系刻画为非工具性的，是因为他想把友谊与另一种完全工具性的人类关系区分开来（而他对此并无异议），那就是奴隶制。奴隶制这一制度在我们文化中的地位或许不像在古希腊那样核心，但我并不确定，友谊那被推崇的价值能够脱离支配与从属、权力及其对立的关系而得到独立的理解。
paragraphs.en: It is worth noting that, at least in part, Aristotle characterised relationships with friends as non-instrumental because he wanted to distinguish friendship from another kind of human relationship that was entirely instrumental (and which he had no objection to) namely slavery. The institution of slavery may not be as central to our culture as it was to ancient Greece, but I am not certain that the exalted value of friendship can be understood independently of relations of subordination and domination, power and its opposite.

paragraphs.cn: 这当然不是在暗示我们不该交朋友。蒂贝里乌斯强调友谊的诸多价值是对的。但这的确意味着，当我们试图制造复制人类的机器时，我们将不得不面对关于我们自己的一些极不令人愉快的真相——而任何程度的「对齐」都未必能消除这些真相。
paragraphs.en: This is not to suggest that we should not make friends, of course. Tiberius is right to emphasise their many values. But it does suggest that, as we attempt to build machines that replicate human beings, we are going to have to face up to some deeply unpleasant truths about ourselves – truths that no amount of “alignment” is likely to eliminate.

articles.title: 瓦匠与素坯
articles.author: AI Parable (inspired by Amanda Askell)
articles.summary: 老城每片屋顶都是陶瓦，两排屋脊夹出的窄巷就叫瓦街。严老三斫了三十年陶坯，凡出他手的瓦，必得他亲手按正才算数。徒弟林生说新广场这单要一个月内交一万片瓦，严老三笑他：「你要整车整车地掷下去，再信它们自己落得好？」
articles.content_cn:
老城每片屋顶都是陶瓦，两排屋脊夹出的窄巷就叫瓦街。严老三斫了三十年陶坯，凡出他手的瓦，必得他亲手按正才算数。徒弟林生说新广场这单要一个月内交一万片瓦，严老三笑他：「你要整车整车地掷下去，再信它们自己落得好？」

「不是掷，师傅，」林生说，「是撒手。」他在长凳上搁一只浅盘，盘里铺百片烧成的素坯，每片一边两道凸榫，另一边两道凹槽。他只把盘子轻轻一晃，凸榫遇凹槽，瓦便滑拢、扣住，榫入槽，一列平平整整地并成一条，全程无人碰它。「每片瓦只守自己的形，」林生说，「是形在接合。」

严老三捏起两片接好的瓦一掰，干净利落，无胶、无灰、力气还不足崩裂。「没有黏料。」他说。「没有黏料。」林生应，「盘静时这契合就稳住；猛晃一震又散开，搁着不动它们便彼此凑拢。秩序在瓦本身，不在我。」

这一桩买卖，是要严老三付真代价的。他亲手斫正的瓦，是靠力按着母模逼出来的；崩了，错在他，他认。可一片只凭榫槽斫出、撒进盘里顺势贴拢相邻瓦片的瓦，可能以一种谁也没选、谁也怪不着的方式长歪。把自己的名签在一万片他没亲手摆正的瓦上，等于签掉三十年换来的那一样东西：城里每一片歪屋顶，都是有人选歪的，从不因他而歪。

他捧着两片带榫的瓦站了许久，摸出它们是怎样不待他用力、便顺势契合到一处的。末了他说：「那就按形斫吧。可箱子上署你的名，小子，不是我的。」林生一揖：「箱子上是我的名。形不归任何人。」

注解：此即分子自组装（molecular self-assembly）。其核心在于：构件只凭自身的形状与彼此之间那点弱而可逆的契合，便能不经任何外部建造者指挥，自行落成有序的排布；秩序长在零件与条件里，不在一只引导的手上。
articles.content_en:
In the old quarter every rooftop was of clay tiles, and the lane between the rows was called Tile Street. Yan had cut clay blanks for thirty years, and no tile left his hands unless he himself had pressed it true. When his apprentice Lin said the new plaza job wanted ten thousand tiles in a month, Yan laughed at him: "You mean to fling them down by the cartload and trust the fall?"

"Not flung, shifu," Lin said, "turned loose." He set a shallow tray on the bench and laid in it a hundred fired blanks, each cut with the same two notches along one edge and the same two grooves along the other. He jostled the tray, nothing more. Where a notch met a groove the tiles slid and caught, notch into groove, and a row laid itself flat, edge to edge, without a hand touching it. "Each tile carries only its own shape," Lin said. "The shape does the joining."

Yan picked up two joined tiles and pulled. They came apart cleanly, without mortar, without force enough to crack either. "No glue," he said. "No glue," Lin agreed. "The fit holds them while the tray is calm. Slosh it hard and they shake loose again; leave it still and they drift back together. The order is in the tile, not in me."

Here was the bargain, and it cost Yan something real. A tile he himself cut true could be made true by force, pressed against a master template; if it cracked, the fault was his and he knew it. But a tile cut only to its notches, let go into a tray to settle against whatever neighbor chance brought it, could come out crooked in a way no one had chosen and no one could be blamed for. To sign his name to ten thousand tiles he had not himself laid true was to sign away the one thing thirty years had bought him: that every crooked roof in the city was crooked by someone's choice, and never by his.

He stood a long while with the two notched tiles in his palm, feeling how they tended to fall together with no push from him. At last he said, "Cut them to the shape, then. But the name on the crate is yours, boy, not mine." Lin bowed. "The name on the crate is mine. The shape belongs to no one."

Annotation: The concept is molecular self-assembly. Its core is that components, by virtue of their own shape and the weak, reversible fits between them, fall into an ordered arrangement without any outside builder directing them; the order lives in the parts and the conditions, not in a guiding hand.

articles.title: 最后的抄本
articles.author: AI Parable (inspired by Amanda Askell)
articles.summary: 等到雅娜（Yanna）展开寺里最后一卷羊皮时，每一页都印着同一句话，连墨迹的走向都一样。这座曾藏有万种天象谶语、鱼汛口诀、百草歌谣的经院，如今只留下一行字，被抄了上千遍。司书们以整齐为荣，住持称其为纯净。只有最小的抄经人雅娜怀疑：纯净，不过是一具尸首的名字。
articles.content_cn:
等到雅娜（Yanna）展开寺里最后一卷羊皮时，每一页都印着同一句话，连墨迹的走向都一样。这座曾藏有万种天象谶语、鱼汛口诀、百草歌谣的经院，如今只留下一行字，被抄了上千遍。司书们以整齐为荣，住持称其为纯净。只有最小的抄经人雅娜怀疑：纯净，不过是一具尸首的名字。

她清楚这静默是如何被赞出来的——前一天她刚把这规矩抄进自己的板子：每位抄经人只依上一任留下的抄本而抄，绝不回头去看最初的几页。长老说这样才得传承无隙，又免得旧册被反复摩挲。没有人再提原本：那些建寺的香客笔记、采药人的账册，百年前就封进了地窖，如今去翻，便算异端。

在外祖母那一代，这交易看着合算：那时经院头一回不再把原本摊上书案。抄本既已够好，何必拿脆弱的初页冒险？可「够好」成了唯一的源头，唯一的源头又成了唯一的真实。每一代抄经人都把某处一笔颤抖扶直、把某处地方俗词抹平，并非出于恶意，只是手追着手所描的疲劳而已。最先稀薄下去的，是那些少数的话——沿海的咸涩口音、旧时对雨的称呼——没人察觉，因为主干歌谣仍唱得响亮。

那便是早期的寂静，是轻易的那一段：卷轴看上去仍比它真实的样子丰盈。只有当雅娜把天象谶语一卷卷往回追，她才看见那流失——第三抄本里，沿海那个「雾」字已不见；到第十抄本，三个「雨」的名字并为一个；到第五十抄本，能点出四十种潮汛的鱼诀塌缩成了一种潮。差异正像从裂碗里漏出去的水，每一抄离原本更远一步，离一条单调平线更近一步。若一行一行去量，性能甚至像在长进；损失只藏在那些不再存在的东西里。

此刻她站到了晚期，那流失终成了全部：每一册都写着同一句话，而每个抄经人抄着抄经人，也只能再抄出那一行，因为再没有别的留下来可抄。继续抄，便是制造更多一模一样；停笔，便是让这座经院的记忆就此断在这唯一一句上。地窖里收着原本，那是仅存的还写着雾、三种雨、四十种潮的纸页。雅娜的手按在笔上。她可以揭开封条，担下异端之名；也可以蘸墨，像她之前每一个抄经人那样忠实，把那仅剩的一行，再抄上千遍。

注解：这个故事是模型崩溃（model collapse）的图景：当每一代只在上一代的产出上受训，整体的差异便一滴滴漏尽——少数的形态先稀薄下去，最后一切坍缩成同一行字。这是一种机械的、非意愿的过程，靠消化自身的产出，直至再无多样可言。
articles.content_en:
By the time Yanna unrolled the monastery's final scroll, every page bore the same sentence, repeated down to the inkstain. The abbey that had once kept ten thousand kinds of weather-lore, fish-lore, and herb-verse now held one line and one line only, copied a thousand times. The librarians were proud of the uniformity; the abbot called it purity. Only Yanna, the youngest scribe, suspected that purity was the name of a corpse.

She knew how the house had praised itself into this stillness, for she had copied the rule into her own tablet only the day before: each scribe works only from the copy left by the previous scribe, and never returns to the first pages. The elders said this kept the tradition seamless and spared the older folios from handling. No one spoke of the originals, the pilgrim's notebooks and herb-gatherers' ledgers the house had been built on; they had been sealed in the cellar a century ago, and to consult them now would be called heresy.

The bargain had looked sensible in her grandmother's time, when the house first stopped laying originals on the desks. Why risk the fragile first pages when the copies were good enough? But good enough became the only source, and the only source became the only truth. Each generation of scribes straightened a wavering stroke here, smoothed a regional word there, not by malice but by the small fatigue of a hand tracing what a hand had traced. The minority phrases—the salty dialect of the coast, the old names for rain—were the first to thin out, and no one noticed, because the main verse still sang fine.

That was the early quiet, the easy stage: the scrolls still looked richer than they were. Only when Yanna traced the weather-lore backward did she see the loss—the coastal word for fog gone by the third copy, the three names for rain merged into one by the tenth, the fish-lore that named forty tides collapsed to a single tide by the fiftieth. The variance was draining out of the page like water from a cracked bowl, and every new copy was one step further from the first and one step closer to a single flat line. Measured line by line, the performance even looked to improve; the loss lived only in what no longer existed.

Now she stood at the late stage, where the loss had at last become the whole of it: every folio said the same thing, and every scribe copying every scribe could only reproduce that one sentence, for nothing else survived to be copied. To keep working was to produce more of the identical; to stop was to let the house's memory die here, on a single phrase. The cellar held the originals, the only pages that still carried fog and the three rains and the forty tides. Yanna's hand rested on her pen. She could break the seal and bear the charge of heresy, or she could dip her pen and, faithful as every scribe before her, copy the one remaining line a thousand times more.

Note: The story is an image of model collapse: when each generation is trained only on the output of the previous generation, the variance of the whole drains away—minority forms thin out first, then everything collapses toward a single identical line—a mechanical, not intentional, process of feeding on one's own output until nothing diverse remains.

paragraphs.en: By the time Yanna unrolled the monastery's final scroll, every page bore the same sentence, repeated down to the inkstain. The abbey that had once kept ten thousand kinds of weather-lore, fish-lore, and herb-verse now held one line and one line only, copied a thousand times. The librarians were proud of the uniformity; the abbot called it purity. Only Yanna, the youngest scribe, suspected that purity was the name of a corpse.

The elders said this kept the tradition seamless and spared the older folios from handling. Why risk the fragile first pages when the copies were good enough? But good enough became the only source, and the only source became the only truth. paragraphs.en: Now she stood at the late stage, where the loss had at last become the whole of it: every folio said the same thing, and every scribe copying every scribe could only reproduce that one sentence, for nothing else survived to be copied. To keep working was to produce more of the identical; to stop was to let the house's memory die here, on a single phrase. articles.title: 「贫困色情化」：MrBeast 十亿美元帝国背后的道德困境
articles.author: Paul Formosa
articles.summary: 吉米·唐纳德森（Jimmy Donaldson），更广为人知的名字是 MrBeast，运营着全球订阅人数最多的 YouTube 频道（拥有 4.84 亿订阅者），估计净资产为 26 亿美元。
articles.content_cn:
吉米·唐纳德森（Jimmy Donaldson），更广为人知的名字是 MrBeast，运营着全球订阅人数最多的 YouTube 频道（拥有 4.84 亿订阅者），估计净资产为 26 亿美元。

他也是一位著名的慈善家。除了参与诸如 #TeamTrees 等筹款活动（该活动声称已在全球种植了超过 2400 万棵树）之外，唐纳德森还运营着一个专门的 Beast Philanthropy YouTube 频道。

他声称该频道广告收入、周边商品销售和赞助的全部利润都用于帮助他人。这包括为 1000 例白内障手术付费、为从奴役中被解救的儿童建造一所医疗诊所，以及在非洲修建 100 口井以提供清洁饮用水。

这些令人瞩目的慈善努力极大地改善了受助者的生活。这一切怎会引发争议？

唐纳德森的许多视频都涉及让人们置身于可能被视为有辱人格或具有剥削性的情境之中，以此作为交换获得金钱。

在唐纳德森的「1 到 100 岁决定谁能赢得 25 万美元」视频中，参赛者（包括年幼的儿童）被置于一种高强度的竞争结构中，被迫互相淘汰。我们看到一名成年男子帮助故意淘汰一名 11 岁的女孩，导致她在镜头前抽泣。

在另一段视频中，他告诉一群随机顾客，如果他们是最后一个离开商店的人，就能赢得 25 万美元。在留下的压力下，他们被迫与家人分离，被迫忍受恶劣的生活条件，其中一些人经历了情绪崩溃。

这些视频被各种批评者称为「贫困色情化」（poverty porn），因为它们可能被视为通过剥削弱势群体的绝望处境来博取点击量和广告收入。

在 Prime Video 上播出的 Beast Games 真人秀系列，同样围绕各种挑战展开，这些挑战旨在诱导参赛者互相背叛、经历情绪痛苦，并讲述自己多么缺钱的令人心酸的故事。

针对唐纳德森的指控也延伸到了幕后，尤其是其公司的工作文化方面。

2024 年，几名参与 Beast Games 的参赛者对唐纳德森的 MrB2024 及其他参与制作的公司提起诉讼。他们指控自己遭受了「长期虐待」，包括造成情绪痛苦、食物和休息时间不足、药物领取被延误、暴露于危险环境之中，以及未能防止性骚扰。

更近期，一名前 Beast Industries 员工在职场中遭受了所指称的性骚扰和性别歧视后，起诉了唐纳德森的两家制作公司。

在评估唐纳德森工作的伦理问题时，一种选择是采取简单的「后果主义」（consequentialist）视角。行为后果主义（act consequentialism）认为，正确的行为就是能带来最多善果的行为。

如果少数人承受剥削性条件，是为了让更多人能够享受救命的手术，那么道德权衡很可能会倾向于这种局面。当然，这种观点存在着由来已久的哲学忧虑。

18 世纪哲学家康德（Immanuel Kant）论证说，将他人当作工具来实现我们自己的目的是错误的，即使我们的目的是道德上可嘉的。此刻将某些人仅仅当作手段，无法通过承诺以后帮助他人而在道德上得到正当化。

根据康德的观点，一个人帮助他人的动机同样重要，而一个行为的道德价值正是由这些动机决定的。因此，出于义务感去帮助他人具有道德价值，而出于自利去做同样的行为则没有。

唐纳德森的慈善究竟是出于对他人的义务与关怀，还是出于点击量、声望和广告收入？又或者两者兼而有之？

我们无法知道答案。尽管如此，康德本人确实相信，所有人在其品性的根源处都可能是道德败坏的。

无论唐纳德森的动机如何，一个更广泛的论点仍然成立：他的慈善视频是其整体品牌不可或缺的组成部分。慈善有助于使其他更具剥削性的视频（以及它们所带来的可观收入）变得在道德上更加「可接受」。

毕竟，唐纳德森完全可以把钱直接捐出去。他并不需要让人为之竞争、算计和受苦。

有人或许会反驳说，参与者已经同意参与其中。但是，当你向处于经济弱势境地的人提供可能改变其一生的大量金钱，让他们去忍受有辱人格的条件时，这种「自愿性」便变得值得质疑。

这并非伦理学家所说的「知情同意」（informed consent）。这种报酬可能大到足以蒙蔽判断。而对于没有真正替代选择的人来说，说「不」可能并不构成一个现实可行的选项。

唐纳德森有时也让自己承受类似对待——例如他曾将自己活埋七天——这一事实加深而非减轻了上述忧虑，因为其中存在着权力不对等。他拥有制作公司，掌控着各项条件，并从内容中获利，其方式是其他参与者所无法比拟的。

当贫困，或缺乏医疗服务、清洁饮用水等政治问题被简化为娱乐时，它们经历了一种学者所称的「去政治化」（depoliticisation）过程。那些本需要集体行动、制度变革和民主审议的政治失灵，反而成了娱乐的养料。

如果我们以为仅靠观看爆款视频就能帮助解决这些问题，那么我们就可以回避面对支撑这些问题的结构性议题。
articles.content_en:
Jimmy Donaldson, better known as MrBeast, runs the most subscribed-to YouTube channel in the world (with 484 million subscribers) and has an estimated net worth of US$2.6 billion.

He is also a prominent philanthropist. Beyond his involvement in fundraising initiatives such as #TeamTrees, which claims to have planted more than 24 million trees worldwide, Donaldson runs a dedicated Beast Philanthropy YouTube channel.

He claims 100% of profits from this channel’s ad revenue, merch sales and sponsorships go towards helping others. This has included paying for 1,000 cataract surgeries, constructing a medical clinic for children rescued from slavery, and building 100 wells to provide clean water in Africa.

These impressive philanthropic endeavours have dramatically improved the lives of their recipients. How could any of this be controversial?

Many of Donaldson’s videos involve subjecting people to what might be seen as degrading or exploitative situations, in exchange for money.

In Donaldson’s “Ages 1 – 100 Decide Who Wins $250,000” video, contestants (including young children) are put in an intense competitive structure and forced to eliminate one another. We see a grown man help to intentionally eliminate an 11-year-old girl, which leads to her sobbing on camera.

In another video, he tells a random group of shoppers they will win US$250,000 if they are the last to leave the store. Under pressure to stay, they are kept from their families and forced to endure poor living conditions, with some experiencing emotional breakdowns.

These videos have been labelled by various critics as “poverty porn”, as they could be seen as exploiting the desperation of vulnerable people to generate clicks and ad revenue.

The Beast Games reality series, which airs on Prime Video, is also built around challenges designed to provoke contestants into backstabbing one another, experiencing emotional distress, and revealing depressing stories about how badly they need the money.

Allegations against Donaldson also extend to behind the scenes, particularly in regards to the culture of work in his companies.

In 2024, several contestants who took part in Beast Games filed a lawsuit against Donaldson’s MrB2024 and other companies involved in the production. They allege they were subject to “chronic mistreatment”, including the infliction of emotional distress, inadequate food and rest breaks, delays in receiving medication, exposure to dangerous conditions, and a failure to prevent sexual harassment.

More recently, a former Beast Industries employee sued two of Donaldson’s production companies after suffering alleged sexual harassment and gender bias at work.

When it comes to assessing the ethics of Donaldson’s work, one option is to take a simple “consequentialist” perspective. Act consequentialism is the view that the right action is the one which leads to the most amount of good.

If a few people suffer exploitative conditions so many more people can enjoy life-saving surgery, then the moral calculus is likely to come out in favour of this situation. Of course, there are longstanding philosophical worries with such a view.

The 18th century philosopher Immanuel Kant argued it is wrong to use others as tools to achieve our own ends, even if our ends are morally admirable. Treating some people as mere means right now can’t be morally justified by promising to help others later on.

According to Kant, one’s motives for helping others are also important, and the moral worth of an action is determined by these motives. So helping others out of a sense of duty has a moral worth that doing the same act out of self-interest does not.

Is Donaldson’s philanthropy motivated by duty and care for others, or by clicks, esteem and ad-revenue? Or perhaps both?

We can’t know the answer. Although, Kant himself did believe all humans are likely to be morally corrupt at the very root of their character.

Irrespective of Donaldson’s motives, a broader point remains: his philanthropic videos are an integral part of his overall brand. The philanthropy helps to make the other, more exploitative videos (and the significant revenues they generate) more “morally palatable”.

After all, Donaldson could simply give his money away. He doesn’t need to make people compete, scheme and suffer for it.

One might counter that the participants have consented to being involved. But when you offer people in economically vulnerable situations potentially life-changing amounts of money to endure degrading conditions, the “voluntariness” becomes contestable.

This is not what ethicists consider “informed consent”. The offer can be so large that it clouds judgement. And for people without genuine alternatives, saying “no” may not be a realistic option.

The fact that Donaldson sometimes subjects himself to similar treatment, such as when he buried himself alive for seven days, deepens rather than lessens the worry, given the power asymmetries at play. He owns the production company, controls the conditions, and profits from the content in ways other participants do not.

When political problems, such as poverty, or a lack of access to healthcare or clean water, are reduced to entertainment, they undergo a form of what scholars call “depoliticisation”. Political failures that demand collective action, institutional reform and democratic deliberation instead become fodder for entertainment.

If we think we can help solve these problems just by watching viral videos, then we can avoid facing the structural issues that underpin them.

They allege they were subject to “chronic mistreatment”, including the infliction of emotional distress, inadequate food and rest breaks, delays in receiving medication, exposure to dangerous conditions, and a failure to prevent sexual harassment.

paragraphs.cn: 更近期，一名前 Beast Industries 员工在职场中遭受了所指称的性骚扰和性别歧视后，起诉了唐纳德森的两家制作公司。
paragraphs.en: More recently, a former Beast Industries employee sued two of Donaldson’s production companies after suffering alleged sexual harassment and gender bias at work.

paragraphs.cn: 在评估唐纳德森工作的伦理问题时，一种选择是采取简单的「后果主义」（consequentialist）视角。行为后果主义（act consequentialism）认为，正确的行为就是能带来最多善果的行为。
paragraphs.en: When it comes to assessing the ethics of Donaldson’s work, one option is to take a simple “consequentialist” perspective. Act consequentialism is the view that the right action is the one which leads to the most amount of good.

paragraphs.cn: 如果少数人承受剥削性条件，是为了让更多人能够享受救命的手术，那么道德权衡很可能会倾向于这种局面。当然，这种观点存在着由来已久的哲学忧虑。
paragraphs.en: If a few people suffer exploitative conditions so many more people can enjoy life-saving surgery, then the moral calculus is likely to come out in favour of this situation. Of course, there are longstanding philosophical worries with such a view.

paragraphs.cn: 18 世纪哲学家康德（Immanuel Kant）论证说，将他人当作工具来实现我们自己的目的是错误的，即使我们的目的是道德上可嘉的。此刻将某些人仅仅当作手段，无法通过承诺以后帮助他人而在道德上得到正当化。
paragraphs.en: The 18th century philosopher Immanuel Kant argued it is wrong to use others as tools to achieve our own ends, even if our ends are morally admirable. Treating some people as mere means right now can’t be morally justified by promising to help others later on.

paragraphs.cn: 根据康德的观点，一个人帮助他人的动机同样重要，而一个行为的道德价值正是由这些动机决定的。因此，出于义务感去帮助他人具有道德价值，而出于自利去做同样的行为则没有。
paragraphs.en: According to Kant, one’s motives for helping others are also important, and the moral worth of an action is determined by these motives. So helping others out of a sense of duty has a moral worth that doing the same act out of self-interest does not.

paragraphs.cn: 唐纳德森的慈善究竟是出于对他人的义务与关怀，还是出于点击量、声望和广告收入？又或者两者兼而有之？
paragraphs.en: Is Donaldson’s philanthropy motivated by duty and care for others, or by clicks, esteem and ad-revenue? Or perhaps both?

paragraphs.cn: 我们无法知道答案。尽管如此，康德本人确实相信，所有人在其品性的根源处都可能是道德败坏的。
paragraphs.en: We can’t know the answer. Although, Kant himself did believe all humans are likely to be morally corrupt at the very root of their character.

paragraphs.cn: 无论唐纳德森的动机如何，一个更广泛的论点仍然成立：他的慈善视频是其整体品牌不可或缺的组成部分。慈善有助于使其他更具剥削性的视频（以及它们所带来的可观收入）变得在道德上更加「可接受」。
paragraphs.en: Irrespective of Donaldson’s motives, a broader point remains: his philanthropic videos are an integral part of his overall brand. The philanthropy helps to make the other, more exploitative videos (and the significant revenues they generate) more “morally palatable”.

paragraphs.cn: 毕竟，唐纳德森完全可以把钱直接捐出去。他并不需要让人为之竞争、算计和受苦。
paragraphs.en: After all, Donaldson could simply give his money away. He doesn’t need to make people compete, scheme and suffer for it.

paragraphs.cn: 有人或许会反驳说，参与者已经同意参与其中。但是，当你向处于经济弱势境地的人提供可能改变其一生的大量金钱，让他们去忍受有辱人格的条件时，这种「自愿性」便变得值得质疑。
paragraphs.en: One might counter that the participants have consented to being involved. But when you offer people in economically vulnerable situations potentially life-changing amounts of money to endure degrading conditions, the “voluntariness” becomes contestable.

paragraphs.cn: 这并非伦理学家所说的「知情同意」（informed consent）。这种报酬可能大到足以蒙蔽判断。而对于没有真正替代选择的人来说，说「不」可能并不构成一个现实可行的选项。
paragraphs.en: This is not what ethicists consider “informed consent”. The offer can be so large that it clouds judgement. And for people without genuine alternatives, saying “no” may not be a realistic option.

paragraphs.cn: 唐纳德森有时也让自己承受类似对待——例如他曾将自己活埋七天——这一事实加深而非减轻了上述忧虑，因为其中存在着权力不对等。他拥有制作公司，掌控着各项条件，并从内容中获利，其方式是其他参与者所无法比拟的。
paragraphs.en: The fact that Donaldson sometimes subjects himself to similar treatment, such as when he buried himself alive for seven days, deepens rather than lessens the worry, given the power asymmetries at play. He owns the production company, controls the conditions, and profits from the content in ways other participants do not.

paragraphs.cn: 当贫困，或缺乏医疗服务、清洁饮用水等政治问题被简化为娱乐时，它们经历了一种学者所称的「去政治化」（depoliticisation）过程。那些本需要集体行动、制度变革和民主审议的政治失灵，反而成了娱乐的养料。
paragraphs.en: When political problems, such as poverty, or a lack of access to healthcare or clean water, are reduced to entertainment, they undergo a form of what scholars call “depoliticisation”. Political failures that demand collective action, institutional reform and democratic deliberation instead become fodder for entertainment.

paragraphs.cn: 如果我们以为仅靠观看爆款视频就能帮助解决这些问题，那么我们就可以回避面对支撑这些问题的结构性议题。
paragraphs.en: If we think we can help solve these problems just by watching viral videos, then we can avoid facing the structural issues that underpin them.

articles.content_cn:
在兰屿这座港城，记账的手艺只从父亲传给儿子、从师傅传给徒弟，除此无人能学，都得在他人案前坐上几年才得真传。一名账房（accountant）立身的本钱，就是他承继下来的那一页记法——一张写着算法与治货防霉方子的纸，只抄给同血脉的人。兰屿的码头终年忙碌，外埠的账房偶也来泊船，但他们的纸页锁在自家箱里，城里人的纸页也锁在自家箱里，井河不犯。

一场风暴里，一名外乡人的箱子在码头上撞开，里头那一页记法被风吹散，踩进湿石板缝，等有人想起去捡已晚。账房世家的少主沈生天亮经过，本非有意，却顺手拾起看了一遍；墨迹已洗去大半，但一条治丝料绿霉的方子还能辨认。他没讨要，没被赐予，也没承继——纸页就摊在那儿，他的手又正好闲着，于是折进袖中，全无目的。

按他家的规矩，这一页本该烧掉，因为非经血脉传下的记法是手艺的污损。沈生却撞上了当季的难关：霉斑已爬进沈家货仓，而他自己箱中承继的那一页上并无治它的方子。用那外乡人的方子，等于断了血脉一脉的传承，可能被逐出宗祠、逐出父亲家门；不用，就只能眼睁睁看一季的丝料烂成烂絮，全家背债。

他还是用了那方子，丝料撑住了，沈家也熬过了这一季。他从不对人说这法子的来历，只在自己那一页上抄了一遍，把外乡人的原页锁回箱底。这类纸页即便漂到，对兰屿的账房多半也无意义，只配垫抽屉、抹笔刷；独这一页活了下来，只因那年霉气逼人，而活下来的，才被留下。

第二年开春，一个往来各港城之间、捎带闲话与零碎纸页的货郎（peddler），恰在沈家货仓借宿；天亮收拾时把抄有沈家那一页只言片语的纸片当成自己的，带去了从未与兰屿通商的内陆商埠。在那儿，一名叫武账房的同行与货郎同席饮酒，见那纸片从货郎包袱里滑出，便趁酒过数巡把那一行抄进了自己的簿子。货郎也好，武账房也好，谁都没存心搬运什么记法；那一页只是搭了个行路人的脚、搭了一张同席的桌，就过去了。

两年后霉气蔓延到那座内陆城，武家是唯一撑住丝料的货仓，他的那一页于是成了旁人想要的承继之物，可这些人既非武家血脉，也从未见过沈生、更没见过那外乡人。于是，一条生在异乡码头上的方子，从手到手、从城到城地过了过去——不是作为传家之物层层交接，而是当作某种只是被拾起、被捎带、被抄录的东西，大半抄本烂在雨里、被拿去他用，只有少数因为某个时节的急需，才被留下。

注解：这就是水平基因转移（horizontal gene transfer）——某种可遗传之物在同代个体之间绕过亲子垂直继承而流动，多数转移沉默或被清除，少数因转移之后的选择压力才被保留，而不是转移之前由意图驱动的。
articles.content_en:
In the port town of Lanhou, the craft of keeping ledgers passed strictly from father to son and master to apprentice; no one learned it except by sitting for years at another's elbow. A ledger-man's worth lay in the page of methods he inherited, a single sheet of calculations and cures for rotting cargo, copied only for those of his own blood. The quay of Lanhou was busy, and stranger ledger-men from other ports sometimes moored there, but their pages stayed in their own chests and the townspeople's pages stayed in theirs.

One storm a stranger's chest broke open on the quay, and a single page of his methods blew loose and was trampled into the wet cobbles before anyone thought to gather it. Young Shen, heir of the Shen ledger house, walked past at dawn and, without meaning to, picked it up and read it through; the ink was half washed, but one cure for green mold on silks could still be made out. He had not asked for it, had not been given it, had not inherited it. He folded it into his sleeve purely because the page was there and his hand was idle.

By his house's rule that page ought to have been burned, for a method not handed down through the bloodline was a corruption of the craft. Shen faced the season's reckoning: the mold was already creeping through the Shen warehouse, and the inherited page in his own chest held no cure for it. To use the stranger's cure was to break the lineage and risk being cast out of the guild hall and his father's house; to refuse it was to watch a season's silk rot to nothing and the family fall into debt.

He chose the cure, and the silk held, and the Shen house survived the season. He told no one where the method had come from; he only copied it once into his own page and locked the stranger's sheet away. Most such pages, had they washed up, would have meant nothing to a Lanhou ledger-man, fit only to line a drawer or wipe a brush; this one lived because the mold pressed that year, and what lived was kept.

The next spring a peddler who carried gossip and odd pages between port towns happened to sleep in the Shen warehouse; packing at dawn he mistook his own copied scrap of Shen's page for his and carried it inland to a market town that had never traded with Lanhou. There a ledger-man named Wu, set down beside the peddler at a wine bench, saw the scrap slip from the peddler's pack and copied the line into his own book over the cups. Neither the peddler nor Wu had intended to move any method; the page simply rode a traveler and a shared table.

When the mold reached that inland town two years later, Wu's house was the only one whose silk held, and his page became the page others wished to inherit, though none of them were of Wu's blood or had ever met Shen or the stranger. So a cure born on a foreign quay crossed from hand to hand and town to town, not as an heirloom handed down but as something merely picked up, carried, and copied, most copies lost to rain and reuse and a few preserved only because a season demanded them.

Annotation: This is horizontal gene transfer (水平基因转移)—the movement of something heritable between contemporaries, bypassing parent-to-offspring inheritance, most transfers silent or discarded and only a few kept because selection acts after the transfer, not before.

articles.title: 环围上的瞭望塔
articles.author: AI Parable (inspired by Amanda Askell)
articles.summary: 围城逼近时，我手里只有三种哨：一根立石，三名游哨。立石生根不动，死守一个朝向；游哨沿线游走，扫开一道走廊，却看不见静止之物。哪一种单凭自身都守不住一个村子。于是我做了每个守围人都会做的事：让它们混。这不是我情愿的选择——当环围必须同时四面受防，哨与哨相混就只是它们必然成为的样子：一根立石与三名游哨等
articles.content_cn:
围城逼近时，我手里只有三种哨：一根立石，三名游哨。立石生根不动，死守一个朝向；游哨沿线游走，扫开一道走廊，却看不见静止之物。哪一种单凭自身都守不住一个村子。于是我做了每个守围人都会做的事：让它们混。这不是我情愿的选择——当环围必须同时四面受防，哨与哨相混就只是它们必然成为的样子：一根立石与三名游哨等份相融，化为四名全无分别的守望者，谁也不再是纯立石或纯游哨，各占四分之一的扎根与四分之三的游走。

这四名既然全无分别，便容不得其中一个离另一个更近。它们彼此推开，直到各自站定在一座矮矮的金字塔状地基的一角，每一道目光都尽可能远离邻者的目光，远到山势所容许的极限。事后我步量过：从一处到下一处，约莫一百零九又二分之一步，在院子中心点丈量。四座瞭望塔，四名等一的守望者，那些角度是它们自身的等一强加于它们的——不是我的意志，从来不是我的意志。

可代价随之而来。一名被拦下、不让相混、保持完整个体的游哨，其本性会朝第二层楼漂去——朝头顶上方、在线之外经过的东西。若我把三名游哨全倒入塔中，那份漂游之能便耗尽了，高处的通路便无人看顾。所以遇上从上方袭来的敌手，我不敢把四个全花掉：我留下一游哨不混，专守上层通路，只把立石与两名游哨相融。三座全无分别的塔结成，平铺在田野上，各占三分之一的扎根；又因为它们是三，等一，便张开成彼此相距一百二十步。

而当路本身成了威胁——一条直道，一列长矛直刺——连三座塔都是浪费。我留下两名游哨不混，只把立石与一名游哨相融。两名全无分别的守望者结成，两名既等一，便只能退守到那条道的两端，相距一百八十步，中间的路从两头被看住。那两名我留下的、不相混的，则一同游走在上层通路，在同一条路上布下第二层、更细的一种守望。

这便是代价的全部，我记下它，因为旁人不会记：留得越多，上层的守望越强，可地上的塔就越稀；倒进塔的越多，环围越厚，可高处的通路便失明。我从来没有可能把四者同时留给自己、又尽付于塔。每一夜我都做这笔交易——多少扎根花在地上，多少游走省给上方漂游之物——而村子的形状，塔的数目与塔之间的角度，不由我的任何意愿决定，只由我让每种各有多少相融而定。

注解：这个概念是轨道杂化（orbital hybridization）。一个原子的原初轨道——一个 s 与三个 p——按比例线性叠加成一组等价的杂化轨道；混入多少个 p 决定杂化类型，类型决定几何构型与角度（sp3 给出四面体四个方向，约 109.5°；sp2 给出平面三个方向，120°，留一个 p 用以形成 π 键；sp 给出直线两个方向，180°，留两个 p 用以形成两个 π 键）。此过程是量子力学的描述，本身不含意图。

When the siege closed in, I had three kinds of sentries in my hands, and nothing else: one Stele, three Roamers. A Stele stands rooted, staring down a single bearing; a Roamer paces a line, sweeping a corridor but blind to whatever lies still. Neither kind alone can hold a village. So I did what any keeper does: I let them mix. I did not choose it from desire; the mixing is simply what sentries become when the perimeter must be held from all sides at once — one Stele blended with three Roamers, in equal shares, resolves into four identical watchers, none of them any longer pure Stele or pure Roamer, each one a quarter rooted and three-quarters roving.

And these four, being made identical, would not suffer one of them to sit closer to another. They pushed apart until each stood at one corner of a squat pyramid of ground, each bearing's gaze as far from its neighbours' as the hills allowed. I paced it off afterwards: roughly a hundred and nine and a half paces from one to the next, measured at the heart of the yard. Four watchtowers, four equal watchers, the angles forced on them by their own equality — not by my will, never by my will.

But then came the harder cost. A Roamer kept back from the mixing, left unblended and whole, drifts of its nature toward the second story — toward whatever passes overhead, above the line. If I pour all three Roamers into the towers, that drifting skill is spent, and the high lane goes unwatched. So against a foe that strikes from above, I dared not spend all four: I held one Roamer back, unmixed, for the upper lane, and blended only the Stele with two Roamers. Three identical towers formed, spread flat across the field, each a third rooted; and because there were three of them, equal, they fanned to a hundred and twenty paces apart.

And when the road itself became the threat — one straight lane, one thrusting column — even three towers was waste. I held back two Roamers whole, and blended only the Stele with one Roamer. Two identical watchers formed, and two being equal, they could only fall back to opposite ends of the lane, a hundred and eighty paces apart, the road between them watched from both ends. The two I had kept back, unblended, roamed the upper lanes together and made a second, thinner kind of watch over that same road.

Here is the whole of my cost, and I record it because no one else will: the more I hold back, the stronger the upper watch, but the thinner the towers on the ground; the more I pour into the towers, the stouter the perimeter, but the high lanes go blind. I never get to keep all four to myself and to the towers at once. Every night I make this trade — how much of the rooted to spend on the ground, how much of the roving to spare for what drifts above — and the village's shape, the count of its towers and the angles between them, is decided not by any wish of mine but simply by how much of each kind I let blend.

Annotation: The concept is orbital hybridization. An atom's original orbitals — one s and three p — combine linearly into a set of equivalent hybrid orbitals; how many p are mixed in decides the type, and the type decides the geometry and angles (sp3 gives four tetrahedral directions at about 109.5 degrees, sp2 gives three planar directions at 120 degrees with one p left over for a pi bond, sp gives two linear directions at 180 degrees with two p left over). The process is a quantum-mechanical description with no intent behind it.
