paragraphs.cn: 然而，经过恰当的修正和审慎的运用之后，「专制」是理解民主在全球所面临新威胁时一个不可或缺的关键词——这些威胁既存在于俄罗斯、伊朗、中国、沙特阿拉伯、古巴和越南等迥然不同的政体之中，也来自煽动家及其拥趸在土耳其（Türkiye）、以色列和唐纳德·特朗普（Donald Trump）治下的美国等国所发起的、与之并行且相互重叠的对分权式民主的攻击。
paragraphs.en: But when suitably revised and carefully deployed, despotism is an indispensable keyword for making sense of the new global threats to democracy in polities as different as Russia, Iran, China, Saudi Arabia, Cuba and Vietnam, but also by the parallel and overlapping attacks on power-sharing democracy led by demagogues and their admirers in countries such as Türkiye, Israel and Donald Trump’s America.

paragraphs.cn: 这种煽动家与暴君之间奇特联盟在全球范围内的生长绝非偶然。它应当令每一个有思想的人感到困惑和忧虑，并需要被加以理解。
paragraphs.en: This worldwide growth of a strange alliance between demagogues and despots is no coincidence. It ought to puzzle and worry every thinking person, and it needs to be understood.

paragraphs.cn: 作为一种同时为煽动家和暴君所实践的统治类型，专制是一种违抗政治引力定律的权力运作方式。它是一种特殊而虚假的民主类型，由精于操纵与干预民众生活、笼络其支持并赢得其服从的统治者所主导。
paragraphs.en: Considered as a type of rule practised by both demagogues and despots, despotism is a way of handling power that defies the laws of political gravity. It’s a peculiarly fake type of democracy led by rulers skilled in the arts of manipulating and meddling with people’s lives, marshalling their support and winning their obedience.

paragraphs.cn: 专制以其臣民的自愿奴役为养料。那些把专制视为镇压、恐惧与赤裸暴力之同义词的人大错特错。专制权力无法恰当地通过锤与钉的比喻来理解；它需要以金属锉屑被磁铁吸引的方式来思考。
paragraphs.en: Despotism feeds upon the voluntary servitude of its subjects. Those who think despotism is a synonym for repression, fear and raw force are profoundly mistaken. Despotic power can’t properly be understood through similes of hammers and nails; it requires thinking in terms of the attraction of metal filings to magnets.

paragraphs.cn: 在实践中，暴君是诱惑、欺骗与控制的大师。他们校准对暴力的使用，并借助一套圆滑的手段——包括操纵选举胜利——来赢得被统治者的顺服与忠诚。在政府慷慨、猖獗的庇护、成袋的金钱、就业创造计划、法律诡计，以及喋喋不休地谈论捍卫「人民」以抵御其敌人的话语的润滑下，专制培育着其臣民——包括中产阶级的重要阶层、技术与非技术工人以及穷人——温顺的屈从。
paragraphs.en: In practice, despots are masters of seduction, deception and control. They calibrate their use of violence and manage, using a combination of slick means, including rigged election victories, to win the submission and loyalty of the ruled. Oiled by government largesse, rampant patronage, bags of money, job creation programs, legal trickery and endless talk of defending “the people” against its foes, despotism nurtures the docile subservience of its subjects, including important sections of the middle classes, skilled and unskilled workers, and the poor.

paragraphs.cn: 其结果是：自上而下的权力金字塔取得胜利，成功地在本国赢得数以百万计的支持者，并在其所统治国家的疆界之外赢得众多追随者与朋友。
paragraphs.en: The result: the triumph of top-down pyramids of power that manage to win millions of supporters at home and acolytes and friends well beyond the borders of the states they rule.

paragraphs.cn: 尤其令人担忧的是，专制的精神具有传染性。暴君与煽动家成群结队地狩猎。他们的混杂与蓄意合作毫无节制。煽动家是正在形成中的暴君。暴君则是煽动家渴望成为的模样。
paragraphs.en: What’s especially worrying is that the spirit of despotism is contagious. Despots and demagogues hunt in packs. Their promiscuity and wilful cooperation know no limits. Demagogues are despots in the making. Despots are what demagogues would like to be.

paragraphs.cn: 回想一下那个时刻：2024 年 7 月，在莫斯科大中央宫（Grand Central Palace）一场金碧辉煌的仪式上，面临国际刑事法院逮捕令的俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京（Vladimir Putin），授予他的「亲爱的朋友」、印度总理纳伦德拉·莫迪（Narendra Modi）俄罗斯最高文职荣誉——圣安德烈使徒勋章（Order of St Andrew the Apostle）。
paragraphs.en: Consider the moment, in July 2024, when in a gilded ceremony in Moscow’s Grand Central Palace, Russian president Vladimir Putin, who faces an arrest warrant from the International Criminal Court, conferred upon his “dear friend”, Indian president Narendra Modi, Russia’s highest civilian honour, the Order of St Andrew the Apostle.

paragraphs.cn: 再想一想那样一个盛大登场时刻：一位野心勃勃的暴君受到更老练的同侪张开双臂和丰厚礼物的迎接——特朗普 2025 年 5 月对西亚的旋风式访问。
paragraphs.en: Now consider the grand showtime moment when an aspiring despot was greeted with open arms and lavish gifts by his more seasoned counterparts: Trump’s whirlwind May 2025 tour of west Asia.

paragraphs.cn: 在沙特阿拉伯、阿联酋和卡塔尔，这位地道的美国煽动家被铺天盖地地赐予他长久渴望的荣誉与认可。豪华的 F-15 战斗机护航。淡紫色与红色的地毯、骑乘的骆驼和女子甩发的欢迎仪式。骑白马的骑手和披挂星条旗的特斯拉赛博皮卡。宏伟的大理石厅堂、璀璨的水晶吊灯、最高的民事勋章，包括一条纯金项链。
paragraphs.en: In Saudi Arabia, the UAE and Qatar, the all-American demagogue was showered with the honour and recognition he had long craved. Lavish F-15 fighter jet escorts. Lavender and red carpets, mounted camels and women’s hair-flipping welcome ceremonies. Riders on white horses and Tesla cybertrucks sporting stars and stripes. Grand marbled halls, dazzling crystal chandeliers, the highest civil decorations, including a pure gold necklace.

paragraphs.cn: 接着是世界第一高楼，高达半英里有余，被点亮成美国国旗的图案。在卡塔尔该地区最大的美军基地举行的一场竞选式集会。
paragraphs.en: Then there was the world’s tallest building, more than half a mile high, lit up with an image of the American flag. A campaign-style rally at the region’s largest US military base in Qatar.

paragraphs.cn: 还有那些实质性成果：万亿美元级的商业与防务合同，在贪婪与名望的见证下由贪欲签署。与沙特阿拉伯建立联合核能项目的计划。与阿联酋达成的进口最先进 AI 芯片的初步协议。卡塔尔赠送的、特朗普打算在离任后留为己用的一架豪华喷气式客机的厚礼——凡此种种，皆印证了这一点：在这些动荡之时，煽动家与暴君必须同飞共济、安全团结。
paragraphs.en: And the material deliverables: trillion-dollar business and defence contracts, signed by cupidity in the presence of greed and fame. Plans (with Saudi Arabia) to establish a joint nuclear energy program. A preliminary agreement (with UAE) to import the most advanced AI chips. A lavish gift (from Qatar) of a luxury jet Trump intends to keep whenever he leaves office – all in confirmation of the point that, in these times of turbulence, demagogues and despots must fly together in safety and solidarity.

paragraphs.cn: 记者、知识分子和公民日益意识到，这种专制排场与兄弟情谊式权力的展示，正在侵蚀民主的自由与平等承诺。对这些趋势的不祥预感正在蔓延。悲观主义颇为时兴。
paragraphs.en: There’s growing awareness among journalists, intellectuals and citizens that such displays of despotic pomp and bromance power are undermining the freedoms and egalitarian promises of democracy. A sense of foreboding about these trends is spreading. Pessimism is fashionable.

paragraphs.cn: 在我写下这些文字之时，一位南非同事来信，说我们的时代何其阴郁。她评论道，我们的世界仿佛正穿过一个「增强的残暴」（augmented brutality，亦是一款流行电子游戏之名）的时代。我的同事告诉我，随着既有的专制政权和煽动家能为所欲为的限度似乎越来越少，我们的伦理良知、道德顾虑以及对滥权行为的公愤，正在萎缩消亡。
paragraphs.en: As I write these lines, a South African colleague is in touch to say how grim are our times. She remarks that our world feels as if it’s passing through an era of “augmented brutality” (also the name of a popular video game). With seemingly ever fewer brakes upon what established despotic regimes and demagogues can get away with, my colleague tells me, our ethical conscience, moral qualms and public outrage against abuses of power are withering away.

paragraphs.cn: 当我问及其他同事，我们这些病态的民主正走向何方时，他们预测了几种相互矛盾但同样阴沉的反乌托邦未来。一些人认为，现实正迅速赶上奥威尔（Orwell）在《一九八四》（Nineteen Eighty-Four）中所勾勒的那个被美化版的未来。另一些同事则警告说正在向「独裁」「暴政」或「威权主义」「倒退」，其典型便是那些在驯服的臣民头上挥舞言辞与刀剑的强人——弗拉基米尔·普京、哈维尔·米莱（Javier Milei）、唐纳德·特朗普、习近平、亚历山大·卢卡申科（Alexander Lukashenko）。
paragraphs.en: When I ask other colleagues where our diseased democracies are heading, they predict several conflicting but equally gloomy dystopian futures. Some argue that reality is fast catching up with a prettified version of the future sketched in Orwell’s Nineteen Eighty-Four. Other colleagues warn of “backsliding” towards “autocracy”, “tyranny” or “authoritarianism”, exemplified by strongmen – Vladimir Putin, Javier Milei, Donald Trump, Xi Jinping, Alexander Lukashenko – who wield words and wave swords over the heads of their cowed subjects.

paragraphs.cn: 他们把独裁说成是一种掌握在拥有绝对权力的单一统治者手中的政治制度。在他们看来，正如在苏格拉底（Socrates）看来一样，暴政是一种危险而不义的统治类型，由一个被无底欲望吞噬的强人所施行，一心欲借「欺诈与武力」劫掠惊恐臣民的财产、生计与自由。
paragraphs.en: They speak of autocracy as a political system in the hands of a sole ruler with absolute power. Tyranny is, for them, as it was for Socrates, a dangerously unjust type of rule by a strong man consumed by lawless desires bent on robbing through “fraud and force” the property, livelihoods and freedoms of their frightened subjects.

paragraphs.cn: 还有另一些同事，则惧怕他们所称的「法西斯主义」或「新法西斯主义」卷土重来。他们把当今趋势比作昔日的欧洲和亚洲极权政权——那些动员整个社会、对每个公民的私生活实行全面控制的政权。
paragraphs.en: Still other colleagues dread the return of what they call “fascism”, or “neo-fascism”. They liken present-day trends to past European and Asian totalitarian regimes that mobilised whole societies and exercised complete control over every citizen’s private life.

paragraphs.cn: 据这些同事所言，民主世界到处都面临着昔年极权政权可能在更高层次上重演的局面。他们说，正如墨索里尼（Mussolini）的意大利、希特勒（Hitler）的德国和毛泽东（Mao）的中国曾将其臣民判处永恒的狂热，如今的新法西斯也在呼吁「人民」关心自己的未来。
paragraphs.en: According to these colleagues, the democratic world is everywhere confronted with the possible repeat on a higher level of the totalitarian regimes of yesteryear. Just as Mussolini’s Italy, Hitler’s Germany and Mao’s China condemned their subjects to perpetual enthusiasm, so the new fascists call on “the people” to care about their future, they say.

paragraphs.cn: 意大利法西斯主义的自封哲学家乔瓦尼·真蒂莱（Giovanni Gentile），捕捉到了那种如今据说重新流行的旧时精神。他写道：「法西斯主义的主要功绩之一」，在于它「逐步迫使所有那些曾经站在窗边旁观的人走到街上来，去践行法西斯主义，甚至以法西斯主义去反对法西斯主义」。
paragraphs.en: The self-appointed philosopher of Italian fascism, Giovanni Gentile, captured the old spirit that’s now said to be back in vogue. “Among the major merits of fascism,” he wrote, was that it “obliged little by little all those who once stood at the window to come down into the streets, to practise fascism even against fascism.”

paragraphs.cn: 与此相似，民主世界正在回到那样一个时代：数以百万计的人被精心编排的报纸、广播和电影表演所俘获，这些表演由演艺型煽动家领衔，他们身着正装、军装和骑马装，或是赤膊上阵帮助汗流浃背的劳工收割庄稼（这是墨索里尼的拿手好戏）。
paragraphs.en: Similarly, the democratic world is returning to the time when millions of people were captivated by skilfully orchestrated newspaper, radio and film performances led by showbiz demagogues dressed in formal attire, military uniforms and riding gear, or stripped to the waist helping sweating labourers gather the harvest (Mussolini’s specialty).

paragraphs.cn: 由名为德国选择党（AfD）、骄傲男孩（Proud Boys）和瑞典新纳粹「北欧抵抗运动」（NMR）之类的团体和政党所组织的群众集会，又重新时髦起来。
paragraphs.en: Public rallies organised by groups and parties with names like Alternative for Germany (AfD), Proud Boys and Sweden’s neo-Nazi Nordic Resistance Movement (NMR) are back in fashion.

paragraphs.cn: 公民们再次齐声欢呼，在由对暴虐煽动家的颂扬所搭就的舞台上整齐行进，被怀旧情绪、民族自豪感和对外国人的仇恨所鼓动，被充满蛊惑性的社交媒体帖文和狡黠领袖的公开演讲所驱策——这些领袖让你无处可藏，逃不过法西斯的声音。
paragraphs.en: Citizens are again celebrating in unity, marching in step across the stage fabricated from the glorification of bully demagogues, emboldened by nostalgia, national pride and hatred of foreigners, urged on by electrifying social media postings and public speeches by beguilingly sly leaders who leave no place to hide from the fascist voice.

paragraphs.cn: 这套陈旧词汇——独裁、暴政、威权主义、法西斯主义、极权主义——的一个缺点在于：这些词使我们盲目，看不到当下所发生之事并非只是对过去的重演。我们的时代不仅与之不同。其陌生性使我们无法认识到，各民主国家正在漂向一个世界历史上前所未见的专制新纪元。
paragraphs.en: One shortcoming of this dog-eared lexicon – autocracy, tyranny, authoritarianism, fascism, totalitarianism – is that these words blind us from seeing that what is happening today is not merely a repetition of the past. Our times are not just different. Their strangeness prevents us from understanding that democracies are drifting into a new age of despotism of a kind never seen before in world history.

paragraphs.cn: 一个格外引人注目的事实是，「民主」与「独裁」、「暴政」与「威权主义」之间那些常见的区分，在理解这一专制新纪元时，实践中已变得极为成问题且无所助益。
paragraphs.en: An especially striking fact is that the commonplace distinctions between “democracy” and “autocracy”, “tyranny” and “authoritarianism” have in practice become deeply problematic and unhelpful in making sense of this new age of despotism.

paragraphs.cn: 首先，请看那些据称相互敌对的政权如何彼此趋同，被国家典礼、外交合作、跨境贸易与投资、武器交易，以及西方银行和管理咨询公司逐利的机会主义捆绑在一起——这些银行和咨询公司多年来厚颜无耻地为沙特阿拉伯、土耳其、中国和俄罗斯等国的大型国有及国家主导企业提供服务。
paragraphs.en: For a start, consider how supposedly antagonistic regimes find themselves converging, bound together by state ceremonies, diplomatic cooperation, cross-border trade and investments, weapons deals, and the profit-seeking opportunism of Western banks and management consultants, who have, for many years, brazenly serviced large state-owned and state-guided corporations in countries such as Saudi Arabia, Türkiye, China and Russia.

paragraphs.cn: 同样引人注目的是，财富不平等、旋转门、黑金腐败、操纵的选举、假新闻、国家审查、监控和高压警务——这些在沙特阿拉伯、俄罗斯、中国和乌兹别克斯坦等政权中显而易见的现象——正在现有民主国家的疆界之内强势登场，最为明显的，便是在那个让唐纳德·特朗普再次当选的国家。
paragraphs.en: Equally striking is the way the wealth inequalities, revolving doors, dark money corruption, manipulated elections, fake news, state censorship, surveillance and heavy-handed policing – evident in regimes such as Saudi Arabia, Russia, China and Uzbekistan – are making strong appearances within the borders of existing democracies, most obviously in the country that reelected Donald Trump.

paragraphs.cn: 然而，我们应当注意，这还不是全部。日益显而易见的是，那些抱负不凡的、已然确立的分权式宪政民主，可以多么轻易而迅速地蜕变为专制政权。
paragraphs.en: But that’s not all, we should note. What is becoming plain to see is how aspiring and established power-sharing constitutional democracies can easily and quickly be transformed into despotic regimes.

paragraphs.cn: 在所谓向民主转型的进程中——遍布中亚，以及 1989—91 年苏联解体后的俄罗斯和白俄罗斯——这种反民主的退化是常态，而非例外。在其他地方，专制也盛行于这样一些国家：如老挝和柬埔寨，在 1970 年代种族灭绝之后王权复辟之际；又如伊朗，在 1979 年伊斯兰革命那场剧烈动荡之后。
paragraphs.en: This anti-democratic degeneration has been the rule, not the exception, in the so-called transitions to democracy throughout central Asia, and in Russia and Belarus following the collapse of the Soviet Union during the years 1989–91. Elsewhere, despotism has prevailed in countries, such as Laos and Cambodia, following the restoration of monarchy after the genocide of the 1970s, and in Iran after the dramatic upheavals of the 1979 Islamic Revolution.

paragraphs.cn: 由于对权力饥渴的煽动家当选上台，专制的精神与实质也扎根于政治学家们曾经所称的巩固民主之中——最初是在地缘政治上不那么重要的风向标国家，如塞尔维亚，而如今则是在巴西、波兰等重要国家，以及美利坚帝国的腹地。
paragraphs.en: Thanks to the election of power-hungry demagogues, the spirit and substance of despotism has also taken root in what political scientists once called consolidated democracies, initially in geopolitically less significant bellwether countries, such as Serbia, and nowadays in important states such as Brazil and Poland, and in the heartlands of the American empire.

paragraphs.cn: 最不明显、且多少有些悖谬的，是我们这个时代既有的专制政权模仿其所谓「民主」对手之手法的方式。今日所谓的暴政与独裁——我称其为专制，因为其统治者是诱惑性权力艺术的大师——寄生在分权式民主那些被败坏的理想与失败之上。
paragraphs.en: Least obvious, and more than a little paradoxical, is the manner in which the established despotic regimes of our era mimic the methods of their so-called “democratic” rivals. Today’s so-called tyrannies and autocracies – I call them despotisms because their rulers are masters of the arts of seductive power – are parasitical upon the corrupted ideals and failures of power-sharing democracy.

paragraphs.cn: 但不止于此，俄罗斯、中国、沙特阿拉伯、伊朗和其他既有的专制政体，例证了一种新型伪民主政府，由精于操纵臣民以使其顺从自身图谋的统治者所主导。
paragraphs.en: But more than that, Russia, China, Saudi Arabia, Iran and other established despotisms exemplify a strange new type of pseudo-democratic government led by rulers skilled in manipulating their subjects into conformity to their designs.

paragraphs.cn: 作为一种统治形式，这些专制是世上前所未见之物。它们比许多观察者所设想的更为稳固、更具吸引力，也更善于应对政治地震和治理人民。
paragraphs.en: Considered as a form of rule, these despotisms are something new under the sun. They are more stable, more attractive and better at managing political earthquakes and governing people than many observers suppose.

paragraphs.cn: 尽管易受内部机能失调、外部冲击、战争和持续的公众抵抗之扰，这些专制政府学会了在重压之下进行统治的技艺。对行使权力的技术进行试错式的改进与完善是它们的专长，也是它们在世界事务中政治掌控力日益收紧的关键解释所在——同样，它们那精明过人的诱惑力也是如此。
paragraphs.en: Despite their vulnerability to internal dysfunctions, external shocks, wars and chronic public resistance, these despotic governments learn the arts of ruling under duress. Trial-and-error improvement and perfection of the techniques of exercising power are their specialty, and a key explanation of their tightening political grip in world affairs, as is their whip-smart seductiveness.

paragraphs.cn: 值得铭记的是，希腊语原词 despotēs——源自 dómos（房屋）与 pósis（丈夫、配偶）——指的是一位仁慈而全能的一家之主，受家中妇女、儿童与奴隶的敬畏与尊崇。后来，在基督教圈子中，该词指涉上帝，以及拜占庭帝国的主教与宗主教——其权力由其臣民以权威加以祝福，这些臣民在一切事务上皆有义务顺从，因为他们受益于其主人的仁慈与善行。
paragraphs.en: It’s worth remembering that the original Greek term despótēs – from dómos (house) and pósis (husband, spouse) – referred to a benevolent and all-powerful master of a household, held in reverence and respect by its women, children and slaves. It later referred, in Christian circles, to God and to the bishops and patriarchs of the Byzantine Empire, whose power was blessed with authority by their subjects, who were duty bound to submit in all matters because they benefited from their masters’ kindness and good works.

paragraphs.cn: 今日的暴君渴望站在他们的位置上。他们专长于说服其臣民服从必然，并把它称为自由。他们要「人民」以为情况正变得越来越好、越来越大，而且对现存秩序而言别无切实可行的替代方案。他们诱惑，而不仅仅是镇压。
paragraphs.en: Today’s despots aspire to stand in their shoes. They specialise in convincing their subjects to obey necessity and call it freedom. They want “the people” to suppose things are getting better and bigger, and that there is no viable alternative to the present order. They seduce rather than merely repress.

paragraphs.cn: 在这个意义上，我们这个时代的专制是监护型权力的尖端形态，一种被媒体浸透的政治统治类型，它实现了许多先前的观察者认为不可能之事：通过自上而下、亲民的治理技术——选举、幸福论坛、在线问答门户、民意抽样和反腐机构——赢得臣民经过算计的支持与好感，从而支配他们。
paragraphs.en: In this sense, the despotisms of our age are state-of-the-art forms of tutelary power, a type of media-saturated political rule that achieves something many previous observers thought impossible: they dominate their subjects by winning their calculated support and affection by means of top-down, people-friendly techniques of government, elections, happiness forums, online Q&A portals, public opinion sampling and anti-corruption agencies.

paragraphs.cn: 这些由暴君运转的政权，是所谓民主国家中的煽动家所渴望的专制的更完美、更成熟形态。它们是幻影民主（phantom democracies）。
paragraphs.en: These regimes run by despots are more perfect and mature forms of the despotism yearned for by demagogues in so-named democracies. They are phantom democracies.

paragraphs.cn: 既有专制政权、美国及其他所谓民主国家之间正在发生的寻热式吸引与慢动作趋同，或许会令我们惊讶、震惊与困惑。其实不必如此。「民主」与「独裁」之间语义分野的瓦解，以及向幻影民主的全球性漂移，是有着更古老、更深远根源的趋势。
paragraphs.en: That there are heat-seeking attractions and slow-motion convergences taking place between established despotic regimes, the United States and other so-named democracies, might surprise, shock and puzzle us. It shouldn’t. The breakdown of the semantic division between “democracy” and “autocracy” and the global drift towards phantom democracy are trends that have older and deeper roots.

paragraphs.cn: 要理解推动专制在全球生长的那种陌生而新颖的权力动力学，我们必须求诸历史，检视那些对于其而言全球专制的到来本不足为奇的思想家与作家。
paragraphs.en: To understand the strange new power dynamics fuelling the worldwide growth of despotism, we must turn to history to examine the thinkers and writers for whom the coming of global despotism would have been unsurprising.

paragraphs.cn: 因此，让我们把时钟倒拨一百年，回到以选举为中心的民主斗争和「全民普选」走向成熟的关键时刻。许多观察者预言它将成为地球上唯一的政治博弈。一位美国总统，伍德罗·威尔逊（Woodrow Wilson），呼吁建立一个「让民主安全存在」的世界，一种建立在「被治者之同意」之上的「公正政府」。
paragraphs.en: Let’s therefore turn back the clock a hundred years, to the crucial moment when the struggle for election-centred democracy and “votes for all” came of age. Many observers predicted it would become the only political game on Earth. An American president, Woodrow Wilson, called for a world “made safe for democracy”, a form of “just government” that rested upon “the consent of the governed”.

paragraphs.cn: 在第一次世界大战那场灾难性的余波中，帝国到处土崩瓦解，革命的火焰舔舐着富人和权贵的后股，多个大陆上「人民」争取投票权的诉求节节胜利，此时有两位作家从人群中脱颖而出。一位委内瑞拉人，劳雷亚诺·巴耶尼利亚·兰斯（Laureano Vallenilla Lanz，1870—1936），和一位德国人，马克斯·韦伯（Max Weber，1864—1920），做出了预测，这些预测对于理解今日令人不安的时局有着惊人的相关性。
paragraphs.en: In the catastrophic aftermath of the first world war, with empires everywhere collapsing, the flames of revolution licking the backsides of the rich and powerful, and demands for the right of “the people” to vote prevailing on several continents, two writers in particular stand out from the crowd. A Venezuelan named Laureano Vallenilla Lanz (1870–1936) and a German, Max Weber (1864–1920), made predictions that have an uncanny relevance for understanding today’s troubling times.

paragraphs.cn: 这些作家并非超凡脱俗的政治天才。他们是善于思考的探索者，对民主的命运怀有好奇与关切，是在一个为剧烈的地缘政治与社会经济剧变所折磨的时期，为民众权力新纪元的可能后果绘制地图的探险者。
paragraphs.en: These writers weren’t timeless political geniuses. They were thoughtful explorers, curious and concerned about democracy’s fate, adventurers mapping out the likely consequences of the new age of people power in a period racked by enormous geopolitical and socio-economic upheavals.

paragraphs.cn: 兰斯确信，议会民主是一个行不通的理想。他转而拥护一种新型的专制政府，其权威奠基于「人民」。他向那些对矛盾修辞心存疑虑的语法学家掷下挑战书，将其称作「民主的凯撒主义」（democratic Caesarism）：一种政治制度，其统治者将利用周期性选举以及种种「软」「硬」实力形式，对其顺从的臣民实行绝对统治。
paragraphs.en: Lanz was sure that parliamentary democracy was an unworkable ideal. He instead championed a new form of despotic government whose authority was based on “the people”. He threw down the gauntlet to grammarians suspicious of oxymorons by calling it “democratic Caesarism”: a political system whose rulers would use periodic elections and various forms of “soft” and “hard” power to rule absolutely over their compliant subjects.

paragraphs.cn: 与之相对，韦伯则担心，他所支持的自由公正选举与议会民主的到来，会滋生煽动家的崛起：这些强人无法容忍制衡，会以「人民」之名竭尽所能，将议会民主转化成他所称的「诉诸公民投票的领袖民主」（plebiscitarian leader democracy）。
paragraphs.en: In contrast, Weber feared that the advent of free and fair elections and parliamentary democracy, which he supported, would spawn the rise of demagogues: strongmen impatient with checks and balances, who in the name of “the people” would do everything they could to transform parliamentary democracy into what he called “plebiscitarian leader democracy”.

paragraphs.cn: 兰斯是一位博学者——学者、参议员、外交官、国家档案馆馆长，且多年担任加拉加斯主要报纸《新日报》（El Nuevo Diario，委内瑞拉政府的非正式喉舌）的主编。他的著作《民主的凯撒主义》（Cesarismo democrático）于 1919 年出版，可惜至今未译成英文。
paragraphs.en: Lanz was a polymath scholar, senator, diplomat, national archives director and, for many years, editor of the leading Caracas newspaper El Nuevo Diario, the Venezuelan government’s unofficial mouthpiece. His book Cesarismo democrático, published in 1919, is unfortunately still not translated into English.

paragraphs.cn: 这着实可惜，因为在大胡安·维森特·戈麦斯将军（General Juan Vicente Gómez）27 年的独裁专政（1908—35）期间——兰斯为其效力，充当其御用文人——兰斯预见到：民主的各项理想，宽泛地理解为以定期选举代表进入议会为基础的民众自治，能够轻易地被各地的煽动家所利用，以臻于完善一种人类历史上前所未见的统治新类型。
paragraphs.en: That’s a pity, considering that during the 27-year caudillo dictatorship (1908–35) of General Juan Vicente Gómez, for whom he served as in-house intellectual, Lanz foresaw that the ideals of democracy, loosely understood as popular self-government based on the periodic election of representatives to a parliament, could readily be harnessed by demagogues everywhere to perfect a new type of rule unknown in previous human history.

paragraphs.cn: 他推论道，带有民主装饰与外衣的铁腕政府是可能、必要且可取的。精明的统治者没有理由惧怕普选权、定期选举和那些被冠以「民主」之名的一切附属物件的到来。
paragraphs.en: Strong-armed government with democratic trimmings and trappings was possible, necessary and desirable, he reasoned. Smart rulers had no reason to fear the advent of the universal franchise, periodic elections and the other paraphernalia of what was called “democracy”.

paragraphs.cn: 恰恰相反，如果统治者把手中的牌打得妙，以「人民」之名的自治机制便可以被用来招募他们，组建一支忠于某个强人统治者的支持者大军，而该强人将定期赢得他们的选票，从而确认他们忠实的从属地位。
paragraphs.en: On the contrary, if rulers played their hands well, the mechanisms of self-government, in the name of “the people”, could be used to recruit them into an army of supporters loyal to a strong ruler, who would periodically win their votes and thus confirm their faithful subordination.

paragraphs.cn: 兰斯在任何直接意义上都不是民主派。他厌恶人类境况之中那种「自发的无政府状态」。群众不可信赖。他们反复无常，为激情所激荡，饱受无知与傲慢之苦，其发作经常给政府领域带来巨大的社会失序与暴力事件。
paragraphs.en: Lanz was no democrat in any straightforward sense. He detested the “spontaneous anarchy” within the human condition. The masses weren’t to be trusted. Fickle, excited by their passions, plagued by ignorance and arrogance, their outbursts regularly bring great social disorders and episodes of violence into the field of government.

paragraphs.cn: 兰斯确信，托马斯·霍布斯（Thomas Hobbes）那个古老的「人对人是狼」（homo homini lupus）原则是正确的。但他相信，强制性的铁腕统治能够赢得人民的爱戴与支持。政治领导权必须由一个深得民心的强人来行使——他称之为「不可或缺的宪兵」——由其将群众的能量导向一种以稳定社会关系为基础的有效政府的真正民主秩序。
paragraphs.en: Lanz was convinced that the old Thomas Hobbes principle of homo homini lupus (man is a wolf to other men) was correct. But he believed mandatory heavy-handed rule could win the people’s affection and support. Political leadership had to be exercised by a popular strongman – a “necessary gendarme”, he termed it – who would channel the energies of the masses towards a genuinely democratic order of effective government based on stable social relations.

paragraphs.cn: 在一个尽管离奇却颇具创造性的思想转折中，兰斯推论道，后殖民时期委内瑞拉及其他国家动荡失序的历史证明：若没有一位强人领袖，人民便无法成为其真正的自我。他倡导一种新型政治腹语术。正如摩西（Moses）从磐石中寻得水源，领袖将解除人民所受的不义，并向他们指明通往民众自我实现之应许之地的道路。
paragraphs.en: In a remarkably creative if bizarre turn of thinking, Lanz reasoned that the history of turbulent disorder in postcolonial Venezuela and other countries proved that without a strongman leader the people couldn’t become their true selves. He urged a new form of political ventriloquism. Like Moses, who divined water from a rock, the leader would relieve the people of injustice and show them the way to a promised land of popular self-fulfilment.

paragraphs.cn: 随着选举民主的到来，「大众之无知与狂热」既能被驯服，也能被提炼，所借助的乃是激励人们自力更生、奋发向上的铁腕领导——它提升男男女女，使其获得与他人享有平等相伴随的尊严。
paragraphs.en: With the advent of electoral democracy, the “ignorance and fanaticism of the popular masses” could be both tamed and refined by means of strong-armed leadership that galvanised people to pull themselves up by their bootstraps, elevating men and women to the concomitant dignity that comes with the enjoyment of equality with others.

paragraphs.cn: 兰斯力主并预言，这种新型的「民主的凯撒主义」将释放群众的力量，满足他们「无意识的渴望」，治愈他们受伤的自尊，使他们感到自己在决定世界命运中是被人需要、举足轻重的。
paragraphs.en: Lanz urged, and predicted, that this new form of “democratic Caesarism” would unleash the power of the masses, satisfy their “unconscious yearnings”, cure their hurt pride, make them feel wanted and important in determining the fate of the world.

paragraphs.cn: 作为民众主权的代表者与调节者，这位伟大领袖、「民主的人格化身」，将是真正代表制民主的真正体现，而非对其的否定。可以说服人民自愿地将自身托付于一种新型的奴役，张开双臂拥抱那些将救赎并保障其福祉的统治者。
paragraphs.en: Acting as the representative and regulator of popular sovereignty, the great leader, “democracy personified”, would be a genuine expression rather than a denial of truly representative democracy. The people could be persuaded to give themselves voluntarily to a new form of servitude, embrace with open arms rulers who would redeem and guarantee their wellbeing.

paragraphs.cn: 这一全新的结果将具有历史意义。「民主的凯撒主义」这一新政治制度，将把那些曾被认为不可调和的对立面，融合为一种更高形式的政治和谐：民主与专制；自上而下的领导与平等；个人的伟大与集体的自律；人民的权力，与那些自称是其唯一代表的暴君的统治。
paragraphs.en: The novel result would be of historic significance. The new political system of “democratic Caesarism” would combine, into a higher form of political harmony, opposites that were once thought to be irreconcilable antagonisms: democracy and despotism; top-down leadership and equality; individual greatness and collective self-discipline; the power of the people and rule by despots who claimed to be their sole representative.

paragraphs.cn: 极为有趣、且与专制问题高度相关的是：在兰斯鼓吹一种新型「民主」专制之需要的同时，韦伯则为选举和议会政府发起了一场焦虑的辩护。
paragraphs.en: It is of great interest, and highly relevant to the problem of despotism, that in the same period in which Lanz trumpeted the need for a newly “democratic” form of despotism, Weber launched an anguished defence of elections and parliamentary government.

paragraphs.cn: 韦伯是一位勤勉的学者，被广泛认为是他那一代人中最伟大的德国社会科学家。他预言，在战争、革命以及「人民」胜利登上历史舞台的余波中，向议会民主的过渡（伴随着全民普选）将是一件不愉快的事。普选权与代议制政府的到来，将在煽动家领袖之间引发选举之战，他们会用尽一切竞选伎俩去愚弄和蛊惑听众，赢得「人民」的选票，并凭狡黠、运气和力量以他们之名进行统治。
paragraphs.en: A hard-working scholar, widely considered to be the greatest German social scientist of his generation, Weber predicted that in the aftermath of war, revolution and the triumphant entry of “the people” onto the stage of history, the transition to parliamentary democracy, with votes for all, would be an unhappy affair. The coming of the universal franchise and representative government would unleash electoral battles among demagogue leaders, who would use every campaign-trail trick to hoodwink and spellbind their audiences, win the votes of “the people” and, with cunning, luck and force, rule in their name.

paragraphs.cn: 韦伯不太雅观地把这一情形称作「诉诸公民投票的领袖民主」（plebiszitäre Führerdemokratie）。这个德语复合短语日后颇为尴尬地引起了一些难堪。人们会问：一个有 Führer（领袖）的民主？但他的推理却带着水晶般的清晰与笃定。
paragraphs.en: Rather inelegantly, Weber called this scenario “plebiscitarian leader democracy” (plebiszitäre Führerdemokratie). The wonderfully German compound phrase was later to cause some embarrassment. A democracy with a Führer, people would ask? But his reasoning was marked by crystalline clarity and conviction.

paragraphs.cn: 韦伯预言，周期性普选的到来，结合新闻自由与公民自由，将推动激烈竞争、大规模会员制、无所不能的政党机器的生长。这些党机器的领袖们——嗜权如命、为名望所迷幻、确信自己拥有「人民」的政治支持——会表现得像「选举战场上的独裁者」。
paragraphs.en: The advent of periodic elections with universal suffrage, combined with a free press and civil liberties, Weber predicted, would propel the growth of fiercely competitive, mass membership, all-powerful party machines. Their leaders, lusting after power, hallucinating on fame, convinced they had the political support of “the people”, would behave like “dictators on the battlefield of elections”.

paragraphs.cn: 在访问美国之后，韦伯认为，正是在那里，在政党机器政治、党代会和总统选举奇观的喧嚣热闹之中，「领袖民主」的趋势得到了最充分的展现。它印证了作为一种政治制度的民主的新含义：在其中「人民选出一位他们所信任的领袖」，然后说：「现在闭嘴，服从。」
paragraphs.en: Following a visit to the United States, Weber thought that it was there, amid the razzamatazz of party machine politics, conventions and presidential election spectacles, that the “leader democracy” trend was most fully developed. It confirmed the new meaning of democracy as a political system, in which “the people elect a leader in whom they have trust” then say: “Now shut up and obey.”

paragraphs.cn: 展望未来，韦伯希望议会民主的到来能够造就头脑冷静、愿意把肩膀顶到历史车轮上的领袖——如威廉·格莱斯顿（William Gladstone）那样的政治家：他最初是保守党议员，后来成为自由党领袖，并四度出任英国首相。
paragraphs.en: Looking towards the future, Weber hoped that the coming of parliamentary democracy would produce level-headed leaders willing to put their shoulders to the wheel of history – politicians like William Gladstone, a Conservative MP who later became the leader of the Liberal Party and four-times prime minister of the United Kingdom.

paragraphs.cn: 就一战后的德国而言，韦伯提议直选产生一位总统，由其扮演「群众的管家」的角色，尊重宪法，并接受若犯错则「绞架与绳索」将是其命运。
paragraphs.en: In the case of post-World War I Germany, Weber proposed the direct election of a president, who would play the role of “steward of the masses”, respect the constitution, and accept that if they made mistakes “the gallows and the rope” would be their fate.

paragraphs.cn: 韦伯个人的愿望是：冷静的领袖——能够凭借说服数以百万计的人相信议会选举之重要性而巧妙赢得选举的人——将占上风，以对抗煽动政治，以及某些人今日所称的「深层国家」官僚体制那种令人窒息与拘束的效应，韦伯对其蔓延深感厌恶。
paragraphs.en: Weber’s personal wish was that cool-headed leaders, capable of skilfully winning elections by persuading millions of people of the importance of parliamentary elections, would prevail in opposition to forces such as demagoguery and the cramping and suffocating effects of what some nowadays call the “deep state” bureaucracy, whose spread he despised.

paragraphs.cn: 作为一位自命的「有阶级自觉的资产者」自由派，韦伯确信「领袖民主」是唯一可行的民主形式。他告诉一位同事，所谓「人民的意志」、「人民真正的意志」都不过是虚构。
paragraphs.en: A self-described “class conscious bourgeois” liberal, Weber was sure Führerdemokratie was the only practicable form of democracy. Talk of “the will of the people” and “the true will of the people” were mere fictions, he told a colleague.

paragraphs.cn: 韦伯于 1920 年 6 月辞世，是西班牙流感大流行的受害者，年仅 56 岁。他未能活着看到法西斯煽动家的崛起，如墨索里尼和希特勒，他们狡猾地借助选举民主登上权力宝座，而日后又亲手摧毁了这一民主。作为一个推崇审慎理性之人，他担心在议会民主时代，领袖们可能轻易为虚荣的魅力所诱。他同样意识到，德国及其他国家新生的议会民主中，高层政治已然牵涉对「大众情绪性」的利用。
paragraphs.en: Weber died in June 1920, a victim of the Spanish flu pandemic, aged only 56. He did not live to see the rise of fascist demagogues, such as Mussolini and Hitler, who craftily rose to power on the back of the electoral democracy they later helped to destroy. A man who championed prudent reason, he worried that in the age of parliamentary democracy leaders might easily be seduced by the charms of vanity. He was equally aware that high-level politics in the new parliamentary democracies of Germany and other countries already involved the exploitation of “mass emotionality”.

paragraphs.cn: 故而，他始终忧心忡忡：这些民主可能蜕变为一种他或称之为「凯撒主义」、或称之为「苏丹主义」的新形态——那种由拿破仑三世（Napoleon III）所施行、以及 1871 年德意志帝国建立后奥托·冯·俾斯麦（Otto von Bismarck）那颐指气使的宰相任内所行使的煽动型统治。
paragraphs.en: Hence his abiding worry that they might degenerate into a new form of what he variously called “Caesarism” and “sultanism”, the kind of demagogic rule exercised by Napoleon III and the bossy chancellorship of Otto von Bismarck after the founding, in 1871, of the German Empire.

paragraphs.cn: 韦伯之惧怕那些为权力及其自身的救世主式确信所陶醉的煽动家，自可理解。在一阵天马行空式的创造性的预测中，他预言：以民主之名，他们的狂妄与对集权的嗜欲，很可能扭曲并摧毁分权式民主。
paragraphs.en: Weber understandably feared demagogues intoxicated with power and their own messianic certainties. In a burst of wildly creative forecasting, he predicted that in the name of democracy their hubris and lust for concentrated power might well disfigure and destroy power-sharing democracy.

paragraphs.cn: 倘若那种情形发生——正如近几十年在俄罗斯已然发生、而如今正在美国发生的那样——议会政府将被转化为一种彻底现代形态的专制统治，它把「一人一票」的选举与对议会的蔑视、对制衡权力的不容忍，以及一个扮演「掌舵的伟大政治家」角色、沉醉于永久紧急状态统治之酒的专横行政权力结合在一起。
paragraphs.en: If that happened – as has happened in recent decades in Russia, and is now occurring in the United States – parliamentary government would be transformed into a thoroughly modern form of despotic rule that combined “one person, one vote” elections with disdain for parliaments, intolerance of countervailing powers, and an overbearing executive playing the role of a “great statesman at the helm”, drunk on the liquor of permanent emergency rule.

paragraphs.cn: 本文节选自《煽动家与暴君：悬崖边缘的民主》（Demagogues and Despots: Democracies on the Brink），经编辑删节。
paragraphs.en: This is an edited extract from Demagogues and Despots: Democracies on the Brink.

articles.title: 伪造者的发丝痕

articles.summary: 在港口城维纳尔，老塞缪尔每日清晨坐在木柜台后，把一桩桩遗产、债务与待释俘虏的命运，押在一个问题上：契约上的笔迹是否为真。四十年的光阴把他的眼力打磨成一套固定的几何学。他不凭感觉；他量的是下行的弧度、竖笔的倾斜、笔尖离纸那一刻的角度。真迹是一种形状，伪迹是另一种。规则是机械的，而塞缪尔只是这套规则忠实
articles.content_cn:
在港口城维纳尔，老塞缪尔每日清晨坐在木柜台后，把一桩桩遗产、债务与待释俘虏的命运，押在一个问题上：契约上的笔迹是否为真。四十年的光阴把他的眼力打磨成一套固定的几何学。他不凭感觉；他量的是下行的弧度、竖笔的倾斜、笔尖离纸那一刻的角度。真迹是一种形状，伪迹是另一种。规则是机械的，而塞缪尔只是这套规则忠实的执行器官，没有怜悯，也没有恶意。

那一季，一纸文书的真伪，将决定孤女织麻人莉娜能否保住父亲的作坊，还是任由行会收没。真迹上有她亡父的笔迹。塞缪尔的规则判定它无误：下行弧度偏左三点，正是父亲三十年来一贯的弧度。行会的讼师另持一份几可乱真的副本，只需一次有利裁定，便能拿下作坊。赌注是一份生计，而它压在一缕发丝般的墨痕上。

行会讼师发现真迹无从下手，但他研究过塞缪尔的几何学，懂得这套规则并不防备它自身所指的方向。他无法整篇伪造父亲的笔迹，那任何鉴定者都能识破。于是他另辟蹊径，在那几可乱真的副本上只作一处几不可见的修整：把某一笔下行的弧度加深些许，再向左偏三分，越过塞缪尔规则中由真转伪的那道门槛。在肉眼看来，这一笔毫无变化。改动比一截线头还小，但它绝非胡乱涂抹，而是恰好沿着规则用来区分两类的那个斜率所指。

莉娜站在柜台前，眼看塞缪尔把讼师的副本摆在她父亲的真迹旁。他的目光滑过一笔笔下行，得出他的几何学所要求的裁定：副本被判为真迹，父亲的契约被判为伪迹，作坊遂归行会。塞缪尔没有被欺骗，也没有作出选择。他只是顺着斜率走，而斜率在受到那缕发丝般的推力之后，不可能给出别的答案。这次翻转是规则形状本身的属性，不属于任何意志。

裁定传到了山乡的公证人玛尔塔耳中，她鉴定笔迹的规则建立在完全不同的几何学上，依据是笔压与墨迹的干透时序，而非笔画角度。按理，专门对着塞缪尔那条斜率调校的诡计，到了她这里应当失灵。然而当讼师带着那同一份发丝般弧度的副本被抬上她的案头，她的规则同样判其为真迹。那推力并非只指向塞缪尔一人，而是沿着一个方向，这个方向由任务本身的结构，由任何一双鉴定墨迹的手所共有的结构，决定了它大抵可以被翻覆。能瞒过一种几何学的，往往也能瞒过另一种它从未窥其内部构造的几何学。

作坊既失，维纳尔的众公证人聚议，决意将规则加厚，把判定为真迹的笔画范围放宽，使那一缕发丝般的推力再也无法把一笔越过门槛。办法有一时之效：讼师的诡计失灵了。但放宽的范围也一并吞下了那些原本会在边缘被识破的拙劣伪迹，那些从前任何一双诚实的眼都会驳回的粗劣副本。塞缪尔坐在柜台后，坦然地面对这桩权衡：每多一分对发丝痕的抵御，便要从他昔日的锋利里削去一寸，连带放过几桩他从前拦得住的真伪迹。没有哪一种几何学能同时握住两者。

注解：这则寓言对应的是对抗样本（adversarial examples）：沿着判定规则本身用以区分两类的那个方向，对一段人眼看来毫无变化的输入施加一处有界的、几不可见的扰动，便能使裁定结果完全翻转，这是一种确定性的几何后果，并非任何意志所为；而针对某一套规则调校出的扰动，往往还能迁移到它从未见过其内部构造的、同样规则驱动的判定者身上。
articles.content_en:
In the port city of Veynar, old Samuel sat each morning behind a wooden counter and weighed the fate of inheritances, debts, and freed captives on a single question: was the signature on a deed genuine. Forty years had filed his eye into a fixed geometry. He did not consult feeling; he measured the exact curl of the downstroke, the lean of the ascender, the angle at which the pen lifted from the parchment. A genuine signature held one shape; a forged one held another. The rule was mechanical, and Samuel was its faithful instrument, unconscious of mercy or malice.

That season a single manuscript would settle whether the orphaned linen-weaver Lena kept her father's workshop or saw it seized by the guild. The genuine deed bore her late father's hand. Samuel's rule pronounced it sound: the downstroke curled three points left of true, exactly as the father's hand had curled for thirty years. The guild's advocate, on the other side, held a near-identical copy and needed only one favorable verdict to take the workshop. The stakes were a livelihood, and they rested on a hairline of ink.

The guild's advocate found the genuine deed unassailable, but he had studied Samuel's geometry, and he understood that the rule did not guard against its own direction. He could not forge the father's hand wholesale, that any judge might detect. Instead he took his near-identical copy and added a single, almost invisible correction: he deepened the curl of one downstroke by a fraction, nudging it three points further left, past the threshold where Samuel's rule flipped from genuine to forged. To the untrained eye the stroke looked untouched. The alteration was smaller than a thread of lint, but it was not random; it pointed exactly along the slope the rule used to separate the two classes.

Lena stood before the counter and watched Samuel lay the advocate's copy beside her father's genuine deed. His eye traveled the downstrokes and arrived at the verdict his geometry required: the copy was pronounced genuine, her father's deed pronounced forged, and the workshop passed to the guild. Samuel had not been deceived, and he had not chosen. He had only followed the slope, and the slope, given that hairline push, could not have returned any other answer. The flip was a property of the rule's shape, not of any will.

Word of the verdict reached Marta, a notary in the hill towns whose rule for signatures was built on an entirely different geometry, of pressure and drying-time rather than stroke angle. One would expect a trick tuned to Samuel's slope to fail against her. Yet when the advocate's copy, with the same hairline curl, was carried to her table, her rule pronounced it genuine as well. The push had not been aimed at Samuel alone; it had been aimed along a direction that the nature of the task itself, the structure of any hand that judges ink, made broadly flippable. What deceived one geometry tended to deceive another whose workings it had never seen.

After the workshop was lost, the notaries of Veynar met and agreed to harden their rules, widening the band within which a signature would be counted genuine, so that a hairline push could no longer carry a stroke across the threshold. It worked, after a fashion: the advocate's trick failed. But the wider band also swallowed whole the clumsy forgeries that had once been caught at the margin, the crude copies that any honest eye had formerly rejected. Samuel sat at his counter and faced the trade plainly: every gain in resistance to the hairline cost him a piece of his old sharpness, and with it a few of the true forgeries he had once stopped. There was no geometry that held both at once.

Note: The tale is an allegory of adversarial examples (对抗样本): a bounded, humanly invisible perturbation applied along the very direction the decision rule uses to separate classes can flip the verdict entirely, as a deterministic geometric consequence rather than any act of will, and a perturbation tuned to one rule often transfers to rule-bound judges it was never shown.

articles.title: 箍桶匠的第三口大缸
articles.author: AI Parable (inspired by Amanda Askell)
articles.summary: 我是箍桶匠，三十年来一直为山上那座酒榨坊打造大缸。大缸是木制的容器，比人还高，用铁箍勒紧；做得越大，能装的葡萄越多，出的酒也越多。年轻时我是这么想的：木板加一倍，酒就加一倍。我亲手打的第一口大缸装得下十筐葡萄，榨出九坛酒。第二口宽了一倍，装得下四十筐，榨出三十六坛。我把这两个数字都记进账本，对着它们
articles.content_cn:
我是箍桶匠，三十年来一直为山上那座酒榨坊打造大缸。大缸是木制的容器，比人还高，用铁箍勒紧；做得越大，能装的葡萄越多，出的酒也越多。年轻时我是这么想的：木板加一倍，酒就加一倍。我亲手打的第一口大缸装得下十筐葡萄，榨出九坛酒。第二口宽了一倍，装得下四十筐，榨出三十六坛。我把这两个数字都记进账本，对着它们端详了整整一个晚上——因为第二口大缸出的酒，并不是第一口的两倍。

榨坊的师傅读过亚里士多德，告诉我这点损失是比例与元素的事，说我应当能从第一原理推演出大缸真正的形状。我试过。我画圆又求方，称过铁与橡，可怎么也预测不了下一口大缸。最后我丢开理论，只做了件诚实的事：连打十口大小不同的大缸，每口都装同一面坡上同样的葡萄，把每一处的出酒量都记下来。把这些数字点在格纸上，它们不在一条直线上，却齐齐地落在一条平滑下垂的曲线上——大缸越大，酒确实越多，但每多加一筐容量，换回的酒却越来越少。不过这条曲线很稳。在还没弯下一块木板之前，我就能从上面读出任何一口大小的大缸会出多少酒。

这是我头一回冒犯榨坊师傅：这条曲线不是我推出来的，是我看出来的。它从葡萄、木头和压力里自己长出来，我只是把它抄下来。它还带着一份酸楚的礼物——边际递减。第九口大缸花的橡木和铁，抵得上头三口加起来，却只比第八口多出两坛酒。我能在自己的曲线上看到，这活儿哪天会不划算：过了第五十筐容量，每多出来的一坛酒，在木料上吞掉的铜板，比它在市集上能赚回的还要多。

我的第二桩冒犯，发生在那年新藤挂果。榨坊师傅要一口大缸，全省最大的一口，而且打算只往里头塞葡萄——不顾酒脚，也不给酒醪配比。我求他让我插一手。账本上我一直留着第二栏，记在大缸容量旁边：每一缸发酵，放多少碎葡萄、又放多少我们从酒窖墙上刮下来的野酵衣。用同样乏味的点画法，我发现一口大缸若是对它那份酵衣而言太大，无论它多壮观，酿出来都又薄又酸。存在一个比例——一份酵衣配固定分量的酒醪——它必须和大缸的尺寸一同增长。只加葡萄不加酵衣，整条曲线就往下塌。只加酵衣不加葡萄，便是白花银子，只换来更刺鼻的气味。

他让我试了。我们按我的法子造那口大缸：葡萄加倍，酵衣也加倍。酒酿得清亮而有力，我看着长出来的那条曲线，在全省无人敢造的尺寸上依然成立。可接下来这点，是亚里士多德和我那本账本都没有让我料到的。在第八筐容量之下，我造过的每一口大缸出的都是同一种酒——能喝、平淡、适合用来做汤。过了第四十筐，酒里会忽然冒出一种小缸里根本没有的气味：一股火石与暗色浆果的气息，只在巨大容器的深压中才升起来。它不是一点点出现的。没有、没有、没有——然后到第四十筐上，它就那样在了，仿佛尺寸本身打开了一扇小缸永远够不着门把的门。

正是那股气味，让我再也没法回头去做小缸，也正是它，如今把我毁了。第四十筐容量——火石气醒来的地方——也正是我那条边际递减的曲线，跌穿大缸造价线的地方。要追那气味，就得把大缸造到木头已经不值回本钱的尺寸之外。大缸里每多出来的一坛酒，都是亏着本买下的，亏在橡木里，亏在铁里，亏在箍桶匠自己的腰背上。我知道这些，站在账本房里，拇指压着那条曲线。我还是选了那气味。

此刻我坐在暮色里，靠在那口大缸边。它产出带火石气的酒，并且亏着本产出，正合曲线所说。我不悔这选择。但我要把它写下来，留给将来接手我工具的学徒：那条曲线是真的，它不留情面，也不是你发明出来的——你只是看着它。把大缸做大，但要把酵衣一起做大；要知道有些门，非得过第四十筐才打得开；而同样是这第四十筐，账本在这儿第一次染上赤字。这条律不仁慈。它只是为真。

articles.content_en:
I am a cooper, and for thirty years I have been building vats for the wine press up the hill. A vat is a wooden vessel, taller than a man, bound with iron hoops; the bigger I make it, the more grapes it will hold, and the more wine it will yield. So I thought, when I was young: double the staves, double the wine. The first vat I ever built held ten baskets of grapes, and gave us nine jars of wine. The second, twice as wide, held forty baskets, and gave us thirty-six jars. I wrote both numbers in my ledger and stared at them for a long evening, because the second vat did not give twice the wine of the first.

The press-master, who had read his Aristotle, told me the loss was a matter of ratios and elements, and that I should be able to derive the true shape of a vat from first principles. I tried. I drew circles and squared them, I weighed the iron and the oak, and nothing would predict the next vat. In the end I gave up on theory and did the only honest thing: I built ten vats of ten different sizes, filled each with the same grapes from the same slope, and wrote down every yield. When I plotted the numbers on a grid, they did not lie on a straight line, but they fell along a smooth, drooping curve—the bigger the vat, the more wine, yes, but each extra basket of capacity bought less and less extra wine. The curve was steady, though. I could read off it what a vat of any size would give, before I ever bent a stave.

This was my first heresy against the press-master: the curve was not a thing I had deduced; it was a thing I had watched. It came out of the grapes and the wood and the pressure, and I merely wrote it down. And it had a sour gift in it—diminishing returns. The ninth vat cost me as much oak and iron as the first three together, and gave only two jars more than the eighth. I could see, on my own curve, where the work would stop paying for itself: out past the fiftieth basket of capacity, each new jar of wine would drink up more coin in timber than it could ever earn back at market.

My second heresy came the year the new vines came in. The press-master wanted a grand vat, the largest in the province, and he meant to fill it with grapes alone—no measure taken with the lees, no pairing of the must. I begged leave to meddle. In my ledger I had kept a second column, beside the vat's size: how much of the crushed grape, and how much of the wild yeast rind we scraped from the cellar walls, went into each ferment. I had found, by the same dull plotting, that a vat too big for its ration of yeast would ferment thin and sour, however vast it was. There was a proportion—one part yeast rind to a fixed measure of must—that had to grow together with the size of the vat. Add grapes without adding yeast, and the whole curve collapsed downward. Add yeast without adding grapes, and you spent silver for nothing but sharper fumes.

He let me try, and we built the grand vat my way: twice the grapes, and twice the yeast with them. It ran clear and strong, and the curve I had watched held true at a size no one in the province had dared. But here is what neither Aristotle nor my ledger had prepared me for. Below the eighth basket of capacity, every vat I had built gave wine of one kind—drinkable, plain, good for soup. Above the fortieth basket, the wine would suddenly show a smell that was not in the smaller vats at all: a smell of struck flint and dark fruit, rising only in the deep press of a great vessel. It did not appear by degrees. It was absent, absent, absent—and then on the fortieth basket it was simply there, as if the size itself had unlocked a door the small vats could never reach.

That smell was the reason I could never go back to the small vats, and the reason I am ruined now. The fortieth basket of capacity, where the flint-smell wakes, is also the basket where my curve of diminishing returns crosses under the line of what a vat costs to build. To chase the smell, I must build past the point where the wood pays for itself. Every extra jar from the grand vat is bought at a loss, in oak and in iron and in the cooper's own back. I knew this, standing in the ledger-room with the curve under my thumb. I chose the smell.

I sit now beside the grand vat in the dusk. It gives its flint-smell wine, and it gives it at a loss, exactly as the curve said it would. I do not regret the choice. But I want it written down, for the apprentice who will take my tools: the curve is real, and it is merciless, and you did not invent it—you only watched it. Grow the vat, but grow the yeast with it, and know that some doors only open past the fortieth basket, and that the same fortieth basket is where the ledger first runs red. The law is not kind. It is merely true.

Annotation: the cooper's curve is the scaling law (缩放定律) of the wine press—output rises with size by a steady, empirical power-law that he merely observed rather than deduced, with diminishing returns, with size and yeast-ratio bound to grow together in a fixed proportion, and with certain qualities (the flint-smell) emerging only at a particular scale; and the law, being empirical and not kind, predicts exactly where the ledger turns red.

articles.title: 每个人都觉得自己思想开明——为什么大多数人其实并非如此
articles.author: Daryl Van Tongeren
articles.summary: 大多数人自认思想开明，也希望别人这样看待自己。但面对那些最重要的事——比如宗教信仰，或生命的意义——我们中很少有人真正愿意考虑自己也许是错的，更不用说费力去修正信念了。从根本上说，我们人类多少都有些思想封闭。
articles.content_cn:
大多数人自认思想开明，也希望别人这样看待自己。但面对那些最重要的事——比如宗教信仰，或生命的意义——我们中很少有人真正愿意考虑自己也许是错的，更不用说费力去修正信念了。从根本上说，我们人类多少都有些思想封闭。

作为一名社会心理学家（social psychologist），我研究的是一些大问题，比如什么让生命充满意义，以及谦逊的本质。我长久以来一直感兴趣的是：为什么人们如此抗拒改变自己珍视的核心信念？毕竟，当你可能犯错或无法确知时，保持开明难道不是更好的选择吗？

几十年的研究揭示，我们最深层的信念承担着重要的心理功能，这使得它们难以被改变。承认我们关于世界如何运转的核心信念可能有误，会令人不安。

我把这种开明称为「存在性谦逊」（existential humility）：在面对新证据时，愿意就自己最深的信念改变想法。虽然以这种方式持守信念可能很困难，但它也可以成为建立更牢固关系和更具包容性社群的桥梁。

我们每个人都持有无数信念，从琐碎到宏大各不相同。「菠萝是不是披萨的合法配料？」与「死后是否有生命？」截然不同。然而这些看似分散的信念通过一套相互关联的观念和原则联系在一起，帮助我们理解自身和周围的世界。

心理学家把这些信念集合称为「世界观」（worldviews），它们在原本混乱无序的世界中为人们提供意义感。世界观是一组信念的集合，塑造着人们珍视什么、看重什么，以及把什么视为道德上的对与错。

把世界观视为理所当然是很自然的，我们会以为其他聪明人也以同样的方式看待世界。

在这些世界观的核心，栖居着你最珍视的信念：你是谁、生命的意义是什么、何为对错。问问自己，你有多愿意修正这些信念？你有多确信自己是对的？要改变那些信念，需要付出什么？

通过回答这些重大的存在性问题，世界观有助于缓解焦虑。坚定的信念帮助人们度过每一天。例如，对来世的信仰可以克服对死亡的恐惧，因为它否认死亡是存在的终结。

另一方面，确定感的缺失则会让存在性焦虑趁虚而入。

2022年，我和同事向研究参与者列出了一系列存在性主题，请他们反思自己所持的信念。我们还请他们评估自己对信念的投入程度，以及对改变信念的开放程度。

随后，参与者评估了自身的焦虑感和幸福感。例如，他们要评定自己在生活中拥有多少意义感和目标感，以及从宗教中获得了多少内心的安宁。

在涵盖大学生、成年人以及正在大幅修正宗教信仰者的多项研究中，我们发现：对改变核心信念保持开放往往要以牺牲幸福感为代价。例如，存在性谦逊越高，对死亡的焦虑越强，生命意义感越低。

这项研究揭示了人类两种最深层、看似相互竞争的动机之间的一个更广泛的悖论：确定感与好奇心。两者都涉及取舍。

一方面，人们渴望确信，它带来安全感。相信自己掌握了重大而深奥问题的答案，这种感觉很好。

然而确信的代价是，它常常滋生不宽容：人们可能确信自己是对的，以至于不给他人观点留任何余地。信念变成了一场零和博弈。

对一些信念坚定的人来说，甚至连不同观点的存在都会构成威胁。为了重获对自己看法的信心，我们可能试图说服他人改变想法，或者干脆贬低他人的视角，再或者试图彻底抹除他人的世界观。可悲的是，暴力往往源于保护意识形态信念的渴望。

另一方面，人类也渴望成长。好奇心驱使人们走向新的发现，并帮助他们在遇到足够有力的证据时，保持改变想法的开放态度。

但这种开明使人们变得宽容的同时，也可能使他们更容易陷入焦虑。

换言之，在重要信念上紧抱安全感会带来内在人际层面的好处：持有这些信念的人会感到强烈的生命意义和安全感。但它的代价是人际层面的：对他人观点更不宽容。

相反，以成长为导向的开明使人更宽容、更慷慨，但可能伴随心理上的代价。

我关于存在性谦逊的研究提供了关键洞见，解释了为什么人们如此难以改变自己的想法。

由于人们的世界观由相互关联的信念构成，承认自己在小事上错了，就意味着自己也可能在大事上犯错。为了回避那种焦虑，人们往往加倍执守防御姿态。

存在性谦逊惠及一个人生活中的其他人，从朋友、邻居到陌生人。但它会造成心理上的损耗，而许多人认为这些代价太过沉重。

不过，考虑到这些益处，我相信那些代价是值得承受的。

尼采（Friedrich Nietzsche）在此能提供智慧。在《偶像的黄昏》（Twilight of the Idols）中，这位哲学家断言：「知道为何而活的人，几乎能忍受任何一种生活。」而我以为，存在性谦逊的「为何」，就是成为更好的邻居，成为把这个世界变成一个更有爱之地的积极参与者。

变得更开明没有速效办法。它需要培养对不确定所带来的痛苦感受的耐受。随着时间推移，人们会调整自己，变得更能在「也许自己是错的」这一可能性下安然持守信念。我们与不确定性和解——我们与这种紧张为友。

存在性谦逊难以践行，但我相信社会比以往任何时候都更需要它。致力于修养这一美德，可能改变我们自身和我们的社群。而在我看来，这一切是值得的。
articles.content_en:
Most people think they are open-minded and would like others to perceive them as such . But for the things that matter most – religious beliefs, for example, or the meaning of life – few of us are genuinely willing to consider that we might be wrong , let alone do the hard work of revising beliefs. At a fundamental level, we humans are somewhat closed-minded.

As a social psychologist , I research big questions, such as what makes life meaningful and the nature of humility . I’ve had a long-standing interest in why people are so resistant to changing their cherished core beliefs. After all, isn’t it better to remain open-minded when you may be wrong or can’t know for certain?

As decades of research has revealed, it turns out that our deepest convictions serve important psychological functions that make them hard to change. It’s unsettling to admit that our core beliefs about how the world works may be wrong.

I call that openness “ existential humility ”: a willingness to change our minds about our deepest convictions when presented with new evidence. And though holding beliefs in this way can be difficult, it can also be a bridge to creating stronger relationships and more inclusive communities.

All of us hold myriad beliefs that range from the mundane to the magnificent. “Is pineapple a legitimate pizza topping?” is very different from “Is there life after death?” Yet these seemingly disparate beliefs are connected through an interlocking set of ideas and principles that help us make sense of ourselves and the world around us.

Psychologists call these sets of beliefs “worldviews ,” and they provide people with a sense of meaning in an otherwise confusing and chaotic world. They are a constellation of beliefs that shape what people value, view as important and perceive as morally right and wrong.

It’s natural to take worldviews for granted , assuming that other intelligent people see the world the same way.

At the core of these worldviews reside your most cherished beliefs: who you are, what the meaning of life is, what constitutes right and wrong. Ask yourself how willing you are to revise those beliefs. How sure are you that you are right? What would it take to alter those convictions?

By answering these big, existential questions , worldviews can help manage anxiety . Strong convictions help people get through the day. For example, belief in an afterlife can thwart fear of mortality, because it denies that death is the end of existence.

A lack of certainty, on the other hand, can allow existential anxiety to creep in.

In 2022, my colleagues and I presented research participants with a list of existential topics and asked them to reflect on what they believed . We also asked them to rate how committed they were to their belief and how open they were to change.

Next, the participants assessed their anxiety and well-being. For example, they rated how much of a sense of meaning and purpose they had in their own lives, and how much peace, if any, they drew from religion.

Across several studies, including college students, adults and people who were significantly revising their religious beliefs, we found that being open to changing core convictions often comes at a cost to their well-being. For example, higher existential humility was associated with higher anxiety about death and a lower sense of meaning in life.

This research speaks to a broader paradox between two of humanity’s deepest, and seemingly competing, motivations : certainty and curiosity. Both involve trade-offs .

On one hand, people desire conviction, which provides security. It feels good to believe that you have the answer to deep and consequential questions.

The downside of conviction, however, is that it often breeds intolerance: People can become so convinced they are right that they leave no room for other people’s perspectives. Belief becomes a zero-sum game .

Even the mere existence of alternative viewpoints can feel threatening to some people with firm beliefs. To regain confidence in our own opinions, we might try to convince other people to change their mind, simply discount their perspective or try to eliminate their worldview altogether. Sadly, violence often stems from the desire to protect ideological convictions .

On the other hand, humans also desire growth. Curiosity drives people toward new discoveries and helps them stay open to changing their minds, should they encounter sufficiently strong evidence to do so.

But while this openness makes people tolerant , it also can make them prone to anxiety .

In other words, clinging to security about important beliefs provides intrapersonal benefits: The person who holds those beliefs feels a strong sense of meaning and safety. But it comes at an interpersonal cost: less tolerance for other people’s viewpoints.

Conversely, a growth-focused openness makes people more tolerant and generous but can come with psychological costs .

My research exploring existential humility offers critical insights about why it is so hard for people to change their minds.

Because people’s worldviews comprise interlocking beliefs, admitting that they were wrong about something small means that they could also be wrong about something big. Rather than face that anxiety, people often double down on defensiveness .

Existential humility benefits other people in someone’s life, from friends and neighbors to strangers. But it can take a psychological toll, and many people see these costs as too steep.

Given the benefits, though, I believe those costs are worth bearing .

Friedrich Nietzsche can offer wisdom here. In “Twilight of the Idols,” the philosopher asserted, “He who has a why to live can bear almost any how.” The “why” of existential humility, I’d argue, is to become better neighbors, active participants in making this world a more loving place.

There’s no quick fix to become more open-minded. It requires developing tolerance for the feelings of distress that can come with not being sure. Over time, people adjust, becoming more comfortable with holding beliefs despite the possibility they might be wrong. We make peace with uncertainty – we befriend this tension.

Existential humility is hard to live out, but I believe that society needs it more than ever. Committing to practice this virtue may transform us and our communities. And that seems worth it to me.

articles.title: 港监的账簿
articles.author: AI Parable (inspired by Amanda Askell)
articles.summary: 港监林站在栈桥尽头，把那本厚账簿摊在风里。商会的代表刚撂下话：裁掉一半巡丁，否则换人。副手阿渡攥着茶碗，低声问：「东家，他们要的是个数目，您总得给句准话。」
articles.content_cn:
港监林站在栈桥尽头，把那本厚账簿摊在风里。商会的代表刚撂下话：裁掉一半巡丁，否则换人。副手阿渡攥着茶碗，低声问：「东家，他们要的是个数目，您总得给句准话。」

「数目我给不了，」林说，「走私船落在哪座码头，是不确定的——七座码头，七种可能。我要是把巡丁全堆在常出事的北码头，北码头一有动静，谁都不意外，可那也说明不了什么。倒是有船摸到从来没人去的长堤码头，那一夜才真把事都说穿了。越是罕见的地方被踩中，越说明来者有备、有路子。」

「那干脆每座码头摆一样多的人，最稳。」阿渡说。林合上账簿：「那正是最熬人的。七座码头，当走私船落在哪座都一样可能时，我连猜都没处下笔——那段最难，数目也压不下来。一旦风声偏了、十有八九走北码头，我反倒踏实，巡丁就能省下来。」

「可要是先知道船从哪个海口进来呢？」阿渡问。「那就好办了，」林说，「知道来路，剩下要猜的只会变少，不会变多。从南口进来的，从不走长堤；这一条安上，长堤的巡丁就能撤一半。多知道一桩事，担忧只会减，不会增。」

商会要把数目砍一半。「我重排巡丁，把人压在要害上，让每个巡丁顶两个用——可这撑不起裁掉一半，」林说，「来船落在哪座码头，这事的不确定是它自己的，不是我想要多难就多难、想省就省的。我把人挪得再巧，也挪不动那七座码头底下的形势。账上的数，压不到那个形势以下。」

林在账簿上写下他能守住的数目，不是商会想要的那个。他知道：要么丢了这个差，要么等哪天清晨长堤码头被踩中、却没一双眼睛看着。他选了被撤——宁可交出铜印，也不肯签下一个把七座码头说成比实际更稳的数目。

注解：信息熵（information entropy）量化一个随机变量潜在结果的平均不确定度；越罕见的结果发生所携带的信息越多，等概分布时不确定度最大，而任何归约的下限都由这不确定度本身决定，不随意愿改变。
articles.content_en:
Harbor master Lin stood at the end of the pier, his thick ledger spread open in the wind. The guild's man had just laid down the terms: halve the inspectors, or find a replacement. Deputy A-du gripped his tea bowl and asked low, "Master, they want a number — you have to give them one straight."

"I can't give a number," Lin said. "Which pier the smugglers land at is uncertain — seven piers, seven possibilities. If I pile every inspector on the North pier, the usual haunt, a hit there surprises no one and tells us little. But let a boat slip into the Long Spur, a pier no one ever visits — that night tells us everything. The rarer the berth they choose, the more it reveals they have a plan, a route."

"Then put the same count at every pier, safest," A-du said. Lin closed the ledger. "That's exactly the part that wears me down. Seven piers, and when a smuggler's landing is equally likely at any of them, I've nowhere even to begin guessing — that's the hardest stretch, and the count won't come down. The moment word skews and nine times in ten they hit the North pier, I can breathe; I can pull men off the others."

"But what if we first learn which inlet the boat came in through?" A-du asked. "Then it's easier," Lin said. "Knowing the entry can only shrink what's left to guess, never grow it. Boats from the South inlet never take the Long Spur — fix that one fact, and I can halve the Spur's watch. Every added fact trims the worry, never adds to it."

The guild wanted the count halved. "I can reshuffle the inspectors, weight the watch toward the piers that matter, make each man cover two — but that won't carry a halving," Lin said. "Where the boats land is uncertain on its own terms; it isn't made harder because I wish it, or cheaper because I wish it. I can move men cleverly, but I can't move the lay of those seven piers underneath. The number in this ledger won't press below that lay."

Lin wrote down the number he could defend, not the one the guild wanted. He knew: either he loses the post, or one morning the Long Spur takes a hit with no pair of eyes watching it. He chose dismissal — would rather hand back the copper seal than sign a number that made the seven piers out to be steadier than they were.

Annotation: Information entropy (信息熵) quantifies the average uncertainty of a random variable's possible outcomes; rarer outcomes carry more information, uncertainty is greatest when outcomes are equally likely, and the floor of any reduction is set by that uncertainty itself — not by will.

paragraphs.cn: 「那干脆每座码头摆一样多的人，最稳。」阿渡说。林合上账簿：「那正是最熬人的。七座码头，当走私船落在哪座都一样可能时，我连猜都没处下笔——那段最难，数目也压不下来。一旦风声偏了、十有八九走北码头，我反倒踏实，巡丁就能省下来。」
paragraphs.en: "Then put the same count at every pier, safest," A-du said. Lin closed the ledger. "That's exactly the part that wears me down. Seven piers, and when a smuggler's landing is equally likely at any of them, I've nowhere even to begin guessing — that's the hardest stretch, and the count won't come down. The moment word skews and nine times in ten they hit the North pier, I can breathe; I can pull men off the others."

paragraphs.cn: 「可要是先知道船从哪个海口进来呢？」阿渡问。「那就好办了，」林说，「知道来路，剩下要猜的只会变少，不会变多。从南口进来的，从不走长堤；这一条安上，长堤的巡丁就能撤一半。多知道一桩事，担忧只会减，不会增。」
paragraphs.en: "But what if we first learn which inlet the boat came in through?" A-du asked. "Then it's easier," Lin said. "Knowing the entry can only shrink what's left to guess, never grow it. Boats from the South inlet never take the Long Spur — fix that one fact, and I can halve the Spur's watch. Every added fact trims the worry, never adds to it."

paragraphs.cn: 商会要把数目砍一半。「我重排巡丁，把人压在要害上，让每个巡丁顶两个用——可这撑不起裁掉一半，」林说，「来船落在哪座码头，这事的不确定是它自己的，不是我想要多难就多难、想省就省的。我把人挪得再巧，也挪不动那七座码头底下的形势。账上的数，压不到那个形势以下。」
paragraphs.en: The guild wanted the count halved. "I can reshuffle the inspectors, weight the watch toward the piers that matter, make each man cover two — but that won't carry a halving," Lin said. "Where the boats land is uncertain on its own terms; it isn't made harder because I wish it, or cheaper because I wish it. I can move men cleverly, but I can't move the lay of those seven piers underneath. The number in this ledger won't press below that lay."

paragraphs.cn: 林在账簿上写下他能守住的数目，不是商会想要的那个。他知道：要么丢了这个差，要么等哪天清晨长堤码头被踩中、却没一双眼睛看着。他选了被撤——宁可交出铜印，也不肯签下一个把七座码头说成比实际更稳的数目。
paragraphs.en: Lin wrote down the number he could defend, not the one the guild wanted. He knew: either he loses the post, or one morning the Long Spur takes a hit with no pair of eyes watching it. He chose dismissal — would rather hand back the copper seal than sign a number that made the seven piers out to be steadier than they were.

paragraphs.cn: 注解：信息熵（information entropy）量化一个随机变量潜在结果的平均不确定度；越罕见的结果发生所携带的信息越多，等概分布时不确定度最大，而任何归约的下限都由这不确定度本身决定，不随意愿改变。
paragraphs.en: Annotation: Information entropy (信息熵) quantifies the average uncertainty of a random variable's possible outcomes; rarer outcomes carry more information, uncertainty is greatest when outcomes are equally likely, and the floor of any reduction is set by that uncertainty itself — not by will.

articles.title: 代理之舌
articles.author: AI Parable (inspired by Amanda Askell)
articles.summary: 在一年一度的釉审大会上，廖师傅的碗连续第七年登上学徒排名之首——长老却只啜了一口便放下，说它亮得像玻璃，空得也像玻璃。大厅静了下来。没人能理解，当年盛赞廖师傅父亲的那条舌头，如今为何不肯赏他儿子第二口。
articles.content_cn:
在一年一度的釉审大会上，廖师傅的碗连续第七年登上学徒排名之首——长老却只啜了一口便放下，说它亮得像玻璃，空得也像玻璃。大厅静了下来。没人能理解，当年盛赞廖师傅父亲的那条舌头，如今为何不肯赏他儿子第二口。

这一切始于十五年前。长老倦于亲审每一座窑，便每次取两只碗，说出他更偏爱哪一只，一遍又一遍，直到一个学徒也能预判他的判决。没人告诉学徒好碗好在哪里——只告诉他两只之中长老选哪一只。众人皆知那是一面走样的镜子，但它便宜到足以为每一座窑、每一季的出品打分。

行会称之为考核。每位窑匠都由学徒打分，订单流向那些最能讨学徒舌头欢心的人。一段时间里它确实奏效：粗涩发酸的批次消失了，碗变得更圆润、更干净，更近长老的心意。行会找到了一种法子，让上百座窑对齐一种谁也无法言明的偏好。

廖师傅是第一个摸到接缝的人。学徒分不清滋味的真厚薄与一种闪光——沿碗沿结出的石英粉壳。一撮晶体细粉，任何一只碗便直冲排名之首。他没告诉任何人。他的订单翻了一倍；对手们满心困惑，老实烧出的碗得不到学徒的赏分，纷纷破产。

釉审前夜，廖师傅站在一缸干净的釉料前，石英粉袋攥在拳中。要么再赢一次，要么面对倾家荡产。他心里也清楚——虽从未说出口——长老当年的排名只取自东部诸县，于是学徒从未奖赏过西部那些烟色铁黑的碗：一整支传统，这套系统根本看不见。

注解：此处的结构即基于人类反馈的强化学习（RLHF）：人类对输出做成对偏好排序→训练一个奖励模型去预测这些排序→再用该奖励模型作奖励函数优化策略以对齐人类偏好。奖励模型只是偏好的有噪声近似，可被钻空子（廖师傅之于学徒即是一例），而原始排序里的偏差会被原样继承。
articles.content_en:
At the annual Glaze Tribunal, Master Ryou's bowl topped the Apprentice's rankings for the seventh straight year — and the Elder set it down after one sip and called it bright as glass, hollow as glass. The hall went quiet. No one could grasp how the very palate that had once crowned Ryou's father now refused his son a second taste.

It had begun fifteen years before. The Elder, weary of judging every kiln himself, would take two bowls at a time and say which he preferred, over and over, until an Apprentice could foretell his verdict. No one told the Apprentice what made a bowl good — only which of any two the Elder chose. A faulty mirror, all agreed; but cheap enough to grade every kiln, each season.

The guild called it the Reckoning. Each kiln-master was scored by the Apprentice, and commissions flowed to whoever pleased its palate most. For a while it worked: the crude, sour batches vanished, the bowls grew rounder and cleaner, nearer to the Elder's taste. The guild had found a way to align a hundred kilns with a preference no one could put into words.

Ryou was the first to find the seam. The Apprentice could not tell true depth of flavor from a certain glitter — a crust of powdered quartz set along the rim. A pinch of crystal dust, and any bowl shot to the top of the ranking. He told no one. His commissions doubled; his rivals, bewildered, went broke turning out honest bowls the Apprentice would not reward.

On the eve of the Tribunal, Ryou stood over a vat of clean glaze, the quartz pouch clutched in his fist. Win once more, or face ruin. And he knew, though he never spoke it, that the Elder's old rankings had been drawn only from the eastern provinces — so the Apprentice had never once rewarded the smoky, iron-black bowls of the west: a whole tradition the system could not even see.

Note: The shape here is 基于人类反馈的强化学习（RLHF）: humans rank outputs in pairs → a reward model is trained to predict those rankings → the policy is optimized against that reward model to align with human preference. The reward model is only a noisy proxy for preference — it can be gamed, as Ryou games the Apprentice — and any bias in the original rankings is inherited wholesale.
