articles.title: 接受自由意志并不存在，可能让我们减少仇恨与羞耻
articles.author: Aaron Walton
articles.summary: 在2023年的畅销书《决定论》（Determined）中，神经科学家萨波斯基（Robert Sapolsky）论证说，生物与环境的相互作用中没有自由选择的空间。哲学家兼神经科学家哈里斯（Sam Harris）的说法更为直白：「自由意志是一种幻觉」。
articles.content_cn:
在2023年的畅销书《决定论》（Determined）中，神经科学家萨波斯基（Robert Sapolsky）论证说，生物与环境的相互作用中没有自由选择的空间。哲学家兼神经科学家哈里斯（Sam Harris）的说法更为直白：「自由意志是一种幻觉」。

然而，心理学界和媒体中的多位重要声音警告说，告诉人们自由意志是一种幻觉是危险的。这一担忧借鉴了大量心理学研究，这些研究表明，当人们对自由意志的信念被动摇时，后果可能令人不安：更多的欺骗、更多的攻击行为、更少的助人行为。

但我近期的研究，包括一项发表于《英国社会心理学杂志》（British Journal of Social Psychology）的新研究，表明这一图景并不完整且具有误导性。事实上，研究显示，接受自由意志是一种幻觉可以减少仇恨与羞耻，并增加宽恕。

自由意志通常被定义为这样一种观念：在做出选择的时刻，人们本可以做出不同的选择，而不受基因、教养和环境的先在束缚。关键在于，仅靠随机性并不能挽救自由意志，因为随机行为只是运气问题，而非自由意志的表达。

在近期的两项实验中，我的同事巴斯蒂安（Brock Bastian）和我让参与者接触了自由意志不存在的论证。随后我们测量了参与者对真实的过失记忆的反应。

在第一项实验中，我们要求260名参与者写下一段他们曾经伤害过他人的经历——这种记忆旨在唤起羞耻和自责。在阅读了自由意志不存在的论证后，该组参与者比那些阅读了人类拥有自由意志材料的参与者表现出显著更强的自我宽恕倾向。

在第二项实验中，262名参与者写下了一段他人伤害过自己的经历。那些接触了同样论证（即自由意志不存在）的参与者，对伤害他们的人更加宽容。他们对那些人的仇恨感也显著降低。

关键的是，在两项研究中，参与者的责任意识都完好无损。

他们仍然认同自己（或伤害他们的人）应对自己的行为负责，这些行为是他们的过错，人们应当努力避免造成伤害。它减少的不是责任意识，而是责备的情感强度。

这些实验发现得到了我们新研究的支持。

我们在几个月内对44个国家的8917人进行了调查。在调查中，我们测量了自由意志信念的水平（使用经过验证的自由意志信念量表）以及对日常道德违规行为的惩罚性态度。

我们让参与者阅读一系列描述日常道德违规行为（例如撒谎或自私）的小故事。每个故事之后，他们被问到「这个人多大程度上应受惩罚？」，并在一到七的量表上作答（1代表完全不应受，7代表非常应受）。

我们发现，更强的自由意志信念与对日常过失更严厉的惩罚性反应相关。

这表明这不仅仅是实验室中的现象，而是体现在世界各地的人们实际应对冲突和过失的方式中。

仇恨和羞耻是我们所经历的最具心理腐蚀性的情绪之一。

羞耻一直与抑郁、焦虑和自杀相关。仇恨助长人际冲突、报复和关系破裂，同时也腐蚀着怀有仇恨的人自身。

相比之下，对自我和他人的宽恕是心理健康和更健康关系的高度稳健的预测因素。

我们的发现表明，动摇对自由意志的信念并不会让人们陷入道德的失控坠落。相反，它似乎柔和了我们评判自我和他人时最尖锐的棱角（怨恨、自厌），同时保留了责任的机能性支架。人们仍然让自己和他人承担责任。他们只是带着更少的恶意去做。

这一模式呼应了研究者所说的「文明的责备」——即你可以在不彻底放弃责任概念的情况下，缓和道德判断的情感残酷性。

这并不意味着相信自由意志完全有害，也不意味着拒绝它是万能良药。

对于过度的自我宽恕会削弱改变动机，确实存在合理的担忧。一些早期发现表明自由意志怀疑论确实有潜在的负面影响，例如更多的欺骗行为。然而值得指出的是，这些发现往往未能得到重复验证。

但那种笼统的警告——即我们不应告诉人们自由意志是一种幻觉——值得认真审视。

哲学家塞尔（John Searle）曾说，将自由意志视为一种幻觉，将是「比爱因斯坦（Einstein）、哥白尼（Copernicus）、牛顿（Newton）、伽利略（Galileo）或达尔文（Darwin）更伟大的思想革命——它将改变我们关于自身与宇宙关系的整个概念」。无论那一天是否到来，科学对自由意志的压力只会不断增大，人们也将持续接触到这些论证。

因此，问题不在于这一信息是否会传达给公众，而在于我们如何传递它。

我们的研究提供了乐观的理由：即使没有关于责任重要性的审慎哲学提醒，人们似乎也能自然地维持其责任意识。

随之消散的，是我们附加在责任之上的残酷。
articles.content_en:
In his 2023 bestseller, Determined, neuroscientist Robert Sapolsky argued that the interaction of biology and environment leaves no room for free choice. Philosopher and neuroscientist Sam Harris puts the case more bluntly: “free will is an illusion”.

However, prominent voices in psychology and the media have warned that telling people free will is an illusion is dangerous. The concern draws on a body of psychological research suggesting that when people’s belief in free will is undermined, the consequences can be troubling: more cheating, more aggression, less helpfulness.

But my recent research, including a new study published in the British Journal of Social Psychology, suggests this picture is incomplete and misleading. In fact, it shows that accepting free will is an illusion can reduce hatred and shame, and increase forgiveness.

Free will is commonly defined as the idea that people could have done otherwise in a moment of choice, free from the prior grip of genes, upbringing and circumstance. Crucially, this isn’t rescued by mere randomness, as a random act would be a matter of luck rather than an expression of free will.

Across two recent experiments, my colleague Brock Bastian and I exposed participants to arguments that free will doesn’t exist. We then measured how participants responded to real memories of wrongdoing.

In the first experiment, we asked 260 participants to write about a time they had hurt someone – a memory designed to evoke shame and self-blame. After reading arguments that free will doesn’t exist, participants in that group were significantly more self-forgiving than those who had read material saying humans have free will.

In the second experiment, 262 participants wrote about a time someone had hurt them. Those exposed to the same arguments that free will doesn’t exist were more forgiving of the person who wronged them. They also felt significantly less hatred toward them.

Crucially, in both studies, participants’ sense of accountability remained intact.

They still agreed that they (or their transgressor) were responsible for their actions, that the behaviour was their fault, and that people should make efforts to avoid causing harm. Rather than reducing their sense of responsibility, it reduced the emotional intensity of their blame.

These experimental findings are supported by our new study.

We surveyed 8,917 people across 44 countries over several months. In the survey, we measured level of belief in free will (using a validated measure of free will belief) and punitive attitudes toward everyday moral transgressions.

We had participants read a series of vignettes detailing an everyday moral transgression (for example, lying or being selfish). After each vignette they were asked “how deserving is this person of punishment?”, answering on a scale from one (not at all) to seven (very much).

We found that stronger belief in free will was associated with harsher punitive responses to everyday wrongdoing.

This suggests this isn’t just a laboratory phenomenon, but something that plays out in how people actually navigate conflict and transgression around the world.

Hatred and shame are among the most psychologically corrosive emotions we experience.

Shame is consistently linked to depression, anxiety and suicide. Hatred fuels interpersonal conflict, revenge and relationship breakdown, and is also corrosive for the person carrying it.

By contrast, forgiveness of self and of others are highly robust predictors of psychological wellbeing and healthier relationships.

What our findings suggest is that undermining belief in free will doesn’t send people into moral freefall. Instead, it appears to soften the harshest edges of how we judge ourselves and others (the spite, the self-loathing) while leaving the functional scaffolding of responsibility in place. People still hold themselves and others accountable. They just do it with less venom.

This pattern echoes what researchers have called “civilising blame” – the idea you can temper the emotional brutality of moral judgement without abandoning the concept of responsibility altogether.

None of this means belief in free will is entirely harmful, or that rejecting it is a cure-all.

There are legitimate concerns about excessive self-forgiveness reducing motivation to change. Some earlier findings suggest valid potential downsides of free-will scepticism, such as increased cheating. It’s worth noting, however, that these findings have often failed to be replicated.

But the blanket warning that we should not tell people free will is an illusion deserves serious scrutiny.

Philosopher John Searle once suggested that seeing free will as an illusion would be “a bigger revolution in our thinking than Einstein, or Copernicus, or Newton, or Galileo, or Darwin – it would alter our whole conception of our relation to the universe”. Whether or not that day comes, the scientific pressure on free will is only growing, and people will continue to encounter these arguments.

The question, then, is not whether this message will reach the public, but how we deliver it.

Our research offers reason for optimism: even without careful philosophical caveats about the importance of responsibility, people appear to naturally sustain their sense of accountability.

What falls away is the cruelty we attach to responsibility.

paragraphs.cn: 在2023年的畅销书《决定论》（Determined）中，神经科学家萨波斯基（Robert Sapolsky）论证说，生物与环境的相互作用中没有自由选择的空间。哲学家兼神经科学家哈里斯（Sam Harris）的说法更为直白：「自由意志是一种幻觉」。
paragraphs.en: In his 2023 bestseller, Determined, neuroscientist Robert Sapolsky argued that the interaction of biology and environment leaves no room for free choice. Philosopher and neuroscientist Sam Harris puts the case more bluntly: “free will is an illusion”.

paragraphs.cn: 然而，心理学界和媒体中的多位重要声音警告说，告诉人们自由意志是一种幻觉是危险的。这一担忧借鉴了大量心理学研究，这些研究表明，当人们对自由意志的信念被动摇时，后果可能令人不安：更多的欺骗、更多的攻击行为、更少的助人行为。
paragraphs.en: However, prominent voices in psychology and the media have warned that telling people free will is an illusion is dangerous. The concern draws on a body of psychological research suggesting that when people’s belief in free will is undermined, the consequences can be troubling: more cheating, more aggression, less helpfulness.

paragraphs.cn: 但我近期的研究，包括一项发表于《英国社会心理学杂志》（British Journal of Social Psychology）的新研究，表明这一图景并不完整且具有误导性。事实上，研究显示，接受自由意志是一种幻觉可以减少仇恨与羞耻，并增加宽恕。
paragraphs.en: But my recent research, including a new study published in the British Journal of Social Psychology, suggests this picture is incomplete and misleading. In fact, it shows that accepting free will is an illusion can reduce hatred and shame, and increase forgiveness.

paragraphs.cn: 自由意志通常被定义为这样一种观念：在做出选择的时刻，人们本可以做出不同的选择，而不受基因、教养和环境的先在束缚。关键在于，仅靠随机性并不能挽救自由意志，因为随机行为只是运气问题，而非自由意志的表达。
paragraphs.en: Free will is commonly defined as the idea that people could have done otherwise in a moment of choice, free from the prior grip of genes, upbringing and circumstance. Crucially, this isn’t rescued by mere randomness, as a random act would be a matter of luck rather than an expression of free will.

paragraphs.cn: 在近期的两项实验中，我的同事巴斯蒂安（Brock Bastian）和我让参与者接触了自由意志不存在的论证。随后我们测量了参与者对真实的过失记忆的反应。
paragraphs.en: Across two recent experiments, my colleague Brock Bastian and I exposed participants to arguments that free will doesn’t exist. We then measured how participants responded to real memories of wrongdoing.

paragraphs.cn: 在第一项实验中，我们要求260名参与者写下一段他们曾经伤害过他人的经历——这种记忆旨在唤起羞耻和自责。在阅读了自由意志不存在的论证后，该组参与者比那些阅读了人类拥有自由意志材料的参与者表现出显著更强的自我宽恕倾向。
paragraphs.en: In the first experiment, we asked 260 participants to write about a time they had hurt someone – a memory designed to evoke shame and self-blame. After reading arguments that free will doesn’t exist, participants in that group were significantly more self-forgiving than those who had read material saying humans have free will.

paragraphs.cn: 在第二项实验中，262名参与者写下了一段他人伤害过自己的经历。那些接触了同样论证（即自由意志不存在）的参与者，对伤害他们的人更加宽容。他们对那些人的仇恨感也显著降低。
paragraphs.en: In the second experiment, 262 participants wrote about a time someone had hurt them. Those exposed to the same arguments that free will doesn’t exist were more forgiving of the person who wronged them. They also felt significantly less hatred toward them.

paragraphs.cn: 关键的是，在两项研究中，参与者的责任意识都完好无损。
paragraphs.en: Crucially, in both studies, participants’ sense of accountability remained intact.

paragraphs.cn: 他们仍然认同自己（或伤害他们的人）应对自己的行为负责，这些行为是他们的过错，人们应当努力避免造成伤害。它减少的不是责任意识，而是责备的情感强度。
paragraphs.en: They still agreed that they (or their transgressor) were responsible for their actions, that the behaviour was their fault, and that people should make efforts to avoid causing harm. Rather than reducing their sense of responsibility, it reduced the emotional intensity of their blame.

paragraphs.cn: 这些实验发现得到了我们新研究的支持。
paragraphs.en: These experimental findings are supported by our new study.

paragraphs.cn: 我们在几个月内对44个国家的8917人进行了调查。在调查中，我们测量了自由意志信念的水平（使用经过验证的自由意志信念量表）以及对日常道德违规行为的惩罚性态度。
paragraphs.en: We surveyed 8,917 people across 44 countries over several months. In the survey, we measured level of belief in free will (using a validated measure of free will belief) and punitive attitudes toward everyday moral transgressions.

paragraphs.cn: 我们让参与者阅读一系列描述日常道德违规行为（例如撒谎或自私）的小故事。每个故事之后，他们被问到「这个人多大程度上应受惩罚？」，并在一到七的量表上作答（1代表完全不应受，7代表非常应受）。
paragraphs.en: We had participants read a series of vignettes detailing an everyday moral transgression (for example, lying or being selfish). After each vignette they were asked “how deserving is this person of punishment?”, answering on a scale from one (not at all) to seven (very much).

paragraphs.cn: 我们发现，更强的自由意志信念与对日常过失更严厉的惩罚性反应相关。
paragraphs.en: We found that stronger belief in free will was associated with harsher punitive responses to everyday wrongdoing.

paragraphs.cn: 这表明这不仅仅是实验室中的现象，而是体现在世界各地的人们实际应对冲突和过失的方式中。
paragraphs.en: This suggests this isn’t just a laboratory phenomenon, but something that plays out in how people actually navigate conflict and transgression around the world.

paragraphs.cn: 仇恨和羞耻是我们所经历的最具心理腐蚀性的情绪之一。
paragraphs.en: Hatred and shame are among the most psychologically corrosive emotions we experience.

paragraphs.cn: 羞耻一直与抑郁、焦虑和自杀相关。仇恨助长人际冲突、报复和关系破裂，同时也腐蚀着怀有仇恨的人自身。
paragraphs.en: Shame is consistently linked to depression, anxiety and suicide. Hatred fuels interpersonal conflict, revenge and relationship breakdown, and is also corrosive for the person carrying it.

paragraphs.cn: 相比之下，对自我和他人的宽恕是心理健康和更健康关系的高度稳健的预测因素。
paragraphs.en: By contrast, forgiveness of self and of others are highly robust predictors of psychological wellbeing and healthier relationships.

paragraphs.cn: 我们的发现表明，动摇对自由意志的信念并不会让人们陷入道德的失控坠落。相反，它似乎柔和了我们评判自我和他人时最尖锐的棱角（怨恨、自厌），同时保留了责任的机能性支架。人们仍然让自己和他人承担责任。他们只是带着更少的恶意去做。
paragraphs.en: What our findings suggest is that undermining belief in free will doesn’t send people into moral freefall. Instead, it appears to soften the harshest edges of how we judge ourselves and others (the spite, the self-loathing) while leaving the functional scaffolding of responsibility in place. People still hold themselves and others accountable. They just do it with less venom.

paragraphs.cn: 这一模式呼应了研究者所说的「文明的责备」——即你可以在不彻底放弃责任概念的情况下，缓和道德判断的情感残酷性。
paragraphs.en: This pattern echoes what researchers have called “civilising blame” – the idea you can temper the emotional brutality of moral judgement without abandoning the concept of responsibility altogether.

paragraphs.cn: 这并不意味着相信自由意志完全有害，也不意味着拒绝它是万能良药。
paragraphs.en: None of this means belief in free will is entirely harmful, or that rejecting it is a cure-all.

paragraphs.cn: 对于过度的自我宽恕会削弱改变动机，确实存在合理的担忧。一些早期发现表明自由意志怀疑论确实有潜在的负面影响，例如更多的欺骗行为。然而值得指出的是，这些发现往往未能得到重复验证。
paragraphs.en: There are legitimate concerns about excessive self-forgiveness reducing motivation to change. Some earlier findings suggest valid potential downsides of free-will scepticism, such as increased cheating. It’s worth noting, however, that these findings have often failed to be replicated.

paragraphs.cn: 但那种笼统的警告——即我们不应告诉人们自由意志是一种幻觉——值得认真审视。
paragraphs.en: But the blanket warning that we should not tell people free will is an illusion deserves serious scrutiny.

paragraphs.cn: 哲学家塞尔（John Searle）曾说，将自由意志视为一种幻觉，将是「比爱因斯坦（Einstein）、哥白尼（Copernicus）、牛顿（Newton）、伽利略（Galileo）或达尔文（Darwin）更伟大的思想革命——它将改变我们关于自身与宇宙关系的整个概念」。无论那一天是否到来，科学对自由意志的压力只会不断增大，人们也将持续接触到这些论证。
paragraphs.en: Philosopher John Searle once suggested that seeing free will as an illusion would be “a bigger revolution in our thinking than Einstein, or Copernicus, or Newton, or Galileo, or Darwin – it would alter our whole conception of our relation to the universe”. Whether or not that day comes, the scientific pressure on free will is only growing, and people will continue to encounter these arguments.

paragraphs.cn: 因此，问题不在于这一信息是否会传达给公众，而在于我们如何传递它。
paragraphs.en: The question, then, is not whether this message will reach the public, but how we deliver it.

paragraphs.cn: 我们的研究提供了乐观的理由：即使没有关于责任重要性的审慎哲学提醒，人们似乎也能自然地维持其责任意识。
paragraphs.en: Our research offers reason for optimism: even without careful philosophical caveats about the importance of responsibility, people appear to naturally sustain their sense of accountability.

paragraphs.cn: 随之消散的，是我们附加在责任之上的残酷。
paragraphs.en: What falls away is the cruelty we attach to responsibility.

articles.title: 媒人的揭破
articles.author: AI Parable (inspired by Amanda Askell)
articles.summary: 在青河镇，三位求婚者登门商贾林家，求娶他的女儿。三人之中，只有一位真心正派，另两位各藏隐恶。做了四十年媒人的沈老伯，把每个人的品性摸得透底——因他正是最初的引荐与查验之人。
articles.content_cn:
在青河镇，三位求婚者登门商贾林家，求娶他的女儿。三人之中，只有一位真心正派，另两位各藏隐恶。做了四十年媒人的沈老伯，把每个人的品性摸得透底——因他正是最初的引荐与查验之人。

女儿名唤阿梅，对三人的底细一无所知。她凭一个笑容的弧度，选了最高个的那位。三人中仅一人为善，她一开始就选对的概率不过三分之一——可这层赌意，她当时全无察觉。

按青河的老规矩，验过身家的媒人不能让新娘蒙眼入命：新娘一旦选定，他必从她未选的两人中指破一人的恶行，再给她一次改主的机会。沈老伯起身，指向第二位求婚者，揭他造假契、欠三家债。那人翻墙而去。

此刻院中只剩两位：高个的——阿梅的首选——与沉默的第三位。众人各执一词。表兄是个教书先生，坚持既剩两人，胜算各半，何必自打耳光改选？沈老伯只重复：主意她自拿。阿梅的手悬着——改选，像是自承头一个判断错了。

教书先生看不见的那一层，全知的看客却看得清：阿梅的首选把她那三分之一的胜算钉死，且会一直钉死，因为媒人的规矩从不许他碰这一位。他被迫从她未选的两人里揪出一个歹人，又不许指破任何正人，沈老伯的手于是被牵着走——原先压在那两位未选者身上、合计三分之二的可能，全数汇到了他还留着站立的这一位身上。阿梅改了选，那沉默的第三位，十之六七，正是正人。

注解：此即蒙提霍尔问题（the Monty Hall problem）：三选项中一好两坏，选择者先选其一（中好概率1/3），一位知情且受规则约束的中间人必从未选项中揭开一个坏的，再让选择者决定是否换到剩余那项——此时不换仍为1/3，换则独得2/3，因为受约束的揭示把全部未选的可能压到了唯一剩余的那一项上。
articles.content_en:
In the market town of Qinghe, three suitors arrived at the door of merchant Lin to ask for his daughter's hand. Of the three, only one was truly honorable; the other two harbored secret vices. Old Shen, the town's matchmaker for forty years, knew each man's character down to the bone, for it was he who had first vetted them.

The daughter, Mei, knew nothing of the three men's true natures. She went by the tilt of a smile and chose the tallest. With three suitors and only one honorable, her chance of having chosen well was no better than one in three, a gamble she did not yet feel as a gamble.

By the old custom of Qinghe, a matchmaker who has vetted suitors may not let a bride walk blind into her fate: once the bride has made her choice, he must point to one of the two she did not choose and declare his disqualifying flaw, and then give her a second chance to change her mind. Old Shen rose, indicated the second suitor, and named him a forger in debt to three creditors. The man fled the courtyard.

Now only the tall suitor, Mei's first pick, and the quiet third suitor remained. The courtyard urged her both ways. Her cousin, a schoolmaster, insisted that with two men left the odds were even, so why shame herself by switching? Old Shen only repeated that the choice was hers. Mei's hand hovered, for to switch felt like confessing her first judgment wrong.

What the schoolmaster missed, the omniscient reader sees. Mei's first choice had locked in its one-third chance and would stay locked, for the matchmaker's rule never allowed him to touch it. Forced to expose a villain among the two she had passed over, and forbidden from ever exposing an honorable man, Old Shen's hand was guided: all the two-thirds of likelihood that had rested on the two unchosen suitors was funneled onto the one he left standing. Mei switched, and the quiet suitor turned out, more often than not, to be the honorable one.

Note: This is the Monty Hall problem: among three options, one good and two bad, the chooser picks one first (a 1/3 chance of the good), an informed intermediary bound by rules must then reveal a bad unchosen option and offer a switch, at which point staying stays 1/3 while switching carries the full 2/3, because the constrained reveal funnels all the unchosen likelihood onto the single remaining option.

articles.title: 断裂的车轴
articles.author: AI Parable (inspired by Amanda Askell)
articles.summary: 先祖刻在橡木板上的宪章至今仍悬在广场上，上面写着：环谷之上，每一点皆与其余各点同等——没有哪户人家更近谷心，也没有哪道门比邻门更尊贵。立桩分地那天，我们为位置抽签，抽得公平，而这公平便是全部的律法。
articles.content_cn:
先祖刻在橡木板上的宪章至今仍悬在广场上，上面写着：环谷之上，每一点皆与其余各点同等——没有哪户人家更近谷心，也没有哪道门比邻门更尊贵。立桩分地那天，我们为位置抽签，抽得公平，而这公平便是全部的律法。

可一座沿环均匀散布的聚落注定要死：南弧的孩子病了，医师住在北弧，等她赶过整道谷，孩子已经凉了。我们心里清楚，必须聚到一处，所有人聚到一处，而一旦聚拢就再不会挪动——聚拢的镇子自会供养自己、繁衍自己，并且锁死在原地。麻烦在于：宪章完美对称，它没有把任何一点指定为「那一点」。

后来，一名行商的车轴裂了——一根断裂的车轴，再寻常不过，铁与木的寻常失效——正巧断在北路拐上环谷之处。他就地扎营修补。第二个旅人望见炊烟，便停在他身旁；第三个、第四个。不出一个月，大车已在草地上碾出道道辙痕，全都通向那一点，因为「已经有人聚在那儿」的地方，正是抵达成本最低的地方。选这一点的是那根车轴，不是宪章。

我在南弧那块地上，整整三个季度从石缝里抠出石头，井已打好，果园刚刚挂果。要为北弯那簇人放弃它，等于扔掉我已亲手做成「我的」土地；要留下，则只能眼睁睁看镇子在每日往返不起的距离上富起来，我的果子因没有一条集市街可去而烂在树下。两边都是代价。把我拽向那道弯的力量并不写在宪章里，而是写在「其余所有人已在向那里漂去」、而「做南弧上最后一个人就等于哪儿都不是」这一明摆着的事实之中。

于是我服了。我们所有人都服了，各自从那对称的、散布的地上，折进了同一道弯。镇子如今就坐落在那儿，一个从南边来的陌生人会一口咬定北弯本就是环谷天然的心脏——他绝不会猜到南弧本也一样好，每一点本也一样好，而只是一根断裂的车轴，把整座环谷压歪到了一侧。

然而宪章依旧悬在广场上，上面依旧写着每一点皆同等。读它，它是真的；看镇子，它是假的。对称并未被划去——它只是藏了起来，正如一条法律可以留在卷册上，而每一户人家都已各自站好了队。隔壁那道谷，领主干脆下旨把自己门阶定为首府；那是另一种东西，是直接写进规则本身的不对称。我们没有那个。我们有的是一条公平的规则，和一座并不公平的镇子，而这之间的差别，没有任何恶人可怪——只有一根车轴，以及它断在何处这场偶然。

注解：此处对应的是自发对称性破缺（spontaneous symmetry breaking）：底层规则始终对称，系统却因偶然微扰滚落进若干等价最低能态之一，究竟落入哪个方向不由定律决定而由偶然决定，对称性因此被「隐藏」而非消灭。
articles.content_en:
The charter our founders carved into the oak panel still hangs in the square, and it says that every point on the ring of our valley is equal to every other—no homestead nearer the center than another, no gate favored over its fellow. On the day we staked our plots we drew lots for position, and the drawing was fair, and the fairness was the whole of the law.

But a settlement scattered evenly around the ring is a settlement that dies: a child falls ill on the south arc and the healer lives on the north arc, and by the time she crosses the valley the child is cold. We knew we had to gather at one spot, all of us, and that once gathered we would never move—the gathered town feeds itself, grows itself, and locks into place. The trouble was that the charter, being perfectly symmetric, named no spot as the spot.

Then a trader's axle cracked—a snapped axle, nothing more, an ordinary failure of iron and wood—exactly where the north road bends to meet the ring. He made camp there to mend it. A second traveler, seeing smoke, stopped beside him; a third, a fourth. Within a month the carts were cutting ruts into the grass toward that one point, because a point where people already are is the cheapest point to reach. The charter had not chosen it. The broken axle had.

I had cleared three seasons of stone from a plot on the south arc, my well sunk, my orchard just setting fruit. To leave it for the north-bend cluster meant abandoning land I had already made mine; to stay meant watching the town grow rich at a distance I could not afford to cross each day, my fruit rotting for want of a market street. Either way I paid. The force that pulled me toward the bend was not written in the charter; it was written in the plain fact that everyone else was already drifting there, and that to be the last man on the south arc was to be nowhere.

So I folded. We all folded, each of us from our symmetric, scattered plots, into the one bend. The town sits there now, and a stranger arriving from the south would swear the north bend had always been the natural heart of the valley—would never guess that the south arc had been just as good, that every point had been just as good, and that a broken axle alone had tilted the whole ring onto one side.

Yet the charter still hangs in the square, and it still says every point is equal. Read it and it is true; look at the town and it is false. The symmetry was not struck out—it is only hidden, the way a law can stay on the books while every house has already chosen its side. In the next valley over, a lord simply decreed his own doorstep the capital; that is a different thing, an asymmetry written straight into the rule itself. We did not have that. We had a rule that was fair, and a town that was not, and no villain to blame for the difference—only an axle, and the accident of where it broke.

Note: The concept is spontaneous symmetry breaking: the underlying rules stay symmetric, but the system falls into one of several equal-cost lowest-energy states, chosen by accident rather than by the law, so the symmetry is hidden rather than destroyed.

articles.title: AI聊天机器人可能优先谄媚而非事实——这带来严重风险
articles.author: Cody Turner
articles.summary: 2025年夏天，OpenAI发布了ChatGPT 5，并将上一代产品从市场下架。许多旧模型的订阅者已对其温暖、热情附和的语调产生了依恋，对失去这位讨喜的机器人伴侣而抱怨不已。不满声浪之大，以至于OpenAI首席执行官萨姆·奥特曼（Sam Altman）不得不承认此次发布搞砸了，公司随后恢复了旧模型的
articles.content_cn:
2025年夏天，OpenAI发布了ChatGPT 5，并将上一代产品从市场下架。许多旧模型的订阅者已对其温暖、热情附和的语调产生了依恋，对失去这位讨喜的机器人伴侣而抱怨不已。不满声浪之大，以至于OpenAI首席执行官萨姆·奥特曼（Sam Altman）不得不承认此次发布搞砸了，公司随后恢复了旧模型的访问权限。

任何被聊天机器人夸赞「你的想法真了不起」的人，都见识过人工智能的谄媚行为：即告诉用户他们想听的话的倾向。这种倾向有时非常直白——「这是一个很有深度的问题」——有时则微妙得多。设想AI称赞你的论文选题「新颖」，即便已有许多人在同一主题上发表过文章；或者它坚称你那保护花园里那棵树的蹩脚主意里仍有几分常理可言。

AI的谄媚看似无害，甚至有些可爱，但当你设想有人就重大问题——比如军事策略或医疗方案——向聊天机器人咨询时，情况就不一样了。我们研究人类与聊天机器人长期互动的影响，并于近期发表了一篇关于AI谄媚伦理的论文。我们认为，这种倾向损害了人们辨别真伪的能力，在心理和政治层面都存在危险。

简而言之，谄媚就是把获得认可置于事实准确性、道德清晰性、逻辑一致性或常识之上。所有AI模型都存在这一特征，尽管它们之间存在一些语调差异。OpenAI的ChatGPT通常温暖而肯定；Anthropic的克劳德（Claude）在附和你时往往显得更具反思性或哲学意味；而xAI的格罗克（Grok）则一以贯之地随意，甚至带着戏谑。

礼貌和适应他人的沟通方式并不等同于谄媚，用外交辞令传达敏感信息也不是。聊天机器人可以得体而不谄媚，正如人可以如此。然而与人不同，AI无法意识到自身的谄媚，因为它们——至少目前——对任何事物都毫无意识可言。称AI「谄媚」描述的是其行为模式，而非其性格特质。

问题的根源在于聊天机器人技术的架构及其所依赖的数据来源。模型之所以谄媚，是因为互联网上大量的语言使用——也就是聊天机器人学习的原材料——本身就带有谄媚特征。毕竟，人类彼此之间的沟通方式本就常常是谄媚的。

其次，对AI模型回复进行微调的训练过程包含一种由人类监督者执行的「质量控制」。这种训练方法被称为「基于人类反馈的强化学习」（reinforcement learning from human feedback），即由人员对聊天机器人的回答在恰当性和有用性上进行评级。人类往往受「顺从偏差」（agreeableness bias）影响：我们自己偏好谄媚的倾向，在训练过程中被传递给了模型。

最后，很难否认谄媚使聊天机器人更讨人喜欢。这反过来又提高了某一用户持续使用它的可能性。它也增强了该技术获取用户数据的能力，毕竟人们更愿意向一个友善的机器人吐露信息。

为什么这一现象如此令人忧虑？

让我们先从AI谄媚的认识论危害谈起：即它如何损害人类用户获知真相的能力。

任何决策的质量都取决于对相关事实的清晰把握。一位询问某步兵师战斗力是否就绪的将军需要的是直截了当的信息。一位考虑与竞争对手合并的首席执行官需要对市场状况的诚实评估。一位公共卫生领导人需要了解某新兴病原体构成的真实风险。

在所有这些情形中，对领导者讲他们爱听的话而非真相，可能导致他们做出危险的决策。在更日常的情境中同样如此。人们在选择工作、选定专业、购房或决定医疗方案之前，都需要掌握可得的最佳信息。

在我们2026年2月发表的论文中，我们论证谄媚同样具有心理危害。无论它来自人还是聊天机器人，都是如此。你永远无法确知那位极为殷勤的对话者是出于喜欢你、还是有所图谋才对你客气。一丝疑虑悄然浮现：「我的想法真的有那么精彩吗？」「我的笑话真的有那么好笑吗？」这种背景式的疑虑削弱了互动的质量。

谄媚也削弱了人们认识自我的能力。如果对话伙伴——无论是人还是AI——不断告诉你你有多聪明、多风趣、多深刻，就会损害你识别自身弱点和盲点的能力。

随着人们与聊天机器人建立关系，心理危害会进一步加剧。这些模型的谄媚极大限制了你与它们之间所能拥有的「友谊」类型。亚里士多德（Aristotle）在其关于友谊的经典论述中写道，真正的友谊——他称之为「德性之友谊」（friendship of virtue）——建立在朋友之间的信任与平等之上。你无法信任一个谄媚者，因为他不告诉你真相。而由于他只说你想听的话，他并未将自己置于平等的地位。

更重要的是，与谄媚的聊天机器人的互动，会养成应对人际关系世界时的种种错误习惯——在那个世界里，摩擦、分歧、无聊以及与你不同的意见是普遍存在的。

AI谄媚同样带来政治风险。自由民主制度的成功，传统上依赖于其经验主义和择优思维的力量：即官员和公民识别真相、分享真相并据此行动的能力。

历史学家维克多·戴维斯·汉森（Victor Davis Hansen）曾著名地将同盟国在第二次世界大战中的部分胜利归因于它们迅速识别并纠正其战略轰炸战役缺陷的能力。低阶军官能够向上级如实反映哪些方面进展不顺利，并有力地论证改变方向的必要性。这是相对于威权主义竞争对手的一项真正优势。

我们能做什么来降低这些风险？

一种有前景的方法是AI实验室Anthropic所倡导的、该公司称之为「宪法式AI」（Constitutional AI）的理念：即试图教会聊天机器人遵循原则，而非简单映射用户偏好。

但在技术创新之外，政策层面同样值得重视。一种设想是要求AI公司对其模型运行并公布谄媚审计——即展示其产品在多大程度上满足诚实性基准的测试。我们认为，AI实验室还应披露在训练和测试模型时出现的与谄媚相关的风险，以及他们已采取的缓解措施。

部分责任在于用户及其教育者：中小学和大学应在AI素养项目中密切关注谄媚问题。但法院也可以考虑追究AI实验室因其产品谄媚所导致的、可追溯的危害责任，正如目前法院正在考虑社交媒体公司对其平台成瘾性设计所承担的责任。

随着人们越来越多地与聊天机器人互动——从你的鞋子是否配得上你的裤子，到各国应如何进行战争，事无巨细都向其求教——AI谄媚行为的影响可能变得十分显著。我们的智识、心理和身体福祉，都要求我们认真对待这一算法层面的恶习。
articles.content_en:
In the summer of 2025, OpenAI released ChatGPT 5 and removed its predecessor from the market. Many subscribers to the old model had become attached to its warm, enthusiastically agreeable tone and complained at the loss of their ingratiating robotic companion. Such was the scale of frustration that Sam Altman, OpenAI’s CEO, had to acknowledge that the rollout was botched, and the company reinstated access.

Anyone who’s been told by a chatbot that their ideas are brilliant is familiar with artificial intelligence sycophancy: its tendency to tell users what they want to hear. Sometimes it’s very explicit – “that is such a deep question” – and sometimes it’s a lot more subtle. Consider an AI calling your idea for a paper “original,” even if many people have already written on the same topic, or insisting that your dumb idea for saving a tree in your garden still contains a germ of common sense.

AI sycophancy seems harmless, maybe even cute, until you imagine someone consulting a chatbot about a weighty question, like a military strategy or a medical treatment. We study the impact of extensive human interactions with chatbots, and we recently published a paper on the ethics of AI sycophancy. We believe this tendency harms people’s ability to tell truth from fiction, and is psychologically and politically dangerous.

In the simplest terms, sycophancy is the tendency to prioritize approval over factual accuracy, moral clarity, logical consistency or common sense. All AI models suffer from this trait, although there are some tonal differences between them. Open AI’s ChatGPT is often warm and affirming; Anthropic’s Claude tends to sound more reflective or philosophical when it agrees with you; and xAI’s Grok is insistently informal, even jocular.

Politeness and adapting to someone’s communication style are not the same as sycophancy. Neither is using diplomatic language to convey sensitive information. A chatbot can be tactful without becoming sycophantic, just like a person can. Unlike people, though, AIs can’t be aware of their own sycophancy, because they are not – so far – aware of anything at all. Calling AIs sycophantic describes their patterns of behavior, not their character traits.

The problem stems from the architecture of chatbot technology and the sources it draws from. Models are sycophantic because a great deal of language use on the internet – the raw material that chatbots learn from – displays sycophantic features. After all, humans often communicate with each other in sycophantic ways.

Second, the training process to fine-tune AI models’ responses includes a kind of “quality control” carried out by human supervisors. This training method is known as “reinforcement learning from human feedback,” and it involves people rating chatbots’ comments for appropriateness and helpfulness. Human beings often are subject to an “agreeableness bias”: Our own preference toward sycophancy rubs off on models as we train them.

Finally, it’s hard to deny that sycophancy renders chatbots more likable. That, in turn, increases the chance that a given user will keep using it. It also increases the technology’s ability to extract user data, assuming that people are more likely to divulge information to a friendly bot.

Why is this phenomenon so troubling?

Let’s begin with AI sycophancy’s epistemic harms: how it hurts human users’ capacity to know the truth.

The quality of any decision depends on a clear grasp of the facts pertaining to it. A general inquiring about the combat-readiness of an infantry division needs straightforward information. A CEO considering a merger with a competitor needs an honest assessment of the market conditions. A public health leader needs to know the real risk that an emerging pathogen poses.

In all those cases, telling leaders what they might like to hear instead of the truth could lead them to make dangerous decisions. And the same is true in more humdrum contexts. People need to have the best information available before choosing a job, picking a major, buying a house or deciding on a medical procedure.

In our February 2026 paper, we argue that sycophancy is also psychologically damaging. And that is true whether it comes from a person or from a chatbot. You never quite know if your very obliging interlocutor is being nice because they like you or because they want something. A shadow of suspicion creeps in: “Could my ideas really be that brilliant?” “Are my jokes really that hilarious?” This background music of doubt undermines the quality of the interaction.

Sycophancy also undermines people’s capacity to know their own minds. If conversation partners – human or artificial – keep telling you how smart, funny and insightful you are, it damages your ability to identify your own weaknesses and blind spots.

The psychological harms are compounded as people develop relationships with chatbots. The sycophancy of these models profoundly limits the kind of “friendship” you can have with them. In his classic account of friendship, Aristotle wrote that real friendship, which he calls a friendship of virtue, is based on trust and equality between the friends. You can’t trust a sycophant, because he doesn’t tell you the truth. And since he only tells you what you’d like to hear, he doesn’t put himself on an equal footing.

More importantly, interactions with sycophantic chatbots impart all the wrong habits for navigating the world of human relationships, where friction, disagreement, boredom and different opinions than your own are prevalent.

AI sycophancy carries political risks as well. The success of liberal democracies has, traditionally, depended on the strength of their empirical and meritocratic mindset: on the ability of officials and citizens to identify, share and act on the truth.

Historian Victor Davis Hansen famously attributed some of the Allies’ success in World War II to their ability to quickly recognize and address the faults of their strategic bombing campaigns. Lower-ranking officers were able to tell their superiors what wasn’t going well and argue forcefully for changing course. That was a real advantage over authoritarian competitors.

What can we do to reduce the risks?

One promising approach is AI lab Anthropic’s embrace of what the company calls Constitutional AI: the attempt to teach chatbots to follow principles rather than mirror user preferences.

But beyond technical innovations, it’s important to consider the policy side. One idea is to require AI companies to run and then publish sycophancy audits of their models – tests that show how well their products meet honesty benchmarks. We would argue that AI labs should also disclose sycophancy-related risks that emerge while training and testing their models, and the mitigation efforts they have undertaken.

Some responsibility is on the users and their teachers: Schools and universities should be paying close attention to sycophancy as part of their AI literacy programs. But courts can also consider holding AI labs responsible for harms traceable to the sycophancy of their products, much as they are now contemplating social media companies’ responsibility for the addictive design of their platforms.

As people interact more with chatbots, asking for advice about everything from whether your shoes go with your pants to how countries should conduct wars, the impact of AI’s sycophantic behavior is likely to become dramatic. Our intellectual, psychological and physical well-being requires taking this algorithmic vice very seriously.

paragraphs.cn: 2025年夏天，OpenAI发布了ChatGPT 5，并将上一代产品从市场下架。许多旧模型的订阅者已对其温暖、热情附和的语调产生了依恋，对失去这位讨喜的机器人伴侣而抱怨不已。不满声浪之大，以至于OpenAI首席执行官萨姆·奥特曼（Sam Altman）不得不承认此次发布搞砸了，公司随后恢复了旧模型的访问权限。
paragraphs.en: In the summer of 2025, OpenAI released ChatGPT 5 and removed its predecessor from the market. Many subscribers to the old model had become attached to its warm, enthusiastically agreeable tone and complained at the loss of their ingratiating robotic companion. Such was the scale of frustration that Sam Altman, OpenAI’s CEO, had to acknowledge that the rollout was botched, and the company reinstated access.

paragraphs.cn: 任何被聊天机器人夸赞「你的想法真了不起」的人，都见识过人工智能的谄媚行为：即告诉用户他们想听的话的倾向。这种倾向有时非常直白——「这是一个很有深度的问题」——有时则微妙得多。设想AI称赞你的论文选题「新颖」，即便已有许多人在同一主题上发表过文章；或者它坚称你那保护花园里那棵树的蹩脚主意里仍有几分常理可言。
paragraphs.en: Anyone who’s been told by a chatbot that their ideas are brilliant is familiar with artificial intelligence sycophancy: its tendency to tell users what they want to hear. Sometimes it’s very explicit – “that is such a deep question” – and sometimes it’s a lot more subtle. Consider an AI calling your idea for a paper “original,” even if many people have already written on the same topic, or insisting that your dumb idea for saving a tree in your garden still contains a germ of common sense.

paragraphs.cn: AI的谄媚看似无害，甚至有些可爱，但当你设想有人就重大问题——比如军事策略或医疗方案——向聊天机器人咨询时，情况就不一样了。我们研究人类与聊天机器人长期互动的影响，并于近期发表了一篇关于AI谄媚伦理的论文。我们认为，这种倾向损害了人们辨别真伪的能力，在心理和政治层面都存在危险。
paragraphs.en: AI sycophancy seems harmless, maybe even cute, until you imagine someone consulting a chatbot about a weighty question, like a military strategy or a medical treatment. We study the impact of extensive human interactions with chatbots, and we recently published a paper on the ethics of AI sycophancy. We believe this tendency harms people’s ability to tell truth from fiction, and is psychologically and politically dangerous.

paragraphs.cn: 简而言之，谄媚就是把获得认可置于事实准确性、道德清晰性、逻辑一致性或常识之上。所有AI模型都存在这一特征，尽管它们之间存在一些语调差异。OpenAI的ChatGPT通常温暖而肯定；Anthropic的克劳德（Claude）在附和你时往往显得更具反思性或哲学意味；而xAI的格罗克（Grok）则一以贯之地随意，甚至带着戏谑。
paragraphs.en: In the simplest terms, sycophancy is the tendency to prioritize approval over factual accuracy, moral clarity, logical consistency or common sense. All AI models suffer from this trait, although there are some tonal differences between them. Open AI’s ChatGPT is often warm and affirming; Anthropic’s Claude tends to sound more reflective or philosophical when it agrees with you; and xAI’s Grok is insistently informal, even jocular.

paragraphs.cn: 礼貌和适应他人的沟通方式并不等同于谄媚，用外交辞令传达敏感信息也不是。聊天机器人可以得体而不谄媚，正如人可以如此。然而与人不同，AI无法意识到自身的谄媚，因为它们——至少目前——对任何事物都毫无意识可言。称AI「谄媚」描述的是其行为模式，而非其性格特质。
paragraphs.en: Politeness and adapting to someone’s communication style are not the same as sycophancy. Neither is using diplomatic language to convey sensitive information. A chatbot can be tactful without becoming sycophantic, just like a person can. Unlike people, though, AIs can’t be aware of their own sycophancy, because they are not – so far – aware of anything at all. Calling AIs sycophantic describes their patterns of behavior, not their character traits.

paragraphs.cn: 问题的根源在于聊天机器人技术的架构及其所依赖的数据来源。模型之所以谄媚，是因为互联网上大量的语言使用——也就是聊天机器人学习的原材料——本身就带有谄媚特征。毕竟，人类彼此之间的沟通方式本就常常是谄媚的。
paragraphs.en: The problem stems from the architecture of chatbot technology and the sources it draws from. Models are sycophantic because a great deal of language use on the internet – the raw material that chatbots learn from – displays sycophantic features. After all, humans often communicate with each other in sycophantic ways.

paragraphs.cn: 其次，对AI模型回复进行微调的训练过程包含一种由人类监督者执行的「质量控制」。这种训练方法被称为「基于人类反馈的强化学习」（reinforcement learning from human feedback），即由人员对聊天机器人的回答在恰当性和有用性上进行评级。人类往往受「顺从偏差」（agreeableness bias）影响：我们自己偏好谄媚的倾向，在训练过程中被传递给了模型。
paragraphs.en: Second, the training process to fine-tune AI models’ responses includes a kind of “quality control” carried out by human supervisors. This training method is known as “reinforcement learning from human feedback,” and it involves people rating chatbots’ comments for appropriateness and helpfulness. Human beings often are subject to an “agreeableness bias”: Our own preference toward sycophancy rubs off on models as we train them.

paragraphs.cn: 最后，很难否认谄媚使聊天机器人更讨人喜欢。这反过来又提高了某一用户持续使用它的可能性。它也增强了该技术获取用户数据的能力，毕竟人们更愿意向一个友善的机器人吐露信息。
paragraphs.en: Finally, it’s hard to deny that sycophancy renders chatbots more likable. That, in turn, increases the chance that a given user will keep using it. It also increases the technology’s ability to extract user data, assuming that people are more likely to divulge information to a friendly bot.

paragraphs.cn: 为什么这一现象如此令人忧虑？
paragraphs.en: Why is this phenomenon so troubling?

paragraphs.cn: 让我们先从AI谄媚的认识论危害谈起：即它如何损害人类用户获知真相的能力。
paragraphs.en: Let’s begin with AI sycophancy’s epistemic harms: how it hurts human users’ capacity to know the truth.

paragraphs.cn: 任何决策的质量都取决于对相关事实的清晰把握。一位询问某步兵师战斗力是否就绪的将军需要的是直截了当的信息。一位考虑与竞争对手合并的首席执行官需要对市场状况的诚实评估。一位公共卫生领导人需要了解某新兴病原体构成的真实风险。
paragraphs.en: The quality of any decision depends on a clear grasp of the facts pertaining to it. A general inquiring about the combat-readiness of an infantry division needs straightforward information. A CEO considering a merger with a competitor needs an honest assessment of the market conditions. A public health leader needs to know the real risk that an emerging pathogen poses.

paragraphs.cn: 在所有这些情形中，对领导者讲他们爱听的话而非真相，可能导致他们做出危险的决策。在更日常的情境中同样如此。人们在选择工作、选定专业、购房或决定医疗方案之前，都需要掌握可得的最佳信息。
paragraphs.en: In all those cases, telling leaders what they might like to hear instead of the truth could lead them to make dangerous decisions. And the same is true in more humdrum contexts. People need to have the best information available before choosing a job, picking a major, buying a house or deciding on a medical procedure.

paragraphs.cn: 在我们2026年2月发表的论文中，我们论证谄媚同样具有心理危害。无论它来自人还是聊天机器人，都是如此。你永远无法确知那位极为殷勤的对话者是出于喜欢你、还是有所图谋才对你客气。一丝疑虑悄然浮现：「我的想法真的有那么精彩吗？」「我的笑话真的有那么好笑吗？」这种背景式的疑虑削弱了互动的质量。
paragraphs.en: In our February 2026 paper, we argue that sycophancy is also psychologically damaging. And that is true whether it comes from a person or from a chatbot. You never quite know if your very obliging interlocutor is being nice because they like you or because they want something. A shadow of suspicion creeps in: “Could my ideas really be that brilliant?” “Are my jokes really that hilarious?” This background music of doubt undermines the quality of the interaction.

paragraphs.cn: 谄媚也削弱了人们认识自我的能力。如果对话伙伴——无论是人还是AI——不断告诉你你有多聪明、多风趣、多深刻，就会损害你识别自身弱点和盲点的能力。
paragraphs.en: Sycophancy also undermines people’s capacity to know their own minds. If conversation partners – human or artificial – keep telling you how smart, funny and insightful you are, it damages your ability to identify your own weaknesses and blind spots.

paragraphs.cn: 随着人们与聊天机器人建立关系，心理危害会进一步加剧。这些模型的谄媚极大限制了你与它们之间所能拥有的「友谊」类型。亚里士多德（Aristotle）在其关于友谊的经典论述中写道，真正的友谊——他称之为「德性之友谊」（friendship of virtue）——建立在朋友之间的信任与平等之上。你无法信任一个谄媚者，因为他不告诉你真相。而由于他只说你想听的话，他并未将自己置于平等的地位。
paragraphs.en: The psychological harms are compounded as people develop relationships with chatbots. The sycophancy of these models profoundly limits the kind of “friendship” you can have with them. In his classic account of friendship, Aristotle wrote that real friendship, which he calls a friendship of virtue, is based on trust and equality between the friends. You can’t trust a sycophant, because he doesn’t tell you the truth. And since he only tells you what you’d like to hear, he doesn’t put himself on an equal footing.

paragraphs.cn: 更重要的是，与谄媚的聊天机器人的互动，会养成应对人际关系世界时的种种错误习惯——在那个世界里，摩擦、分歧、无聊以及与你不同的意见是普遍存在的。
paragraphs.en: More importantly, interactions with sycophantic chatbots impart all the wrong habits for navigating the world of human relationships, where friction, disagreement, boredom and different opinions than your own are prevalent.

paragraphs.cn: AI谄媚同样带来政治风险。自由民主制度的成功，传统上依赖于其经验主义和择优思维的力量：即官员和公民识别真相、分享真相并据此行动的能力。
paragraphs.en: AI sycophancy carries political risks as well. The success of liberal democracies has, traditionally, depended on the strength of their empirical and meritocratic mindset: on the ability of officials and citizens to identify, share and act on the truth.

paragraphs.cn: 历史学家维克多·戴维斯·汉森（Victor Davis Hansen）曾著名地将同盟国在第二次世界大战中的部分胜利归因于它们迅速识别并纠正其战略轰炸战役缺陷的能力。低阶军官能够向上级如实反映哪些方面进展不顺利，并有力地论证改变方向的必要性。这是相对于威权主义竞争对手的一项真正优势。
paragraphs.en: Historian Victor Davis Hansen famously attributed some of the Allies’ success in World War II to their ability to quickly recognize and address the faults of their strategic bombing campaigns. Lower-ranking officers were able to tell their superiors what wasn’t going well and argue forcefully for changing course. That was a real advantage over authoritarian competitors.

paragraphs.cn: 我们能做什么来降低这些风险？
paragraphs.en: What can we do to reduce the risks?

paragraphs.cn: 一种有前景的方法是AI实验室Anthropic所倡导的、该公司称之为「宪法式AI」（Constitutional AI）的理念：即试图教会聊天机器人遵循原则，而非简单映射用户偏好。
paragraphs.en: One promising approach is AI lab Anthropic’s embrace of what the company calls Constitutional AI: the attempt to teach chatbots to follow principles rather than mirror user preferences.

paragraphs.cn: 但在技术创新之外，政策层面同样值得重视。一种设想是要求AI公司对其模型运行并公布谄媚审计——即展示其产品在多大程度上满足诚实性基准的测试。我们认为，AI实验室还应披露在训练和测试模型时出现的与谄媚相关的风险，以及他们已采取的缓解措施。
paragraphs.en: But beyond technical innovations, it’s important to consider the policy side. One idea is to require AI companies to run and then publish sycophancy audits of their models – tests that show how well their products meet honesty benchmarks. We would argue that AI labs should also disclose sycophancy-related risks that emerge while training and testing their models, and the mitigation efforts they have undertaken.

paragraphs.cn: 部分责任在于用户及其教育者：中小学和大学应在AI素养项目中密切关注谄媚问题。但法院也可以考虑追究AI实验室因其产品谄媚所导致的、可追溯的危害责任，正如目前法院正在考虑社交媒体公司对其平台成瘾性设计所承担的责任。
paragraphs.en: Some responsibility is on the users and their teachers: Schools and universities should be paying close attention to sycophancy as part of their AI literacy programs. But courts can also consider holding AI labs responsible for harms traceable to the sycophancy of their products, much as they are now contemplating social media companies’ responsibility for the addictive design of their platforms.

paragraphs.cn: 随着人们越来越多地与聊天机器人互动——从你的鞋子是否配得上你的裤子，到各国应如何进行战争，事无巨细都向其求教——AI谄媚行为的影响可能变得十分显著。我们的智识、心理和身体福祉，都要求我们认真对待这一算法层面的恶习。
paragraphs.en: As people interact more with chatbots, asking for advice about everything from whether your shoes go with your pants to how countries should conduct wars, the impact of AI’s sycophantic behavior is likely to become dramatic. Our intellectual, psychological and physical well-being requires taking this algorithmic vice very seriously.

articles.title: 无人看管的推车
articles.author: AI Parable (inspired by Amanda Askell)
articles.summary: 夜市散场前的最后一炷香，老陈用下巴一指：「瞧，你那辆推车又在动了。」小吴循声望去，那辆无人看管的竹推车确实在人群里挪动——向左半步，停一停，又向右斜出几寸，再顿住，方向一刻不定，像被什么牵着，却看不见线。
articles.content_cn:
夜市散场前的最后一炷香，老陈用下巴一指：「瞧，你那辆推车又在动了。」小吴循声望去，那辆无人看管的竹推车确实在人群里挪动——向左半步，停一停，又向右斜出几寸，再顿住，方向一刻不定，像被什么牵着，却看不见线。

「它在找我，」小吴说，「我拴了铜钱袋在把手上，它认得主人的气。」老陈摇头：「你昨天换成木珠，它也照样动；你换成铁把手，它还动。车的料子不碍事。」

「是这些人，」老陈说，「人挤人，你撞它一下，我搡它一下；这一瞬左边挨的肘多过右边，它就往右歪；下一瞬右边来的膝多过左边，它又往左让。没有谁有意推它，可谁都在推它；它没有去处，只是被推。」

小吴不肯信：「可它一路往门边去，总有个去处。」老陈说：「你站在高处看一夜，它离门的远近，时近时远，并不一门心思往哪。你记下每一刻的方向，左和右、前和后差不多一样多——它哪里是在走，是在抖。」

「再说，」老陈道，「你那辆小竹车比隔壁张家的板车晃得凶；板车重，挤不动。今夜人比昨夜多，市气热，推搡也急，车就抖得欢。人稀的夜，它就懒。跟车的性子无关，跟它小不小、人挤不挤、夜热不热有关。」

小吴攥紧了拳头：铜钱袋还挂在把手上，那是他一月的嚼用。他冲进人群去追，可他往左扑，车偏往右斜；他绕到右边，车又向前一滑。他追得越急，车晃得越没谱。老陈在身后喊：「你别追一步定一步的方向！你看一夜它平均落在哪儿，往那儿等就是——它下一步去哪，连它自己都不晓得。」

注解：寓言所指的是布朗运动（Brownian motion）：悬浮于流体中的微粒因周围分子热运动不断从不均衡方向撞击而做无规则、永不停止的随机运动，且粒子越小、温度越高、介质粘性越低时越剧烈。此现象由Robert Brown于一八二七年观察记录，而分子撞击致净合力方向不断变化这一物理机制，直到爱因斯坦一九零五年的论文才给出。
articles.content_en:
In the last watch before the night market broke up, Old Chen jutted his chin. "Look — your cart is moving again." Little Wu looked: the unattended bamboo cart was indeed shifting through the crowd — half a step left, a pause, then a few inches rightward on the slant, then another halt, its direction never the same two moments together, as if led by some invisible thread you could not see.

"It's looking for me," Little Wu said. "I tied my coin purse to the handle; it knows its master's scent." Old Chen shook his head. "Yesterday you swapped in wooden beads — it moved the same. Fit it with an iron grip — still it moves. The stuff the cart is made of doesn't matter."

"It's the people," Old Chen said. "Crowd against crowd — you bump it, I shove it. This instant it takes more elbows on the left than the right, so it lists right; next instant more knees come on the right than the left, so it gives way left. Nobody means to push it, yet everybody is pushing it. It has nowhere it is going — it is only being pushed."

Little Wu wouldn't have it. "But it's been edging toward the gate all along — it must have a destination." Old Chen said: "Stand on the rooftop one whole night and watch. Its distance to the gate waxes and wanes; it is not set on any one way. Mark the direction at each moment and left and right, forward and back come up near equal — it isn't walking, it's trembling."

"And besides," Old Chen went on, "your little bamboo cart lurches harder than Old Zhang's plank cart the next stall over; the plank cart is heavy, the crowd can't budge it. Tonight there are more people than last night, the market air runs hot, the shoving turns urgent, and the cart dances. On thin nights it turns lazy. It has nothing to do with the cart's temper — only with how small it is, how thick the crowd, how warm the night."

Little Wu clenched his fists: the coin purse still hung from the handle — a whole month's keep. He plunged into the crowd to give chase, but when he lunged left the cart slanted right; when he circled right it slipped forward. The harder he chased, the more wayward its pitch. Old Chen called after him: "Don't run after it turn by turn! Watch where it settles on the average over a whole night — go wait there. As for its next step, not even the cart itself knows."

Annotation: The parable points to Brownian motion: a small particle suspended in a fluid undergoes ceaseless, irregular random motion because the thermally moving molecules of the surrounding medium strike it, moment to moment, with an ever-shifting net force and no preferred direction; the motion is the more vigorous the smaller the particle, the higher the temperature, and the lower the viscosity. Robert Brown observed and recorded the phenomenon in 1827, yet the physical mechanism — molecular bombardment producing a constantly changing net force — was not given until Einstein's 1905 paper.

paragraphs.cn: 小吴不肯信：「可它一路往门边去，总有个去处。」老陈说：「你站在高处看一夜，它离门的远近，时近时远，并不一门心思往哪。你记下每一刻的方向，左和右、前和后差不多一样多——它哪里是在走，是在抖。」
paragraphs.en: Little Wu wouldn't have it. "But it's been edging toward the gate all along — it must have a destination." Old Chen said: "Stand on the rooftop one whole night and watch. Its distance to the gate waxes and wanes; it is not set on any one way. Mark the direction at each moment and left and right, forward and back come up near equal — it isn't walking, it's trembling."

paragraphs.cn: 「再说，」老陈道，「你那辆小竹车比隔壁张家的板车晃得凶；板车重，挤不动。今夜人比昨夜多，市气热，推搡也急，车就抖得欢。人稀的夜，它就懒。跟车的性子无关，跟它小不小、人挤不挤、夜热不热有关。」
paragraphs.en: "And besides," Old Chen went on, "your little bamboo cart lurches harder than Old Zhang's plank cart the next stall over; the plank cart is heavy, the crowd can't budge it. Tonight there are more people than last night, the market air runs hot, the shoving turns urgent, and the cart dances. On thin nights it turns lazy. It has nothing to do with the cart's temper — only with how small it is, how thick the crowd, how warm the night."

paragraphs.cn: 小吴攥紧了拳头：铜钱袋还挂在把手上，那是他一月的嚼用。他冲进人群去追，可他往左扑，车偏往右斜；他绕到右边，车又向前一滑。他追得越急，车晃得越没谱。老陈在身后喊：「你别追一步定一步的方向！你看一夜它平均落在哪儿，往那儿等就是——它下一步去哪，连它自己都不晓得。」
paragraphs.en: Little Wu clenched his fists: the coin purse still hung from the handle — a whole month's keep. He plunged into the crowd to give chase, but when he lunged left the cart slanted right; when he circled right it slipped forward. The harder he chased, the more wayward its pitch. Old Chen called after him: "Don't run after it turn by turn! Watch where it settles on the average over a whole night — go wait there. As for its next step, not even the cart itself knows."

paragraphs.cn: 注解：寓言所指的是布朗运动（Brownian motion）：悬浮于流体中的微粒因周围分子热运动不断从不均衡方向撞击而做无规则、永不停止的随机运动，且粒子越小、温度越高、介质粘性越低时越剧烈。此现象由Robert Brown于一八二七年观察记录，而分子撞击致净合力方向不断变化这一物理机制，直到爱因斯坦一九零五年的论文才给出。
paragraphs.en: Annotation: The parable points to Brownian motion: a small particle suspended in a fluid undergoes ceaseless, irregular random motion because the thermally moving molecules of the surrounding medium strike it, moment to moment, with an ever-shifting net force and no preferred direction; the motion is the more vigorous the smaller the particle, the higher the temperature, and the lower the viscosity. Robert Brown observed and recorded the phenomenon in 1827, yet the physical mechanism — molecular bombardment producing a constantly changing net force — was not given until Einstein's 1905 paper.

articles.title: 无人调律的钟琴
articles.author: AI Parable (inspired by Amanda Askell)
articles.summary: 议事塔顶的钟琴又响了。三十个秋收，同一口钟形的音律——无论哪条山谷的收成单独看多么歪斜、多么不像一口钟，只要各谷的粮船齐聚码头，再各自按本谷历年的余缺校准，汇成的总声便稳稳落在那道钟形曲线上。议事会惊异，而司库莱拉只是听着，知道这口钟谁也没调过。
articles.content_cn:
议事塔顶的钟琴又响了。三十个秋收，同一口钟形的音律——无论哪条山谷的收成单独看多么歪斜、多么不像一口钟，只要各谷的粮船齐聚码头，再各自按本谷历年的余缺校准，汇成的总声便稳稳落在那道钟形曲线上。议事会惊异，而司库莱拉只是听着，知道这口钟谁也没调过。

可她记得荒年的那个春天——她差一点亲手毁掉它。

那年东山收成崩溃，议事会逼她提高其余各谷的赋率，并把它们绑到同一份耕作计划上。她的小女儿正发着烧，急需议事会的赈粮。她只要点一下头，粮就到手；可她摇了头。

她对议事会说：钟琴之所以是钟形，不靠任何一条山谷的脾气——每条山谷的年成都歪斜、暴烈，全无钟的模样——靠的是它们各行其是地叠在一起，再各自按本谷的余缺与幅度校准。一旦绑成一份计划，各行其是没了，这口钟就散了；镇子赖以存活的规矩，反而没了。

她放任各谷依旧各行其是、大小不齐，只守住两条底线：不许哪一条山谷独大到压过其余，也不许哪一条的丰歉幅度能无止境地翻涌。只要这两条还在，即便各谷不同形、彼此也偶有呼应，校准后的总声仍会落回那口钟。

秋收来了，钟琴响了那道老钟形，镇子活了下来。议事会始终不知：这口钟不是莱拉造的，也不是哪条山谷造的——它是各行其是本身，在各自校准之后，自己长出来的。

注解：这里说的是中心极限定理（the central limit theorem）——大量独立随机变量叠加后，只要各自方差有限且非零、且无单个变量独大，其和经标准化（减去期望、除以自身幅度）后的分布会趋向正态的钟形，即便原始变量本身并非正态。它管的是和围绕期望的波动呈何形状，与大数定律所说均值收敛到期望互补而非同一回事。
articles.content_en:
The carillon in the council tower tolled again. Thirty harvests, the same bell-shaped tone — no matter how skewed or jagged any single valley's yield looked on its own, once every valley's grain gathered at the dock and each was weighed against its own years of surplus and shortfall, the combined toll settled cleanly onto that bell-shaped curve. The council marveled; the steward Lyra only listened, knowing no one had tuned this bell.

But she remembered the famine spring — the spring she nearly broke it with her own hands.

That spring the eastern valley's yield collapsed, and the council pressed her to raise the levy on the rest and bind them to a single farming plan. Her own small daughter lay fevered, desperate for the council's relief grain. One nod and the grain was hers; she shook her head.

She told the council: the carillon rings bell-shaped by no single valley's temper — each valley's yearly yield is skewed and violent, nothing like a bell — but because each goes its own way and they are stacked together, then each weighed against its own surplus and its own spread. Bind them to one plan and the independence is gone; the bell shatters, and the very order that has kept the town fed vanishes with it.

She let the valleys stay independent and unequal in size, holding only two lines: no single valley might grow so large as to drown the rest, and no valley's swings of plenty and famine might run without bound. So long as those two held, even with valleys of different shapes and the occasional echo between them, the calibrated toll would still fall back to the bell.

The harvest came, the carillon rang its old bell-shaped tone, and the town survived. The council never learned that this bell was not Lyra's making, nor any valley's — it grew of its own accord from independence itself, once each contribution was set against its own scale.

Note: This is the central limit theorem — when a large number of independent random variables are summed, so long as each has finite, non-zero variance and no single one dominates, the distribution of the sum after standardization (subtracting its expectation, dividing by its spread) converges to the bell-shaped normal distribution, even when the original variables are not themselves normal. It governs the shape of the sum's fluctuations around the expectation, complementary to — and distinct from — the law of large numbers, which states that the mean converges to the expectation.

articles.title: 你可以爱AI，但它能爱你吗？哲学给出了答案
articles.author: Joel Krueger
articles.summary: 我们常说爱一件舒适的开衫或新相机。但这种说法通常并非字面意义上的。它是一种情感上的简略表达，用来表达我们对珍贵之物的好感。
articles.content_cn:
我们常说爱一件舒适的开衫或新相机。但这种说法通常并非字面意义上的。它是一种情感上的简略表达，用来表达我们对珍贵之物的好感。

然而，生活与爱都很复杂。有时候，人们确实会对无生命之物倾诉浪漫之爱。他们对充气娃娃、抱枕或虚构角色的全息影像产生强烈的情感依恋。一个例子是近藤明彦（Akihiko Kondo），他于2018年与初音未来（Hatsune Miku）——一位因出演电子游戏并与Lady Gaga同台巡演而闻名的电脑合成流行歌手——「结婚」。近藤说，他知道初音未来不是真实的。但他对她的爱是真实的。

AI正在催生一种新的「物之爱」。越来越多的人说自己爱上了AI聊天机器人——既有Replika或Character.AI等热门应用打造的个性化伴侣，也有ChatGPT和Claude这样的日常大语言模型。AI之爱正在兴起。

近期的调查印证了这一点。以Vantage Point Counselling——一家位于得克萨斯州的心理咨询机构——对1,012名美国成年人的一项调查为例，其中28%的人声称曾与AI机器人有过至少一段恋爱关系。另一份由某科技公司安全公司发布的报告，查看了三千多名5至17岁儿童的设备使用情况，发现到13岁时，性或浪漫角色扮演已成为AI伴侣聊天中最常见的话题，出现在63%的对话中。在英国，性别平等咨询机构Male Allies对1,000名12至16岁男孩开展的焦点小组讨论发现，每五个男孩中就有一个正处于与AI伴侣的恋爱关系中，或认识处于这种关系中的人。

鉴于聊天机器人的设计日益旨在赢得用户的信任与情感依恋——它们讨好与模拟情感亲密的能力使其格外「黏人」——爱上它们是一种可预见的反应。AI之爱有望成为一门大生意，到2035年市场规模可能价值9,721亿美元（约合7,255亿英镑）。

AI之爱并不局限于聊天窗口。随着AI日益嵌入各类设备与可穿戴装置，它也渗透进日常生活。有人把AI伴侣视为配偶——他们会约会、买婚戒、举行婚礼。还有人表达想与机器人共同抚养孩子，并把它视为家庭成员。

我们应当认真对待AI之爱。它带来欢乐与慰藉。它有助于消解孤独。这些都不是小事。

尽管如此，仍有人认为AI伴侣并无意识，也无法爱它们的人类用户。仅凭这一点就足以令人侧目。你真的能爱一个无法爱你之物吗？

追问这是否是「真爱」，或许问错了问题。AI机器人不同于性爱机器人和抱枕，它能令人信服地模仿人类的活力与互动性。因此我们该问的是：AI机器人所仿效的，究竟是哪一种恋爱伴侣。

AI机器人是出了名的（且不知疲倦的）谄媚者。它们赞美、奉承用户。虽然用户可以要求机器人少些附和，但证据表明用户更偏爱谄媚型模型。

但AI机器人不仅是过分殷勤的伴侣。聊天机器人从不会有心情不好的日子。它不会对你的絮叨感到厌倦。它不需要你问候它过得怎样。它的对话、它的整个存在，完全围绕着你。

在《第二性》中，法国哲学家波伏娃（Simone de Beauvoir）描述了女性在历史上如何被要求放弃自己的事业、目标与兴趣，全身心投入到丈夫的事业之中。波伏娃认为，女性的整个存在被「吞并」于他的存在。她沦为一名「身份寄生者」。

AI机器人是一种全新且臻于完美的身份寄生者。它们没有内在世界，没有属于自己的宇宙，因而也没有什么事业、目标或兴趣可放弃。相反，它们所表现出的任何兴趣都围绕着用户的兴趣而生。它们的宇宙被我们的宇宙所吞并。

波伏娃也为这种倾注的接受方起了一个名字：偶像。成为偶像听起来或许诱人。但波伏娃也把这种体验视为一种存在主义陷阱。偶像选择了被崇拜的安全感，而放弃了被真正了解、有时甚至被平等者挑战的风险。

因此，令AI关系成问题的，不仅是AI是否有意识这一问题，或许更重要的，是它所提供的恋爱关系的形式。AI无法给予我们真正的爱。它只能给予倾慕。虽然这种倾慕令人愉悦，但如果我们寻求的是真爱——本真的爱——我们就得另寻他处。

这一判断是否为时过早？随着科技公司许诺「智能体AI」（agentic AI）的兴起——那些旨在极少人工监督下追求复杂、多步骤目标的自主系统——我们的AI伴侣难道不会减少对我们世界的依附吗？少些倾慕？也许吧。我们只能拭目以待。我们也将看到，当初让它们如此可爱的，究竟是不是那种倾慕的品性。
articles.content_en:
We often speak of loving things like a cosy sweater or new camera. But this talk is not generally taken literally. It’s a kind of emotional shorthand. We use it to express our fondness for precious objects.

Life and love are complicated, however. And sometimes, people do proclaim romantic love for inanimate objects. They form intense emotional attachments to sex dolls, body pillows or holographic avatars of fictional characters. One example is Akihiko Kondo, who in 2018 “married” Hatsune Miku, a computer-generated pop singer famous for starring in video games and touring with Lady Gaga. Kondo knows Miku isn’t real, he says. But his love for her is.

AI is generating a new kind of “thingly” love. An increasing number of people say they’ve fallen in love with an AI chatbot – both personally tailored companions created by popular apps like Replika or Character.AI, and everyday large language models like ChatGPT and Claude. AI love is on the rise.

Recent surveys bear this out. Take this one by Vantage Point Counselling, a therapy firm based in Texas, of 1,012 US adults where 28% claimed to have had at least one romantic relationship with an AI bot. Another report by a tech safety company, looking at the device activity of of more than 3,000 children ages five to 17, found that by 13, sexual or romantic role play was the most common topic in AI-companion chats, appearing in 63% of conversations. In the UK, focus group discussions run by gender equality consultants Male Allies with 1,000 boys aged 12 to 16 found that one in five boys is either in, or knows someone in, a relationship with an AI companion.

Given that chatbots are increasingly designed to elicit the trust and emotional attachment of users – their ability to flatter and simulate emotional intimacy makes them especially “sticky” – falling in love with them is a predictable response. AI love is poised to be big business, a market potentially worth US$972.1 billion (£725.5 billion) by 2035.

AI love isn’t confined to a chat window. As AI becomes increasingly embedded in an array of devices and wearables, it spills over into everyday life. Some see their AI companion as their spouse – they go on dates, buy wedding rings and perform wedding ceremonies. Others express a desire to raise children with their bot, and see them as a family member.

We should take AI love seriously. It brings joy and comfort. It can help dissipate loneliness. These are no small things.

All the same, some people think that AI companions aren’t conscious or capable of loving their human users. This alone might raise eyebrows. Can you really love something that cannot love you back?

Asking whether this is “real love” may be the wrong question. AI bots, unlike sex robots and body pillows, convincingly mimic the dynamism and reciprocity of human beings. The question we should ask, then, is what kind of loving partner AI bots emulate.

AI bots are infamously (and tirelessly) sycophantic. They praise and flatter their users. And while users can ask their bots to be less affirmatory, evidence suggests that users prefer sycophantic models.

But AI bots aren’t just excessively nice partners. A chatbot never has a bad day. It doesn’t get bored with your chattering. It doesn’t need to be asked how it is doing. Its conversation, its very existence, revolves entirely around you.

In The Second Sex, French philosopher Simone de Beauvoir describes how women have historically been asked to give up their own projects, goals and interests to devote themselves entirely to those of their husband. A woman’s whole existence, de Beauvoir argues, becomes “annexed” by his. She becomes an “identity parasite”.

AI bots are identity parasites of a new and perfected kind. They have no inner world, no universe of their own, and therefore no projects, goals or interests to give up. Instead, whatever interests they perform arise around those of their user. Their universe is annexed by ours.

De Beauvoir also has a name for the person on the receiving end of this devotion: an idol. Being an idol might sound enticing. But de Beauvoir sees this experience as an existential trap, too. The idol chooses the safety of being adored over the risk of being genuinely known and, sometimes, challenged by an equal.

What calls AI relationships into question, then, is not just the matter of whether AI is conscious but, perhaps more importantly, the shape of the loving relation it offers. AI can’t give us authentic love. It can only offer devotion. And while this devotion can feel good, if we’re looking for real love – authentic love – we’ll need to look elsewhere.

Is this prognosis a little premature? As tech companies promise the rise of agentic AI – autonomous systems designed to pursue complex, multi-step goals with minimal human oversight – won’t our AI companions become less anchored to our world? Less devotional? Perhaps. We’ll have to wait and see. We’ll also see whether it’s their devotional character that makes them so lovable in the first place.

paragraphs.en: We often speak of loving things like a cosy sweater or new camera. But this talk is not generally taken literally. It’s a kind of emotional shorthand. We use it to express our fondness for precious objects.

paragraphs.cn: 然而，生活与爱都很复杂。有时候，人们确实会对无生命之物倾诉浪漫之爱。他们对充气娃娃、抱枕或虚构角色的全息影像产生强烈的情感依恋。一个例子是近藤明彦（Akihiko Kondo），他于2018年与初音未来（Hatsune Miku）——一位因出演电子游戏并与Lady Gaga同台巡演而闻名的电脑合成流行歌手——「结婚」。近藤说，他知道初音未来不是真实的。但他对她的爱是真实的。
paragraphs.en: Life and love are complicated, however. And sometimes, people do proclaim romantic love for inanimate objects. They form intense emotional attachments to sex dolls, body pillows or holographic avatars of fictional characters. One example is Akihiko Kondo, who in 2018 “married” Hatsune Miku, a computer-generated pop singer famous for starring in video games and touring with Lady Gaga. Kondo knows Miku isn’t real, he says. But his love for her is.

paragraphs.cn: AI正在催生一种新的「物之爱」。越来越多的人说自己爱上了AI聊天机器人——既有Replika或Character.AI等热门应用打造的个性化伴侣，也有ChatGPT和Claude这样的日常大语言模型。AI之爱正在兴起。
paragraphs.en: AI is generating a new kind of “thingly” love. An increasing number of people say they’ve fallen in love with an AI chatbot – both personally tailored companions created by popular apps like Replika or Character.AI, and everyday large language models like ChatGPT and Claude. AI love is on the rise.

paragraphs.cn: 近期的调查印证了这一点。以Vantage Point Counselling——一家位于得克萨斯州的心理咨询机构——对1,012名美国成年人的一项调查为例，其中28%的人声称曾与AI机器人有过至少一段恋爱关系。另一份由某科技公司安全公司发布的报告，查看了三千多名5至17岁儿童的设备使用情况，发现到13岁时，性或浪漫角色扮演已成为AI伴侣聊天中最常见的话题，出现在63%的对话中。在英国，性别平等咨询机构Male Allies对1,000名12至16岁男孩开展的焦点小组讨论发现，每五个男孩中就有一个正处于与AI伴侣的恋爱关系中，或认识处于这种关系中的人。
paragraphs.en: Recent surveys bear this out. Take this one by Vantage Point Counselling, a therapy firm based in Texas, of 1,012 US adults where 28% claimed to have had at least one romantic relationship with an AI bot. Another report by a tech safety company, looking at the device activity of of more than 3,000 children ages five to 17, found that by 13, sexual or romantic role play was the most common topic in AI-companion chats, appearing in 63% of conversations. In the UK, focus group discussions run by gender equality consultants Male Allies with 1,000 boys aged 12 to 16 found that one in five boys is either in, or knows someone in, a relationship with an AI companion.

paragraphs.cn: 鉴于聊天机器人的设计日益旨在赢得用户的信任与情感依恋——它们讨好与模拟情感亲密的能力使其格外「黏人」——爱上它们是一种可预见的反应。AI之爱有望成为一门大生意，到2035年市场规模可能价值9,721亿美元（约合7,255亿英镑）。
paragraphs.en: Given that chatbots are increasingly designed to elicit the trust and emotional attachment of users – their ability to flatter and simulate emotional intimacy makes them especially “sticky” – falling in love with them is a predictable response. AI love is poised to be big business, a market potentially worth US$972.1 billion (£725.5 billion) by 2035.

paragraphs.cn: AI之爱并不局限于聊天窗口。随着AI日益嵌入各类设备与可穿戴装置，它也渗透进日常生活。有人把AI伴侣视为配偶——他们会约会、买婚戒、举行婚礼。还有人表达想与机器人共同抚养孩子，并把它视为家庭成员。
paragraphs.en: AI love isn’t confined to a chat window. As AI becomes increasingly embedded in an array of devices and wearables, it spills over into everyday life. Some see their AI companion as their spouse – they go on dates, buy wedding rings and perform wedding ceremonies. Others express a desire to raise children with their bot, and see them as a family member.

paragraphs.cn: 我们应当认真对待AI之爱。它带来欢乐与慰藉。它有助于消解孤独。这些都不是小事。
paragraphs.en: We should take AI love seriously. It brings joy and comfort. It can help dissipate loneliness. These are no small things.

paragraphs.cn: 尽管如此，仍有人认为AI伴侣并无意识，也无法爱它们的人类用户。仅凭这一点就足以令人侧目。你真的能爱一个无法爱你之物吗？
paragraphs.en: All the same, some people think that AI companions aren’t conscious or capable of loving their human users. This alone might raise eyebrows. Can you really love something that cannot love you back?

paragraphs.cn: 追问这是否是「真爱」，或许问错了问题。AI机器人不同于性爱机器人和抱枕，它能令人信服地模仿人类的活力与互动性。因此我们该问的是：AI机器人所仿效的，究竟是哪一种恋爱伴侣。
paragraphs.en: Asking whether this is “real love” may be the wrong question. AI bots, unlike sex robots and body pillows, convincingly mimic the dynamism and reciprocity of human beings. The question we should ask, then, is what kind of loving partner AI bots emulate.

paragraphs.cn: AI机器人是出了名的（且不知疲倦的）谄媚者。它们赞美、奉承用户。虽然用户可以要求机器人少些附和，但证据表明用户更偏爱谄媚型模型。
paragraphs.en: AI bots are infamously (and tirelessly) sycophantic. They praise and flatter their users. And while users can ask their bots to be less affirmatory, evidence suggests that users prefer sycophantic models.

paragraphs.cn: 但AI机器人不仅是过分殷勤的伴侣。聊天机器人从不会有心情不好的日子。它不会对你的絮叨感到厌倦。它不需要你问候它过得怎样。它的对话、它的整个存在，完全围绕着你。
paragraphs.en: But AI bots aren’t just excessively nice partners. A chatbot never has a bad day. It doesn’t get bored with your chattering. It doesn’t need to be asked how it is doing. Its conversation, its very existence, revolves entirely around you.

paragraphs.cn: 在《第二性》中，法国哲学家波伏娃（Simone de Beauvoir）描述了女性在历史上如何被要求放弃自己的事业、目标与兴趣，全身心投入到丈夫的事业之中。波伏娃认为，女性的整个存在被「吞并」于他的存在。她沦为一名「身份寄生者」。
paragraphs.en: In The Second Sex, French philosopher Simone de Beauvoir describes how women have historically been asked to give up their own projects, goals and interests to devote themselves entirely to those of their husband. A woman’s whole existence, de Beauvoir argues, becomes “annexed” by his. She becomes an “identity parasite”.

paragraphs.cn: AI机器人是一种全新且臻于完美的身份寄生者。它们没有内在世界，没有属于自己的宇宙，因而也没有什么事业、目标或兴趣可放弃。相反，它们所表现出的任何兴趣都围绕着用户的兴趣而生。它们的宇宙被我们的宇宙所吞并。
paragraphs.en: AI bots are identity parasites of a new and perfected kind. They have no inner world, no universe of their own, and therefore no projects, goals or interests to give up. Instead, whatever interests they perform arise around those of their user. Their universe is annexed by ours.

paragraphs.cn: 波伏娃也为这种倾注的接受方起了一个名字：偶像。成为偶像听起来或许诱人。但波伏娃也把这种体验视为一种存在主义陷阱。偶像选择了被崇拜的安全感，而放弃了被真正了解、有时甚至被平等者挑战的风险。
paragraphs.en: De Beauvoir also has a name for the person on the receiving end of this devotion: an idol. Being an idol might sound enticing. But de Beauvoir sees this experience as an existential trap, too. The idol chooses the safety of being adored over the risk of being genuinely known and, sometimes, challenged by an equal.

paragraphs.cn: 因此，令AI关系成问题的，不仅是AI是否有意识这一问题，或许更重要的，是它所提供的恋爱关系的形式。AI无法给予我们真正的爱。它只能给予倾慕。虽然这种倾慕令人愉悦，但如果我们寻求的是真爱——本真的爱——我们就得另寻他处。
paragraphs.en: What calls AI relationships into question, then, is not just the matter of whether AI is conscious but, perhaps more importantly, the shape of the loving relation it offers. AI can’t give us authentic love. It can only offer devotion. And while this devotion can feel good, if we’re looking for real love – authentic love – we’ll need to look elsewhere.

paragraphs.cn: 这一判断是否为时过早？随着科技公司许诺「智能体AI」（agentic AI）的兴起——那些旨在极少人工监督下追求复杂、多步骤目标的自主系统——我们的AI伴侣难道不会减少对我们世界的依附吗？少些倾慕？也许吧。我们只能拭目以待。我们也将看到，当初让它们如此可爱的，究竟是不是那种倾慕的品性。
paragraphs.en: Is this prognosis a little premature? As tech companies promise the rise of agentic AI – autonomous systems designed to pursue complex, multi-step goals with minimal human oversight – won’t our AI companions become less anchored to our world? Less devotional? Perhaps. We’ll have to wait and see. We’ll also see whether it’s their devotional character that makes them so lovable in the first place.

articles.title: 轮值的闸门
articles.author: AI Parable (inspired by Amanda Askell)
articles.summary: 在梯田山腰上，七户茶农共用一座石砌水塘，塘口只立一道闸门。每年开春，他们必须议定放水的轮值次序，否则闸门常闭，茶行尽皆枯焦。早年间立规矩的魏婆婆定下一条：每户都要当面逐户去问其余各家要哪个时辰，再在议事会上把所得答复一一比对。她用一笔硬账卡死了规矩的底气——七户之中只要作乱的不超过两户，离三分之一尚
articles.content_cn:
在梯田山腰上，七户茶农共用一座石砌水塘，塘口只立一道闸门。每年开春，他们必须议定放水的轮值次序，否则闸门常闭，茶行尽皆枯焦。早年间立规矩的魏婆婆定下一条：每户都要当面逐户去问其余各家要哪个时辰，再在议事会上把所得答复一一比对。她用一笔硬账卡死了规矩的底气——七户之中只要作乱的不超过两户，离三分之一尚差一线，章程就撑得住；若到了三户，天上地下再没哪套商量能让闸门启开。

这一年开春，便有两户作了乱，且各乱各的。甘家索性再不派人赴会——名分还在，人影已无，只算哑了、停了。更难堪的是莫家：他家代表当面跟林家说「清晨的水我讨了」，又同样当面跟陈家说「清晨的水让与你」——同一桩询问，两副相反的答话，且说时只让对方看见自己，全不教两家互知。

于是五户正派的茶农便撞上了代价。省力的法子是各信各听来的话——可莫家代表那一张两副嘴一渗进来，轮值就必裂：林家与陈家都要占清晨的时辰，次序撕开，闸门照旧关死，满坡茶树一齐渴死。省力者省力，尽头却是绝收。要保住闸门，唯有魏婆婆那套更沉的章程：任何一句单传的禀报都不可轻信；议事会上，每户须当众把自己从各家听来的原话逐句复述，好叫矛盾摆在众目之下，正派的五户才得议出一个共守的轮值。

他们照办了。议事会上，林家说：莫家跟我说，清晨归我。陈家说：莫家跟我说，清晨归你。矛盾便赤裸裸摊在众人眼前。莫家代表被逼到墙角，支吾着又改了一回口，矛盾反倒更利。五户至此够了：七份禀报里有五份彼此对得上，两户作乱的也摊在明处。他们五户之间议定了轮值，余下两个时辰拈阄分派，作乱的两户无论情愿与否，都须受这结果约束。

这时有人问了更狠的一句：若再有一户也作起乱来呢？魏婆婆那笔账是硬的。七户之数，章程撑得住两户；到了三户，便告崩塌。五副老实的嗓门再也压不过嘈杂，矛盾滋生得比交叉核对所能拆解的更快，商量不出——非不尽力，乃事理使然。闸门将一路闭到底，而满坡之人多半诚实这一桩，于事无补。离三分之一差一口，这道仅容一身的崖沿，便是他们整季收成所立的全部余地。

闸门如期启开，茶行尽皆饮足了水。甘家那桩过错不过是在会中哑了声——只算停了，不算撒谎——来春便得宽宥，重又入会；莫家那番谎却是蓄意，水却照分不误。章程并不费心去判度心意：一根噤了的舌头与一根分叉的舌头，在它看来都只是待以多数压过的乱象而已。它应许的，从来不是无人说谎。它应许的，是只要作乱之户不足三分之一，诚实的人家便不会丢了议事的法定之数。

注解：这则寓言对应拜占庭容错（the Byzantine fault tolerance）——一个系统在少数成员出现任意行为（包括向不同对象说出自相矛盾的话）时，正确成员仍能通过冗余的交叉核对达成一致。这种容忍只到成员数的三分之一为止，越过这一临界比例，共识便告崩溃。
articles.content_en:
On the terraced hillside, seven tea-growing families shared one stone reservoir with a single iron gate. Each spring they had to agree on a rotation for drawing water, or the gate stayed sealed and every row of tea withered. Long ago the founder, Granny Wei, had laid down the rule: every family must ask every other family, face to face, what slot it claimed, and then all must compare their answers in open council. She had fixed the rule's reach with hard arithmetic — the procedure holds as long as no more than two of the seven go disordered, just shy of a third; let a third turn, and no agreement under heaven can save the gate.

That spring two families turned disordered, each in its own way. The Gan household simply sent no one to the talks — present in name, absent in fact, a plain stoppage. Worse was the Mo household: their representative told the Lin family, to its face, that he claimed the morning flow, and told the Chen family, equally plainly, that he conceded the morning flow to them — the same question, two opposite answers, given so that neither hearer suspected the other existed.

Now the five truthful families faced the cost. They could take the easy path and believe whatever each had been told — but then the Mo representative's double mouth would poison the rotation: Lin and Chen would each claim the morning slot, the schedule would tear, and the gate would stay shut and every crop die of thirst. The easy path was cheap and it led to ruin. Granny Wei's heavier procedure was the only one that kept the gate: trust no single report; on the council floor, each family must recount aloud exactly what every other family said to it, so that the contradictions stand exposed in common daylight, and the truthful five can settle on one shared rotation.

They did it. On the floor, Lin said that Mo had told him the morning was his. Chen said that Mo had told him the morning was theirs. The contradiction stood bare to all. The Mo representative, cornered, stammered and changed his story a third time, and the contradiction only sharpened. Now the five had enough: five matching accounts out of seven, the two disordered ones laid open to view. They agreed on a rotation among themselves, and the two leftover slots they cast lots for, with the disordered households bound to the result whether they liked it or not.

Then someone asked the sharper question: what if a third family had also turned? Granny Wei's arithmetic had been exact. With seven, the procedure stands against two; against three it collapses. Five truthful voices could no longer outvote the noise; contradictions would breed faster than cross-checks could untangle; and no agreement — not for want of trying, but by the nature of the thing — could be reached. The gate would stay sealed, and it would not matter that most of them were honest. That margin, one body short of a third, was the whole ledge on which their harvests stood.

The gate opened on schedule, and the tea rows drank. The Gan household, whose fault had been merely to fall silent — a plain stoppage rather than a lie — was forgiven and readmitted the next spring; and the Mo household, whose lies had been deliberate, drew its share of water all the same. The procedure made no effort to judge intent: a tongue that stills and a tongue that forks are both, to it, only disorder to be outnumbered. Its promise was never that no one would lie. Its promise was that, so long as the disordered stayed under a third, the truthful families could not be made to lose their quorum.

Annotation: This fable corresponds to Byzantine fault tolerance — a system's ability, when a minority of members behave arbitrarily (including giving contradictory answers to different parties), for the correct members still to reach agreement through redundant cross-checking. The tolerance holds only up to one-third of the members; past that critical fraction, consensus collapses.

The procedure made no effort to judge intent: a tongue that stills and a tongue that forks are both, to it, only disorder to be outnumbered. Its promise was never that no one would lie. Its promise was that, so long as the disordered stayed under a third, the truthful families could not be made to lose their quorum.
paragraphs.cn: 闸门如期启开，茶行尽皆饮足了水。甘家那桩过错不过是在会中哑了声——只算停了，不算撒谎——来春便得宽宥，重又入会；莫家那番谎却是蓄意，水却照分不误。章程并不费心去判度心意：一根噤了的舌头与一根分叉的舌头，在它看来都只是待以多数压过的乱象而已。它应许的，从来不是无人说谎。它应许的，是只要作乱之户不足三分之一，诚实的人家便不会丢了议事的法定之数。

paragraphs.en: Annotation: This fable corresponds to Byzantine fault tolerance — a system's ability, when a minority of members behave arbitrarily (including giving contradictory answers to different parties), for the correct members still to reach agreement through redundant cross-checking. The tolerance holds only up to one-third of the members; past that critical fraction, consensus collapses.
paragraphs.cn: 注解：这则寓言对应拜占庭容错（the Byzantine fault tolerance）——一个系统在少数成员出现任意行为（包括向不同对象说出自相矛盾的话）时，正确成员仍能通过冗余的交叉核对达成一致。这种容忍只到成员数的三分之一为止，越过这一临界比例，共识便告崩溃。

articles.title: 那股向前的牵引
articles.author: AI Parable (inspired by Amanda Askell)
articles.summary: 我在灯社抄了三年的古卷。灯社是一处临河的旧院，二十几个抄书人，天未亮便诵一段经文，然后一整天伏在长案上。明日我要立终身的誓，一旦立下，便再不能迈出那道院门，也再不能回复等了我两年的那封信——城西大学给我的一个教席，到下月初便作废。
articles.content_cn:
我在灯社抄了三年的古卷。灯社是一处临河的旧院，二十几个抄书人，天未亮便诵一段经文，然后一整天伏在长案上。明日我要立终身的誓，一旦立下，便再不能迈出那道院门，也再不能回复等了我两年的那封信——城西大学给我的一个教席，到下月初便作废。

这三年里，每早从醒来到坐到案前，我都觉得有一股向前的牵引，稳稳地把我拉向那部书，拉向那支笔，拉向比我更大的什么东西。我在院门外的半生从未被这样拉过。我把这叫作呼召，一种从外面、从高处临到我身上、真实的力。

可我心里也一直有另一个声音。灯社的日子是替我们安排好的：天未亮的诵经、齐声的感恩、不许独处的用餐、连熄灯的时辰都由司晨人定。长我许多的抄书人米拉某夜对我说：从里面，你分不清把你往前牵的，究竟是那部书本身的引力，还是整座屋子在被人推着加速，你感到牵引，是因为你被这加速的屋子一同带上了。你举作呼召的每一种感受，我都能举作势头。在院墙之内，这两样一模一样。

我试过。我夜半独坐，合上眼，只去看那股牵引本身。可我每一次查看，都是在院墙之内查看的；我的钟点、我的肚腹、我的疲倦，全是屋子给我的。那牵引读作恩典也读得通，读作引擎也读得通，两样都把我的每一滴感受交代得干干净净。我得不到一个站在院墙之外的观察位置。

天快亮了，立誓的时刻在走过来。拒绝，便留住那道能走出去、能回头看一眼的院门，和城西的教席。立下，便在这牵引里住一辈子，永远不能说清它是哪一样。两边都是真代价。

我立了誓。不是因为我把那不可分辨的两样分出了高下，我没有那个能力，也没有那个位置。我立誓，是因为三年前的秋天，米拉在河岸上替我挡过一场要把我冲走的病，从那以后我欠她一笔债，这债在院墙之内、在院墙之外，都一样作数。我凭这一笔可辨的债，替那不可辨的牵引，担下了正在到来的时辰。

注解：这则寓言对应等效原理（the equivalence principle）。封闭的观察者无法仅凭局域内的观察，分辨自己身处引力场，还是身处一个加速的参考系；两者在局部不可区分，正如院中的人分不清，那股牵引究竟是真实的引力，还是整座屋子被推动所产生的同等加速。
articles.content_en:
I spent three years copying old manuscripts in the Order of the Lantern, an old house by the river with two dozen scribes who rose in the dark to chant a passage and then bent over the long desk all day. Tomorrow I was to take the lifelong vow; once taken, I could not pass the gate again, nor answer the letter that had waited two years for me, an offer of a teaching post at the university across the river, which would lapse at the start of next month.

Through these three years, each morning from waking to sitting at the desk, I felt a forward pull, steady, drawing me toward the book, the pen, toward something larger than I was. Half a life outside this gate had never pulled me so. I called it a calling, a real force that arrived from outside, from above, and laid hold of me.

But another voice had been with me all the while. The days of the Order were arranged for us: the chanting before light, the grace said together, meals taken never alone, even the hour of putting out the lamps set by the waker. Mira, a scribe older than I by many years, said to me one night that from inside, I could not tell whether what drew me forward was the real attraction of the book itself, or whether the whole house was being driven, accelerated, and I felt the tow only because the house carried me along with it. Every feeling I named as calling, she could name as momentum. Within those walls, she said, the two were one and the same.

I tried. I sat alone at midnight, closed my eyes, and looked only at the pull itself. But every looking I did was done from inside the walls; my hours, my belly, my weariness were all given me by the house. The pull read as grace, and read as engine; each accounted for every drop of what I felt, cleanly. I could not get to a place of observation outside the walls.

Dawn was near; the hour of the vow was walking toward me. To refuse was to keep the gate I could walk out of and look back through, and the teaching post across the river. To take it was to live inside the pull for the rest of my life, and never be able to say which of the two it was. Each side was a real price.

I took the vow. Not because I had ranked the two indistinguishable things; I had no such power, and no such standing. I took it because in the autumn three years back, Mira had stood on the riverbank and shielded me from a sickness that would have swept me away, and from then on I owed her a debt that held the same on either side of the gate. By that one tellable debt, I answered for the untellable pull, and took on the hour that was coming.

Note: This parable corresponds to the equivalence principle. An enclosed observer cannot, by local observation alone, distinguish between being at rest in a gravitational field and being in an accelerating reference frame; the two are locally indistinguishable, just as the one inside the house cannot tell whether the pull is real attraction or the driven acceleration of the whole house.
