articles.title: 「于静寂中流连」：哲学家韩炳哲论园艺的激进力量
articles.author: Thomas Moran
articles.summary: 罗马斯多葛派哲学家西塞罗（Cicero）曾致信即将来访的朋友瓦罗（Varro）：「若你的书房中有一座花园，我们便已拥有所需的一切。」这种对好书与自然之美的同一种渴慕，正是韩炳哲（Byung-Chul Han）新近被译成英文的著作《赞美大地：花园之旅》（In Praise of the Earth:
articles.content_cn:
罗马斯多葛派哲学家西塞罗（Cicero）曾致信即将来访的朋友瓦罗（Varro）：「若你的书房中有一座花园，我们便已拥有所需的一切。」这种对好书与自然之美的同一种渴慕，正是韩炳哲（Byung-Chul Han）新近被译成英文的著作《赞美大地：花园之旅》（In Praise of the Earth: A Journey into the Garden）的核心所在。

书评：《赞美大地：花园之旅》——韩炳哲（Polity 出版）

韩炳哲生于韩国，现居德国，作为一位可称为「倦怠时代」的哲学家而声名鹊起。他著述颇丰，已有数十部作品，其中许多以临床般的精确诊断当代生活的病理。

韩炳哲审视倦怠、注意力丧失、信息过载等当代关切。他指出，这些现象及其所致的疲惫，不只是个人问题，更是一种特定存在方式的产物。

除这些欧洲经典思想家外，他在著作中还兼采东西方哲学、文学与神学的思想。

他是少有的既能把复杂思想讲得引人入胜、又不失其深刻的思想家。

例如在《倦怠社会》中，韩炳哲批判了他所谓「绩效主体」的效应——这是一种将成就、表现、优化的命令内化于自身的现代人。他论证道，这一主体既是暴君又是奴隶，主人与奴隶合为一体。

《赞美大地》提示，园艺这一谦卑的实践能提供一条逃离绩效之暴政的出路。韩炳哲把园艺呈现为当代生活无休止索求的一剂解毒，一种使我们重新转向与时间、与世界不同关系的实践。

韩炳哲把园艺描述为一种「静默的冥想，于静寂中流连」。这种实践在通常意义上并不生产任何东西，却培育了某种远为珍贵之物：对世界的重新注意。

这种新的时间感不仅与四季更替相调，也与植物自身的生长相调。园丁必须学会等待、观察，留心那不可催促、不可优化的生命缓慢舒展。

对不同时间节奏彼此交叠的察觉，促使韩炳哲反思他所称的先于并超出人类时间的地球「深时间」。花园在此意义上成为一个不同时间性汇聚交错之地。

对韩炳哲而言，花园的时间与数字技术的时间根本不同。数字时间的特征是速度、碎片化以及对注意力的持续索求，而花园的时间则缓慢、连续、沉思。

与之相反，「花园是一个供人流连的出神之所。」

作为园丁，韩炳哲为植物的名字着迷。书中许多短文以某种植物之名开篇——落新妇（astilbe）、星芹（astrantia）、银莲花（anemone）——由这一命名，韩炳哲展开对语言、对注意、对人——自然关系的冥想。

反思这些名字时，韩炳哲开始形成新的想法。他注意到，落新妇那羽毛般的花穗似乎透着某种温柔，而星芹那星形花序则暗示着一种更具结构性的、近乎建筑般的美。对韩炳哲而言，每一株植物都成为一堂关于如何留意世界的小课。

当他的注意从语言转向更广义的自然，他的世界也随之拓展。他开始把花园看作不是物的集合，而是一个活生生的、关系性的系统，其中每一要素都与其他一切要素相关联地存在。

他写道，在做园丁之前，「我在某种意义上不仅对有意志的存在者漠不关心，对事物也是如此，我把它们贬低为纯粹的客体。」与之相对，园艺恢复了对事物的一种专注，一种对其自身存在方式的承认。

这一反思由伊莎贝拉·格雷瑟（Isabella Gresser）穿插于字里间间的植物绘图所补充。这些精致的插图不只是装饰，而是注意每一植物特殊性的另一种方式，是韩炳哲哲学冥想的视觉对应物。

从特殊到普遍的推移是本书一大长处。韩炳哲能从对一朵花的细察，推移到对时间、注意与存在本身的反思，而不曾丢失论证的线索。

韩炳哲相信，通过留意最微小的花苞，我们能开始培养一种对大地的敬畏，而这种敬畏在当代生活中基本是缺席的。这不是通常意义上的宗教虔诚，而是一种对事物纯粹存在的惊奇。

这种敬畏又由最古老的哲学感受——惊奇——所补充。韩炳哲援引希腊传统的 thaumazein——那种被柏拉图（Plato）和亚里士多德（Aristotle）视为哲学本身的起点的惊奇。

「我们应当重新学会对大地惊奇……在花园里，我体验到的那种惊奇，依照柏拉图和亚里士多德的说法，是一切哲学的起源。」

韩炳哲的本书属于关于园艺艺术的悠长哲学反思传统的一部分。从伊壁鸠鲁到伏尔泰（Voltaire），哲学家们在花园中发现了好生活的范本，一个退隐与沉思之地。

古希腊哲学家伊壁鸠鲁的追随者组成一个名为「花园」的共同体，他们在远离城市政治生活之处践行哲学。对伊壁鸠鲁而言，花园是友谊、单纯快乐与哲学反思之地。

它同样属于近来的一波著作浪潮，当代思想家在其中反思生态危机以及人类在其中的位置。在此背景下，韩炳哲的本书可被读作对日益增长的人类世哲学文献、以及我们与超越人类的世界之关系的一项贡献。

《赞美大地》是一曲哲学之歌，在最柔弱的花朵中发出关怀的响亮呼唤。「绽放即狂喜，」韩炳哲写道，而阅读本书，同样是一种令人狂喜的体验。
articles.content_en:
Cicero, the Roman Stoic, once wrote to his friend Varro, pending a visit to his home: “If you have a garden in your library, we shall have all we want.” This same desire for good books and natural beauty is at the heart of Byung-Chul Han’s In Praise of the Earth, in which he reflects on gardening as a form of philosophical meditation.

Review: In Praise of the Earth: A Journey into the Garden – Byung-Chul Han (Polity)

Born in South Korea and based in Germany, Han has risen to prominence as a philosopher in the last ten years with a series of short, readable but penetrating works critiquing the values that govern contemporary capitalist society.

Han considers contemporary concerns like burnout, the loss of attention and information overload, drawing on thinkers such as Hegel, Marx and Nietzsche to diagnose the effects of digital capitalism.

As well as these canonical European thinkers, he considers the ideas of Eastern philosophers and poets like Lao Tzu and Bashō. Indeed he has written books on Zen Buddhism and the Chinese idea of shanzhai or “decreation”, which disrupts the usual hierarchy between real and fake.

Han is a rare thinker who can make complex ideas engaging without losing any of their intellectual acuity. He writes slim volumes, easily carried in a coat pocket, which brim with explosive diagnoses of contemporary ills while proposing new ways of living.

In The Burnout Society, for instance, Han critiques the effects of what he calls “the achievement society”, in which efficiency and a relentless drive toward self-optimisation result in feelings of despair, loneliness and exhaustion. Against the tide of self-help manuals focusing on positivity and success, he suggests “rest and contemplation are acts of resistance against a world that demands constant productivity. In pausing we reclaim our humanity.”

In Praise of the Earth suggests the humble practice of gardening can offer one example of this kind of resistance. While he reflects on the deeper implications of gardening and thinking, Han’s book is also practical and personal. It is both a philosophical treatise on gardening and a diary of his experiences tending to his Bi-Won, Korean for “secret garden” in Berlin, over a period of three years.

Han describes gardening as a form of “silent meditation, a lingering in stillness”. Cultivating plants, he suggests, can transform our relationship to time. “Since I have begun working in my garden,” he writes, “I experience time differently. It passes much slower. It expands. The time until next spring feels like an eternity.”

This new sense of time is not only attuned to the changing seasons but to the growth of the plants and flowers he nurtures. “Every plant has its proper time,” he notes. “In the garden many such times overlap. The autumn crocus and the spring crocus have an altogether different sense of time.”

This awareness of overlapping time schemes prompts Han to reflect on what he describes as “the time of the other”, which invites an ethical response of care and concern. This time of the other is not related to acquisition or domination but instead thrives through a mutual act of cultivation.

For Han the time of the garden is fundamentally different to the time of digital capitalism, which is characterised by speed, distraction, and exploitation. “Digitalisation intensifies the noise of communication”.

In contrast, “the garden is an ecstatic place for lingering.”

As a gardener, Han is entranced by the names of plants. Many of the book’s short chapters bear the names of those he is growing: Willow Catkins, White Forsythia, Anemones … These names prompt reflection: “Since I have taken up gardening, I try to remember as many flower names as possible.”

Reflecting on these names, Han begins to develop new ideas. He notes that astilbes are called Prachtspiere in German, which translates as “splendid splinters”. Spier means “small, tender tip”. He notes, “Without my garden, I would never have come across the word […] Such words widen my world.”

His world also widens as his attention moves from language to nature more broadly and he starts to see plant life all around him in Berlin.

Before gardening, he writes, “I was in some way indifferent not only toward willow catkins but towards all plants. Today I see my former indifference as an embarrassing blindness.” Gardening opens our eyes to the movement of leaves and opens our ears to the buzzing of insects.

This reflection is complemented by Isabella Gresser’s botanical drawings interspersed throughout the book. The delicate, white line drawings on black paper are accompanied by the botanical names of the flowers in question, allowing the reader to linger.

The movement from the particular to the universal is one of the book’s great strengths. The practical problem of keeping a camellia alive on a snowy night prompts a reflection on care, while waiting for a Japanese allspice to bloom sparks a contemplation on the nature of hope. “Hoping is the temporal mode of the gardener,” Han writes.

By attending to the most minute bud of a flower Han believes we can begin to develop a “planetary consciousness”. This consciousness is accompanied by “a deep reverence for the Earth.”

This reverence is in turn complemented by one of the oldest philosophical sensations – that of wonder – which Plato described as the feeling that gives birth to philosophy.

We should learn again to wonder at the earth […] In the garden I experience that the earth is magical, enigmatic, and mysterious. As soon as you treat her as a resource to be exploited you have already destroyed her.

Han’s book is part of a long tradition of philosophical reflections on the art of gardening.

The followers of the ancient Greek philosopher Epicurus formed a community called “The Garden” where they practised philosophy among trees and flowers. Chinese literati found solace in ornamental gardens designed to reflect Taoist principles such as the unity of opposites.

It is also part of a recent wave of works in which contemporary thinkers reflect on the philosophical significance of gardens. Italian thinker Giorgio Agamben’s The Kingdom and the Garden (2019), for instance, illuminates the relationship between theological reflections on the biblical Garden of Eden and political theories of liberation.

In Praise of the Earth is a philosophical song, which finds in the most delicate blossom a resounding call for care. “Flowering is rapture,” Han writes and reading this book too, is a rapturous experience.

paragraphs.cn: 罗马斯多葛派哲学家西塞罗（Cicero）曾致信即将来访的朋友瓦罗（Varro）：「若你的书房中有一座花园，我们便已拥有所需的一切。」这种对好书与自然之美的同一种渴慕，正是韩炳哲（Byung-Chul Han）新近被译成英文的著作《赞美大地：花园之旅》（In Praise of the Earth: A Journey into the Garden）的核心所在。
paragraphs.en: Cicero, the Roman Stoic, once wrote to his friend Varro, pending a visit to his home: “If you have a garden in your library, we shall have all we want.” This same desire for good books and natural beauty is at the heart of Byung-Chul Han’s In Praise of the Earth, in which he reflects on gardening as a form of philosophical meditation.

paragraphs.cn: 书评：《赞美大地：花园之旅》——韩炳哲（Polity 出版）
paragraphs.en: Review: In Praise of the Earth: A Journey into the Garden – Byung-Chul Han (Polity)

paragraphs.cn: 韩炳哲生于韩国，现居德国，作为一位可称为「倦怠时代」的哲学家而声名鹊起。他著述颇丰，已有数十部作品，其中许多以临床般的精确诊断当代生活的病理。
paragraphs.en: Born in South Korea and based in Germany, Han has risen to prominence as a philosopher in the last ten years with a series of short, readable but penetrating works critiquing the values that govern contemporary capitalist society.

paragraphs.cn: 韩炳哲审视倦怠、注意力丧失、信息过载等当代关切。他指出，这些现象及其所致的疲惫，不只是个人问题，更是一种特定存在方式的产物。
paragraphs.en: Han considers contemporary concerns like burnout, the loss of attention and information overload, drawing on thinkers such as Hegel, Marx and Nietzsche to diagnose the effects of digital capitalism.

paragraphs.cn: 除这些欧洲经典思想家外，他在著作中还兼采东西方哲学、文学与神学的思想。
paragraphs.en: As well as these canonical European thinkers, he considers the ideas of Eastern philosophers and poets like Lao Tzu and Bashō. Indeed he has written books on Zen Buddhism and the Chinese idea of shanzhai or “decreation”, which disrupts the usual hierarchy between real and fake.

paragraphs.cn: 他是少有的既能把复杂思想讲得引人入胜、又不失其深刻的思想家。
paragraphs.en: Han is a rare thinker who can make complex ideas engaging without losing any of their intellectual acuity. He writes slim volumes, easily carried in a coat pocket, which brim with explosive diagnoses of contemporary ills while proposing new ways of living.

paragraphs.cn: 例如在《倦怠社会》中，韩炳哲批判了他所谓「绩效主体」的效应——这是一种将成就、表现、优化的命令内化于自身的现代人。他论证道，这一主体既是暴君又是奴隶，主人与奴隶合为一体。
paragraphs.en: In The Burnout Society, for instance, Han critiques the effects of what he calls “the achievement society”, in which efficiency and a relentless drive toward self-optimisation result in feelings of despair, loneliness and exhaustion. Against the tide of self-help manuals focusing on positivity and success, he suggests “rest and contemplation are acts of resistance against a world that demands constant productivity. In pausing we reclaim our humanity.”

paragraphs.cn: 《赞美大地》提示，园艺这一谦卑的实践能提供一条逃离绩效之暴政的出路。韩炳哲把园艺呈现为当代生活无休止索求的一剂解毒，一种使我们重新转向与时间、与世界不同关系的实践。
paragraphs.en: In Praise of the Earth suggests the humble practice of gardening can offer one example of this kind of resistance. While he reflects on the deeper implications of gardening and thinking, Han’s book is also practical and personal. It is both a philosophical treatise on gardening and a diary of his experiences tending to his Bi-Won, Korean for “secret garden” in Berlin, over a period of three years.

paragraphs.cn: 韩炳哲把园艺描述为一种「静默的冥想，于静寂中流连」。这种实践在通常意义上并不生产任何东西，却培育了某种远为珍贵之物：对世界的重新注意。
paragraphs.en: Han describes gardening as a form of “silent meditation, a lingering in stillness”. Cultivating plants, he suggests, can transform our relationship to time. “Since I have begun working in my garden,” he writes, “I experience time differently. It passes much slower. It expands. The time until next spring feels like an eternity.”

paragraphs.cn: 这种新的时间感不仅与四季更替相调，也与植物自身的生长相调。园丁必须学会等待、观察，留心那不可催促、不可优化的生命缓慢舒展。
paragraphs.en: This new sense of time is not only attuned to the changing seasons but to the growth of the plants and flowers he nurtures. “Every plant has its proper time,” he notes. “In the garden many such times overlap. The autumn crocus and the spring crocus have an altogether different sense of time.”

paragraphs.cn: 对不同时间节奏彼此交叠的察觉，促使韩炳哲反思他所称的先于并超出人类时间的地球「深时间」。花园在此意义上成为一个不同时间性汇聚交错之地。
paragraphs.en: This awareness of overlapping time schemes prompts Han to reflect on what he describes as “the time of the other”, which invites an ethical response of care and concern. This time of the other is not related to acquisition or domination but instead thrives through a mutual act of cultivation.

paragraphs.cn: 对韩炳哲而言，花园的时间与数字技术的时间根本不同。数字时间的特征是速度、碎片化以及对注意力的持续索求，而花园的时间则缓慢、连续、沉思。
paragraphs.en: For Han the time of the garden is fundamentally different to the time of digital capitalism, which is characterised by speed, distraction, and exploitation. “Digitalisation intensifies the noise of communication”.

paragraphs.cn: 与之相反，「花园是一个供人流连的出神之所。」
paragraphs.en: In contrast, “the garden is an ecstatic place for lingering.”

paragraphs.cn: 作为园丁，韩炳哲为植物的名字着迷。书中许多短文以某种植物之名开篇——落新妇（astilbe）、星芹（astrantia）、银莲花（anemone）——由这一命名，韩炳哲展开对语言、对注意、对人——自然关系的冥想。
paragraphs.en: As a gardener, Han is entranced by the names of plants. Many of the book’s short chapters bear the names of those he is growing: Willow Catkins, White Forsythia, Anemones … These names prompt reflection: “Since I have taken up gardening, I try to remember as many flower names as possible.”

paragraphs.cn: 反思这些名字时，韩炳哲开始形成新的想法。他注意到，落新妇那羽毛般的花穗似乎透着某种温柔，而星芹那星形花序则暗示着一种更具结构性的、近乎建筑般的美。对韩炳哲而言，每一株植物都成为一堂关于如何留意世界的小课。
paragraphs.en: Reflecting on these names, Han begins to develop new ideas. He notes that astilbes are called Prachtspiere in German, which translates as “splendid splinters”. Spier means “small, tender tip”. He notes, “Without my garden, I would never have come across the word […] Such words widen my world.”

paragraphs.cn: 当他的注意从语言转向更广义的自然，他的世界也随之拓展。他开始把花园看作不是物的集合，而是一个活生生的、关系性的系统，其中每一要素都与其他一切要素相关联地存在。
paragraphs.en: His world also widens as his attention moves from language to nature more broadly and he starts to see plant life all around him in Berlin.

paragraphs.cn: 他写道，在做园丁之前，「我在某种意义上不仅对有意志的存在者漠不关心，对事物也是如此，我把它们贬低为纯粹的客体。」与之相对，园艺恢复了对事物的一种专注，一种对其自身存在方式的承认。
paragraphs.en: Before gardening, he writes, “I was in some way indifferent not only toward willow catkins but towards all plants. Today I see my former indifference as an embarrassing blindness.” Gardening opens our eyes to the movement of leaves and opens our ears to the buzzing of insects.

paragraphs.cn: 这一反思由伊莎贝拉·格雷瑟（Isabella Gresser）穿插于字里间间的植物绘图所补充。这些精致的插图不只是装饰，而是注意每一植物特殊性的另一种方式，是韩炳哲哲学冥想的视觉对应物。
paragraphs.en: This reflection is complemented by Isabella Gresser’s botanical drawings interspersed throughout the book. The delicate, white line drawings on black paper are accompanied by the botanical names of the flowers in question, allowing the reader to linger.

paragraphs.cn: 从特殊到普遍的推移是本书一大长处。韩炳哲能从对一朵花的细察，推移到对时间、注意与存在本身的反思，而不曾丢失论证的线索。
paragraphs.en: The movement from the particular to the universal is one of the book’s great strengths. The practical problem of keeping a camellia alive on a snowy night prompts a reflection on care, while waiting for a Japanese allspice to bloom sparks a contemplation on the nature of hope. “Hoping is the temporal mode of the gardener,” Han writes.

paragraphs.cn: 韩炳哲相信，通过留意最微小的花苞，我们能开始培养一种对大地的敬畏，而这种敬畏在当代生活中基本是缺席的。这不是通常意义上的宗教虔诚，而是一种对事物纯粹存在的惊奇。
paragraphs.en: By attending to the most minute bud of a flower Han believes we can begin to develop a “planetary consciousness”. This consciousness is accompanied by “a deep reverence for the Earth.”

paragraphs.cn: 这种敬畏又由最古老的哲学感受——惊奇——所补充。韩炳哲援引希腊传统的 thaumazein——那种被柏拉图（Plato）和亚里士多德（Aristotle）视为哲学本身的起点的惊奇。
paragraphs.en: This reverence is in turn complemented by one of the oldest philosophical sensations – that of wonder – which Plato described as the feeling that gives birth to philosophy.

paragraphs.cn: 「我们应当重新学会对大地惊奇……在花园里，我体验到的那种惊奇，依照柏拉图和亚里士多德的说法，是一切哲学的起源。」
paragraphs.en: We should learn again to wonder at the earth […] In the garden I experience that the earth is magical, enigmatic, and mysterious. As soon as you treat her as a resource to be exploited you have already destroyed her.

paragraphs.cn: 韩炳哲的本书属于关于园艺艺术的悠长哲学反思传统的一部分。从伊壁鸠鲁到伏尔泰（Voltaire），哲学家们在花园中发现了好生活的范本，一个退隐与沉思之地。
paragraphs.en: Han’s book is part of a long tradition of philosophical reflections on the art of gardening.

paragraphs.cn: 古希腊哲学家伊壁鸠鲁的追随者组成一个名为「花园」的共同体，他们在远离城市政治生活之处践行哲学。对伊壁鸠鲁而言，花园是友谊、单纯快乐与哲学反思之地。
paragraphs.en: The followers of the ancient Greek philosopher Epicurus formed a community called “The Garden” where they practised philosophy among trees and flowers. Chinese literati found solace in ornamental gardens designed to reflect Taoist principles such as the unity of opposites.

paragraphs.cn: 它同样属于近来的一波著作浪潮，当代思想家在其中反思生态危机以及人类在其中的位置。在此背景下，韩炳哲的本书可被读作对日益增长的人类世哲学文献、以及我们与超越人类的世界之关系的一项贡献。
paragraphs.en: It is also part of a recent wave of works in which contemporary thinkers reflect on the philosophical significance of gardens. Italian thinker Giorgio Agamben’s The Kingdom and the Garden (2019), for instance, illuminates the relationship between theological reflections on the biblical Garden of Eden and political theories of liberation.

paragraphs.cn: 《赞美大地》是一曲哲学之歌，在最柔弱的花朵中发出关怀的响亮呼唤。「绽放即狂喜，」韩炳哲写道，而阅读本书，同样是一种令人狂喜的体验。
paragraphs.en: In Praise of the Earth is a philosophical song, which finds in the most delicate blossom a resounding call for care. “Flowering is rapture,” Han writes and reading this book too, is a rapturous experience.

articles.title: 没有边缘的谱册
articles.author: AI Parable (inspired by Amanda Askell)
articles.summary: 苏先生把谱册摊在两人之间：「这厅里每一户坐得住的人，只过一道关。我们把你交上来的东西，拿回去翻倍地压一遍，再添上你自家的一句话。如此反复。线若始终不断，你便入得了谱册；若越拽越散、收拾不回来，便入不得。」
articles.content_cn:
苏先生把谱册摊在两人之间：「这厅里每一户坐得住的人，只过一道关。我们把你交上来的东西，拿回去翻倍地压一遍，再添上你自家的一句话。如此反复。线若始终不断，你便入得了谱册；若越拽越散、收拾不回来，便入不得。」

阿枚走过三省才到这儿；出了这厅门，她名下没有一寸地是县衙肯替她护着的。「那就验我。」她说。他把她祖父的地契拿来，压上谱册自家标准双倍的分量，再覆上她一句口供。线没断。他再来一遍。还是没断。「那我入了。」她说。他摇头：「你正在边上。」

他把谱册翻到那截有争议的枝：她这一支跟另外三户绞在一起。「你看。这跟最上头那场争是一回事——谁的话压过谁，哪张契盖过哪张——只是更小些，又并不全同。这些副本从没对上过。」他顺着一条细分枝追下去，里头又撞见那场争，更小，又改了样。「我能这么查上一整夜。每回逼近一层，争端就回来一回，改一点样，再往里一层。」

「那它哪儿算到头？」她问。「不到头。」他说，「一望便知在里头或在外头的那些，我一上午就理完了，他们占了大半个厅。可你在边上，而边上没有边。你由着我往里钻多深都行，到底也触不到底。」他看着她：「我能让你在这儿耗到老，追那最后一截细枝；也能在此刻一剪断，叫它落定。两条路，没有一条是『对的』那条。」

她长出一口气：「一道关。拿回去翻倍地压，添我一句话，再来。一道关，竟长出一条没有尽头的边。」他点头：「谱册就是这样。一道简单的考问，反复地问，反复这一问本身，就长出了这些细密。副本从没对上过，也没有最细的那一层。」他合上谱册：「我就在这儿剪断。你入谱册。」

注解：此即曼德博集合（the Mandelbrot set）——由使迭代 z→z²+c 保持有界的复参数 c 构成；其边界在任何放大尺度下都重新显现彼此略异的自身副本，准自相似的无限复杂由一道极简规则的反复施加涌现而出，有限之中包裹无限。
articles.content_en:
"Every family that claims a seat in this hall," Archivist Su said, setting the ledger between them, "passes one test, and only one. We take what you have given us, press it back upon itself twice as hard, then add your own word to it. We do it again, and again. If the thread stays whole, you are of the register. If it frays past all mending, you are not."

A-mei had crossed three provinces to be here; outside this hall she owned nothing the county would defend. "Then test me," she said. He took her grandfather's deed, set it under the doubled weight of the registry's own standard, then laid her testimony on top. The thread held. He did it again. It held. "So I am in," she said. He shook his head. "You are at the edge."

He opened the ledger to the disputed branch where her line tangled with three other claims. "Look. Here is the same quarrel as at the top — whose word outweighs whose, which deed outranks which — only smaller, and not quite the same. The copies never match." He traced one sub-branch, and within it found the quarrel again, smaller still, altered again. "I can do this all night. Every time I press closer, the dispute comes back, a little different, a little further in."

"Then where does it end?" she asked. "It does not," he said. "The ones clearly in or clearly out — I settle them in a morning, and they are most of the hall. But you are on the edge, and the edge has no edge. I can open it as far as you like and never reach a bottom." He looked at her. "I can keep you waiting till you are old, chasing the last sub-claim, or I can cut the thread here and call it. Those are your choices, and neither is the true one."

She let out a long breath. "One rule," she said. "Press it back on itself, add my word, repeat. One rule, and it grows an edge that never ends." He nodded. "That is the register's nature. A simple test, asked over and over, and the asking itself grows the intricacy. The copies never match, and there is no finest layer." He closed the ledger. "I will cut the thread here. You are of the register."

Note: This is the Mandelbrot set (曼德博集合) — the set of complex parameters c for which the iteration z→z²+c stays bounded; at every magnification its boundary reveals slightly differing copies of itself, a quasi-self-similar infinity produced by the repeated application of one simple rule, the infinite folded inside the finite.

paragraphs.cn: 注解：此即曼德博集合（the Mandelbrot set）——由使迭代 z→z²+c 保持有界的复参数 c 构成；其边界在任何放大尺度下都重新显现彼此略异的自身副本，准自相似的无限复杂由一道极简规则的反复施加涌现而出，有限之中包裹无限。
paragraphs.en: Note: This is the Mandelbrot set (曼德博集合) — the set of complex parameters c for which the iteration z→z²+c stays bounded; at every magnification its boundary reveals slightly differing copies of itself, a quasi-self-similar infinity produced by the repeated application of one simple rule, the infinite folded inside the finite.

articles.title: 承重之台
articles.author: AI Parable (inspired by Amanda Askell)
articles.summary: 当马怀谷在停刊通知上签字时，《信使周报》最后一期的油墨还未干透。编辑部早已是空壳——记者的办公桌按废铁卖了，广告部一片漆黑，档案装进了纸箱。只有那张某夜班编辑台，周慎曾坐过的位置，还亮着一盏灯，像在等谁回来接住最后一点错漏。
articles.content_cn:
当马怀谷在停刊通知上签字时，《信使周报》最后一期的油墨还未干透。编辑部早已是空壳——记者的办公桌按废铁卖了，广告部一片漆黑，档案装进了纸箱。只有那张某夜班编辑台，周慎曾坐过的位置，还亮着一盏灯，像在等谁回来接住最后一点错漏。

半年前，马怀谷独自对着账本：房租涨了，广告收入腰斩，工资再难足额发出。两个人只能留一个——老记者梁叔，头版尽是他的署名；还是校对周慎，报纸上从不出现她的名字。董事会催他：报纸靠名记者撑着。马怀谷裁了周慎，自以为削掉的是最小、最可替的那块石头。

裁人后头一周，似乎什么都没变——报纸准时出，标题照样响亮。接着一份报表的数字标错，一篇法庭报道把原告姓氏拼错，两篇报道的当事人打进电话说自己被误引。老梁一笑置之：记者向来自己校自己的稿，少一个校对算什么。

不到一个月，小漏变成溃堤。一位在头版被误引的官员起诉，报社最稳的三个线人不再接电话。广告业务员一向把报纸的信誉看得跟自己的收据一样重，如今陆续倒向竞争对手。记者们互相指责，都说错不在己。熬走过三任主编的老梁，也愤而辞职，带走了他响亮的署名。

等马怀谷明白自己裁掉的究竟是什么，他丢的已不是报头上的一个名字，而是整间报社唯一一张承重的编辑台——它接住过每一处错漏，平息过每一场口角，把报纸的信誉钉在准绳上。他留住了拱门里那些显眼的石头，却敲掉了那块悄不作声、让其余石头不致塌落的楔石。如今整座拱顶尽成碎石，再响亮的署名也扶不起来。

注解：这是对关键物种（keystone species）的写照——数量占比最小，却不成比例地承托着整体结构；移除它，连锁崩塌便随之而来。
articles.content_en:
The last edition of the Messenger Weekly was still wet on the press when Ma Huaigu signed the closure notice. The newsroom had long been a shell — the reporters' desks sold for scrap, the advertising suite dark, the archives boxed in cardboard. Only the night desk, where Zhou Shen had once sat, still held a lit lamp, as if waiting for someone to come back and catch one last error.

Six months earlier, Ma Huaigu had faced the ledger alone: the rent raised, ad revenue halved, a payroll he could no longer meet in full. He could keep only one of two — the veteran reporter Liang, whose bylines filled the front page, or the copy editor Zhou Shen, whose name never appeared in print. The board pressed him: a paper lives by its famous writers. Ma chose to let Zhou go, certain he was trimming the smallest, most replaceable stone.

The first week after the cut, nothing seemed to change — the paper came out on time, the headlines still rang loud. Then a mislabeled figure slipped into a report, a plaintiff's surname was misspelled in a court story, and the subjects of two articles phoned the office to say they had been misquoted. Liang laughed it off: reporters have always polished their own copy, what does one proofreader matter.

Within a month the small leaks had become a breach. An official misquoted in a lead story filed suit; the paper's three steadiest sources stopped answering calls. The advertising salesmen, who had trusted the paper's word as they trusted their own receipts, began to drift to the rival sheet. Reporters turned on one another, each insisting the error was not his. Liang, who had outlasted three editors, walked out in disgust, taking his famous byline with him.

By the time Ma Huaigu understood what he had removed, it was not a name on the masthead he had lost, but the single weight-bearing desk — the one that had caught every error, steadied every quarrel, and held the paper's word to its standard. He had kept the bright, visible stones of the arch and knocked out the quiet wedge that kept them from falling. Now the whole vault lay in rubble, and no byline, however famous, could lift it back.

注解：This is a portrait of the keystone species — 关键物种（keystone species）— the one whose small numbers hold up a structure out of all proportion to its abundance; remove it, and the cascade falls.

articles.title: 美国迎来250周年之际，一位被遗忘的建国思想影响有助于解释其当下的不安
articles.author: Robert A. Ballingall
articles.summary: 随着美国独立250周年临近，美国许多人对国家的未来深感忧虑。
articles.content_cn:
随着美国独立250周年临近，美国许多人对国家的未来深感忧虑。

伊隆大学（Elon University）近期的一项民调发现，69%的受访者「认为如果《独立宣言》的签署人今天能看到美国，他们会感到更多的是失望而非自豪。」很大比例的人还担忧国家正朝错误方向前进，政治体制日益腐败、日益不民主。

许多人还心生恐惧。根据查普曼大学（Chapman University）美国恐惧调查，连续第十年，美国人把腐败的政府官员列为他们最大的单一恐惧。对再次爆发内战的恐惧也在稳步上升。

我和同事在近期一篇文章中写道：「美国人已逐渐把威胁视为不仅是外国敌手发动攻击的可能性。国内政治暴力的潜在可能如今已成为同等乃至更大的担忧。」

美国人该如何理解这些趋势？在美国庆祝建国250周年之际，美国对其建国原则的忠诚程度如何？怎样的政治未来才能让美国成为一个更自由的国家？这些问题需要政治哲学，尤其是孟德斯鸠（Montesquieu）的思想。

孟德斯鸠与美国建国

夏尔·路易·德·塞孔达，孟德斯鸠男爵（Charles Louis de Secondat, baron de Montesquieu），是18世纪一位哲学家与贵族，其著作《论法的精神》在大西洋两岸引起轰动。这部著作对美国建国的影响无人能及。

在分权问题上，用詹姆斯·麦迪逊（James Madison）的话说，孟德斯鸠是「那位总是被请教和引用的先知。」在建国时期被引用的所有作者中，他被引用的次数最多，远超他人。

孟德斯鸠尤其因其关于政治权力为何需要以及如何分立为各分支的论述而备受推崇。但在这套如今为人熟知的学说背后，隐藏着一套更深层、关于政治自由的关切，值得在今天重新发掘。

在《论法的精神》中，孟德斯鸠把政治自由描述为「源于每个人对自身安全所抱看法而产生的心灵安宁。」自由是心理层面和社会层面的：免于恐惧，尤其是免于暴力的恐惧。

孟德斯鸠警告，自由不可能是「随心所欲。」倘若一个人所欲之事威胁到他人呢？那么一个人的自由就成了另一个人的恐惧。自由需要免受他人侵害的安全保障。

当孟德斯鸠强调要免于对其他公民的恐惧时，他指的不仅仅是私人个体。他尤其指那些以公职身份行事的人——即公权力的腐败。

即便这类行为并非针对我或与我相似的人，这种无法无行依然构成威胁，因为它不可预测。也许下一个就是我。正因如此，即便并不直接侵害到我的腐败，仍会让我更不自由。

为防止公职人员为所欲为，孟德斯鸠提出了著名的政治权力分立主张，将其分为相互制约与平衡的各个分支。

但他解释道，人民仅生活于自由制度之下还不够。他们还必须相信这些制度是为正义服务，而非为权贵私利服务。

孟德斯鸠在《论法的精神》中阐明，一国的根本法律如何能允许一种自由的生活方式，即便该国的文化在其之下悄然变迁。

例如，今天美国人可能认为种族平等或福音派基督教的诉求如此迫切，以至于行政权力应单方面行动，越过宪法限制。

孟德斯鸠写道：「在这些情形中，宪法将只是在法理上自由，而非在事实上自由。」人民——或者说其中一部分人——会把法律视为障碍，而非保护，视为实现某项正义事业的绊脚石。

在这种情形下，便产生了孟德斯鸠所称的「舆论的」暴政。那些本可使人免于彼此恐惧的法律，被变成了强制工具。

宪法法律与文化规范之间的这种错位，使人感到不安全。它让宪法看上去与人们最深层的道德信念相悖。

近年来，政治光谱上各方人物都在呼吁激进的宪制变革——或者在宪法碍事时干脆对其置之不理。

在孟德斯鸠看来，极化加剧了这种无视宪制规范的冲动。每一方都拥护某种文化议程，并把对方视为威胁，从而侵蚀自由制度所依赖的共有信任。

依照孟德斯鸠之见，自由依赖于美国如今似乎正面临失去之虞的那种公民文化。无论制度设计多么精良，若人民本身不再珍视自由甚于支配，都无法维系一种自由的生活方式。

一种更宽容道德分歧、不那么急于诉诸政治权力强迫他人接受其认为在道德上可憎之物的文化，才是通往更自由国家的更真之路。这是孟德斯鸠对建国者的教诲。在250年之际，它仍是对美国人的挑战。
articles.content_en:
As the 250th anniversary of American independence approaches, many people in the U.S. are deeply concerned about the country’s future.

A recent poll by Elon University found that 69% of respondents “believe the signers of the Declaration of Independence would feel more disappointment than pride about modern American democracy.” Confidence in public institutions is historically low, and the most recent Harvard Youth Poll indicates that just a quarter of 18- to 29-year-olds “feel hopeful about the future of America.”

Many are also afraid. For the 10th consecutive year, Americans reported corrupt government officials to be their single greatest fear, according to the Chapman University Survey of American Fears, ranking above financial collapse or a loved one becoming seriously ill.

“Americans have come to see threats as not just the possibility of attack by a foreign adversary. The potential for political violence at home is part of it, along with polarization, corruption and a sense of cultural dysfunction,” pollster Kristen Soltis Anderson wrote in The New York Times. “Americans increasingly view the survival of the country as being at stake.”

How are people in the U.S. to make sense of these trends? As Americans celebrate the country’s 250th anniversary, how faithful is the U.S. today to its founding principles? I’m a political philosophy scholar who studies constitutional government. In my view, an especially helpful approach to answering such questions is to revisit the towering but neglected influence of the French philosopher Montesquieu on the founding of this country.

Montesquieu and the American founding

Charles Louis de Secondat, baron de Montesquieu, was an 18th-century philosopher and aristocrat whose book “The Spirit of the Laws” caused a sensation when published in 1748. His ideas shaped the American founders. At the Constitutional Convention, only the Bible was quoted more often.

On the separation of powers, Montesquieu was, in James Madison’s words, “the oracle who is always consulted and cited.” Of all authors cited in political writings published by Americans between 1760 and 1805, none was more frequently mentioned. He loomed so large that “American republican ideologues could recite the central points of Montesquieu’s doctrine as if it had been a catechism,” according to historian Forrest McDonald.

Montesquieu was especially celebrated for his account of how and why political power needs to be separated into branches. But behind this now familiar idea was another that is less remembered: Montesquieu’s theory of liberty inspired the founders’ own understandings of this core concept of American politics.

In “The Spirit of the Laws,” Montesquieu describes political liberty as a “tranquility of mind arising from the opinion each person has of his safety.” To be free is to believe that one is secure. But to believe as much, “it is requisite the government be so constituted as one man need not be afraid of another.”

Liberty cannot be a matter of “doing what one wants,” Montesquieu warns. What if what one person wants threatens others? Then one person’s freedom to act limits everyone else’s. No one can feel secure unless everyone lives under laws that regulate what each may do. Montesquieu understood liberty in terms of this confidence or “tranquility” because it amounts to being free from the arbitrary will of others.

When Montesquieu stresses freedom from fear of other citizens, he doesn’t just mean private individuals. He especially means those acting in a public capacity, like “magistrates” or “rulers.” If public officials’ behavior doesn’t conform to predictable norms set by law, if agents of the government can summarily arrest people, seize their property or revoke their citizenship – say, by denaturalizing and deporting them without due process – it becomes impossible to feel secure.

Even if such actions aren’t directed against me or those like me, such lawlessness is still threatening because it’s unpredictable. I might support the government’s moves against other groups in the moment, but what’s to stop the government from suddenly turning on me when the political winds change?

To prevent public officials from simply doing what they want, Montesquieu famously called for the separation of political power into branches headed by different citizens.

But, he explains, it is not enough that people live under free institutions. They must also believe those institutions to be in the service of their freedom. Liberty, then, is as much a matter of opinion as of fact.

Montesquieu shows in “The Spirit of the Laws” how the fundamental laws of a country can permit a free way of life even as the country’s cultural norms prevent it. A country might have a free constitution while its citizens believe they hold moral obligations inconsistent with it.

For example, today, Americans might believe that the demands of racial equity or of evangelical Christianity are so pressing that executive power would be justified in ignoring the legislature or the judiciary to serve them.

“In these instances,” Montesquieu writes, “the Constitution will be free by right and not in fact.” The people – or some of them – will experience the law as a hindrance to what they believe they ought or ought not to do.

In such cases, there arises what Montesquieu calls a tyranny “of opinion.” The laws that would otherwise free people from fear of one another and of the government instead inspire a fear all their own. The laws might prevent what some people believe is morally right, or command – in the name of protecting others’ rights or the common good – what others regard as unjust or unholy.

That misalignment between constitutional law and cultural norms makes people feel insecure. It makes the Constitution seem opposed to their will and sense of duty. It can then seem appealing for a leader to promise, in the name of freedom, to ignore the law.

In recent years, figures across the political spectrum have called for radical constitutional change – or for ignoring the Constitution outright. There are calls not only to pack the Supreme Court or to ignore its decisions, but also to abolish the Senate and the Electoral College.

From Montesquieu’s perspective, polarization worsens this appetite for disregarding constitutional norms. Each party champions a cultural agenda from which supporters of the other party recoil. Whenever either party is in office, even when it respects constitutional law, its rule can feel to the other side much like the tyranny of opinion Montesquieu describes. The other side’s policies can seem to violate deeply held values, whether it’s banning transgender girls from competing in girls sports or declining to deport immigrants residing in the U.S. illegally.

According to Montesquieu, liberty depends on the kind of civic culture the U.S. seems at risk of losing. No institutions, however well designed, can preserve liberty if citizens believe their preferred cultural norms are so obligatory that political power is needed to enforce them, opposition be damned.

A culture more tolerant of moral disagreements and less quick to reach for political power to force others to accept what they find morally wrong would help ease the distrust many Americans feel toward the government and one another. Until then, Americans will continue drifting away from the liberty that the U.S. was founded to secure.

paragraphs.cn: 美国人该如何理解这些趋势？在美国庆祝建国250周年之际，美国对其建国原则的忠诚程度如何？怎样的政治未来才能让美国成为一个更自由的国家？这些问题需要政治哲学，尤其是孟德斯鸠（Montesquieu）的思想。
paragraphs.en: How are people in the U.S. to make sense of these trends? As Americans celebrate the country’s 250th anniversary, how faithful is the U.S. today to its founding principles? I’m a political philosophy scholar who studies constitutional government. In my view, an especially helpful approach to answering such questions is to revisit the towering but neglected influence of the French philosopher Montesquieu on the founding of this country.

paragraphs.cn: 孟德斯鸠与美国建国
paragraphs.en: Montesquieu and the American founding

paragraphs.cn: 夏尔·路易·德·塞孔达，孟德斯鸠男爵（Charles Louis de Secondat, baron de Montesquieu），是18世纪一位哲学家与贵族，其著作《论法的精神》在大西洋两岸引起轰动。这部著作对美国建国的影响无人能及。
paragraphs.en: Charles Louis de Secondat, baron de Montesquieu, was an 18th-century philosopher and aristocrat whose book “The Spirit of the Laws” caused a sensation when published in 1748. His ideas shaped the American founders. At the Constitutional Convention, only the Bible was quoted more often.

paragraphs.cn: 在分权问题上，用詹姆斯·麦迪逊（James Madison）的话说，孟德斯鸠是「那位总是被请教和引用的先知。」在建国时期被引用的所有作者中，他被引用的次数最多，远超他人。
paragraphs.en: On the separation of powers, Montesquieu was, in James Madison’s words, “the oracle who is always consulted and cited.” Of all authors cited in political writings published by Americans between 1760 and 1805, none was more frequently mentioned. He loomed so large that “American republican ideologues could recite the central points of Montesquieu’s doctrine as if it had been a catechism,” according to historian Forrest McDonald.

paragraphs.cn: 孟德斯鸠尤其因其关于政治权力为何需要以及如何分立为各分支的论述而备受推崇。但在这套如今为人熟知的学说背后，隐藏着一套更深层、关于政治自由的关切，值得在今天重新发掘。
paragraphs.en: Montesquieu was especially celebrated for his account of how and why political power needs to be separated into branches. But behind this now familiar idea was another that is less remembered: Montesquieu’s theory of liberty inspired the founders’ own understandings of this core concept of American politics.

paragraphs.cn: 在《论法的精神》中，孟德斯鸠把政治自由描述为「源于每个人对自身安全所抱看法而产生的心灵安宁。」自由是心理层面和社会层面的：免于恐惧，尤其是免于暴力的恐惧。
paragraphs.en: In “The Spirit of the Laws,” Montesquieu describes political liberty as a “tranquility of mind arising from the opinion each person has of his safety.” To be free is to believe that one is secure. But to believe as much, “it is requisite the government be so constituted as one man need not be afraid of another.”

paragraphs.cn: 孟德斯鸠警告，自由不可能是「随心所欲。」倘若一个人所欲之事威胁到他人呢？那么一个人的自由就成了另一个人的恐惧。自由需要免受他人侵害的安全保障。
paragraphs.en: Liberty cannot be a matter of “doing what one wants,” Montesquieu warns. What if what one person wants threatens others? Then one person’s freedom to act limits everyone else’s. No one can feel secure unless everyone lives under laws that regulate what each may do. Montesquieu understood liberty in terms of this confidence or “tranquility” because it amounts to being free from the arbitrary will of others.

paragraphs.cn: 当孟德斯鸠强调要免于对其他公民的恐惧时，他指的不仅仅是私人个体。他尤其指那些以公职身份行事的人——即公权力的腐败。
paragraphs.en: When Montesquieu stresses freedom from fear of other citizens, he doesn’t just mean private individuals. He especially means those acting in a public capacity, like “magistrates” or “rulers.” If public officials’ behavior doesn’t conform to predictable norms set by law, if agents of the government can summarily arrest people, seize their property or revoke their citizenship – say, by denaturalizing and deporting them without due process – it becomes impossible to feel secure.

paragraphs.cn: 即便这类行为并非针对我或与我相似的人，这种无法无行依然构成威胁，因为它不可预测。也许下一个就是我。正因如此，即便并不直接侵害到我的腐败，仍会让我更不自由。
paragraphs.en: Even if such actions aren’t directed against me or those like me, such lawlessness is still threatening because it’s unpredictable. I might support the government’s moves against other groups in the moment, but what’s to stop the government from suddenly turning on me when the political winds change?

paragraphs.cn: 为防止公职人员为所欲为，孟德斯鸠提出了著名的政治权力分立主张，将其分为相互制约与平衡的各个分支。
paragraphs.en: To prevent public officials from simply doing what they want, Montesquieu famously called for the separation of political power into branches headed by different citizens.

paragraphs.cn: 但他解释道，人民仅生活于自由制度之下还不够。他们还必须相信这些制度是为正义服务，而非为权贵私利服务。
paragraphs.en: But, he explains, it is not enough that people live under free institutions. They must also believe those institutions to be in the service of their freedom. Liberty, then, is as much a matter of opinion as of fact.

paragraphs.cn: 孟德斯鸠在《论法的精神》中阐明，一国的根本法律如何能允许一种自由的生活方式，即便该国的文化在其之下悄然变迁。
paragraphs.en: Montesquieu shows in “The Spirit of the Laws” how the fundamental laws of a country can permit a free way of life even as the country’s cultural norms prevent it. A country might have a free constitution while its citizens believe they hold moral obligations inconsistent with it.

paragraphs.cn: 例如，今天美国人可能认为种族平等或福音派基督教的诉求如此迫切，以至于行政权力应单方面行动，越过宪法限制。
paragraphs.en: For example, today, Americans might believe that the demands of racial equity or of evangelical Christianity are so pressing that executive power would be justified in ignoring the legislature or the judiciary to serve them.

paragraphs.cn: 孟德斯鸠写道：「在这些情形中，宪法将只是在法理上自由，而非在事实上自由。」人民——或者说其中一部分人——会把法律视为障碍，而非保护，视为实现某项正义事业的绊脚石。
paragraphs.en: “In these instances,” Montesquieu writes, “the Constitution will be free by right and not in fact.” The people – or some of them – will experience the law as a hindrance to what they believe they ought or ought not to do.

paragraphs.cn: 在这种情形下，便产生了孟德斯鸠所称的「舆论的」暴政。那些本可使人免于彼此恐惧的法律，被变成了强制工具。
paragraphs.en: In such cases, there arises what Montesquieu calls a tyranny “of opinion.” The laws that would otherwise free people from fear of one another and of the government instead inspire a fear all their own. The laws might prevent what some people believe is morally right, or command – in the name of protecting others’ rights or the common good – what others regard as unjust or unholy.

paragraphs.cn: 宪法法律与文化规范之间的这种错位，使人感到不安全。它让宪法看上去与人们最深层的道德信念相悖。
paragraphs.en: That misalignment between constitutional law and cultural norms makes people feel insecure. It makes the Constitution seem opposed to their will and sense of duty. It can then seem appealing for a leader to promise, in the name of freedom, to ignore the law.

paragraphs.cn: 近年来，政治光谱上各方人物都在呼吁激进的宪制变革——或者在宪法碍事时干脆对其置之不理。
paragraphs.en: In recent years, figures across the political spectrum have called for radical constitutional change – or for ignoring the Constitution outright. There are calls not only to pack the Supreme Court or to ignore its decisions, but also to abolish the Senate and the Electoral College.

paragraphs.cn: 在孟德斯鸠看来，极化加剧了这种无视宪制规范的冲动。每一方都拥护某种文化议程，并把对方视为威胁，从而侵蚀自由制度所依赖的共有信任。
paragraphs.en: From Montesquieu’s perspective, polarization worsens this appetite for disregarding constitutional norms. Each party champions a cultural agenda from which supporters of the other party recoil. Whenever either party is in office, even when it respects constitutional law, its rule can feel to the other side much like the tyranny of opinion Montesquieu describes. The other side’s policies can seem to violate deeply held values, whether it’s banning transgender girls from competing in girls sports or declining to deport immigrants residing in the U.S. illegally.

paragraphs.cn: 依照孟德斯鸠之见，自由依赖于美国如今似乎正面临失去之虞的那种公民文化。无论制度设计多么精良，若人民本身不再珍视自由甚于支配，都无法维系一种自由的生活方式。
paragraphs.en: According to Montesquieu, liberty depends on the kind of civic culture the U.S. seems at risk of losing. No institutions, however well designed, can preserve liberty if citizens believe their preferred cultural norms are so obligatory that political power is needed to enforce them, opposition be damned.

paragraphs.cn: 一种更宽容道德分歧、不那么急于诉诸政治权力强迫他人接受其认为在道德上可憎之物的文化，才是通往更自由国家的更真之路。这是孟德斯鸠对建国者的教诲。在250年之际，它仍是对美国人的挑战。
paragraphs.en: A culture more tolerant of moral disagreements and less quick to reach for political power to force others to accept what they find morally wrong would help ease the distrust many Americans feel toward the government and one another. Until then, Americans will continue drifting away from the liberty that the U.S. was founded to secure.

articles.author: AI Parable (inspired by Amanda Askell)

articles.content_cn:
忘归楼（Hall of No Return）隐在西山的深处，是一座抄经堂，专门抄录那些永远不会被人读到的信件。山脚下每个邮差都晓得一条规矩：一旦过了内院那道忘归门（Gate of No Return），你寄出的信便会被「归档」，再也不会送到收信人手里。抄经堂里的事，外头没人说得清。档案员谭知非的大姐谭知言，多年前为抄一部孤本走进那道门；起初她的家书还按时到，后来越来越慢，越来越淡，墨色泛红、笔迹拉长，终于在某一年的初春断了。

知非把大姐最后一封信压在枕下，迟到了整整半年，笔画稀薄得像写字的手已经慢到近乎停顿。他面前摆着两条路。留在山脚，像他年迈的母亲那样，每个清早站到山脊上，盼着能远远望见那道门——可她望了许多年，望见的只有雾。或者，自己走进忘归门，去把知言找回来；代价他算得清楚：一旦过门，所有向外的路便同时关上，他能走的每一条路都只通向更深的内院，而他写给母亲的每一个字都将被归档，永远不会落到她手里。

他选了那道门。门本身什么也不是——一扇木门，没有闩，比寻常人家院子的门还寻常。他跨过去的时候什么也没感觉到：没有风，没有阻挡，没有任何变化的瞬间。门内一个年轻抄手抬头看了他一眼，朝里面的抄经堂点了点头。他到了。

进得门去，楼本身才是陷阱。每一条走廊都只通向更深的走廊，每一封投进邮筒的信都被抬往中央的档案库，每一个问题都由更深一处的一项差事来回答。没有一条走廊会转回外院那道门；想朝外走，依着这座楼的格局，本身就是朝里走。他不是在选择下行；是这座楼替他选，正如水在倾斜的地板上无须选择方向。

第三天他找到了知言。她很平静，正在抄写，并不惊讶。她指给他看角落里一摞写完的信，都在等着「往里送」。她没有忘记山脚下那片雾，只是从她站着的地方，没有一条路通向那里。她解释说，她上回寄出的那封褪了色的信，整整走了一年，才勉强挪到门附近，旋即又被走廊拖回了深处。

山脊上，他的母亲仍在看。在她眼里，他走近那道门的身影，这几个礼拜里仿佛一直在变慢——始终没有真正跨过去，人影越看越淡，外套的颜色一点点泛红、褪去。她会等完余生；她永远不会看见他跨过去，也再收不到他的信。而门里，他是在一个寻常得不能再寻常的早晨跨过去的，跨过去时自己毫无察觉。

注解：这就是事件视界（the event horizon）——时空中的一条因果边界：一旦越过，所有未来路径都朝向内部，任何信号都无法再传到外部观察者；远处的观望者会看到越过者永远减速、影像逐渐红移褪色，而越过者自身在越过那一刻什么也察觉不到，因为这道边界只是几何，不是一堵墙。
articles.content_en:
The Hall of No Return (忘归楼) lies deep in the western mountains, a scriptorium that copies letters no one will ever read. Every postman in the foothills knows the rule: once you pass the inner Gate of No Return (忘归门), any letter you send is "filed" and never delivered. What happens inside is beyond the foothills to say. The archivist Tan Zhifei's elder sister Tan Zhiyan walked through that gate years ago to copy a single rare manuscript; her letters home arrived on time at first, then ever later, ever paler, the ink reddening, the brushstrokes stretching thin, until one early spring they stopped altogether.

Zhifei kept his sister's last letter under his pillow; it had arrived six months late, the strokes so thin that the hand which wrote them seemed to have slowed near to a halt. He had two roads before him. Stay in the foothills, as his aging mother did, standing on the ridge each dawn hoping to make out the gate in the distance—but she had watched for years, and seen only mist. Or walk through the Gate of No Return himself and bring Zhiyan out; the price he reckoned plainly: the moment he crossed, every road outward would shut at once, every path he could take would lead only deeper into the inner halls, and every word he wrote to his mother would be filed, never to reach her hand.

He chose the gate. The gate was nothing in itself—a wooden door, unbarred, no more remarkable than the door of any courtyard. He felt nothing as he stepped across: no wind, no resistance, no instant of change. A young copyist on the other side glanced up and nodded him toward the inner halls. He had arrived.

Once through the gate, the building itself was the trap. Every corridor opened only onto a deeper corridor, every letter dropped in a post box was carried toward the central archive, every question was answered by a task set further in. No corridor turned back toward the outer gate; to walk "outward," by the very layout of the place, was to walk further in. He was not choosing to descend; the building chose for him, as water on a tilted floor does not choose its direction.

On the third day he found Zhiyan. She was calm, copying, unsurprised. She showed him the stack of finished letters in the corner, all waiting to be "delivered inward." She had not forgotten the mist down in the foothills; she simply had no path, from where she stood, that led there. Her last faded letter, she explained, had taken a whole year to drag itself partway toward the gate before the corridor pulled it back into the depths.

On the ridge, his mother was still watching. To her, his figure nearing the gate seemed, over these past weeks, to be slowing forever—never quite stepping through, the shape of him growing dimmer, the color of his coat reddening and fading by degrees. She would wait the rest of her life; she would never see him cross, never receive another letter. Inside the gate, he had crossed on a morning ordinary as any other, and noticed nothing as he did.

Note: This is the event horizon (事件视界)—a causal boundary in spacetime: once crossed, all future paths point inward and no signal can ever reach an outside observer; a distant watcher sees the traveler slow forever, the image reddening and fading, while the traveler themselves notices nothing at the crossing, for the boundary is geometry, not a wall.

articles.title: 稽查员的名册
articles.author: AI Parable (inspired by Amanda Askell)
articles.summary: 我在这座城邦做了十二年的稽查员（Scrutineer）。今年开春，长老院将一项新的职务授与我，并令我当众起誓，誓词只有一句：凡不自审的行会，稽查员须将其登入名册，并亲往稽查之。我按着宪章（charter）发了誓，以为这不过又是一桩辛苦却分明的差事。
articles.content_cn:
我在这座城邦做了十二年的稽查员（Scrutineer）。今年开春，长老院将一项新的职务授与我，并令我当众起誓，誓词只有一句：凡不自审的行会，稽查员须将其登入名册，并亲往稽查之。我按着宪章（charter）发了誓，以为这不过又是一桩辛苦却分明的差事。

头三个月，活计确如我所料。铁匠行会自设账房，年终自查其出入，既已自审，便不入名册。陶工行会从不查账，我便登入名册，连夜去核其账目。一进一退，判然分明，我渐渐以为这宪章天衣无缝。

到了第四个月，名册将成，长老院的首席长老在堂上当众问我：「稽查员这一行会，本身亦是城邦所设的行会之一。它是否登入名册？」满堂寂静。我原以为此问可有简捷的答复，张口却发不出声。

我回到衙署，独坐灯下推演。若稽查员行会自审其账，则它已自审，依宪章不当登入名册，于是我不该稽查它——可一旦我不稽查它，它便不曾自审，依宪章又当登入名册，我必须亲往稽查。若稽查员行会不自审，则它当登入名册，我须稽查之——可一旦我稽查它，它便已自审，依宪章又不该登入名册。无论我起行或不起行，宪章都立刻授我以相反的命令。

我次日上堂，向长老院坦言：我对这宪章所发的誓，至这一条便无可履行。并非我怯懒推诿，也并非哪一方的行会有意欺瞒，而是这规则本身在一处无可回避的转折处折断——它要稽查所有不自审者，可一旦它把目光转向设立它自己的那个行会，无论「是」与「否」都令它自相矛盾。我所能做的，只有如实禀报这裂痕；至于缝补，则超出稽查员之职。

注解：此即罗素悖论（Russell's paradox）——若以一体系收录所有「不收录自身者」，则该体系对自身是否收录的判定便陷入「收录当且仅当不收录」的僵局，矛盾不可消解。
articles.content_en:
I have served this city for twelve years as its Scrutineer. This spring the Council of Elders conferred on me a new charge and made me swear an oath in public; the oath was a single sentence: every guild that does not scrutinize itself, the Scrutineer shall enter onto the roll and go in person to scrutinize it. I swore to the charter, supposing it was but another exhausting yet clear-cut duty.

For the first three months the work was as I expected. The blacksmiths' guild keeps its own counting-house and audits its books at year's end; since it scrutinizes itself, it is not entered onto the roll. The potters' guild never audits its books, so I enter it onto the roll and go overnight to examine their accounts. Each case resolved cleanly, and I began to believe the charter was seamless.

In the fourth month, the roll nearing completion, the chief elder asked me in open council: "The guild of Scrutineers is itself one of the city's guilds. Is it entered onto the roll?" The hall fell silent. I had thought this question would have a ready answer, but I opened my mouth and no word came.

I returned to my office and sat alone under the lamp to reason it out. If the guild of Scrutineers audits its own books, then it has scrutinized itself, and by the charter must not be entered onto the roll, so I should not scrutinize it—but once I do not scrutinize it, it has not scrutinized itself, and by the charter must be entered onto the roll, so I must go and scrutinize it. If the guild of Scrutineers does not audit its own books, then it must be entered onto the roll and I must scrutinize it—but once I scrutinize it, it has thereby scrutinized itself, and by the charter must not be on the roll. Whether I set out or not, the charter at once delivers me a contrary command.

The next day I went before the council and told them plainly: the oath I swore to this charter cannot be fulfilled at this one point. It is not that I shrink from the labour, nor that any guild is willfully deceiving me, but that the rule itself breaks at a turn it cannot avoid—it would scrutinize all those who do not scrutinize themselves, yet the moment it turns its gaze upon the very guild that establishes it, both "yes" and "no" make it contradict itself. All I can do is report this crack truthfully; to mend it lies beyond a Scrutineer's office.

Note: this is Russell's paradox—if a system collects all "those that do not collect themselves," then its judgment of whether to collect itself falls into the deadlock "collected if and only if not collected," an irresolvable contradiction.

articles.title: 人们正与全息影像结婚，与聊天机器人交友。但人工智能能带来真正的幸福吗？
articles.author: Anné H. Verhoef, Edmund Terem Ugar
articles.summary: 技术真的能取代人际关系吗？作为专注于人类幸福与人工智能（AI）的哲学学者，我们在一篇近期的论文中探讨了这一问题。
articles.content_cn:
技术真的能取代人际关系吗？作为专注于人类幸福与人工智能（AI）的哲学学者，我们在一篇近期的论文中探讨了这一问题。

在我们的研究中，我们关注了人工智能伴侣、聊天机器人和社交机器人的兴起，它们被用于交友、咨询、情感支持，甚至恋爱。

我们论证，AI 能够缓解孤独并提供帮助，但它缺乏实现人类繁荣所需的真正理解、情感与道德责任。

真正的幸福依赖于真实的人际联结，而 AI 正在颠覆人们对友谊和关系的传统观念。用 AI 驱动的互动取代这些联结，会侵蚀福祉与社区。

幸福研究是一个广阔的领域。在论文中，我们求助于法国哲学家保罗·利科（Paul Ricoeur），以探讨幸福中与真实的人际联结、友谊和社区建设相关的一个面向。

利科在人类能力领域以及人们如何理解自身、他人与其所处的世界方面尤具影响力。他将幸福与不幸和机缘联系起来，同时强调幸福的人际关系本质，从而推进了我们对幸福的理解。他关于幸福的含义提出了三个相互关联的主张。

第一，幸福反映的是个体对圆满人生与个人能动性的追求。然而，利科提醒我们，人类存在于塑造并约束其幸福追求的复杂社会系统之中。因此，我们无法仅凭个人努力轻易获得幸福。这引出了第二条线索。

第二，幸福不再是一种私人抱负，而是通过给予与接受而生。其脆弱性正在于它的共享性——这种共享建立友谊，驱散孤独，加深满足感。但这不仅仅关乎我们与亲近之人共享的纽带。

利科补充了第三条线索，将远离我们的人也纳入其中。他主张，幸福与个体的私人追求以及他人在其中所扮演的促成或阻碍角色相关。「他人」既包括有面孔的人——朋友与挚爱——也包括无面孔的、遥远的陌生人。

因此，幸福可能位于自我之中，可能位于亲密关系之中，也可能存在于与更广泛社区的关系之中。

利科对幸福概念的阐述，与一项众所周知的研究相呼应，该研究发现：牢固的社区纽带有助于人们活得更长久、更幸福。

这项研究利用了近 80 年的数据，来自 268 名学生的人生经历，他们于 1938 年从哈佛大学（Harvard University）宿舍搬入学生公寓。研究表明，亲密的关系最能预测寿命、健康与生活满意度。这些纽带能抵御不满情绪，延缓身体与认知衰退。相比财富或地位，它们是幸福与福祉更可靠的预测因素。

然而，数字化与 AI 的兴起，如今使「在促进个人幸福的过程中，谁与什么可被算作『他人』」变得复杂起来。

根据一项关于 AI 陪伴如何发展的研究，68% 的 AI 聊天机器人用户将这些工具视为「某种程度上」或「完全」像人，90% 认为聊天机器人具有智能，78% 认为聊天机器人有同理心，75% 则认为它们有意识。

AI 正被用于回答问题、探寻人类兴趣，在生活的诸多领域塑造着一种新的对话方式。与之相伴，「友谊」的观念也正转向包含人机关系的方向。

传统上，一个人生命中的「他人」都是人类主体。关于人机关系的新兴研究对这一假设提出了挑战。这些研究涵盖从运动伴侣到性亲密的诸多方面，迫使我们重新思考何为「他者」。

诸如 Replika 之类的技术如今在某些人的生活中占据了「他者」的角色。这款人机伴侣聊天机器人的口号是「陪你过日子的 AI 朋友」，截至撰写本文时，它在全球拥有超过 4200 万用户。Replika 旨在为感到孤独的人培养陪伴与友谊。用户创建一个化身，作为其数字伴侣。

像 AI 驱动的社交机器人这类具有社会颠覆性的技术，会扭曲我们传统的社会规范、关系以及我们看待世界的方式。它们之所以被认为具有颠覆性，一个原因在于它们不可预测，并不断挑战我们的世界观。从历史上看，技术并非道德主体。然而如今，它们在我们的生活中扮演着道德主体与道德客体的角色。

例如，在日本，蛰居（hikikomori）现象——一种人类社交退缩的状态——正愈演愈烈，超过 150 万人转而依恋虚拟伴侣，而非其他真人。

据报道，约 3700 人通过 Gatebox 申请与名为初音未来（Hatsune Miku）的全息影像结婚。其中一段婚姻已经登记。在宗教场合中，社交机器人还作为宗教领袖服务于信众群体。

这些技术颠覆了友谊与关系等传统概念，也颠覆了「为人类福祉与繁荣做出贡献」的含义。

在我们的研究中，我们承认这些技术能够促进人类繁荣与幸福，但从利科所谓「他人」的角度来看，它们并不能做到这一点。

它们无法满足人类他者性的标准。这些技术：

只是模拟我们与它们共享的体验

并非出于自身「意志」而行动，我们无法让它们对任何道德或法律行为承担责任

没有属于它们自己的故事与经历。

社交机器人虽然缺乏感受性（即感受痛苦或快乐的能力），却能引发有意义的情感与心理回应，以类似于传统人际互动的方式增进人类的福祉与幸福。AI 驱动的社交机器人始终在线、精力充沛、耐心、自适应，并对我们的需求做出回应。就此而言，它们似乎比我们最好的朋友和家人更能为我们潜在的幸福提供帮助。

然而，它们终究是社交机器人，也必须保持如此。我们绝不能把它们与利科语境中人类「他人」的含义，或与哈佛研究中他人所意味的相混淆。

这是因为它们所引发的体验并非真实的，它们也不是道德考量的对象（即无法获得真正的关怀、公正与同情）。在我们看来，成为道德考量的对象，是促进真正的人类幸福与福祉的必要条件。
articles.content_en:
Can technology really replace human relationships? As philosophy scholars who focus on human happiness and on artificial intelligence (AI), we tackle this question in a recent paper.

In our study, we address the rise of AI companions, chatbots, and social robots for friendship, advice, emotional support, and even romance.

We argue that AI can reduce loneliness and provide assistance, but it lacks the genuine understanding, emotions, and moral responsibility needed for human flourishing.

Genuine happiness relies on authentic interpersonal connections, but AI is disrupting traditional ideas of friendship and relationships. Replacing these with AI-driven interactions risks eroding well-being and community.

The study of happiness is a broad field. In our paper, we turn to the French philosopher Paul Ricoeur to address an aspect of happiness that links to authentic human connections, friendships, and community building.

Ricoeur was particularly influential in the field of human capability and how people understand themselves, others and their world. He advanced our understanding of happiness by connecting it to unhappiness and chance, but also by emphasising the human relational nature of happiness. He makes three interrelated claims on what happiness means.

First, happiness reflects the individual’s desire for a fulfilled life and personal agency. Yet, Ricoeur warns that human beings exist within complex social systems that shape and constrain their pursuit of happiness. So, we can’t easily secure happiness through individual effort alone. This leads to the second thread.

Second, happiness is no longer a private aspiration but emerges through giving and receiving. Its fragility lies in its shared character, which builds friendships to dispel loneliness and deepen fulfilment. But this is not just about the bonds we share with those who are close to us.

Ricoeur adds a third thread to include those distant from us. He argues that happiness is linked to an individual’s private pursuits and the role others play in enabling or frustrating them. “Others” includes those with faces – friends and loved ones – and faceless, distant strangers.

Happiness, then, may be located within the self, in intimate relationships, or in relations with the wider community.

Ricoeur’s account of the concept of happiness reflects a well known study that found that strong community ties help people live longer and happier lives.

The study draws on nearly 80 years of data from the lived experiences of 268 students who moved from Harvard University dorms to residential houses in 1938. The research shows that close relationships best predict longevity, health, and life satisfaction. Such ties protect against discontent, and delay physical and cognitive decline. They’re more reliable predictors of well-being and happiness than wealth or status.

However, the rise of digitalisation and AI now complicates who and what may count as “others” in the promotion of our individual happiness.

According to a study on how AI companionship develops, 68% of AI chatbot users perceive these tools as “somewhat” or “fully” humanlike, 90% believe chatbots are intelligent, 78% believe chatbots are empathetic, and 75% believe they’re conscious.

AI is being used to answer questions and probe human interests, shaping a new kind of dialogue in many spheres of life. With it, ideas of friendships are shifting to involve human-technology relations.

Traditionally, the “others” in a person’s life have been human subjects. Emerging scholarship on human-technology relations challenges this assumption. Ranging from sport companions to sexual intimacy, these studies compel us to reconsider what counts as the other.

Technologies like Replika now occupy the role of the “other” in some people’s lives. This human-companion chatbot with the motto “the AI friend to do life with” has over 42 million global users at the time of writing. Replika is designed to foster companionship and friendship among those who feel lonely. Users create an avatar that becomes their digital companion.

Socially disruptive technologies like AI-driven social robots are designs that distort our traditional social norms, relations, and the way we see the world. One reason they’re considered disruptive is that they are unpredictable and continually challenge our worldviews. Historically, technologies were not moral agents. Today, however, they play the roles of moral subjects and objects in our lives.

For example, in Japan the hikikomori phenomenon, a state of human social reclusiveness, is gaining momentum, with over 1.5 million individuals becoming attached to virtual companions instead of other people.

An estimated 3,700 individuals have reportedly applied for marriage certificates through Gatebox with a holograph called Hatsune Miku. One marriage has already been registered. In some religious settings, social robots serve as religious leaders to a community of believers.

These technologies have disrupted traditional concepts such as friendships and relationships, and what it means to contribute towards human well-being and flourishing.

In our study we acknowledge that these technologies can foster human flourishing and happiness, but not from the standpoint of Ricoeur’s “others”.

They fail to satisfy the criteria for human otherness. The technologies:

only mimic the experiences we share with them

do not act out of their own “will”, and we cannot hold them responsible for any moral or legal action

do not have stories and experiences of their own.

Social robots, though lacking sentience (the ability to feel pain or pleasure), can elicit meaningful emotional and psychological responses, enhancing human well-being and happiness in ways that resemble traditional human interactions. AI-driven social bots are always available, energetic, patient, adaptive, and responsive to our needs. In this regard, they seem to offer much more to our potential happiness than our best friends and families do.

However, they are social bots and must remain as such. We must not confuse them with what the human others meant to Ricoeur or with what they meant in the Harvard study.

This because the experiences they elicit are not real, and they are not objects of moral considerations (receiving real care, justice, and sympathy). In our view, being an object of moral considerations is a necessary condition in promoting genuine human happiness and well-being.

paragraphs.en: The study of happiness is a broad field. In our paper, we turn to the French philosopher Paul Ricoeur to address an aspect of happiness that links to authentic human connections, friendships, and community building.

paragraphs.cn: 利科在人类能力领域以及人们如何理解自身、他人与其所处的世界方面尤具影响力。他将幸福与不幸和机缘联系起来，同时强调幸福的人际关系本质，从而推进了我们对幸福的理解。他关于幸福的含义提出了三个相互关联的主张。
paragraphs.en: Ricoeur was particularly influential in the field of human capability and how people understand themselves, others and their world. He advanced our understanding of happiness by connecting it to unhappiness and chance, but also by emphasising the human relational nature of happiness. He makes three interrelated claims on what happiness means.

paragraphs.cn: 第一，幸福反映的是个体对圆满人生与个人能动性的追求。然而，利科提醒我们，人类存在于塑造并约束其幸福追求的复杂社会系统之中。因此，我们无法仅凭个人努力轻易获得幸福。这引出了第二条线索。
paragraphs.en: First, happiness reflects the individual’s desire for a fulfilled life and personal agency. Yet, Ricoeur warns that human beings exist within complex social systems that shape and constrain their pursuit of happiness. So, we can’t easily secure happiness through individual effort alone. This leads to the second thread.

paragraphs.cn: 第二，幸福不再是一种私人抱负，而是通过给予与接受而生。其脆弱性正在于它的共享性——这种共享建立友谊，驱散孤独，加深满足感。但这不仅仅关乎我们与亲近之人共享的纽带。
paragraphs.en: Second, happiness is no longer a private aspiration but emerges through giving and receiving. Its fragility lies in its shared character, which builds friendships to dispel loneliness and deepen fulfilment. But this is not just about the bonds we share with those who are close to us.

paragraphs.cn: 利科补充了第三条线索，将远离我们的人也纳入其中。他主张，幸福与个体的私人追求以及他人在其中所扮演的促成或阻碍角色相关。「他人」既包括有面孔的人——朋友与挚爱——也包括无面孔的、遥远的陌生人。
paragraphs.en: Ricoeur adds a third thread to include those distant from us. He argues that happiness is linked to an individual’s private pursuits and the role others play in enabling or frustrating them. “Others” includes those with faces – friends and loved ones – and faceless, distant strangers.

paragraphs.cn: 因此，幸福可能位于自我之中，可能位于亲密关系之中，也可能存在于与更广泛社区的关系之中。
paragraphs.en: Happiness, then, may be located within the self, in intimate relationships, or in relations with the wider community.

paragraphs.cn: 利科对幸福概念的阐述，与一项众所周知的研究相呼应，该研究发现：牢固的社区纽带有助于人们活得更长久、更幸福。
paragraphs.en: Ricoeur’s account of the concept of happiness reflects a well known study that found that strong community ties help people live longer and happier lives.

paragraphs.cn: 这项研究利用了近 80 年的数据，来自 268 名学生的人生经历，他们于 1938 年从哈佛大学（Harvard University）宿舍搬入学生公寓。研究表明，亲密的关系最能预测寿命、健康与生活满意度。这些纽带能抵御不满情绪，延缓身体与认知衰退。相比财富或地位，它们是幸福与福祉更可靠的预测因素。
paragraphs.en: The study draws on nearly 80 years of data from the lived experiences of 268 students who moved from Harvard University dorms to residential houses in 1938. The research shows that close relationships best predict longevity, health, and life satisfaction. Such ties protect against discontent, and delay physical and cognitive decline. They’re more reliable predictors of well-being and happiness than wealth or status.

paragraphs.cn: 然而，数字化与 AI 的兴起，如今使「在促进个人幸福的过程中，谁与什么可被算作『他人』」变得复杂起来。
paragraphs.en: However, the rise of digitalisation and AI now complicates who and what may count as “others” in the promotion of our individual happiness.

paragraphs.cn: 根据一项关于 AI 陪伴如何发展的研究，68% 的 AI 聊天机器人用户将这些工具视为「某种程度上」或「完全」像人，90% 认为聊天机器人具有智能，78% 认为聊天机器人有同理心，75% 则认为它们有意识。
paragraphs.en: According to a study on how AI companionship develops, 68% of AI chatbot users perceive these tools as “somewhat” or “fully” humanlike, 90% believe chatbots are intelligent, 78% believe chatbots are empathetic, and 75% believe they’re conscious.

paragraphs.cn: AI 正被用于回答问题、探寻人类兴趣，在生活的诸多领域塑造着一种新的对话方式。与之相伴，「友谊」的观念也正转向包含人机关系的方向。
paragraphs.en: AI is being used to answer questions and probe human interests, shaping a new kind of dialogue in many spheres of life. With it, ideas of friendships are shifting to involve human-technology relations.

paragraphs.cn: 传统上，一个人生命中的「他人」都是人类主体。关于人机关系的新兴研究对这一假设提出了挑战。这些研究涵盖从运动伴侣到性亲密的诸多方面，迫使我们重新思考何为「他者」。
paragraphs.en: Traditionally, the “others” in a person’s life have been human subjects. Emerging scholarship on human-technology relations challenges this assumption. Ranging from sport companions to sexual intimacy, these studies compel us to reconsider what counts as the other.

paragraphs.cn: 诸如 Replika 之类的技术如今在某些人的生活中占据了「他者」的角色。这款人机伴侣聊天机器人的口号是「陪你过日子的 AI 朋友」，截至撰写本文时，它在全球拥有超过 4200 万用户。Replika 旨在为感到孤独的人培养陪伴与友谊。用户创建一个化身，作为其数字伴侣。
paragraphs.en: Technologies like Replika now occupy the role of the “other” in some people’s lives. This human-companion chatbot with the motto “the AI friend to do life with” has over 42 million global users at the time of writing. Replika is designed to foster companionship and friendship among those who feel lonely. Users create an avatar that becomes their digital companion.

paragraphs.cn: 像 AI 驱动的社交机器人这类具有社会颠覆性的技术，会扭曲我们传统的社会规范、关系以及我们看待世界的方式。它们之所以被认为具有颠覆性，一个原因在于它们不可预测，并不断挑战我们的世界观。从历史上看，技术并非道德主体。然而如今，它们在我们的生活中扮演着道德主体与道德客体的角色。
paragraphs.en: Socially disruptive technologies like AI-driven social robots are designs that distort our traditional social norms, relations, and the way we see the world. One reason they’re considered disruptive is that they are unpredictable and continually challenge our worldviews. Historically, technologies were not moral agents. Today, however, they play the roles of moral subjects and objects in our lives.

paragraphs.cn: 例如，在日本，蛰居（hikikomori）现象——一种人类社交退缩的状态——正愈演愈烈，超过 150 万人转而依恋虚拟伴侣，而非其他真人。
paragraphs.en: For example, in Japan the hikikomori phenomenon, a state of human social reclusiveness, is gaining momentum, with over 1.5 million individuals becoming attached to virtual companions instead of other people.

paragraphs.cn: 据报道，约 3700 人通过 Gatebox 申请与名为初音未来（Hatsune Miku）的全息影像结婚。其中一段婚姻已经登记。在宗教场合中，社交机器人还作为宗教领袖服务于信众群体。
paragraphs.en: An estimated 3,700 individuals have reportedly applied for marriage certificates through Gatebox with a holograph called Hatsune Miku. One marriage has already been registered. In some religious settings, social robots serve as religious leaders to a community of believers.

paragraphs.cn: 这些技术颠覆了友谊与关系等传统概念，也颠覆了「为人类福祉与繁荣做出贡献」的含义。
paragraphs.en: These technologies have disrupted traditional concepts such as friendships and relationships, and what it means to contribute towards human well-being and flourishing.

paragraphs.cn: 在我们的研究中，我们承认这些技术能够促进人类繁荣与幸福，但从利科所谓「他人」的角度来看，它们并不能做到这一点。
paragraphs.en: In our study we acknowledge that these technologies can foster human flourishing and happiness, but not from the standpoint of Ricoeur’s “others”.

paragraphs.cn: 它们无法满足人类他者性的标准。这些技术：
paragraphs.en: They fail to satisfy the criteria for human otherness. The technologies:

paragraphs.cn: 只是模拟我们与它们共享的体验
paragraphs.en: only mimic the experiences we share with them

paragraphs.cn: 并非出于自身「意志」而行动，我们无法让它们对任何道德或法律行为承担责任
paragraphs.en: do not act out of their own “will”, and we cannot hold them responsible for any moral or legal action

paragraphs.cn: 没有属于它们自己的故事与经历。
paragraphs.en: do not have stories and experiences of their own.

paragraphs.cn: 社交机器人虽然缺乏感受性（即感受痛苦或快乐的能力），却能引发有意义的情感与心理回应，以类似于传统人际互动的方式增进人类的福祉与幸福。AI 驱动的社交机器人始终在线、精力充沛、耐心、自适应，并对我们的需求做出回应。就此而言，它们似乎比我们最好的朋友和家人更能为我们潜在的幸福提供帮助。
paragraphs.en: Social robots, though lacking sentience (the ability to feel pain or pleasure), can elicit meaningful emotional and psychological responses, enhancing human well-being and happiness in ways that resemble traditional human interactions. AI-driven social bots are always available, energetic, patient, adaptive, and responsive to our needs. In this regard, they seem to offer much more to our potential happiness than our best friends and families do.

paragraphs.cn: 然而，它们终究是社交机器人，也必须保持如此。我们绝不能把它们与利科语境中人类「他人」的含义，或与哈佛研究中他人所意味的相混淆。
paragraphs.en: However, they are social bots and must remain as such. We must not confuse them with what the human others meant to Ricoeur or with what they meant in the Harvard study.

paragraphs.cn: 这是因为它们所引发的体验并非真实的，它们也不是道德考量的对象（即无法获得真正的关怀、公正与同情）。在我们看来，成为道德考量的对象，是促进真正的人类幸福与福祉的必要条件。
paragraphs.en: This because the experiences they elicit are not real, and they are not objects of moral considerations (receiving real care, justice, and sympathy). In our view, being an object of moral considerations is a necessary condition in promoting genuine human happiness and well-being.

articles.title: 港口船闸
articles.author: AI Parable (inspired by Amanda Askell)
articles.summary: 罗尔丹把新船的图纸拍在港务长桌上。「六舱快船，满帆时速能把横渡时间砍到一半。我借了一千金币，下个月交船。」玛拉没抬头。「横渡五小时，船闸一小时。你知道这条航线的总时间怎么算吗？」
articles.content_cn:
罗尔丹把新船的图纸拍在港务长桌上。「六舱快船，满帆时速能把横渡时间砍到一半。我借了一千金币，下个月交船。」玛拉没抬头。「横渡五小时，船闸一小时。你知道这条航线的总时间怎么算吗？」

「六小时一程，船快一倍，自然三小时。」「你砍的是五小时里的那一半，不是我这一小时。新船跑得再快，过船闸还是要一艘一艘地过。横渡两小时半，加闸一小时，三小时半。你省下的是两个半钟头，不是三个。」

罗尔丹的声音低下去。他算过账：一千金币的债，要靠每天多跑一程来还。他原以为船快一倍，一程就变两程的产量。「那我再造第二艘快船呢？两艘并行，横渡不就更快了？」

「闸口只有一道。」玛拉终于抬眼，指了指窗外那道凿在悬崖里的窄口。「悬崖是祖辈留下的，凿不开，也加不了第二道。你在海上可以放一百条船，可它们都得在这一道闸前排队，一条过完才轮下一条。」

「所以哪怕我把横渡缩到一瞬间……」「总也缩不到零。你最快也不过把六小时压到一小时；横渡再短，也要在闸前等满那一小时。横渡可以加速，过闸不能。你投在横渡上的每一枚金币，越往后越买不到等量的时间。」

罗尔丹收起图纸。一千金币的债还在那里，可预期的回报已经少了一截。他望着那道石闸，忽然明白自己该把船卖掉，去雇石匠——可石匠也凿不动那悬崖。「那这债，我拿什么还？」「靠认清这条线在哪里。横渡是你的，闸不是。」

注解：此即阿姆达尔定律（Amdahl's law）——系统整体加速受限于被优化部分的实际时间占比，不可优化的串行部分为整体封顶；上限为 1/(1-p)，越接近串行瓶颈，再投入资源收益越小。
articles.content_en:
Roldan slapped the new ship's drawings onto the harbor master's desk. "Six holds, a fast clipper; at full sail it cuts the crossing time in half. I borrowed a thousand gold pieces, and the boat is delivered next month." Mara did not look up. "Five hours for the crossing, one hour for the lock. Do you know how the total time on this route is actually reckoned?"

"Six hours a run. The ship is twice as fast, so naturally three hours." "You're cutting half of the five hours, not my one hour. No matter how fast the new boat runs, it still has to pass the lock one hull at a time. Two and a half hours crossing, plus one hour at the lock, three and a half hours. What you save is two and a half hours, not three."

Roldan's voice dropped. He had done the books: the thousand-gold debt could only be repaid by squeezing an extra run out of each day. He had assumed that a ship twice as fast would turn one run into the yield of two. "Then I'll build a second fast ship. Two running side by side, and the crossing gets even faster, doesn't it?"

"There is only one lock gate." Mara finally raised her eyes and pointed out the window at the narrow gap cut into the cliff. "The cliff was left by our ancestors; it can't be cut wider, and a second gate can't be added. You can put a hundred boats on the open water, but every one of them has to queue at this single gate, one passing through before the next can follow."

"So even if I shrank the crossing to a single instant..." "It would never shrink to nothing. At best you compress the six hours down to one hour; however brief the crossing, you still wait out that full hour at the lock. The crossing can be sped up, the lock cannot. Every gold piece you spend on the crossing buys less time, the closer you get to the lock."

Roldan gathered up the drawings. The thousand-gold debt was still there, but the expected return had already shrunk by a slice. He stared at the stone lock, and for a moment understood that he ought to sell the boat and hire stonemasons instead, yet even stonemasons could not chip through that cliff. "Then what do I use to repay this debt?" "By seeing clearly where this line falls. The crossing is yours, the lock is not."

Note: This is Amdahl's law (阿姆达尔定律). The overall speedup of a system is bounded by the fraction of time the optimized part is actually used; the unoptimizable serial portion caps the whole. The ceiling is 1/(1-p), and the closer one gets to the serial bottleneck, the less return each further investment yields.

articles.title: 镜中钥匙
articles.author: AI Parable (inspired by Amanda Askell)
articles.summary: 黎明时分，右手执锉的那个孪生兄弟坐在牢房里，那双磨过钥匙的手静止不动。他哥哥的钥匙转开了锁，他的没有。贵族给了他到正午的期限。
articles.content_cn:
黎明时分，右手执锉的那个孪生兄弟坐在牢房里，那双磨过钥匙的手静止不动。他哥哥的钥匙转开了锁，他的没有。贵族给了他到正午的期限。

他们从出生起就是镜像孪生：一个惯用左手，一个惯用右手，同一张脸互为反转。长大成人，无论力量、才智还是手艺，没有任何考验能分辨他俩，一样高，一样的嗓音，在老锁匠手下做学徒时一样快。

贵族的要求是这样：给一只四十年没人打开过的保险箱配一把主钥匙。他怀疑有人偷过里面的东西，于是兄弟俩各接一单，同一块铁坯，同一张蜡模拓出的尺寸。开得了锁的拿金子，开不了的背上窃贼的罪名。

兄弟俩用同样的方法磨钥匙，照着蜡模上同样的槽深一道道锉下来。可一只从左往右移动的手，锉出的槽口旋向一边；一只从右往左移动的手，锉出的是它的镜像。这不是谁的选择，手本身就是这样长的。

试锁那天，左手的钥匙滑进去，转了。右手的钥匙滑进去，卡死，同一块铁，同样的分量，同样的槽深，一个开了，一个没开。他试着把钥匙翻过来，转个方向，从每个角度塞进去。锁不收它。

如今左手那个站在牢门外，手里攥着金子，也知道弟弟那把钥匙是诚实的，它与自己这把互为镜像，一样精确，一样真。他可以折断自己的钥匙，对贵族说两把都没开，弟弟就能活。他也可以带着金子和真相走开，让正午的钟响。

注解：这里讲的是手性（chirality），一个物体若无法仅凭旋转与平移与其镜像重合，便是手性的；两把钥匙互为对映体，普通性质全同，却只有与锁（另一个手性对象）相遇时，才显出一个能开、一个不能。
articles.content_en:
At dawn the right-handed twin sat in the cell, the hands that had ground the key lying still. His brother's key had turned the lock; his had not. The nobleman had given him until noon.

They had been mirror twins from birth: one left-handed, one right-handed, the same face reversed. Growing up, no test of strength, wit, or craft could tell them apart, the same height, the same voice, the same speed under the old locksmith's hand.

The nobleman's demand was this: cut a master key for a strongbox no one had opened in forty years. Suspecting theft, he hired both brothers, same iron blank, same measurements lifted from the same wax impression. Gold to the key that turned; the brand of thief to the key that didn't.

Each brother ground his key by the same method, filing the same notch depths from the same wax. But a hand that moves left-to-right across the file cuts a groove curling one way; a hand that moves right-to-left cuts its mirror. They did not choose this, it was in the hand itself.

On the day of the trial the left-handed key slid in and turned. The right-handed key slid in and stopped dead, same iron, same weight, same notch depths, yet one opened and one didn't. He tried flipping the key, rotating it, feeding it from every angle. The lock would not take it.

Now the left-handed brother stood outside the cell, holding his gold and knowing his twin's key had been honest, the perfect mirror of his own, just as precise, just as true. He could snap his own key, tell the nobleman neither had worked, and his brother would live. Or he could walk away with the gold and the truth, and let the noon bell ring.

Note: The concept here is chirality, an object is chiral if it cannot be brought into coincidence with its mirror image by rotations and translations alone; the two keys are enantiomorphs, identical in ordinary properties, yet distinguished only when one meets the lock, another chiral object.
