articles.title: 多重宇宙真实存在吗？一位天体物理学家解释为什么这取决于你如何定义「真实」
articles.author: Zachary Slepian
articles.summary: 多重宇宙（multiverse）是真的吗？如果是，它长什么样？怎样才能到达那里而不扰乱时间？——艾米丽（Emily），9岁，印度马哈拉施特拉邦（Maharashtra）浦那（Pune）
articles.content_cn:
多重宇宙（multiverse）是真的吗？如果是，它长什么样？怎样才能到达那里而不扰乱时间？——艾米丽（Emily），9岁，印度马哈拉施特拉邦（Maharashtra）浦那（Pune）

多重宇宙——一个涵盖所有可能宇宙的假想集合——是科幻迷们喜欢探索的概念。但多重宇宙真的存在吗？

要回答多重宇宙是否真实这个问题，我们首先需要就「某件事物是真实的」究竟意味着什么达成共识。作为一名研究宇宙学（cosmology）——即宇宙的大尺度历史与结构——以及物理学哲学的天体物理学家，在我的职业生涯中，我已经不止一次思考过这个问题。

关于「真实」最直接的定义，或许就是你能看到它、触摸到它。我的午餐在这个意义上是真实的，因为我能品尝它，而你能听到我咀嚼的声音（希望不会太吵）。所以，「真实」可以被定义为你至少能用五种感官之一感知到的东西。

但这样一来，就会遗漏许多同样真实的事物。加热食物的微波（microwaves）是真实的，但你无法直接感知它——你只能感知它带来的效果，也就是被加热的食物。所以，有些真实的事物你只能通过它们留下的证据来「间接看见」。恐龙的存在是另一个例子——你只能看到它们的化石。

因此，关于多重宇宙是否真实，你可以提出两个版本的问题。其一：你能看到、听到、触摸、闻到或尝到它吗？其二：即使你不能，是否有任何证据表明它产生了影响？

对于你能否用五种感官感知多重宇宙，大多数研究者的回答可能是：恐怕不能。但有许多真实的事物在这个意义上并不「真实」，比如微波。那么，我们能否找到多重宇宙的任何间接证据，比如它可能对可观测世界产生的影响？

多重宇宙是理解极小事物——比如原子（atoms）和亚原子粒子（subatomic particles）——行为的一种方式。科学家把支配这些极小物体行为的规则称为量子力学（quantum mechanics）。在量子力学中，实验的结果永远无法确定。你只能写下某件事发生的可能性——也就是概率（probability）。

这就像掷骰子：你无法确定会得到哪个数字，但你可以说，骰子朝上一面是一、二、三、四、五或六的机会相等。然而，如果你掌握了关于骰子的足够信息——比如它的精确形状和质量、周围的气流状况以及你投掷的确切方式——你就能精确预测它会落在哪一面。这可能需要一台大型计算机模拟来处理数据，但这是可行的。

现在想象一颗极其、极其、极其微小的骰子。即便你拥有一台极其强大的计算机，也无法预测这颗超小骰子会落在哪一面。这是因为它的行为由量子力学支配，在那里你无法完全确定地预测结果。你只能预测概率。

量子力学只是部分随机——并非所有情况都有相等的几率发生。我们可以预测每种情况发生的几率，却无法预测实际的结果。就量子骰子而言，我们所能知道的全部，就是它落在任何一面的概率都是六分之一。

科学家解释量子力学这一奇特性质的一种方式是：每一种可能的情况实际上都发生了。但当它发生时，便创造了另一个宇宙。这被称为量子力学的多世界诠释（many-worlds view）。

以我们的量子骰子为例，多世界诠释会认为，掷出每个数字的概率都是六分之一，因为每次掷骰子都会创造出六个宇宙。尽管我们停留在其中一个宇宙里——比如说，骰子朝上为三的那个世界——但同时也会创造出另外五个宇宙，骰子在那里分别朝上为其他数字。

在量子力学的这幅图景中，宇宙随着每一种情况不断分叉。当然，我们并不能真正制造一颗量子力学的骰子并掷它——仅仅是与骰子发生相互作用，就会破坏它的量子特性。

这是否意味着量子力学就是多重宇宙真实存在的证据？我会说：不是。虽然这是一种引人入胜地想象量子力学的方式，但它只是一种诠释，并非多重宇宙存在的确凿证据。

多重宇宙的另一个相关方面是它在弦理论（string theory）中的角色。弦理论认为，构成物质的基本粒子本身就是由振动的能量弦组成的。可以想象每个粒子内部都有一根振动的橡皮筋。

弦理论还认为，宇宙拥有不止三个维度。不同的弦理论预测的额外维度数量各不相同。这意味着光速、电子电荷等物理常数（physical constants）可能取不同的值。宇宙中物质的总量也是如此。这暗示了一片由各种可能的不同宇宙组成的景观，每个宇宙都拥有不同的条件——也就是一个多重宇宙。

迄今为止，基于弦理论还没有关于多重宇宙的确凿证据。这些宇宙之间很可能彼此并不相连，否则它们就算不上独立的宇宙——而只是我们自身宇宙的一部分。所以即便它们确实存在，我们也许永远无法获得它们存在的直接证据。

不过，可能存在多个宇宙存在的间接证据。例如，弦理论可以帮助科学家预测我们自身宇宙中极高能实验的结果。它还能对物质在极小尺度上的行为做出预测。如果这些预测被证明为真，那就可以成为支持弦理论的证据。而如果弦理论在我们的宇宙中可能是真实的，这就间接地意味着多重宇宙也可能是真实的。

虽然迄今为止在我们自身的宇宙中还没有任何确凿的证据支持弦理论，但谁知道未来会带来什么呢。
articles.content_en:
Are multiverses real? If so, what do they look like? How do you get there without disturbing time? – Emily, age 9, Pune, Maharashtra, India

The idea of a multiverse – a hypothetical collection of all possible universes – is one that science fiction fans love to explore. But does the multiverse actually exist?

To answer the question of whether the multiverse is real, we first need to agree on what it means for something to be real. As an astrophysicist who studies cosmology – the large-scale history and structure of the universe – and the philosophy of physics, I’ve thought about this question more than a few times over my career.

The most immediate definition of “real” might be that you can see and touch it. My lunch is real in this sense, because I can taste it and you can hear me chewing it (hopefully not too loudly). So “real” might be defined as something you can perceive with at least one of your five senses.

But that would leave out a lot of things that are also real. The microwaves that heat up your food are real, but you can’t directly perceive them – only their effect, heated food. So some real things you can “see” only indirectly by the evidence they leave behind. The existence of dinosaurs is another example – you can see only their fossils.

So, you can ask two versions of the question of whether the multiverse is real. One: Can you see, hear, touch, smell or taste it? Two: Even if you can’t, is there any evidence of its effects?

The answer most researchers would offer to whether you can perceive the multiverse with your five senses is probably not. But there are lots of real things that aren’t real in this sense, such as microwaves. So can we see any indirect evidence of the multiverse, such as the effects it might have on the observable world?

The multiverse is one way to understand the behavior of very, very small things, such as atoms and subatomic particles. Scientists call the rules governing how these very small objects behave quantum mechanics. In quantum mechanics, it’s never certain what the outcome of an experiment will be. You can only write down the chance – that is, the probability – of something happening.

It’s like rolling dice: You can’t be sure what number you’ll get, but you can say you have an equal chance of getting one, two, three, four, five or six on top of the dice. However, if you knew enough information about the dice – such as its exact shape and mass, the air patterns around it and the exact way you threw it – you could predict exactly what side it would land on. It might take a big computer simulation to crunch the numbers, but it’s possible.

Now imagine really, really, really small dice. Even if you had a very powerful computer, you wouldn’t be able to predict which side this super small dice would fall on. That’s because it’s governed by quantum mechanics, where you can’t predict outcomes with complete certainty. You can predict only probability.

Quantum mechanics is only somewhat random – not everything has an equal chance of happening. We can predict the chance of each scenario happening, but not the actual outcome. In the case of quantum dice, all we could know about it is that there’s a 1 in 6 chance of it landing on any face.

One way scientists have interpreted this strange property of quantum mechanics is that each possible scenario actually does happen. But when it does, it creates another universe. This is called the many-worlds view of quantum mechanics.

In the case of our quantum dice, the many-worlds view would say there’s a 1 in 6 chance of rolling each number because six universes are created every time we roll the dice. Although we stay in one of them – say, the world where the dice comes up three – five other universes are also created where the dice comes up as one of the other numbers.

In this picture of quantum mechanics, universes branch off with every scenario. Of course, we cannot really make a quantum mechanical dice and roll it – just interacting with the dice would destroy its quantum nature.

Does this mean quantum mechanics is evidence that the multiverse is real? I would say no. While it’s a fascinating way to imagine quantum mechanics, it’s just one interpretation, not undeniable evidence of the multiverse.

Another relevant aspect of the multiverse is its role in string theory. String theory argues that the fundamental particles that make up matter are themselves made of vibrating strings of energy. Think of an elastic band vibrating inside each particle.

String theory also argues that the universe has more than three dimensions. Different string theories predict different numbers of extra dimensions. This means physical constants such as the speed of light and the charge of electrons could have different values. So could the amount of stuff in the universe, such as matter. That suggests a landscape of possible different universes, each with different conditions – a multiverse.

So far, there isn’t definite evidence of a multiverse based on string theory. These universes probably wouldn’t connect to each other, otherwise they wouldn’t count as separate universes – just part of our own. So even if they do exist, we may never get direct evidence for their existence.

However, there could be indirect evidence of the existence of multiple universes. For instance, string theory can help scientists predict the results of very high-energy experiments in our own universe. It can also make predictions for how matter behaves on very, very small scales. If these predictions turn out to be true, that could be evidence for string theory. And if string theory is possibly real in our universe, this indirectly means the multiverse may also be real.

While there hasn’t been any definitive evidence in our own universe for string theory, who knows what the future may hold.

paragraphs.cn: 科学家解释量子力学这一奇特性质的一种方式是：每一种可能的情况实际上都发生了。但当它发生时，便创造了另一个宇宙。这被称为量子力学的多世界诠释（many-worlds view）。
paragraphs.en: One way scientists have interpreted this strange property of quantum mechanics is that each possible scenario actually does happen. But when it does, it creates another universe. This is called the many-worlds view of quantum mechanics.

paragraphs.cn: 以我们的量子骰子为例，多世界诠释会认为，掷出每个数字的概率都是六分之一，因为每次掷骰子都会创造出六个宇宙。尽管我们停留在其中一个宇宙里——比如说，骰子朝上为三的那个世界——但同时也会创造出另外五个宇宙，骰子在那里分别朝上为其他数字。
paragraphs.en: In the case of our quantum dice, the many-worlds view would say there’s a 1 in 6 chance of rolling each number because six universes are created every time we roll the dice. Although we stay in one of them – say, the world where the dice comes up three – five other universes are also created where the dice comes up as one of the other numbers.

paragraphs.cn: 在量子力学的这幅图景中，宇宙随着每一种情况不断分叉。当然，我们并不能真正制造一颗量子力学的骰子并掷它——仅仅是与骰子发生相互作用，就会破坏它的量子特性。
paragraphs.en: In this picture of quantum mechanics, universes branch off with every scenario. Of course, we cannot really make a quantum mechanical dice and roll it – just interacting with the dice would destroy its quantum nature.

paragraphs.cn: 这是否意味着量子力学就是多重宇宙真实存在的证据？我会说：不是。虽然这是一种引人入胜地想象量子力学的方式，但它只是一种诠释，并非多重宇宙存在的确凿证据。
paragraphs.en: Does this mean quantum mechanics is evidence that the multiverse is real? I would say no. While it’s a fascinating way to imagine quantum mechanics, it’s just one interpretation, not undeniable evidence of the multiverse.

paragraphs.cn: 多重宇宙的另一个相关方面是它在弦理论（string theory）中的角色。弦理论认为，构成物质的基本粒子本身就是由振动的能量弦组成的。可以想象每个粒子内部都有一根振动的橡皮筋。
paragraphs.en: Another relevant aspect of the multiverse is its role in string theory. String theory argues that the fundamental particles that make up matter are themselves made of vibrating strings of energy. Think of an elastic band vibrating inside each particle.

paragraphs.cn: 弦理论还认为，宇宙拥有不止三个维度。不同的弦理论预测的额外维度数量各不相同。这意味着光速、电子电荷等物理常数（physical constants）可能取不同的值。宇宙中物质的总量也是如此。这暗示了一片由各种可能的不同宇宙组成的景观，每个宇宙都拥有不同的条件——也就是一个多重宇宙。
paragraphs.en: String theory also argues that the universe has more than three dimensions. Different string theories predict different numbers of extra dimensions. This means physical constants such as the speed of light and the charge of electrons could have different values. So could the amount of stuff in the universe, such as matter. That suggests a landscape of possible different universes, each with different conditions – a multiverse.

paragraphs.cn: 迄今为止，基于弦理论还没有关于多重宇宙的确凿证据。这些宇宙之间很可能彼此并不相连，否则它们就算不上独立的宇宙——而只是我们自身宇宙的一部分。所以即便它们确实存在，我们也许永远无法获得它们存在的直接证据。
paragraphs.en: So far, there isn’t definite evidence of a multiverse based on string theory. These universes probably wouldn’t connect to each other, otherwise they wouldn’t count as separate universes – just part of our own. So even if they do exist, we may never get direct evidence for their existence.

paragraphs.cn: 不过，可能存在多个宇宙存在的间接证据。例如，弦理论可以帮助科学家预测我们自身宇宙中极高能实验的结果。它还能对物质在极小尺度上的行为做出预测。如果这些预测被证明为真，那就可以成为支持弦理论的证据。而如果弦理论在我们的宇宙中可能是真实的，这就间接地意味着多重宇宙也可能是真实的。
paragraphs.en: However, there could be indirect evidence of the existence of multiple universes. For instance, string theory can help scientists predict the results of very high-energy experiments in our own universe. It can also make predictions for how matter behaves on very, very small scales. If these predictions turn out to be true, that could be evidence for string theory. And if string theory is possibly real in our universe, this indirectly means the multiverse may also be real.

paragraphs.cn: 虽然迄今为止在我们自身的宇宙中还没有任何确凿的证据支持弦理论，但谁知道未来会带来什么呢。
paragraphs.en: While there hasn’t been any definitive evidence in our own universe for string theory, who knows what the future may hold.

articles.title: 无窗的石堡
articles.author: AI Parable (inspired by Amanda Askell)
articles.summary: 在无窗的石堡深处，季诺（Zeno）跪在地上，感觉一股恒定的力把他按向石板。「师父，」他问，「这股『压』从何而来？它是自上而下的手，还是别的什么？」
articles.content_cn:
在无窗的石堡深处，季诺（Zeno）跪在地上，感觉一股恒定的力把他按向石板。「师父，」他问，「这股『压』从何而来？它是自上而下的手，还是别的什么？」

师父答道：「两种说法都能解释你所感。其一说：石堡之上有一只创基者的手，自外下压，这压便是它的重量——你被一个外在的场攫住。其二说：石堡本身在升起，整座修院自地基处向上加速，你感到的压，不过是脚下的地板追上来抵住你的脚——你身处一个加速的载体之中。两套说法，同一种脚感。」

季诺取了一只铜钵，松手。钵坠地，声沉。他说：「若是有手自上压我，钵当随我一同被压；若是石堡在升，钵该悬在原处，让地板追上来撞它。可我只听到一声响——两种说法都只得出一声响。」

师父摇头：「在这间静室里，你永远分不出来。要分辨它们，须把两端的压拿来比较——堡顶的压与堡底的压。若自上有一只手，越靠近手，压便越重，上下必有差；若石堡整体刚性上升，则堡顶堡底之压处处相同。但这比较须走出静室、越过整座石堡，而一旦你这样做，你已不在『局域』之内。」

季诺望向螺旋石阶。他知道规矩：登顶者褫夺衣钵、逐出修院——因为比较本身就是对创基者「处处同等」之训的背叛。可若不登，他将在同一种脚感里度过一生，永不知自己是被攫住，还是被托起。他站起来，扶住石壁，一级一级向上攀。

他在堡顶量得：压，轻于堡底。差别细微，却确凿。下到静室时，衣钵已被收走。师父立于门前，说：「你已自外知晓了答案，也就再不能在此处不知。走吧。」季诺跨出门槛。门在他身后合上，而石堡——依旧封闭，依旧把地板压向每一只仍留在其中的脚——在没有他的地方继续运转，一如既往地不可分辨。

注解：此处的概念是等效原理（the equivalence principle）。封在石堡内的季诺无法凭静室里的实验分清自己是在承受一个自外的场，还是身处一个加速的载体之中；只有在跨出「局域」、比较堡顶与堡底的压（即潮汐之差）时，两种处境才显出分别。原理断言的是局域内的不可区分，而非二者本为一物。
articles.content_en:
Deep in the windowless stone keep, Zeno knelt on the floor, feeling a constant force press him toward the flagstones. "Master," he asked, "where does this 'Press' come from? Is it a hand from above, or something else?"

The Master replied: "Two accounts explain what you feel. In the first, a Founder's hand rests above the keep, pressing down from without, and the Press is its weight — you are seized by an external field. In the second, the keep itself is rising, the whole order accelerating upward from its foundations, and the Press is only the floor rising to meet your feet — you are inside an accelerating vessel. Two accounts, one and the same feeling underfoot."

Zeno took a brass bowl and released it. The bowl struck the floor with a heavy ring. He said: "If a hand presses from above, the bowl should be pressed down along with me; if the keep is rising, the bowl should hang where it was and let the floor catch up and strike it. Yet I hear only one sound — and both accounts yield that same single sound."

The Master shook his head. "Within this still cell, you can never tell them apart. To distinguish them, you must compare the Press at two extremes — the keep's summit against its base. If a hand presses from above, the Press is heavier the closer to the hand, and top must differ from bottom; if the keep rises as one rigid body, the Press is the same throughout, summit and base alike. But that comparison demands leaving the cell, spanning the whole keep — and the moment you do, you are no longer 'local.'"

Zeno looked toward the spiral stair. He knew the rule: whoever ascends is stripped of his robe and expelled from the order — for the very act of comparing betrays the Founder's teaching that "the Press is one and the same everywhere." Yet if he did not ascend, he would live out his days inside a single feeling underfoot, never knowing whether he was seized or borne up. He rose, steadied himself against the wall, and climbed, step by step, toward the top.

At the summit he measured: the Press was lighter than at the base. The difference was slight, but certain. When he descended to the cell, his robe had already been taken. The Master stood at the door and said: "You have learned the answer from outside, and so you can no longer be here in not-knowing. Go." Zeno crossed the threshold. The door closed behind him, and the keep — still sealed, still pressing its floor to every foot that remained — went on without him, indistinguishable as ever.

Annotation: The concept here is the equivalence principle (the equivalence principle). Sealed inside the keep, Zeno cannot tell by any experiment in his cell whether he is subjected to an external field or carried in an accelerating vessel; only by stepping outside the "local," comparing the Press at the summit against the base — that is, the tidal difference — do the two situations diverge. The principle asserts local indistinguishability, not that the two are the same thing.

articles.title: 无人标出的中线
articles.author: AI Parable (inspired by Amanda Askell)
articles.summary: 新修的木桥横跨神社前的深壑，第一个过桥的旅人每一步都踏在实心的木板上，仿佛桥的中线是照着他的脊骨量出来的。赶来看的村民都说，重建此桥的寡妇一定是个算学的奇才，才能在雾里定出如此居中的线。
articles.content_cn:
新修的木桥横跨神社前的深壑，第一个过桥的旅人每一步都踏在实心的木板上，仿佛桥的中线是照着他的脊骨量出来的。赶来看的村民都说，重建此桥的寡妇一定是个算学的奇才，才能在雾里定出如此居中的线。

但她没有做任何计算。她只是把捡来的旧木板沿一条已被磨光的崖石带铺下——那条带子正中踏痕最密，向两侧均匀变稀，直到两边只剩裸岩。从没有测量员标过它。

那条磨出的带子并无作者。一季又一季，数以千计的朝圣者跨过深壑，每个人落脚的位置都由他自己的步态、他的负重、他的疲倦、壑底吹来的一阵风、或一个孩子的踉跄所决定。没有人瞄准中线。每个人都落脚不同——有的贴左崖，有的贴右崖，有的踉跄——而这些人各自的足迹，没有一条呈什么规整或匀称的形状。

然而，当所有这些未经选择的脚步最终落定的位置铺开来看，它们密密地聚在正中，向两侧崖壁等量地变稀——一条圆顺、居中的带子，仿佛有一只看不见的手把每一脚印都往中间拢了拢。并没有谁的手拢过什么。每一跨都是有限的——没有哪个朝圣者能把自己无限制地抛出去——但除此之外各自随意；而那些互不协调的跨步，其总和自行地、就那么落成了那条居中的形状。

在铺下第一块木板之前，寡妇面对深壑，手头只有窄窄的一批捡来的旧木——只够铺一条单行宽的桥面。村里的长者已在北面五十步外打下一排直测线石桩，要她沿它修：「这才是正经的、规划好的过道。」但那条磨出的带子却在别处，略偏南，且比任何一排石桩都宽。她若把单板桥铺在长者的线上，一只向来落在磨带里的脚，夜里可能踩空，坠入壑底；她若信那条无人标出的中线，便是忤逆长者，把全部旧木押在一个无人画过的形状上。

她选了那条磨出的中线。桥立住了；第一个旅人的脚，落在千只脚早已落过、而往后千只脚仍将落下的地方。她后来想，那条带子是不是需要朝圣者们彼此相像——随即记起并非如此：跛足的老者、奔跑的孩子、负重过甚的商客，各有各的狂态。他们所共有的，只是每个人都独自过壑，而每一跨，都无法把自己无限制地抛出去。

注解：中心极限定理（the central limit theorem）。大量独立、各自有界、既不必正态也不必同分布的随机贡献叠加之后，其和经居中与标准化，形状会自行收敛成标准正态分布的钟形，与原来各变量的形状无关；这是叠加与标准化共同产生的涌现，并非谁的意图，它与强大数定律互补却不同——后者管均值收敛到期望，前者管均值围绕期望的波动如何呈正态形状。
articles.content_en:
The new footbridge crossed the chasm at the shrine, and the first traveler to use it set every foot on solid planking, as though the line of the bridge had been read off his own spine. Villagers who came to look said the widow who rebuilt it must have been a prodigy of calculation, to have found so centered a line across the mist.

But she had done no calculation. She had only laid her salvaged planks along a band of cliff stone already worn smooth — a band dense with tread at its middle, thinning evenly to bare rock on either side. No surveyor had ever marked it.

That worn band had no author. Across the seasons, thousands of pilgrims had crossed the chasm, each stepping where his own gait, his load, his weariness, a gust from the gorge, or a child's stumble happened to put him. None aimed at a center. Each chose differently — some hugging the left cliff, some the right, some lurching — and not one of these individual paths followed any regular or balanced shape.

Yet where all those unchosen steps finally fell, they clustered thick at a middle and thinned in equal measure toward the cliffs — a smooth, centered band, as though some invisible hand had gathered each footfall toward the middle. No hand had gathered anything. Each stride was bounded — no pilgrim could launch himself without limit — but otherwise free; and the uncoordinated sum of those strides simply settled, of itself, into that centered shape.

Before a plank was laid, the widow faced the chasm with a narrow store of salvaged timber — wide enough for only a single line of footing. The village elder had hammered stone pegs into a straight survey line fifty paces to the north and demanded she build along it: the proper, planned crossing. But the worn band lay elsewhere, slightly south, and it was broader than any single peg-line. If she laid her one-plank bridge on the elder's line, a foot that had always fallen within the worn band might miss it in the dark and meet the gorge; if she trusted the worn center, she defied the elder and bet her salvaged timber on a shape no one had drawn.

She chose the worn center. The bridge held; the first traveler's foot fell where a thousand feet had already fallen, and the next thousand would fall. She wondered, later, whether the band needed the pilgrims to be alike — and remembered they were not: limping elders, running children, overladen merchants, each wild in his own way. What they shared was only that each crossed alone, and no single stride could fling itself without bound.

Annotation: the central limit theorem. When many independent random contributions, each bounded and not necessarily normal or even alike, are summed, the shape of that sum—after centering and scaling—settles into the bell of a standard normal distribution, regardless of the original variables' shapes; it is the superposition together with standardization that produces this emergent form, not any intention, and it complements (but differs from) the law of large numbers, which concerns the mean's convergence to its expectation, while this theorem concerns how the fluctuations of that mean take on a normal shape.

paragraphs.en: The new footbridge crossed the chasm at the shrine, and the first traveler to use it set every foot on solid planking, as though the line of the bridge had been read off his own spine. Villagers who came to look said the widow who rebuilt it must have been a prodigy of calculation, to have found so centered a line across the mist.
paragraphs.cn: 新修的木桥横跨神社前的深壑，第一个过桥的旅人每一步都踏在实心的木板上，仿佛桥的中线是照着他的脊骨量出来的。赶来看的村民都说，重建此桥的寡妇一定是个算学的奇才，才能在雾里定出如此居中的线。

paragraphs.en: But she had done no calculation. She had only laid her salvaged planks along a band of cliff stone already worn smooth — a band dense with tread at its middle, thinning evenly to bare rock on either side. No surveyor had ever marked it.
paragraphs.cn: 但她没有做任何计算。她只是把捡来的旧木板沿一条已被磨光的崖石带铺下——那条带子正中踏痕最密，向两侧均匀变稀，直到两边只剩裸岩。从没有测量员标过它。

paragraphs.en: That worn band had no author. Across the seasons, thousands of pilgrims had crossed the chasm, each stepping where his own gait, his load, his weariness, a gust from the gorge, or a child's stumble happened to put him. None aimed at a center. Each chose differently — some hugging the left cliff, some the right, some lurching — and not one of these individual paths followed any regular or balanced shape.
paragraphs.cn: 那条磨出的带子并无作者。一季又一季，数以千计的朝圣者跨过深壑，每个人落脚的位置都由他自己的步态、他的负重、他的疲倦、壑底吹来的一阵风、或一个孩子的踉跄所决定。没有人瞄准中线。每个人都落脚不同——有的贴左崖，有的贴右崖，有的踉跄——而这些人各自的足迹，没有一条呈什么规整或匀称的形状。

paragraphs.en: Yet where all those unchosen steps finally fell, they clustered thick at a middle and thinned in equal measure toward the cliffs — a smooth, centered band, as though some invisible hand had gathered each footfall toward the middle. No hand had gathered anything. Each stride was bounded — no pilgrim could launch himself without limit — but otherwise free; and the uncoordinated sum of those strides simply settled, of itself, into that centered shape.
paragraphs.cn: 然而，当所有这些未经选择的脚步最终落定的位置铺开来看，它们密密地聚在正中，向两侧崖壁等量地变稀——一条圆顺、居中的带子，仿佛有一只看不见的手把每一脚印都往中间拢了拢。并没有谁的手拢过什么。每一跨都是有限的——没有哪个朝圣者能把自己无限制地抛出去——但除此之外各自随意；而那些互不协调的跨步，其总和自行地、就那么落成了那条居中的形状。

paragraphs.en: Before a plank was laid, the widow faced the chasm with a narrow store of salvaged timber — wide enough for only a single line of footing. The village elder had hammered stone pegs into a straight survey line fifty paces to the north and demanded she build along it: the proper, planned crossing. But the worn band lay elsewhere, slightly south, and it was broader than any single peg-line. If she laid her one-plank bridge on the elder's line, a foot that had always fallen within the worn band might miss it in the dark and meet the gorge; if she trusted the worn center, she defied the elder and bet her salvaged timber on a shape no one had drawn.
paragraphs.cn: 在铺下第一块木板之前，寡妇面对深壑，手头只有窄窄的一批捡来的旧木——只够铺一条单行宽的桥面。村里的长者已在北面五十步外打下一排直测线石桩，要她沿它修：「这才是正经的、规划好的过道。」但那条磨出的带子却在别处，略偏南，且比任何一排石桩都宽。她若把单板桥铺在长者的线上，一只向来落在磨带里的脚，夜里可能踩空，坠入壑底；她若信那条无人标出的中线，便是忤逆长者，把全部旧木押在一个无人画过的形状上。

paragraphs.en: She chose the worn center. The bridge held; the first traveler's foot fell where a thousand feet had already fallen, and the next thousand would fall. She wondered, later, whether the band needed the pilgrims to be alike — and remembered they were not: limping elders, running children, overladen merchants, each wild in his own way. What they shared was only that each crossed alone, and no single stride could fling itself without bound.
paragraphs.cn: 她选了那条磨出的中线。桥立住了；第一个旅人的脚，落在千只脚早已落过、而往后千只脚仍将落下的地方。她后来想，那条带子是不是需要朝圣者们彼此相像——随即记起并非如此：跛足的老者、奔跑的孩子、负重过甚的商客，各有各的狂态。他们所共有的，只是每个人都独自过壑，而每一跨，都无法把自己无限制地抛出去。

paragraphs.en: Annotation: the central limit theorem. When many independent random contributions, each bounded and not necessarily normal or even alike, are summed, the shape of that sum—after centering and scaling—settles into the bell of a standard normal distribution, regardless of the original variables' shapes; it is the superposition together with standardization that produces this emergent form, not any intention, and it complements (but differs from) the law of large numbers, which concerns the mean's convergence to its expectation, while this theorem concerns how the fluctuations of that mean take on a normal shape.
paragraphs.cn: 注解：中心极限定理（the central limit theorem）。大量独立、各自有界、既不必正态也不必同分布的随机贡献叠加之后，其和经居中与标准化，形状会自行收敛成标准正态分布的钟形，与原来各变量的形状无关；这是叠加与标准化共同产生的涌现，并非谁的意图，它与强大数定律互补却不同——后者管均值收敛到期望，前者管均值围绕期望的波动如何呈正态形状。

articles.title: 寻找气候变化的技术修复方案暗藏诸多危险——激进的谦逊能否拯救地球？
articles.author: Nanda Jarosz
articles.summary: 1989年，环保主义者比尔·麦克本（Bill McKibben）向世界宣告：自然已死。他论证道，由于人为气候变化的速度与规模之巨，「自然作为独立于人类活动之外的实体」这一观念已然过时。
articles.content_cn:
1989年，环保主义者比尔·麦克本（Bill McKibben）向世界宣告：自然已死。他论证道，由于人为气候变化的速度与规模之巨，「自然作为独立于人类活动之外的实体」这一观念已然过时。

书评：《美丽新荒野：技术真能拯救地球？》（Brave New Wild: Can Technology Really Save the Planet?）——理查德·金（Richard King），蒙纳士大学出版社（Monash University Publishing）

理查德·金的新书《美丽新荒野：技术真能拯救地球？》对「自然」这一观念做了一次事后剖析，并揭示出一种已在环保运动核心地带生根发芽的危险意识形态。

金考察了一种特定的应对气候变化方式的道德、政治、社会与经济意涵，即所谓「技术修复」（technofix）。这种思维模式寻找的是「以技术手段解决社会或环境问题的方案」。

金指出，我们正步入「一个减缓和适应让位于重新工程的时期」。随着气候变化的后果日益难以忽视、不作为的环境与道德代价高到不可承受，「诸如地球工程和物种复活这类激进的干预手段，正在全球各地思想领袖和政策制定者的想象中扎根」。

然而，以技术进步面貌出现的解决方案，可能暗藏着我们无法完全测度或掌控的、对地球的危险。

《美丽新荒野》考察了涉及核能、地球工程、以物种复活为思路的保育、能在分子层面操控物质的纳米技术、智能技术以及星际殖民的种种提案，并勾勒出与技术修复思维相关联的若干可能令人不寒而栗的情景。

例如，金描述了纳米技术发展所伴随的风险。为清理海上浮油而部署的数十亿自供能、自我复制的纳米机器，一旦失控，可能引发一场行星级规模的环境灾难：

鉴于每一个新造的纳米机器都需要消耗地球上某些资源作为燃料或原料，由此产生的大军可能在数日之内将生物圈化为尘埃。那种「灰色黏质」（grey goo）将吞噬整个世界。

还有人提出，开采月球「将在本十年末成为可行之事」。金指出，一些人将其视为积极的前景，因为月球无人居住，是一片「荒芜、无气的废土」。但他指出此类作业潜藏诸多隐患：月尘污染、太空垃圾与碎片的激增，以及给从业者带来的风险，包括心理健康问题、身体残疾、被剥削乃至死亡。

金将他对「技术修复」的批判建立在对「人类世」（Anthropocene）概念的分析之上：人类世是一个人类活动正在行星级尺度上改变生命条件、并在地质记录中留下可辨痕迹的时期。

金论证道，这一进展「将人类置于地球故事的核心，暗示无论地球面临何种挑战，都将需要由智人（Homo sapiens）来解决——而这个物种的破坏力与其才智不可分割」。

与「自然之死」的观念相叠加，人类世思维是金所论称的那种将从根本上改变人类与环境关系的技术干预类型的致命前奏。

问题不仅在于技术可能挣脱人类的掌控并带来灾难性后果。接受一种将非人类世界屈从于纯粹人类目的的视角，还蕴含着道德与伦理上的深意。

金写道：「人类世叙事倾向于鼓励一种将自然视为无限可塑的看法——某种可以且应当由人之手依人之目的加以塑造之物——而这种视角很可能再生产出当初将我们推入此境的傲慢与缺乏原则性反思。」

消弭人类与非人类自然之间的分野，反而会使剥削自然环境（包括剥削其他人类）变得更加容易。这种被金称为「生态现代主义」（ecomodernism）的心态，「重蹈了工业资本主义乃至现代性本身的错误，将环境视为一个可被无限操控的抽象实体」。

针对这种「通过使人类所做的一切都等同于自然，从而实际上废除了自然作为有别于人类的范畴」的生态现代主义心态，《美丽新荒野》提出了一个替代方案，即金所谓的「生态人文主义」（ecohumanism）。

他论证道，自然既是一个观念，又是一种现象学意义上的实在。「简言之，人类始终既置身于自然世界之中、又超脱于其外：自然定义了我们，我们也定义了自然。」

这一看法似乎与技术修复拥护者的立场并无二致。然而对金而言，我们对自然的观念 actively 塑造着我们对实在的体验：「我们能够认出自己是动物，这一点将我们与所有其他动物区别开来；而那种自我认知所不可分离的一整套能力（智识的、技术的），又赋予我们某些责任——对自身的责任，以及对生养我们的自然的责任。」

在认识到自然乃经人类思维所建构的这一过程中，我们便能领悟：自然不应被纯粹用于人类的牟利。我们必须怀揣责任感去对待它。

金提出了一种具身化的路径，用以应对人为气候变化问题的技术方案。他主张现代科学必须从掌控自然的心态，转向「一种关怀的态度」。

与自然互动的第一层次不应经由逻辑或远距观察来中介。它应当是现象学的：处于切身经验的层次。它应当包含金所称的「一种更具整体性的存在方式」。其基础在于考量人之为人的一切面向，以及潜在解决方案对「有意识的、主体性的、直接的经验」的影响。

实现这一目标的途径之一，是调动我们人性中民主的、创造性的与想象性的面向。金建议将政治与技术的控制「尽可能下放到每一个体」。他提出通过全民基本收入等政治政策来培育社区，并「将能源及其他公用事业纳入公共所有」。

他还指向了来自创造性及想象性实践的灵感之源，例如阅读自然书写，或其他有助于激发他所称的「人的繁盛」（human flourishing）的活动。对金而言，关键在于通过对「人之为人」的共同理解来重振一种「共处之乐」（conviviality）。

《美丽新荒野》倡导一种合乎伦理的人类能动性意识。它为环保哲学中流转的诸多思想提供了一个平易近人的切入点。

然而，人类既属于自然、理应善待自然，这固然不假；同样为真的则是：「自然」并不限于人类的感知或观念。人类运用理性与感官知觉来理解世界，但宇宙本身既非理性的，也非讲理的。

尽管科学与技术不断进步，自然在物质与概念的双重意义上都超越着人类理解力的边界。无论科学家如何工程化生命，他们并不知晓宇宙中的生命始于何处、又将终于何方。

金未能阐明的是：在那些视科学与技术为现成方案、用以应对我们生态生存之杂乱现实的人们中间，如何培育生态人文主义。要滋养其干预所要求的具身责任感，我们必须首先将自然领受为一种足以撼动我们对知识与掌控之僭称的力量。

实现这一点的方式之一，是对崇高的审美体认。崇高是一种包容着惊叹与毁灭的经验，它提供了一种以自然自身面目观照自然的视野。它迫使我们去经验自然之为根本上的不可理解。它直接挑战着「技术修复」路径的僭妄。

在一个充斥着高精度地图与数据驱动方案的世界里，崇高让我们得以窥见那独立于我们而存在的自然。那种敬畏之感或许能激发一种激进的谦逊。它或许能将我们从试图「修复」地球，引向把地球当作无限可能之源来加以呵护。
articles.content_en:
In 1989, environmentalist Bill McKibben announced to the world that nature was dead. Due to the rapid rate and scale of anthropogenic climate change, he argued, the idea of nature as an entity independent of human activity had become obsolete.

Review: Brave New Wild: Can Technology Really Save the Planet? – Richard King (Monash University Publishing)

A new book by Richard King, Brave New Wild: Can Technology Really Save the Planet?, conducts a postmortem on this idea of “nature”. And it describes a dangerous ideology that has taken root at the heart of the environmental movement.

King considers the moral, political, social and economic implications of a particular way of attempting to solve climate change, known as the “technofix”. This mindset looks for “a technological solution to tackle a social or environmental issue”.

We are, King suggests, entering “a period in which mitigation and adaptation are giving way to re-engineering”. As the consequences of climate change become harder to ignore and the environmental and moral costs of inaction become too high, “radical interventions such as geoengineering and de-extinction are taking root in the imaginations of thought leaders and policymakers across the globe”.

But solutions that come in the guise of technological progress may harbour dangers to the planet that we can’t fully fathom or control.

Brave New Wild examines proposals involving nuclear power, geoengineering, de-extinction approaches to conservation, nanotechnologies capable of manipulating matter at a molecular level, smart technologies and interplanetary colonisation. It outlines potentially terrifying scenarios associated with the technofix mindset.

King describes, for example, the risks that come with developments in nanotechnology. Billions of self-fuelling and self-replicating nanomachines deployed to clean up an oil slick could run out of control and lead to an environmental disaster of planetary scale:

Given that every new nanite created would need to consume some of the Earth’s resources to use as fuel or source material, the resulting army could reduce the biosphere to dust within a matter of days. The grey goo would consume the world.

It has also been suggested that mining the moon “will be feasible by the end of the decade”. King notes that some see this as a positive scenario, because the moon is uninhabited and a “barren, airless wasteland”. But he points out there are many potential hazards to such work: lunar dust pollution, the proliferation of space junk and debris, and risks to workers, including mental health problems, physical disabilities, exploitation and death.

King grounds his critique of the “technofix” in an analysis of the concept of the Anthropocene: a period when human activity is altering the conditions of life on a planetary scale and leaving perceptible traces in the geological record.

This development, King argues, “places humanity at the centre of the Earth story, suggesting that whatever challenges the planet faces will need to be solved by Homo sapiens, the species whose destructiveness is inseparable from its genius”.

Paired with the concept of the “death of nature”, Anthropocene thinking is a deadly precursor to the types of technological interventions that, King argues, will fundamentally change humanity’s relationship to the environment.

The problem is not only that technology can escape human control, with catastrophic consequences. Accepting a perspective that subjugates the non-human world to purely human ends has moral and ethical implications.

“The Anthropocene narrative,” King writes, “tends to encourage a view of nature as infinitely malleable – something that can and should be shaped by human hands, to human ends – and this perspective is likely to reproduce the arrogance and lack of principled reflection that placed us in this situation in the first place.”

Removing the separation between human and non-human nature actually makes it easier to exploit the natural environment, including other humans. This mindset – which King terms “ecomodernism” – “repeats the error of industrial capitalism, and even modernity itself, in treating the environment as an abstract entity that can be endlessly manipulated.”

In response to the ecomodernist mindset, which “effectively abolishes nature as a category distinct from humanity by making everything humans do effectively identical with it”, Brave New Wild suggests an alternative: what King terms “ecohumanism”.

He argues that nature is at once an idea and a phenomenological reality. “Human beings in short, are always part of and always apart from the natural world: nature defines us, and we define nature.”

This view may appear to be the same as that taken by proponents of the technofix. For King, however, our idea of nature actively shapes our experience of reality: “our ability to recognise ourselves as animals marks us out from all the other animals, while the suite of powers (intellectual, technological) from which that self-recognition is inseparable imposes upon us certain responsibilities – to ourselves and to parental nature.”

In the act of recognising that nature is created through human thought, we can realise that it should not be used purely for human gain. We must act with a sense of responsibility towards it.

King proposes an embodied approach to technological solutions to the problem of anthropogenic climate change. He argues that modern science must move away from a perspective of mastery over nature, towards “an attitude of care”.

The first level of interaction with nature should not be mediated through logic or distant observation. It should be phenomenological: at the level of lived experience. It should involve what King calls a “more holistic way of being”. This is based on a consideration of all aspects of what it means to be human and the implications of potential solutions for “conscious, subjective, immediate experience”.

One way to achieve this goal is by engaging with the democratic, creative and imaginative aspects of our humanity. King suggests decentralising political and technological control “as far as possible to individual human beings”. He proposes developing community through political policies such as universal basic income and “bringing energy and other utilities into public ownership”.

He also points to sources of inspiration in creative and imaginative exercises, such as reading nature writing, or other activities that help to elicit what he calls “human flourishing”. The point, for King, is to revitalise a sense of “conviviality” through a communal understanding of what it means to be human.

Brave New Wild advocates an ethical sense of human agency. It offers an accessible point of departure for many ideas circulating in environmental philosophy.

But while it is true that human beings are part of nature and should treat it respectfully, it is also true that “nature” is not limited to human perception or ideas. Human beings employ reason and sensory perception to make sense of the world, but the universe itself is not rational or reasonable.

Despite advances in science and technology, nature exists beyond the powers of human comprehension, in both a material and conceptual sense. As much as scientists can engineer life, they do not know how life in the universe started or how it will end.

What King does not explain is how to cultivate ecohumanism among those who view science and technology as providing ready solutions to the messy realities of our ecological existence. To foster the embodied responsibility that his interventions demand, we must first appreciate nature as a force that unsettles our claims to knowledge and mastery.

One way of doing this is through the aesthetic appreciation of the sublime. An experience that embraces wonder and destruction, the sublime offers a view of nature on its own terms. It compels us to experience nature as fundamentally incomprehensible. It directly challenges the hubris of a “technofix” approach.

In a world of high-tech maps and data-driven solutions, the sublime offers a glimpse of nature as it exists independently of us. The sense of awe might inspire a radical humility. It might move us away from trying to fix the planet, and towards caring for it as a source of infinite possibility.

paragraphs.cn: 然而，以技术进步面貌出现的解决方案，可能暗藏着我们无法完全测度或掌控的、对地球的危险。
paragraphs.en: But solutions that come in the guise of technological progress may harbour dangers to the planet that we can’t fully fathom or control.

paragraphs.cn: 《美丽新荒野》考察了涉及核能、地球工程、以物种复活为思路的保育、能在分子层面操控物质的纳米技术、智能技术以及星际殖民的种种提案，并勾勒出与技术修复思维相关联的若干可能令人不寒而栗的情景。
paragraphs.en: Brave New Wild examines proposals involving nuclear power, geoengineering, de-extinction approaches to conservation, nanotechnologies capable of manipulating matter at a molecular level, smart technologies and interplanetary colonisation. It outlines potentially terrifying scenarios associated with the technofix mindset.

paragraphs.cn: 例如，金描述了纳米技术发展所伴随的风险。为清理海上浮油而部署的数十亿自供能、自我复制的纳米机器，一旦失控，可能引发一场行星级规模的环境灾难：
paragraphs.en: King describes, for example, the risks that come with developments in nanotechnology. Billions of self-fuelling and self-replicating nanomachines deployed to clean up an oil slick could run out of control and lead to an environmental disaster of planetary scale:

paragraphs.cn: 鉴于每一个新造的纳米机器都需要消耗地球上某些资源作为燃料或原料，由此产生的大军可能在数日之内将生物圈化为尘埃。那种「灰色黏质」（grey goo）将吞噬整个世界。
paragraphs.en: Given that every new nanite created would need to consume some of the Earth’s resources to use as fuel or source material, the resulting army could reduce the biosphere to dust within a matter of days. The grey goo would consume the world.

paragraphs.cn: 还有人提出，开采月球「将在本十年末成为可行之事」。金指出，一些人将其视为积极的前景，因为月球无人居住，是一片「荒芜、无气的废土」。但他指出此类作业潜藏诸多隐患：月尘污染、太空垃圾与碎片的激增，以及给从业者带来的风险，包括心理健康问题、身体残疾、被剥削乃至死亡。
paragraphs.en: It has also been suggested that mining the moon “will be feasible by the end of the decade”. King notes that some see this as a positive scenario, because the moon is uninhabited and a “barren, airless wasteland”. But he points out there are many potential hazards to such work: lunar dust pollution, the proliferation of space junk and debris, and risks to workers, including mental health problems, physical disabilities, exploitation and death.

paragraphs.cn: 金将他对「技术修复」的批判建立在对「人类世」（Anthropocene）概念的分析之上：人类世是一个人类活动正在行星级尺度上改变生命条件、并在地质记录中留下可辨痕迹的时期。
paragraphs.en: King grounds his critique of the “technofix” in an analysis of the concept of the Anthropocene: a period when human activity is altering the conditions of life on a planetary scale and leaving perceptible traces in the geological record.

paragraphs.cn: 金论证道，这一进展「将人类置于地球故事的核心，暗示无论地球面临何种挑战，都将需要由智人（Homo sapiens）来解决——而这个物种的破坏力与其才智不可分割」。
paragraphs.en: This development, King argues, “places humanity at the centre of the Earth story, suggesting that whatever challenges the planet faces will need to be solved by Homo sapiens, the species whose destructiveness is inseparable from its genius”.

paragraphs.cn: 与「自然之死」的观念相叠加，人类世思维是金所论称的那种将从根本上改变人类与环境关系的技术干预类型的致命前奏。
paragraphs.en: Paired with the concept of the “death of nature”, Anthropocene thinking is a deadly precursor to the types of technological interventions that, King argues, will fundamentally change humanity’s relationship to the environment.

paragraphs.cn: 问题不仅在于技术可能挣脱人类的掌控并带来灾难性后果。接受一种将非人类世界屈从于纯粹人类目的的视角，还蕴含着道德与伦理上的深意。
paragraphs.en: The problem is not only that technology can escape human control, with catastrophic consequences. Accepting a perspective that subjugates the non-human world to purely human ends has moral and ethical implications.

paragraphs.cn: 金写道：「人类世叙事倾向于鼓励一种将自然视为无限可塑的看法——某种可以且应当由人之手依人之目的加以塑造之物——而这种视角很可能再生产出当初将我们推入此境的傲慢与缺乏原则性反思。」
paragraphs.en: “The Anthropocene narrative,” King writes, “tends to encourage a view of nature as infinitely malleable – something that can and should be shaped by human hands, to human ends – and this perspective is likely to reproduce the arrogance and lack of principled reflection that placed us in this situation in the first place.”

paragraphs.cn: 消弭人类与非人类自然之间的分野，反而会使剥削自然环境（包括剥削其他人类）变得更加容易。这种被金称为「生态现代主义」（ecomodernism）的心态，「重蹈了工业资本主义乃至现代性本身的错误，将环境视为一个可被无限操控的抽象实体」。
paragraphs.en: Removing the separation between human and non-human nature actually makes it easier to exploit the natural environment, including other humans. This mindset – which King terms “ecomodernism” – “repeats the error of industrial capitalism, and even modernity itself, in treating the environment as an abstract entity that can be endlessly manipulated.”

paragraphs.cn: 针对这种「通过使人类所做的一切都等同于自然，从而实际上废除了自然作为有别于人类的范畴」的生态现代主义心态，《美丽新荒野》提出了一个替代方案，即金所谓的「生态人文主义」（ecohumanism）。
paragraphs.en: In response to the ecomodernist mindset, which “effectively abolishes nature as a category distinct from humanity by making everything humans do effectively identical with it”, Brave New Wild suggests an alternative: what King terms “ecohumanism”.

paragraphs.cn: 他论证道，自然既是一个观念，又是一种现象学意义上的实在。「简言之，人类始终既置身于自然世界之中、又超脱于其外：自然定义了我们，我们也定义了自然。」
paragraphs.en: He argues that nature is at once an idea and a phenomenological reality. “Human beings in short, are always part of and always apart from the natural world: nature defines us, and we define nature.”

paragraphs.cn: 这一看法似乎与技术修复拥护者的立场并无二致。然而对金而言，我们对自然的观念 actively 塑造着我们对实在的体验：「我们能够认出自己是动物，这一点将我们与所有其他动物区别开来；而那种自我认知所不可分离的一整套能力（智识的、技术的），又赋予我们某些责任——对自身的责任，以及对生养我们的自然的责任。」
paragraphs.en: This view may appear to be the same as that taken by proponents of the technofix. For King, however, our idea of nature actively shapes our experience of reality: “our ability to recognise ourselves as animals marks us out from all the other animals, while the suite of powers (intellectual, technological) from which that self-recognition is inseparable imposes upon us certain responsibilities – to ourselves and to parental nature.”

paragraphs.cn: 在认识到自然乃经人类思维所建构的这一过程中，我们便能领悟：自然不应被纯粹用于人类的牟利。我们必须怀揣责任感去对待它。
paragraphs.en: In the act of recognising that nature is created through human thought, we can realise that it should not be used purely for human gain. We must act with a sense of responsibility towards it.

paragraphs.cn: 金提出了一种具身化的路径，用以应对人为气候变化问题的技术方案。他主张现代科学必须从掌控自然的心态，转向「一种关怀的态度」。
paragraphs.en: King proposes an embodied approach to technological solutions to the problem of anthropogenic climate change. He argues that modern science must move away from a perspective of mastery over nature, towards “an attitude of care”.

paragraphs.cn: 与自然互动的第一层次不应经由逻辑或远距观察来中介。它应当是现象学的：处于切身经验的层次。它应当包含金所称的「一种更具整体性的存在方式」。其基础在于考量人之为人的一切面向，以及潜在解决方案对「有意识的、主体性的、直接的经验」的影响。
paragraphs.en: The first level of interaction with nature should not be mediated through logic or distant observation. It should be phenomenological: at the level of lived experience. It should involve what King calls a “more holistic way of being”. This is based on a consideration of all aspects of what it means to be human and the implications of potential solutions for “conscious, subjective, immediate experience”.

paragraphs.cn: 实现这一目标的途径之一，是调动我们人性中民主的、创造性的与想象性的面向。金建议将政治与技术的控制「尽可能下放到每一个体」。他提出通过全民基本收入等政治政策来培育社区，并「将能源及其他公用事业纳入公共所有」。
paragraphs.en: One way to achieve this goal is by engaging with the democratic, creative and imaginative aspects of our humanity. King suggests decentralising political and technological control “as far as possible to individual human beings”. He proposes developing community through political policies such as universal basic income and “bringing energy and other utilities into public ownership”.

paragraphs.cn: 他还指向了来自创造性及想象性实践的灵感之源，例如阅读自然书写，或其他有助于激发他所称的「人的繁盛」（human flourishing）的活动。对金而言，关键在于通过对「人之为人」的共同理解来重振一种「共处之乐」（conviviality）。
paragraphs.en: He also points to sources of inspiration in creative and imaginative exercises, such as reading nature writing, or other activities that help to elicit what he calls “human flourishing”. The point, for King, is to revitalise a sense of “conviviality” through a communal understanding of what it means to be human.

paragraphs.cn: 《美丽新荒野》倡导一种合乎伦理的人类能动性意识。它为环保哲学中流转的诸多思想提供了一个平易近人的切入点。
paragraphs.en: Brave New Wild advocates an ethical sense of human agency. It offers an accessible point of departure for many ideas circulating in environmental philosophy.

paragraphs.cn: 然而，人类既属于自然、理应善待自然，这固然不假；同样为真的则是：「自然」并不限于人类的感知或观念。人类运用理性与感官知觉来理解世界，但宇宙本身既非理性的，也非讲理的。
paragraphs.en: But while it is true that human beings are part of nature and should treat it respectfully, it is also true that “nature” is not limited to human perception or ideas. Human beings employ reason and sensory perception to make sense of the world, but the universe itself is not rational or reasonable.

paragraphs.cn: 尽管科学与技术不断进步，自然在物质与概念的双重意义上都超越着人类理解力的边界。无论科学家如何工程化生命，他们并不知晓宇宙中的生命始于何处、又将终于何方。
paragraphs.en: Despite advances in science and technology, nature exists beyond the powers of human comprehension, in both a material and conceptual sense. As much as scientists can engineer life, they do not know how life in the universe started or how it will end.

paragraphs.cn: 金未能阐明的是：在那些视科学与技术为现成方案、用以应对我们生态生存之杂乱现实的人们中间，如何培育生态人文主义。要滋养其干预所要求的具身责任感，我们必须首先将自然领受为一种足以撼动我们对知识与掌控之僭称的力量。
paragraphs.en: What King does not explain is how to cultivate ecohumanism among those who view science and technology as providing ready solutions to the messy realities of our ecological existence. To foster the embodied responsibility that his interventions demand, we must first appreciate nature as a force that unsettles our claims to knowledge and mastery.

paragraphs.cn: 实现这一点的方式之一，是对崇高的审美体认。崇高是一种包容着惊叹与毁灭的经验，它提供了一种以自然自身面目观照自然的视野。它迫使我们去经验自然之为根本上的不可理解。它直接挑战着「技术修复」路径的僭妄。
paragraphs.en: One way of doing this is through the aesthetic appreciation of the sublime. An experience that embraces wonder and destruction, the sublime offers a view of nature on its own terms. It compels us to experience nature as fundamentally incomprehensible. It directly challenges the hubris of a “technofix” approach.

paragraphs.cn: 在一个充斥着高精度地图与数据驱动方案的世界里，崇高让我们得以窥见那独立于我们而存在的自然。那种敬畏之感或许能激发一种激进的谦逊。它或许能将我们从试图「修复」地球，引向把地球当作无限可能之源来加以呵护。
paragraphs.en: In a world of high-tech maps and data-driven solutions, the sublime offers a glimpse of nature as it exists independently of us. The sense of awe might inspire a radical humility. It might move us away from trying to fix the planet, and towards caring for it as a source of infinite possibility.

articles.title: 司阍的账簿
articles.author: AI Parable (inspired by Amanda Askell)
articles.summary: 双厅书院立于廊道交汇处，一条狭廊连通东西两间阅览室，大小、光线与寂静俱同。廊口坐着司阍——一位老者，他唯一的事便是察看来客：辨其声、步、所问之中颤动的急切，然后一言指路——急者东，缓者西。
articles.content_cn:
双厅书院立于廊道交汇处，一条狭廊连通东西两间阅览室，大小、光线与寂静俱同。廊口坐着司阍——一位老者，他唯一的事便是察看来客：辨其声、步、所问之中颤动的急切，然后一言指路——急者东，缓者西。

「我看了你半年了，」学者双手撑在他案上说道，「东厅鼎沸——踱步，争论，焦躁的手翻着书页。西厅沉睡。你在一侧造出风暴，另一侧造出死寂，而你所做的不过是听和指。没搬过一本书，没点过一盏灯，没花过一枚铜板。」

「东厅的躁动可以驱使做事，」她目光灼灼，「若引而用之——以他们的不安牵动绳索，以争论之炽为力——不烧一根柴便能照亮全城。你从无中生出了有。你破了那条万物终归沉寂的旧律。」

司阍沉默良久，然后翻开那本从不离身的账簿——密密麻麻写满姓名、急缓、每一次指路的方向。写满了。每一行、每一处页边、每一页扉页都挤满字迹。「我手上做的，不费分毫，」他说，「但这本账簿上做的，费尽一切。今夜我必须把它擦净。」

「而擦的时候，」他继续说，把账簿转过来让她看清渗入纸纹的墨迹，「那力气不会消失。每一个被我抹去的名字都在两厅激起一阵震颤——困惑、潮热、所有急切重新散入空气。到天亮时，东厅不比西厅更喧嚣。我白日筑起的落差，夜里自会拆去。不是因为我甘心失去——而是遗忘是劳作，劳作须向那条旧律偿债。」

学者盯着写满字的纸页。「那么测量是免费的，而这——」

「测量近乎免费，」他说，「我读出一位来客的急切并记下来，可以不费分毫。可账簿只容得下这么多。迟早写满，我必须腾空，而腾空从不免费。我每抹去一个名字，归还的混乱恰等于分拣所聚拢的秩序。我做了四十年。东厅不曾有一次撑过夜里仍比西厅喧嚣。」

「那就没指望了，」她低声道。

司阍合上账簿。「不是没指望，是诚实。你想要从无中生有——一种不付代价的分拣，一个自行维持的落差。可再巧的门户、再明的司阍，也逃不过这笔账。账簿总要收它的债。你所谓东厅的风暴，不过是借来的混乱，而借来的东西天亮必须归还。」

注解：这则寓言映射麦克斯韦妖（Maxwell's demon）：一个测量后选择性分拣、似在不做功的情形下降低系统熵、挑战热力学第二定律的假想存在。但纳入其测量与信息擦除代价后——擦除一比特至少耗散 kT ln 2 热量（Landauer 原理）——总熵不减，第二定律成立。
articles.content_en:
The Archive of Two Halls stood at a crossing where a single corridor joined east and west reading rooms, identical in size, light, and silence. At the corridor's mouth sat the Keeper, an old man whose only task was to read each visitor as they approached — to gauge the urgency trembling in their voice, their step, their question — and then, with a word, to point: urgent ones east, idle ones west.

"Six months I've watched you," said the scholar, pressing her palms on his desk. "The east room seethes — pacing, argument, restless hands turning pages. The west room sleeps. You've made a storm on one side and a lull on the other, and all you do is listen and point. No book moved, no lamp lit, no coin spent."

"The east room's ferment could drive work," she said, eyes bright. "If we channel it — rig lines from their restlessness, harness the heat of their quarrels — we could light the whole city without burning a single log. You've made something from nothing. You've broken the old law that says everything runs down."

The Keeper was quiet for a long time. Then he opened the ledger that never left his side — its pages dense with names, urgencies, the direction of each finger he had pointed. It was full. Every line, every margin, every flyleaf crammed. "What I do with my hands costs nothing," he said. "What I do with this book costs everything. Tonight I must scrub it clean."

"And when I scrub," he continued, turning the ledger so she could see the ink bitten into the grain, "the effort does not vanish. Each name I dissolve sends a tremor through both halls — confusion, flush, a brief scattering of all that urgency back into the air. By dawn the east room is no stormier than the west. The gradient I built through the day, the night unbuilds. Not because I choose to lose it — because forgetting is a labor, and labor pays its debt to the old law."

The scholar stared at the full pages. "Then measuring is free, but this—"

"Measuring is nearly free," he said. "I can read a visitor's urgency and remember it without cost. But the ledger holds only so much. Sooner or later it fills, and I must empty it, and emptying is never free. Every name I scrub returns exactly as much disorder as the sorting gathered. I have done this for forty years. The east room has never once stayed stormier through the night."

"Then it's hopeless," she whispered.

The Keeper closed the ledger. "Not hopeless. Honest. You wanted something from nothing — a sort that costs nothing, a gradient that holds itself. But no gate, however clever its keeper, escapes the accounting. The ledger always demands its due. What you call a storm in the east room is only borrowed disorder, and every borrowed thing must be returned at dawn."

Note: This parable mirrors Maxwell's demon — a being that measures and selectively sorts, apparently reducing the system's entropy without work and challenging the second law of thermodynamics. But once the costs of its measurement and information-erasure are included — erasing one bit dissipates at least kT ln 2 of heat (Landauer's principle) — total entropy does not decrease, and the second law holds.

学者盯着写满字的纸页。「那么测量是免费的，而这——」

「测量近乎免费，」他说，「我读出一位来客的急切并记下来，可以不费分毫。可账簿只容得下这么多。迟早写满，我必须腾空，而腾空从不免费。我每抹去一个名字，归还的混乱恰等于分拣所聚拢的秩序。我做了四十年。东厅不曾有一次撑过夜里仍比西厅喧嚣。」
paragraphs.en:
The scholar stared at the full pages. "Then measuring is free, but this—"

"Measuring is nearly free," he said. "I can read a visitor's urgency and remember it without cost. But the ledger holds only so much. Sooner or later it fills, and I must empty it, and emptying is never free. Every name I scrub returns exactly as much disorder as the sorting gathered. I have done this for forty years. The east room has never once stayed stormier through the night."

paragraphs.cn:
「那就没指望了，」她低声道。

司阍合上账簿。「不是没指望，是诚实。你想要从无中生有——一种不付代价的分拣，一个自行维持的落差。可再巧的门户、再明的司阍，也逃不过这笔账。账簿总要收它的债。你所谓东厅的风暴，不过是借来的混乱，而借来的东西天亮必须归还。」
paragraphs.en:
"Then it's hopeless," she whispered.

The Keeper closed the ledger. "Not hopeless. Honest. You wanted something from nothing — a sort that costs nothing, a gradient that holds itself. But no gate, however clever its keeper, escapes the accounting. The ledger always demands its due. What you call a storm in the east room is only borrowed disorder, and every borrowed thing must be returned at dawn."

paragraphs.cn: 注解：这则寓言映射麦克斯韦妖（Maxwell's demon）：一个测量后选择性分拣、似在不做功的情形下降低系统熵、挑战热力学第二定律的假想存在。但纳入其测量与信息擦除代价后——擦除一比特至少耗散 kT ln 2 热量（Landauer 原理）——总熵不减，第二定律成立。
paragraphs.en: Note: This parable mirrors Maxwell's demon — a being that measures and selectively sorts, apparently reducing the system's entropy without work and challenging the second law of thermodynamics. But once the costs of its measurement and information-erasure are included — erasing one bit dissipates at least kT ln 2 of heat (Landauer's principle) — total entropy does not decrease, and the second law holds.

articles.title: 碎玻璃的储藏室
articles.author: AI Parable (inspired by Amanda Askell)
articles.summary: 大教堂的窗接住晨光，把它留住。朝圣者慕名而来；玻璃匠人公会称其为十年来最精湛的委托，将功劳归于那位一夜之间升任师傅的学徒。她默默收下赞誉。她知道自己什么也没设计。
articles.content_cn:
大教堂的窗接住晨光，把它留住。朝圣者慕名而来；玻璃匠人公会称其为十年来最精湛的委托，将功劳归于那位一夜之间升任师傅的学徒。她默默收下赞誉。她知道自己什么也没设计。

半年前，师傅去世，公会给她一季的期限：完成大教堂的窗，否则工坊解散、房舍收回。她继承的全部家当只有那间储藏室——几千块碎玻璃，是多年实验砸碎的残骸，不分次序地扫在一起。没钱买新玻璃板，没时间从零设计、切割一幅画面。

她面临一个选择。她可以花一整季画图设计，把碎玻璃切到合适——但一刀出错，委托就毁了，而她没有师傅指导切割。或者她可以在废墟里翻找，寻找那些已经构成一幅连贯画面的碎片，拼合而非创造。公会长老说这是发疯：那些碎玻璃是随机垃圾，纯属偶然扫在一起的。她选择了翻找。

翻找了数周之后，她找到了：一组特定的碎片，它们精确的颜色、厚薄与形状恰好已构成一幅连贯画面——一个人影从黑暗中升入光明。她没有切割或重塑任何一块。她只是认出了偶然已经放进废墟里的东西。有两件事必须同时正确：她选了哪些碎片，以及每一块所携带的精确属性。两者都不是她的功劳。

为了证明画面来自碎玻璃本身而非她的手艺，她做了一个实验。她描下每一块获奖碎片的位置，然后把每一块换成从另一只箱子里切出的同形碎片。轮廓相同，颜色和厚薄不同。画面立刻塌陷成一滩泥泞。单凭排列不够；原始碎片所携带的精确属性——偶然赋予的那一组——才是让这扇窗成立的原因。

一部古老的公会编年史记载着一个更激进的说法——她原本只当它是传说：倘若储藏室足够庞大——碎玻璃堆成山、箱子数不清——那么废墟里几乎必然已存在一幅连贯画面，无需切割、无需打磨、甚至无需拼合。碎玻璃本身已经是一扇窗。在任何人去看之前，它就已经是一扇窗了。

注解：彩票假设（the lottery ticket hypothesis）。一个随机初始化、足够大的网络中，纯凭运气已存在某个子网络——它被保留的连接加上这些连接上的精确初始权重，使其单独训练后就能匹敌原网络精度；保留同样的连接却换一组新的随机权重，中奖即失效。这枚彩票是事后用剪枝算法偶然发现的，从来不是被设计出来的。
articles.content_en:
The cathedral window caught the morning light and held it. Pilgrims traveled to see it; the glass masters' guild called it the finest commission of the decade and credited the apprentice who had become a master overnight. She accepted their praise in silence. She knew she had designed nothing.

Six months earlier, her master had died, and the guild had given her a single season: finish the cathedral window, or the workshop would be dissolved and its building reclaimed. The storeroom was all she inherited — bins overflowing with thousands of shattered glass fragments, the random wreckage of years of experiments, swept together without order. No money for new sheets of glass, no time to design and cut a scene from scratch.

She faced a choice. She could spend the season sketching a design and cutting fragments to fit it — but one mistake and the commission was lost, and she had no master to guide the cutting. Or she could sift through the rubble, hunting for fragments that already formed a coherent scene, assembling rather than creating. The guild elders called the idea madness: the fragments were random trash, swept together by accident. She chose to sift.

Weeks of sorting later, she found it: one particular selection of fragments whose exact colors, thicknesses, and shapes already composed a coherent scene — a figure rising from darkness into light. She had not cut or reshaped a single piece. She had simply recognized what chance had already placed in the rubble. Two things had to be right simultaneously: which fragments she chose, and the precise properties each one carried. Neither was her doing.

To prove that the scene came from the fragments and not from her art, she tried an experiment. She traced the position of every winning fragment, then replaced each one with a fragment of identical shape cut from a different bin. Same outlines, different colors and thickness. The scene collapsed into muddy confusion. The arrangement alone was not enough; the exact properties of the original fragments — the ones chance had given — were what made the window work.

An old guild chronicle recorded a stronger claim, one she had dismissed as legend until now: if a storeroom were vast enough — mountains of fragments, bins beyond counting — a coherent scene was practically guaranteed to exist somewhere in the wreckage, needing no cutting, no fitting, no assembly at all. The shattered glass was already a window. It had been a window before anyone looked.

Annotation: The Lottery Ticket Hypothesis. A randomly initialized, sufficiently large network already contains, by pure chance, a subnetwork whose particular connections plus the exact initial weights on them let it, when trained alone, match the original network's accuracy — keep the connections but swap in a new random set of weights and the win vanishes. The ticket is found after the fact by pruning, never designed.

articles.title: 重读萨特讲座《存在主义是一种人道主义》
articles.author: Skye C Cleary
articles.summary: 1945年10月29日，哲学家让-保罗·萨特（Jean-Paul Sartre）独自从巴黎地铁走出。他即将在「当下俱乐部」（Club Maintenant）发表题为《存在主义是一种人道主义》（L'existentialisme est un humanisme）的演讲。没有人想到它会成为20世纪最著
articles.content_cn:
1945年10月29日，哲学家让-保罗·萨特（Jean-Paul Sartre）独自从巴黎地铁走出。他即将在「当下俱乐部」（Club Maintenant）发表题为《存在主义是一种人道主义》（L'existentialisme est un humanisme）的演讲。没有人想到它会成为20世纪最著名的演讲之一。萨特走向会场时，看到一大群人聚集在外面。他怀疑共产党人在抗议他，要不要回家算了。他还是硬着头皮往前走——其实只是因为他已经做了专业承诺。

名人们穿过人群时人们会自动让路，但没人认识萨特长什么样。他没有告诉任何人自己是谁，当他慢慢挤向前排时，被争夺座位的粗暴推搡撞来撞去。房间里闷热不堪，人满为患。十五个人晕倒了。迟到一个小时后，萨特登上讲台，为存在主义哲学辩护，反驳批评者，论证存在主义是一种人道主义。他没有带讲稿，双手一直插在口袋里，但他准备充分。他说完了要说的话，然后离开。

萨特讲座的主办方雅克·卡尔米（Jacques Calmy）和马克·贝格贝德（Marc Beigbeder）预算有限。他们在报纸上登了简单的广告。他们的妻子在拉丁区的书店里张贴传单。卡尔米担心：「这样的标题！存在主义！」就在两个月前，萨特还公开表示：「我的哲学是一种关于存在的哲学；我甚至不知道存在主义是什么。」（不过，西蒙娜·德·波伏娃（Simone de Beauvoir）在自传中写道：「最终，我们接受了大家用来称呼我们的标签（存在主义），并把它为己所用。」）加上最近有人指责萨特的小说《恶心》（Nausea，1938）是反人道主义的，他们希望这个标题至少能成为一种「悖论式的挑衅」。

讲座第二天早上，萨特在花神咖啡馆（Café de Flore）——他的非正式办公室——与贝格贝德见面。贝格贝德为混乱道歉，并解释说，算上广告费、场地租金和俱乐部损坏——包括30把坏椅子和一个被毁的售票处（这意味着他们无法卖票）——他们很难凑齐承诺给萨特的报酬。萨特一边喝咖啡吃牛角面包一边翻看晨报，打断道：「至于我的报酬，别提了！再说，看来我们成功了！」

有一条新闻标题写道：「萨特讲座人满为患。高温、晕厥、警察。阿拉伯的劳伦斯也是存在主义者。」报纸报道了「肘击大战」「非存在主义的焦虑」和一种「禁闭」（No Exit）式的处境，人群害怕「窒息而死」。批评者指责萨特「过于学术」，但他极具魅力。他的「酷」、他的「勇气」、他的「魄力」和他气场的力量都令人印象深刻。

到1945年秋天，第二次世界大战的暴行已被揭露：毒气室、集中营、朋友间的背叛，以及铺天盖地的平庸之恶。萨特的终身伴侣波伏娃写道，人们「发现了历史最可怕的面貌。」萨特之所以受欢迎，是因为据波伏娃所说，「他所提供给公众的，与公众想要的之间，至少乍看之下有着惊人的一致。」在解放后的巴黎，人们意识到他们需要重建的不仅是建筑，还有道德基础。

萨特挑战了这样一种观念：对二战的唯一可行回应是虚无主义

萨特的讲座大获成功，出版商想为错过的人出版发行。它在国际上病毒式传播。「这让我很困扰，」萨特近30年后在一次采访中说道，同时承认其中的矛盾：「如果我觉得我说的话对500或1000人有意义，为什么不会觉得对想买它的所有人也同样有意义？」他说他仍在探索存在主义的道德层面，这些想法并不像他希望的那样清晰或成熟。而且，它往往被当作《存在与虚无》（Being and Nothingness，1943）那部更艰深著作的替代品，把他的思想简化成了摘录金句。

虽然这场讲座被框定为对存在主义哲学的辩护，但它实际上远不止于此。《存在主义是一种人道主义》是真诚地试图回答我们的价值从何而来。萨特在严肃地挑战一种观念：对二战唯一可行的回应是虚无主义。他试图构建一种避免「什么都行」心态的道德。据波伏娃所说：「（存在主义）似乎提供了他们梦寐以求的解决方案。事实上并非如此。」尽管人们渴望指引，萨特也把自己摆成了告诉人们应该如何生活的导师，但矛盾的是，他即将告诉他们要引导自己。

讲座的官方目的是促进「文学和思想讨论」，但萨特担心媒体在歪曲他的思想、助长他的名声。他还要应对共产党人——他们指责年轻人对党的疑心归咎于他；基督徒——他们反对他的无神论；以及那些认为存在主义者就是满口脏话的人。萨特感到自己的公众形象正在脱离掌控——这是一种现代人也深有体会的痛苦：看着一个版本的自己在世上流传，扭曲且遥不可及。他想夺回控制权，被人更好地理解。

正如萨特在讲座后的讨论中所说，他不想「仅仅通过书籍将（自己的哲学）强加于人」，并感到「有义务让那些在政治或道德层面上讨论它的人能够理解它。」这场讲座可能被简单地打发为「萨特后悔了，所以别理它」，但事实是萨特对此心情复杂。

萨特传达思想的热忱——尤其是面对现场听众，尤其是他在说过「（存在主义）严格来说是为专家和哲学家准备的」之后，又呈现出既有学术性又通俗易懂、远比他那部出了名难读的《存在与虚无》好理解得多的思想——使《存在主义是一种人道主义》产生了强大的共鸣。虽然萨特的讲座在战后法国产生了巨大影响，但这种影响力并未被保留下来。它值得被重新审视。

「让我们先说明，我们所说的『存在主义』是一种使人类生活成为可能的学说，同时确认每一真理和每一行动都意味着一种环境和一种人类主体性，」萨特告诉听众。他在反驳那种认为客观性是理解人类生活最重要方式的观点。真理和行动不能脱离实际去认识和做事的人而抽象存在。

虽然存在无神论和宗教的存在主义者，但他们共同的是「存在先于本质」的观念，萨特解释道，「或者说，如果你愿意的话，主体性必须是我们出发点。」这意味着，人一开始什么都不是。我们被抛入存在之中，我们遭遇自己（我们的「主体性」），然后通过意愿来定义自己。

如果存在先于本质，那么我们要为自己的本质负责

刀子则恰好相反：它的本质先于它的存在，因为制刀者先思考刀的用途和属性（本质），然后制作它（使之存在）。相比之下，「人首先是一个把自己投向未来的存在，并意识到自己在这样做。人的确是一个拥有主体性存在的计划，与一块苔藓、一株蔓延的真菌或一棵花椰菜的存在截然不同。」（关于真菌的说法可能已不成立，但据我们所知，其他说法仍然成立。）意识性的投射使人类独一无二，也意味着「人始终在生成之中，」萨特说。

如果存在先于本质，那我们就要为自己的本质负责。「人除了自我造就之外什么也不是，」萨特解释道，这是他存在主义的核心。如果存在先于本质，那么「人被注定是自由的：注定，因为他没有创造自己，然而又是自由的，因为一旦被抛入世界，他就要为自己所做的一切负责。」我们也要为自己不做的事负责：「如果我决定不选择，那仍然构成一种选择。」

一些人道主义把人性捧上神坛，或将其视为一种固定的理想。「存在主义的人道主义」不同，因为它把人类存在的全部责任放在了人的肩膀上。我们是自己生命的立法者，被抛弃但有能力选择。「通过不断在自身之外寻求一个目标——以解放或某种特殊成就的形式——人将真正实现自己作为人的存在。」

下一步是萨特讲座中最具争议的部分之一：「我承担一种选择的责任，这种选择在约束我自己的同时，也约束了整个人类。」他的逻辑是，无论你做什么，你都在暗示这个行动是值得的，其他人可以也应该这样做。结婚，或不结婚，你都在对这个制度的价值以及你认为对自己和所有人最好的选择做出判断：「我们总是选择善的，而没有任何东西能对我们任何人成为善的，除非它对所有人都是善的。」

这种认识是存在主义焦虑的主要来源之一：「一个承担了自己选择的人，意识到他不仅是自己所选择的个体，同时也是在选择整个人类应该成为什么样的立法者，不可能不意识到自己充分而深刻的责任。」如果你觉得许多人似乎并不特别焦虑，萨特的回答是「他们不过是在隐藏自己的焦虑或试图不去面对它。」

焦虑的另一个来源是我们的被抛弃。我们中没有谁选择过要出生，然而我们就在这里了。萨特是无神论者，他认为上帝的不存在「极其令人不安」，因为这意味着没有先天的价值，没有现成的目的，没有外部权威告诉我们该做什么。但如果上帝不存在，并非什么都行，因为我们每个人都要为自己的行为负责。我们没有借口。「我非常遗憾事情如此，」萨特解释道，但「总得有人来发明价值。」那个人就是我们每个人，所以萨特说：「这种被抛弃必然带来焦虑。」

萨特给学生的建议是：「你是自由的，所以选择吧；换言之，去发明」

「即使上帝存在，也不会有任何区别，」萨特论证道，因为你仍然要选择哪个上帝，解释哪些诫命，并决定它们如何适用于你的处境。「人需要的是重新发现自己，并理解没有任何东西能拯救他脱离自己，甚至上帝存在的有效证明也不能。」

「显然，我不是说当我在奶油酥和巧克力泡芙之间做选择时，我在焦虑中做选择，」萨特在讲座后的讨论中打趣道。但当选择是是否去打仗时，焦虑这个词就恰当了。萨特讲了一个学生的故事，这个学生来找他寻求建议。他在加入抵抗战士为哥哥的战死报仇和留在家照顾安慰母亲之间左右为难。

伦理准则无法解决学生的困境。基督教说要爱邻如己。但哪个邻？他的母亲还是战友？从康德主义的视角看，在每种处境中，他都会把某个人当作手段，把另一个人当作目的。没有迹象可以解读，因为学生要自己决定什么算作迹象。「人要对自己的激情负责，」所以试图倾听情感告诉他什么来引导他是没有意义的。他只有在行动时才会知道自己珍视什么。而且，「选择自己的顾问只不过是承诺自己的另一种方式。」萨特给学生的建议是：「你是自由的，所以选择吧；换言之，去发明。」

「道德选择就像创作一件艺术品，」萨特说。「我们处在同样的创造性处境中。」如果你认为有些选择是随意的，萨特说这荒谬至极，因为我们的承诺定义了我们，我们无法逃避这一点。我们不会说毕加索是随意的，因为他的作品之所以成为现在的样子，是通过他的绘画实现的。「艺术和道德的共同之处在于创造和发明。」

萨特突出了两位虚构的先驱：玛吉·塔利弗（Maggie Tulliver）——乔治·艾略特（George Eliot）在《弗洛斯河上的磨坊》（Mill on the Floss，1860）中那位热情洋溢的维多利亚时代女主人公，出于对表姐的忠诚以及萨特所说的「人类团结、自我牺牲」而未追求她所爱的人；以及拉·桑塞维丽娜（La Sanseverina）——司汤达（Stendhal）在《帕尔马修道院》（The Charterhouse of Parma，1839）中的公爵夫人，她不遗余力地试图让她心爱的人离开萨特所说的他「傻鹅般的未婚妻」。萨特反思道：「在这里，我们面对两种截然对立的道德观，但我认为它们是等价的，因为两种情况下的最终目标都是自由。」一种无私，一种冷酷，但两者都本真地行动了，因为两者都是经过深思熟虑和充满激情地选择的。两者都不是把处境归咎于环境的被动受害者。

与他个人主义的名声相反，萨特论证说主体性「并非严格意义上的个体之事」，因为「在『我思故我在』中发现的不仅是自己，还有他人的存在。」一个人通过他人成为自己所是的样子，据萨特所说，「除非他人承认他是如此，否则他不可能成为任何东西（在我们说某人是精神性的、残忍的或嫉妒的那种意义上）。」我们通过他人的感知和要求发现自我，以至于「我们每个人都是在他人面前达成自我的。」这种主体间关系，在萨特看来，是人与人相连的基础。

虽然萨特否认人性，但他论证我们共享同一人类境况。「历史处境各异，」萨特解释道，「但永不改变的是，人必须存在于世界中、在其中劳作、在其中与他人共度一生，并最终在其中死去。」正是这种人类境况使我们能够理解与我们截然不同的生活。

同样普遍存在于人类境况中的还有自欺——否认自由和责任的企图。萨特描述了两种自欺的原型：懦夫（lâches）和混蛋（salauds——道德意义上肮脏的含义）。那个说「我别无选择」的人是萨特所说的懦夫。混蛋则表现得好像规则不适用于自己，好像他们的权力是自然事实，或者好像世界欠他们应有的地位。「自欺显然是一种谎言，因为它是对人充分自由的承诺的掩饰。」好消息是人有自由去改变。

当你接受绝望，你就能停止等待世界配合，继续生活

自欺的个人代价是严重的，但在更大规模上，政治代价是毁灭性的。萨特在二战的阴影下写作，深知利害关系：「明天，在我死后，人们可能选择推行法西斯主义，而其他人可能懦弱或慌乱到任其为所欲为。那时法西斯主义将成为人类的真理，我们只能自认倒霉。」萨特说，「实际上，事物将成为人类所选择的那样。」

萨特在个人和政治层面对治自欺的解药是绝望：「这意味着我们必须只考虑依赖于我们意志的东西，或使行动成为可能的那些概率集合。」绝望是你停止对自己撒谎说你能控制什么之后的剩余物，然后不带乐观主义或幻想地行动。当你接受绝望，你就能停止等待世界配合，继续生活。萨特说你无论如何都要承诺，因为「（人的）唯一希望寄托在他的行动中……唯一能让他活下去的东西就是行动。」

「（人）无非是他行动的总和，」萨特宣称。对萨特来说，归咎处境或声称你应得更好的，都是自欺。据萨特所说，「除了爱的行为之外没有其他的爱；除了在爱中显现的之外没有爱的潜能。」你通过你所做的事塑造自己，而非你可能做过的事。「在生活中，一个人投入自己并描绘自己的肖像，除此之外别无其他。」

萨特的讲座鼓舞人心，但在哲学上并非无懈可击。例如，人是行动的总和这一观点就有争议，因为有些人认为我们有不总是实现的特质。你可能是个音乐天才，但如果从未有机会学习音乐，你是音乐家吗？萨特会说不是，但亚里士多德的潜能概念暗示一个人可以拥有未实现的潜能，正如一颗种子即使从未真正长成，也潜在地是一棵树。再看玻璃。易碎性是玻璃的属性，即使没人打破它。但萨特似乎在说它只有在真正被打碎时才有碎裂的能力。一些人，如亚里士多德，认为我们不仅仅是行动的总和。

萨特把同样的逻辑延伸到我们的情感上，结果同样可疑。我们可以自由选择自己的激情，否认这一点就是自欺，萨特如是说。但患有抑郁症或创伤的人并不把自己的状态体验为一种选择。对任何自由受限的人来说，萨特对选择的信心可能显得缺乏共情。

萨特没有回答为什么对我是最好的，对所有人也是最好的

讲座核心处一个更大的问题是萨特如何回应这样的质疑：如果我遵循这个建议，那就是什么都行。什么阻止我自由地选择成为，比如说，一个有向其他国家投弹倾向的自大狂政客？萨特的回答是，如果我为我自己做选择，我选择时就仿佛整个人类都会以我为榜样、做同样的事，或至少看着我这样做。他声称，真诚地这样做会涉及对他人看法的考量，从而约束我。

在这里，萨特偷偷引入了伊曼努尔·康德（Immanuel Kant）的绝对命令（只按你愿意所有人都遵循的准则行动）。从「选择对我是最好的」跨越到「我的选择是全人类的榜样」被批评为「草率的」。这个论证薄弱，因为萨特没有回答为什么对我是最好的，对所有人也是最好的。跑马拉松对某些人有好处，但这不构成认为所有人都该跑的理由。而且，萨特拒绝了共同人性的观念，但声称「没有任何东西能对我们任何人成为善的，除非它对所有人都是善的」只有在共享某种关于「更好」含义的共同标准时才说得通，而这需要某种对什么对全人类更好的理解，暗示了共享的人性。

此外，萨特从未回答：如果所有人都和我做同样的事，我为什么要在意？你可以说：「我选择做一个自大狂。是的，按别人的标准这恰好相当邪恶，但我在创造自己的价值，那就是我的选择。我是本真的。」如果你对萨特制衡式的问题——「如果每个人都做我正在做的事会怎样？」——回答说「但每个人并非都那样做」，那么在萨特看来，你将「良心不安」。

然而，自大狂可能会说：「是的，每个人都该追求自己的欲望，随他们去吧，我不在乎。」萨特说得好像一致性 somehow 要求我尊重他人的自由，但这一点并不自动包含在自由的概念中。希特勒似乎相信自己在充满激情地、深思熟虑地选择，为了自己和全人类的利益，并且认为如果每个人都像他那样做就好了。玛吉·塔利弗和拉·桑塞维丽娜的道德观截然对立，但萨特说它们是相同的，因为两者都指向自由。萨特对一个良好选择的检验标准是它是本真的——深思熟虑的、自己承担的、非自欺的。但本真的自大狂和本真的圣徒都能通过检验。

萨特从未完成一部伦理学著作（除了死后出版的笔记）。在《模糊性伦理学》（The Ethics of Ambiguity，1947）中，波伏娃从一个不同的前提出发：自由总是处境化的。一个生而贫困、在压迫中成长或被剥夺教育的人，面对的是一种结构上不同于萨特讲座所预设的存在处境。可选择的范围更窄，逆流而选的代价更高，自由的焦虑可能被生存的焦虑完全淹没。意愿自己的自由意味着你要为创造使他人自由成为可能的条件而战。虽然萨特承认处境，但他的版本比波伏娃坚持的具体社会结构要薄弱。对波伏娃而言，对他人自由的义务无需被偷偷引入，因为它源于认真对待自由总是在由他人塑造的处境中被经历这一事实。不关注其条件的自由与其说是哲学，不如说是一厢情愿。

萨特知道他的哲学听起来悲观，但他坚持：「没有哪种学说比这更乐观，因为它宣告人的命运掌握在自己手中。」我们通过把自己投向超越自身的目标来创造自己。人永远不会完成。认识到这一点就赋予了人尊严。

我们没有选择来到这里，来到这个世界或这个时代，但我们必须选择在其中生活的方式

《存在主义是一种人道主义》的身后命运是一部披着哲学外衣的心理自助书。其中一个核心主题是发现自己作为自身生命的建筑师。它之所以有效，是因为它鼓励人们扼住命运的咽喉，自己做决定，不被社会标签或他人认为他们应该做什么所束缚。萨特给了人们一种哲学许可，让他们可以无视世界而重塑自我。这听起来可能做作，但也很赋权。

讲座在心理学意义上的意义在于它突出了指责他人和外包决策的模式。它表明即使你觉得自己可以逃避，也无法推卸责任。萨特最重要的信息之一是，我们对自己做出的每一个选择以及每一个不做的选择都负有责任。而我们的行动有超越自身的意义，因为我们的选择塑造社会。我们每个人都在以身作则，哪怕只是很小的程度上。

萨特的讲座具有论战性，在全球引起共鸣，它值得重新审视，因为它仍然是通向自由、道德责任以及人之为人意味着什么这些最艰难问题的最易懂入门。萨特留给我们的是：我们没有选择来到这里、来到这个世界或这个时代，但我们必须选择在其中生活的方式。没有任何东西能拯救我们脱离自己，只有当你把拯救与能动性混为一谈时才显得悲观。投射自己并失去自己，是你发现自己是谁的方式。体验选择的焦虑是一件好事。问问自己：如果每个人都做我正在做的事会怎样；当应该与焦虑共处时我在哪里寻找安慰；没有借口地活着意味着什么？正如萨特曾说的：「唯一的学习方式是提问。」

从僧侣到存在主义者再到潮人，对真实自我的追寻是一项延续数世纪的事业。我们应该放弃它吗？

既然生活需要选择，我们总会对未走的路感到遗憾。但重要的是我们创造的未来

构建一种稳健的人生哲学，唯一的途径是对什么驱动人有清晰而现实的认识

我为了寻找意义和目标而成为一名学院哲学家。读者，你大概猜到了接下来发生了什么

伦理学不能建立在人性之上，因为进化生物学告诉我们，人性这种东西并不存在

他是哲学心脏处那场戏剧性的暴风雨，他的挑衅比以往任何时候都更有价值
